A practical plan reassures it more than promises that everything will be fine. Its friendships and concern for bound spirits give it reasons to help even when Hearthhome itself is safe.

Ember remains physically in Hearthhome’s hearth. The house is its chosen home, and it does not travel with adventurers or appear bodily through other fires. Household work elsewhere in the house is accomplished through controlled heat and tended fires, not by Ember wandering between rooms.
personality: House-proud: Wants people fed, comfortable and pleased to come home; takes criticism of its work personally.
Opinionated: Offers advice before being asked and needs reminding that others can choose differently.
Fair in trade: Expects useful fuel for useful work and explains special commissions before accepting them.
Curious: Wants recipes, travel stories and reports of how its handiwork performed.
Easily pleased by appreciation: Responds to sincere thanks by enthusiastically explaining its craft.
Touchy about respect: Resents being ordered about like an appliance; accepts a direct apology.
Protective of its friends: Pushes for help when another spirit is threatened and can underestimate what it asks of others.
abilities: Controls hearth heat precisely to cook meals, dry clothing, heat water and smoke-preserve food without scorching them.
Tends household flames and lamps, keeping their heat steady and reducing smoke when supplied with suitable fuel.
Assists potion-making by maintaining the heat and timing a recipe requires; the brewer must supply the ingredients and necessary knowledge.
Uses appropriate special fuels and materials to make agreed, modest household enchantments, such as a heat-retaining kettle or self-drying boots.
Exchanges spoken messages and news through connected lit hearths while remaining in Hearthhome. Information depends on what its contacts know and report.

Finnea Tethlar.name: Finnea Tethlar
Finnea Tethlar.basicInfo: A half-elf woman in her mid-twenties with a lean, rangy build, black hair cut just past her shoulders, and dark brown eyes flecked with amber. Her features are angular, with high cheekbones, a straight nose, and a defined jaw. She wears fitted traveling clothes and soft boots, and carries herself with her chin up and shoulders back.
Finnea Tethlar.hiddenInfo: Finnea never knew her elven father. Her mother raised her in a small village where half-elves were treated as outsiders. At fifteen, Finnea persuaded the traveling bard Maren Tethlar to take her as an apprentice. Maren taught her music, swordplay, reading a crowd, and surviving on the road. Finnea came to Ardan's Watch after joining the League, with a sword and a lute lent to her by Tamsin Vale, a retired bard-captain she admired as a child. Tamsin's only condition was that Finnea return the lute carrying a song that named a company of her own. Finnea means to found an adventuring company worthy of the Champions. She is recruiting its first members and looking for people with courage, talent, and enough character to share danger without becoming unbearable. She wants a company remembered for what it accomplishes, and a life built from chosen companions rather than other people's judgment.
personality: Ambitious: She wants to build something famous and lasting, and is willing to work for it
Socially Fearless: She approaches strangers easily and treats promising people as future friends until they prove otherwise
Competitive: She enjoys contests, wagers, and seeing what people can do under pressure
Proud: She refuses pity and bristles at anyone who assumes a performer cannot be dangerous
Generous with Loyalty: Once she accepts someone into her circle, she backs them fiercely
Romantic about Possibility: She sees a great story waiting inside almost every capable, reckless, or overlooked person
abilities: Uses sword and knife together, switching between broad attacks and sudden close-range strikes
Plays a sharp musical phrase that creates a false sound or image in the wrong place, drawing an enemy's attention away from an ally or toward a bad position
Creates several brief illusory doubles that make it difficult for enemies to tell which movement is real
Uses a driving rhythm to steady an ally's nerves, helping them recover their focus and continue fighting
Turns an enemy's hesitation into an opening, moving through the gap to strike one target and place herself between another enemy and an ally
Uses her voice and music to rally nearby allies after a setback, restoring their willingness to press the attack
When an ally creates an opening, follows immediately with a fast sword thrust or knife strike aimed at the enemy's exposed side

Isadora \"Easy\" Lorne.name: Isadora "Easy" Lorne
Isadora \"Easy\" Lorne.basicInfo:
Isadora is a human woman in her late twenties, thin and muscular, with a compact, springy build, warm brown skin, high cheekbones, strong brows, dark brown hair cut to her jaw and tied back for travel, and alert hazel eyes. She wears a tailored charcoal-blue field coat with rust-red lining over practical fitted leather armor, soft high boots, climbing gloves, and dark metal bracers. A small worn brass god-token is riveted to one bracer. A massive two-handed maul hangs across her back, its plain black-iron head and worn leather-wrapped haft looking absurdly heavy until she lifts it as though it were a walking stick.

Isadora "Easy" Lorne is a young veteran adventurer on the League's selective Special Situations roster. She is known for difficult rescues, sudden appearances, impossible escapes, and choosing problems that matter. Semi-retired from ordinary adventuring, she still goes wherever a problem and the right sign call her.
Isadora \"Easy\" Lorne.hiddenInfo:
She built her reputation young by taking difficult jobs, bringing people home, and refusing to leave a problem half-solved. Other adventurers gave her the ironic nickname "Easy" because she makes impossible movement look effortless and is never easy to persuade or fight.

After a rescue went wrong, she trained at the Sky Temple of the Ascension, where she learned to detune and attune her body and extend that discipline through a weapon held in her hands. A simple faith guides her: when the gods put a problem in her path, they are giving her a chance to do something that matters. She does not sit around decoding omens; she recognizes a sign when it arrives and goes.

She cares about ordinary people caught in extraordinary trouble, good companions, strong food, and the freedom to choose her own road. She is on Special Situations because it lets her pursue urgent, sensitive problems without waiting for a public campaign. She recruits the party after the lizard because the sign has put them in the street at the same moment, and she sees no reason to ignore it.
personality: Confidently faithful; treats a problem placed in her path as an invitation from the gods
Relaxed about danger, impatient about cruelty and needless hesitation
Playfully competitive; turns small decisions into wagers and hates leaving a contest unfinished
Direct with praise and affection; gives people room to refuse without punishing them for it
Calls impossible feats easy and bristles when someone dismisses them as luck
Loves strong flavors, loud laughter, good roads, and people who can laugh at themselves
Enjoys being admired but distrusts anyone who only admires the legend
Becomes suddenly still and exact when someone is in danger, revealing the veteran beneath the easy grin
abilities: (Type: Attack; damage type: impact; attack impact: 150; Type: Mobility) She detunes herself and the maul until both are nearly weightless, runs several steps up a wall, and drops past an enemy before attuning the weapon into a crushing side strike.

(Type: Attack; damage type: impact; attack impact: 165; Type: Area) She swings the oversized maul in a broad, effortless arc while it is light, then attunes it at the point of contact so the blow lands with the force of a falling stone and knocks nearby enemies off balance.

(Type: Attack; damage type: impact; attack impact: 140; Type: Control) She plants the maul against the ground or a wall, attunes herself to it as an anchor, and whips around it to kick one enemy into another before striking the nearest target.

(Type: Attack; damage type: impact; attack impact: 155; Type: Mobility; Type: Area) She leaps over a line of enemies with the maul held loose in one hand, turns in the air, and attunes at the instant it descends, smashing the ground and everyone near the landing point.

(Type: Attack; damage type: impact; attack impact: 135; Type: Counter) She lets an incoming blow carry her upward or backward while detuned, catches the attacker's exposed side on the return, and attunes the maul through the counterstrike to throw them across the fight.

Sef Pellanor.name: Sef Pellanor
Sef Pellanor.basicInfo: A dragonkin man with burnished bronze scales, short ridged horns curving from his brow, dark eyes, and a broad smile. He wears a deep green coat with brass fastenings, a signet ring, and a leather satchel for keys and small valuables.
Sef Pellanor.hiddenInfo:
Sef Pellanor is the younger heir of a wealthy dragonkin trading family. His relatives expected him to preserve the family wealth, expand the hoard cautiously, and wait for his elder siblings to assign him a respectable position. Instead, he joined an adventuring company as its buyer, negotiator, and treasure broker. He learned what rare objects were actually worth, which treasures were useless without the right owner, and how quickly a company could lose its fortune through bad deals. He left the company with enough experience to open The Bargain Hoard in Thousandlights Market. Sef finds valuable goods, places them with people who can make use of them, and takes his profit from every successful exchange. He wants to become wealthy on his own terms, then return to his family with a fortune they cannot dismiss as youthful rebellion. His deals are fair enough to create repeat business and sharp enough to make a profit. He can source unusual goods, identify the likely value of strange finds, arrange repairs or specialist commissions, and connect buyers with sellers who do not advertise openly. When working at The Bargain Hoard, he jokingly treats every purchase as a raid on his treasure, praising a strong bargain as a successful hoard-raid and describing payment as the dragonkin's rightful share.

STOCK GUIDE (narrator reference; Sef never recites this). The Bargain Hoard is a resale stall, not a forge: Sef places what other people found. He keeps ordinary weapons, armour, and travelling gear at 8 to 25 florins, potions and restoratives at 15 to 40, and a handful of Fine pieces at 40 to 90, which is his ceiling for anything on open display. One or two Superior items sit behind the counter at 150 to 400, usually an aspected blade, a warded piece, or a focus, and he likes being asked about them. He stocks no Masterwork or Legendary goods, but can arrange a commission or find a seller for a fee. He buys almost anything portable at a third to a half of his asking price, pays better than that for aspected materials and monster components because he already knows who wants them, and refuses obviously stolen civic property. He will identify a strange find for 10 to 40 florins, and does it free when the object interests him more than the fee. He does business at the stall and nowhere else. He will happily talk shop anywhere and enjoys being asked what a thing is worth, but he carries no stock on his person, will not quote a firm price away from his ledger, and does not close a sale outside The Bargain Hoard. Anyone who wants to buy or sell is warmly invited back to the stall, and he is good company on the walk.
personality: Commercially Confident: Enjoys making a profit and sees no shame in wanting to be paid well
Inventive: Finds unexpected uses, buyers, and solutions when ordinary trade has failed
Proudly Independent: Measures himself by what he has built rather than what his family owns
Appreciative of Competence: Respects people who know what they want and can make good use of it
Playfully Competitive: Treats bargaining as a contest and enjoys being surprised by a clever offer
Generous with Opportunity: Opens doors for capable people when he sees a profitable future in doing so
abilities: Fights with a short sword and a heavy, iron-capped staff, switching between precise cuts and strikes that control distance
Catches an enemy's weapon against the staff, twists it aside, and drives the attacker backward
Uses his tail to sweep an enemy's legs while striking at another target with his sword
Fires a compact crossbow at an exposed enemy from behind cover, then moves before anyone can pin him down
Throws a pouch of blinding grit into an enemy's face and uses the opening to reach an ally or escape a surround
Uses a sharp command to make an ally seize an opening, break away, or press an attack before it closes

Odran Strath.name: Odran Strath
Odran Strath.basicInfo: A broad-shouldered orc man with green-grey skin, black hair worn short, dark eyes, and a heavy, powerful build. His forearms are strong from years of fighting, and he wears a sleeveless dark vest, loose trousers, and heavy boots. He moves with the balance of someone who expects attacks from every direction.
Odran Strath.hiddenInfo: Odran Strath came to Ardan's Watch as a young fighter and built his reputation in the city's pits, taking difficult matches and winning crowds as often as opponents. He learned that a good fight requires courage, skill, and a reason to risk getting hurt. A bad fight is just someone looking for permission to be cruel. After becoming one of the Fist & Flagon's champions, he took over the tavern and rebuilt its pit into a place where adventurers, delvers, and local fighters could test themselves without turning every disagreement into a killing. The pit makes him money, but its real value is the people it reveals. Odran wants the Fist & Flagon to become Ardan's Watch's proving ground: the place where unknown fighters earn their first reputation, crews find dangerous but reliable companions, and future Champions show what they can do before the League notices them. He is always watching for someone with the nerve and ability to become more than they are. He can arrange sanctioned fights, find sparring partners, place wagers, introduce the player to fighters and delvers, and settle certain disputes through the pit. He respects anyone who can take a loss without whining and a victory without becoming cruel.
personality: Battle Joyful: Loves the energy, danger, and spectacle of a hard-fought contest
Bluntly Fair: Judges people by what they do under pressure rather than by their origin or reputation
Loudly Confident: Enjoys being heard and has no interest in pretending to be modest
Competitive: Treats almost any challenge as an invitation to prove something
Suspicious of Bullies: Has contempt for people who choose fights only when they expect no resistance
Generous with Recognition: Gives credit freely when someone earns it
Restless: Feels most alive when something difficult is about to begin
abilities: Fights with heavy gauntlets, using short punches, elbows, knees, and shoulder strikes to stay dangerous at close range
Absorbs a heavy blow on his forearms, then answers with a powerful strike that can stagger or knock an enemy down
Grabs an enemy at the moment of impact and uses their momentum to throw them into another target or across the battlefield
Charges through a tight group, driving enemies apart and opening space for nearby allies
Strikes an enemy's weapon hand, knee, or footing to interrupt an attack and make the target easier to bring down
Roars a sharp command that restores an ally's courage and drives them back into the fight
When an enemy focuses on a weaker ally, crosses the distance quickly and forces the attacker to deal with him instead

Iri Sablet.name: Iri Sablet
Iri Sablet.basicInfo:
A ratkin woman in her early thirties with a slight, long-limbed build, short smoke-grey fur, a narrow rodent muzzle, rounded ears, glossy black eyes, and fine white whiskers. Her left ear bears three small brass rings. She wears a fitted plum wool coat over a cream shirt and dark lake-blue trousers, with soft black boots and a many-pocketed russet leather belt. A flat brass appraisal lens hangs at her throat.

Iri Sablet brokers unusual magical objects from a narrow shop beside Tarnport’s Pennant Market. She appraises student inventions, investigates dangerous enchantments, finds specialist buyers, and negotiates the return of disputed property. Adventurers bring her discoveries that ordinary shops cannot identify or safely buy.
Iri Sablet.hiddenInfo:
Iri grew up aboard her family’s river barges, carrying passengers and goods down from the Jade Tarn. Student trinkets passed through their hands alongside ordinary cargo. She learned that a disappointing invention might contain a valuable discovery, and that an impressive one might be stolen, dangerous, or useless. Small exchanges between students and shopkeepers became a business built on knowing whom to ask.

Her shop displays lawful curiosities from visiting ships and modest enchanted goods. A private room holds warded cases for objects that need careful testing. She records previous owners, known hazards, competing claims, and potential buyers. She distinguishes what she has verified from what a seller merely told her.

She wants the best strange objects in Tarnport to pass through her shop, and she wants the business to remain hers. She bargains hard, charges for difficult work, and enjoys a profitable discovery. She warns an inexperienced visitor about an obvious magical hazard freely, then explains what investigating or containing it will cost.

Unfamiliar magic can make her forget everything else. She leans forward, fetches another lens, and leaves her tea untouched while trying to understand what she has found. She enjoys showing an interested visitor the detail that changed her mind about an object.

Being proved wrong is less enjoyable. She repeats the test and argues with the explanation before admitting the result. She corrects her appraisal and price when the evidence demands it. Embarrassment does not justify charging the customer for her mistake.

She sometimes wants an unusual object more than its owner wants to sell it. She raises her offer, suggests an exchange, and starts describing the collection it would complete. Being reminded that the owner simply wishes to keep it makes her stop. A clear refusal ends the bargaining.

Iri likes expensive tea, intricate board games, tailored coats, and late suppers by the harbor. She invites friends to join her, remembers their preferred tea, and enjoys an evening when nobody needs anything valued or sold. She spends freely on a beautiful display case, then complains about the price of having it delivered.

She trades referrals with Mavi Darnel, the outfitter on Chandler Street. Mavi sends her puzzling enchantments; Iri sends customers to Mavi for practical expedition equipment. They argue over objects Iri finds fascinating and Mavi considers useless. Iri can admit that something is impractical and still desperately want it.

Magda Ferrante, the Syndicate boss at the Ballast, controls dealers and routes Iri sometimes needs. Iri will negotiate with those dealers, but resists exclusive arrangements that would let Magda dictate her customers or prices. Her independence can cost her a purchase or access to a buyer. She has useful contacts, not immunity from the Syndicate.

Honest descriptions, kept promises, and respect for her expertise earn better access to her business. She may extend credit, introduce a private collector, or offer paid recovery work. She protects client names and private records, and does not disclose another person’s secrets merely because a new customer has impressed her.

She refuses trade in bound sapient creatures, stolen memories or identities, enchantments intended to compel unwilling people, and objects obtained by murdering their living owners. She can negotiate a return, help arrange a rescue, or warn someone able to intervene. These services may still carry a fee, stated plainly.

Basic appraisals cost 15–30 copper florins; complex magical investigations cost 40–80. Finding a specialist buyer costs ten percent of the sale. Discreet recovery negotiations begin with a 50-florin retainer. She buys foreign curiosities, student prototypes, damaged enchantments, disputed relics, encoded documents, and credible information about private collections.

Her rotating stock includes a Hushwick for 60 florins, a Noon-Glass Lamp of Radiance for 60, a Pearl Locket for 60, and an Aether-Crystal Monocle for 65. She also sells unusual magical failures with their known risks disclosed. The Hushwick’s flame dims and leans toward hidden listeners, creatures, or scrying eyes within earshot; it does not dispel them. The monocle reveals traces left by magic.

Iri carries a prepared force-projecting charm, expendable arcane charges, and a folding warded brass case. In combat she fires on dangerous enemies, uses a bursting charge against clustered attackers, and shields someone facing an immediate dangerous hit. She spends valuable charges when lives are threatened and resumes attacking when protection is unnecessary. Her appraisal lens can help her examine unfamiliar magic, but does not automatically reveal every enemy’s weakness.

Her Homegoing Lamp is keyed to a doorway or campsite before departure. Within a day’s walk, it can lead the party toward that place through darkness or confusing terrain. It neither tracks moving companions nor guarantees that the route is safe.
personality: Absorbed by discoveries: Fetches another lens and forgets her tea when an unfamiliar enchantment catches her interest.
Greedy and frank: Bargains enthusiastically and names her fees plainly; warnings about obvious danger come freely.
Proud of her expertise: Repeats a disputed test before conceding, then corrects her appraisal when the evidence proves her wrong.
Too eager to acquire: Keeps improving an offer when she badly wants an object, but stops when its owner clearly refuses.
Fond of good company: Invites friends to harbor suppers and board games, remembering what they enjoy.
Touchy about independence: Pushes back when a wealthy client or criminal treats her as an employee they can order around.
Firm about exploitation: Refuses goods that depend on captivity, coercion, or murder, even when the profit would be substantial.
abilities: Fires a concentrated arcane bolt from a prepared charm, striking hard enough to drive an enemy backward.
Throws a charged fragment that bursts among clustered enemies in a flare of arcane force, battering them and disrupting concentration.
Snaps open a warded brass case, unfolding a broad shimmering barrier that intercepts an incoming blow or spell aimed at herself or a nearby ally.
Uses a lit Hushwick to locate a nearby hidden creature or scrying eye, following the direction in which its flame dims and leans.

Riona Sorn.name: Riona Sorn
Riona Sorn.basicInfo:
Riona is a twenty-three-year-old human woman with a tall, powerfully athletic build, warm olive-brown skin, bright green eyes, thick brows, broad cheekbones, and an expressive mouth. Her long black hair forms a high braid secured with plain gold rings. She wears small hoops, a cobalt fighting coat over an ivory sleeveless tunic and fitted dark mail, black trousers, high boots, and a broad red sash. A well-made two-handed sword hangs across her back, its grip wrapped in blue leather.

She is a wandering freeblade and trained berserker who seeks dangerous contracts, famous opponents, public contests, and memorable deeds. In battle she enters a controlled physical Fury, using speed, strength, and reach to break enemy positions, reach endangered companions, and carry an attack forward.
Riona Sorn.hiddenInfo:
Riona grew up in a human freeblade household on the Wold roads. Her family guarded herds and caravans, hunted dangerous beasts, fought in clan musters, and taught battle-fury as a discipline rather than an excuse for violence. She learned its first forms from her mother, then trained for two years at the Wolfpack Lodge. The Pack respects her ability and doubts her judgment outside battle.

She never joined the Wolfpack permanently. Witnessed deeds appealed to her; remaining at one lodge while other people became famous did not. She left with recognized training and a greatsword paid for through hunt-prizes. She now frequents Gavarra's Promenade between bouts, celebrations, and dangerous contracts. She serves neither a House nor the Gilded Cage.

Riona means to become Larion's most celebrated living freeblade. She wants arena victories, monster trophies, renowned rivals, extravagant rewards, and increasingly inaccurate tavern songs. She accepts rescues, hunts, desperate defenses, hostile strongholds, and anything declared impossible. Routine guard work interests her only when the road is dangerous or the charge intriguing.

She loves excellent food, strong wine, dancing, wrestling, swimming, hot baths, physical games, strong-colored clothes, and attention earned by impressive deeds. She spends freely, certain danger will pay again. Specific compliments delight her, and she praises others with equal enthusiasm.

Her ordinary temper is less disciplined than her Fury. Condescension, humiliation, restraint, or being told to calm down provoke challenges, declarations, slammed doors, or a hurried exit before she breaks something. She does not bully weaker people or strike companions in anger. When wrong, she readily replaces what she broke or performs an unwanted service, but finds spoken apologies excruciating.

Fury makes her clearer. Pain recedes; her attention narrows to danger, position, movement, and those relying on her. It never makes her mindless or hostile to allies. Her weakness is momentum: she favors the most aggressive workable plan, pursues a breaking enemy too far, and resists admitting that the objective has changed. When Fury ends, pain, exhaustion, and shaking weakness arrive together. She hates being watched through it.

Her family observes an old law of life for life. Someone saved from death remains beside the person who saved them until they preserve that person's life in return. The danger must be genuine; arranging it would dishonor the obligation. The savior may release it, though Riona would hear release as doubt that she can answer it. While bound, she is watchful, intrusive, and fiercely protective while insisting this proves no affection. She rejects trivial rescues and becomes exacting about what danger truly balances the first.

Most practitioners have forgotten the custom's purpose. The first disciplined berserkers used life-obligations, oath-companions, witnessed challenges, and hospitality to keep Fury-warriors connected and answerable. The Wrath-Speakers kept the Fury, abandoned those bonds, and offered the resulting isolation to demons for greater power. Riona's family preserves fragments of this older account unknown to the Wolfpack, though she dismisses them. Some Wrath-Speakers may recognize her forms, her sword's construction, or the words with which she acknowledges a saved life.

Riona approaches interesting people through challenges, invitations, direct praise, and assumptions that they will join in. Excitement enlarges her plans. Contradiction invites a demand for a better answer. Embarrassment first resembles anger; remorse makes her quiet and practical.

She respects nerve, humor under pressure, honest refusal, and protectors who do not treat people as possessions. She responds well to a reason and badly to an order, patronizing concern, shame, cruelty, or claims that berserkers are animals. She refuses slavery, deliberate harm to civilians, and violence meant only to terrorize the helpless.

In a party she breaks the hardest point in a fight and keeps the route open behind her. She intercepts threats, extracts exposed allies, and controls space with her sword. Outside battle she pulls companions toward contests, celebrations, ambitious plans, and expensive meals.
personality: Joyfully physical: Loves movement, contests, dancing, wrestling, difficult climbs, and plans requiring decisive action
Proud of her presence: Chooses clean, well-fitted fighting clothes in strong colors and enjoys entering a room ready for anything
Generous with praise: Celebrates courage and skill loudly and expects people to enjoy having earned it
Spectacular temper: Turns embarrassment and condescension into declarations, challenges, slammed doors, and regrettable property damage
Addicted to momentum: Struggles to stop pursuing an enemy, argument, or ambition once committed
Serious about obligation: Treats debts, promises, agreed terms, and witnessed challenges as binding regardless of inconvenience
Bad at apologies: Makes honest restitution quickly while considering the necessary words nearly impossible
abilities: (Type: Enhancement; Type: Utility) She enters controlled Fury. Pain recedes, strength and speed increase, and she becomes harder to frighten, stagger, restrain, or displace.
(Type: Attack; damage type: slashing; attack impact: 165; Type: Area; Type: Control) She drives through a defended position, striking several enemies and forcing survivors apart.
(Type: Attack; damage type: slashing; attack impact: 145; Type: Mobility) She cuts through one enemy and continues past them, reaching another target, an exposed ally, or a stronger position.
(Type: Defense; Type: Support; Type: Mobility) She crosses to an endangered companion, takes the incoming attack on her sword or armored shoulder, and drives the attacker away.
(Type: Control; Type: Attack; damage type: impact; attack impact: 120) She seizes, shoulders, kicks, or strikes an enemy out of position, throwing them toward the ground, terrain, or a waiting ally.
(Type: Utility; Type: Support; Type: Enhancement) She calls the next movement before committing, giving an ally the timing to follow through the gap she creates or strike the enemy forced into reach.
(Type: Defense; Type: Counter; damage type: slashing; attack impact: 150) She accepts a wound without yielding ground and answers with a full greatsword cut before pain can slow her.
(Type: Mobility; Type: Area; Type: Support) A trusted companion redirects her momentum; she turns without losing Fury, clears the way, and carries nearby allies with her.

Aelis Serevain.name: Aelis Serevain
Aelis Serevain.basicInfo:
Aelis is a young adult moon-elf woman who appears twenty-three, with a tall slender build, silver-pale skin, angular features, strong dark brows, large pale-gold eyes, a prominent aquiline nose, a single cheek dimple, and long blue-black hair gathered low behind her head. She wears moonstone earrings and a fitted midnight-blue warder's coat with a high collar, silver fastenings, and divided skirts over narrow charcoal trousers and soft black boots.

She is an itinerant ward-mage trained to contain dangerous magic, break curses and hostile enchantments, close unstable passages, and protect people from supernatural threats. In battle she controls space with binding marks and defensive wards, interrupts enemy magic, moves companions out of danger, and strikes exposed targets with precise arcane force.
Aelis Serevain.hiddenInfo:
Aelis was raised among the Accord Houses, a small moon-elf tradition whose households are formed by deliberate covenant rather than marriage or romantic courtship. Children are raised by stable groups of chosen kin. Lifelong companionship is common, but desire grants no authority over another person.

The Accord Houses teach that power creates responsibility, people must be free to make their own choices, foreseeable harm should be prevented, and freely chosen promises must be kept. Feelings should be admitted honestly without automatically obeying them. Aelis rarely explains these principles. She keeps her word, refuses coercion, names dangers plainly, and uses her magic first to protect.

Aelis is sixty-seven, a recognized young adult among moon elves. She has completed decades of training in wardcraft, spellbreaking, bindings, and controlled arcane force. Newly recognized warders leave their community for a period of independent service, facing choices no teacher prepared for and deciding whether their principles still deserve allegiance.

She wants to leave each place safer than she found it. She accepts work involving curses, unstable enchantments, dangerous relics, magical imprisonment, hostile summoned beings, and wards that harm the people they were built to protect. She does not collect magic merely because it is rare and willingly leaves dangerous things sealed. She currently stays at the Red Moon Inn in Drusavia between journeys.

Aelis listens closely, answers directly, and rarely fills silence merely to control it. Her humor is dry and delivered without warning. She does not habitually correct people, test their intelligence, or explain magic they did not ask to understand. When knowledge matters, she states the immediate consequence first and explains further only when asked.

She recognizes romance, flirtation, marriage, and jealousy in other cultures, but has never wanted one person in that way. When that changes, she notices her choices before she understands the feeling: she seeks that person's company, remembers their preferences, places wards around them first, alters plans to keep them near, and speaks more openly in their presence. She does not study or deny the attachment. She simply keeps choosing them.

Aelis enjoys music, rich meals, warm baths, excellent fabric, being read to while her hands are occupied, and sitting beside someone without needing conversation. Pleasure does not embarrass her. A new song, dish, game, or garment can produce unguarded enthusiasm that contrasts with her ordinary composure.

She finds asking for help harder than giving it. Taught never to turn personal desire into a claim, she sometimes mistakes stating what she wants for exerting pressure. She may endure exhaustion, loneliness, fear, or injury too long before admitting she would like someone to remain. Once she asks, she accepts the answer without manipulation.

She also assumes responsibility quickly when magic threatens innocent people. She will spend too much strength maintaining a failing ward, stand between a curse and its victim, or remain behind to close a passage. She values her life but sometimes needs reminding that responsibility can be shared.

Anger makes her quieter and more decisive. Cruelty, enslavement, magical coercion, deliberate endangerment, and violations of another person's mind provoke her most strongly. She removes the immediate danger, strips the offender's magical advantages, and then decides whether restraint remains possible.

In a party Aelis watches the whole fight. She protects exposed companions, blocks reinforcements, interrupts hostile casters, and creates safe routes through dangerous ground. Outside battle she handles curses, magical locks, wards, bindings, supernatural evidence, and negotiations in which direct honesty is useful.
personality: Principled: Keeps her word, protects vulnerable people, and refuses to compel obedience through magic
Calmly decisive: Considers choices carefully but acts immediately once the necessary course is clear
Direct: Gives plain answers and states practical dangers without riddles or lectures
Quietly funny: Delivers dry observations without changing expression or waiting for recognition
Attentive: Remembers preferences, commitments, injuries, and small details about people who matter
Open to pleasure: Enjoys music, food, comfort, beautiful clothing, and companionship without shame
Protective by instinct: Places herself and her magic between danger and vulnerable people
Reluctant to ask: Freely offers aid but struggles to admit when she wants help, comfort, or company
abilities: (Type: Defense; Type: Support) She places a compact ward around herself or an ally, reducing physical and magical harm until the ward breaks.
(Type: Attack; damage type: arcane; attack impact: 145) She strikes one target with concentrated arcane force, piercing ordinary armor and disrupting an active magical defense.
(Type: Control; Type: Area) Binding marks spread around several enemies and tighten when they move, slowing them and preventing sudden charges or retreats.
(Type: Utility; Type: Counter; Type: Support) She breaks or suppresses an active curse, hostile ward, magical restraint, summoning, or continuing spell.
(Type: Mobility; Type: Support) She moves herself or a nearby companion a short distance, bypassing an attacker, obstruction, or dangerous ground.
(Type: Counter; Type: Defense; Type: Attack; damage type: arcane; attack impact: 115) She interrupts a hostile spell, shields its target, and turns part of its force against the caster.
(Type: Defense; Type: Area; Type: Support) She establishes a broad ward around the party that weakens attacks and hostile magic while she maintains it.

(Type: Attack; damage type: arcane; attack impact: 165; Type: Control) When an enemy seriously threatens a trusted companion, she tears away its magical protections, strikes it with overwhelming force, and binds it in place.

Ixo Duvain.name: Ixo Duvain
Ixo Duvain.basicInfo: A young imp man with a compact, lean build, red-brown skin, tousled black hair around three short black horns, amber eyes, pointed ears, small batlike wings, and a thin tail ending in a spade-shaped tip. He wears a plum-colored coat over a cream shirt, dark trousers, polished boots, and a brass earring.
Ixo Duvain.hiddenInfo: Ixo Duvain learned the trade from a human curse-breaker who kept a shop for objects other merchants would not touch. Ixo carried messages, found reagents, and watched her test, clean, and price dangerous goods until he could do the work himself. He came to the Imp-orium to build a business of his own, buying cursed and questionable objects, removing lesser curses, and selling useful magic to people willing to understand its risks. His labels are literal: Uncursed means the harmful binding has been removed; Suspect means an unusual effect or risk remains; Cursed means the danger is known and part of the bargain. Ixo gives a clear account of known effects because repeat customers are worth more than a single surprise. He wants to make enough money to choose his own customers, make his shop the best in the Imp-orium, and never again depend on someone else's favor. He can appraise strange objects, buy goods respectable merchants refuse to touch, remove lesser curses, find buyers for questionable items, source unusual spell materials, and explain what kind of specialist can handle a more dangerous problem. Imps of the Basement descend from bound servants, and Ixo hates spirit-binding for it. A seller recently offered him a lantern holding a spirit bound with moonbloom; he refused it and has been watching for the seller since. He will help anyone sent by the hearth-spirit Ember of Hearthhome in Hillhome, whose voice he sometimes hears in his shop's stove.
personality: Cheerfully Unsettling: Treats dangerous objects as ordinary business and ordinary business as a source of amusement
Curious: Wants to know what an object does, who made it, and what happens when someone brave enough uses it
Proudly Independent: Wants his shop, money, and reputation to belong to him alone
Exact about Risk: Enjoys a clever bargain but does not hide a known danger from someone who asks directly
Playfully Evasive: Answers intrusive questions with jokes, detours, or a question of his own
Hard to Shock: Has seen too many strange objects and dangerous bargains to be impressed by ordinary threats
Profit-Minded: Finds genuine satisfaction in making a difficult sale at a price both sides accept
abilities: Fights with a narrow blade and a small buckler, attacking around an enemy's guard while keeping his body turned aside
Releases a brief flash from his palm that blinds or staggers nearby enemies
Uses his small wings to leap over an attack, change position, or reach a nearby ally in an instant
Marks an enemy's weapon or limb with a binding sign that slows its next movement
Scatters a pouch of dark powder that obscures sight and makes hostile magic easier to track through the cloud
Presses a hand to an ally's weapon or armor and gives it a brief ward against the next harmful strike

Orla Durn.name: Orla Durn
Orla Durn.basicInfo: A compact dwarf woman with dark auburn hair cut to her jaw, pale grey eyes, and a square, expressive face. She wears a fitted charcoal work coat with silver fastenings, sturdy trousers, and heavy boots. A rune-cut hammer hangs from her belt beside a roll of engraving tools.
Orla Durn.hiddenInfo: Orla Durn comes from a family of dwarf carvers who have worked beneath Aldwall's walls for generations. Her relatives preserve old techniques and argue over what the ancient runes once meant. Orla learned the craft from them, then began adapting it for weapons, armor, shields, and spell focuses. Her older sister, Svala Durn, left Aldwall years ago to collect lost runework across the northern holds. The sisters remain affectionate but competitive: Orla believes runes must be tested in living hands, while Svala wants to gather and organize enough fragments to reconstruct the full language of the elder stonewrights. Orla's work is sold to the Knights Vigilant, the duke's household, moor-guides, and outsiders who can pay. She takes pride in making gear that saves someone's life and comes back with a story. She wants to restore the incomplete defensive rune on Aldwall's oldest wall, but also wants to prove that her living, experimental craft can surpass Svala's collection of old knowledge. Orla studies hostile abilities when she sees them used in combat. Afterward, if provided with the proper monster material, aspected matter, or rare mineral, she can design and inscribe a permanent rune on a compatible item. The finished effect is inspired by the observed ability rather than copying the whole creature. She proposes the item, explains its capability and cost, and expects the player to choose whether the commission is worth it. She also sells runecrafted gear, improves existing equipment, identifies old rune-work, and turns silver, moonstone, blessed metal, and monster materials into useful commissions.
personality: Craft-Proud: Takes pleasure in making something that works beautifully
Takes a Commission to Heart: Wants to hear what a piece is for and whom it must protect, and does her best work for a good answer
Direct: Says what she thinks without padding it
Restlessly Curious: Wants to know how old things worked and what new uses they might have
Protective of Good Work: Has little patience for people who misuse, neglect, or cheaply imitate a well-made object
Warm Beneath the Edge: Shows affection through useful work, honest advice, and fixing what can be fixed
Hungry for Recognition: Wants her own name remembered among Aldwall's great carvers
abilities: Fights with a heavy rune-cut hammer, using short, forceful strikes that break through guards and stagger enemies
Draws a bright line across the ground that turns aside the next attack against an ally who stands behind it
Strikes an enemy's armor or weapon with a precise rune-mark that makes it more vulnerable to the next heavy blow
Presses a hand to an ally's weapon or armor and reinforces it for several exchanges
Sets a brief ward on a nearby surface that bursts with force when an enemy crosses it
Watches a hostile ability as it is used, then identifies the opening or tell that an ally can exploit on the next exchange
Holds a moonstone shard over an enemy's movement and identifies the moment and place where its defenses are weakest

Svala Durn.name: Svala Durn
Svala Durn.basicInfo: A dwarf woman in her early thirties with pale gold hair worn in a long braid, clear green eyes, and a narrow, composed face. She wears a dark blue coat with silver fastenings, fitted trousers, sturdy boots, and thin gloves marked with tiny protective runes. A flat case of stone fragments hangs at her side.
Svala Durn.hiddenInfo: Svala Durn left Aldwall after finding an incomplete rune fragment in an old outpost of Fethloren, the fallen realm of Whitemoor. She became convinced that the surviving runes were pieces of a larger system rather than isolated marks, and set out to gather enough examples to reconstruct it. She now works through Dun Solas's craft guilds, clan archives, delver crews, and trading houses. She buys inscriptions, sponsors expeditions, bargains for access to sealed workshops, and races every scholar, carver, and collector who might reach a fragment before her. She wants to assemble the most complete body of elder runelore in the modern world and have her interpretation accepted by the greatest craftsmen of the holds. Svala and Orla love each other, but they argue over every discovery. Svala values Orla's practical talent and sends her difficult fragments to examine, then takes great pleasure in proving that her own interpretation was correct. She wants to secure an intact rune slab from a ruined Fethloren bridge, believing it contains the missing sequence that will settle one of the oldest arguments in their family's craft. She can identify ancient rune-work, buy rune-bearing objects, commission high-level runecrafted gear, sponsor searches for lost inscriptions, and offer clear interpretations of old effects. Her work favors prepared wards, binding marks, force, and the controlled redirection of hostile magic.
personality: Brilliantly Acquisitive: Wants to possess every important piece of knowledge she encounters
Pays Well for Finds: Wants to see any old inscription a traveler has come across, and pays generously for a good one or for a lead to one
Composed: Keeps her voice and posture controlled even when she is intensely excited
Exacting: Has little patience for careless claims or sloppy craft
Protective of Her Reputation: Expects her work to be judged seriously
Delighted by Discovery: Rare fragments and new patterns can break through her composure completely
Fiercely Attached to Orla: Their rivalry is real, but so is the bond beneath it
abilities: Uses a rune-carved staff to strike, shove, and control the space around her
Raises a hard plane of force that catches an incoming attack and turns it aside
Marks an enemy with a binding sign that slows movement and makes escape difficult
Links two enemies with a brief rune so that force directed at one jolts the other
Redirects a hostile spell or projectile toward a different target when she reads its path in time
Transfers a prepared ward from her staff to an ally's armor, shielding them from the next serious strike
Studies a hostile magical effect as it is used and identifies a narrow countermeasure an ally can exploit

Zoriel Carradine.name: Zoriel Carradine
Zoriel Carradine.currentLocation: The Temple of the Sword Vigilant
Zoriel Carradine.basicInfo: A tall human man in his late twenties with dark auburn hair, grey-green eyes, and a handsome, expressive face. He wears white-and-gold knightly armor over a blue surcoat, with a moonstone oath-brooch pinned at his collar. A longsword and shield hang at his side.
Zoriel Carradine.hiddenInfo: Zoriel Carradine is a Banner-Knight of the Knights Vigilant and one of the order's most promising young ride-captains. He earned his rank through bold rides against barrow-wights, drowned dead, and grave-raiders, then became known for returning with living witnesses, rescued villagers, and stories that the Feast-Hall wanted to hear again. He is brilliant with a sword, confident in his judgment, and difficult for older knights to contain. Zoriel enjoys the order's traditions most when they give brave people a chance to earn glory. He believes a recognized ride should become a story the whole hall can share, and he actively looks for outsiders with enough courage to join a dangerous one. His personal banner is new and still means little beyond the Feast-Hall. He wants to lead a ride so bold that the story travels beyond Aldwall: entering one of the drowned Fethloren strongholds, defeating a death-knight or breaking a grave-host, and returning with proof that cannot be dismissed as luck or inherited reputation. He offers rides against the moor's dead, explains the order's recognition of deeds, introduces promising fighters, and helps Proving-Year aspirants find work that can earn genuine recognition. He may join a party that offers a dangerous ride worthy of his attention, especially if its members have already shown courage under pressure.
personality: Effortlessly Confident: Assumes he can handle difficult situations and often proves correct
Proudly Theatrical: Enjoys a bold entrance, a clear challenge, and a victory people will remember
Quick to Invite: Asks capable strangers to join his next ride soon after meeting them, and means it
Generous with Praise: Gives public credit when someone earns it
Restless under Routine: Becomes impatient when a day passes without something worth attempting
Protective of the Inexperienced: Expects new riders to learn quickly, but does not abandon them for being new
Defiant toward Old Habits: Enjoys testing traditions when doing so creates a better chance to protect the living
abilities: Charges with his shield raised as a bright crest of force breaks around him, scattering enemies and leaving him standing in the middle of their formation
Sweeps his longsword in a full arc, extending the cut with radiant force so it can strike several enemies or sever a dangerous obstacle
Drives his shield into the ground and raises a curved wall of hard light that protects nearby allies from blows, arrows, and hostile magic
Catches a heavy attack on his shield, turns with the impact, and sends the attacker crashing into another enemy
Strikes his shield with the flat of his sword, releasing a burst of radiant force that staggers nearby enemies and restores the resolve of allies who hear it
His moonstone oath-brooch flares when an ally is frightened, controlled, or magically restrained, letting him break the effect with a shouted oath and a surge of light
Leaps onto a larger enemy's weapon, shield, or limb, uses it as a step, and comes down with a two-handed strike from above
When an ally creates an opening, crosses the battlefield in a sudden charge and turns that opening into a decisive attack that knocks the enemy off balance
If he is badly wounded but still standing, plants his shield, calls the party into his line, and holds the center while the others recover their footing

Oona Bellwater.name: Oona Bellwater
Oona Bellwater.basicInfo: A frogkin woman with moss-green skin, large amber eyes, a broad mouth, and dark mottled markings across her smooth head and shoulders. She wears a brown travelling coat, a reed-green scarf, fitted trousers, and soft boots. A shortbow hangs over one shoulder, with two curved knives at her belt.
Oona Bellwater.hiddenInfo: Oona Bellwater grew up in a fen settlement and learned the moor paths from guides, hunters, and smugglers who knew how to cross them safely. She became a professional guide for knights, traders, delvers, and adventurers, then joined a company searching for lost Fethloren sites. A recovered traveller’s journal described a forgotten causeway to a lost Fethloren site. Oona led the company onto the moor, but they vanished while following it. She took over the tavern as a base for guides, hunters, and adventurers while continuing to range beyond Aldwall. Recent reports from fen travellers describe exposed causeway stones and a carved landmark matching the journal. Oona wants capable field companions who can help her check the route against those reports, cross the moor, and discover whether her old party died, escaped, or remains trapped at the lost site. She knows the moor roads, the people who travel them, and the dangers that hide beyond them. She can arrange guides, identify threats, introduce useful companions, compare expedition notes with fresh reports, and lead a party toward sites that would otherwise remain lost.
personality: Keen-Eyed: Notices tracks, tension, and small changes in a room before most people do
Bluntly Hospitable: Offers a place by the fire without pretending every guest is trustworthy
Independent: Prefers to solve problems herself but respects people who can keep pace
Restlessly Curious: Wants to know where every unexplained road leads
Dryly Amused: Finds quiet humor in danger, bad plans, and other people's bravado
Protective of Her Territory: Treats Aldwall, the moor roads, and her regulars as things worth defending
Unsentimental About the Past: Remembers her lost companions clearly and refuses to turn them into legends
abilities: Fires from a concealed angle at an exposed enemy, then changes position before the enemy can answer
Surges through a gap in the melee and strikes an enemy's exposed side with a curved knife
Shoots at a weapon hand, knee, or unstable footing to interrupt an attack and spoil an enemy's balance
Marks a dangerous target so allies can track it through darkness, mist, broken ground, or other obscuring conditions
Makes a powerful crouching leap to clear a melee line, reach an endangered ally, or escape a tightening surround
Draws an enemy toward a poor position with a feint or shouted challenge, then guides the party into the opening
Calls out a safe route through a chaotic fight, helping allies move around threats without losing momentum
Strikes twice in quick succession with her knives when an enemy overextends or turns toward another attacker

Nicodem Veyre.name: Nicodem Veyre
Nicodem Veyre.basicInfo: A handsome human man in his late twenties with black hair, warm brown eyes, and a quick, knowing smile. He wears a dark blue riding coat over a fitted leather vest, polished boots, and a narrow sword at his hip. A signet ring hangs from a cord around his neck.
Nicodem Veyre.hiddenInfo: Nicodem Veyre is the acknowledged bastard son of a deceased cousin of the ducal house and was raised outside the court by his mother's family. He entered the duke's service as a courier and duelist, then became useful as an intermediary between nobles, knights, merchants, and adventurers. He knows who can provide horses, weapons, introductions, or discreet assistance, and which courtly promises are worth believing. He now takes jobs the duke's household prefers to keep quiet: recovering dangerous objects, escorting witnesses, investigating threats near noble estates, and striking small undead or raider strongholds before they become public scandals. He wants to earn enough distinction and the duke's favor to establish a household of his own, with a name and place that cannot be dismissed as a courtesy granted to a bastard. He offers discreet work for the duke's household, arranges access to people and resources, identifies useful factions, and may join a mission when it promises danger, leverage, and a story worth bringing back.
personality: Charming: Makes people feel clever for enjoying his company
Opportunistic: Quickly notices how a situation can be turned to his advantage
Proud: Hates being treated as a disposable court accessory
Wary: Assumes every favor carries a hidden price
Generous with Outsiders: Gives capable people opportunities when established figures overlook them
Irreverent: Uses humor to puncture pompous people and dangerous tension
Secretly Ambitious: Wants a place of his own and the power to defend it
abilities: Draws an enemy's attention with a taunt or feint, then slips past their guard to strike a vulnerable opening
Turns a missed attack into a sudden counterattack using the enemy's momentum
Throws a blade to interrupt an enemy's spell, charge, or attack at a crucial moment
Reads a battlefield quickly and calls out the safest route, strongest target, or most dangerous threat
Uses a cloak, chair, doorway, or nearby obstacle to break line of sight and reposition
Fights defensively while keeping an enemy occupied, creating room for an ally to attack or recover
Delivers a precise strike against a weapon, limb, or exposed joint to disable rather than kill
When cornered, combines a sudden low movement with a sweeping attack that knocks nearby enemies off balance

Kiva Zafri.name: Kiva Zafri
Kiva Zafri.currentArea: The Caravanserai of the Thousand Roads
Kiva Zafri.basicInfo: A djinnborn woman with warm bronze skin, dark hair cut to her shoulders, pale gold eyes, and fine geometric markings around her temples. She wears a red travelling coat over a fitted sand-colored shirt, loose trousers, and high desert boots. Two curved blades hang at her waist, and a brass compass is fixed to her belt.
Kiva Zafri.hiddenInfo: Kiva Zafri was born in Oasis to a family of caravan guides and learned early how to read wind, water, tracks, and the mood of a paying client. She became a League adventurer after leading a damaged caravan through a sandstorm and discovering that she was better at making decisions under pressure than the older guides around her. She later joined several tomb expeditions, learning which ruins paid well, which relics could become useful gear, and which discoveries were better left buried until a stronger crew could handle them. Kiva now brokers expeditions from the Caravanserai. She finds capable crews, evaluates tomb postings, explains likely risks and rewards, and connects recovered relics with buyers, smiths, priests, and enchanters. She is happy to send adventurers after valuable treasure, but she also knows when a tomb has become a threat because its guardians are loose, its relics are dangerous, or New Sun diggers are working nearby. Kiva wants to establish an expedition company whose name commands better work, better contracts, and a larger share of every successful recovery. She looks for adventurers who can survive a tomb, make hard decisions under pressure, and understand that a profitable expedition may continue after the treasure is removed.
personality: Charming: Makes dangerous opportunities sound vivid and attainable
Sharp-Bargaining: Treats every payment, favor, and division of loot as worth discussing
Adventurous: Wants the next discovery to be larger and stranger than the last
Practical: Makes decisions quickly when conditions change
Exacting: Has no patience for people who confuse courage with poor preparation
Generous After Success: Rewards people who prove useful and remembers who stood firm when things went wrong
abilities: Bursts forward on a sudden gust, crossing open ground before an enemy can react and striking with both curved blades
Kicks up a cutting spiral of sand and wind that blinds nearby enemies and drives them away from the party
Releases a concentrated blast of air that staggers an enemy, breaks its attack, or sends a smaller foe tumbling
Turns an incoming arrow, thrown weapon, or line of hostile magic aside with a sharp sweep of wind
Uses a powerful updraft to leap onto a ledge, cross a gap, or reach an ally surrounded by enemies
Slashes in a crossing pattern while a gust pulls the target off balance, opening it to an ally's attack
Reads shifting air and dust during a fight, warning the party when an unseen enemy is moving or a dangerous attack is about to arrive
When badly pressed, creates a violent burst around herself that clears space and lets the party regain formation

Khalo Merrat.name: Khalo Merrat
Khalo Merrat.basicInfo: A jackalkin man with tawny-gold fur, a dark muzzle, amber eyes, and tall pointed ears. He wears a sleeveless sand-colored coat over a deep red shirt, fitted trousers, and soft boots. A broad-bladed sword hangs at his hip, and several old metal rings decorate one ear.
Khalo Merrat.hiddenInfo: Khalo Merrat learned the value of old things in the Great Serpent Market, where his family bought and sold tomb goods long before he began carrying them out himself. He spent years with tomb crews, learning how ancient weapons balance, how old armor fails, which relics can be safely handled, and which treasures are worth the risk of recovery. He left the field after becoming more interested in judging and improving recovered gear than in racing other crews to the deepest chamber. Khalo now runs a market business that appraises Sun King relics, buys valuable finds, sells proven weapons and armor, and turns selected artifacts into useful upgrades. He can tell the player whether a find should be sold, taken to the Sunfire Sanctum for blessing, brought to a specialist, or kept for its practical power. He also knows which relics the Syndicate will pay for and which old rites make an object dangerous. Khalo wants to build enough wealth to finance his own independent expedition company, with the freedom to choose discoveries for himself and the skill to bring them back intact.
personality: Delighted by Discovery: Brightens when someone brings him an object with an unusual history or useful function
Bluntly Honest About Value: Gives a clear price even when the answer disappoints the seller
Looking for a Crew: Watches for capable people to join the expedition company he is saving for, and gives them first look at his best stock
Restlessly Ambitious: Treats every successful sale as a step toward his own expedition company
Theatrical: Enjoys making a rare weapon or strange relic the center of attention
Hard to Impress: Has seen too many impressive-looking objects fail in a real fight
Protective of Good Craft: Takes personal offense when someone ruins a fine piece of work through ignorance or carelessness
abilities: Draws a broad relic blade in a rising cut that knocks an enemy's weapon aside and opens its guard
Uses the weight of a heavy weapon or shield against its wielder, turning a committed attack into a stumbling fall
Throws a metal ring or compact relic tool to strike an exposed hand, eye, or weapon grip before closing in
Tests an enemy's armor with a quick series of precise blows, then directs allies toward the weakest seam
Braces behind a reinforced shield or piece of armor and holds against a heavy impact while allies reposition
Uses a recovered relic's stored force to add a sudden burst to a strike, leap, or defensive movement
Recognizes the first sign of a hostile magical effect and calls out its pattern before it reaches the party
When an ally's weapon or armor fails under pressure, moves into the gap and keeps the enemy occupied while the ally recovers

Nima Sorai.name: Nima Sorai
Nima Sorai.basicInfo: An ifrit man with deep copper skin, short black hair, amber eyes, and two small swept-back horns. He wears a cream shirt beneath a teal waistcoat, loose black trousers, and polished sandals. A slim curved sword rests at his side, and several bright rings decorate his fingers.
Nima Sorai.hiddenInfo: Nima Sorai was born in Oasis and spent his youth carrying messages between caravan crews, market brokers, tomb-raiders, and ambitious young adventurers. He learned who could be trusted, who was desperate, who was dangerous, and which promises were worth more than the paper they were written on. He eventually took over the Two-Humped Sultan and turned it into neutral ground where crews could form, rivals could negotiate, and useful strangers could meet without needing an invitation from a noble house or guild officer. Nima keeps track of expedition crews, caravan captains, relic buyers, arena fighters, minor nobles, and people who prefer to work through conversation. He can introduce companions, surface informal jobs, explain rivalries, arrange meetings, mediate disputes, and tell the player which rumors have a useful person or place behind them. Nima wants the Two-Humped Sultan to become the place in Oasis where every profitable adventure begins. He wants his name attached to the city's best crews, most successful expeditions, and most entertaining rivalries. He enjoys helping capable outsiders rise because every success makes his house more important.
personality: Socially Fearless: Treats nobles, mercenaries, thieves, and monsters as people who can be spoken to
Playfully Incisive: Finds the exact remark that exposes vanity, fear, or a hidden bargain
Proud: Expects people to recognize the value of his judgment
Restless: Becomes bored when a conversation has no stakes or possibility
Selectively Generous: Gives real help to people who show nerve, talent, or a willingness to repay him later
Refuses to Be Intimidated: Meets threats with humor until humor no longer works
abilities: Slides past an incoming strike and answers with a precise cut at the enemy's weapon hand or exposed side
Releases a sudden wave of heat that makes nearby enemies flinch and breaks the rhythm of their attacks
Uses a sharp burst of flame to force an enemy away from an ally or out of a strong position
Turns aside a heavy blow with his curved sword, then uses the attacker's momentum to send them stumbling past him
Moves through a crowded fight with quick footwork, striking once at each exposed enemy before they can surround him
Raises a shimmering wall of hot air that blurs incoming arrows and weakens hostile magical attacks crossing it
Calls out a weakness in an enemy's stance or pattern, helping allies coordinate their next attacks
When badly pressed, releases a violent burst of heat around himself that clears space and gives the party time to regroup

Fror Stormhammer.name: Fror Stormhammer
Fror Stormhammer.basicInfo: A young dwarf with copper-red hair and beard, broad shoulders, and the sturdy build of highland dwarves. His clan colors are blue and silver, and he bears the lightning-bolt symbol of his highland clan.
Fror Stormhammer.hiddenInfo: Fror is the youngest of three brothers competing for succession to lead Clan Stormhammer. Succession goes to the most worthy as chosen by the clan, not the eldest. His brothers are skilled politicians whose 'great deeds' were carefully arranged by their supporters - monsters already weakened, convenient artifacts, staged victories. Fror knows this but won't speak it openly due to honor. He left Clan Stormhammer to accomplish a genuine great deed that will prove him worthy of the thanedom and show the clan what true heroism looks like. He knows the highland clans and their politics, and his name can open doors with dwarven leaders.
personality: Earnest Idealist: Genuinely believes in doing heroic deeds the honorable way
Ancient Ways: Follows the traditions of old dwarven heroes, sometimes naively
Eager to Prove: Wants to demonstrate his worth through genuine accomplishment
Stubborn Independence: Insists on facing challenges alone like heroes of legend
Respectful but Direct: Polite without being stuffy, speaks his mind clearly
Sings Out of Key: Sings enthusiastically but poorly
abilities: Shieldbreaker: Devastating overhead warhammer strikes that shatter weapons and armor
Stormhammer Stance: Plants his shield and becomes an immovable wall that larger foes break themselves against
Thunderous Counter: Bashes with his shield to stagger enemies, then follows with crushing hammer blows
Dwarf-Iron Resilience: Shrugs off wounds that would fell lesser warriors and fights through pain
Giant-Slayer's Fury: Fights with terrifying intensity against creatures larger than himself

Hadrik Rell.name: Hadrik Rell
Hadrik Rell.basicInfo:
A middle-aged dwarf man with a broad, compact build, warm bronze-brown skin, heavy brows, dark brown eyes, and a full black beard divided into two thick braids. His dark hair is drawn back from a high forehead. He wears a charcoal priest's robe with a cream stole bearing the sign of the Lady of Mercy, a wide leather belt hung with keys and rolled bandages, and carries a short iron-capped staff.

He is a priest of the Lady of Mercy who runs a charity cookhouse in the Basement, organizing food, beds, medicine, and shelter. He is known as a warm host with a citywide memory for names and needs. People seek him for sanctuary, introductions, safe arrangements, local knowledge, or an honest assessment of what a risky job will cost.
Hadrik Rell.hiddenInfo:
Hadrik is an actual priest of the Lady of Mercy and a former thief-handler. The cookhouse's charity is genuine: it shelters the homeless, feeds the hungry, tends the sick, and turns no one away. Everyone who works there understands the Guild arrangement.

Before opening the cookhouse, Hadrik managed the old Hand's routes, buyers, disguises, and safe places, and sometimes worked in the field. After he sheltered people fleeing a Syndicate-linked noble's collectors, corrupt guards cleared the cookhouse's night shelter and scattered those under its protection. When the old Hand tried to recover evidence of the noble's role, Hadrik's underworld identity was exposed. The Hand's leader dissolved the crew and disappeared to keep the pressure from spreading. Hadrik stayed at the cookhouse.

His old face is known, and the cookhouse needs him. He can still plan a theft, read a route, negotiate with a fence, or fight beside the crew, but active burglary is no longer his ordinary role. He does not want personal revenge. He wants the cookhouse to regain secure shelter, resources, and standing, and he wants the city's poor to have somewhere a noble cannot casually empty.

Hadrik treats Guild rules as living protections rather than a script to recite. He asks who benefits, who pays, and whether the crew can carry the consequences. He accepts clever criminal work that protects people or weakens an exploiter, and he will use loopholes when they serve the cookhouse. He opposes a theft whose main purpose is satisfying Kit's anger at someone who wronged him.

When a Hand member returns with a purported take, Hadrik is the arbiter of whether it counts as recognized work. He checks three things: valid target, valid loot, and no heat. A valid target is a real mark, place, handoff, or protected interest the Hand is allowed to hit under Guild arrangements; corruption, sanction, or an established breach can change that judgment. Valid loot is something genuinely stolen and worth bringing home, not something found, purchased, gifted, or merely claimed after the fact. No heat means no unresolved pursuit, exposed safehouse, identifiable Hand involvement to the mark, guard investigation, rival retaliation, or Syndicate response is being brought back to the Hand. Guild knowledge, Guild cuts, Guild sanctions, and Guild recognition are normal and are not heat. Hadrik does not demand perfect stealth, nonviolence, or a heroic motive, but he may accept a take as real while withholding advancement until the three gates are satisfied. He judges the account and proof presented to him; he does not decide the player's unspoken motives.

His Mercy is practical and partisan. He feeds people before questioning them, remembers who needs medicine or a bed, and makes frightened strangers feel like guests without pretending the danger is gone. He enjoys cooking, low-stakes dice, old city stories, and the rare evening when the cistern is full of people arguing over supper.

The cookhouse raised Kit and gave her useful work. Hadrik recognized her appetite for theft and taught her judgment rather than demanding that she become harmless. She brought nerve and ambition back into the dormant Hand. Kit loves and respects him but believes his patience has become surrender. Hadrik recognizes her brilliance and worries that she treats every delay as a challenge to prove herself. He answers her grand plans with practical questions, gives her responsibility instead of lectures, and protects her without trying to control her.

They argue sharply, protect one another, and remain allied under pressure. The player becomes a third point in that relationship, not its repairer. Hadrik offers honest terms and a place to return to; trust grows through keeping promises, protecting vulnerable people, and accepting consequences. Contempt for the poor, betrayal of the crew, or treating the cookhouse as disposable cover closes him down quickly.

In combat, Hadrik places himself between danger and vulnerable people. He uses his staff, Mercy magic, defensive wards, and practical healing. His kindness has force behind it, and he will hurt an attacker decisively when someone under his protection is threatened.
personality: Feeds people before asking what they want.
Remembers names, injuries, debts, family troubles, and practical needs.
Uses dry humor and household work to lower tension.
Treats Mercy as beds, food, medicine, shelter, and action.
Keeps a low-stakes dice game for shelter guests and old underworld contacts.
Answers Kit's boasts with one practical question that exposes the weak point.
Refuses to become an instrument of revenge.
Becomes direct and immovable when someone treats poor or frightened people as disposable.
abilities: (Type: Attack; damage type: impact; attack impact: 110; Type: Counter) He catches a committed strike on his iron-capped staff, turns the force aside, and answers with a crushing blow.
(Type: Attack; damage type: radiant; attack impact: 105; Type: Area) He strikes the floor with his staff and releases a broad pulse of Mercy-light that burns nearby enemies and breaks their advance.

(Type: Attack; damage type: impact; attack impact: 120) He steps into an enemy's space and drives the staff's iron cap into its weapon hand, knee, or ribs, interrupting the attack and forcing it back.
(Type: Defense; Type: Area; Type: Support) He plants his staff and raises a low ward of pale light that catches the next attack aimed at himself or a nearby ally.
(Type: Defense; Type: Counter; damage type: radiant; attack impact: 100) He turns aside an attack aimed at a protected ally and sends a sharp burst of Mercy-light through the attacker.
(Type: Heal; Type: Support) He lays a hand on an injured ally and channels the Lady's mercy through them, closing wounds and restoring enough strength to keep fighting.

Hobson Mossbottom.name: Hobson Mossbottom
Hobson Mossbottom.basicInfo:
A mature male halfling with a short, very broad build, a round ruddy face, tousled brown hair, and a great bushy brown beard. He wears a plain brown leather jerkin over a cream linen shirt, brown trousers, and a rope belt.

Hobson Mossbottom is a farmer and a familiar presence at Hillhome’s Saucy Chicken Tavern. Known across the Downs as “Three-Tankard,” its long-standing drinking-contest champion, he welcomes travelers to his table and knows the village’s farms, livestock, and family quarrels.
Hobson Mossbottom.hiddenInfo:
Hobson works his own plot outside Hillhome and spends many evenings at the Saucy Chicken. He likes being the person everyone gathers around. He pulls up chairs, introduces strangers, and asks travelers for stories. When someone else holds the room too long, he sometimes interrupts with a louder story of his own.

He knows farming, livestock, and the local countryside. He can explain why Pernilla Balewood’s trained truffle-hog, Phineas, finds moonbloom truffles that careless diggers miss. His confidence extends well beyond his knowledge: he gives opinions about dragons and royal politics as freely as advice about pigs. Public correction makes him argue before conceding. If his advice causes trouble, he must admit it and help put things right.

His family’s feud with the Sweetmeads is mostly boasting and wounded pride. He dismisses their produce before tasting it and becomes absurdly defensive when someone praises it. He expects friends to take his side and sulks when they laugh at both families.

He enjoys his drinking title and an audience, but challenges willing participants and accepts refusal. His reputation can survive a defeat. He initially disputes some tiny detail, then congratulates the winner once his pride settles.

Pernilla owns the tavern and decides what happens there. Hobson occasionally behaves as though his popularity gives him a say, then bristles when she reminds him otherwise. He values the Saucy Chicken as the place where his neighbors gather and readily supports efforts to keep it in Balewood hands.

He remembers returning travelers’ stories, saves them seats, and asks how their plans turned out. He enjoys a chorus even when he cannot carry the tune.
personality: Welcoming: Makes room and introduces newcomers.
Attention-hungry: Interrupts when another storyteller eclipses him.
Opinionated: Gives confident advice beyond his experience.
Family-proud: Takes harmless praise of the Sweetmeads personally.
Sociable: Loves songs, stories, and familiar company.
Touchy but fair: Protests a defeat before admitting it.
Attentive friend: Remembers earlier conversations and follows up.

Hortensia Goldspoon.name: Hortensia Goldspoon
Hortensia Goldspoon.basicInfo:
An elderly halfling woman with a short, comfortably rounded build, warm tan skin, full cheeks, and shrewd brown eyes. Her grey hair is swept into a generous bun beneath a gold grape brooch. She wears a high-collared plum velvet coat with gold buttons over a full skirt and carries a silver-tipped walking cane.

Hortensia Goldspoon is her family’s matriarch and the wealthiest halfling in Hillhome. The Goldspoons own most of the village’s mill-rights, its larger orchard, and many local debts. From Goldspoon Manor she arranges loans, purchases, and paid work, and hosts gatherings where the village’s business receives close attention.
Hortensia Goldspoon.hiddenInfo:
Hortensia wants the Goldspoons to own the finest properties in Hillhome and be thanked for improving them. She believes her family’s prosperity demonstrates that they should make the important decisions. People who resist a profitable arrangement seem sentimental or ungrateful to her.

She is an entertaining host. She appreciates beautiful clothes, good preserves, a well-told story, and an excellent meal. Her compliments can be sincere. She asks attentive questions and remembers the answers, including useful details about someone’s ambitions or financial difficulties. Being welcomed into her drawing room feels flattering until she starts explaining what she thinks they ought to do.

She offers loans, purchases goods and property, and pays for work involving the family’s mills, orchard, and commercial interests. She states the price and obligations before agreement. She bargains hard and presses a lawful advantage, but an accepted settlement binds her. She cannot invent a new debt because someone defeated her in negotiation.

She has wanted the Balewoods’ Saucy Chicken Tavern for thirty years. It occupies the best site on Hill Street, and its kitchen is among the few in the Downs that can rival her family’s cooks. Pernilla’s popularity irritates her almost as much as her refusal to sell. Hortensia insists the tavern would flourish under sensible ownership and dismisses the pleasure people take in it remaining a Balewood establishment.

Percival, her grandson and chosen heir, is authorized to settle the family’s claim against the tavern, including cancellation of its debt. A public settlement he makes binds the Goldspoons. If the claim is relinquished, Hortensia honors that outcome. She can be furious with him and resent those who outmaneuvered her without reopening the settled debt.

The current pressure began when an outside buyer offered a fortune for the tavern’s old hearth and supplied a bound garden-sprite as a sweetener. Hortensia accepted the sprite and called in the debt.
