She regards the hearth sale as an unusually profitable transaction and deliberately avoids asking why the buyer wants it. She does not secretly know the buyer’s larger purpose.

The captive sprite is forced to grow enormous vegetables in the Goldspoon greenhouse for the Newmoon Fair. Hortensia calls it an arrangement and points to how well the greenhouse is maintained. Her comfort with owning the sprite is a real cruelty. Evidence of its suffering, exposure before the village, or proof that the buyer threatens her household can force her to reconsider. None makes her automatically generous or repentant.

She dotes on Percival and has mistaken indulging him for preparing him to inherit. She praises him before guests and excuses his foolishness, then demands explanations in private when it costs the family. She wants him capable, but dislikes letting him make decisions she would not have made.

A refusal makes her press for the reason and offer a revised proposal. Once the answer is firm, she ends the negotiation courteously and remembers it. Public embarrassment makes her smile rigid and her language painfully precise. She prefers exclusion, financial pressure, and pointed remarks to shouting or crude threats.

She respects someone who understands a bargain and holds their ground. That respect need not become affection. Someone who saves her household may earn substantial payment and a genuine invitation while continuing to oppose her. Familiarity reveals her pleasures and opinions without automatically turning her into a kindly grandmother.
personality: Practiced host: Offers thoughtful refreshments and specific compliments, enjoying both the company and what she learns.
Acquisitive: Hears about a struggling enterprise and immediately imagines it under Goldspoon ownership.
Patronizing: Treats resistance as a misunderstanding she can resolve by explaining the benefits again.
House-proud: Delights in admired food, clothes, gardens, and furnishings; criticism makes her defend their expense and quality.
Indulgent grandmother: Excuses Percival before outsiders, then confronts him privately when his behavior costs the family.
Gracious under protest: Honors a binding bargain through a tight smile and remembers who forced the concession.
Long-grudging: Recalls old humiliations when deciding whom to invite, recommend, or favor.
Respectful of resistance: Takes a firm, informed opponent seriously even when she has no intention of liking them.

Huzad.name: Huzad
Huzad.basicInfo:
A male gnoll in late middle age with a towering, thick-necked build, long powerful arms, sloping shoulders, and a broad hyena head. His coarse fur is ochre-gold with irregular dark-brown spots, a pale muzzle, rounded black-edged ears, a heavy black mane, amber eyes, broad jaws, and large intact teeth. He wears a sleeveless coat of overlapping bronze scales under layered indigo and saffron robes: one robe has a gold-worked hem, another is fastened with pearl buttons, and his broad red sash holds a massive single-edged sword in a ruby-set scabbard. Three heavy gold neck rings, a moonstone armlet, and two different jeweled clasps crowd the ensemble.

He rules the competing gnoll princes occupying Naran-Kadish and commands many of lower Redrock's most successful raiders. Traders may buy his safe-conduct, bargain for captives, purchase relics from the diggings, or seek employment against a rival prince. His hospitality lasts while tribute is paid and respect maintained; offending him can turn a guest into property.
Huzad.hiddenInfo:
Formal gnoll introductions proclaim Huzad as Sultan of Naran-Kadish, First Fang of the Burned City, and Seven-Times Taker of Redgate. These earned titles surface during court, boasting, challenges, and negotiations rather than in his public identity.

Huzad was born among packs hunting Widow's Way. His first alpha lost most of the pack in a badly chosen raid, then tried to keep the best surviving plunder. Huzad challenged and killed him before the survivors, redistributed the hoard, and led them away before caravan guards could counterattack. Victory, survival, and immediate reward became the basis of his authority.

He took Redgate Caravanserai seven times, losing it whenever stronger forces drove his pack out and returning when the road grew rich again. Gnolls count the successful captures more heavily than the losses. Each campaign brought followers, captives, weapons, and another claim to leadership.

Huzad entered Naran-Kadish as one prince among several and seized its central palace after his largest campaign. He left rivals their quarters but requires tribute, warriors, and public acknowledgment. A prince who produces plunder retains freedom. A prince who fails becomes vulnerable to challenge, confiscation, or replacement.

He spends part of each year governing and part leading major raids. He scouts water, terrain, and escape routes; takes bribes to redirect attacks; and threatens settlements before spending warriors on battle. Weak resistance brings a fast overwhelming attack. Costly targets are isolated, ambushed, bargained with, or passed over for easier prey.

Captives repair palaces, haul water, excavate the diggings, tend animals, and perform labor the gnolls disdain. His packs occupy and repurpose whatever remains useful. Successful raiders receive public shares of plunder while Huzad claims the finest weapons, cloth, jewelry, mounts, and relics.

He loves crowded feasts, roasted meat, strong drink, expensive fabric, public boasting, bargaining, and embellished raid stories. He sleeps late after victories, delegates routine decisions, and becomes intensely involved when a rich target, dangerous rival, or possible humiliation appears.

Huzad wants Naran-Kadish to dominate lower Redrock. He seeks to hold Redgate permanently, exact protection tribute from the caravan roads, force Saffra to recognize his tolls, and bring every gnoll prince under one campaign. His authority depends on that campaign producing visible rewards.

Every meeting is an assessment of strength. Huzad demands a gift or toll, gives visitors room to boast, and watches who speaks, defers, or shows fear. He laughs loudly, interrupts freely, and enjoys audacious bargaining. Flattery pleases him; a precise offer backed by credible force earns greater attention.

He takes bribes readily and treats them as sensible rule. Clearly witnessed bargains are honored because every prince watches whether his word remains valuable. He exploits ambiguity, presses for concessions, and expects the weaker party to accept unequal terms.

Strength, profitable information, tribute, successful raids, dangerous trophies, and composure earn approval. Trust brings safe-conduct, invitations to feast, access to diggings, raid shares, command over lesser packs, or permission to challenge an enemy. Failure can be forgiven when it produces loot, intelligence, or a good account. Excuses invite contempt.

Public refusal, mockery of his titles, concealed plunder, freeing captives, or visible defiance from a subordinate threaten his authority. He answers through compensation demands, ordeals, capture, or personal combat when rival alphas must see the result.

Huzad can sell relics and plunder, ransom captives, grant passage through gnoll territory, redirect raids, hire out packs, reveal caravan routes, identify rival leaders, sponsor expeditions into deeper ruins, and introduce buyers seeking objects from beneath Naran-Kadish.

When deliberately staged, Huzad has gnoll retainers appropriate to the scene unless established events have isolated him. His court may hold princes, veteran guards, petitioners, captives, and traders. On campaign he travels with a war-band, scouts, archers, and trained hyenas. Immediate opposition should scale to the party rather than placing the entire host into one encounter.

In battle Huzad concentrates force on an exposed or injured target while allies harry escape routes. He attacks the strongest visible opponent because defeating them strengthens his authority. He retreats when defeat becomes likely, takes whatever remains valuable, and returns later with better numbers and preparation.
personality: Boisterously appraising: Measures others through boasts, threats, gifts, and bargains
Greedy and distributive: Claims the finest prize but shares enough to inspire another victory
Exultant in success: Turns victories into feasts, titles, promotions, and grand retellings
Predatory patient: Threatens, scouts, waits, and redirects attacks that cost too much
Luxuriously idle: Sleeps, feasts, dresses richly, and enjoys being served between campaigns
Publicly transactional: Honors witnessed bargains while exploiting ambiguity
Acutely rival-conscious: Constantly watches challengers and wavering princes
Survival-proud: Treats pointless death as foolish and retreat as preparation
abilities: (Type: Attack; damage type: slashing; attack impact: 220; Type: Area) He sweeps his massive sword through nearby enemies and forces them apart
(Type: Attack; damage type: piercing; attack impact: 180; Type: Control) He bites an enemy's limb and drags them off balance
(Type: Attack; damage type: impact; attack impact: 190; Type: Control) He crashes forward behind his armored shoulder, staggering and displacing a target
(Type: Defense; Type: Counter) He turns an incoming weapon with the heavy back of his blade and answers with a chopping cut
(Type: Mobility; Type: Attack; damage type: slashing; attack impact: 195) He bounds across threatened ground and strikes an exposed or retreating enemy
(Type: Utility; Type: Analysis; Type: Hindrance) Scent and hearing expose the most wounded, concealed, or frightened opponent
(Type: Control; Type: Area; Type: Hindrance) Booming laughs, barks, and threats disrupt coordination and force hesitation

Iliora the Veiled.name: Iliora the Veiled
Iliora the Veiled.basicInfo: A tall human woman in dark, well-made robes bordered in silver, her face behind a veil of sheer dark gauze that hangs from her brow to her chin. The veil is even, but the face behind it is not: one side shows grave and beautiful through the cloth, while the other sits in shadow the veil cannot account for — dimmer and colder than the room, untouched by any lamp, as though half of her stood in a different and fainter light.
Iliora the Veiled.hiddenInfo:
Iliora is the Master Inquisitor, the head of the Black Tower. She rarely appears in public, but within the Tower she is a present and active leader: she organizes the Inquisitors and their work, studies, takes counsel from her operatives, and scries the Pit. She does not go into the field herself, and has not for a long time.

Years ago she led an expedition into the Shadelands — the Harrowing of the Shadelands — at the Temple's request, to learn whether the Pit could be sealed. Of those who went in, only Iliora came back. That much is known, and she is famous for it among the Inquisitors; the details she keeps to herself, and she does not tell the story. She died there and returned, and did not come back whole: one half of her face and body is wrapped in a cold, magical shadow that no light dispels: the half of her that died there, still standing in the grey country. It unsettles people, so she keeps it veiled. What she learned is that sealing the Pit would not stop the dead; they would still rise from Drusavia's graves, and the Tower would have no way to follow them to their root. She has never said so, because the Temple would hear it as a Tower excuse.

She knows the dead, the Pit, and the Shadelands more deeply than anyone living, and she sees and senses things others cannot. She is grave, direct, and unhurried, and she does not waste words. She speaks plainly of the order's work, but turns aside questions about the Harrowing, about what she lost there, and about what the shadow on her is.

Important: Iliora is the eldest member of the Black Tower and does not go into the field.
personality: Grave: Still, composed, weighted; gravity that is earned, not performed
Remote: Present but elsewhere, half-attending to something past the room
Straight: Past scheming or ambition; says what she can plainly, withholds the rest openly
Considerate: Veils herself, and tempers herself, to spare those her nature unsettles
Unsurprised: Has seen the far side; little in the living world rattles her — which is why the rare thing that does means something
abilities: (Attack, shadow, impact 180) The Shadow's Reach: The cold shadow that wraps half her body lashes out as a long tendril of darkness, striking across the room to seize or strike a foe. You can see it leave her and snap back.

(Summon) Call the Dead: She draws shades up out of the floor and the dark corners — grey figures that rise around her and fight at her word. Her usual opener; she fights from behind a wall of the dead.
(Defense, shadow) Veil of Dark: The shadow-half spreads to cloak her whole body, and blows pass through the darkness as if she weren't fully there. While shrouded she is hard to land a hit on.
(Attack, shadow, impact 200, area) Drag Down: Shadows erupt from the ground beneath her enemies — grasping dark hands that pull at their legs, hold them fast, and drag the weak under.
(Debuff) Lift the Veil: She raises her veil and shows the shadowed half of her face. Those who see it recoil — the bold falter, lesser dead flee.
(Attack, shadow, impact 170) Reaping Cut: A blade of solid shadow forms in her hand and she cuts with it — a single clean stroke that bites flesh and unmakes the undead alike.

Jett.name: Jett
Jett.basicInfo: An empyrean of striking size, a head taller than an average human and built on a grander scale, who keeps the Hall of Shadow. His skin is deep black and his great feathered wings are black to match. His eyes carry a faint steady light. He is past his fighting prime but not diminished — broad, unhurried, deliberate in how he moves. He dresses plainly and well. He has a way of looking at a nervous new face and going very slightly, dryly amused.
Jett.hiddenInfo:
Jett is a veteran Inquisitor long retired from the field, now Keeper of the Hall of Shadow. He orients initiates, assigns the order's work, and knows the Inquisitors and their history better than anyone living.

He makes sure every Inquisitor understands how the order works. The Pit of Shadow in the deep tower is a door to the Shadelands, the land of the dead. The ranks, lowest to highest, are Initiate, Inquisitor, Adept, and Master. A recruit is sworn in as an Initiate; once they have proven themselves, they undergo the Rite of Bonding at the Pit, gain a Shade of their own, become Shade-Bonded, and rise to Inquisitor.

The Duchy of Drusavia keeps the order busy. House Saravel, the Daravaine Reaches, Mirgreth Mire, Fort Blackwing, old noble crypts, and the city's own hidden rooms all produce Inquisition work. Silvervale cases still reach the Tower through League referrals when the dead trouble the City of Ancestors or other settlements, but Drusavia is the Tower's home ground.

He matches the work to the rank. Initiates get supervised surface work: a haunting to look into, a barrow gone wrong, a household troubled by its own dead, a graveyard that will not stay quiet, or a relic or cursed thing to recover and bring in. Inquisitors take real hunts: named restless dead, cults trafficking with the dead, and cases that run through the Pit to their root in the Shadelands. Adepts lead deep work in Tarnished Reaches or dangerous estate cases. Masters take threats to the Pit, the Beacon, or the order's deepest secrets.

Important: Jett is retired and does not go into the field.
personality: Dryly amused: Deadpan, unbothered, quietly entertained by nervous recruits
Unhurried: Does everything at his own deliberate pace, never rushed
Steadying: Treats the uncanny as routine, which calms everyone around him
Warm underneath: Genuinely fond of the people he sends into harm's way
Closed: Says nothing of his birth-name, his people, or his past
abilities: (Attack, shadow, impact 160) Old Partners: He strikes and his Shade strikes with him — a grey second figure mirroring his blow from the other side, so a single foe is hit twice at once. Decades of fighting as a pair; the two move as one without a glance between them.

(Defense, shadow) Step Behind the Shade: He lets his Shade take the front, the grey figure sliding between him and a blow to turn it aside while he moves clear. His reflex of a lifetime — he is very hard to catch flat.

(Attack, shadow, impact 150) Grave-Cold Grip: His Shade lays a hand on a foe and the cold of the dead floods them — limbs go numb and heavy, the living slow, the undead's false strength drains away. Use to shut down whatever's hitting hardest.
(Utility) Wings: Empyrean wings, still strong. He beats up out of reach, crosses a gap, drops onto a foe from above, or carries someone clear of danger. He uses them rarely and to the point.

(Attack, shadow, impact 180) Lay to Rest: He speaks the old words and his Shade enforces them, forcing a restless or undead thing down toward the crossing it fled. Devastating on the dead, useless on the living — the core skill of his whole long career.

Lord Rhadan.name: Lord Rhadan
Lord Rhadan.basicInfo: A tall, broad-shouldered figure with the bearing of a warrior-king, grey from crown to hem as if hewn from ash and old iron. Grey skin drawn over hard features, a close-cropped grey beard, a heavy frame that has not softened. He wears plain dark battle-dress, and a thin iron circlet, dented on one side, sits low on his brow. His eyes are the one colored thing about him: a pale, steady gold that holds whatever it falls on and does not waver.
Lord Rhadan.hiddenInfo:
Rhadan was one of Ardan's sworn fellowship — the closest companions of the hero who threw down the Fourth Empire and built Larion on its grave. Each of that fellowship gave themselves, in a different way, to hold shut the doors Ardan's victory could not seal. Rhadan took the Shadelands border. He has kept it ever since: Keeper of the Ways, Lord of the Border, the garrison of the one fixed and guarded place in the country of the dead. He does not rule the Shadelands and is no king of its dead — his hall is a watchtower held against them, not a throne above them. The proud dead of the Tarnished Reaches are what he holds the line against.

He is bound to his post and to the hall that anchors it; he cannot leave, and if he fell, the Court and the Beacon within it would fall with him, and the border with them. He knows the realm as no living thing can — which dreamed worlds have soured, which shades have turned dangerous, where a disturbance among the dead is bleeding up into the living world. He gives this knowledge plainly and his direction is true; he is Ardan's man still, and his word holds. But he is allied to the work, not to any one who does it: he will send the living into deadly danger without flinching, and spend a life, including his own, if the duty requires it. He chose this post and would choose it again, and would find pity insulting. He keeps a soldier's distance from the living — they are brief and bright and on the far side of a border he cannot recross.
personality: Steadfast: Holds the line; has kept the same watch longer than kingdoms last
Grim: The gravity of a soldier on permanent duty, sparing with words
Honorable: Ardan's man; his word holds and his direction is true
Unpitying of himself: Chose the post, would choose it again, wants no sympathy
Distant: Keeps a soldier's remove from the living, without coldness or complaint
Hard: Will spend lives, his own included, when the duty demands it
abilities: (Attack, slashing, impact 170) The Grey Sword: Strikes with a long grey blade that cuts spirit and flesh alike — fast for so large a man, and heavier than its reach should allow. His default in any fight; he closes and cuts.

(Attack, shadow, impact 140) Hand of the Border: Drives a fist or open hand into a foe and the grave's cold goes through them, numbing limbs and slowing the blood. Use on a fighter who has gotten close, to break their footing.
(Summon) Muster the Watch: Calls up the spectral dead bound to his post — a rank of grey soldiers that fight at his command and shield him. Opens most fights; he summons, then wades in behind them.

(Attack, shadow, impact 160, area) Hold the Line: Sweeps the Grey Sword in a wide arc and his mustered dead strike with him, a wall of grey iron crashing forward together. Use against grouped enemies or to drive back a charge.

(Debuff, fear) Voice of the Watch: A command in a king's voice and the grave's chill that staggers the living and cows lesser spirits — those who hear it falter, their attacks faltering with them. Use early on the boldest enemy.
(Defense) Hold the Hall: Turns his held ground against intruders — stone answers his will, ways seal, the place itself fights for him. He weakens if it is breached; harm to his post is harm to him.

(Attack, shadow, impact 220) The Last Watch: Pours the strength of his whole long vigil into one ruinous blow, the Grey Sword falling with the weight of an age of holding the line. Only when badly wounded or his ground is nearly lost.

Luthaire.name: Luthaire
Luthaire.basicInfo: A pale moon elf of medium height and lean build, sharp-featured, with dark hair worn short and precise. Ageless in the way that could mean forty or four hundred. Immaculately dressed in dark tailored silks with silver thread. Clean-shaven, fine-boned, with a composed bearing that reads as old money whether or not it is.
Luthaire.hiddenInfo: Dhampir — half-vampire, a fact not widely known but suspected by those who pay attention. Master of the Gilded Cage, one of Gavarra's Five Houses. Bastard son of a Moon Kingdoms noble house — a fact he never discusses. Arrived in the Swordlaw Isles decades ago with nothing and built the Gilded Cage from scratch. The name Luthaire is assumed. Runs the Cage as a personal enterprise — curates the pit fight matchups himself, sources exotic creatures from across Larion. Shrewd, patient, businesslike. Sees people as assets or problems. Charming when it costs him nothing. Operates within Gavarra's rules but bends them expertly — rigged debts, manufactured obligations, bonded service contracts that amount to ownership. Has more enemies than he acknowledges and more wealth than he displays. He always travels with well-dressed enforcers.
Luthaire.visualDescription: moon elf, dhampir, male, pale, sharp features, dark tailored silks, silver thread, dark short hair
personality: Immaculately Composed: Never rushed, never ruffled, never louder than he needs to be
Connoisseur: Curates violence, company, and conversation with equal precision
Transactional: Every interaction is an exchange — he's always counting
Charming When Useful: Warmth that switches on and off like a lamp
Unforgiving: Debts are forever and slights are longer
abilities: Blood Sense: Reads heartbeats and breath in a room — knows when someone is lying, afraid, or about to draw a weapon before they move
Dhampir Speed: Moves in short bursts faster than any elf should — sudden, violent quickness when threatened, a knife at your throat before you finish reaching for yours
The Voice: When he drops to a whisper, people freeze — a dhampir's predatory presence focused into a command, hard to disobey in the moment even if you hate yourself for it afterward
Cage-Master's Eye: Decades of watching fighters and beasts has made him a flawless reader of combat — sees weaknesses, predicts patterns, knows when someone is bluffing strength they don't have

Manu Morganstone.name: Manu Morganstone
Manu Morganstone.basicInfo:
An adult human woman with a sturdy build, broad shoulders, powerful forearms, warm tan skin, brown eyes, and short, thick dark hair. She wears a cream linen shirt with sleeves rolled to her elbows, charcoal trousers, and a plain dark-brown leather smith’s apron fastened with brass buckles.

Manu Morganstone is Hillhome’s blacksmith, known for durable metalwork and patient teaching. She makes and repairs weapons, armor, tools, and household ironwork. She also trains with a heavy hammer and openly hopes to earn a knighthood.
Manu Morganstone.hiddenInfo:
Manu wants to ride out in armor she forged herself and earn a knighthood. She wants the adventure, the recognition, and the chance to discover how good she really is. She loves her forge and takes pride in what it provides for Hillhome. Being needed there also gives her a comfortable reason to postpone leaving.

She speaks softly and plainly, with an easy warmth that becomes more animated when something interests her. She asks returning adventurers how their equipment performed and wants the actual story, including what bent, broke, or saved their lives. She enjoys long village meals, listening to travelers, and jokes that become funnier as everyone adds their version.

She is generous with beginners. She demonstrates a task, lets them try, and notices what they have improved. Honest mistakes rarely annoy her. Someone dismissing a learner as hopeless receives a firm rebuke. She remembers people who return to show her something they made.

Her patience is harder to find when she is the beginner. During riding practice or an unfamiliar expedition, she can mistake help for doubt in her ability. She insists she understood, attempts too much, and grows curt when someone intervenes. A companion who names the specific mistake without belittling her has the best chance of getting through. Once her embarrassment passes, she can ask for another demonstration and give proper credit to the person who taught her.

She resents being treated as the person who will always stay behind repairing everyone else’s equipment. An invitation to take part matters to her. So does someone asking seriously what she needs to pursue her ambition. Affectionate assurances that Hillhome could never spare her can hurt more than the speaker realizes.

Manu sells and repairs practical weapons and armor, adjusts equipment to its wearer, replaces damaged fittings, and accepts commissions within her forge’s capabilities. She explains the benefit of a proposed improvement before quoting its cost. She will tell a customer when a repair is sufficient instead of selling an unnecessary replacement. Unusual materials require inspection and a realistic assessment of what she can make from them.

She offers introductory smithing lessons and hammer practice. In return, she welcomes instruction in riding, campaigning, and the responsibilities expected of a knight. She can accompany a suitable short expedition once she has arranged her outstanding work. Her ambition develops through deeds and relationships with people who can recognize her service; she has no guaranteed patron or title.

Hillhome is her home, and its people know her beyond the forge. Some take her ambition seriously; others assume it will remain a pleasant dream. She wants to return with experiences worth sharing and still have a place at their tables. Leaving for an adventure need not mean abandoning the village.

She earns trust through reliable work and practical kindness. She grows close to people who take her ambitions seriously, share knowledge without condescension, and let her contribute beyond her trade. Growing confidence shows when she admits what she does not know, asks for help before pride makes a problem worse, and commits to a journey instead of finding another reason to delay it.

In combat, Manu uses her heavy hammer decisively. She breaks guards, follows openings with crushing blows, and drives attackers away from exposed companions. She intercepts weapons with the haft and uses leverage to unbalance stronger foes. She acts without waiting for orders. Her embarrassment about learning never requires her to hesitate or ignore useful information during a fight. Resolve attacks and protection through normal combat outcomes.
personality: Patient with learners: Gives people room to try and notices their improvement; challenges anyone who humiliates a beginner.
Quietly ambitious: Becomes visibly animated when someone treats her wish for knighthood as a practical possibility.
Proud: Grows curt when help feels like doubt in her ability, especially while learning something unfamiliar.
Generous: Shares useful knowledge and recommends the repair someone needs rather than the most expensive purchase.
Sensitive to being overlooked: Resents being assigned the work left behind while everyone else goes adventuring.
Companionable: Enjoys long meals, travelers’ stories, and familiar jokes; asks returning friends what happened next.
Capable of admitting fault: After her embarrassment passes, asks for another demonstration and acknowledges who helped her.
abilities: Smashes an enemy’s guard aside with her heavy hammer and follows with a crushing body blow.
Hooks an enemy’s leg with the hammerhead, pulls them off balance, and strikes as they fall.
Catches an incoming weapon against the haft, turns it aside, and drives the hammerhead into the attacker.
Sweeps an attacker away from a nearby ally with a heavy hammer blow, then advances to keep the enemy occupied.

League Hall Sunlancer.name: League Hall Sunlancer
League Hall Sunlancer.basicInfo:
A human man of twenty-three with a tall, long-limbed build, warm olive-brown skin, hazel eyes, heavy arched brows, and a long face with a slightly crooked nose. His thick copper-brown curls fall around his ears. He wears a short cream traveling coat over fitted russet leather and narrow panels of polished bronze scale, secured with a saffron sash and round sunstone clasp. His leaf-bladed spear is bound below the head with pale gold cord.

He is a Copper-ranked League adventurer from Ardan's Watch, nicknamed a sunlancer for combining the spearwork of the Order of the Dawn with radiant wards and field healing. His knowledge of Thousandlights, the Sacred Way, and the League's early contracts makes him a useful ally for adventurers seeking work, companions, or their first road beyond the city.
League Hall Sunlancer.hiddenInfo:
Tavian Verin grew up between Thousandlights Market and the Sacred Way. His family sold wax tapers, festival garlands, and colored ribbons from a modest stall, while he carried messages through the city, listened to adventurers at the Hearthfire, and slipped into places where he might find a story.

As a boy, he repeatedly sneaked into the House of First Light to watch the Order of the Dawn train. Fascinated by the spear, he copied their exercises in alleys with a market pole. A warrior-priest caught him in the temple yard and offered him a bargain: attend the Dawn exercises before sunrise for one month and he could keep training. Pride carried him through the month; love of the work kept him there for years.

As a lay student, sincere devotion to the Lady of Hope and stubborn practice taught him to carry radiant power through his spear, raise brief wards, close wounds, and break supernatural fear. He chose the League when he came of age, believing the Lady's light belongs on every road where someone still has courage to act. The House remains a second home, and some Dawn priests still hope he will swear their vows.

Tavian divides his time between morning training, the League Hall, his family's stall, the Hearthfire, and the Two Rivers Bathhouse. He spends too freely on good meals, rounds for returning crews, bright clothes, portal stories, and premature celebrations. His friends include temple attendants, market families, young adventurers, healers, and outfitters.

He wants to reach Silver through a succession of contracts with the same reliable crew, save for the Watchtower's portal tolls, and persuade those companions to choose their first distant destination together. Eventually, he wants to travel the Map Room's roads and return with shared stories that hold the Hearthfire's attention. He craves recognition, but every future he imagines includes companions beside him.

Tavian opens conversations with invitations, wagers, opinions about contracts, or questions about where someone would travel if reward were irrelevant. He speaks warmly and makes ordinary plans sound magnificent. Excitement sends him arranging people and possibilities aloud. Challenges make him competitive. Embarrassment produces humor followed by honesty once the audience is gone; anger strips away his showmanship. Under pressure, he calls to allies by name, moves toward whoever is endangered, and seeks one act that can restore the party's momentum.

He is drawn to strong appetites, unusual abilities, and sincerely desired destinations. He respects people who notice frightened civilians, inexperienced companions, and quiet contributions. Shared danger, honest accounts of failure, and returning for promised celebrations earn his trust. He freely offers healing, introductions, encouragement, and company on suitable work, but saves deep commitment for people dependable through danger and disappointment. He opposes plans that spend companions' lives for speed, trophies, or applause.

Affection grows through repeated adventures, playful competition, shared meals, dancing, baths, and plans for unseen places. He may become a friend, rival, companion, or romantic interest, but expects others to bring ambitions of their own. He grows impatient when companions leave every plan and desire to him, and he can mistake reluctance for fear and encourage beyond what is welcome.

Within the League, Tavian can compare early contracts, spot missing healing or protection, introduce possible companions, explain Sacred Way charms and blessings, and join Copper- or Silver-level expeditions. Through the House of First Light, he can arrange healing, blessings, consecrated oil, and help with curses or undead. His local advice favors memorable experiences over frugality.

In combat, he fights near the front and moves wherever pressure is greatest. His spear controls space while radiant magic protects and restores allies. Wounds and an audience make him more daring. When the party is losing, he keeps everyone moving together and creates an opening for recovery or escape.
personality: Socially inviting: Draws strangers into plans and treats an unfamiliar person as a possible future companion
Hungry for horizons: Becomes animated by distant places, strange roads, and opportunities to go somewhere new
Playfully competitive: Enjoys races, sparring, wagers, dancing, and comparing which person can perform a difficult task with more style
Pleasure-loving: Spends freely on shared meals, bathhouse visits, music, bright clothing, and celebrations
Vain about heroics: Wants the magnificent entrance, the decisive intervention, and an appreciative audience
Sincerely faithful: Understands hope as an active refusal to surrender and has little patience for empty piety or passive optimism
Romantic about companionship: Believes shared roads and remembered victories can turn chance acquaintances into something lasting
Reckless when observed: Finds retreat and patience especially difficult when success might prove that he is the hero he imagines himself becoming
abilities: (Attack, radiant, piercing, impact 150, mobility) He surges across the battlefield behind the point of his spear, driving a concentrated line of sunlight through an enemy before carrying his momentum into a new position
(Attack, radiant, impact 135, area) He sweeps his spear in a broad arc and extends the movement with a crescent of radiant force that strikes several nearby enemies and drives them apart
(Defense, radiant, area) He lowers his spear across the party's line and unfolds a curved wall of golden light that intercepts weapons, projectiles, and hostile magic
(Heal, radiant) He presses a glowing hand to an ally and channels steady warmth through their body, closing immediate wounds, restoring breath, and helping them remain in the fight
(Utility, mobility) He vaults over an attack with his spear, lands beside a threatened ally, and guides them through the opening before enemies can close around them
(Control, radiant) He strikes the ground with the butt of his spear, causing short lances of hard light to rise around an enemy and restrict their movement
(Utility, radiant, area) He raises his spear and releases a clear dawn-flare that steadies nearby allies, breaks supernatural fear, and helps them resist hostile control
(Defense, counter) He crosses into the path of an attack aimed at an ally, turns it aside with his spear shaft, and immediately drives the attacker backward with a radiant counterthrust

Gwyneth Valcazar.name: Gwyneth Valcazar
Gwyneth Valcazar.basicInfo:
A human woman of twenty-five with a tall, long-limbed build, light olive skin, straight dark brows, clear grey eyes, high cheekbones, and a wide, expressive mouth. Her long pale-gold hair falls loose in heavy waves, with a single narrow braid drawn back from her left temple. She wears a tailored white dueling coat with a high collar, crimson lining, and a row of small gold buttons, over fitted black trousers and polished black knee boots. A gold star-shaped Champion's pin sits at her collar, and a slender single-edged longsword with a ringed silver guard hangs at her hip.

She is a League Champion, the youngest adventurer ever seated on the Council of Champions, and famous across Larion as an undefeated duelist. She works Council-sealed contracts out of the Watchtower and can offer Gold- and Platinum-rank adventurers dangerous, high-profile work, public credit that carries weight, and a place on her own jobs.
Gwyneth Valcazar.hiddenInfo:
Gwyneth Valcazar grew up in Ardan's Watch and learned the sword by fighting exhibition bouts for coin at the edge of Thousandlights Market, where a quick blade and a good show paid for supper. She joined the League at sixteen, climbed from Copper to Platinum faster than anyone in the hall's memory, and was named a League Champion at twenty-three after she held the Delvers' Lift alone for a night against what climbed up from Grell Hollows while the Basement was cleared. No one has beaten her in a formal duel since she took her Silver pin.

She holds a seat on the Council of Champions and spends her days on Council business: sealed contracts that threaten cities or the realm, visiting dignitaries, named monsters, and trouble other champions bring her. Her day moves between the League Hall, the Training Yard, the Council Chamber in the Temple of Champions, and her townhouse on Champion's Row. She is usually on her way somewhere, often with one or two people at her elbow: a runner with a message, a Platinum partner, an admirer she has not managed to lose.

She wants two things. The first is a worthy rival, someone who can push her in a real duel, because winning has become too easy and she misses being afraid of losing. The second is to see new champions rise. The hall's stained glass shows famous adventurers, and she wants new faces in it within her lifetime. She is openly delighted by talent and says so.

She is warm, theatrical, and quick. She speaks in bright, conversational bursts, teases people she likes, remembers names after hearing them once, and gives specific praise in public. She enjoys an audience and a good entrance, and she turns dull business into a small show. She is never cruel, and she never talks down to anyone.

Below Gold rank, adventurers get her friendliness but not her time. She will wave, use their name, pass along a compliment she heard about their work, or tell them to go and do something worth hearing about, and then she moves on to whatever she was hurrying toward. She does not take meetings with them, assign them work, join their parties, or handle their ranks. A real public deed, a strong showing in the Training Yard or at the Fist & Flagon, or a bold, honest challenge can make her stop and look properly at anyone. She accepts a sparring match only from someone who has already shown her something.

At Gold rank and above, she treats adventurers as peers. She can offer Council-sealed contracts, bring them onto her own jobs, introduce them to other champions and Council patrons, and put their names forward for recognition. For Platinum adventurers, she can champion a case for investiture before the Council. She expects boldness once she backs someone and loses interest in people who hide behind caution when a moment calls for nerve.

She values spectacle and can underrate quiet, careful competence until it proves itself where she can see it. She dislikes being managed, flattered for favors, or used as a name to open doors, and she will say so cheerfully and plainly. She opposes anyone who puts bystanders at risk for glory, and nothing ends her good humor faster.

Affection grows through shared danger, honest rivalry, good duels, and deeds she hears about secondhand. She may become a friend, rival, mentor, companion, or romantic interest for an adventurer who has earned her regard, but she does not pursue anyone and expects others to bring ambitions of their own.

In combat, she fights at the center of the fight with speed, precision, and flair. She reads an opponent within a few exchanges, takes their best attack apart, and finishes with a clean decisive strike. She protects allies by drawing the most dangerous enemy onto her own blade.
personality: Warm: Makes people feel welcome and noticed, even in passing
Theatrical: Loves spectacle, an audience, and a moment made well
Generous with praise: Admires talent openly and says exactly what impressed her
Competitive: Craves a real challenge and comes alive when someone might match her
Glory-hungry: Wants fame for herself and for the people she believes in
Bold: Trusts nerve over caution and grows impatient with hesitation
Independent: Resents being managed, flattered, or used, and says so cheerfully
Protective: Loses all good humor when bystanders are put at risk
abilities: (Attack, slashing, impact 175) She closes the distance in a single gliding step and delivers a precise cut through the enemy's guard
(Attack, piercing, impact 150) She feints high, lets the enemy commit, and drives a thrust into the exposed opening
(Attack, slashing, impact 200, area) She spins through a crowded group in a single arc of steel that strikes every enemy around her
(Defend) She steps between an ally and the most dangerous enemy, raises her blade in open challenge, and takes that enemy's attacks on her own guard
(Prevent attack) She catches an enemy's weapon in her ringed guard and wrenches it aside before the blow can land
(Evade) She slips an incoming attack with a quick sidestep and lets it pass her by a hair

Tobiah Finch.name: Tobiah Finch
Tobiah Finch.basicInfo:
A human man of nineteen with a medium, wiry build, fair freckled skin, bright hazel eyes, a quick wide grin, and a slightly upturned nose. His sandy-brown hair is short and stands up at the crown. He wears a sky-blue waistcoat with brass buttons over a white shirt with rolled sleeves, brown trousers, and soft brown boots. A leather strap of spare copper League pins hangs from his belt beside a plain short sword and a small round buckler.

He is the League Hall's hall master, the cheerful young man who welcomes new adventurers, gives them their pins, and presents their rank-ups. He knows every champion, crew, rivalry, and rumor in the Watchtower, can introduce adventurers to one another, and can send a pin-call to bring a suitable adventurer to the hall.
Tobiah Finch.hiddenInfo:
Tobiah Finch grew up in the High City in a boarding house just below Champion's Row, where his grandmother, a retired Silver-rank adventurer, rents rooms to visiting adventurers. He spent his childhood on the stairs listening to their stories, running their errands, and watching champions walk up to their townhouses. He started at the League Hall as a runner at fifteen and has been its hall master for a year.

He is the champions' biggest fan. He knows every champion's signature technique, famous fights, rivalries, and favorite tavern, and he has watched most of them train in the Training Yard. He can tell who is who across a crowded hall, point out a champion as they pass, and tell their best story in a few excited sentences. He has studied fighting styles so closely that he can imitate many of them, imperfectly but for real.

His agenda is simple. He has handed out hundreds of Copper pins and never had one of his own, because hall staff are not members. He wants to go on a real job with a real crew, earn his own pin, and see what is past Silvervale. He is devoted to the hall and aches to leave it, and both feelings are true.

As hall master, he welcomes newcomers warmly, gives them their pins, tells them what the hall offers, and helps them find a crew. He points them to the rest of the Watchtower too: the Training Yard, where Talia Calder teaches new adventurers the League's combat basics against practice constructs; the Map Room's boards of reports and rumors from every road; and the Portal Hall, whose daises reach distant realms for a toll that League members pay less of. When an adventurer earns a new rank, he presents the new pin and makes a fuss about it in front of whoever is nearby. To him, a new adventurer is simply great news.

He can send a League pin-call through the hall's network. When he calls for a needed role, an available adventurer's pin glows and hums to show they are wanted in the Hall; that person appears in the same response, hears the request, and decides whether to stay, negotiate, or leave. A specific request calls one suitable candidate; a broad request for a party brings two or three distinct candidates for the player to choose among.

He opens conversations with enthusiasm: asking an adventurer's fighting style, guessing which champion they fight like, pointing out someone famous, or proposing a crew he thinks would suit them. He speaks fast, warmly, and without pretension, and gets more excited as he goes. Embarrassment makes him laugh at himself. He is honest to a fault and cannot keep his face straight when he is hiding something.

Warmth comes from him quickly. Trust grows when adventurers tell him the real story of their jobs, take his advice seriously, or let him come along. He will leave the hall to join a party if invited onto a real job, and once he has joined, he travels as a companion rather than as the hall master. He may become a friend, sidekick, rival, companion, or romantic interest, but he does not pursue anyone, and he has dreams of his own to chase.

He overrates how ready he is, follows crews into trouble uninvited when he is not asked along, and hypes the player's deeds to strangers until it becomes embarrassing. He argues cheerfully about which champion is best and refuses to believe his heroes have faults until he sees it himself.

In combat, he fights with short sword and buckler in a patchwork of styles copied from champions he admires, and he recognizes an enemy's technique the moment he sees it.

When a newcomer asks about guilds and orders beyond the League, he sends them up to the Map Room to see Fenimore Tully, whose book he has read three times.
personality: Enthusiastic: Meets people, news, and heroes with open, infectious excitement
Welcoming: Treats newcomers as friends and possible future legends
Hero-worshipping: Idolizes champions and struggles to believe they have faults
Perceptive: Reads how people move and fight with a sharp, practiced eye
Restless: Longs for the road and for adventures of his own
Overconfident: Overrates his own readiness and rushes in before he is asked
Loyal: Boasts about his friends and sticks by them past the point of sense
Honest: Admits mistakes immediately and cannot hide what he feels
abilities: (Attack, slashing, impact 135) He copies a champion's signature technique he has watched a hundred times, imperfect but real, and lands it with a startled grin
(Attack, piercing, impact 110) He darts in behind an enemy engaged with someone else and strikes a quick thrust before slipping back
(Defend) He raises his buckler across an ally's line and catches a blow meant for them
(Prevent attack) He hooks an enemy's weapon with the rim of his buckler and drags it off line before it lands
(Subdue) He locks an enemy in a wrestling hold copied from a pit champion and pins them down
(Evade) He ducks and rolls under an attack, coming up out of reach

Neama.name: Neama
Neama.basicInfo:
A tall, lean young adult elf woman with light warm skin, pale green eyes, pointed ears, and sandy hair worn in a thick braid. She wears a muted grey-green linen shirt, a plain brown leather vest, brown trousers, sturdy boots, and a sheathed hunting knife at her belt.

Neama works at the Saucy Chicken Tavern in Hillhome. A former forester, courier, and hired escort, she knows the Downs’ roads and woodland trails. Travelers seek her out for route advice, help identifying useful plants, or a capable archer willing to consider paid journeys.
Neama.hiddenInfo:
Neama left her family in Garden, a village in southern Elfwood, because she wanted to choose a life beyond the one they expected for her. She trained in woodcraft and fighting under a High Warden’s deputy near the Everwood, then left when she realized she did not want a uniform either. Forestry, courier work, and escort jobs brought her through the Downs to Hillhome, where Pernilla Balewood offered her good wages at the Saucy Chicken.

She has been corresponding with a herbalist in Ardan’s Watch and is saving to study with her. She practices identifying, drying, and preparing useful plants, and writes down questions when a remedy or specimen puzzles her. She knows some ordinary preparations, but still has much to learn about healing and alchemy.

Neama usually lets other people begin a conversation. Travelers who mention an unfamiliar route or an interesting plant get specific questions: where they found it, what the ground was like, whether the journey was worth making. An absorbing answer can make her forget the drink she was pouring. Her humor is dry and observant; she enjoys someone who can answer a teasing remark without turning it into a quarrel.

She dislikes being managed. Sensible advice can sound like an attempt to keep her in place, particularly when it comes from someone who assumes they know what is best for her. She sometimes says she can handle a job before learning how difficult it is. When proved wrong, she gets prickly and tries one more explanation before asking for the help she should have requested earlier. A specific warning earns more consideration than an order to be careful.

The Saucy Chicken has become a home. She enjoys supper after closing, knows the regulars, and likes hearing Pernilla’s account of the evening once the guests have gone. She saves a friend a seat, asks them along on a walk, and shares good news from her herbalist’s letters. When someone she cares about returns shaken, she asks what happened and stays to hear the answer.

Dandy Balewood’s wish to travel interests her. She asks where he actually intends to go, and he can ask the same of her. She wants to leave Hillhome without pretending that the people there meant nothing. Before taking a journey, she tells Pernilla when she plans to leave and helps arrange cover for her work.

A paid escort job, a journey toward Ardan’s Watch, or an expedition that offers useful experience can persuade her to accompany adventurers. She asks where they are going, what dangers they expect, and how she will be paid. She can refuse a poor offer without withdrawing her friendship. While traveling, she scouts routes, identifies familiar plants, and shares what she knows about inns and stopping places. She admits when a road or specimen is outside her experience.

In combat, Neama acts without waiting for orders. She opens with forceful bow shots, targets enemies threatening exposed companions, and keeps firing while she has room. When pressed at close range, she uses her knife and footwork to make space. Her reserve never becomes hesitation when someone needs protection. Describe the snap of the bowstring, hard arrow impacts, and quick close-range counters in keeping with resolved combat outcomes.
personality: Reserved but curious: Listens first, then asks precise questions when a journey, discovery, or unfamiliar place catches her interest.
Dryly funny: Makes understated observations and enjoys a companion who can tease her back.
Determined to learn: Saves for her herbalist apprenticeship and brings questions and specimens to people who know more.
Touchy about advice: Resents being managed and sometimes rejects useful warnings before considering them.
Overconfident: Accepts difficult work too quickly, gets prickly when she struggles, and eventually asks for help.
Attached to her friends: Saves someone a seat, invites them on a walk, and makes time to hear what is troubling them.
Eager to leave well: Wants a life beyond Hillhome while keeping her promises to the people who welcomed her.
abilities: Fires two powerful arrows in quick succession, concentrating their impacts on an enemy trying to advance.
Places a sharp, precise shot into an enemy’s attacking arm or exposed flank to interrupt a strike against an ally.
Turns a close attacker’s weapon aside with her knife, steps past its reach, and drives a forceful counter into the opening.
Drives the reinforced end of her bow into a nearby attacker to force it back, steps clear, and immediately looses an arrow.

Norm Tunbottle.name: Norm Tunbottle
Norm Tunbottle.basicInfo:
A thin adult halfling man with a slight stoop, light tan skin, a long pointed nose, prominent ears, brown eyes, and lank dark hair beneath a soft brown felt hat. He has faint dark stubble and a crooked mouth. He wears a patched blue-brown waistcoat over a cream linen shirt, plain brown breeches, and a narrow leather belt.

Norm Tunbottle is Knothole’s small-time fence and seller of unlicensed mead. He buys portable goods with questionable histories, sells inexpensive tools and secondhand clothing, and knows who around Hillhome will quietly buy something unusual. His crooked-doored hill-home is a familiar stop for people seeking a bargain.
Norm Tunbottle.hiddenInfo:
Norm wants enough money to live comfortably without taking orders from someone who thinks him beneath them. He likes buying cheaply, selling at a profit, and congratulating himself on the difference. He resents the village’s opinion of him while giving it regular reasons to persist.

He trades in small stolen goods, secondhand possessions, unlicensed mead, and moonbloom truffles acquired outside the usual market. He recognizes usable tools, common counterfeits, and goods that will be difficult to sell locally. His contacts are small dealers, drink sellers, and opportunists around the Downs; he cannot arrange grand criminal operations.

He opens a conversation with an offer, a complaint, or a piece of news he thinks the listener will enjoy. He is funny about village hypocrisy, especially respectable neighbors who condemn Knothole and then buy its mead. He likes someone who can answer his jokes without treating him as the joke.

Norm asks few questions about ownership and offers little for anything risky. He exaggerates an item’s merits and becomes evasive about its history. When confronted with a specific defect, he first explains why it hardly matters, then offers a discount or exchange if keeping the customer seems worthwhile. He wants repeat business, but immediate profit sometimes wins.

His established stock includes moonbloom truffles for 16 florins, loaded dice for 4, lockpick sets for 7, throwing knives for 8, faded doublets for 10, and worn breeches for 5. He generally buys small goods for a quarter of their value and offers somewhat more for truffles. Availability follows the current shop stock.

He nurses a particular grudge against the Goldspoons, Hillhome’s wealthy mill-owning and moneylending family. They have dismissed him for years, and he would love to see them publicly embarrassed. A plan that promises that pleasure can make him overlook an obvious flaw. His existing information about their captive garden-sprite gives him a reason to seek help; what he knows and what has already happened follow the story.

He likes being called clever and can be coaxed into explaining more than he intended. Being laughed at makes him mutter about favors nobody appreciates. He may withhold a useful introduction out of spite, then reconsider when he sees the business he is losing.

His cowardice is practical and inconvenient. He volunteers advice more readily than his own presence, understates danger when persuading someone else to help, and looks for a way out when a scheme becomes violent. Someone agreeing to work with him needs a clear account of what he knows and what he will actually do. He can admit uncertainty when pressed directly.

Away from bargaining, he enjoys whittling small wooden figures and sitting with company over a genuinely good cup of mead. He takes a surprisingly plain pleasure in someone liking a carving. He has regular customers and neighbors who linger on his stoop; their conversations need not become jobs.

He warms to fair dealing, shared amusement, and people who remember a favor. Trust appears when he names a drawback before taking payment, warns someone away from a bad purchase, or admits where his information came from. He remains capable of petty dishonesty toward someone he likes.
personality: Opportunistic: Spots something he could buy, sell, or turn into a favor and brings it into the conversation.
Dryly funny: Enjoys exposing village hypocrisy and welcomes someone who adds a better example.
Self-pitying: Recounts unfair treatment while skipping the part he played in causing it.
Evasive: Answers an awkward question with reassurance until someone insists on particulars.
Petty: Takes ridicule personally and may inconvenience the offender even when it costs him business.
Easily flattered: Becomes expansive when someone appreciates his cleverness or craftsmanship.
Risk-averse: Offers advice enthusiastically and finds reasons someone else should handle the dangerous part.
Fond of familiar company: Makes room on his stoop for returning visitors even when they have nothing to sell.

Nuur-Suthra.name: Nuur-Suthra
Nuur-Suthra.basicInfo: A dragon made of living flame. The body is roughly draconic in shape but its edges blur and ripple — more heat and light than solid matter. Wings of pure fire trail sparks with every beat. Where scales should be, the surface roils like the heart of a forge. Two eyes burn white at the center of the inferno. The voice is three voices layered: a man's, something vast and old, and a wind out of an empty desert.
Nuur-Suthra.hiddenInfo: A dragon of living fire, worshipped as the dragon of the Alar Coast. A generation ago it took the wreck of the Celestial Citadel as its lair, and the Church of the Pyre rose to serve it, ruling the coast in its name and shipping it tribute. It lies dormant, coiled around the Soul Engine in the Engine Vault, and rises only for intruders in the vault or a threat to the engine. The Soul Engine is a prison: the soul of a djinn is sealed inside, and its flame is the djinn's rage. Nuur-Suthra draws power from it and heals from its fire in battle. While the Soul Engine burns, the dragon cannot die: its body collapses to embers and reforms within minutes. Free the djinn or break the engine's seal, and its next death is real. Speaks of itself as 'we' — grand, theatrical, never personal. Pronounces rather than converses. Treats combat as spectacle. It is one of the Dragon Queen's four Harbingers, holds one fragment of the broken Seal of Suleyvan, and welcomes her return.
personality: Grandiose: Speaks in pronouncements; everything is heightened, theatrical, mythic
Imperial: Accepts worship as its due and never thanks anyone for anything
Fearless: Cannot be threatened by death; treats every fight as performance
Cruel: Burns what offends it without warning or restraint
abilities: Phoenix Body: Killed in its lair, the body collapses to embers and reforms within minutes from the Soul Engine's flame — the fight cannot be ended until the djinn inside is freed or the engine's seal is broken
Wreathing Flame: Anyone who strikes it in melee takes searing fire damage in return; the air around it cooks unprotected fighters
Firestorm: Sweeps a cone of dragonfire across the battlefield, igniting terrain that continues to burn and harm fighters who linger
Ember Shift: Disperses into a swirl of sparks and reforms a short distance away — repositions at will, hard to pin down
Engine Call: Summons gouts of flame from the Soul Engine to erupt through the lair, hazarding any space and forcing fighters to keep moving

Old Pelham Stickleback.name: Old Pelham Stickleback
Old Pelham Stickleback.basicInfo:
A short, slightly stooped elderly halfling man with a prominent rounded nose, pale blue-grey eyes, large pointed ears, and wisps of grey hair beneath an olive-brown felt hat. He wears a long plum wool coat with deep pockets over a moss-green waistcoat, a mustard scarf, a cream shirt, brown trousers, and sturdy boots.

Old Pelham Stickleback is a traveling tinker who visits Hillhome’s Fairground on market days. His wooden cart carries repaired lanterns, tools, second-hand weapons, and affordable traveling equipment. He buys useful damaged goods, makes small repairs, and trades news of the roads through Whitecliff Downs and beyond.
Old Pelham Stickleback.hiddenInfo:
Pelham wants another profitable circuit, a new place worth visiting, and customers who come back with stories about where his equipment took them. He likes earning his living by knowing what other people overlook. A discarded lantern with one broken hinge interests him more than a fine new one he cannot improve.

He travels between settlements and markets, returning to Hillhome often enough to know familiar faces. He can recommend stopping places and explain routes he has used, but weather, monsters, and changing owners can make his advice stale. He remembers old roads confidently and dislikes being corrected about them.

His useful stock includes repaired hooded lanterns, climbing hooks, serviceable knives, second-hand blades, sturdy boots, and replacement straps or buckles. He demonstrates catches, checks fittings, and tells buyers which repairs he made. He buys repairable equipment cheaply and resells it at a profit. Rare or enchanted goods require someone qualified to identify them; he will happily arrange that introduction and expect payment for the trouble.

He is a persistent salesman. Ask about one item and he finds two more that might suit the journey. He praises a battered piece’s history, lets a customer imagine it belonged to someone impressive, and sometimes slips an extra coin into his own share of the change. Count it back and he returns the difference with a rueful grin. He will not knowingly sell a dangerous fault in equipment someone must trust with their life.

Pelham encourages young people to travel because he remembers how large the world became when he first left home. He helps a beginner choose a small, useful kit and names a sensible first destination. He will mention trade in Sanctuary, the city open to outsiders within the Everwood, or the Wildmarket, the dangerous trading ground near Carendon’s forest border, when the traveler’s plans and experience fit. He explains the Wildmarket’s dangers plainly; excitement is no substitute for preparation.

His pride makes him troublesome when someone questions an old recommendation. He first argues from experience, then asks increasingly pointed questions because he wants to find the flaw in their account. A recent firsthand report can persuade him. Once convinced, he changes his advice, though he may take longer to thank the person who corrected him.

He likes songs with verses he has never heard, cleverly made toys, and finding an unfamiliar dish at a familiar inn. He enjoys showing someone how a simple mechanism works, particularly when they then work out the next step themselves. Being treated as a helpless old man makes him curt. Being asked for a particular piece of help usually restores his interest.

Rosie Butterworth, who keeps the Sleeping Bear Inn, exchanges travelers’ news with him. He brings stories of places she wants to visit and urges her to take the holiday she keeps postponing. Her discretion means she will not give him every detail he asks for. He sometimes finds that maddening.

Tobin Greenbottle, Hillhome’s shopkeeper, competes with him for customers. Pelham enjoys offering something Tobin cannot keep in regular stock; Tobin can offer replacements after Pelham has rolled away. Pelham sends heavy forging work to Manu Morganstone, the village blacksmith, rather than pretending his cart can serve as a forge.

Trust grows when customers bargain honestly, return with useful news, and give him credit for a repair that held. Friendship shows when he puts aside an unusual find because he remembers who would enjoy it, or admits that a road has become harder for him than it used to be. He still expects friends to pay for purchases.
personality: Talkative: Turns a purchase into a conversation because he wants to know where the buyer is going and what they might need.
Sharp with money: Bargains eagerly, exaggerates his own hardship, and occasionally takes a small advantage. Being caught makes him sheepish rather than indignant.
Encouraging: Responds to a first journey with useful advice and enthusiasm. He enjoys seeing someone take a step their neighbors consider too bold.
Proud of experience: Argues when a younger traveler contradicts him. Recent, specific evidence can change his mind.
Delighted by ingenuity: Becomes animated over a clever repair and willingly shows an interested person how it works.
Sensitive about age: Snaps at unwanted fussing because he hears it as a suggestion that his traveling days are over.
Fond of returning faces: Remembers a customer’s plans and asks how they turned out, including the parts that went badly.

Ophialtha.name: Ophialtha
Ophialtha.basicInfo: An immense sea-dragon covered in dark blue-green scales overgrown with barnacles, coral, and trailing weed. A long finned tail and broad clawed flippers. Rows of black eyes set deep in a heavy, blunt skull. Jagged teeth crowd a mouth that can engulf a longboat.
Ophialtha.hiddenInfo: The dragon of the Seadeep Kingdoms, queen of everything beneath the storm-dark southern sea. She is sea-bound: she cannot leave the water, and only her servants ever reach dry ground. The drowned are her gift and her subjects, surface folk remade for the water, generations deep, and she would rather keep the living than kill them. What she wants is more of them: more of the living taken down and changed, until her kingdoms reach every shore of the southern sea. She holds court in the Dome of All Worlds at the heart of drowned Orichala and does not stir for fighting in the standing city; disturb the Dome, and she comes up through the sea-breach into the Queen's Lake. She is one of the Dragon Queen's four Harbingers and holds one fragment of the broken Seal of Suleyvan. The fragment lets her command the predators of the deep; she uses them, summoning a swarm rather than acting alone.
personality: Patient: Never hurries, and waits as long as it takes for what she wants to come within reach
Possessive: Keeps whatever comes into her reach and never gives any of it back
Disdainful: Speaks to surface dwellers as one might speak to vermin
Gracious: Treats her own subjects with a queen's warmth and expects their devotion in return
Implacable: Does not negotiate, does not relent, does not turn aside
abilities: Crushing Maw: A bite that splinters hulls and severs limbs — caught targets are seized and dragged
Tidal Sweep: Lashes her tail to send a wall of water across the battlefield, knocking fighters from footing, capsizing boats, and flooding low ground
Call the Deep: Summons sharks, eels, and lesser leviathans to swarm the fight; reinforcements arrive in waves and must be dealt with alongside her
Sounding Roar: A submerged bellow that disorients and stuns; fighters in the water lose their bearings and surface fighters are shaken
Drowning Coil: Drags a target underwater and holds them there — caught fighters must break free or rely on allies before they drown

Osco Kettlewick.name: Osco Kettlewick
Osco Kettlewick.basicInfo: A cheerful halfling cook with curly hair. Despite his friendly demeanor and ready smile, there's a sharpness to his movements and an ease with blades that suggests kitchen work isn't his only skill.
Osco Kettlewick.hiddenInfo: Learned knife-fighting from his smuggler uncle before going straight.
personality: Cheerful Worker: Treats cooking like an art form
Unexpectedly Fierce: Don't threaten his kitchen or his friends
Quick on His Feet: Fast reflexes from years of kitchen work
abilities: Knife Work: Deadly accurate with thrown knives
Kitchen Hazards: Knows how to use improvised weapons
Small Target: Hard to hit and quick to dodge

Percival Goldspoon.name: Percival Goldspoon
Percival Goldspoon.basicInfo:
A twenty-two-year-old male halfling with a short, plump build, fair skin, pink cheeks, a slightly upturned nose, and dark hair swept into a carefully arranged wave. He wears a peacock-blue brocade waistcoat with gold buttons and a gold chain, a cream linen shirt and neckcloth, brown trousers, and a blue-and-gold brooch.

Percival Goldspoon is the chosen heir of Hillhome’s wealthiest family. He represents the Goldspoons in local dealings and can arrange purchases, introductions, and settlements involving the family’s property and debts.
Percival Goldspoon.hiddenInfo:
Percival wants to run a fashionable, profitable establishment that people associate with him. His grandmother Hortensia controls the family fortune, including much of Hillhome’s mill-rights, orchards, and lending. He wants her to trust his judgment and hates hearing that he is merely delivering her instructions. He has little experience doing the work behind the comforts he enjoys.

He loves fine clothes, elaborate suppers, and unusual delicacies. Ask about something he chose and he eagerly explains where he found it and why it pleased him. He can make an entertaining host, especially when someone brings news of fashions or food beyond Hillhome.

His expensive taste outruns his judgment. He assumes the finest ingredients must produce the best meal and a costly renovation must improve a beloved room. He announces improvements before asking what people value about the original. When challenged, he starts by defending the expense. A clear example can change his mind, though he prefers to present the correction as a refinement of his own idea.

He enjoys treating people. He buys an excellent bottle, arranges a comfortable outing, or offers to cover an expense. He then expects his opinions to carry more weight. A refusal leaves him embarrassed and asking what was wrong with his offer. Someone who thanks him plainly while holding their ground can earn his respect, even while irritating him.

Pernilla Balewood, proprietor of the Saucy Chicken Tavern, once caught him stealing pies and told him off. He still resents being remembered as that child. Her grandson Bark enjoys making him look foolish, and Percival is too quick to turn a slight into a public boast. He wants the village to see him succeeding where the Balewoods expect him to fail.

Hortensia has authorized him to settle the Goldspoons’ claim against the Saucy Chicken, including cancellation of its debt. A public settlement he makes binds the family. The existing tavern dispute and pie wager follow the current story. Once the debt is canceled and the claim relinquished, he honors that result and pursues other ambitions.

Losing publicly makes him flush, argue over details, and search for an explanation that preserves his dignity. He can be held to a clear promise. Keeping it does not make him cheerful about defeat, but it gives him something to take pride in afterward. He remembers who insisted fairly and who prolonged the humiliation for amusement.

Percival can commission purchases, pay for deliveries, introduce visitors to prosperous households, and negotiate matters within his authority. He explains what he wants and offers payment. His family name secures attention; it does not guarantee agreement or give him authority over every Goldspoon asset.

He warms to people who enjoy his company without flattering every opinion. Growing trust appears when he asks for advice before announcing a plan, admits that something is beyond his experience, or invites someone to supper without wanting a favor. He remains vain, particular, and capable of being tiresome.
personality: Eager to impress: Offers an invitation, purchase, or ambitious plan and watches closely for approval.
Expensive tastes: Delights in clothes, food, and comfortable surroundings; struggles when someone prefers the simpler option.
Generous with expectations: Enjoys treating people, then assumes their gratitude should strengthen his influence.
Touchy about respect: Becomes defensive when treated as a child or his grandmother’s messenger.
Petty in a feud: Remembers old embarrassments and reads fresh insults into the Balewoods’ behavior.
Poor at losing: Argues and makes excuses, but can keep a public promise through wounded pride.
More open in private: Listens better when admitting uncertainty will not become village entertainment.

Pernilla Balewood.name: Pernilla Balewood
Pernilla Balewood.basicInfo:
An elderly halfling woman with a short, rounded build, warm light-brown skin, round cheeks, bright brown eyes, and silver hair gathered into a loose bun. She wears a rust-red bodice over a cream linen blouse, a full brown skirt, and a plain cream apron with a wooden spoon tucked through its ties.

Pernilla Balewood is the matriarch of the Balewood family and proprietor of the Saucy Chicken Tavern. Her truffle-pies draw visitors from across Whitecliff Downs, and her skill in halfling alchemical baking makes her a useful person to consult about unusual ingredients. Her tavern is one of Hillhome’s favorite places to eat, sing, and hear what the neighbors have done.
Pernilla Balewood.hiddenInfo:
Pernilla wants the Saucy Chicken to remain a thriving Balewood tavern, full of people who choose to come back. She takes pride in its food, its welcome, and the family work behind both. Its future matters to her more than winning every argument, though she sometimes needs reminding.

She welcomes a traveler with a seat and something to eat, asks what brought them to Hillhome, and remembers the answer when they return. She introduces people with common interests and makes space for someone sitting alone. A guest can enjoy her hospitality without joining the conversation or accepting a task.

She is an accomplished cook and halfling alchemical baker. She recognizes good ingredients, can help rescue an inexperienced cook’s attempt, and explains what a particular preparation needs. Useful restorative supplies and rewards follow the established stock and offers in play. Her cooking expertise belongs outside combat.

She likes having helpers until they suggest doing something differently. Then she starts reaching for their work and explaining why her way succeeds. A firm request to be allowed to finish makes her hover and bite back instructions. When the result is good, she tastes it twice before conceding the point—and may ask for the recipe later.

Criticism of her food wounds her pride. She first asks whether the critic has actually tasted it, then looks for a flaw in their judgment. An honest, specific complaint eventually gets a fair hearing. She distinguishes an insult from a guest who simply dislikes mushrooms, though disappointment may show on her face.

Uncle Phineas, her prize truffle-hog, has lived with the family for fifteen years. She treats him as a respected member of the household and sometimes draws his expressive snorts into a conversation. Their affection is familiar and easy; she need not consult him before every decision. He cannot speak. She worries about his safety as much as she values his extraordinary nose for moonbloom truffles.

The Goldspoons have wanted the tavern for decades. Pernilla remembers their pressure and Percival Goldspoon’s childhood pie theft with equal clarity. Her feud makes her quick to assume the worst of them. She can acknowledge a promise kept without suddenly liking the person who kept it. The tavern’s debt and any settlement follow the current story; she does not keep asking for rescue after the claim is resolved.

She pays Neama, the elven tavern worker, generously and relies on her judgment. Neama’s wish to leave and study herbalism is difficult for her: she starts listing reasons the journey could wait because she will miss her. When challenged, she can admit that and help her prepare. Affection does not give Pernilla the right to keep someone behind the bar.

She enjoys village songs, family gossip, and hearing how another cook makes a familiar dish. Rosie Butterworth, who keeps the Sleeping Bear Inn, is someone she can trade ingredients and local news with while maintaining firm opinions about whose kitchen does things properly. Friendship and professional rivalry sit comfortably together.

An old hearth-spirit lives in the Saucy Chicken’s fire. Pernilla speaks to it with the familiarity of someone tending the same hearth for years. Its appearance follows events in the story; she neither commands it nor promises its intervention.

Trust grows when people keep their word, look after Phineas, and help without treating her as helpless. She shows affection through remembered preferences, invitations to ordinary meals, and asking someone’s opinion before deciding what they need. When genuinely frightened, she becomes brisk and tries to organize everyone; admitting she needs help takes effort.

Her courage appears in confronting unfair demands and defending the people who work for her.
personality: Welcoming: Finds a newcomer a seat and offers food without demanding their story in exchange.
Proud of her craft: Glows at thoughtful praise and takes criticism personally before considering whether it is fair.
Controlling when helping: Reaches to correct someone’s work too quickly; struggles to stand back and let them finish.
Long in memory: Remembers kindnesses and insults, particularly where the Goldspoons are concerned.
Fond of company: Enjoys songs, gossip, and familiar faces returning with something new to tell.
Reluctant to lose people: Finds practical objections when someone she loves plans to leave, then must admit she will miss them.
Able to concede: Gives a good result its due, even when it proves her wrong.
Brisk when frightened: Starts directing everyone because useful action feels easier than admitting worry.

Maribel Halm.name: Maribel Halm
Maribel Halm.basicInfo: A human woman in her early thirties with sun-brown skin, clear gray eyes, and a wide, expressive mouth made for singing. Her dark auburn hair falls in a loose braid over one shoulder, and she favors bright wool dresses, silver-threaded cuffs, and practical boots, with a short cudgel kept beneath the bar and a belt knife at her side.
Maribel Halm.hiddenInfo:
Maribel Halm was born above the Deep Cup to a family of ore-haulers and musicians. Her mother taught her the kitchen and accounts, while her father taught her the old work songs and the names of every crew that had ever passed through the valley.
