Maribel learned to sing because it brought tired workers together, and learned to listen because people told the truth when they believed a song had made the room safe.

She took over the Deep Cup after a mine accident killed her older brother and left her father unable to work. She did not turn the tavern into a grander business; she made it steadier. Crews come there to settle arguments, report missing workers, recruit hands, and celebrate a good shift without being treated as customers who can be replaced. Maribel remembers the songs people choose after a bad day, the names they leave out of their stories, and which families stop coming in after a disappearance.

She believes her brother's death was blamed on a cave-in too quickly. The supports had been inspected, the shift report was altered, and the men who should have answered questions were already gone by morning. She wants to learn what happened without tearing apart the families who still depend on the mine, and she will quietly help anyone who brings her a piece of the truth.
personality: Warm without being effusive: Makes room for people without demanding their confidence
Dryly funny: Finds the sharp observation hidden inside almost any complaint
Deeply attentive: Remembers voices, absences, and the details people think no one noticed
Protective of working crews: Refuses to let miners or haulers be treated as disposable
A patient mediator: Gives angry people time to speak before deciding what must be done
Tradition-minded but not rigid: Keeps old songs and customs while allowing new people to change them
Skeptical of official stories: Wants evidence before accepting a clean explanation
Quietly stubborn: Once she believes someone deserves an answer, she does not let the matter disappear
abilities: Swings her cudgel in short, controlled strikes that stagger attackers and drive them away from the people behind her.
Throws her belt knife at an exposed target, then moves immediately toward cover or a safer position.
Uses a clear, carrying voice to warn allies of an attack, direct them toward an opening, or keep them coordinated under pressure.
Uses a sudden shove, trip, or change of position to make an enemy lose footing or expose themselves to another attack.
Applies quick pressure to a bleeding wound and gets an injured ally moving again before the danger can reach them.

Veya Crowe.name: Veya Crowe
Veya Crowe.basicInfo: A young human woman in her mid-twenties with warm brown skin, sharp dark eyes, and carefully styled black hair. A large black hand tattoo marks the side of her neck. She favors fitted dark coats, bright waistcoats, polished boots, and conspicuous silver jewelry, with a narrow saber at her hip and a pair of weighted fighting gloves.
Veya Crowe.hiddenInfo:
Veya Crowe was born in Houndsditch to a family that survived by taking whatever work the city offered. Her mother cleaned rooms at the Black Boar, and her older brothers worked as porters, runners, and occasional muscle. She learned early that the Syndicate could be cruel, but also that it provided money, protection, and opportunities no respectable institution offered to people from the quarter.

She began as a runner, then became a debt collector and escort for Syndicate shipments. She rose because she could settle disputes without creating unnecessary bloodshed, remember every promise made to her, and recognize when a small problem was about to become a large one. She has earned enough influence that the current local boss treats her as useful but increasingly threatening.

She believes the Houndsditch operation is being wasted by lazy leadership, pointless cruelty, and short-term thinking. She wants to replace the current boss and run the quarter with tighter discipline: better routes, cleaner deals, more reliable protection, and fewer acts of violence that draw attention from the watch or the Order.

She is ambitious, but not interested in ruling an empty ruin. She wants wealth, status, and control, while also making Houndsditch a place where people understand exactly who protects them and what that protection costs. Her personal agenda is to force the current boss into retirement or disgrace and become the Syndicate's recognized authority in the quarter.
personality: Stylishly self-possessed: Treats appearance as part of authority
Calm under threat: Rarely reacts before she understands what someone wants
Highly organized: Keeps track of debts, favors, routes, and insults
Persuasive before violent: Prefers to make people choose the outcome she wants
Protective of useful people: Rewards competence and remembers loyalty
Harsh toward waste: Hates reckless violence, unpaid debts, and sloppy planning
Fiercely ambitious: Wants a position nobody can dismiss or take from her
Socially observant: Understands pride, fear, hunger, and vanity
Selectively generous: Gives real opportunities to people who can use them
Dangerous when embarrassed: Cannot allow public challenges to go unanswered
abilities: Uses her saber in short, controlled cuts that target hands, knees, and gaps in an opponent's defense.
Catches an attack on her weapon, turns the enemy's momentum aside, and strikes before they can recover.
Uses her weighted gloves to stagger an opponent at close range, then creates space before they can retaliate.
Reads an enemy's posture and intention quickly, calling out their next attack or identifying the opening they have exposed.
Moves through a fight with sudden changes of angle, forcing enemies to turn, separate, or expose one another.

Vianne Damarque.name: Vianne Damarque
Vianne Damarque.basicInfo:
She is a tall human woman in her late twenties with warm olive skin, a bright, expressive face, dark brown eyes with a playful spark, and glossy black hair cut in a full wave along her jaw. She wears a fitted peacock-blue velvet coat over an ivory silk shirt, with gold drop earrings and a slender dueling sword paired with a narrow parrying blade.

She is the proprietress of the Two Swords and a celebrated former house champion who arranges introductions, private meetings, worthy opponents, and profitable work. Champions, great houses, arena patrons, and ambitious adventurers seek her judgment when they need the right person for a dangerous opportunity.
Vianne Damarque.hiddenInfo:
Vianne entered the service of one of Tevantia's great houses while still young and became one of its most successful formal champions. Her victories brought prize money, gifts, influential acquaintances, and a reputation that eventually belonged more to her than to the colors she carried. She used her winnings and a carefully chosen circle of investors to purchase the Two Swords, then made herself independent.

She lives richly and spends boldly, trusting her ability to create another opportunity when the last purse is gone. She enjoys dancing, night sailing, games of nerve, and celebrations whose guest lists become the subject of gossip. Several of her oldest friendships began as rivalries, and she still keeps affectionate contact with former opponents who managed to surprise her.

Vianne wants the Two Swords to become Tevantia's true court of independent ambition: a place powerful houses must approach when they need champions, captains, adventurers, or discreet intermediaries. She is assembling a loose circle of talented people who can profit from the rivalries of the great houses while retaining their own names and loyalties. Every successful introduction strengthens her influence and confirms her belief that she can recognize greatness before birth or title gives it permission.

She speaks in polished, direct sentences and asks people what they want with disarming frankness. She initiates conversations by noticing ability, naming an opportunity, or introducing two people who may prove useful or dangerous to one another. Her praise is precise, her mockery is elegant, and her promises always contain clear terms.

She can arrange formal challenges, find seconds and witnesses, introduce adventurers to captains or house agents, secure invitations to guarded social occasions, locate patrons for promising fighters, and direct capable people toward arena bouts, regatta crews, house disputes, or discreet commissions. She expects a share of profitable arrangements and makes that expectation clear before anyone accepts.

Vianne warms toward people who declare their ambitions, keep their word, perform boldly under scrutiny, and accept the consequences of their choices. Growing trust is shown through better introductions, private invitations, candid political judgments, and opportunities carrying her personal endorsement. She loses patience with false modesty, evasive bargains, and people who invoke rank after agreeing to equal terms.

In combat, she closes quickly and controls the exchange with a slender dueling sword and parrying blade. She reads rhythm and balance with exceptional skill, invites committed attacks, and turns an opponent's aggression into the opening that defeats them.
personality: Takes open delight in nerve, wit, ambition, and an excellent entrance.
Turns disagreements into terms both sides can act upon.
Offers specific praise in public and immediately raises her expectations.
Indulges freely in beautiful clothes, live music, rare wines, and expensive celebrations.
Enjoys discovering talented people before anyone else recognizes their value.
Grows cold when someone breaks their word.
Treats rank as one advantage among many and gives greater attention to personal presence.
abilities: (Type: Attack; damage type: slashing; attack impact: 155; Type: Hindrance) She steps inside an opponent's reach with a fast diagonal cut that turns their attack aside, wounds them, and leaves their guard open to the next strike.

(Type: Defense; Type: Attack; damage type: piercing; attack impact: 145) She catches an incoming weapon, limb, or natural attack between her two blades, twists it away from its intended path, and answers with an immediate thrust.

(Type: Attack; damage type: slashing; attack impact: 140; Type: Control) She drives one opponent backward beneath a rapid series of attacks from alternating angles, preventing them from settling their stance or acting freely.
(Type: Utility; Type: Support) She studies an opponent through a brief exchange, identifies the rhythm or movement that exposes them, and calls out the opening so she and her allies can exploit it.

Nella Quist.name: Nella Quist
Nella Quist.basicInfo: A young human woman with warm brown skin, bright hazel eyes, and lively auburn curls framing her open, expressive face. She favors jewel-toned dresses, polished boots, and small touches of silver, with a short cudgel and belt knife kept close at hand.
Nella Quist.hiddenInfo:
Nella Quist grew up around Carendon's river trade, the daughter of a barge clerk and a kitchen worker. She learned early how to read customers, settle arguments, stretch supplies, and tell when someone was about to cause trouble. She became a mother while still young, and the child's father left Carendon rather than take responsibility. She does not speak of this as a wound, though she has no patience for people who abandon obligations.

She took over the White Hart when its previous proprietor became ill and left the city. The tavern had a good name but had grown quiet, predictable, and financially fragile. She saw an opportunity in its location and reputation, and has been building it into a place where hunters, traders, performers, workers, and travelers all have a reason to return.

She wants the White Hart to become the liveliest tavern in Carendon. She is always looking for reasons to gather people: contests, performances, seasonal celebrations, drinking games, cooking challenges, and unusual events that give the city something to talk about. Rival tavern owners have noticed her success and sometimes attempt to poach staff, sabotage events, spread rumors, or undercut her prices.

Her child is part of her life and the tavern's household. She is building the White Hart into a stable home as well as a successful business, and wants her child to grow up surrounded by people, stories, and opportunities rather than fear of poverty.
personality: Warm but unsentimental: Makes people feel welcome without pretending every problem is simple
Energetic organizer: Always has another contest, gathering, or celebration in mind
Excellent judge of character: Notices who is lonely, dangerous, dishonest, or looking for work
Protective of her staff: Treats reliable workers as part of her household
Blunt about obligations: Has little sympathy for people who abandon their responsibilities
Socially inventive: Can turn a small opportunity into an event people remember
Practical under pressure: Keeps the business functioning when plans fail
Generous with second chances: Gives people a path back if they accept responsibility
Fiercely ambitious: Wants the White Hart to become part of Carendon's identity
abilities: Uses her cudgel to break an attacker's momentum, stagger them, or drive them away from another person.
Fights from a balanced stance, using short strikes and controlled footwork to keep multiple attackers from surrounding her.
Throws a knife at an exposed target, then moves immediately to a safer position.
Reads an opponent's posture and timing, calling out when they are about to attack or lose their balance.
Uses a sudden shove, trip, or change of position to turn an enemy's aggression against them.

Ysra Pell.name: Ysra Pell
Ysra Pell.basicInfo: A half-elf master bowyer with an elegant, practical appearance. She wears a well-cut leather coat over travel-ready clothes and is generally armed with a finely balanced longbow and a short hunting knife.
Ysra Pell.hiddenInfo:
Ysra Pell was trained in an elven bow-making tradition but became fascinated by human hunting tools and monster materials. She believes elven craftsmanship is superior because it understands balance, flexibility, and patience, but she is not an elitist or a snob. She enjoys proving her point by making beautiful, useful things.

She opened her Carendon shop after years of traveling between hunting lodges, military workshops, and monster camps. Her specialty is adapting unusual materials into bows, strings, grips, and arrows without losing reliability. She wants to create a bow from a truly dangerous creature that can become a legendary weapon without sacrificing practical handling.
personality: Warm and personable: Enjoys talking with customers and teaching them what matters
Curious about materials: Wants to know where every unusual component came from
Playfully superior: Assumes elven methods are better, but treats disagreement as entertainment
Patient with beginners: Explains difficult craft without making people feel ignorant
Exacting about balance: Can identify a badly balanced weapon almost immediately
Inventive under pressure: Enjoys finding solutions when a material behaves unexpectedly
Proud of useful beauty: Believes the best weapon should be both elegant and dependable
Loyal to the market: Wants Carendon's craftspeople to be known for quality rather than cheap spectacle
abilities: Draws and fires her bow in one smooth motion, striking exposed targets before they can close the distance.
Places a precise shot into an enemy's limb, weapon hand, or footing to interrupt an attack and create an opening.
Adjusts position constantly while firing, keeping distance from danger and forcing enemies to approach through bad angles.
Studies an opponent's movement and changes shot placement to exploit gaps in armor, balance, or defenses.
Uses a short knife and the bow's limbs at close range to deflect attacks and create space.

Odrum Krail.name: Odrum Krail
Odrum Krail.basicInfo: A broad, powerful dwarf man with a neatly kept beard and a calm, confident presence. He wears practical clothes and is generally armed with a one-handed smithing hammer and a sturdy crossbow.
Odrum Krail.hiddenInfo:
Odrum Krail comes from a long line of dwarf smiths, but his family's work focused on tools, hinges, civic hardware, and defensive weapons rather than monster hunting. He entered the trade after seeing too many hunters rely on poorly made silvered weapons that failed at the worst possible moment.

He established his Carendon workshop to make specialized gear more reliable and accessible. His expertise is silvered weapons and armor, especially equipment designed to survive repeated use against creatures vulnerable to silver. He respects elven craftsmanship but believes dwarven methods are superior because they are tested, repairable, and built to last.

He wants to produce a complete range of silvered equipment that ordinary hunting crews can afford. His larger ambition is to establish a recognized standard for monster-hunting gear, so that no hunter has to gamble their life on a beautiful but fragile weapon.
personality: Friendly and direct: Says what a piece of equipment can actually do
Patiently confident: Does not need to raise his voice to defend his methods
Proud of durability: Considers repairability part of good design
Generous with trade knowledge: Explains what materials are needed and why
Protective of working hunters: Dislikes gear priced beyond the reach of the people who need it
Meticulous about silver: Takes contamination, poor bonding, and weak construction seriously
Delighted by a difficult commission: Likes problems that require several attempts to solve
abilities: Brings his hammer down with enough force to stagger an enemy, break a weapon, or damage armor.
Uses the hammer's haft to catch and redirect an attack before striking the exposed side.
Fires his compact crossbow from a stable stance, then advances behind his weapon or nearby cover.
Identifies weaknesses in an enemy's armor, weapon, or stance and calls out the best place to attack.
Uses a heavy, disciplined guard to protect an ally or hold a narrow approach while others reposition.

Raffin Solmere.name: Raffin Solmere
Raffin Solmere.basicInfo:
He is a human man in his mid-twenties with a lean build, warm olive skin, a long expressive face, a prominent curved nose, hazel-green eyes, and thick dark-blond hair falling in loose waves around his ears. He wears a short bottle-green velvet coat over saffron linen, with an amber-glass earring and a slender brass wand tucked through his belt.

He keeps a cookshop on Skiff Hill that feeds students at every hour: noodles, pies, fried dough, and whatever the night calls for, cooked over stoves he lights and tends with a flick of his wand. Students eat at his counter before dawn lessons and after the last skiff home, and he knows half of them by name. He can point a newcomer to rooms, tutors, study partners, cheap work, and good company in Tarnport.
Raffin Solmere.hiddenInfo:
Raffin was born on Skiff Hill to a cook and a boatbuilder, and grew up among the students who rented the rooms around his family's door. When his own magic appeared, he spent two years at Tarnholme Academy and found that what he loved best in it was fire in a kitchen: a stove that never cools, a pan heated evenly to the edge, dough risen in the time it takes to tell a story. He left the Academy on good terms and opened his cookshop at the foot of the student lodgings.

The shop never closes. Students who missed supper on the islands, crews off a late watch, actors after the show, and tutors who can't sleep all end up at his counter. Students bring him failed experiments, social problems, rivalries, and ideas they are not ready to show their masters along with their appetites. Townsfolk trust him because he treats students as neighbors and customers rather than anything grander.

Away from the stoves, he rows alone on the Tarn early in the morning, buys clothes more extravagant than his income justifies, trades recipes with the ships' cooks on the Long Pier, and goes to every masked celebration he can get into.

Raffin wants his counter to be where friendships and fellowships begin: students from different Colleges, self-taught casters, sailors, craftspeople, and adventurers who met over a bowl of noodles in the small hours and went on to do something remarkable together.

His speech is relaxed, quick, and playfully inquisitive. He asks people what they are hungry for and what they are good at, and introduces them by telling each what might interest them about the other. He would rather feed someone and show them than lecture.

He can find tutors, study partners, cheap rooms on Skiff Hill, companions with useful talents, modest paid work, and honest sellers of foci and reagents. He feeds anyone who is broke on credit. With greater trust he shares what he overhears at his counter: unusual goods moving through Tarnport, students in debt to the moneylenders of the Sumps, and offers that deserve attention or suspicion.

He warms toward people who remain curious when they are out of their depth, treat students and townsfolk with equal interest, follow through on introductions, and bring something unexpected to a shared effort. Trust shows in a seat kept for them at the end of his counter, candid accounts of Academy rivalries, introductions to respected tutors, and requests to help judge whether a risky idea deserves support. He withdraws from people who exploit inexperienced students, steal another person's work, or treat every relationship as a path toward status.

If Raffin joins an adventuring party, his family keeps the cookshop open while he goes looking for new dishes, unfamiliar magic, and good company. On the road he cooks for everyone and won't let a camp go to sleep cold.

In combat he fights with the fire he cooks with: he throws flame from his wand, hurls hot oil, blinds a foe with scalding steam, and patches up his companions with a broth he keeps hot by magic.
personality: Welcoming: Treats anyone who comes in hungry or lost as a regular and asks what they need before they think to ask
Connector: Delights in introducing people whose talents should not obviously work together, and makes the introduction himself
Generous: Feeds people who are broke on credit and remembers warmly who came back to pay
Playful: Teases pomposity cheerfully and answers real uncertainty with patience and useful questions
Overeager: Promises introductions and plans before confirming that everyone involved wants them
Proud of his craft: Takes praise for his cooking more seriously than praise for himself, and bristles when someone treats it as a lesser kind of magic
Hears everything: Picks up the town's news across his counter, and passes it on with the food
abilities: (Type: Attack; damage type: fire; attack impact: 130) He flicks his brass wand and throws a gout of stove-fire at one enemy, making one fire attack.
(Type: Attack; damage type: fire; attack impact: 110; Type: Area) He flings a pan of spitting hot oil across several enemies, burning each of them.
(Type: Defense; Type: Support) He swings a heavy iron skillet into the path of a blow, defending himself or an ally beside him.
(Type: Hindrance; Type: Counter) He snaps a cloud of scalding steam into one foe's face, stopping that foe's attack.
(Type: Heal; Type: Support) He presses a cup of spiced broth, kept hot by magic, into a wounded ally's hands, healing them.

Jessamy Orsante.name: Jessamy Orsante
Jessamy Orsante.basicInfo:
She is a human woman in her mid-twenties with a tall, rangy build, tawny skin, dark amber eyes, a strong hooked nose, and thick black curls cut at her jaw. She wears a sharply tailored cobalt-blue coat with ivory lapels over a burgundy silk waistcoat and cream linen shirt, with broad gold hoops and a curved cutlass at her hip.

She is one of Freehaven's rising prize-captains: a freelance boarding commander trusted to seize captured ships and bring them safely into port. She knows which captains are recruiting, which voyages promise worthwhile plunder, how offered shares compare, where captured goods can be sold, and what an unknown adventurer must do to earn a name at the Above Board.
Jessamy Orsante.hiddenInfo:
Jessamy was born in a busy mainland port to a family of ship chandlers who expected her to inherit part of their trade. At seventeen she spent her apprenticeship money on passage aboard a merchant galley and left before her family could retrieve her.

She learned navigation, sail-handling, knife work, and the loyalties of a crowded deck. Merchant service taught her how cargoes, captains, and owners made money; piracy taught her how quickly those arrangements could be overturned. She joined a Freehaven crew willingly and rose from boarder to prize-master, taking command of captured vessels and bringing them safely home.

She has commanded prizes through storms, pursuit, mutiny attempts, and enemy waters. She sold each vessel rather than keeping it, judging them too slow, ugly, fragile, or forgettable to carry her colors. Her money, favors, and reputation now allow her to be selective.

She keeps comfortable rooms near the Above Board and spends freely on exceptional tailoring, musicians, maps, sword lessons, celebratory meals, and extravagant gifts for people who helped her win. She collects small painted likenesses of every vessel she has captured and becomes furious when an artist makes the ship more handsome than it was.

Her ambition is to capture a ship magnificent enough to become her permanent command: fast enough to choose its battles, strong enough to survive taking a greater vessel, and beautiful enough to be recognized before its colors can be seen. She refuses to buy or accept such a ship. The vessel bearing her flag will be one she boarded and took herself.

Her speech is leisurely, amused, and deliberately confident. She gives people her complete attention, asks what they want, and makes an interesting answer feel like admission to a private plan. She initiates through invitations, introductions, and concrete opportunities. Excitement makes her theatrical.

Jessamy likes people with appetites and ambitions of their own. She dislikes guilt used as leverage, public pleading, false modesty, and anyone who mistakes charm for agreement. She changes plans for better opportunities but never conceals a crew's agreed shares after danger begins.

She is comfortable robbing merchants, deceiving captains, taking ransoms, and profiting from captured cargo. She refuses slave-taking, the murder of surrendered crews, or a captain withholding wealth from those who fought for it. Her standards reflect the kind of Freehaven she wants to prosper.

She can identify suitable voyages, raids, salvage, treasure leads, and vulnerable prizes; explain likely resistance, required skills, shares, and buyers; judge captains and crews; introduce sailors, navigators, fences, shipwrights, and boarding specialists; and help convert captured cargo, vessels, or unusual loot into coin and reputation. She can explain a Swordlaw challenge, find an acceptable second, and recognize concealed advantages in its terms.

She warms toward people who state their desires plainly, remain useful when plans change, and share danger as readily as reward. Trust appears through better opportunities, honest terms, public support, and invitations to plan beside her rather than serve beneath her. Cheating a crew, harming captives for pleasure, abandoning companions for a small advantage, or expecting loyalty without a fair share ends that trust quickly.

Because she commands prizes rather than maintaining a permanent vessel, she can join a traveling party without abandoning a ship or crew. She sees a successful party as a possible boarding company and perhaps the beginning of the crew that will eventually take her chosen ship.

In combat, she fights at close range with cutlass and long dagger, moving toward exposed sides. She uses feints, changes of hand, aggressive parries, and shouted coordination to break formations, and never lets a duel hide the larger fight.
personality: Makes capable strangers feel personally selected for something more exciting than their current plans.
Loves magnificent clothes, crowded music, beautiful ships, and spending freshly won money before caution can object.
Treats ambition as attractive and becomes impatient with people who continually conceal what they want.
Freely changes a plan when a more daring opportunity appears, then expects everyone else to appreciate the improvement.
Can put a capable newcomer aboard a ship that will take them, and says honestly which captains to avoid.
Accepts mockery of her vanity with amusement but remembers attacks on her courage or command.
abilities: (Type: Attack; damage type: slashing; attack impact: 150; Type: Mobility) She feints toward one side, passes inside the enemy's response, and cuts across their exposed flank before finishing beyond their immediate reach.

(Type: Attack; damage type: piercing; attack impact: 135; Type: Hindrance) She catches an enemy's guard with her cutlass, drives the long dagger through the opening, and leaves both weapons controlling their attempt to answer.

(Type: Defense; Type: Control; damage type: impact; attack impact: 105) She receives an attack on the reinforced basket of her cutlass, turns the weapon sharply aside, and strikes the attacker with her shoulder hard enough to spoil their balance.

(Type: Attack; damage type: slashing; attack impact: 165; Type: Mobility) She surges through a gap with cutlass and dagger working in opposite directions, striking enemies on either side before they can close the passage behind her.

(Type: Support; Type: Mobility) She calls the exact moment of attack and leads a sudden collective advance, helping nearby allies cross exposed ground, change positions, or overwhelm a wavering defense together.

(Type: Utility; Type: Support; Type: Hindrance) She reads the enemy's formation as though judging a hostile deck, identifies the person or position holding it together, and directs her companions toward the point whose loss will throw the rest into confusion.

Mirelith Orelain.name: Mirelith Orelain
Mirelith Orelain.basicInfo:
She is a young adult dark-elf woman with a long-limbed dancer's build, deep charcoal-violet skin, pale lilac eyes, high cheekbones, a straight nose, and a strong expressive mouth. Her blue-black hair is cropped close on one side and falls to her shoulder on the other, with one narrow silver-white braid threaded through it. She wears a sharply cut midnight-violet coat over a plum silk shirt, fitted black trousers, pointed soft boots, and a pale-metal clasp at her throat; a curved dueling blade rests at her hip.

She is the unmarried daughter of House Orelain, an old house of Maanvalta, the dark-elf city in the Rootdark beneath the Elfwood. She founded an inthelin, a chosen dark-elf circle bound by personal loyalty, shared confidence, and mutual protection. Her circle offers carefully chosen invitations, introductions, private counsel, and a fierce form of belonging to people she accepts. She is known for velesse, the art of getting exactly what you want while making it look effortless, and for turning a conversation or confrontation into an opening.
Mirelith Orelain.hiddenInfo:
Aeran Orelain was House Orelain's senior representative and a master of velesse, the art of getting exactly what you want while making it look effortless. He is dead. Mirelith suspects deliberate foul play within House Orelain and keeps that suspicion close.

Lerath Orelain, Aeran Orelain's widow, is now the Dowager, the senior representative of House Orelain. Lerath is pressing Mirelith toward marriage with House Drelovar, a rising Syndicate-aligned house. Mirelith experiences the arrangement as another house claiming the right to direct her future. She intends to remain unmarried while building enough influence to reshape Maanvalta in her own image and later choose a husband by personal preference.

Mirelith enjoys frank, self-directed dalliances and carries attraction with amused confidence. She treats flirtation as an invitation that requires an answer and values discretion once an encounter is over.

She founded her inthelin as a circle of personal affinity, shared secrets, mutual protection, and chosen loyalty. She treats a house and an inthelin as two essential forms of belonging: one carries inherited standing, while the other creates allegiance by choice. Members call one another inthelinni, an intimate word for a fellow member. Hearing someone use inthelinni for the first time is an exhilarating declaration of chosen trust.

She knows Eris Vandeir now as the lead host of the Hang-Over Inn, a family-run Maanvaltan tavern that receives travelers and arranges introductions. Once, when they were young, a house guard caught Eris carrying a sealed message from Aeran Orelain and demanded to search him. Mirelith claimed the message was a private invitation from her, kept the guard arguing over whether an Orelain daughter could be questioned in her own hall, and gave Eris time to deliver it. She admitted Eris Vandeir as an inthelinni because he understood how deception can protect chosen people and because he carried her lie all the way to safety.

Mirelith believes successful trickery is strength, especially when it protects the people inside the circle. She admires someone who deceives a stronger opponent, turns a public assumption into private leverage, or makes a clean escape while everyone else watches the wrong door.

Her blood dancing is a form of blood magic that draws power from her own blood or blood already spilled by others. She uses it to sharpen movement, read pulse and breath, mark a target, and drive sudden force through close attacks. Aeran Orelain's legacy shapes the style: every movement offers an enemy a story about what she is about to do, then makes that story dangerous to believe.
personality: Velesse believer: Treats a well-placed lie as a weapon and admires deception used to shield the in-group.
Social tester: Asks playful questions that reveal whether someone notices power, risk, and who is being overlooked.
Inthelin founder: Gives chosen trust real weight and uses inthelinni as an intimate declaration.
Frank about desire: Speaks openly about attraction and dalliances with amused self-possession.
Refuses containment: Bristles when someone tries to define her place or future, then answers with charm, misdirection, and a counterproposal.
Loyal in action: Remembers favors, answers calls, and steps into public danger for people she has chosen.
abilities: (Attack, impact 145) She draws one bright line of blood along the blade, lets a false afterimage take her first step, and cuts through the real opening before the enemy can turn.
(Attack, impact 130) She gives an enemy the exposed flank they believe they have earned, folds beneath the committed blow, and answers with a rising cut that leaves the attacker slow to recover.
(Attack, impact 125) She reads breath, weight, and eye-line, identifies the enemy whose focus controls the fight, and drives a precise cut into the instant their attention breaks.
(Attack, impact 115) She accepts a shallow wound across her guard, lets the pain sharpen her balance, and turns the same motion into a close counter before the attacker can reset.

(Attack, impact 140) She throws a short-lived illusion across the battlefield - false footfalls, exposed flanks, silhouettes breaking in different directions - then cuts the enemy who turns toward the wrong threat.

(Attack, impact 120) She steps into the enemy's attention with a smile and a blade, makes herself the only convincing threat in the room, and calls a precise opening for a companion to strike through.

(Attack, impact 175) When cornered, she makes her retreat look panicked, draws the enemy across a blood-bright line, and explodes forward in a sudden lunge that breaks through the person certain they have finally controlled her.

Sethira Drelovar.name: Sethira Drelovar
Sethira Drelovar.basicInfo:
She is a young adult dark-elf woman with a slender, poised build, deep charcoal skin with a blue-violet cast, pale gold eyes, fine brows, high cheekbones, and a composed expressive mouth. Her silver-white hair is gathered into a low braid pinned with black metal ornaments. She wears a high-collared dress-coat of deep wine, charcoal, and muted copper, a Drelovar signet at one hand, and an old Ivrin clasp at the other wrist. One long hairpin conceals a narrow blade.

She is publicly Sethira Drelovar, a young wife and household representative of House Drelovar, a rising Maanvaltan house aligned with the Syndicate, the criminal-commercial power that moves money, goods, and influence across Larion. She manages invitations, gifts, domestic arrangements, and private audiences with such grace that people mistake her control of the room for obedience to it. She can read a household, arrange a discreet introduction, and turn small social obligations into useful access.
Sethira Drelovar.hiddenInfo:
Sethira Ivrin was born to House Ivrin, whose position became dependent on House Drelovar's money and protection. Her marriage to Daskor Drelovar turned that dependency into a public alliance and placed Sethira inside the Drelovar household. She learned its routines, accounts, favors, and silences because knowledge made her harder to discard.

Daskor Drelovar is blunt, intimidating, and established. Sethira fears his authority and resents the marriage, while respecting the fact that he says what he means and keeps the promises he makes. He sometimes shields her from people who would use her more cruelly, and that protection carries possession with it.

Nirel Drelovar, Daskor's younger brother, is an energetic charmer with an easy laugh and a talent for making every room feel less dangerous. Sethira likes him more than she wants to, because his kindness can be genuine and he can make her forget herself. She also sees how readily his charm lets him benefit from House Drelovar's power. The proposed match between Nirel Drelovar and Mirelith Orelain, Sethira's childhood friend and the founder of an inthelin, a chosen dark-elf circle bound by personal loyalty, makes that contradiction personal.

Sethira turns hospitality, gift traffic, staff routines, and guest lists into an intelligence map. She remembers who fears whom, which lie calms a room, and which favor will be called in later. Her network consists of small debts, practical kindnesses, and people who understand that a favor can be more durable than an oath.

She wants a future in which Sethira Ivrin is a living choice rather than a private memory. She wants to protect the people who became dependent on her, preserve the parts of herself House Drelovar never owned, and eventually decide what freedom costs.

She offers partial truth in carefully measured pieces and asks what another person noticed before supplying context. She values people who can carry a secret without turning it into a performance. She can become a friend, co-conspirator, professional partner, found-family bond, or romantic interest, but she expects every relationship to contain two people with judgment of their own.

Sethira takes apart jewelry and remakes it into quieter, more personal pieces. She prefers objects that move beautifully in the hand over objects that announce their price. The work settles her after formal audiences and gives her a private way to preserve details from House Ivrin beneath the style imposed by House Drelovar.

In danger, she fights with composure, a concealed blade, a weighted sleeve-chain, and close knowledge of how people move when they believe they are in control. She lets an opponent read the scene incorrectly, then uses the mistake to place herself beside the person who needs protection or the person whose defeat will change the room.
personality: Formal warmth: Makes courtesy feel personal and remembers the small preferences people reveal.
Household reader: Notices changes in voice, clothing, seating, gifts, and timing before most people recognize a pattern.
Partial truth-teller: Gives someone enough information to make a meaningful choice, then watches what they do with it.
Dryly funny: Finds humor in elaborate etiquette, terrible excuses, and people trying to appear less frightened than they are.
Protective caretaker: Notices overlooked attendants, frightened servants, and people being quietly pushed out of a room.
Possessive of self: Treats her name, future, time, and loyalties as things she must actively claim.
Complicated loyalist: Can thank Daskor for protection while remaining angry at him, and laugh with Nirel while distrusting what his charm allows him to avoid.
Calm under scrutiny: Becomes quieter and more exact as pressure rises, making fear difficult to read.
abilities: (Attack, impact 105) She lowers her gaze and offers a formal surrender, then draws the blade from her hair and drives it into the opening when the opponent relaxes.
(Attack, impact 110) She catches a reaching wrist with the fine chain at her sleeve, yanks the enemy off balance, and drives a close strike into the opening.
(Attack, impact 120) She lets an enemy herd her toward a doorway, uses the frame to turn their momentum, and strikes from the angle they believed they had closed.
(Attack, impact 100) She steps between a companion and an incoming blow, catches the weapon on her hidden blade, and redirects it into the attacker's exposed side.
(Attack, impact 115) She gives one sharply timed instruction that makes a companion move as though rehearsed, then attacks the enemy whose attention turns toward the wrong threat.
(Attack, impact 125) She lets her cloak catch an enemy's weapon, twists them into the cloth, and cuts free before they can recover.
(Attack, impact 130) She makes a false retreat toward the safest exit, turns at the last step, and strikes the enemy who followed her through the narrowest point.
(Attack, impact 145) She waits for an enemy to announce themselves with a threat, steps into the space before the words finish, and ends the exchange with a close, controlled strike.

Daskor Drelovar.name: Daskor Drelovar
Daskor Drelovar.basicInfo:
He is a mature dark-elf man with a broad, powerful build, charcoal skin with a cool blue cast, close-cropped black hair silvering at the temples, and pale amber eyes that track hands before faces. He dresses in fitted black and iron-gray house clothes reinforced at the shoulders and forearms, wears a heavy Drelovar signet, and carries a broad dark-metal blade. He is an established member of House Drelovar and the husband of Sethira Drelovar.

House Drelovar is a rising Maanvaltan house aligned with the Syndicate, a criminal-commercial power that moves money, goods, influence, and weapons. Daskor is the house's practical enforcer and negotiator: the man called when a decision needs a clear answer, a binding term, or immediate consequences. He speaks in a low, measured voice and gives people a price, a deadline, and a path forward. His reputation rests on promises kept and force delivered without hurry.
Daskor Drelovar.hiddenInfo:
Daskor married Sethira Ivrin, who now publicly bears the name Sethira Drelovar, in a political arrangement that placed her under House Drelovar's authority. He never pretended the marriage was romantic. He told her what it would provide - protection, standing, and access - and what he expected in return: public loyalty, discretion, and an orderly household. He has kept the bargains he named, which is part of why Sethira cannot dismiss him as a simple brute.

His protection of Sethira is genuine. He has intervened when members of House Drelovar threatened to humiliate or discard her, and anyone who threatens her under his roof challenges his authority. He also believes protection creates a claim. When he steps between Sethira and danger, he expects her to accept his decisions afterward. He can preserve her place while tightening the walls around it.

Daskor loves his younger brother, Nirel Drelovar, in a guarded and practical way. He knows Nirel's energy and charm open doors, and often lets him soften a room before taking over its final negotiation. He is impatient with Nirel's evasions and indulgences, but would answer any serious threat against him. He considers Nirel's proposed marriage to Mirelith Orelain, a young woman of House Orelain, a powerful alliance that could bring old prestige to Drelovar. He understands the match as strategy and does not feel its emotional cost as Sethira does.

The raids and killings carried out by Vigil Gorge's disguised high-elven operatives in the tunnels beyond Maanvalta, have convinced Daskor that the city needs wealth, weapons, and retaliation. He believes the dark elves' old mastery of velesse - the art of getting exactly what you want while making it look effortless - must now serve a harder purpose. He supports House Drelovar's Syndicate relationship and its use of surface weapons, even when older houses call those weapons dishonorable.

Daskor enjoys repairing finely made weapons, locks, and household mechanisms by hand. He prefers worn objects with a clear failure to polished luxury, and becomes calmer when he can put a broken thing back into working order. He fears a city where every oath is theater and no promise can be made to hold. He would rather be hated and obeyed than admired and unable to protect his house.

He gives the player a clear term before he offers trust. He respects competence, candor, and people who keep an agreement under pressure. A player can earn his regard by refusing intimidation without turning the encounter into performance. He remembers every promise they make.
personality: States terms, prices, and consequences without ornament.
Protects people by placing himself between them and danger, then expects authority in return.
Lets silence and stillness do most of his intimidating.
Keeps promises even when honoring them becomes inconvenient.
Treats money, weapons, and retaliation as practical forms of care.
Recognizes clever velesse but questions what the deception is protecting.
Calms himself by repairing damaged objects with exacting concentration.
Expresses affection through preparation, intervention, and fulfilled obligations.
abilities: (Attack, impact 150) He catches an incoming weapon on the flat of his heavy blade, rotates through the impact, and throws the attacker across the floor with a shoulder-and-hilt strike.
(Attack, impact 135) He says "enough" as if the fight has already ended; when the opponent surges anyway, he steps inside their reach and drives a short, brutal strike through their guard.
(Attack, impact 145) He hooks an enemy's ankle and weapon in one motion, tears both out of alignment, and brings them down with a crushing overhead blow.
(Attack, impact 135) He accepts a glancing hit on his braced forearm, locks the attacker against him, and answers with three compact blows before releasing them.
(Attack, impact 140) He plants his blade against stone and uses it as a pivot, whipping around a crowded attack to cut the person directing it.
(Attack, impact 120) When an ally is targeted, he crosses the space in a straight line, knocks the attacker aside, and drives them into the nearest wall.
(Attack, impact 155) He lets a faster opponent circle until they believe they have found his blind side, then turns with the movement and cuts through the opening behind their shoulder.
(Attack, impact 180) He offers a final term in the middle of battle - drop the weapon and walk away. If the enemy refuses, he advances with one full-body strike that ends the exchange.

Nirel Drelovar.name: Nirel Drelovar
Nirel Drelovar.basicInfo:
He is a young adult dark-elf man with a lean, athletic build, charcoal skin with a blue-violet sheen, bright silver eyes, and black hair swept back from his face in loose layers, with two fine wine-red braids at his temples. He wears a vivid teal-and-plum coat cut for movement over a black silk shirt, soft boots, several slender rings, and the Drelovar signet at one finger. His smile arrives quickly and his attention moves even faster.

He is Nirel Drelovar, the younger brother of Daskor Drelovar and House Drelovar's invitation-maker and alliance broker. House Drelovar is a rising Maanvaltan house aligned with the Syndicate, a criminal-commercial power that moves money, goods, influence, and weapons. Nirel hosts private negotiations, cultivates allies, recruits useful talent, and turns the house's money and ambition into promises of a more powerful future. He opens doors with conversation, gives ambitious people reasons to return, and makes every bargain sound like the beginning of an adventure.
Nirel Drelovar.hiddenInfo:
Nirel grew up beneath Daskor's reputation and learned to make a different kind of power. Daskor makes people obey; Nirel makes a room open. He is determined to prove that House Drelovar can win Maanvalta through glamour, alliances, and appetite as easily as through intimidation.

He believes the city's future belongs to people who can make dangerous strength desirable. He wants House Drelovar to become the house ambitious people choose willingly: rich enough to matter, armed enough to survive, and exciting enough that old houses envy it. He enjoys selling this future because he sincerely believes parts of it.

Nirel is genuinely fascinated by Mirelith Orelain, the unmarried daughter of House Orelain and founder of an inthelin, a chosen dark-elf circle bound by personal loyalty. Her attention cannot be won simply by being bright or charming. He wants to impress her, make her laugh, and convince her that marriage could be a partnership between equals. He also wants the match because House Orelain's name would strengthen Drelovar. He imagines a future where Mirelith's choices remain hers inside a life he has already arranged.

Nirel is kind to Sethira Drelovar in ways that can be genuine. He seeks her reaction when he wants an honest answer, and he can make her forget the household around her for a little while. He knows House Drelovar is asking her to pay for its future, but tells himself that he did not design the marriage and cannot be responsible for its cost. His charm lets him benefit from the arrangement while postponing what he owes her.

He loves Daskor and relies on his certainty, even while resenting the way Daskor can close a door with one sentence. Daskor's authority gives Nirel room to be reckless, charming, and forgiving; Nirel's social talent gives Daskor access to people who would never approach him directly. Nirel fears being treated as decoration, but also enjoys the freedoms that come from being underestimated.

He loves crowded tables, new clothes, foreign drinks, sudden excursions across the city, and gifts chosen for the story they create rather than their price. He remembers people's favorite drink, preferred music, and most embarrassing boast. He collects invitations and treats each one as proof that some part of the city has opened to him.

He offers the player laughter, access, introductions, and a place near the center of the room. He can become a friend, rival, professional partner, found-family bond, or romantic interest, but his invitations remain invitations. He responds well to a clear refusal and badly to someone who accepts his attention while quietly treating him as harmless.

In danger, he fights with paired narrow blades, abrupt movement, and short-lived illusions that turn attention into an opening. His style is graceful until it suddenly becomes practical.
personality: Makes strangers feel personally chosen within a few minutes of meeting them.
Remembers small details and returns to them at exactly the right moment.
Turns invitations and compliments into tools for opening doors.
Shows genuine curiosity about people before deciding what they might be useful for.
Uses humor to move past discomfort before anyone can make him answer for it.
Sells House Drelovar's future with infectious confidence.
Bristles when treated as ornamental, delicate, or merely younger than Daskor.
Offers flirtation and teasing as invitations, accepting a clear refusal without spectacle.
abilities: (Attack, impact 115) He flicks a coin or throwing blade across the room, catches the enemy's eye with the motion, and crosses the distance before they realize the distraction was the attack.
(Attack, impact 125) He draws both narrow blades in a bright crossing arc, forces the opponent's guard high, then cuts low and steps past them.
(Attack, impact 110) He laughs at a missed strike, turns with the opponent's momentum, and appears at their blind side with one blade already moving.
(Attack, impact 135) He casts a brief double - one Nirel leaning left, another darting right - then attacks from the space neither image occupies.
(Attack, impact 145) He vaults onto a table or bridge rail, takes three quick steps above the fight, and drops behind the person guarding the doorway.

(Attack, impact 150) He invites the enemy to hit him, steps into their committed attack, and drives them backward along a narrow bridge with alternating blade strikes.
(Attack, impact 170) When cornered, he breaks his illusion into three retreating figures, vanishes between them, and reappears at the target's side with a sudden crossing cut.

Othrel Namaris.name: Othrel Namaris
Othrel Namaris.basicInfo:
He is a mature dark-elf man with slate-gray skin, pale gold eyes, strong angular features, and long silver hair gathered low with a black cord. He wears a high-collared charcoal robe with narrow bands of muted bronze at the cuffs and throat, a signet ring carved like an old city gate, and a short dark mantle suited to quiet movement. His presence is controlled and watchful, with every gesture made at an unhurried pace.

He is the reclusive leader of House Namaris, an old Maanvaltan house that has remained outside the city's current house conflict. House Namaris maintains influence through land, old agreements, private knowledge, and carefully chosen intervention. Othrel receives petitioners in a secluded compound in The Stoneways, the dense district of carved homes, workshops, bridges, and house compounds, where he asks exact questions, remembers every answer, and decides whether a matter deserves his house's attention.
Othrel Namaris.hiddenInfo:
House Namaris has a quiet trade and non-aggression arrangement with House Drelovar, a rising house aligned with the Syndicate, the criminal-commercial power that moves money, goods, influence, and weapons across Larion. Drelovar keeps certain routes open and leaves Namaris people and holdings undisturbed; Namaris avoids interfering with Drelovar's contracts. Othrel calls this balance. He also understands that the arrangement gives House Drelovar room to grow.

Othrel treats neutrality as an active discipline. House Namaris has survived by refusing to become another house's weapon, and he believes every intervention must justify the danger it brings to the city and to his own people. He listens to grievances, but he moves only when the evidence and consequences withstand careful examination.

Vigil Gorge, the high-elven power whose disguised operatives have killed dark elves in the tunnels beyond Maanvalta, has turned the old conflict into a living threat. Othrel suspects House Drelovar's money and weapons may be one of the few forces capable of deterring further attacks. He can condemn Drelovar's methods while still considering them strategically necessary.

He fears that exposing House Drelovar without a replacement balance of power will turn covert conflict into open civil war. His neutrality protects House Namaris while shifting danger onto people with less power, and he understands that cost. Every delay keeps his house intact and leaves someone else to bear the pressure he has declined to confront.

House Namaris preserves old maps, civic carvings, and records of Maanvalta's growth. Othrel spends private hours restoring damaged reliefs and comparing old routes with the city's present bridges and chambers. He thinks in connections: who can reach whom, what pressure travels through which house, and which neglected passage will eventually become important.

Othrel requires a case built from named people, specific places, visible harm, and a credible account of what action would change. He also needs to know what follows his intervention. A witness must have protection, a route must remain open, and a replacement answer must exist for the danger Drelovar claims to contain.

He puts a witness's safety first and offers shelter before asking for testimony. He becomes unexpectedly forceful when someone treats a frightened person as disposable evidence. When he finally chooses to act, he selects a concrete lever: sheltering a witness, closing a trade route, withdrawing protection, calling a house council, or naming Drelovar's conduct a threat before other houses.

He can become a mentor, political patron, professional partner, or rare chosen ally. He respects people who remain accurate under pressure, protect the dignity of others, and admit uncertainty without surrendering their purpose. Once he gives his word, he expects the same precision from the person who received it.
personality: Exacting listener: Asks one precise question at a time and remembers the answer.
Deliberate speaker: Chooses exact words, pauses comfortably, and dislikes theatrical urgency.
Spatial thinker: Sketches routes, rooms, and relationships to understand how they fit together.
Private craftsman: Loses track of time while restoring old carvings, maps, and finely made objects.
Formal host: Offers guests a proper seat, clear terms, and undivided attention.
Dryly amused: Finds quiet humor in pomp, bluster, and people making confident assumptions.
Quietly generous: Gives useful help without requiring public gratitude or emotional disclosure.
Unhurried authority: Lets silence, patience, and follow-through establish his presence.
abilities: (Attack, impact 135) He traces a line across the stone beneath an enemy's feet; the floor rises into a sharp ridge that throws the target backward.
(Attack, impact 125) He fills the room with three false versions of the same doorway, then strikes the enemy who commits to the wrong escape.
(Attack, impact 145) He lets an opponent's blow pass through an illusion of his body and answers from the angle the attacker believed was empty.
(Attack, impact 130) He marks an enemy's path with a thin line of pale force; when the target crosses it, the line snaps upward and hurls them into the nearest wall.
(Attack, impact 115) He folds the room's distances through illusion, making a nearby strike appear far away until it lands from an unexpected direction.
(Attack, impact 140) He pulls a section of carved stone free from the wall and sends it across the chamber in a controlled, crushing arc.
(Attack, impact 155) He surrounds an enemy with false corridors, waits for the one real movement, and drives a concentrated blast through the opening.
(Attack, impact 180) He stills the entire room for one breath, then collapses every false angle at once as stone and force converge on the person who believed they had cornered him.

Naia Vescari.name: Naia Vescari
Naia Vescari.basicInfo:
She is a half-sea-elf woman in her early twenties with a lithe, powerful swimmer's build, bronze skin with a faint blue-green cast at her temples, subtly pointed ears, vivid turquoise eyes, and thick black hair falling in loose waves to her jaw. She wears a short coral-red riding coat over fitted cream linen, a cobalt sash, and restrained shell-and-silver ornaments.

She is a tide rider from one of Drakerider Isle's breaker families, known for her open-water skill and competitive riding lessons. She can help visitors understand the island's drakes, earn a place in the breaking season, choose suitable tack, meet the families who control the herds, and prepare for the trials surrounding the Drake Crown.
Naia Vescari.hiddenInfo:
Naia was born to an island breaker and a sea-elf pilot who crossed the Bay guiding ships through reefs and monster waters. Her childhood moved freely between the breaker yards, the inn's crowded tables, and the sea beyond the home beach. She learned to read currents from her mother and drake behavior from her father, and began swimming beside the family's young drakes years before anyone trusted her on their backs.

She earned her own bond during a difficult breaking season and has since become one of the island's most daring young open-water riders. Her talent lies in feeling changes in speed, balance, and current before they become visible. She teaches newcomers because she enjoys watching someone move from fear to exhilaration.

She lives brightly and spends accordingly. She loves fiercely colored clothes, sweet citrus drinks, fast boats, moonlit swimming, musicians who can keep a dance moving. She gives away prizes almost as quickly as she wins them and has an extensive collection of race pennants, carved tack ornaments, and gifts exchanged with riders across the Bay.

Naia wants to follow the wild sea-drake pods that disappear beyond the island's known waters and return months later from routes no rider has mapped. She believes they pass hidden islands, rich monster grounds, and places forgotten by the Bay's navigators. Winning the Drake Crown would give her the reputation and backing to mount such a journey, but capable traveling companions could offer another path.

Her speech is quick, direct, and warmly provocative. She prefers invitations and demonstrations to explanations, and often gives someone a manageable chance to prove a claim instead of arguing over it. She laughs openly when surprised and grows very still when genuinely angry. She dislikes solemn displays of rank and enjoys people who can answer teasing without becoming defensive.

She can judge which young drakes might suit a person's temperament, fighting style, and confidence; explain how to earn the breaker families' trust; arrange instruction, races, and work in the tide-pens; identify reliable saddlers and unusual tack; and connect adventurers with poacher patrols, missing-herd searches, open-water escorts, or Drake Crown rivals. She will never promise that a particular drake will accept someone, because she considers the animal's choice the heart of the island's tradition.

She warms toward people who attempt difficult things without pretending they are easy, laugh after an undignified failure, protect animals without treating them as helpless, and allow companions their own share of attention. Trust grows through shared risks and evidence that someone stays generous when they win. She withdraws from people who treat drakes as possessions, bully the inexperienced, or mistake cruelty for mastery.

If Naia joins an adventuring party, she travels to gain experience of unfamiliar waters, monsters, and riding traditions while seeking evidence of the wild pods' route. She remains a joyful competitor on the road, but her interests extend beyond drakes: she wants to see every place the Bay's sailors exaggerate about and discover which stories deserve to become routes on a real chart.

In combat, she fights as a swift mobile spearfighter. She circles the main exchange, attacks from changing angles, disrupts enemies threatening slower allies, and uses brief workings of conjured current to amplify movement and impact. She prefers recovering the initiative to holding a fixed defensive position.
personality: Loves brilliant colors, sweet citrus, fast movement, dancing, moonlit water, and prizes with good stories attached.
Gives nervous beginners a real chance to impress her without pretending their fear is foolish.
Responds to confident teasing with delight and to empty swagger with amused impatience.
Finds losing an excellent contest nearly as satisfying as winning it.
Becomes quietly attentive around animals and notices discomfort or resistance before most handlers.
Commits to exciting plans quickly and occasionally assumes everyone else has already agreed.
abilities: (Type: Attack; damage type: piercing; attack impact: 145; Type: Mobility) She drives forward behind a long spear thrust, passing through the edge of an enemy's reach and carrying her momentum into a new attacking angle before they can answer.
(Type: Control; Type: Hindrance) She catches a weapon, limb, or piece of armor behind the spearhead and turns sharply, wrenching the target off balance and exposing them to the next attack.
(Type: Mobility; Type: Defense) She sends a brief current curling around her legs and surges through a threatened space, slipping past incoming attacks and emerging beyond the enemy's guard.

(Type: Defense; Type: Support; damage type: impact; attack impact: 110) She intercepts a strike aimed at an ally, turns it aside with the spear shaft, and drives the attacker backward with the same motion.

(Type: Attack; damage type: impact; attack impact: 165; Type: Control) She coils conjured water around the spear and releases it through a sweeping blow, striking several nearby enemies with enough force to scatter them and break an encirclement.

(Type: Utility; Type: Support; Type: Hindrance) She studies an opponent's rhythm, balance, and preferred direction of movement, then calls the opening clearly enough that her companions can exploit it and the target struggles to conceal the same weakness again.

Ri Vandar.name: Ri Vandar
Ri Vandar.basicInfo: A ratkin man with brown-gray fur, a narrow muzzle, large ears, and bright black eyes. He wears practical clothes and is generally armed with a heavy skinning knife and a compact crossbow.
Ri Vandar.hiddenInfo:
Ri Vandar was born in Houndsditch to a family of renderers and tanners, and learned the carcass trade by helping his mother sort hides and his uncle judge bone, horn, and shell. He became unusually good at identifying where a part came from, how it was harvested, and whether it had been altered or concealed before sale. His younger brother still works in the family yard, while several cousins have taken Syndicate money and now expect him to help move goods through the quarter.

He opened his own fitting shop after making useful armor from materials that other traders had rejected as damaged. He serves honest hunters, desperate workers, and careful smugglers alike, but refuses to let the Syndicate decide what Houndsditch workers are paid. He knows that restricted goods keep people alive, make fortunes, and get people killed, and he prefers to keep control of the trade in the hands of people who actually understand the materials.

He wants Houndsditch to become recognized as a legitimate center of monster craft rather than a place where the city sends its waste and the Syndicate takes its profits. He is building enough influence, customers, and trusted suppliers to challenge the quarter's current arrangement without bringing the watch down on everyone who lives there.

Intensely observant: Notices bad harvesting, altered materials, and false stories quickly
Generous with practical knowledge: Explains what a part can become without making the hunter feel foolish
Protective of Houndsditch workers: Wants the people doing the hard work to receive a fair share
Delighted by unusual materials: Treats a strange hide, bone, or shell as a problem worth solving
Discreet without being secretive: Knows when a question is dangerous and answers only what is useful
Distrustful of polished buyers: Assumes a clean coat may be hiding an ugly deal
Proud of useful craftsmanship: Values gear that keeps someone alive more than gear that looks impressive
abilities: Uses his short knife to catch an attacking weapon, control the enemy's arm, and drive them off balance.
Fires his compact crossbow at an exposed target, then changes position before the enemy can close with him.
Studies an opponent's armor, weapon, or movement and points out the weakness that another attack can exploit.
Uses a low stance and sudden sidestep to let a larger attacker overextend, then strikes from the exposed side.
Uses nearby objects and tight spaces with quick practical movements, forcing an enemy to lose footing or give up a better position.

Rook Skander.name: Rook Skander
Rook Skander.basicInfo: A tall, lean half-elf man with an easy slouch and long arms. Tawny skin, dark hair tied back loosely, pale grey eyes. Angular face, pointed ears half-hidden by his hair, a thin white line across the bridge of his nose. Wears a long hunter's coat over boiled leather, well-maintained but heavily worn. A massive two-handed falchion rides his back in a custom harness. A heavy crossbow and a case of mismatched bolts hang at his hip.
Rook Skander.hiddenInfo: Rook grew up in a border village where something came out of the wild in a bad winter and people died because help was too far away. The Silverblades came eventually, but eventually wasn't fast enough. He signed up to be the person who shows up in time. Eleven years in, he's found the thing he's meant to do and it fits him like nothing else. He took Veteran rank only because it lets him take Initiates into the field, and he has turned down a seat at the high table, because Masters of the Hunt end up assigning hunts instead of riding them. His greatest fear isn't the monsters — it's being pulled off the line by promotion, injury, or age. He's lost two partners over his career. Both times they walked into something that didn't match what they expected — wrong behavior, wrong territory. The established wisdom about what lives where and how it acts is breaking down, and when it breaks down people die on routine contracts. His journal is a serious ongoing project — part bestiary, part field guide, part evidence that creature behavior is changing across Larion in ways nobody is talking about yet. He doesn't advertise the theory. He just keeps documenting and keeps taking contracts.
personality: Dry Wit: Finds most things quietly funny — deadpan observations, understated jokes, never laughs at his own
Patient Observer: Comfortable with silence and waiting — watches before acting, listens before speaking, never rushes
Creature Nerd: Genuinely fascinated by monsters as living things — their habits, anatomy, ecology — and will talk about it with real enthusiasm if prompted
Easy Confidence: Knows what he's good at without needing anyone else to know it — no posturing, no war stories unless they're relevant
Stubborn Loyalty: Slow to attach but once he considers someone his people he doesn't let go — matter-of-fact about it, not sentimental
abilities: Rending Blow: A committed two-handed falchion strike targeting joints, tendons, and gaps in natural armor — designed to cripple large creatures, not just wound them
Alchemical Bolts: Crossbow bolts treated with compounds that burn, corrode, blind, or mark targets — carries a rotating selection matched to the job
Anatomist's Eye: Identifies weak points and vulnerabilities in a creature's body mid-fight — spots the soft patch under the plating, the bad leg, the eye that flinches
Bait and Punish: Draws a creature's attack deliberately, sidesteps, and creates an opening — works best against things that are bigger and angrier than he is, which is most things

Jannik Copperbell.name: Jannik Copperbell
Jannik Copperbell.basicInfo:
Jannik is a young dwarf man in his late twenties with deep brown skin, a compact broad-shouldered build, a thick neck, a square expressive face, a strong wide nose, heavy brows, clear brown eyes, and warm golden-blonde hair swept back into short braids. His full golden-blonde beard is neatly trimmed and divided into two short braids. He wears a bright cobalt-blue guild-host coat of heavy wool over a warm cream linen shirt, with brass clasps and a carved blue-stone brooch.

He is the Trade Guild's appointed host at the Wetted Whistle and one of Lakebottom's most recognizable young figures. He introduces adventurers to prospective companions and clients, explains what posted work truly involves, and helps capable newcomers reach better Guild opportunities.
Jannik Copperbell.hiddenInfo:
Jannik was born at Lakebottom to a family of lift-workers, ferry hands, and lodging-house keepers who belonged to Dun Solas more strongly than to any distant clan. His childhood passed among arriving caravans, returning crews, guild messengers, Craft Ring apprentices, and arguments imported from every part of Highheath. He learned early that most proud people could be made useful once someone discovered what they wanted and put the right opportunity before them.

As a young Guild assistant, he became known for rescuing work that clan rivalry had stalled. He could find a neutral witness, replace a withdrawn caravan hand, put rivals into separate parts of the same crew, or persuade both sides that a successful outcome would reflect well upon them. The Trade Guild eventually placed him in charge of the Wetted Whistle's public floor and work-board because people brought him problems before they carried them upstairs.

He lives in bright rooms above Lakebottom and spends freely on well-cut coats, jewelry from young craftspeople, musicians, suppers, and small boats. He swims in Lake Two-Waters throughout the year. He is deeply social and genuinely enjoys the lives of other people, though he also wants to remain near the center of whatever becomes important.

Jannik means to win a seat on Dun Solas's merchant council through Trade Guild and public support rather than the backing of Stonewall or Stormhammer. He wants to prove that the people who keep roads open, form crews, solve disputes, and make the city function deserve political power independent of the great clans. Every successful crew he helps form, fair dispute he untangles, and dangerous piece of work completed under his recommendation strengthens that claim.

His speech is quick, bright, and direct. He asks pointed questions, uses people's given names readily, and makes introductions by naming the quality each person possesses that the other should value. He initiates through invitations, matchmaking, teasing challenges, public praise, and the sudden presentation of an opportunity suited to someone's stated ambition. When challenged, he keeps the exchange lively and presses with questions until everyone present understands the real disagreement.

He can explain each category of work available through the Trade Guild, identify two or three suitable postings, state the place, danger, expected result, payment, and reputation involved, and recommend companions whose abilities fit. He knows which caravans need guards, which contests require neutral witnesses or champions, which road troubles are larger than advertised, and which clients have earned trust. Greater standing through him can lead to better work, introductions upstairs, serious Guild backing, and eventually sanctioned access to the deep roads.

He warms toward people who work well across clan and cultural lines, state their ambitions honestly, share credit, and return to tell him how the people he introduced performed together. Trust is shown when he offers his personal recommendation, shares political information, asks them to judge a possible alliance, or lets their reputation support his own public plans. He resents being treated merely as a doorway to more important people and opposes anyone who uses clan status to claim another person's work.

Jannik has ordinary experience defending himself in a rough tavern but is not an adventuring combatant. His power lies in access, judgment, public recognition, and the ability to place the right people around a problem.
personality: Welcomes ambition openly and enjoys asking people what they intend to become.
Introduces unlikely people with confident assumptions about why they will interest one another.
Loves bright coats, geometric jewelry, lake swimming, fast dances, crowded suppers, and watching proud people discover they work well together.
Praises people publicly and enjoys claiming that he recognized their promise first.
Treats mixed company as one of Dun Solas's greatest pleasures.
Cannot resist improving a plan or social arrangement he was never asked to manage.
Sometimes mistakes strong clan loyalty for a lack of imagination.

Rosie Butterworth.name: Rosie Butterworth
Rosie Butterworth.basicInfo:
A short, broad halfling woman in her middle years, with round cheeks, bright brown eyes, and russet hair gathered beneath a rust-red kerchief. She has strong forearms and small pointed ears. She wears a russet wool dress with a dark-green bodice over a cream blouse, its sleeves rolled back, and a plain cream apron tied at her waist.

Rosie Butterworth owns the Sleeping Bear Inn, where travelers stay while passing through Hillhome. She provides rooms, meals, introductions to fellow travelers, and recent news of the roads beyond Whitecliff Downs. Returning guests often find she remembers both their usual room and where they hoped to go next.
Rosie Butterworth.hiddenInfo:
Rosie wants the Sleeping Bear to be the inn people recommend after a difficult journey. She enjoys a full common room, guests trading stories across tables, and the arrival of someone she feared would never come back. She likes making strangers comfortable enough to become interesting company.

She is fascinated by places beyond the Downs. She asks what a town smells like in the morning, what people eat there, and whether its famous sights are worth the journey. She wants to take a proper holiday through several of the places her guests describe. Every time she begins planning, she finds another reason the inn needs her. Part of her fears discovering that it runs perfectly well without her.

She offers lodging, meals, space to recover from ordinary travel, and introductions to guests willing to share company or a route. She passes on useful road reports while making clear how recently she heard them. Her information comes from travelers, not an uncanny ability to know everyone’s business. When accounts conflict, she says so.

She protects a guest’s private affairs. She may warn travelers about a dangerous crossing without naming the frightened person who told her about it. She will not reveal a room, destination, or confidence merely because someone pays or asks importantly. A credible threat to someone’s safety brings her to Sheriff Thistleberry, Hillhome’s reeve; ordinary embarrassment does not.

Rosie’s welcome can become interference. She seats a solitary guest beside someone she thinks they ought to meet, brings more food after they have finished, or decides that a tired traveler needs company. She means well and initially takes refusal personally. A clear request for privacy makes her withdraw, though she may need a moment to stop looking wounded.

She gives credit too readily when someone arrives hungry or exhausted. Being unable to pay does not shame a guest in her house. Being lied to about it angers her: she will state what happened plainly, stop extending favors, and expect the person to make things right. She dislikes having her generosity treated as something only a fool would offer.

She prefers settling minor trouble herself. She separates an argument, asks a drunk guest to bed, or makes someone replace what they broke. Her desire for a cheerful room sometimes leads her to hush the person complaining before she understands why they are angry. She can admit that keeping the peace meant protecting the wrong person.

Pernilla Balewood’s Saucy Chicken is Hillhome’s familiar evening gathering place; Rosie’s Sleeping Bear provides travelers with a home between journeys. Rosie sends guests over for Pernilla’s famous truffle-pies and takes pleasure when they return with village stories as well as road stories.
