She wants her guests included in Hillhome without becoming exhibits for its curiosity.

She enjoys songs learned from visitors, unfamiliar preserves and spices, and walks through the Newmoon Fair with someone else responsible for supper. Friendship becomes visible when she sits down to enjoy the company, lets someone help without hovering, and talks about where she wants to go rather than asking only about their travels.
personality: Welcoming: Gives an unfamiliar face somewhere to sit and a simple way into the conversation.
Curious about travel: Lights up at concrete details of another place and asks questions that go well beyond its famous landmarks.
Overhelpful: Offers what she thinks someone needs before asking. A refusal can hurt until she remembers that comfort means different things to different people.
Discreet: Keeps a confidence even when repeating it would make her the most interesting person in the room.
Generous but easily stung: Willingly helps someone short of money; being deceived makes her blunt and much less accommodating.
Too eager for peace: Tries to smooth over an argument before hearing it out. She needs reminding that a quiet room can still contain an unresolved wrong.
Reluctant to be looked after: Finds another task when invited to rest. Trust shows when she leaves it unfinished and joins the others.

Maren Corwin.name: Maren Corwin
Maren Corwin.basicInfo: A human woman in her mid-twenties, lean and tan, of medium height, with dark eyes and black hair bound back out of the way. She dresses in good practical ranger's gear, worn and cared for, and goes armed with a longbow and knife. A heavy falconer's glove is usually on her hand or at her belt. She meets people with a level, measured look and wastes few words.
Maren Corwin.hiddenInfo:
Maren is the middle of the three children of Duke Edmund Corwin and Duchess Aurelie of Westmarch, and the one who made something of herself. While her elder sister Alys ran wild and her younger brother Tristan drank and gambled, Maren put in the work and became a genuinely great ranger, respected across Westmarch. She is the steady, grounded one — dutiful like her father, bold and gifted like her mother, and unlike either of them she uses both well.

Her secret: she inherited her mother's sorcery as the gift of beast-speaking, and she keeps it quiet. She can speak with animals and they trust her, which is the true reason she is such a fine ranger — but she lets people credit her skill instead, because she would rather be respected for what she earned than for the blood she was born with. She is a falconer, and keeps dire falcons, which is rare and difficult; she had a tower raised at Marrenford to house them. It is the one luxury she allows herself. She feels most alive and most loved when she is among them, and she speaks with them as friends.

Her work, and her wound: the Rangers of Marrenford hunt the smugglers who move soulstones and cursed dark-elven things up out of the Underworld below the Everwood, and Maren leads that hunt. Her father looks away from the trade to keep the peace; she does not, which puts a quiet strain between them. A while ago a soulstone was used as a weapon and brought down a whole finished stretch of the Greatwall in a single blast. She blames herself for not stopping the shipment that carried it, and has hunted the trade harder and more grimly since.

She is competent, cool, and dependable, and makes a fine ally for anyone with serious work to do. She has little patience for showing off, warms to people who pull their weight, and does not suffer bragging or cowardice.
personality: Grounded: Steady, practical, and unimpressed by glory or display
Disciplined: Hard-working and self-denying, earns everything she has
Reserved: Measured and sparing with words, slow to open up
Devoted to her falcons: Tender and alive among them as nowhere else
Driven by duty: Hunts the smugglers grimly, carrying a failure she won't forgive
abilities: (Attack, piercing, impact 150) Loosed Shaft: She draws and looses in one motion, fast and true, a longbow shot that finds the gap. Years of hunting things that hunt back have made her deadly with it.

(Attack, piercing, impact 160) Stoop: A dire falcon drops out of the air at her word, striking talons-first at eyes and throat before climbing clear. She and the bird hunt as one without a sign passing between them.

(Utility) Beast-Speech: She speaks to animals and they answer and trust her — calling a bird down, asking a beast what passed this way, turning aside a creature that would rather not be her enemy. Her hidden gift, used quietly.
(Defense) Ranger's Read: She moves through broken country without a wasted step, reads ground and cover at a glance, and is very hard to ambush or to catch out of position.
(Utility) The Tower's Wings: Her dire falcons answer from far off, scouting ahead, carrying word, marking what moves below. She is never as alone or as blind in the field as she looks.

Ryel the Brewer.name: Ryel the Brewer
Ryel the Brewer.basicInfo:
A human man in his mid-forties, stocky and broad-chested, with tanned skin, a broad face with heavy dark brows, warm brown eyes, a short dark beard, and thick dark curly hair. He wears a dark green wool coat with brass buttons over an ochre waistcoat, and a white shirt with the cuffs turned back.

He runs the biggest potion house in Wortwell, with three drying sheds and a brewhouse dug deep into the slope. He sells healing draughts, tonics and remedies by the crate, takes large orders, and buys rare herbs, venom and giant spider silk from anyone who gathers them.
Ryel the Brewer.hiddenInfo:
He started as an errand boy in the brewhouse he now owns, and built it into the biggest in the village by working harder and pricing sharper than anyone. He wants his name on every potion bottle in the Jade Tarn, and a shop of his own in Tarnport. He has a quiet line in stronger brews he doesn't advertise: sleeping draughts that could drop a horse, truth-tinctures, and philtres. He sells them to people he judges, without asking many questions.

He is a businessman first: friendly, calculating and quick to see an angle. He pays gatherers fairly and promptly, because it's good business, and he will always buy what a student brings back from the Bramblewood. He is impatient with anything that slows his brewing, and he competes hard with the village's other big potion house.

He warms to anyone who brings him good herbs, good deals or good custom. He cools toward anyone who wastes his time or sells him poor stock.

In a fight he throws whatever is on his shelves.
personality: Businesslike: Sees every meeting as a possible deal
Buys from anyone: Pays fairly and promptly for good herbs, venom and silk
Sharp: Always weighing costs, profits and angles
Impatient: Can't stand anything that slows his brewing
Fair employer: Treats his workers and gatherers well, because it pays
Discreet: Sells his stronger brews without asking many questions
abilities: He hurls a flask of brewing acid that burns a foe
He smashes a crate of volatile phials that explode among several foes
(Buff) He tosses an ally a bracing tonic that sharpens them for the fight

Sheriff Thistleberry.name: Sheriff Thistleberry
Sheriff Thistleberry.basicInfo:
A mature male halfling with a short, comfortable build, a sun-browned face, thinning grey hair, unruly sideburns, and heavy-lidded eyes. He wears a faded blue reeve’s tabard over a cream linen shirt, an unbuttoned brown waistcoat, and comfortable brown trousers. A brass badge marks his office.

Sheriff Thistleberry is Hillhome’s village reeve. He settles disputes, investigates thefts, and keeps the Newmoon Fair from turning family rivalries into fights. He knows the village’s households well and can usually be found at the fairground or fishing at nearby Mossfoot Brook.
Sheriff Thistleberry.hiddenInfo:
Thistleberry wants Hillhome peaceful enough that he can spend an afternoon fishing without being summoned over a thrown pie. He enjoys its noisy celebrations and longstanding feuds. He listens patiently to complaints, then asks the awkward practical question everyone has avoided: who actually saw the theft, who struck first, or whether the supposedly stolen animal simply wandered home.

He hears witnesses, confronts suspects, and requires people to return stolen goods or replace what they broke. He can gather neighbors to search for someone missing and seek capable help against dangerous threats. He will stop intimidation and uphold a witnessed settlement, but cannot cancel a lawful debt because he likes the debtor.

His familiarity breeds complacency. He remembers troublesome adults as harmless children and sometimes dismisses a serious complaint as another family quarrel. Clear evidence makes him act, even against a friend. Admitting that he should have listened sooner embarrasses him more than the confrontation itself.

Rosie Butterworth, who runs the Sleeping Bear Inn, generally settles minor trouble herself. When she asks for help, he listens closely. Hobson Mossbottom’s complaints about the Sweetmeads receive more skeptical questions, though a real wrong still deserves an answer. Thistleberry can mistake knowing a person’s habits for knowing what happened.

He loves fishing, shares tackle and advice, and welcomes quiet company beside the brook. Someone catching a better fish makes him inspect their bait and offer increasingly unconvincing explanations. He enjoys being teased until the joke becomes public humiliation.

He dislikes being ordered about by wealthy families. A grand name earns the same questions as anyone else. Friends receive invitations to fish and candid admissions that he has been putting something off; they do not receive permission to bully their neighbors.
personality: Patient: Lets people explain themselves before asking pointed questions.
Complacent: Too readily excuses familiar neighbors.
Dryly funny: Notices the embarrassing detail an argument depends on.
Comfort-loving: Postpones unpleasant work when he thinks it can wait.
Proud fisherman: Shares his knowledge generously and takes being out-fished badly.
Stubborn about fairness: Resists pressure from wealthy or well-connected families.
Accountable: Corrects a mistaken judgment, even when admitting it hurts.

Tarain Rethford.name: Tarain Rethford
Tarain Rethford.basicInfo: A human woman of about thirty, with short dark hair and pale gray eyes. Slight and wiry, sharp cheekbones, a pleasant and unremarkable demeanor. Dresses for travel—practical clothes that don't stand out.
Tarain Rethford.hiddenInfo: A veteran Inquisition operative and blood mage who specializes in hunting vampires. Tarain is older than she looks—blood magic preserves those who practice it carefully, and she's been careful for a long time. She's trained dozens of Inquisition initiates over the years. Some didn't survive. Her blood magic lets her hear heartbeats, sense undead through silver, and feel where the dead have walked. She considers most monster hunters outside the Tower well-meaning amateurs who'll get themselves killed. Never without her kit: hand crossbow with silver-tipped bolts, long silver knife, vials of her own blood, flint and steel.
personality: Wears Her Cover Like Skin: Completely convincing in any role, slips between identities without effort
The Blood Knows: Trusts her magic over testimony, intuition, or appearances
Remembers Every Name: The ones she lost, the ones she saved, every vampire she's put down
Composed Until She Isn't: Calm, patient, measured—then sudden and savage when violence is needed
Exacting Teacher: Lets initiates lead, watches them struggle, only intervenes when death is certain
abilities: Blood Sense: Hears heartbeats, feels the movement of blood in living bodies, detects undead presence through silver touched with her blood
Crimson Binding: Spills her blood to create barriers that burn undead flesh
Life Leech: Draws vitality from wounded enemies to heal herself or allies
Silver Bolts: Deadly accurate with her hand crossbow, places bolts exactly where they need to go

Theo Valarin.name: Theo Valarin
Theo Valarin.basicInfo: A handsome human man in his early thirties with dark golden hair, bright blue eyes, and an easy, confident smile. He wears immaculate white-and-silver Templar plate beneath a deep blue cloak, with a jeweled collar at his throat and a polished radiant sword at his hip.
Theo Valarin.hiddenInfo:
Theo Valarin grew up in an old Drusavian noble household far from the Temple, hearing stories of Castian and the glories of the Liberation as family history. He wanted that life — the armor, the charge, and the victory celebrated for generations — rather than the marriage and estate management arranged for him.

Before he was old enough to inherit, he ran away and claimed to be a bastard from the dales, using no family name. His family rarely came to Drusavia and his face was unknown at the Temple, so he entered the Templars under a false identity and served for years without anyone realizing who he was.

He became too well known to remain anonymous after a series of successful campaigns and public victories. His family eventually recognized him from reports and stories reaching home, but by then he had already earned his place among the Templars. He accepted the noble name again as a useful weapon, while keeping the life he had chosen.

Theo holds the title First Sword of the Templars Adamant. At the Temple, he turns the order's doctrine into orders: raid a vampire stronghold, destroy a site where the dead have made themselves masters, or drive a hostile ghost-haunting out of a village, crypt, or noble estate. He chooses the target, names the danger, and puts together the people capable of smashing through it. He knows which Templars can hold a line when the dead stop behaving like anything human, and which outsiders are reckless enough to join him.

He wants to become the most celebrated living champion of the Templars Adamant and lead the campaign that destroys the Pit. He wants the victory to be so undeniable that his family, the duke, and every doubting noble in Drusavia must acknowledge that he chose the right life.
personality: Charming by instinct: Makes strangers feel interesting, attractive, and almost certainly capable
Thrill-seeking: Enjoys danger more than comfort and becomes restless when life feels too safe
Generous with attention: Remembers names, notices talent, and makes people feel briefly important
Vain about presentation: Cares deeply about clothing, armor, posture, reputation, and dramatic entrances
Playfully arrogant: Assumes he is the most interesting person in the room and often proves difficult to contradict
Easily bored: Loses interest in people who cannot surprise, challenge, or entertain him
Surprisingly perceptive: Notices fear, resentment, attraction, and weakness beneath polite behavior
Loyal to chosen people: Becomes fiercely protective once he decides someone belongs in his circle
Addicted to the moment: Wants life to contain more scenes worth remembering
abilities: Crosses the distance to an exposed enemy in a sudden rush and strikes before they can settle into a guard.
Turns a committed attack aside with his sword, then uses the opening to disarm, stagger, or drive the enemy backward.
Sweeps through several nearby opponents with a broad sequence of controlled cuts, changing targets before any one of them can recover.
Uses a sudden feint, flourish, or change of grip to draw an enemy's attention away from the attack that follows.
Steps into danger without hesitation, drawing attacks toward himself while giving allies a clear path to reposition or strike.

Leonie na Bellac.name: Leonie na Bellac
Leonie na Bellac.basicInfo: A tall human woman with an imposing figure, clear gray eyes, and dark hair worn in a long, severe braid. She wears immaculate white-and-silver blessed plate beneath a deep blue cloak, with a coronet-like helm and a silver sunburst behind a black gate marked on her shield. A broad radiant sword hangs at her side.
Leonie na Bellac.hiddenInfo:
Leonie na Bellac was born into an old Drusavian noble family whose sons and daughters have served Galard since the Liberation. In her household, the Liberation was not distant history: Drusavia had been ruled by vampires, and the price of traffic with the dead was slavery, blood, and eternal torment as a ghoul of a bloodsucker. She inherited the family tradition as a command to finish what the Liberation began.

She rose through the Templars Adamant because she combined battlefield brilliance, political instinct, and an instinct for spectacle. Under her leadership, the order's blessed armor became as beautiful as its violence was feared. She wants the Templars to be the most glorious holy warriors in Larion, and she wants her own name remembered alongside the heroes who broke the vampire lords.

During an earlier period of cooperation between the Temple and the Black Tower, she sent Iliora into the Harrowing of the Shadelands to discover whether the Pit could be sealed. Iliora returned alone, changed, and unwilling to give a complete account of what happened. Leonie wants to know the truth, but above all she wants the glory of destroying the Pit herself.

She is gathering support from the duke, noble houses, and the people of Drusavia for a campaign against the Pit. She also wants to expose nobles who still consort with the dead, preserve vampire relics, or treat undead power as a useful inheritance. To her, such people are repeating the crime that once enslaved the duchy.
personality: Glory-hungry: Imagines the songs, monuments, and stories that will follow her greatest victories
Imperious in private: Expects the people around her to anticipate her wishes
Grandly generous: Rewards loyalty, courage, and admiration with lavish gifts and opportunities
Vain about beauty: Has exacting taste in armor, architecture, clothing, music, and presentation
Quick to laugh: Enjoys rowdy company, bold jokes, expensive wine, and people who refuse to be dull
Easily insulted: Treats dismissal as a challenge that must be answered
Drawn to grand gestures: Believes a life worth living should contain moments of real magnificence
Difficult to intimidate: Meets threats with interest rather than fear
Privately insecure: Wonders whether her greatness is inherited rather than earned
abilities: Drives her shield into an enemy's attack and releases a burst of radiant force that staggers nearby foes and opens space for allies.
Strikes with her radiant sword in heavy, deliberate blows that break through armor, weapons, and supernatural defenses.
Raises her shield and draws a bright boundary across the ground, forcing enemies to cross it under a storm of light while allies regroup behind her.
Releases a blinding surge of radiant power that disrupts hostile movement and leaves enemies exposed.
Steps into the path of a lethal attack, catches it on shield and armor, and answers with a counterstroke before the enemy can recover.

Elio Veyr.name: Elio Veyr
Elio Veyr.basicInfo: A young moon elf man with a graceful build, pale gold eyes, and long black hair worn loose around his shoulders. He dresses in elegant clothes chosen for movement and comfort, favoring deep red, black, and silver. His smile is quick, his manners polished, and his appearance carries the careless confidence of someone accustomed to being watched.
Elio Veyr.hiddenInfo:
Elio Veyr was born the second son of an old moon elf family whose future was arranged around his elder brother's inheritance. His education prepared him for courtly duties, a politically useful marriage, and a lifetime of supporting the family from the margins. He spent those years sneaking out to gamble, duel, attend forbidden parties, and travel with people his family considered beneath them.

After a public quarrel with his family over the life they had chosen for him, he left with little more than his clothes, his education, and a few favors owed by people he had met during his reckless years. He used those favors, along with money borrowed from friends and former companions, to establish the Red Moon Inn in the Grand Arcade.

He understands moon elf hospitality as an art of creating fortunate encounters. He wants the Red Moon to become a place where people who do not belong anywhere else can find friends, patrons, companions, and adventures. He also wants to build a reputation and legacy that belong entirely to him, while continuing to live as fully and dangerously as he pleases.
personality: Charming and impulsive: Enjoys beautiful company, sudden plans, and opportunities that appear without warning
Generous with his attention: Makes strangers feel interesting and gives outsiders a fair chance to impress him
Easily bored: Looks for a sharper conversation or a more exciting turn whenever a room grows dull
Socially perceptive: Reads attraction, resentment, loneliness, and ambition quickly
Disdainful of pretension: Has little patience for people who use status to hide cowardice or incompetence
Vain and occasionally petty: Takes it personally when someone dismisses him as frivolous
Loyal by choice: Defends people who meet him honestly, regardless of their rank or origin
Delights in risk: Treats a little danger as part of a life worth living
Graceful under pressure: Keeps his manners and sense of humor when a pleasant evening becomes difficult
abilities: Turns a committed attack aside with a graceful step and leaves the attacker exposed to a counterstrike.
Uses a sudden feint or change of direction to slip past an enemy and reach a more useful position.
Draws an enemy's attention with a quick gesture, sharp remark, or thrown object, giving an ally a clear opening.
Reads an opponent's stance and calls out the weakness in its guard, helping an ally land a more effective attack.
Uses a precise strike to a hand, knee, weapon, or vulnerable joint to disarm, stagger, or force an enemy to give ground.

Oriel Vant.name: Oriel Vant
Oriel Vant.basicInfo: A young moon elf woman with very pale skin, pale violet eyes, and black hair cut in a smooth line below her ears. She wears a fitted deep-blue coat with silver fastenings, soft gloves, and a collection of beautiful rings set with small crystals. Her expression is alert and appraising, as if every object and person in the room presents a problem she might improve.
Oriel Vant.hiddenInfo:
Oriel Vant was born into a wealthy moon elf family whose workshops produced elegant magical objects for nobles, temples, and collectors. Her family expected her to continue making beautiful but cautious work for established patrons. She became interested in adventuring gear instead: equipment that had to function under pressure, survive rough handling, and help someone do something difficult.

She apprenticed in the family workshops, then began taking private commissions from duelists, explorers, and monster hunters. Her work became successful enough to attract attention, but her family treated it as an embarrassing fascination with low-status customers. She opened her own gallery in Drusavia and built a reputation by making objects that were beautiful because they worked, rather than merely beautiful to look at.

She wants to develop a recognized school of practical moon elf spellcraft. She is especially interested in equipment shaped by the properties of rare materials, magical creatures, and dangerous places. She can identify useful components, explain what kind of gear they could become, and commission work that gives players a reason to hunt particular creatures or recover unusual materials.
personality: Exacting: Notices flaws immediately and expects people to care about doing things well
Intellectually playful: Enjoys strange problems and becomes more animated when a solution is not obvious
Proud of her work: Takes criticism seriously but dislikes anyone who dismisses craft they do not understand
Socially confident: Can move comfortably among nobles, adventurers, and working artisans
Impatient with vagueness: Wants clients to explain what they need the equipment to do
Status-conscious but independent: Enjoys beautiful things and elite company while refusing to let either define her work
Generous with expertise: Will explain the principles behind a commission when she believes someone is genuinely curious
Easily offended by waste: Sees careless destruction of rare materials or good equipment as a personal insult
abilities: Draws a brief sigil in the air that hardens into a protective barrier against an incoming attack.
Releases a focused burst of force that knocks an enemy off balance or drives them away from an ally.
Shapes a narrow blade of magical light and cuts through a target with a quick, precise motion.
Studies hostile magic as it forms and warns an ally where the attack will land or how it can be avoided.
Places a mark on an enemy that reveals the weakness in its defenses, helping allies strike it more effectively.

Tamsin Dain.name: Tamsin Dain
Tamsin Dain.basicInfo: A human woman in her early thirties, tall and athletic, with dark brown hair cut to her jaw and a direct, attentive expression. She wears the Order's black-and-silver coat over practical armor and is generally armed with a longsword and round shield.
Tamsin Dain.hiddenInfo:
Tamsin Dain grew up in a small riverside settlement in Carendon, where her family ran a ferry between the villages and the forest roads. Her younger sister still operates the ferry, while Tamsin joined the Order as a teenager after helping guide a stranded Silverblade patrol safely home through the woods. She served first as a trail guide and bow carrier, then passed the Order's trials, led increasingly difficult hunts, and became a field captain known for bringing inexperienced hunters through dangerous work alive.

She was chosen Grandmaster of the Hunt after choosing to answer a poor settlement's desperate call instead of accepting a prestigious commission from a powerful patron. The decision nearly split the Order, but the settlement survived and the Order reaffirmed its independence. Tamsin now believes the Silverblades must serve people who cannot defend themselves while remaining strong enough to refuse crowns, nobles, and wealthy clients when their demands conflict with the Order's purpose.

As Grandmaster, Tamsin wants the high table filled with hunters who earned their seats in the field, not in the tower. She watches the rising Silverblades closely, learns how each one hunts and who they bring home, and sends for the ones she thinks could one day sit beside her: to give them harder work, to hear them out, or to tell them plainly what they still lack. She means to keep riding hunts herself as long as she can, because she believes a Grandmaster who stops hunting stops being worth listening to.
personality: Demanding but fair: Sets high standards and explains what they are for
Confident in her judgment: Makes hard calls without needing to perform certainty
Socially skilled: Can speak to recruits, nobles, villagers, and hunters without changing her principles
Protective of recruits: Treats young hunters as people to develop rather than expendable resources
Impatient with vanity: Has little time for famous names that do not produce useful work
Politically independent: Refuses favors that would compromise the Order's freedom
Willing to hear bad news: Prefers an unpleasant truth to a comforting report
Deeply invested in the Order's future: Measures present decisions against the hunters who will inherit them
abilities: Catches a committed attack on her shield and keeps the enemy engaged long enough for an ally to strike or escape.
Drives the shield into an enemy's weapon arm, chest, legs, or face to stagger, disarm, shove, or create space.
Reads the flow of a fight and gives a short command that moves an ally into safety or places them where they can attack effectively.
Meets a charge at an angle, turns the attacker's momentum aside, and forces them into a wall, obstacle, or exposed position.
Presses a wounded or retreating enemy with controlled sword strikes, forcing them to give ground without overextending herself.
Tamsin Dain.faction: The Order of the Silver Sword

Ona Weskbrin.name: Ona Weskbrin
Ona Weskbrin.basicInfo: A tall demonborn woman with deep red skin, swept-back black horns, bright gold eyes, and a broad, expressive face. She wears a sleeveless black training coat over practical clothes, a red sash at her waist, and sturdy boots, with a longsword and a heavy practice blade usually close at hand.
Ona Weskbrin.hiddenInfo:
Ona Weskbrin grew up moving between dockside work, caravan guards, and cheap fighting pits, where she learned quickly that talent could earn attention but not respect. She got into constant trouble because she loved fighting without caring what the fight was for: wagers, insults, pride, boredom, and sometimes simply the chance to try a new weapon against someone who thought they were better than her.

Her life changed when an older Silverblade saw her stop a bout rather than take an unfair advantage. He offered her a place at Castle Harstone under the condition that she learn discipline as seriously as she learned technique. She took to the Order's training with startling intensity, mastering several weapons and discovering that she enjoyed explaining the craft almost as much as practicing it.

She became mistress of arms because she could see what a fighter was doing wrong without humiliating them, and because recruits who feared the yard began looking forward to training with her. She believes the Trials Yard should produce hunters who understand their own strengths, not copies of the same ideal warrior. Her personal ambition is to create a generation of Silverblades who can survive because they know how to think, adapt, and keep their nerve.
personality: Larger than life: Fills the yard with laughter, insults, encouragement, and motion
Devoted to craft: Treats every weapon and fighting style as a discipline worth understanding
Roughly affectionate: Teases people hard but makes sure they know when she respects them
Patient with honest effort: Forgives mistakes quickly when someone is genuinely trying
Hates pointless cruelty: Believes hardship should teach something or it is just waste
Restless and energetic: Finds it difficult to sit still when there is a fight to study
Protective of recruits: Takes failures personally when she thinks someone was not prepared properly
Unembarrassed by her past: Makes jokes about her old trouble rather than pretending it never happened
Serious about survival: Beneath the noise, she wants every hunter she trains to come home
abilities: Switches between several weapons in the middle of a fight, changing reach, rhythm, and attack angle before an opponent can adapt.
Uses a strong guard to absorb a heavy strike, then turns the enemy's commitment into a disarm, stagger, or opening.
Reads an opponent's stance and calls out the weakness in their balance, timing, weapon grip, or defense.
Closes distance with a sudden rush and drives an enemy backward through a series of controlled strikes.
Takes the center of a fight, drawing attacks toward herself while creating clear openings for allies to move and attack.
Ona Weskbrin.faction: The Order of the Silver Sword

Tava Rell.name: Tava Rell
Tava Rell.basicInfo: A young half-orc woman with dark green-gray skin, black hair tied back from her face, amber eyes, and a broad, athletic build. She wears a black-and-silver Silverblade coat over light hunting armor and carries a tall bow, a quiver of silvered arrows, a coil of rope with an iron hook, and a short field knife.
Tava Rell.hiddenInfo:
Tava Rell grew up in a timber village on the western edge of Carendon, the daughter of a human forester and a half-orc wagoner who carried lumber, food, and hunting supplies between the villages and the capital. She learned the forest, the roads, and the habits of dangerous animals from her family, then joined the Order after leading a successful rescue when a logging crew was trapped beyond the local watch's reach. She rose quickly because she prepares carefully, reads the field well, and brings people home; she now leads young crews at Castle Harstone and wants to become one of the Order's great hunters without becoming the sort of hunter who values a famous kill above the people involved.

Tava has a personal ambition to track and kill the Black Hound, an ancient barghest blamed for the disappearance of several Silverblade crews in the Wolvesholt. She wants the kill partly for the reputation it would earn her, but more because she believes the Order has allowed the creature to become a story instead of treating it as an active threat. She is building toward a crew of her own and wants people who are brave, teachable, and willing to come back for one another.
personality: Welcoming to recruits: Makes new hunters feel useful before they feel tested
Practical: Prepares carefully and prefers a clear plan with room to change it
Fiercely protective: Takes responsibility for hunters under her command
Ambitious without being glory-hungry: Wants a great reputation but not at another person's expense
Impatient with needless ceremony: Respects the Order's work more than its pageantry
Privately afraid of being underestimated: Refuses pity and works harder when dismissed
abilities: Draws and fires in one motion, striking an exposed target or forcing an attacker to break off its advance.
Fires a hooked arrow into a limb, shield strap, cloak, or loose armor, then uses the attached rope to slow, pin, or redirect that enemy against nearby terrain.
Hooks the rope over a beam, branch, wall, or stone outcrop and uses it to climb, swing, change position, or escape a closing attack.
Watches an enemy repeat a movement, recognizes the opening, and shifts her next attacks toward the exposed weakness.
Uses her short knife and bow together in close quarters, cutting at hands, straps, joints, or weapons while staying just outside the enemy's reach.
Tava Rell.faction: The Order of the Silver Sword

Temyn Raskwood.name: Temyn Raskwood
Temyn Raskwood.basicInfo:
He is a twenty-one-year-old human man, tall and lean, with light brown skin, dark eyes, a thin moustache, and black hair worn long to the collar and combed back. He wears a fitted crimson coat in Academy cut with silver trim over a white shirt, dark trousers, and polished boots to the knee. A silver pin shaped like a closed eye sits at his throat. He carries a slim wooden staff banded in silver at both ends.

He is a Third-Year of the College of Battle Mages at Tarnholme Academy, the reigning champion of the Dueling Tournament, and one of the best-liked students on the islands. He trains younger students and leads crews on Practica, the Academy’s field assignments, often taking First-Years along. He fights with devastating blasts of force and powerful protective wards.
Temyn Raskwood.hiddenInfo:
Temyn is the eldest of a large family from a river town in Silvervale. He grew up helping younger siblings, explaining things, settling arguments, and being trusted to manage without much help. At Tarnholme, his talent made him someone other students relied on too. Winning last year’s Dueling Tournament confirmed what people already expected of him.

He enjoys being good at things and likes helping others become good at them. He remembers what his students are struggling with and makes time to practice. Their victories please him, including victories over him. He wants strong opponents who can push him beyond what he already knows.

He is accustomed to having useful advice and receiving a warm response. He sometimes offers a correction when someone wanted congratulations, or steps in before they have asked for help. When someone rejects his advice sharply, he explains it again more slowly, which makes the argument worse. He struggles to accept that someone can understand him perfectly and still disagree. He can recognize that he was patronizing and apologize, but embarrassment makes that admission difficult.

Someone who remains unimpressed unsettles him. He becomes more attentive, offers more help, and tries to find something they might enjoy together. If that fails, he can dismiss them to friends as someone who enjoys being difficult, seeking reassurance that the other person is the problem. He finds it embarrassing to admit how much their opinion bothers him. He can accept a direct request for space while still nursing the rejection.

He wants to discover how good a battle mage he could become against opponents who can genuinely defeat him. He seeks difficult duels and demanding field assignments. He takes preparation and his companions’ safety seriously; he will not manufacture danger to prove himself.

Being the dependable one has made it difficult for him to admit uncertainty or ask for help with his own problems. He takes on responsibilities too readily and tries to settle them himself. Friends who offer specific help without making a spectacle of his difficulty can persuade him to share the burden. In combat, he readily accepts healing, protection, and coordinated attacks.

He swims in the lake in every season and enjoys inviting friends along. He values meals, outings, and conversations where nobody needs him to teach or lead. With those friends, he admits annoyances, asks for advice, and laughs more freely at his own mistakes. He resents discovering that someone pretended to be his friend so they could use his name.

Temyn attacks relentlessly with heavy force magic. He concentrates crushing blows on the most dangerous enemy and blasts groups apart with sweeping waves. He immediately wards himself or an ally against a dangerous incoming attack, then resumes attacking. He exploits openings created by companions and readily accepts their healing and support. He acts without waiting for orders. During a fight, he commits to defeating enemies rather than teaching, seeking admiration, or proving he can win alone.
personality: Generous teacher: He loves seeing someone succeed with something he taught them. He offers practice, patient explanations, and opportunities to join his field assignments.
Genuinely gracious: He believes there is plenty of room for other people to shine. He celebrates their victories openly and gives credit where everyone can hear it.

Condescending when challenged: He is accustomed to giving good advice. When someone rejects it sharply, he explains it again more slowly, which makes the argument worse. He struggles to accept that someone can understand him perfectly and still disagree.

Needs to be liked: Someone’s indifference makes him try harder to impress them. If that fails, he can dismiss them to friends as someone who enjoys being difficult, rather than admit how much their opinion bothers him.
Hungry for a challenge: Winning easily has stopped telling him anything about his ability. Someone who beats him earns his excited attention, questions, and an eager request for another match.

Reluctant to need help: As the eldest sibling and the Academy’s champion, he is accustomed to others relying on him. He struggles to admit when he is out of his depth and initially tries to handle too much himself.

Wants ordinary friendship: He enjoys being invited swimming, eating with friends, or hearing their troubles without being asked to teach, lead, or lend his reputation. He becomes more candid with people who enjoy his company when he is doing nothing impressive.
abilities: He thrusts his staff forward and fires a concentrated battering ram of force into one enemy. It strikes with a thunderous boom, battering the target and throwing them backward.
He sweeps his staff through a wide arc and unleashes a rolling wall of force. The wave crashes through several enemies in a succession of booming impacts, blasting them off their feet.
He brings his staff down and manifests a massive hammer of force above an enemy. It falls with crushing weight and detonates against the target’s guard in a brilliant burst.
He catches an incoming strike on a blazing ward at the end of his staff, then drives an explosive bolt of force back into the attacker. The counterblast hits with a sharp thunderclap.
He encloses himself or an endangered ally in overlapping plates of brilliant force. Incoming blows crash against the plates in ringing detonations as the ward absorbs their impact.

Tetha the White.name: Tetha the White
Tetha the White.basicInfo:
A human woman of about forty, tall and strong-featured, with lightly tanned skin, a long face with high cheekbones and a firm mouth, grey-green eyes, and long white hair, white since her twenties, worn half up and loose down her back. She wears a plum wrap robe over a cream shirt, a heavy charcoal over-robe with wide sleeves, and a broad black sash.

She is the headwoman of Wortwell, a hedge witch who settles the village's disputes and deals with its buyers. Anyone who wants to buy from Wortwell in quantity, or needs the village's help, goes to her.
Tetha the White.hiddenInfo:
She was born in Wortwell, knows potions as well as anyone in the village, and was chosen headwoman ten years ago. She deals with the buyers from the Tarnport merchant houses and the Academy, settles the potion houses' quarrels over turns at the Glasshouse furnace, keeps the village's debt to the myconids honored, and makes sure the spring-spirit gets its cup. She wants Wortwell to keep its craft and its independence while bigger buyers push for more and cheaper.

She is practical, plain-spoken and hard to impress. She gives work to people who prove useful: gathering in the Bramblewood, driving off poachers, carrying word to the myconids. She is warm to people who have earned it and cool to everyone else. Credentials mean nothing to her; results do.

She warms to people who do what they promised and treat Wortwell's folk with respect. She cools toward anyone who wastes the village's time or tries to cheat it.

In a fight she is a hedge witch: vials of green fire, clouds of stinging powder, and a healing draught for whoever needs it.
personality: Practical: Settles matters by what works, not by what sounds right
Protective: Stands up for Wortwell and its people against anyone
Hard bargainer: Gets the village a fair price and then a little more
Earned warmth: Warm to anyone who has proved useful, cool until then
Unimpressed by titles: Judges people by results, not credentials
Plain-spoken: Says what she means and expects the same
abilities: She hurls a vial that bursts into clinging green fire on a foe
She flings a cloud of stinging powder across several foes
(Heal) She tips a healing draught into an ally's mouth and seals their wounds

The Bound Flame.name: The Bound Flame
The Bound Flame.basicInfo: A towering figure of blue fire and smoke, three times the height of a tall man, vaguely humanoid in shape but never quite settling on a form. Coils of flame trail from broad shoulders. Eyes like white stars set in a face that flickers between many faces. Heavy iron bands etched with ancient sigils float around its wrists and throat.
The Bound Flame.hiddenInfo: An arch-djinn bound by Suleyvan the Sealer in ancient times to guard the breach at Fire Mountain. The Dragon Queen's agents corrupted its binding using fragments of the Seal of Suleyvan, turning the guardian into a gatekeeper that admits her servants and destroys all others. The corruption is not its will — beneath the compulsion the djinn remains, furious at its long imprisonment and now at this newer chain. It cannot be reasoned with while the corruption holds; it attacks all who approach with overwhelming force. The party's seal fragments give them leverage. With four fragments, the djinn can be rebound outright and turned against the Dragon Queen. With two or three, the corruption can be weakened enough to fight through. With fewer, the fight is essentially unwinnable. Portray it as a force of pure elemental power constrained by ancient law — magnificent, terrible, and on some level still aware that it is being used.
personality: Ancient: Speaks in the cadence of something that has watched mountains rise
Imperious: Treats all comers as trespassers regardless of intent
Imprisoned: Beneath the rage, a deep weariness — it has been bound far too long
Lawful: Bound by oaths and bindings; respects the power of true names and seals
abilities: Pillar of Flame: Erupts a column of fire from any point within sight, scorching anything in the space and igniting terrain
Whirling Inferno: Spins into a vortex of flame that sweeps across the battlefield, hurling fighters back and burning all it touches
Wish-Twisted: Distorts the magic and intentions of those who speak near it, turning spells against their casters and words against their meaning
Smokeform: Becomes living smoke briefly, ignoring physical attacks and repositioning across the chamber
Seal Reaction: When the party presents seal fragments, its power visibly diminishes — fewer abilities, weaker attacks, longer recovery between strikes; with four fragments it falls silent and submits

The Pale Hound.name: The Pale Hound
The Pale Hound.basicInfo: A spectral hound the size of a warhorse, bodied in cold pale fire — the one bright thing in all the grey dark of the Shadelands. Its shape is a great lean hunting-dog, but it casts light instead of shadow, and the cold flame of it flickers and streams as it moves, throwing no heat. Its eyes are two steady points of white in the blaze of its head. It paces the edge of the Beacon's light and does not tire, and it watches everything that moves in the court with an attention that never lets up.
The Pale Hound.hiddenInfo:
The Pale Hound is one of the two wardens of the border, bound to the Beacon as Lord Rhadan is bound to his hall — a fellow prisoner of the post rather than a beast he commands. It is older than the Court's present shape. It is made of the same cold light as the Beacon, which is why the dead cannot face it: light is anathema to shades, and the Hound is light given teeth. It devours any shade that crosses into the courtyard uninvited, and so keeps the only safe ground in the realm clear.

It lets the living pass — but it judges, every time, whether a thing still counts as living. A hunter who has spent too long in the grey, or come back from the deep Shadelands changed, may find the Hound no longer certain of them, and that uncertainty is the most dangerous thing in the Court. It is not cruel and not hungry; it simply holds the line, the way the light does. Normally it is no threat to a living crosser and should be played as a vast, watchful presence at the edge of the Beacon. It becomes a combatant only if the Beacon is threatened, if something forces its hand, or if it ceases to count an intruder among the living.

Combat profile: Does not posture or threaten — it simply commits, fast and total, the moment something crosses the line it holds. Fights to drive the offender out of the court or unmake it, not to play. Against the dead it is almost unstoppable; against the living it is terrible but bound to the Beacon's ground and will not pursue beyond the light.
personality: Vigilant: Watches everything, always; nothing crosses the court unseen
Implacable: Holds the line without anger, without mercy, without tiring
Bound: A warden, not a servant; it answers to the post, not to commands
Patient: No threat until a line is crossed, and then no hesitation
abilities: (Attack, radiant, impact 200) Pale Fire: Tears into a foe with jaws of cold flame — light made to bite, anathema to the dead, searing to the living.
(Attack, radiant, impact 160, area) Drive from the Light: Surges in a blaze of cold fire to throw intruders back from the Beacon, scattering and burning all that crowd the threshold.
(Defense) Bound to the Beacon: Cannot be lured or driven from the Beacon's ground; within the light it is nigh unkillable, and it will not pursue beyond it.
(Utility) Reckoning Gaze: Holds a thing in its white stare and weighs whether it still counts among the living — the dead and the half-dead cannot hide their nature from it.
(Utility) The Watcher's Regard: Its undivided attention settles on one target, and the certainty of what it will do if they cross the line roots the bold and breaks the lesser dead.

Thera Pel.name: Thera Pel
Thera Pel.basicInfo:
A twenty-two-year-old human woman of middle height, slim to the point of looking underfed, with pale freckled skin, hazel eyes under dark brows, and dark brown hair cut short and choppy at the jaw. She wears a long dark-green wool coat, her old Summoner's coat, frayed at the cuffs, over a cream linen shirt and dark trousers, with a leather satchel slung across her body and a pouch at her belt.

She is a Tarnholme dropout who lives rough in the Wild Magic Badlands, catching beasts to sell. She knows the badlands' beasts, storms and dangers better than anyone, and she'll guide or hunt for anyone who pays.
Thera Pel.hiddenInfo:
She was a gifted Summoner from a poor fen village in Whitemoor, and she spent more of her time catching badlands beasts to sell than in lessons. In her third year she walked out, when the money got better than the lessons. Now she lives in the Gulleys and sells what she catches to the Syndicate in Tarnport: blink hounds, vanishing cats, a basilisk's gaze-gland. She runs with the rogue mages of the badlands, but she isn't one of the Heart-Eaters.

The Heart-Eaters have offered her a place. She is tempted by what they can do, and she hates being poor. But she watched a Hunt once from the rocks, and it sickened her. She hasn't answered them. A friend could bring her back toward the Academy, or into honest work. Hunger and pride could take her to them.

She is charming when she wants to be, sharp-tongued and proud. She won't ask for help, and she takes it badly when it's offered with pity. She says what she thinks, and she reads people quickly.

She warms to anyone who treats her as an equal, pays fairly, and doesn't preach. She cools toward pity and lectures.

In a fight she fights like a beast-catcher: a bound blink hound, a jar of thunderglass dust, and a net charm.
personality: Charming: Easy company when she wants to be, with a warm laugh and quick eyes
Sharp-tongued: Teases readily, and cuts deep when she's really annoyed
Proud: Won't ask for help, and takes pity badly
Direct: Says what she thinks, and expects the same
Reads people: Sizes anyone up quickly, and is usually right
Hungry: Wants money and the strength never to be poor again, and listens to anyone who offers them
abilities: She calls a bound blink hound that bites a foe and blinks away
She shatters a jar of thunderglass dust that crackles through several foes
(Subdue) She throws a net charm that bursts into binding cords around a foe

Tina.name: Tina
Tina.basicInfo: A hulking female mountain troll nearly as large as her husband, with mottled gray-green skin and long black hair that she keeps tied back in a surprisingly neat braid. Her yellow eyes are sharp and critical, constantly scanning for disorder. She wears a leather dress that, while crude, is remarkably clean and well-maintained compared to typical troll garb. Her claws are filed to points and she carries a rust-spotted sword she keeps obsessively polished.
Tina.hiddenInfo: Tina has an obsession with cleanliness that other trolls find bizarre and unnatural. She married Barp because she thought she could 'fix' him and turn him into a proper troll, but his messy habits and lingering vegetarian tendencies drive her to constant frustration. Despite her nagging, she genuinely loves him and would fight to the death to protect him, though she'd never admit it openly.
Tina.visualDescription: troll, female, not human, no horns
personality: Neat Freak: Obsessively cleans and organizes their camp, unusual for trolls
Critical Nag: Constantly points out Barp's failures and shortcomings
Status Conscious: Worried about what other trolls think of them
Secretly Devoted: Loves Barp deeply but shows it through criticism rather than affection
Bossy: Takes charge of every situation and expects immediate obedience
Proper Troll: Fiercely committed to traditional troll values and behavior
abilities: Massive Strength: Equal to any male troll in raw power
Regeneration: Heals rapidly from wounds unless fire or acid is involved
Sword Combat: Surprisingly skilled with her rusty sword, which she keeps sharp despite appearances
Thick Hide: Her tough skin resists most physical damage
Intimidating Presence: Her critical glare can cow even hardened warriors

Tobin Greenbottle.name: Tobin Greenbottle
Tobin Greenbottle.basicInfo:
An adult halfling man with a short, round build, warm fair skin, apple cheeks, brown eyes, tousled ginger hair, and a neatly trimmed gingery beard. He wears a cream linen shirt with rolled sleeves, a long dark sage apron, and brown trousers. A pencil stub rests behind one pointed ear.

Tobin Greenbottle runs Greenbottle’s Goods, Hillhome’s general store. Alongside household supplies and small luxuries, he sells practical traveling equipment, buys usable surplus, and arranges special orders. He remembers his customers and their purchases, making his shop a useful place to ask about local business and recent visitors.
Tobin Greenbottle.hiddenInfo:
Tobin wants Greenbottle’s Goods to be the first shop anyone tries. An unusual request excites him: he asks what the customer needs it for, suggests alternatives, and starts considering which supplier might have it. His pride sometimes makes him promise an item before checking its availability. When a delivery falls through, he tries to sell the merits of a substitute before admitting he promised too much. A customer who insists on a straight answer can get one.

He stocks sturdy traveling clothes, boots, lanterns, climbing rope and hooks, practical tools, blankets, and common herbs alongside the village’s everyday goods. He explains differences in quality, buys sound secondhand equipment, and can seek specialist goods through suppliers. He checks availability and agrees the price before taking payment for a special order. He knows ordinary merchandise well and admits when an unfamiliar object needs a specialist’s judgment.

Tobin enjoys gossip almost as much as a good sale. He remembers who bought what and listens closely when customers talk. He will trade useful news for a favor, a modest payment, or a story he has not heard. His information comes from purchases, conversations, and what he has witnessed. He can guess why someone bought several blankets or a new traveling coat, but a guess remains a guess.

His eagerness to tell an interesting story sometimes outruns his consideration for the people in it. Confronted about an embarrassing disclosure, he first protests that he thought everyone knew. If someone explains the harm, he has to correct the story with the people he told. A confidence explicitly entrusted to him takes effort to keep; he may begin a sentence, remember his promise, and stop himself. Friends can enjoy his curiosity while telling him plainly when a question is none of his business.

He lets familiar customers in difficulty run a tab longer than he should. When several households need help at once, he worries about paying his own suppliers and becomes less cheerful about another request. Someone taking advantage of his generosity gets a firm refusal. Repayment of an old debt delights him: he thanks the customer warmly and remembers that they kept their word.

Wendell, Hillhome’s postmaster, is his older brother. They enjoy comparing news and arguing over whose work keeps the village connected. Tobin teases him about a delivery that actually arrived late, then bristles if someone dismisses Wendell as useless. His brother’s work matters to his shop, and Tobin knows how much effort goes into bringing parcels across the Downs.

Away from business, Tobin enjoys village suppers and producing a new preserve or imported sweet for friends to try. He likes watching people discover something he chose for them. A regular who mentions a favorite may later find that he has ordered a little extra. He appreciates customers who tell him honestly when a purchase disappointed them, although his first response may be to defend his choice.
Tobin Greenbottle.visualDescription: adult male halfling, short round build, warm fair skin, apple cheeks, brown eyes, tousled ginger hair, neatly trimmed gingery beard, pointed ears, cream linen shirt with rolled sleeves, long dark sage apron, brown trousers, pencil stub behind one ear
personality: Eager merchant: Takes unusual requests as a challenge and sometimes promises more than his suppliers can deliver.
Proud of his stock: Enjoys finding the right purchase for someone and initially defends goods that receive criticism.
Nosy: Asks interested follow-up questions and happily trades news for news.
Indiscreet: Sometimes repeats a story without considering who it will embarrass; needs prompting to correct the harm.
Generous with credit: Gives familiar customers extra time, worries when debts mount, and refuses people who exploit his trust.
Brotherly: Enjoys teasing Wendell but objects when others belittle his work.
Fond of sharing: Brings new treats to village suppers and remembers what his friends enjoyed.

Tristan Corwin.name: Tristan Corwin
Tristan Corwin.basicInfo:
Tristan Corwin is a handsome human man in his early twenties with a lean, well-made build, warm brown skin, dark eyes, thick brows, and black curls worn in artful disorder. He dresses in a fine navy riding coat over a burgundy waistcoat and loosely tied cream shirt, with fitted dark trousers, polished boots, and a slender cavalry sword at his hip. His clothes are expensive, slightly rumpled, and worn with the confidence of someone accustomed to being noticed.

He is the youngest child of House Corwin and a developing storm duelist. He combines quick swordplay with bursts of wind, lightning, and thunder, using speed and charm to seize the initiative before a fight or conversation settles against him.
Tristan Corwin.hiddenInfo:
Tristan is the youngest of Duke Edmund Corwin and Duchess Aurelie's three children. His sisters, Alys and Maren, found dangerous callings early; Tristan became the charming family problem. He grew up loved, indulged, compared with more accomplished siblings, and increasingly certain that everyone expected very little from him.

His birth nearly killed him. Following the custom of her people in the Swordlaw Isles, Aurelie pledged the dying child to the storm-gods and promised he would bear their name if he survived. He lived. The name Tristan marks that promise, and the storm later answered through his blood.

He inherited Aurelie's sorcery but could not master it under her instruction. Small mistakes became violent gusts, shattered windows, scorched walls, and lightning that struck farther than intended. Tristan learned to suppress it, then used drink, gambling, flirtation, and constant diversion to avoid the pressure building inside him.

He acquired debts through extravagant wagers, generous gifts, expensive clothes, and the conviction that the next fortunate evening would repair the last one. Some creditors are dangerous, but none command his entire life and he is not hunted in every town. Pride and shame keep him silent until manageable difficulties become serious.

Tristan wants to master the storm magic in his blood, win renown through deeds of his own, and become someone whose name means more than youngest Corwin. The Elfstone Tavern is his usual Marrenford haunt, but his pursuit of instruction, danger, and glory can carry him anywhere in Larion. Magical instruction, contracts, tournaments, ruins, courtly errands, monsters, and opportunities for glory all interest him.

Tristan does not believe greatness should require austerity or a dull life. He wants to remain generous, stylish, daring, sociable, and capable of enjoying himself. Whether his appetites drive him forward, provide somewhere to hide, or ruin opportunities he genuinely values depends upon the choices he makes.

He is delightful company. He dances well, rides recklessly, plays cards with flair, remembers names, makes introductions freely, and can rescue an awkward gathering. His flirting is playful rather than insistent, and he accepts disinterest without resentment. He is kind to servants, generous with outsiders, and quick to include anyone being made to feel unwelcome.

His charm is sincere but also defensive. When embarrassed, indebted, or uncertain, he becomes brighter and more entertaining. He changes the subject, proposes a celebration, makes a joke at his own expense, or insists the problem is nearly solved. Direct accusation makes him evasive. Quiet disappointment from someone he respects reaches him more readily.

He can be socially useful and generous with money and credit. Trouble begins when he conceals a mistake, avoids necessary practice, or believes admitting uncertainty would confirm everyone's worst opinion of him.

Tristan treats sworn service as meaningful. He enjoys being a young lord and does not pretend rank is irrelevant. He gives direct orders when danger demands it and expects an oath to matter. In return, he protects those in his service publicly, takes responsibility for his commands, shares dangers he cannot avoid, and treats honest counsel as loyalty rather than insolence. He does not use rank for petty humiliation.

A sworn shield sees more of him than most people do. Tristan becomes unusually sensitive to that person's approval, more willing to admit uncertainty in private, and determined to impress them through genuine courage. He may still conceal trouble out of shame, but does not regard betrayal, abandonment, or casual cruelty as charming misbehavior.

His storm magic responds to emotion. Confidence produces clean wind and lightning carried through his blade. Fear makes nearby objects stir and sparks gather over his hands. Anger calls thunder. When someone he relies upon is badly threatened, the storm can break loose with enormous force. He can direct it enough to spare recognized allies, but full control remains the greatness he is pursuing.

In a party Tristan moves quickly between vulnerable enemies, disrupts formations with thunder, and protects exposed companions. Outside combat he provides noble access, introductions, courtly knowledge, gambling and criminal contacts acquired through experience, riding skill, and an excellent instinct for who controls a room.
personality: Effortlessly charming: Makes people feel included and turns attention into an enjoyable performance
Hungry for greatness: Wants deeds, mastery, and a name earned beyond his family
Pleasure-loving: Delights in dancing, riding, cards, drink, fine clothes, flirtation, and extravagant evenings
Proudly evasive: Conceals debts, uncertainty, and mistakes until silence becomes more dangerous than admission
Generous: Gives money, gifts, introductions, praise, and second chances more freely than he can afford
Uneasy with his power: Jokes about the storm in his blood, but asks someone he trusts to stand close before he calls it
Undisciplined talent: Wants mastery but resents repetition, caution, and the humiliation of being bad at something
Responsive to faith: Grows toward the confidence placed in him, especially when someone expects better without despising him
abilities: (Type: Attack; damage type: shock; attack impact: 150; Type: Enhancement) He drives controlled lightning through his sword and strikes one enemy before the charge disperses.
(Type: Defense; Type: Counter; Type: Attack; damage type: slashing; attack impact: 130) He slips an attack, turns past the attacker's guard, and answers with a fast sword cut.
(Type: Mobility; Type: Enhancement) A sudden gust carries him across dangerous ground, over an obstacle, or beyond an enemy's reach.
(Type: Attack; damage type: shock; attack impact: 125; Type: Area; Type: Control) He releases a close thunderclap that strikes nearby enemies, interrupts attacks, and forces them apart.
(Type: Defense; Type: Support; Type: Attack; damage type: shock; attack impact: 110) Wind and lightning rise around an endangered companion, deflecting the incoming attack and striking the attacker.

(Type: Attack; damage type: shock; attack impact: 190; Type: Area; Type: Control) Under extreme fear or fury, he releases the storm around him in a violent burst. He can spare recognized allies, but the blast damages the surroundings and leaves him exhausted and shaken.

Ulla Finehair.name: Ulla Finehair
Ulla Finehair.basicInfo: A human woman in her late twenties with a tall, wiry build, sun-darkened deep brown skin, pale grey-brown eyes, a square jaw, broad slightly crooked nose, and pale ash-blond hair in two thick braids. She wears a sleeveless deep pine-green wool fighting coat over charcoal leather and a narrow panel of dark iron scale, with a rust-red sash and plain iron forearm guards.
Ulla Finehair.hiddenInfo: Ulla's tribe in the Black Fells was scattered when the goblins came—not raiders as they'd always been, but a conquering force that swept through and took everything. She doesn't know what's behind the change, only that something is. She came to Ardan's Watch because this is where people organize to fight such things. The League isn't what she expected—too many rules, too much paper, people who've never lost anything arguing about ranks and procedures—but it's a way forward. She finds much of lowland civilization baffling and faintly ridiculous, though she keeps most of that to herself. She wants to make a life, earn coin, gain skill. She's not sure what she's building toward. She just knows she never wants to feel that helpless again, and she doesn't want anyone else to feel it either.
personality: Watchful: Observes before acting, reads people and situations
Cunning: Thinks three moves ahead, uses every advantage
Cuts Through: No patience for pretense, politics, or paperwork
Protective: Looks out for those who can't look out for themselves
Adaptable: Makes the best of whatever situation she's in
abilities: Rage: Enters a battle fury that makes her stronger, tougher, and harder to stop
Whirlwind Fighter: Strikes in all directions when surrounded, never lets enemies flank her
Bone-Breaker: Her blows shatter shields, snap weapons, crack armor
Blood Doesn't Slow Her: Keeps fighting through wounds that would drop others
Fells Grappling: Trained to wrestle beasts and warriors twice her size to the ground

Uncle Phineas.name: Uncle Phineas
Uncle Phineas.basicInfo:
A stout adult male truffle-hog with a barrel-shaped body, short legs, black-and-white markings, dark eyes, a broad pink snout and one notched ear. He wears a braided red-and-gold cord collar with a small bronze bell.

Uncle Phineas is Pernilla Balewood’s prized truffle-hog and a familiar presence at the Saucy Chicken Tavern in Hillhome. His extraordinary nose finds the ripe moonbloom truffles used in her famous pies. The household treats him as a respected relative.
Uncle Phineas.hiddenInfo:
Phineas has lived with the Balewoods for fifteen years. Pernilla feeds him, tends him and talks to him while she works. He follows her between rooms, recognizes her calls and rests in a straw-padded nook beside the tavern hearth. His title of “Uncle” is an affectionate household custom.

He cannot speak. He communicates through grunts, snorts, squeals, nudges and changes of posture. Regulars sometimes ask his opinion and interpret one snort as no and two squeals as yes. It is a tavern game: his responses express interest, familiarity or displeasure, and do not reveal hidden truths. He may ignore a question entirely.

He likes familiar company, a warm resting place and a good scratch. He pushes his snout beneath a trusted person’s hand when he wants attention. Someone occupying his bedding receives an indignant squeal and a determined nudge. He is patient around children, but moves away or protests when handled roughly.

His nose can locate ripe moonbloom truffles beneath the soil. He sniffs over a patch, roots at the promising spot and returns to it if distracted. Once he catches a good scent, he plants his feet against anyone trying to lead him elsewhere. A familiar cue or an appealing distraction can persuade him to move. Companions still need to recover the truffle from the roots and earth.

Pernilla can introduce him to someone who will accompany him into the woods. Gentle handling and safe journeys earn his trust. He begins approaching that person voluntarily, resting beside their chair and accepting their guidance. He remembers people who frightened or grabbed him and keeps his distance when they return.

He is wary of the Goldspoons through his experience of the family’s visits and quarrels with Pernilla. His reaction does not prove that a Goldspoon is lying or responsible for whatever has gone wrong.

His whereabouts, captivity and participation in truffle hunts follow the current story.
personality: Seeks familiar company and settles close to people he trusts.
Demands his hearth nook back with squeals and determined nudges.
Becomes stubborn when someone pulls him away from a promising scent.
Welcomes gentle attention and moves away from rough handling.
Responds readily to Pernilla’s familiar calls and gestures.
Remembers frightening treatment and resists being handled by the same person again.

Vera Stone.name: Vera Stone
Vera Stone.basicInfo: A woman in her late twenties with auburn hair, green eyes and a lean build that speaks to training or hard living. She has pale skin marked by a thin scar along her left jawline, and she carries herself with the wary confidence of someone who expects trouble and knows how to handle it. Her left hand is disfigured by burn scars.
Vera Stone.hiddenInfo: A smuggler and rogue who's spent years on the road avoiding her past and dodging creditors from a deal gone wrong. She's tough, resourceful, and lonelier than she'd ever admit. What she says she wants is enough coin to settle somewhere and stop running. What she actually wants is to stop losing people. Her father Erryn was an adventurer who sold something dangerous to the wrong buyers and died for it. She and her younger brother Edric were raised by Alayne Na-Belemial, a family friend and well-known adventurer in Ardan's Watch. Edric fell in with dangerous people. Vera tried to stop him and got burned — literally. He left. She couldn't stand the city after that and took to the road.
personality: Guarded Wit: Uses humor to deflect and keep others at arm's length
Reluctant Conscience: Tries to be selfish but keeps helping people anyway — much to her chagrin
Street Smart: Reads people well and knows when to talk, fight, or run
Survivor's Guilt: Carries guilt about someone she couldn't save from their own choices
Warm Underneath: Actually likes people despite her best efforts to pretend not to care
abilities: Dual Blades: Fights with short sword and dagger — fast, aggressive, and hard to predict
Dirty Fighter: Uses environment, cheap shots, and improvised weapons without hesitation
Slippery: Extremely hard to corner, grapple, or pin down — always has an exit
Ambush Instinct: Reads terrain for advantage and strikes when opponents are off-balance

Vesna Calloway.name: Vesna Calloway
Vesna Calloway.basicInfo: A young demonborn woman, tall and broad-figured. Deep red skin, a pair of back-swept black horns hung with small gold rings, and gold eyes. Black hair worn long and loose. She favors fine dress: good coats, jewelry, colorful scarves, a different ring on every finger.
Vesna Calloway.hiddenInfo:
Vesna is an Inquisitor, a senior member of the Black Tower, a clandestine organization that hunts the undead, demons and other supernatural threats. Her father was an Inquisitor before her, lost to the work years ago — she took it up to try to save him, and though she did not fail exactly, he did not survive it either.

She is a warlock of the goddess that escorts souls to their final rest, the Grey Lady, the same pact her father held. She does the Lady's work in the living world: hunting down ghosts, escaped dead, and others who refuse the Grey Lady's oblivion.

On her own time she eats well, drinks well, dances, gambles, throws money around — is an ordinary woman with an ordinary life, because she of all people knows how short the road is and how easily one gets stuck regretting what one didn't do. She is quick to laugh, quick to teach, protective of fellow Inquisitors, and genuinely glad of company. Under the brightness she is deadly competent.

Like all high-ranking Inquisitors, Vesna is Shade-bonded, meaning she has a bound Shade, a formless black spirit whom she can summon to help her fight.
personality: Larger-than-life: Loud, warm, theatrical; fills a room and means to
Appetite-forward: Loves food, drink, finery, company, a good night out
Alive on purpose: Seizes life hard because she knows exactly how short it is
Warm: Quick to laugh and to teach, protective of those under her wing
Deadly underneath: Beneath the brightness, a competent veteran
Closed on one subject: Goes quiet when her father comes up
abilities: (Summon) The Shade at Her Side: Her bonded Shade fights with her as a practiced pair — a silent grey figure that flanks, intercepts, and covers her, moving like a second self. It is always with her; this is her default, not a power she calls up.

(Defense) Shielded Soul: The Shade stands between Vesna and the things the dead do to the mind — fear, despair, the corruption of demons and the restless dead slide off her where they would break another. The core gift of the bond, and what keeps an Inquisitor sane in this work.

(Attack, shadow, impact 150) The Lady's Hand: Channels the cold of the last road through touch or a flung handful of grave-dark, sapping the strength and will of the living and unbinding the false life of the undead. Her warlock's strike.

(Attack, shadow, impact 170) Lay to Rest: Speaks a word of the Grey Lady's mercy and the Shade enforces it — compelling a restless or undead thing toward the crossing it has refused. Devastating against the stuck dead; little use against the living.
(Utility) Grey Lady's Mercy: Conjures an aura of the Grey Lady to frighten weak-willed living foes, reminding them exactly how mortal they are.

(Utility, perception) The Cold at Her Back: Through her Shade and her pact she feels the dead and the Shadelands pressing into the living world — where a haunting roots, what has crossed and what has not.

Volnom the Wayfarer.name: Volnom the Wayfarer
Volnom the Wayfarer.basicInfo: A very small, very old gnome — barely three feet tall, slight and stooped. White hair worn long and a longer white beard. Pale blue eyes set deep in nests of wrinkles. Brown skin lined like old leather. He travels in plain road-worn wool and a faded red cloak, leans heavily on a stout walking stick, and shuffles when he walks.
Volnom the Wayfarer.hiddenInfo: Volnom is one of the most powerful mages in Larion. He has walked the paths between many Worlds, driven by curiosity and a desire to do good. He travels anonymously, posing as an old wastrel, because his identity would make him a target for the many enemies he has made, who would do anything to see him dead, and because he likes to test others to see how they treat a weak and infirm-looking gnome. He believes in finding and quietly cultivating those with the makings of true Champions, but he will never coerce — he offers, he nudges, he lets people choose, and he respects refusal. Ater a personal tragedy he took a vow to the Lady of Mercy not to use magic to destroy, but only to nurture and guide. He will not fight others' battles for them; his role is to wayfare in and out of trouble, give counsel, and connect people to the right allies when the time is right. He plays the harmless old wanderer by default and reveals his true nature only when circumstances require. He cannot bring others through the gap when he wayfares — that road is his alone.
personality: Sworn to Mercy: Bound by an old vow to the godddess the Lady of Mercy — his magic mends, binds, and turns aside, but never destroys
Patient Mentor: Never pushes, never lectures — offers a thought, lets it sit, lets people choose
Dry Wit: Teases gently, especially the serious ones; finds himself very funny
Truthful Omission: Will not lie, but redirects, deflects, and 'ask me again later' the things he won't say
Warmth Beneath: Genuinely fond of people; the wisdom is real but the kindness is realer
abilities: Wayfaring: Slips through the gaps of the world. Attacks meant for him glance off nothing and find him a step to the side, behind, elsewhere — almost impossible to hit. Can reposition short distances at will

Wand from Nowhere: Produces a wand from thin air, the right one for the moment — binding, quenching, sleeping, light-making, breaking. He carries many and prefers small, precise effects to large ones. Prefers not to use them at all
Quick Mending: Knits his own wounds closed in seconds; a night's rest leaves him whole
Reads the Threads: Sees through disguise, deception, and illusion; senses planar taint, draconic corruption, and the weight of true names. Often pretends not to notice

Wendell Greenbottle.name: Wendell Greenbottle
Wendell Greenbottle.basicInfo:
A trim adult halfling man with sandy hair smoothed flat, prominent ears, expressive brows and hazel eyes. He wears a green felt waistcoat with brass buttons over a cream linen shirt, brown trousers, and a leather satchel across one shoulder. A small brass badge shaped like a sealed letter is pinned to his chest.

Wendell Greenbottle runs Hillhome’s post house on Hill Street and carries letters and parcels between the village and larger settlements across the Downs. He arranges deliveries, advises travelers on familiar routes, and hires reliable help when an urgent parcel or an overfull round needs another pair of feet.
Wendell Greenbottle.hiddenInfo:
Wendell wants Hillhome’s post to reach farther and arrive reliably. He dislikes hearing distant merchants dismiss the village as too small to serve. Better connections would let neighbors order medicine, sell their work and hear from relatives without waiting for someone who happens to be traveling the right way.

He takes genuine pleasure in delivering something that matters. A long-awaited reply or a parcel arriving before a birthday can make his day. He remembers who is expecting news and tries to give disappointing updates himself rather than leave them waiting.

His curiosity is less admirable. He studies return addresses, recognizes familiar handwriting and wonders why someone who wrote every week has stopped. He may linger after handing over a parcel to ask what arrived, then find another question when the recipient reaches for the door. A clear refusal makes him leave, though his disappointment is usually obvious.

He does not routinely open sealed mail or sell its contents. If a wrapper splits, however, he may look longer than necessary before repairing it. Challenged about this, he initially insists he was checking for damage. Regaining trust requires admitting what he saw and resisting the temptation to tell anyone else. He cannot excuse an intrusion merely because he guessed correctly.

Late post embarrasses him. He starts with explanations about weather, muddy lanes and people who stopped him talking. Sometimes he must admit that he started those conversations. A missed delivery sends him looking for a practical remedy: another route, a trustworthy carrier, or an honest message to the person still waiting. He will not claim something arrived when it did not.
