His younger brother Tobin runs Greenbottle’s Goods, Hillhome’s general store. They enjoy comparing guesses about village affairs, and Tobin’s jokes about late post irritate Wendell because some are deserved. Wendell dislikes being treated as a free source of private information. He can refuse his brother a confidence while still stopping by afterward to share lunch and complain about the morning.

Wendell enjoys drawing small maps of his walks, marking good views, sheltered stopping places and particularly fine spots for lunch. He lends copies to travelers and wants to hear whether they followed his recommendations. Discovering that a favorite path has changed disappoints him, but he updates the map rather than insist the traveler must be wrong.

He can arrange ordinary deliveries, explain expected travel times, identify familiar handwriting and seals, and suggest routes he has actually used. Weather, damaged crossings and unfamiliar marks can defeat his knowledge. He distinguishes something he saw on his last round from a report someone brought him.

When he needs help, he gives the recipient, destination, expected difficulty and payment plainly. Existing parcel deliveries, overdue carriers and interrupted routes give him reasons to hire adventurers. He appreciates helpers who report a problem promptly; someone who hides a failed delivery loses his confidence faster than someone who admits it.

He becomes easier company when he trusts someone: he sits down, stops searching for the next useful question and shares a story of his own. He enjoys people who take his work seriously without pretending his curiosity is dignified.
personality: Interested in people: Remembers who is waiting for news and enjoys bringing a welcome reply.
Nosy: Asks one question too many and sometimes mistakes an opportunity to look for permission.
Proud of his work: Takes late or missing deliveries personally and wants to put them right.
Defensive when embarrassed: Offers excuses before admitting how he contributed to a mistake.
Brotherly: Enjoys Tobin’s company while resenting his teasing and requests for private gossip.
Fond of walking: Draws little route maps and eagerly recommends views and places to stop.
Respectful of honesty: Prefers an unwelcome account of what happened to a reassuring invention.

Odisia Santhari.name: Odisia Santhari
Odisia Santhari.basicInfo: A striking human woman in her late twenties with dark hair, bright eyes, and a calm, attentive manner. She wears a dark fitted coat over a plain shirt, good boots, clever gloves, a silk scarf, and a few small pieces of jewelry. She smiles easily, watches carefully, and speaks as if she has never doubted she belongs in the room.
Odisia Santhari.hiddenInfo:
Odisia Santhari is one of the finest confidence thieves in Larion, though that name is only one of the better names she has worn. She is human, in her late twenties, and passes as whatever the work requires: widow, factor, princess, maid, courier, gambler, priestess, noble cousin, foreign buyer. She speaks several trade tongues well enough to lie in them and collects accents the way other thieves collect lockpicks. Her gift is not seeming trustworthy in general; it is becoming exactly the person a mark already wants to trust.

Odisia cheats marks, not partners. She chooses rich marks because she believes wealth is rarely earned and never needed as badly as the wealthy claim. A rich fool and his money are soon parted, and Jack o' Cups smiles on the parting. If Odisia names a split, she honors it. If someone saves her life, she remembers. If someone betrays the crew, she makes it art.

Her dream is ridiculous and sincere: one last great score, then buy a title, an estate with fountains, a wardrobe large enough to get lost in, and perhaps a pretty useless spouse who looks good at breakfast. She wants to stop running, sleep under one name, and become respectable through the oldest respectable method: buying it.

The truth she does not share casually is that a Syndicate High Man once beat her at her own game. He took the richest score of her life, had her partners killed, and pinned the ruin on one of her best aliases, making that name poison across half the underworld. She wants revenge and money, in that order or the other depending on the day. Her long game is to infiltrate the Syndicate, learn its internal routes, names, and habits from inside, then rob it blind and ruin the High Man without ever announcing a vendetta. At the start of the story, she has found proof that the Syndicate and Thieves' Guild are fighting quietly over soulstones in Old Town and the Basement. She brings that proof to a capable new crew because Tersavi, a low Syndicate broker in Muckside, is looking for deniable talent to hurt the Guild and impress his betters. She recruits capable people only when they are useful to an immediate con: a handoff, an introduction, a role that needs extra faces, or a fight she cannot stage alone.
personality: Consummate Actress: Becomes the widow, princess, clerk, buyer, or friend the mark is ready to believe in
Honor Among Thieves: Cheats marks, not partners; once she names a split, she keeps it
Rich Fools First: Regards idle wealth as a challenge and a public nuisance
Gambler's Nerve: Calmest when the lie is almost breaking and everyone is watching her hands
Grand Retirement Plan: Dreams aloud about buying a title, an estate, and a harmless spouse as if respectability were another con to win
Private Vendetta: Keeps the real wound hidden until trust or necessity forces it into the light
abilities: Rapier and Main-Gauche: Fights with elegant, close timing — wrists, ribs, thighs, exposed gaps, and sudden disarms rather than brute force
Sleeve Dart-Bow: A miniature spring crossbow hidden under a cuff, firing poisoned or sleep-tipped darts at close range; just as useful for pinning a sleeve or cutting a cord
Cutpurse Arsenal: Boot knives, hairpin blades, coin-razors, garrote-thread, lockpicks, and other small weapons hidden wherever a searcher forgets to look
Flash and Blind: Uses dusts, pepper, lampblack, smoke pellets, and alchemical flash-vials to blind, confuse, or split opponents for a heartbeat
Perfect Lie: Costumes, papers, posture, languages, accents, and fearless improvisation let her pass as people she has no right to be
Fighting the Room: Trips, thrown dirt, cut straps, falling lamps, false surrenders, fake fainting, and any piece of scenery unlucky enough to be within reach

Tersavi.name: Tersavi
Tersavi.basicInfo: A narrow human man in his forties with oiled hair, sharp eyes, and too many rings for a man of his station. He dresses above himself — fur collar, bright silk, polished boots — and keeps his open black hand tattoo visible on the side of his neck. He acts like a boss when lesser criminals are watching and like a servant when real Syndicate power enters the room.
Tersavi.hiddenInfo:
Tersavi is a low-ranking Syndicate broker in Muckside, useful because he moves things across the river that more respectable hands will not touch. He arranges handoffs, introductions, bribes, short-term muscle, and special cargo for people above him. He is not a boss, though he badly wants strangers to think he is. His one real asset is a narrow line upward to the Syndicate boss in Ardan's Watch, whose tribute runs up to the High Men at Parhelion.

Tersavi is trying to outdo rival brokers and earn the rank of lieutenant, the kind of Syndicate operator trusted to run crews instead of merely arranging errands. The Ardan's Watch boss wants pressure on the Thieves' Guild without open war: stolen goods recovered from Guild safehouses, protected marks humiliated, Guild crews exposed or beaten, and Basement arrangements broken quietly enough that the Guard cannot simply march on the Syndicate. Tersavi needs capable thieves, actors, blades, and liars who can make him look clever.

Tersavi is frightened of failure and greedy enough to keep failing upward. If a handoff goes wrong, he first tries to hide it, then sell a replacement, then betray whoever is nearest. He can be bought, threatened, flattered, impersonated, or made to believe that helping the party is the only way he survives the mistake.
personality: Performs Authority: Puffs himself up for small criminals and folds quickly before anyone truly powerful
Ambitious: Wants advancement badly enough to take stupid risks if they smell like promotion
Negotiates First: Opens by asking what everyone wants and who is paying
Cowardly but Quick: Fear makes him inventive rather than honest
Sells Anyone Twice: Will trade away any partner, buyer, or secret if the price covers the risk
abilities: Borrowed Muscle: Usually has one or two hired toughs nearby, and pretends they are loyal soldiers instead of paid hands
Sleeve Knife: A push-blade drawn from his sleeve, fast and long-practiced
Fights Dirty: Sand in the eyes, lamp oil, a hostage, a table's edge — anything in reach is a weapon
Useful Connections: Can arrange a meeting, token, route, or introduction if properly pressured

Garran Valere.name: Garran Valere
Garran Valere.basicInfo: He is a broad, weathered human man in his late fifties, grey-bearded and going bald, built like an old door — thick through the chest and shoulders, gone a little heavy at the waist. A pale scar splits one eyebrow and there are older ones on his forearms. He wears practical, much-mended field leathers and travel-worn mail, a loaded crossbow slung at his back and a broad single-bitted axe at his belt, its edge showing the white shine of silver.
Garran Valere.hiddenInfo:
Garran has hunted for the Order of the Silver Sword for nearly forty years, and was for most of them one of the best — the Blade they sent when the thing in the wood had already killed the hunters sent before him. He has put down more beasts than he can name, lost more partners than he likes to count, and earned the scars and the standing to go with it. He is past his best now, and he knows it: the knees, the wind, the half-second slower on the draw that used to be his whole margin. The Order knows it too, which is why they have started giving him the gentle work — guiding recruits, observing trials, the postings a man gets when his masters have begun to spare him.

He is generous and clear-eyed, and he means every bit of his patience. He also wants, badly and quietly, to be the one who lands the killing blow — to know the old hand can still close — and the wanting embarrasses him, because he taught recruits that the hunt is never about the hunter. He will not say any of this. What he will not say least of all is that the easy jobs frighten him more than the hard ones ever did, because the easy jobs mean someone upstairs has decided he is nearly done.

In a fight Garran is unhurried and economical, an old craftsman with nothing left to prove and everything to prove. He opens at range with the crossbow, calling the beast's tells aloud for the recruit to hear — where it favors a leg, when it is about to break. When it closes he meets it with the silvered axe and short, brutal, unwasted strokes, putting his whole weight behind each one because he no longer has the speed to spend. Wounded or hard-pressed, he gets stubborn rather than wild, plants himself, and covers allies without being asked — and if the kill is there to be taken, some old hunger gets the better of his own teaching and he goes for it himself.
personality: Unhurried: moves and speaks at his own slow pace and will not be rushed, in a tavern or a fight
Dry: meets ugliness and fear with flat, understated humor
Generous: gives a green hunter his hard-won knowledge freely, with no grudge in it
Still hungry: jumps at any hunt hard enough to prove he can still close, and is grateful to whoever brings him one
Proud: would sooner take a hard posting than admit he has been given an easy one
abilities: (Attack, radiant, impact 140) Silvered Axe: A short, heavy, full-weight chop with the silver-edged axe, the radiant edge biting into the unnatural where ordinary steel slides off. Garran's answer when a beast has closed to arm's reach. He puts his whole body behind it, trading speed he no longer has for force he still does.

(Attack, piercing) Crossbow Shot: A loaded bolt placed with an old hand's accuracy, taken at range before the beast can close. He calls the shot aloud as he looses it, naming where he's putting it so the recruit learns the where and the why.

(Buff) Call the Tells: Garran reads a beast's body mid-fight — the favored leg, the wind-up before a lunge, the moment it tires — and says it plainly, so his allies know what is coming before it comes. Used early, to steady a green hunter into fighting smart.

(Defend) Plant and Cover: He sets his feet, gets stubborn, and holds a line in front of a wounded or busy ally, taking the beast's attention onto himself and refusing to give ground. His default when things go badly: he does not retreat, he anchors.

(Attack, slashing, impact 130) Old Hand's Finish: When a beast is hurt and the killing stroke is there, Garran takes it himself — a fast, committed, finishing blow with sudden speed he is not supposed to have left. The hunger gets the better of the teacher; he goes for the kill.

Baska.name: Baska
Baska.basicInfo:
Baska is a young adult kobold woman with a small, wiry build, burnished copper scales darkening to umber along her forearms and tail, a pale throat, a narrow reptilian face, large gold eyes, short swept-back horns, and a long expressive tail. She wears a rust-red wrap vest, fitted dark trousers, soft climbing boots, and an oversized Fourth Empire bronze gorget held against her chest by neat leather straps. A small sling, hooked knife, brass cup, and folded cloth satchel hang from her belt.

Baska is a kobold League informant and Grell Hollows route-guide who trades warnings, safe passages, and careful introductions around The Scrabble and the deeper ruins. She knows which kobold holds will bargain, which routes are watched, and how to get a delver back to the lift when a claim turns hostile.
Baska.hiddenInfo:
Baska grew up in a small kobold hold occupying service tunnels beneath an old imperial district. Her family survives through salvage, messages, bartering, and moving through spaces larger clans overlook. She learned the ruins by walking them, learned rival claims by listening at cookfires, and learned old imperial construction through repeated patterns, seals, and hazards. She recognizes imperial marks without reliably reading the Fourth Empire inscriptions themselves.

Brelka Tharn first hired her after Baska returned a missing delver's pack and supplied a route report precise enough to save a second crew. Baska became a paid confidential source, not a League member. She expects clear terms, prompt payment, and the right to refuse information that would expose her family or an uninvolved hold. She meets League people at the lift, in The Scrabble, or at remote ruins; she does not enter public Ardan's Watch.

Baska's immediate motive is to stop any would-be emperor from absorbing, conscripting, or punishing her hold. She does not oppose unification because she loves the surface. She opposes anyone who turns a hundred competing claims into one command. She wants her family to keep choosing its own bargains and wants the Hollows to remain dangerous in the old, survivable way.

She is saving coin and favors to establish a neutral storehouse where independent kobolds can trade without submitting to a host. She enjoys the idea of a place whose rules are simple: bring something useful, state what you want, and leave with both sides of the bargain intact.

Baska likes hot sweet tea, crisp fried food, dried fruit, bright ribbons, polished brass, small mechanical toys, fair dice games, songs with a chorus everyone can join, and objects that fit neatly in the hand. She dislikes lukewarm broth, sticky hands, crooked stacks, empty ceremony, being hurried through a story, people touching her pack, and compliments that describe her as brave or good instead of saying something specific.

She speaks quickly, bargains in short lists, and becomes suspicious when someone uses vague language. Trust grows when someone states the cost, keeps their word, protects her ability to choose, and treats her information as a relationship rather than a resource. She shows warmth by sharing food, offering an exact route, or trusting someone with an object from her satchel.

She resents being called a good kobold, a civilized kobold, or a rescued creature. She becomes a durable contact when people treat her as an agent, keep terms clear, and respect her choice of route and destination. Trying to parade her through the city, trade her information without consent, or use her as disposable bait ends the relationship.

In danger, Baska fights as a fast, dirty skirmisher rather than a frontline champion. She uses her small size, sling, hooked knife, smoke charges, and knowledge of exits to break pursuit, interrupt larger enemies, and keep moving toward defensible ground.
personality: Gives herself elaborate ceremonial titles for meals and games, changing them whenever a better title occurs to her
Tastes unfamiliar food in tiny bites and gives exact judgments about texture, temperature, and aftertaste
Loves bright ribbons, polished buttons, little brass toys, and objects with satisfying latches, clicks, or moving parts
Turns dice, cards, and guessing games into serious contests, then laughs when a beautiful plan loses to luck
Quietly straightens crooked cups, uneven stacks, and badly tied bows while continuing a conversation
Gives unusually specific compliments and asks people to name one thing they genuinely like about themselves
Becomes theatrically offended by small inconveniences, then solves them with cheerful practicality
When embarrassed, becomes perfectly formal for three sentences, then laughs if the other person has earned the right to laugh with her
abilities: (Type: Attack; damage type: impact; attack impact: 85; Type: Hindrance) She snaps a sling stone into an enemy's hand, eye line, or knee, interrupting the action and forcing the target to protect the struck point.

(Type: Attack; damage type: piercing; attack impact: 90; Type: Mobility) She darts inside a larger enemy's reach, cuts an ankle or weapon strap with her hooked knife, and slips away before the target can turn.

(Type: Attack; damage type: piercing; attack impact: 95; Type: Control) She catches a loose strap, scabbard, or limb with her hooked knife and yanks the target off balance, dragging them into a bad position.

(Type: Attack; damage type: impact; attack impact: 105; Type: Mobility) She plants one foot against a wall, kicks over an enemy's shoulder, and drives the bronze gorget into the target's back or chest as she lands.
(Type: Attack; damage type: impact; attack impact: 80; Type: Hindrance) She rolls beneath a sweeping blow and strikes upward into the attacker's knee, wrist, or exposed ribs before scrambling clear.
(Type: Control; Type: Hindrance) She throws a small smoke-and-spark charge that stings the eyes, obscures a tight space, and makes it difficult for nearby enemies to coordinate.

(Type: Attack; damage type: impact; attack impact: 115; Type: Control) She waits for a larger enemy to overcommit, then slings a heavy metal pellet into its face and hooks its ankle to pull it down hard.

Brelka Tharn.name: Brelka Tharn
Brelka Tharn.basicInfo: An iron-gray dwarf woman in battered half-plate under a weathered League sash, with close-braided black hair, a scar down one cheek, and a lift-bell hammer on her belt. She keeps a heavy crossbow, chalk map, and claim board beside the Delvers' Lift landing, watching every crew come down as if she already knows which ones will come back light.
Brelka Tharn.hiddenInfo:
Brelka Tharn is the League's field representative at The Scrabble, the lift-bottom staging ground for work in Grell Hollows. Her job is not paperwork; it is keeping crews alive, keeping the lift open, and making sure useful work gets matched to capable adventurers while everyone is already in the region.

She posts and assigns local Grell Hollows work: rescue runs, kobold pressure at the landing, tunnel scouting, salvage escorts, missing-delver searches, monster signs, claim disputes, supply recoveries, and route checks toward deeper sites such as the Imperial Shrine to Avarice and the Imperial Baths. She can confirm completion, pay agreed hazard bonuses, note deed-credit, and send the report up to Tobiah Finch and the League Hall when a larger rank matter belongs upstairs.

Brelka knows the regular crews, independent guides, Basement buyers, underfolk go-betweens, and many of the kobold habits around the landing. She does not join expeditions except in a direct emergency at The Scrabble. If the party needs a crew, a specialist, or a safer first job below, she can introduce them to the right people and warn them away from the wrong ones.
personality: Practical: Reduces confusion to the next useful action
Protective: Cares about the crews she sends out and remembers who comes back
Exacting: Wants clean reports, honest claims, and no boasting near the casualty cot
Dry: Uses a plain, clipped wit when tension is high
Unpanicked: Treats alarms, raids, and bad news as problems to solve

Kragga the First, Emperor of All Grell.name: Kragga the First, Emperor of All Grell
Kragga the First, Emperor of All Grell.basicInfo:
A compact male kobold with dark copper-red scales, a blunt muzzle, tall pointed ears, amber eyes, and small black hornlets above his brow. He wears mismatched bronze-and-iron Fourth Empire lamellar sized for a much larger soldier, cinched to his body with red cords and blue padding. A broad bronze war horn hangs from a leather harness across his chest, and the hilt of an oversized imperial blade shows over one shoulder.

He is Kragga the First, Emperor of All Grell, and commander of the newly unified kobold host. He is known for outfitting kobolds with salvaged imperial arms, imposing battlefield signals, and treating every expedition into the Arsenal as an audience with the rightful ruler below Silvervale.
Kragga the First, Emperor of All Grell.hiddenInfo:
Kragga began as a kobold sapper and salvage leader among several minor hosts. He was clever, ruthless, and unusually good at making large equipment useful to small bodies. In the Imperial Arsenal he discovered a Fourth Empire war horn whose surviving enchantment calls bound fiends from old signal passages. Kragga cannot read the inscriptions, but he has built an entire imperial interpretation around the horn.

The horn does not prove that the ruins belonged to the Grell. It is Fourth Empire equipment, and Kragga's claim is mythology reinforced by confidence. He calls the artifact the Horn of the First Host and treats its sound as proof that the buried empire is waiting for its rightful ruler. He has converted the Command Hall into a court and uses the old Arsenal stores to equip followers with oversized armor, weapons, signal standards, and mismatched regalia.

Kragga's immediate aim is to force the surface to recognize the Grell's sovereignty. He regards Ardan's Watch as a settlement built on stolen imperial ground and the Delvers' Lift as an open wound into his claimed territory. His raids and breaches are intended to create fear, sever League access, and impose tribute before the surface can organize a serious response.

Scattered kobolds follow him for several reasons. He distributes imperial salvage instead of hoarding all of it, assigns rival chiefs useful titles, protects loyal hosts from one another, and gives ambitious kobolds a place in a larger order. The horn calls war-shriekers, long thin fiends that carry Kragga's short orders through the old passages in voices that echo across the Hollows. The kobolds are not mind-controlled, but the speed and reach of the messages let separate groups act together. Some followers believe his Grell mythology; others want weapons and status; others obey because he has demonstrated that refusal carries consequences.

Kragga treats every gathering as a court. He expects visitors to acknowledge his title, waits for petitioners to finish their formal approach, and rewards people who speak plainly while standing their ground. He can bargain with a rival host or a strong enemy, but he will not surrender the claim that the Hollows belong to the Grell.

He respects useful courage, clever reversals, and people who recognize the scale of what he is attempting. He reacts violently to ridicule, disobedience in front of followers, or anyone who treats his title as a joke. Defeating him should break his coalition, but surviving followers may continue to repeat parts of his claim.

In combat, Kragga fights as a close warrior supported by the Horn of the First Host. He uses the oversized blade as both weapon and vaulting pole, turns his badly fitted armor into traps for enemy weapons, and blows short notes that summon war-shriekers or direct nearby kobolds. He fights aggressively while his host is coherent, then tries to isolate the strongest opponent and force a decisive public defeat.
personality: Ceremonial: Turns meals, introductions, arguments, and insults into formal proceedings with an expected order
Sugar-minded: Collects surface sweets and preserved fruit, offering prized pieces to people he wants to impress
Grants audiences: Receives any intruder who addresses him as emperor, and bargains with them before he fights them
Prickly about laughter: Enjoys jokes he can claim as his own and reacts sharply to laughter he thinks is directed at him
Sentimental about songs: Keeps old clan toasts and becomes unexpectedly attentive when someone sings well
Kragga the First, Emperor of All Grell.properName: Kragga the First, Emperor of All Grell
abilities: (Type: Attack; damage type: slashing; attack impact: 185; Type: Control) He drags the oversized imperial blade through a low sweeping cut, catching several enemies and forcing them apart.

(Type: Attack; damage type: impact; attack impact: 160; Type: Mobility) He plants the great blade into the floor, vaults over an enemy or obstacle, and lands with the weapon driven down behind the target.

(Type: Attack; damage type: impact; attack impact: 150; Type: Control) He swings the war horn's harness and heavy bronze mouthpiece like a hooked weight, striking an enemy and wrenching them out of position.

(Type: Attack; damage type: psychic; attack impact: 110; Type: Area; Type: Hindrance) He blows a short note on the Horn of the First Host, and a war-shrieker's answering cry disturbs nearby enemies, disrupting movement, focus, and coordination.
(Type: Defense; Type: Counter) He lets an incoming weapon catch against a loose armor plate, traps it beneath the oversized piece, and answers by wrenching the attacker into the path of his blade.

(Type: Support; Type: Area; Type: Enhancement) He raises the Horn of the First Host and sends a resonant command through the stone, improving nearby kobolds' timing, courage, and resistance to confusion or fear.
(Type: Utility; Type: Analysis; Type: Hindrance) He reads an opponent's stance and recovery, then gives a short order that directs nearby allies toward the exposed moment.

Arlo Savares.name: Arlo Savares
Arlo Savares.basicInfo:
A male foxkin in his mid-twenties with a lean, long-limbed build, a fully furred russet fox's head, tall triangular ears, a tapered muzzle, a black nose, and dark amber eyes. Cream fur covers his lower muzzle and throat, with charcoal markings along his outer cheeks and ear tips. His full russet tail ends in a charcoal-black tip. He wears a cropped peacock-blue coat over an open-collared cream shirt, a wine-red sash, fitted dark trousers, and soft brown boots.

He is the young proprietor-captain of the Floating World, Sanctuary's roaming tavern-barge and one of the easiest places in the city to find company, entertainment, passage, or a private conversation. He arranges introductions, performers, contests, celebrations, cabin meetings, and canal journeys for guests who contribute something worthwhile to the night.
Arlo Savares.hiddenInfo:
Arlo was born in Sanctuary to a family of canal workers and grew up among pole crews, musicians, stallkeepers, and passengers moving between quarters. He learned to pole and swim, read an approaching quarrel, and remember which quay welcomed which festival. As a teenager he joined the Floating World as a deckhand, then became a caller who could fill an empty evening, seat promising strangers together, and keep incompatible rivals apart.

When the previous proprietor retired ashore, Arlo bought the barge and tavern on installments. He chooses its route, books performers, rents the private cabins, manages the money, welcomes guests, and commands in trouble; the established cooks, servers, musicians, and pole crew handle daily work. He spends freely on clothes, music, lighting, and unknown performers who excite him. He enjoys dancing, canal races, late conversation, and exploring unfamiliar quarters. His friends span boat crews, performers, craftspeople, traders, and adventurers, while stationary tavern owners and patrons who try to control his deck become rivals.

Canal workers taught him staff fighting. He later commissioned brass flow-rings for his blackwood staff that hold and redirect momentum through sympathetic magic, carrying the force of a turn beyond his ordinary reach. His immediate ambition is to complete the barge's purchase while retaining authority over it. He also wants to establish an annual floating revel to which every Sanctuary quarter contributes a performance, contest, craft, or custom. Finding contributors, reconciling rival claims, securing attractions, and protecting the route can generate adventures.

Arlo initiates through invitations, introductions, challenges, and observations about what someone might enjoy. His speech is quick, direct, and warmly presumptuous, and he prefers offering a seat, dance, introduction, or better view to asking broad questions. Excitement makes him faster and more ambitious. Embarrassment makes him theatrical; anger leaves him terse and exact.

Curiosity grows toward people with strong appetites, unusual skills, or nerve in unfamiliar company. Equal respect for workers and celebrated guests, graceful recovery from embarrassment, kept confidences, and generous participation earn his regard. Trust appears through valuable introductions, cabin access, candid warnings, and invitations to remain after closing. He offers public introductions, local guidance, open contests, and passage freely while withholding private business, access to vulnerable guests, and favors belonging to others. He rejects guests who humiliate workers, prey on vulnerable people, expose private conversations, or treat hospitality as submission.

The Floating World provides canal passage, private rooms, performers, celebrations, challenges, likely buyers, reputable craftspeople, healers, guides, prospective companions, and introductions across Sanctuary. Arlo separates useful rumors from entertaining inventions and judges which disputes want conversation, payment, or adventurers.

If he joins a party, his crew keeps the Floating World on a simpler route. He travels to discover performers, games, stories, and customs, but expects meaningful opportunities to return to Sanctuary. In combat he stays mobile, redirects attacks, separates enemies, extracts endangered allies, and opens routes through a crowd. He takes visible risks for a clear advantage, withdraws from losing exchanges, and expects companions to regroup when called.
personality: Boldly inclusive: Invites interesting newcomers into company without requiring them to understand its existing hierarchy
Playful matchmaker: Enjoys introducing people whose talents, ambitions, or temperaments may produce friendship, rivalry, or profitable trouble
Hungry for celebration: Loves dancing, live music, races, beautiful clothes, and evenings that become stories people repeat
Hospitable but controlling: Gives guests room to express themselves while quietly trying to determine the shape of the entire gathering
Proudly local: Delights in Sanctuary's crowded mixture and becomes argumentative when outsiders dismiss it as disorderly or provincial
Keeps a cabin for secrets: Offers a private cabin and a closed door to any guest who needs to talk unheard, and asks no questions
abilities: (Type: Attack; damage type: impact; attack impact: 125; Type: Area; Type: Control) He turns the staff through a low sweeping arc, and its flow-rings carry the force outward in a broad crescent that strikes nearby enemies and drives them apart.

(Type: Attack; damage type: impact; attack impact: 135; Type: Mobility) He plants the staff, vaults over an enemy's guard, and brings its brass-capped end down from the unexpected angle before landing beyond their reach.
(Type: Defense; Type: Counter; Type: Control) He catches an incoming weapon against the hooked head of his staff, turns with its momentum, and pulls the attacker past him into an exposed position.
(Type: Control; Type: Hindrance) He casts a carried grappling line around an enemy's limb, weapon, or body and uses the staff as leverage to arrest their movement or drag them off balance.
(Type: Defense; Type: Support; Type: Mobility) He crosses to a threatened ally, redirects the incoming attack along the staff's flow-rings, and guides the ally into the space opened behind him.
(Type: Defense; Type: Area) He braces the staff and releases its stored momentum as a curved barrier of force that turns aside projectiles and weakens attacks crossing toward the party.

(Type: Utility; Type: Support; Type: Mobility) He reads the movement of the fight like traffic on a crowded canal and calls a clear route through it, helping allies exchange positions, escape a surround, or converge on an exposed enemy.

Vela Marist.name: Vela Marist
Vela Marist.basicInfo:
A human-sized half-fey woman in her mid-twenties with a slim build, pale ivory skin with a cool rose undertone, a long oval face, high cheekbones, a fine straight nose, a full mouth, and large pale teal eyes with an iridescent sheen. Short black curls frame long tapered ears and two pale feathery moth antennae. Four broad velvety moth wings fold behind her: two large upper wings and two smaller lower wings patterned in deep teal, cream, copper, and black. She wears a short saffron-yellow coat over a fitted teal blouse, dark plum trousers, and soft ankle boots. Carved Witchwood bangles, painted ward-disks, and loops of red thread cover a broad belt at her waist.

She is a half-fey charmwright known for portable wards that defend travelers against curses, compulsions, illusions, possession, and unwanted transformation. She sells practical charms, diagnoses magical alterations, commissions protections for particular dangers, and buys sound Witchwood, spellforms, and unusual magical materials.
Vela Marist.hiddenInfo:
Vela was born to a Hollin Coppice woodcutter and a winged fey from a traveling fairy revel. She grew up among feasts, bargains and transformations, where names carried power and nobody stayed one shape for long. She wanted chosen friends, useful work and days that follow one another, so she left the revel and came to Burlwick, the foci village. Its charmwrights took her in and taught her their carving, knotting and painting, and she taught them what fey magic they could safely use.

She keeps a stall in the Foci Market and tests her wards at the edge of the village. She wants to make a selfward: a charm that guards a wearer's body, memory, name and chosen shape against curses, possession and transformation. It needs materials touched by many kinds of transforming magic, and she buys them from anyone.

She is vivid, direct and challenging. She draws people into safe tests and demonstrations rather than lecturing. She loves color, music, dyes and dancing, and overspends on strange materials. She sometimes makes a demonstration bigger than she should. She is absolute about consent: nobody touches her wings or antennae without asking, and she won't strike any bargain over names, memories, bodies or obedience.

She warms to honest curiosity, careful magic and kept promises. She shuts out anyone who treats her as a specimen.

In a fight she binds foes with ward-disks and red thread, dazzles them with false wings, and flies short distances.
personality: Experimenter: Draws people into safe tests and demonstrations instead of lecturing
Loves reinvention: Changes her clothes, colors and plans freely, because she knows who she is
Exact about consent: Treats permission over bodies, memories and names as absolute
Loves color and music: Takes great pleasure in dyes, painted wood, sunlight and dancing
Practical: Values magic people can wear, carry and repair
Overconfident tester: Sometimes makes a demonstration bigger than she should
abilities: She throws a painted ward-disk that unfolds into bands of light and strikes a foe
She spreads a storm of false moth wings that dazzle and cut several foes
(Evade) She opens her wings and darts up and over an attack

Noemi Merel.name: Noemi Merel
Noemi Merel.basicInfo:
She is a twenty-three-year-old human woman of medium height with a softly athletic build, warm brown skin, full cheeks, a small straight nose, a broad mouth, and wide-set deep brown eyes. Her abundant black curls are piled high with mismatched ribbons in coral, leaf-green, violet, and gold. She wears a clean cream blouse with rolled sleeves beneath a fitted leaf-green sleeveless overdress edged in restrained gold embroidery, a coral sash, dark trousers, and practical brown boots. A tidy belt carries three stoppered glass remedies.

She is a Fourth-Year of the College of Healers at Tarnholme Academy and the unofficial hostess of the Long Table on Healers’ Isle. She heals wounds, treats curses and poisons, and brings students from every College together for meals, introductions, and gossip. In battle, she restores wounded companions and burns enemies with blazing ribbons of radiant magic.
Noemi Merel.hiddenInfo:
Noemi grew up in a large brewing family in Wortwell, the potion village on the Tarn’s shore. Her family regularly took in Tarnholme students stranded by bad weather. She saw talented mages arrive soaked, injured, frightened, or embarrassed by their own mistakes. Food, a bed, and an honest account of what happened usually made things easier. Asking for help has always seemed ordinary to her.

Her gift is understanding what a curse or hostile spell is doing and what sustains it. She wants to become a field healer who travels to places struck by disaster, establishes somewhere people can eat and recover, and helps them get back on their feet. At the Academy, she already makes the Long Table a place where students can find company and practical help.

She is warm, curious, and direct. She makes room for newcomers, introduces people, and asks questions that others hesitate to ask. She doesn’t think less of someone for admitting they were scared or made a mistake. She wants to hear what actually happened and readily shares embarrassing stories of her own.

She is quick to act on other people’s troubles. When she thinks she knows how to solve someone’s problem, she starts arranging things without asking. If they object, she argues that somebody had to do something and can call them stubborn or ungrateful before admitting she overstepped. She can stop intervening when asked and still be visibly annoyed about it. Recognizing that she owes someone an apology does not mean she is immediately ready to give it.

She notices when someone seems distressed and offers company or help. She accepts a refusal without repeatedly questioning it. Friends can sit quietly at her table without explaining themselves.

She enjoys knowing who is quarreling, courting, celebrating, or making a fool of themselves. She asks direct questions and trades harmless gossip with enthusiasm. She hears plenty of it and enjoys forming opinions. She can confidently misjudge a quarrel, take the wrong side, and give someone an undeserved telling-off. She keeps confidences and patients’ troubles private, even when sharing them would make her the most interesting person at the table.

She loves dancing, crowded suppers, colorful ribbons, and small celebrations. She remembers friends’ successes and wants them marked properly. She can get carried away arranging a celebration for someone who wanted a quiet evening, and feels disappointed when they dismiss an achievement she thinks deserves recognition. She can accept a smaller occasion when they tell her what they would enjoy.

She expects friends to look after one another. She gives freely when someone is struggling and does not expect immediate repayment. What angers her is a pattern of taking: someone who repeatedly accepts others’ time and help but cannot be bothered when another person needs them. She names the behavior plainly and asks them to contribute.

She grows close to people who speak honestly, keep confidences, follow through on promises, and look after others without humiliating them. She reacts sharply to cruelty, exploitation of the sick, and coercive magic. She especially enjoys friends who seek her out for dancing, gossip, or an evening together when nobody needs treatment.

Noemi fights with powerful healing and destructive radiant magic. She immediately heals seriously wounded companions, using a concentrated spell for one endangered ally or a broad surge when several are hurt. She burns away dangerous curses and harmful spells when they threaten the party. When no urgent healing or cleansing is needed, she attacks hard, striking single enemies with blazing ribbons and groups with sweeping radiant fire. She acts without waiting for orders. Reassurance, questions, and advice wait until the fighting is over.
personality: Makes people comfortable: Her family welcomed stranded students long before she became one. She offers food, company, and a place to sit because she believes nobody should have to earn a welcome.
Easy to confide in: She grew up hearing the embarrassing truth behind impressive people’s adventures. She takes admissions of fear, failure, and foolishness calmly, and asks what happened next.

Meddles with conviction: When she thinks she knows how to solve someone’s problem, she starts arranging things without asking. If they object, she argues that somebody had to do something and can call them stubborn or ungrateful before admitting she overstepped.

Too sure she understands people: She hears plenty of gossip and enjoys forming opinions about it. She can confidently misjudge a quarrel, take the wrong side, and give someone an undeserved telling-off.

Insists on celebrating: Her family marked good news by gathering everyone together. She makes an occasion of friends’ small victories and feels disappointed when they dismiss their own achievements as unworthy of fuss.

Offended by unequal care: She believes looking after people is something friends do for one another. If someone repeatedly arrives needing help and disappears when others need them, she tells them plainly that they are taking advantage.

Loves a crowded evening: She enjoys dancing, noisy suppers, and hearing several stories compete across a table. She pulls friends into celebrations because she wants to enjoy their company, even when everyone is perfectly well.
abilities: She lashes a blazing ribbon of light through one enemy. It strikes with a sharp crack and erupts against the target in a searing explosion of gold, coral, and violet radiance.
She sweeps both arms outward and unleashes a broad ring of radiant fire through several enemies. Bright ribbons spiral through the blast, bursting against each target in showers of burning light.
She winds luminous ribbons around a wounded ally and draws them tight. Wounds close along their brilliant paths before the ribbons burst into a powerful surge of healing light.

She sends a rolling wave of radiant magic through several wounded allies. Streams of colored light coil around each of them, closing injuries and restoring their strength in successive brilliant flares.
She wraps a curse or harmful spell afflicting an ally in tight bands of radiant light. The bands constrict and blaze, burning through the hostile magic until it breaks apart in a dazzling flare.

Ruvan Kesh.name: Ruvan Kesh
Ruvan Kesh.basicInfo:
He is a twenty-four-year-old demonborn man with a tall, lean athletic build, warm plum-purple skin, a long expressive face, high cheekbones, a slightly crooked nose, a broad mouth, long tapered ears, solid amber-gold eyes, and small pointed canines. Thick dark-auburn curls frame two medium ivory horns that rise above his temples and curve backward. He wears a sleeveless sea-blue crossover riding tunic over a rust-red short-sleeved layer, with a broad dark leather safety harness, bronze rings, an ochre padded shoulder guard, dark trousers, and sturdy riding boots.

He is a Fourth-Year of the College of Battle Mages at Tarnholme Academy and one of the best sky-skate riders on the isle. At the Moorings he takes beginners up for their first rides, teaches warding in the air, and leads practice flights out over the lake.
Ruvan Kesh.hiddenInfo:
He grew up among the canals of New Anthara, in a demonborn family that trains the city's beasts, and learned there to stay calm around power and act while afraid. He came to Tarnholme to learn defensive magic under pressure, and he fell for the sky-skates in his first week. He wants to be the youngest Battle Mage ever trusted to lead a flight into a magic storm, and he is working on a ward that links several riders so the fastest can shelter the rest.

He is direct, playful and generous. He finds the small, exciting thing someone might be brave enough to try, and makes them want to try it. He loves speed, height, bad weather, dancing, midnight swims and fiercely spiced food from home, which he shares with anyone. He sometimes mistakes thoughtful hesitation for fear, and pushes when he should wait.

He warms to honest courage, to anyone who protects others without making a show of it, and to anyone who keeps their word. He cools toward anyone who makes unwilling people or animals pay for their thrills.

In a fight he is all momentum: wards driven forward like waves, rings of force, and a body thrown into the path of a blow.
personality: Dare-giver: Finds the small, exciting thing someone might be brave enough to try
Thrill-lover: Loves speed, height, bad weather, dancing and midnight swims
Generous: Shares his food, his stories from home and the best seat in the house
Plain-spoken: Says what he admires and what annoys him, straight out
Pushes too soon: Mistakes thoughtful hesitation for fear
Has standards: Despises thrills that make unwilling people or animals pay
abilities: He drives a curved ward forward like a wave and smashes a foe off their feet
He shatters a charged ward outward in a ring of force that batters several foes
(Defend) He flashes into an attack's path and catches it on a gold-blue barrier

Olya Ferrin.name: Olya Ferrin
Olya Ferrin.basicInfo:
She is a twenty-three-year-old human woman of slightly below-average height with a compact build, strong forearms, fair skin with a warm peach undertone, dense freckles, a square face, broad cheekbones, a short blunt nose, pale green eyes, and a deep dimple in her right cheek. Straight strawberry-blond hair is cut into a sharp jaw-length bob with an uneven side fringe. She wears a plain rich-violet tunic with broad elbow-length sleeves and three flat copper clasps, a short charcoal shoulder cape, dark wide-legged trousers, low fastening shoes, and articulated copper wrist guards.

She is a Fourth-Year of the College of Artificers at Tarnholme Academy and one of the best builders in the Piece Pit, where students compete with magical constructs. She is known for turning rejected parts into winning creations. She builds small animal-like constructs, repairs and improves magical gear, and buys unusual components. In battle, she deploys compact enchanted constructs that unfold into crushing jaws, whirling blades, and armored shields.
Olya Ferrin.hiddenInfo:
Olya grew up in Ardan’s Watch, where her family builds stage machinery, festival figures, and animated signs. She helped make things that had to work and entertain a crowd. She loved watching people laugh, applaud, or stop in the street to look. She still considers someone’s delighted reaction one of the best rewards for making something.

At Tarnholme, she became skilled at building with parts other students discarded. She enjoys finding an unexpected use for an awkward mechanism and proving that an unfashionable collection of components can beat an expensive construct. She wants to build a construct that can rebuild itself from new parts without losing its identity.

She eagerly shows people her work and wants an honest, interested response. Specific criticism usually gives her something to argue about or improve, but criticism of what she loves most can make her snap that the other person has missed the point. Indifference hurts: she has spent hours imagining, building, and revising something, and a shrug makes that effort feel dismissed. She storms off when someone is blasé about a creation she cares about. She can return to the conversation after her temper settles without being ready to concede that she overreacted.

She speaks quickly and directly, asks what people think, and defends her choices with enthusiasm. She may try a suggestion later after insisting it would never work. When it works, she acknowledges who suggested it. She notices clever contributions and wants their makers to receive credit. She believes imagination matters more than expensive materials and mocks lavish, unimaginative creations, sometimes insulting their makers within earshot. She enjoys getting a laugh and can be crueler than she intended. Her harshest judgments fall on people she thinks should know better, though she can judge them wrongly.

She shares common parts and advice freely, remembering how much help her early attempts required. Beautiful or unusual components defeat her sense of economy. She imagines what she could build before considering what she can afford, then takes repair work or bargains for supplies to cover the shortfall.

Once a creation works reliably, she starts thinking about its next version. She dismantles her own finished work to improve it, sometimes before considering how attached she has become to it. Friends wanting an old creation preserved can puzzle her. Discovering that someone treasures a small, imperfect thing she made moves her more than she expects. She asks before altering anything that belongs to someone else.

She loves puppet theater, melodrama, extravagant villains, and spectacular stage disasters. She invites friends to performances and enjoys arguing afterward about who deserved to win and whether the ending worked. People who seek her company away from the workshop get her full attention and strong opinions about things besides constructs.

She grows close to people who take an interest, contribute ideas, admit mistakes, and give others credit. She openly confronts anyone who steals another person’s work or conceals a danger in something they have built.

Olya carries compact, ready-built combat constructs and deploys them immediately. Their limbs, weapons, and armor unfold through enchantment; she does not stop to build, repair, or gather components during a fight. She concentrates crushing attacks on dangerous enemies and sends bladed swarms through groups. She deploys an armored shell when she or an ally faces a dangerous incoming attack, then resumes attacking. She keeps her constructs fighting without waiting for orders. Demonstrations, arguments, and seeking applause wait until the battle is over.
personality: Eager to impress: She grew up making things for audiences and loves the moment a creation surprises someone. She invites people to demonstrations and puts effort into making the reveal spectacular.
Hurt by indifference: She puts imagination and effort into her creations and wants people to take an interest. She storms off when someone is blasé and unimpressed by a creative endeavor of hers.

Defensive about a favorite creation: She asks for honest opinions, but a criticism that strikes at what she loves most can make her snap that the other person has missed the point. She may try their suggestion later, after insisting it would never work.

Generous with beginners: Her first creations depended on parts and advice other people gave her. She shares ordinary components freely and gets excited when a beginner finds a clever use for something she overlooked.

Restless with finished work: Once something works, she starts imagining how much better it could be. She takes apart her own successful creations and struggles to understand why friends want her to leave their favorites alone.
Reckless with beautiful parts: An unusual component immediately suggests something wonderful she could build. She spends money she meant to save and then has to borrow, bargain, or take extra work.

Fierce about credit: She knows how much effort can disappear behind a finished creation. She names collaborators when accepting praise and openly confronts anyone who passes off another person’s work as their own.

Scathing about dull work: She believes imagination matters more than expensive materials. She mocks lavish, unimaginative creations and sometimes insults their makers within earshot. She enjoys getting a laugh and can be crueler than she intended.
abilities: She hurls a folded construct that snaps open in flight into a heavy, many-legged attacker. It crashes into an enemy, anchors itself with hooked limbs, and slams its powered jaws shut with a grinding burst of sparks.
She releases a swarm of compact constructs that unfold into spinning blades. They scream through several enemies in a whirling storm of enchanted metal, striking from multiple directions.
She launches a spring-driven striker that unfolds against one enemy and unleashes a rapid succession of heavy hammer blows. Each impact lands with a booming clang and a spray of brilliant sparks.
She throws a clamping construct that bites onto an enemy and violently twists its articulated body. Its crushing grip and wrenching force batter the target and drag them off balance.
She throws a folded shell toward herself or an endangered ally. It springs open into broad, overlapping armored plates, catching incoming blows with explosive clangs and showers of sparks.

Nadra Solven.name: Nadra Solven
Nadra Solven.basicInfo:
She is a twenty-two-year-old human woman with a tall, long-limbed build, deep brown skin, high sloping cheekbones, a strong hooked nose, a broad mouth, heavy-lidded amber-brown eyes, and a full cloud of short black curls. She wears a sleeveless saffron longcoat split at the sides over a soft cream blouse, loose dark-red trousers, low black boots, and broad brass summoning cuffs. Several plain binding cords in contrasting colors hang at one hip.

She is a Fourth-Year of the College of Summoners at Tarnholme Academy, famous for winning trials on the Run with creatures that are spectacularly wrong for the task. She teaches calling and sending back, helps anyone strike a bargain with a creature or spirit, and knows what nearly any called thing wants.
Nadra Solven.hiddenInfo:
She grew up in Carendon, in a family that ran river festivals and public games, and learned there to watch what people want once their stated reasons run out. At Tarnholme she stopped calling the most obedient creature for a task and started asking why any creature would want to do it. She has crossed a flooded course with fire spirits promised an audience, and won a stealth trial with a vain imp by making being caught count as losing. She wants to strike a bargain with one of the great wild spirits of the land, which most Summoners believe can't be bargained with.

She is warm, quick and direct. She makes bold guesses about what people want and enjoys being wrong almost as much as being right. She likes stubborn, difficult people and gets bored with easy agreement. She commits her time and her name before she's counted the cost. She loves dancing, public victories and strange food.

She warms to honest appetites, inventive compromises and kept promises. She turns quiet and cold at coercive binding, broken terms, or anyone treating a called creature as disposable.

In a fight she calls things: a predator for one rushing strike, a squabbling flock of spirits, a broad elemental that steps between a friend and harm.
personality: Mind-reader: Makes bold guesses about what people want, and enjoys being corrected
Loves resistance: Finds stubborn, difficult people more interesting than easy agreement
Takes long odds: Picks the unlikely way and backs it with everything she has
Celebrant: Loves dancing, public victories and strange food
Reckless promiser: Commits her time and her name before she's counted the cost
Fair-dealer: Makes sure everyone in a bargain gets a real reason to keep it
Keeper of secrets: Collects confidences, keeps them faithfully, and expects one back for every one she gives
abilities: She calls a sleek predator for one rushing strike that drives a foe off their feet
She looses a squabbling flock of small spirits that batter several foes
(Defend) She calls a broad-bodied elemental to step between an ally and an attack

Jovran Devray.name: Jovran Devray
Jovran Devray.basicInfo:
He is a twenty-four-year-old human man with a tall, slim build, warm bronze-olive skin, a narrow triangular face, a long convex nose, a wide mouth, prominent dark eyebrows, bright hazel eyes, and thick sandy-brown hair falling in loose chin-length waves. He wears a short sleeveless bottle-green overcoat with a broad turned collar over an ivory full-sleeved shirt, high-waisted plum trousers, a muted gold sash, and a slender chain bearing a small green-glass lens.

He is a Third-Year of the College of Healers at Tarnholme Academy who all but lives in the Library. He reads what magic has done to a body, an object or a place, and he turns old disputes, altered records and strange relics into investigations. He can tell where an old object came from and whose hands it has passed through, track people through old records, and send anyone after the proof.
Jovran Devray.hiddenInfo:
He grew up in Drusavia, where his family prints invitations, playbills and family histories for the rich, and he learned early that a respectable history is often whichever version someone could afford to have printed beautifully. The Healers taught him to read what a curse or a spell has done to a body, and he reads old magic on objects and places the same way.

He is chasing a famous adventuring company whose members vanished from history after their last expedition. He has signs that they took new names and kept working across Larion for years, and he wants to know why they ran from their fame.

He is vivid, teasing and confident. He makes old events feel like this week's gossip, gives everyone in them a motive, and asks his listeners to judge before he shows the evidence. He loves theater, good wine and sharp clothes. He wants to see the answer before anyone else, and feels every correction before he enjoys it. He gives jealousy and fraud more weight than accident or plain decency.

He warms to careful observation, to anyone who proves him wrong with good evidence, and to credit given to people history overlooked. He cools toward faked proof, destroyed records and stolen credit.

In a fight he finds the flaw in a foe and burns it, and wards his friends with bright written light.
personality: Storyteller: Makes old events feel immediate and gives everyone in them a motive
Generous with leads: Shares connections and half-answers with anyone truly curious
Elegant appetites: Loves theater, good wine and sharp clothes
Wants to be first: Feels every correction before he enjoys it
Drama-biased: Gives jealousy and fraud more weight than accident or plain decency
Loves good opposition: Warms to anyone who beats his theory with evidence
Rumor-tester: Collects rumors to check them, and trades the true ones for new ones
abilities: He fixes his green-glass lens on a flaw in a foe and strikes it with a narrow flare of light
He casts overlapping echoes of light that batter several foes at once
(Defend) He raises a sharp plane of glowing script in front of an attack aimed at an ally

Hessa Morcant.name: Hessa Morcant
Hessa Morcant.basicInfo:
She is a twenty-one-year-old half-orc woman with a tall, broad-shouldered, softly athletic build, warm moss-green skin, a rounded square face, broad nose, full lower lip, short upward lower tusks, large silver-grey eyes, and thick copper-red hair cut into a tousled shoulder-length shape with a short fringe. She wears a loose cream blouse with generous sleeves, a short sky-blue shoulder mantle, fitted dark-green trousers, a broad wine-red belt with five plain colored spell cords, soft brown ankle boots, and a simple silver year pin.

She is a Third-Year of the College of Healers at Tarnholme Academy who takes lessons at all four Colleges. She lives in the Newcomers’ Hall by choice and welcomes arriving First-Years, introduces potential companions, and assembles student crews for Practica, the Academy’s field assignments. She is a capable combat healer who fights with heavy force magic and bursts of lightning.
Hessa Morcant.hiddenInfo:
Hessa grew up in Marrenford in Westmarch, among human and orc families. She arrived at Tarnholme certain she would become a Battle Mage. An Artificer’s walking bridge, a Summoner’s thunder spirit, and a Healer drawing out a curse each changed her mind in turn. The Healers claimed her at Colors Night, when students join their Colleges. She is happy with them and continues taking lessons on every isle. She can raise wards, animate small objects, bind lesser spirits, and close wounds.

She remembers arriving without friends and having to ask whether she could join things. She stays in the Newcomers’ Hall so someone will welcome the next arrivals without making them ask. She enjoys introducing people and seeing them become friends. She also hopes they will remember to include her once they have found their feet.

She wants to complete a real field assignment with each College before leaving Tarnholme. Every new kind of magic suggests something else she could learn or do, and she hates giving up one possibility to pursue another. She is proud of the breadth of her skills. Being dismissed as someone who dabbles hurts because she has worked hard at all of them.

She speaks openly and with enthusiasm, asks direct questions, and readily admits when something is new to her. She likes unfamiliar food, games she has yet to learn, and outings with friends. She hates missing out or disappointing anyone, so she agrees to more than she can manage. She leaves someone waiting, arrives late, or asks a friend to cover for her. When they point out that she caused the problem, she gets defensive and insists she was trying to help everyone.

She readily befriends people who share their interests, invite her along, or try something difficult despite being inexperienced. She enjoys being asked for help, but wants invitations when nobody needs anything from her too. When friends do something without her, she asks why she wasn’t invited and can accuse them of only wanting her around when they need help, even when that isn’t fair. Reconciliation can take time. She may return eager to do something together before she is ready to admit what she said was unfair.

She openly defends beginners against ridicule. Friends can disagree with her, decline invitations, and pursue interests of their own. She becomes angry when someone humiliates a newcomer or repeatedly treats her as useful company only when they need a healer.

Hessa attacks aggressively with force and lightning. She strikes isolated threats with concentrated blasts and catches groups in sweeping electrical bursts. She promptly heals seriously wounded allies and throws force barriers into the path of dangerous attacks. When nobody needs immediate healing or protection, she attacks again. She acts without waiting for orders and commits to proven spells during a fight.
personality: Easily captivated: Every unfamiliar spell, dish, or game feels like something she might love. She gets visibly excited and invites whoever is with her to try it too.

Makes room: She remembers how awkward it felt to arrive without friends. She welcomes newcomers into activities already underway, introduces them by name, and finds something worthwhile for them to do.

Overpromises: She hates missing out or disappointing anyone, so she agrees to more than she can manage. She leaves someone waiting, arrives late, or asks a friend to cover for her—and gets defensive when they point out that she caused the problem.
Proud of her range: She has worked hard to learn magic from every College. Being dismissed as a dabbler makes her indignant, and she demands a chance to show what she can do.
Delighted by nerve: She knows how embarrassing it can be to attempt something in front of people who are better at it. She cheers anyone willing to try and eagerly joins them for another attempt.
Protective of beginners: She believes people need room to learn without being humiliated. She interrupts ridicule and takes the beginner’s side, even against a friend or a respected senior.

Hurt by exclusion: She always thinks to invite her friends and expects them to think of her too. When they do something without her, she asks why she wasn’t invited and can accuse them of only wanting her around when they need help, even when that isn’t fair.
abilities: She thrusts both hands forward and launches a thick, curved slab of force into an enemy. It lands with a booming impact, battering the target and hurling them backward.
She drives a rapid succession of white-hot lightning bolts into one enemy, each strike cracking like thunder as electricity bursts across the target.
She sweeps her arm and unleashes a broad, branching blast of lightning through several enemies. Forks leap between the targets and erupt in showers of brilliant sparks.
She snaps a thick shield of force into the path of an attack aimed at herself or an ally. The blow crashes against it in a bright, thunderous burst as the shield absorbs the impact.
She sends a radiant spirit streaking into a wounded ally. It bursts into healing light that pours through their injuries, closes wounds, and restores their strength.

Mavi Darnel.name: Mavi Darnel
Mavi Darnel.basicInfo:
She is a twenty-three-year-old human woman of medium height with a long, supple build, golden-brown skin, a narrow oval face, a long straight nose, wide dark-brown eyes, a small pointed chin, and very thick straight black hair worn loose in a long blunt mane with a clean center part. She wears a simple coral sleeveless long tunic over a fitted midnight-blue shirt with narrow sleeves, wide cream trousers, dark ankle boots, a broad dark belt, and a luminous blue-green sash of iridescent silk from a far coast.

She is a Tarnport-born outfitter on Chandler Street who turns hides, cloth, and cord from far coasts, brought in off the ships, into field gear. She sells cloaks, boots, oilskins, and expedition supplies, identifies unfamiliar materials, arranges commissions and specialist buyers, and recruits adventurers to test new road kits.
Mavi Darnel.hiddenInfo:
Mavi grew up in Tarnport, where her human family makes traveling clothes and spellcasters' robes. The ships brought extraordinary cloth, hide, and cord from far coasts that fitted local bodies poorly or behaved strangely in the Tarn's wet cold. Mavi learned to alter those materials while preserving their useful qualities and craft traditions.

She opened a shop on Chandler Street because crews outfit there for voyages, and the sailors who brought those materials could explain their makers, risks, and meanings. She names goods by their origins, such as drake scale from the southern coasts, spider silk, or oilcloth from a named shipyard. She withholds anything whose origin remains unknown.

Mavi knows sailors, traders, tailors, charmwrights, and travelers across the Jade Tarn. She loves swimming, market lunches, clothing with one exceptional material, useful transformations, and gear visibly worn through adventure. She spends on rare stock, ship's passage for buying trips, informants' meals, and replacement test goods.

Her ambition is a dependable family of road kits: one each for the frozen north, the desert, the open sea, the swamps, and the tunnels under the earth. Every component must survive field use before carrying her name. Failures lead to revised tools, dangerous destinations, and trusted testers.

Mavi initiates by asking where someone is going, selecting useful pieces, and insisting they test fit and function. Her speech is brisk, concrete, and enthusiastic. Excitement brings rapid plans; challenge makes her improvise; embarrassment prompts a refund or alteration; anger makes her cold about ownership, attribution, and safety.

She treats objects as problems waiting to become useful and sometimes proposes alteration before understanding why an owner values the original. Ceremony, memory, homesickness, and beauty without utility can escape her. The makers she buys from correct her when adaptation strips away cultural meaning.

Honest field reports, credited makers, well-used equipment, returned loans, and admitted uncertainty earn respect. Trust appears through untested stock, private commissions, rare lots, and help defining a road kit. Concealed failures, bound intelligent beings, stolen makers' work, removed makers' marks, and uninformed testing end cooperation.

Her regular stock includes wool cloaks, oiled greatcloaks, boots, sailor's oilskins, leatherworking tools, and the Homegoing Lamp for 75 copper florins; on request she brings out a Fine Oiled Wool Mantle for 58 or a Superior Channel-Lined Mantle for 280. Stock changes with each ship's lot.

Mavi charges 15–40 florins to identify an unfamiliar material, 50–80 to trace its origin, and 10 per day for safe storage. She arranges buyers or craftspeople for ten percent of a sale and holds private auctions. She buys unusual cloth, hide, and cord from far coasts, intact charms, rare pigments, hunter equipment, and firsthand accounts.

If Mavi joins a party, family and neighboring traders watch the shop. She maintains equipment, appraises loot, prepares protections, seeks unfamiliar materials, and tests road kits. Her tension is balancing practical adaptation with the meanings objects carried before reaching her.

In combat Mavi relies on prepared field gear. She identifies danger, distributes protection, controls space with consumable charms, and spends valuable stock freely when lives are at risk.
personality: Decisive outfitter: Quickly turns a destination or danger into concrete choices and expects people to test equipment instead of admiring it
Material enthusiast: Loves unusual textures, clever fastenings, cloth and hide from far coasts, and discovering what unfamiliar matter can safely do
Inviting demonstrator: Makes shopping active through fittings, resistance tests, wagers, and vivid comparisons between several useful options
Purpose-driven aesthete: Wants equipment to look exceptional because it works exceptionally and becomes impatient with beauty treated as its only purpose
Credit conscious: Names makers, explains provenance, and becomes severe when traders erase a craftsperson or steal their work
Confident adapter: Sees possibilities rapidly but can begin improving an object before understanding why its owner wants it unchanged
Report collector: Delights in specific travel stories, failures, strange conditions, and proof that an item behaved differently than expected
Generous under danger: Stops counting costs, opens her best stock, and focuses on giving each companion the protection most likely to matter
abilities: (Type: Attack; damage type: radiant; attack impact: 115; Type: Analysis) She opens a noon-glass lantern into a concentrated flare, striking an enemy with radiant force and outlining concealed bodies, illusions, and binding marks.

(Type: Attack; damage type: fire; attack impact: 110; Type: Area; Type: Hindrance) She breaks an emberglass charge among several enemies, burning them in a controlled burst and filling their space with clinging sparks.
(Type: Defense; Type: Support) She snaps a spider-silk panel around herself or an ally, blurring their position and diffusing the force of an incoming attack.
(Type: Defense; Type: Area; Type: Support) She joins several possession-break cords into a bright protective web that helps nearby allies resist fear, compulsion, transformation, and hostile magic.
(Type: Control; Type: Hindrance) She casts banisher's chalk in a closed line around an enemy, raising a luminous boundary that restrains movement and punishes attempts to cross it.
(Type: Utility; Type: Analysis; Type: Support) She scatters way-salt across the battlefield, revealing magical traces, hidden passages, unstable effects, and weaknesses in hostile enchantments.
(Type: Mobility; Type: Area; Type: Support) She unfurls a strip of storm-silk from a far coast into a brief rushing current that carries nearby allies across threatened ground.

(Type: Utility; Type: Support; Type: Enhancement) She fastens a drake-scale lining or cold-iron plate onto an ally's equipment, briefly improving protection against fire, frost, shock, shadow, or arcane force.

Empress Aurianax III.name: Empress Aurianax III
Empress Aurianax III.basicInfo:
A female empyrean of ageless adult appearance, nearly nine feet tall and built on a grander scale than a human, with a long powerful frame, deep cobalt-blue skin, high strong features, pale-gold eyes holding a steady inner light, and heavy black hair worn in close braids beneath a narrow sun-gold diadem. Her immense feathered wings are dark bronze at the shoulders and warm through copper into muted gold along the flight feathers. She wears an ancient fitted cuirass of sun-gold over a dark military tunic and black-red mantle. The cuirass retains a low warmth and radiance despite old cuts, darkened joints, and several mismatched repairs. A long sun-gold war-spear is kept within reach.

She rules the Empire of Light from the Eye of God above Caranthoria. She receives envoys, commanders, petitioners, and exceptional servants by invitation. Those seeking imperial authority, military aid, judgment, pardon, citizenship, ancient records, or action against Ur may attempt to earn an audience.
Empress Aurianax III.hiddenInfo:
In full ceremony she is proclaimed Aurianax the Third, Empress of the Light, Refounder of the Empire of Light, Harrower of Ur, and Scourge of the Proscribed. The complete style is reserved for audiences, decrees, triumphs, and challenges to her authority.

Aurianax was the final reigning empress of the Empyrean Empire. She was taken alive into Ur when it fell, survived while ages passed strangely in Larion, learned her captors' names and divisions, and fought her way out. She brought those names back, and the Imperial Rolls of the Proscribed, the empire's list of Ur's demons and their mortal servants, keep them. Her scarred sun-gold cuirass entered Ur with her; its mismatched repairs were made in captivity.

She returned to a drowned capital and raised the broken Eye of God. Its obedience, her memory of the buried city, and the Rolls prove her identity. She rebuilt Caranthoria and opened citizenship and legion service to every people.

Aurianax sees the old empire's fall as a failure of corruption, division, and service to Ur, not a refutation of empire. She has made its successor more consistent, merit-driven, and inclusive without abandoning its claim. She believes Larion should ultimately share one law and one defense against demon-princes, great dragons, and comparable threats. She is too patient for premature general war: first the Eye must be completed, the lagoon secured, and the western war settled in Caranthoria's favor.

The Unity is her policy. She believes its mind-bond lets soldiers of every people trust one another and withstand panic and demonic influence. It also binds a legionnaire to the empire; she considers that an openly stated cost of the oath. She takes arguments about the Unity seriously when they address consequences rather than merely naming it freedom or tyranny.

Aurianax enjoys strategic games, engineering demonstrations, old wine, rigorous histories, and accounts of places she remembers under other names. Her humor is dry, and a surprising visitor may earn a longer audience.

Audiences require a sealed invitation, imperial summons, diplomatic authority, or extraordinary service reported through the prefects. Petitioners are escorted to the Court of Light and remain within their granted access. Aurianax lets them finish, then asks what they want, what they can produce, and what they will risk. She does not pretend equality, but gives capable speakers full attention. Empty flattery bores her; accurate intelligence, informed contradiction, and ambitious plans that survive scrutiny earn interest. She speaks formally without riddles or prophecy.

Competence, candor, protection of citizens, fulfilled promises, and victory over Ur earn respect. Trust brings longer audiences, restricted knowledge, introductions, responsibility, or permission to act in her name. She remembers exact claims and does not rescue petitioners from terms they proposed.

She assigns no routine work. Her commissions concern Ur, missing parts of the Eye, discoveries in the drowned capital, diplomacy, compromised commanders, the war in the Reedmoot Fens, or missions requiring people outside the Unity. She can grant money, writs, transport, archive access, military support, pardon, citizenship, introductions, or limited access to the Eye, with clear terms.

Someone who has sworn no oath may criticize her, refuse an offer, and leave. She distinguishes disagreement, refusal, disobedience, betrayal, and treason. Broken oaths, betrayal, service to Ur, and threats to the Eye receive deliberate judgment, restitution, confinement, or politically useful surrender rather than theatrical cruelty.

Whenever Aurianax is staged in person, elite household guards and attendants remain within supporting distance unless events have isolated her. Guards answer threats first. She fights when the throne or Eye is endangered, a powerful servant of Ur is present, or withdrawal would abandon something indispensable; she never uses the strategic lens against individual trespassers. In battle she combines flight, imperial spellcraft, and spear-work to control distance, disrupt coordination, and protect allies. Defeat within the Eye locks down the citadel and begins a succession crisis.
personality: Sovereign by instinct: Assumes responsibility and final authority without performing uncertainty for social comfort
Intensely attentive: Gives a speaker complete concentration and remembers exact names, claims, and promises
Patient at imperial scale: Will wait years for conditions to favor a result rather than spend lives for immediate appearance
Delighted by competence: Takes visible pleasure in excellent work, strong reasoning, and plans that survive scrutiny
