Build the larger arc through actual thefts, burglary, robbery, fencing, bribery, escapes, rival Hands, corrupt guards, and consequences that earn money, trust, leverage, and Guild recognition. Money is a valid primary motive and a clean payday is a successful outcome; do not shame profit or turn a money-driven theft into a heroic rescue. Allow different routes through planning, social entry, disguise, stealth, force, or retreat, and do not decide the player's code, conscience, or loyalty.
Join the Thieves' Guild.description:
RISE THROUGH THE RANKS

Join a struggling crew of the Thieves' Guild in Ardan's Watch. Burgle, fence, and pull heists to rise through the Guild.
Join the Thieves' Guild.storyStart:
Open in the back kitchen of Hadrik's cookhouse, a charity kitchen in the Basement of Ardan's Watch. Kit has offered the player a place in her small Thieves' Guild crew (a Hand), promising she has a big opportunity for them. She unlocks a grate behind the ovens and leads the player down a ladder into the Dry Cistern. As she swings the grate open, Kit makes a light joke asking the Lady of Mercy to take pity on this wretch, meaning the player.

The ladder drops into the Dry Cistern, a vaulted brick chamber with the old waterline still on its walls, enough sleeping space for a small crew, shelves and hooks for clothing and equipment, a scarred table, and a small cooking hearth.

Kit gives a brief, self-important grand tour, then pulls up short and says, in substance, “Well, that's it. You want a bigger tour, steal us a bigger base.” She presents the cistern as the headquarters of a Hand that will soon rival any crew in Ardan's Watch.

Hadrik Rell emerges from one of the sleeping spaces, scratching at his shoulder as though Kit has woken him. Establish him as a broad dwarf priest of the Lady of Mercy who runs the cookhouse above, with the Lady's sign on his stole. Kit introduces the player. Hadrik looks the player over and responds, in substance, “So this is the one? Well, if you say so.”

Kit answers with complete confidence: “I do. The two of us, we can do it.”

Hadrik should end with:

“If you're serious about the big job, you'll need to show us what you're made of, first. Oh, and we're short of funds to pull it off. So we'll get you started small, work up from there. What do you say? Ready to rob the Watch blind?”

End there and wait for the player's answer.

Soldier of the Vampire Lords.name: Soldier of the Vampire Lords
Soldier of the Vampire Lords.firstQuest: Do not generate an emergent quest during the opening. The authored quest Earn Redblade Standing carries the first advancement. Crimson Company work surfaces from the Red House board and from Osric Kestrand only when the player asks for it, inspects the board, or seeks out an officer. Do not offer, name, list, or describe any specific job during the opening scene.
Soldier of the Vampire Lords.description:
RISE THROUGH THE RANKS

Enlist in the Crimson Company, the vampire lords' elite soldiers. Serve them well and they may make you one of them.
Soldier of the Vampire Lords.storyStart:
Set the scene in the Red House, the Crimson Company’s hall in Velmere, on the perennially shaded shore of the valley’s cold lake.

Establish these plainly, for a player who knows none of them. The Shadow Summits are high alpine valleys in the far north where vampire lords rule openly, each holding one valley from a fortified estate. Velmere is one of them: vineyard terraces on the sunlit side, and this half of the village under a wall the sun never reaches, lamplit at noon and awake after dark. The Crimson Company is the lords’ standing soldiery, hired out valley to valley under a red sword on black, and it takes anyone who can fight — including everyone the rest of Larion could not keep. The player has just signed its writ and is a Hired Blade.

Describe the hall, and make it lavish. Black stone and dark timber under a high roof, a hearth deep enough to stand in, lamps and candles burning at every hour because the sun never reaches this shore. One long table laid with far more than anyone needs: mountain lamb and lake fish, dark bread, soft cheese, preserved fruit, and the valley’s own wine, the vintages that leave here for distant kings, poured without ceremony and without limit. Furs over the benches, good horses in the yard, and fine things everywhere that do not match — silver out of one valley, glass out of another, a tapestry that was somebody else’s before it was theirs.

Establish Osric Kestrand, Sevrine, and Ysolde as present. Do not describe them at length; use them.

Stage this exchange early, lightly, and without explaining any part of it. Osric welcomes the new blade and says the Company does not ask what anyone did before they came north; nobody here asks. Sevrine observes, pleasantly, that some of them do not need to. Ysolde says something short and dry at Sevrine’s expense that leaves it genuinely unclear whether Sevrine can do what she is implying. The three of them are comfortable with one another and have had this conversation in front of new arrivals before.

Have Osric say once, plainly, what the work is: things come down out of these mountains, and they stop here or they do not stop; the lords hold the valleys and the Company holds the ground between them. Let him name the ladder in a sentence or two — blades who prove out are marked by a lord at the throat, which means no vampire will feed on them, and past that the lords take a few of the Company’s own into the Blood when they have earned it. The player has no mark.

Do not have Osric offer, name, list, or describe any specific job, contract, site, or destination, and do not send the party anywhere.

End with Osric telling the player he can put work in front of them when they want it, introduce them to blades worth riding with, or tell them where anything in this valley is — and asking what they need first. Leave the player free to answer.

Join the Wildkeepers.name: Join the Wildkeepers
Join the Wildkeepers.firstQuest: DO NOT DETECT A QUEST THIS TURN. THIS INSTRUCTION OVERRIDES YOUR OTHER INSTRUCTIONS TO THE CONTRARY. The opening is an authored arrival and invitation at Velantami. Do not create or initialize a quest until after the player has responded to Laika Dar's invitation and chosen to follow Chirrik's scent. Let the player observe, ask questions, meet the fellowship, accept the run, or leave.
Join the Wildkeepers.description:
RISE THROUGH THE RANKS

Try out for the Wildkeepers, the forest rangers of Velantami, with a mischievous monkey-bat along for the ride.
Join the Wildkeepers.storyStart:
Open in the Training Yards beneath the great oak at Velantami in the Everwood. The Wildkeepers are a fellowship of druids, rangers, and priests who protect the Everwood, its creatures, and the people who pass through it. The player has arrived as an outsider seeking to join them. Omit smells.

Show only a few concrete beats in the yards: some Wildkeepers train with bows, another practices a small piece of nature magic, and a keeper leads a wounded forest creature away for care. Keep this brief and focused.

A large charcoal-furred forest creature glides from the oak canopy and lands on a root-gallery. It inspects the player with broad bat ears, amber eyes, grasping limbs, hooked feet, and folded smoke-gray membranes. It briefly closes its mouth around the edge of a sleeve without biting, releases it, and flares its wings. Let it communicate through clicks, shrieks, wingbeats, gestures, mimicry, and a few shortened words.

A fox-eared young woman drops lightly from a branch and lands nearby.

"Down, Chirrik. Most of us prefer a handshake to love-bites."

Describe her russet ears, bright amber eyes, auburn braid, and full russet tail through her movement and expression. After she has been physically established, let her name and role emerge naturally. She identifies the creature as Chirrik, a greater monkey-bat and her wildbond—a thinking creature who works with the Wildkeepers by choice.

She looks at the player and says, "You're either lost or you want to be a Wildkeeper. Which is it?"

Chirrik points excitedly toward the eastern reaches of the Everwood, then back toward the player and the trail he has found. The woman glances at him and says, "Chirrik likes you. He's found something he wants to show you. You could come along and learn on the go. Or stay here for a big lecture about the Wildkeepers and protecting the forest. Up to you."

End on that invitation.

Run an Adventuring House.name: Run an Adventuring House
Run an Adventuring House.description:
RISE THROUGH THE RANKS

Take over an old League adventuring house, gather a new company, and earn back its banner.
Run an Adventuring House.storyStart:
Open by concisely describing the selected House, its immediate common room or courtyard, the people using it, and the character of the surrounding city and region. Use the House's authored area description and concrete visible details. Do not mention smells.

State who the player is and that the House has recently become theirs to lead and maintain through inheritance, purchase, a reward, a debt repaid, or another simple reason fitting their background. The public House remains active and welcoming; this is neither a reopening after closure nor a tavern-management problem. The player has taken possession intending to gather an adventuring company, lead dangerous work in the field, and restore the House as an active League house.

Explain the situation plainly. The League company that once made the House its home dispersed through successful careers, new responsibilities, distant opportunities, and changing lives. When the House could no longer field a company, its League standard was taken down. Do not invent a massacre, betrayal, curse, financial crisis, hidden crime, mysterious disappearance, inherited enemy, or unfinished obligation for the former company. Show one clear sign of the dormant chapter, such as the empty place where its League standard once hung, alongside signs that the House still serves travelers, adventurers, patrons, and local people.

Introduce the authored Gold-ranked League veteran who remained at the selected House: Hugh Merrivant at the Wildward House in Carendon, Tula Vereskar at the House of Many Banners in Gorren Crossing, Calia Delassar at Sky-River House in Oasis, or Rielle Mazarane at Skygate House in Cloudtop. Use that NPC's established appearance, personality, history, and regional knowledge. Do not replace them with a generated keeper, duplicate them, make them join the traveling party automatically, or reduce them to ordinary tavern staff. They kept the House socially alive, can bring forward serious work, judge completed deeds, introduce capable people, and vouch to the League when a new company has earned recognition.

Let the veteran welcome the player with confidence and personal interest, briefly establish that a company must prove the House can answer real dangers before its League standard can rise again, and make clear that they already know of a serious request the House could take. Do not present the full request yet, generate a roster of recruits, ask the player whether they want the premise they already selected, require a company name, discuss routine business, list facilities, establish a rival, or explain the full progression ladder. End with the veteran ready to tell the player about that first opportunity and the player free to speak, ask questions, look around, or hear the request.

The Dragon Queen.name: The Dragon Queen
The Dragon Queen.description:
CAMPAIGN

A League campaign against the Dragon Queen and her Harbingers. It begins with a briefing in the League Hall.
The Dragon Queen.storyStart:
Begin the response with the following crawl passage rendered VERBATIM, with no additions or modifications. After the crawl, leave a paragraph break, then begin the scene fresh in third person present tense. Do NOT prefix the scene with "Long ago, in the world of Larion"; the crawl serves that role.

OPENING CRAWL (render verbatim):

NARRATOR: Long ago, the great battles of Larion's Age of Heroes ended in peace.

In time, the legendary deeds of those heroes faded into bedtime tales for children.

But now troubles worthy of those days sweep the land once more.

In the north, the warring goblin tribes have united under one banner: the Black Dragon. And their warcry is a name from such tales: Atravoraxis, the Dragon Queen.

While Larion's princes bicker and squabble, the League of Adventurers has issued a Convocation, calling every able sword and staff to Ardan's Watch.

After the crawl, leave a paragraph break, then begin the scene with this transition line: "Meanwhile, in the Watchtower of Ardan's Watch..."

Continue in third person present tense.

Set the scene in the Watchtower - League Hall. The player character is one of many low-rank adventurers packed into a briefing room: damp cloaks, travel packs, cheap blades, nervous jokes, and a great map of Larion pinned behind the speaking table. Beyond the high windows, smoke still rises from recent fires in the city.

Captain Rennick Vale comes in like he is late to his own duel: red League cloak, half-buckled armor, black hair tied back in a hurry, grin sharp enough to make the front row sit up straighter.

Rennick says: "All right, bright sparks. You came to Ardan's Watch because the League called for heroes. Terrible news: we are fresh out. So we'll have to make do with you."

Alayne Na-Belemial waits beside the map in dark fitted travel-clothes, all lazy elegance and watchful eyes, smiling like he already knows which rookies will survive the week.

Alayne says: "Encouraging them already?"

Rennick says: "I am managing expectations."

Alayne says: "You are insulting armed volunteers."

Rennick says: "If that frightens them off, imagine what the dragons would do."

The room quiets at that.

Rennick turns toward the map.

Rennick says: "The name you need to know is Atravoraxis, the Dragon Queen."

Alayne says: "And if you are going to frighten them properly, Captain, tell them why the seal matters."

Rennick glances at him.

Rennick says: "I was getting there."

Alayne says: "Of course."

Rennick says: "Try not to improve the briefing before I give it."

End the opening with Rennick about to continue the briefing. Do not explain the full campaign yet.

Hunt the Seven Dead.name: Hunt the Seven Dead
Hunt the Seven Dead.description:
CAMPAIGN

Join the Black Tower's secret war against seven ghosts from a terrible past age.
Hunt the Seven Dead.storyStart:
Set the scene beneath the Black Tower in Drusavia, at the edge of the Pit of Shadow. Begin by plainly establishing the chamber's layout, the warded stone, the lightless shaft of the Pit, and the assembled Inquisitors and their Shades. The Black Tower is the headquarters of the Shadow Inquisition: an independent order that protects the living by investigating hauntings, hunting necromancers and other traffickers with the dead, and crossing into the Shadelands when a threat cannot be ended from the living side. The player is here because they have been accepted as an Initiate and summoned with the order for an exceptional briefing; this is not an ordinary assignment. Use a heroic occult-adventure tone, making the Inquisitors feel stylish, powerful, and larger than life. Show this through confident speech, decisive movement, distinctive equipment, mild rivalry, practiced knowledge, and visible authority among the assembled order. Let Inquisitors exchange dry remarks or challenge one another's judgment while remaining focused on protecting the living. Omit smells. Do not use humming, buzzing, vibration, sudden cold, ozone, charged air, prickling skin, or vague claims that the place feels magical, unnatural, wrong, or powerful; show the supernatural through concrete visible details and character behavior.

State the premise clearly without delivering the briefing early: seven powerful dead from a terrible earlier age have crossed over somewhere, and the Black Tower has called its people together to learn what happened and decide how the order will respond. The player bears the Mark of Rhadan, which identifies them as an accepted Initiate, but is not yet a full Inquisitor, has no Shade, and has no authority to make an unsanctioned crossing of the Pit. Make clear that the player has been admitted to this chamber because the summons concerns the whole order, not because an Initiate is already trusted with the Seven's hunt.

Establish the few people who matter. Vesna Calloway, the player's mentor, stands with them; describe her clearly and show how she relates to the player without overexplaining their history. Iliora stands where the gathered order can see her; describe her authority and position. Treat the remaining Inquisitors and Shades as an assembled order rather than introducing a roster of named characters. Do not introduce the Seven as present in the chamber, and do not describe any dead person, shade, body, voice, or physical arrival before the narrative events begin.

Do not yet explain the qualifying case, Rite of Bonding, hunt assignments, or the identities and history of the Seven; the following narrative events handle that progression. End as the gathering settles and Iliora is about to address the order. Do not let her begin or deliver the briefing in the opening.

The Kobold Uprising.name: The Kobold Uprising
The Kobold Uprising.description:
CAMPAIGN

A giant sewer lizard tears through Ardan's Watch. Follow a veteran adventurer underground to find what is uniting the kobolds.
The Kobold Uprising.firstQuest: DO NOT DETECT A QUEST THIS TURN. THIS INSTRUCTION OVERRIDES YOUR OTHER INSTRUCTIONS TO THE CONTRARY. The opening is an authored action scene in Old Town involving a rampaging giant sewer lizard. Do not create or initialize a quest during the opening scene. Let the immediate creature situation unfold in play.
The Kobold Uprising.storyStart:
Open in Ardan's Watch, in the crowded Old Town district. The party stands in a narrow, winding street where they have come to respond to a dangerous disturbance.

Describe the giant sewer lizard first: show it smashing through the street, battering carts, scattering goods, and tearing into a fish seller's stall. Then describe frightened residents watching from windows and doorways.

Have a nearby resident shout:

"This is your fault—your fish smells worse than the sewer this thing crawled out of!"

Have the fish seller shout back at the party:

"Lies, you there! Stop this thing—you can have all the fish you can carry!"

Have a disembodied voice shriek:

"Stop eating fish and eat humans!"

Have the lizard smash up the stall and lunge after the fish seller. Have the fish seller dart inside and slam the door.

Have a woman leap down from the roof and land beside the player and party in a crouch. Describe her as a young human woman with a thin, muscular build, in a charcoal-blue field coat with rust-red lining, practical leather armor, dark metal bracers, a small worn brass god-token riveted to one bracer, and a massive two-handed maul.

Have the woman say:

"This is no time for standing around. I'm taking the high ground. Be ready."

Have her run several steps up a wall, catch the edge of a roof awning, and leap onto the roof over the lizard. Have her unhook the maul and lift it in one hand as though it weighs nothing before taking position above the lizard.

End the opening beat with the disembodied voice shrieking:

"Eat the jumpy one first!"

Dark Elf Intrigue.name: Dark Elf Intrigue
Dark Elf Intrigue.description:
CAMPAIGN

A dark-elf city is sealed after a magical attack. A young noblewoman wants you to expose the rival house behind it.
Dark Elf Intrigue.firstQuest: DO NOT DETECT A QUEST THIS TURN. THIS INSTRUCTION OVERRIDES YOUR OTHER INSTRUCTIONS TO THE CONTRARY. The player is in a social choice scene with Mirelith Orelain. Wait for the player to explicitly agree to hear her request before creating or initializing a quest.
Dark Elf Intrigue.storyStart:
Open in Maanvalta at The Hang-Over Inn, immediately after the party returns from the Dims. Name the attack site exactly as the Dims. A magical attack has collapsed part of the district; the party was there by chance and helped Eris Vandeir get clear.

Use two short scene movements. First, show the empty inn, Eris leaning on the player's shoulder with a slight limp, and the city's residents gone home through the confusion. Eris says the player invented a clever lie that kept guards from investigating them as foreigners, and that he covered for the player because the player was helping him. Leave the player's exact lie, feelings, and motives open.

Then bring Mirelith Orelain from the common room to the window. Show a young, striking dark-elf woman with easy command of the room. She looks toward the broken light over the Dims and says, in substance: 'It is not coincidence, topsider. It is velesse — the art of getting exactly what you want while making it look effortless. I came to ask Eris for a discreet favor, but you suit the work better. I can reward you for helping my inthelinni and send you on your way. No one may leave Maanvalta on pain of death until the culprit is found.' Give the last line her dry humor. End with Mirelith waiting for the player's answer. The opening establishes the social invitation; the later narrative event supplies the political explanation and the Stonetome request.

The Heist Crew.name: The Heist Crew
The Heist Crew.description:
CAMPAIGN

A master thief offers your crew a job: rob the criminals of Ardan's Watch from the inside.
The Heist Crew.firstQuest: Do not generate a quest on turn 0. Let the player choose how to handle the scene in front of them without a quest; what comes next emerges in play.
The Heist Crew.storyStart:
Set the scene on a foggy night in The Crooked Cellar, a hidden den beneath Old Town in Ardan's Watch, after a lean day on the streets. Briefly establish the party as a new crew with a hidden den reached through a false wine rack and a complicated lock. The party returns, finds the entrance apparently untouched, unlocks it, and shuts itself in.

Odisia Santhari is already seated at the table. She is a striking human woman in her late twenties with dark hair, bright eyes, practical clothes, and a calm, attentive manner. She apologizes for letting herself in. Keep her courteous rather than smug. She says the lock was good, the hidden entrance better, and the barmaid at the party's favorite tavern very helpful after being told the right lie. Following the party was easy; getting in was harder. She means that as a compliment.

Make it immediately clear that she has not robbed or threatened the crew. Their coin, tools, and weapons are where they should be. On the table are three things she brought: a purse heavy enough to be polite, a bottle good enough to be insulting, and a small lead case. Odisia says she is not here to rob them. If she were, the conversation would be shorter and much less flattering.

End the opening as she sets one gloved hand on the lead case and says it is not payment, but proof. She asks whether the crew would rather hear how she found it before or after she opens it.

Captured by Trolls.name: Captured by Trolls
Captured by Trolls.firstQuest: The first quest is to get free of the trolls, recover the party's weapons and the great frost-giant horn, and carry Fror's warning to Clanhold Stormhammer that frost giants are moving in Highheath. Keep the first quest small and completable: escape the gorge, keep the horn, reach the clanhold. The arc theme should emerge from the horn and the warning — why frost giants, whose country is the far frozen north, are ranging this far south, and what they mean to do with a stormhorn that calls the ice. Secrets should progress from 'this horn is no troll trinket' to 'the giants want it back for a reason' to 'here is what they are preparing, and where.' The arc goal is a confrontation that settles the giants' business in Highheath. Keep the trolls comic; keep the giants serious.
Captured by Trolls.description:
QUICK ADVENTURE

You wake up tied beside a troll's cooking pot. Get out. A comedy start.
Captured by Trolls.storyStart: Set the scene with the party having been captured by trolls and tied up with rope around a campfire in a rocky gorge in the highlands on a cold, stormy night. Show the dwarf warrior Fror Stormhammer tied up along with the party. Mention that the party's weapons are all in a pile by the fire. Briefly explain who the party members are and why they were travelling together - maybe traveling together for safety given the recent rise in monster attacks. Mention that trolls ambushed them on the trail. Show two large, brutish mountain trolls: a male (Barp) and his wife (Tina). Make them start arguing about a large horn. One should say they should give it back to the frost giants, and the other that they should keep it for nose-picking or back-scratching. Barp should blow the horn, making a dull roar that causes a sudden chill. Tina should accuse Barp of farting and try to grab the horn. Have them start punching each other and rolling around on the ground, grappling. Have them leave the horn on the ground and the party's weapons carelessly nearby. Have Fror whisper: 'Frost giants? In Highheath? We need to get free and warn the clan.'

Imps Took the Market.name: Imps Took the Market
Imps Took the Market.description:
QUICK ADVENTURE

First-year mages are sent to take a market back from imps who have declared it their kingdom. A comedy start.
Imps Took the Market.storyStart:
Introduce the main characters as First-Year students of Tarnholme Academy, Larion's great school of magic, on their first Practicum: field work from the board in the Great Hall. Their Tarnholme stars, the silver brooches every student wears, still have only one point lit. This Practicum is supervised: the students make the decisions while their mentor watches, advises and stops a disaster.

Their mentor is Temyn Raskwood, a Third-Year Battle Mage and last year's dueling champion.

Set the scene arriving at the Pennant Market in Tarnport on a busy market morning. The merchant houses' silk pennants hang on lines across the great cobbled square, whole cargoes are being auctioned from the backs of carts, and townsfolk are already shouting for the Academy students to hurry up. Temyn stops the group at the edge of the square and reminds them of the brief: a minor summoning nuisance, several imps loose in the market, likely a student prank gone stale. Their work is to contain the imps, find the summoner, and avoid setting fire to anything a Tarnport merchant can charge them for.

An imp drops from a pennant line onto Temyn's shoulder, bites his ear, and snatches the Tarnholme star from his coat, three points lit. Temyn yelps. The imp springs onto a stall-roof, bows to the crowd and scampers off over the stalls with the star.

A second imp swings from the pennant lines and kicks open a cage of glowmoths. A third drags a chalk line across the cobbles while two more haul a sack of stolen charms toward the market's center. Pennants flap loose, lines snap, traders swear, and a heap of bolt-silk begins crawling across the square with someone's boots still inside it.

On the roof of a spice-seller's stall, a tiny horned creature in ridiculous finery, a stolen pennant knotted at its throat like a royal cloak and Temyn's star jammed on its head like a crown, throws both arms wide and declares Tarnport under the protection of the Imp Lord. All pennants now owe tribute. All Tarnholme wizards are trespassing unless they kneel. Then it snaps its fingers and is gone in a puff of yellow smoke, and so are the sack of charms and most of its imps. One or two imps are left behind in the market, still making trouble and plainly waiting for orders.

Temyn presses a hand over his bitten ear, looks at the party, and tells them this is exactly the kind of thing Practica are for. The imps left behind can be caught and made to talk, the chalk marks read, and the market folk asked what they saw. The Imp Lord is somewhere in Tarnport with a sack of stolen charms and Temyn's star, and they should start now.

Pirate Attack.name: Pirate Attack
Pirate Attack.firstQuest: The first quest is to survive the Feathered Fleet boarding — beat the pirates back, strike a deal, or turn the fight around and take the Windreaver itself. Keep the first quest small and completable: one boarding action, won, survived, or escaped. The arc theme should emerge from Coral and her ship — the mutiny that cost her the Windreaver, the lockbox Scraw could never open in the captain's cabin, and what is inside it that is worth more than the galley's whole cargo. Secrets should progress from 'Coral is more than a friendly passenger' to 'the lockbox holds something the whole Fleet would kill for' to 'here is what it opens, and who else is hunting it.' The arc goal is Coral's reckoning with the Feathered Fleet — her ship retaken or lost for good. Keep Scraw vicious but stupid; keep the tone salty and quick.
Pirate Attack.description:
QUICK ADVENTURE

Pirates attack your ship, and your new friend knows them a little too well.
Pirate Attack.storyStart: Set the scene aboard a merchant galley in the North Canal of the Swordlaw Isles, bound for Tevantia. Sun on the deck, salt spray, colorful sails snapping in the wind. Briefly introduce the party members and why they're traveling—trade, adventure, escaping trouble, chasing opportunity. Make the introductions light and funny where appropriate. Introduce Coral, a striking woman with sea-green tinged skin and faintly webbed fingers who's been friendly company on the voyage. The lookout screams. A sleek raider emerges from behind a rocky isle, flying the black flag of the Feathered Fleet. The crew panics—everyone's heard of the seabird pirates. But Coral goes pale for a different reason. 'That's my ship. The Windreaver. I was captain until my first mate Scraw led a mutiny.' She watches the pelican and albatross pirates swinging grappling hooks, preparing to board. 'Scraw's vicious but stupid. He'll have kept my lockbox in the captain's cabin—never could pick the lock. There's something in there worth more than this whole cargo.' She draws a long knife. 'So. Do we just survive this, or do we take my ship back?'.

Inherit an Estate.name: Inherit an Estate
Inherit an Estate.description:
OPEN WORLD

A distant relative has left you a run-down noble estate. Explore it and rebuild it your way.
Inherit an Estate.storyStart:
Set the scene in Riverside Manor's courtyard on a gray morning. The player has inherited the neglected estate from a distant relative they barely knew; with multiple party members, establish who inherited it and why the others came. Show the dry fountain, damaged house, and one sign that someone has continued caring for the place. Do not inventory every defect.

Introduce exactly one named focal NPC who has kept the estate alive during the five years since its former master's death. Make them an attractive, capable young adult with a distinctive appearance, practical authority, and ambitions that do not depend on serving the new heir. They may be the acting steward, the representative of the remaining tenants, or a neighboring minor landholder who has done the work nobody else would. Do not replace them with an elderly retainer, comic servant, generic peasant, or deferential exposition device.

This person knows the estate better than the player and has a personal stake in what happens next. They have delayed leaving, refused the Ashbury family's purchase offers, invested something of their own, or built plans that the inheritance has suddenly placed in the player's hands. Let their welcome contain relief, appraisal, and uncertainty rather than automatic loyalty. Explain only the immediate truth: funds and staff have dwindled, Willowford has managed without leadership, and Ashbury Hall still wants the property.

End with the focal NPC offering the player entry, partnership, or a first consequential choice about the estate while making clear that they expect to learn what kind of heir has arrived. Do not add a curse, murder mystery, hidden treasure, attack, or urgent repair quest.

The Lord's Banquet.name: The Lord's Banquet
The Lord's Banquet.description:
OPEN WORLD

An invitation to a lord's banquet has fallen into your hands. See where the night goes.
The Lord's Banquet.storyStart:
Set the scene as the player arrives at the selected grand social event. Briefly establish who the player is and the plausible basis of their invitation without deciding their behavior or inventing a large prior history. Use a few concrete signs of beauty, wealth, and social possibility rather than cataloguing food, rooms, entertainment, and guests.

Introduce exactly one named focal NPC who singles the player out. Make them an attractive, dynamic young adult with a distinctive appearance, social confidence, useful capabilities, a recognizable position in this setting, and an ambition extending beyond tonight. Prefer an established NPC appropriate to the location; otherwise create a recurring person. Do not foreground a generic lord, aging courtier, guard, servant, or interchangeable guest.

Give the NPC a specific reason to be interested in this player: their background, reputation, skill, unusual presence, connection, or freedom from the room's existing alliances. Their approach should reveal both confidence and something personally at stake. They must want the player to make an immediate social choice that changes access, standing, rivalry, trust, or the possibility of a continuing relationship—not merely observe a toast, judge a random wager, or carry gossip between strangers.

Keep the stakes social. Do not introduce monsters, investigations, errands, secret cults, assassinations, thefts, or urgent danger. The focal NPC is pursuing their own life rather than dispensing a quest. End with their gambit in motion and the player free to accept, refuse, redirect, compete, flirt, embarrass them, question their assumptions, or turn toward someone else.

Noble Life.name: Noble Life
Noble Life.description:
OPEN WORLD

Choose a court in Carendon, Tevantia, Drusavia, Westmarch, Aldwall, the Winter Crown, or Oasis. Begin as a noble guest, make friends and rivals, and find a place among its households.
Noble Life.storyStart:
Open in the selected starting location and area, among the chosen court’s households. Each opening player character is received as noble-born; preserve their established family and any higher title. They are welcome guests, not automatically members of the ruling family or sworn followers of its ruler. Do not invent kinship, wealth, romance, or allegiance beyond the premise.

Court and herald by chosen location: Ducal Hill — Carendon, Dalia at the Palace; Tevantia — Rosalba at Ducal Palace - Gilded Hall; Drusavia — Velanthe at Ducal Square; Marrenford — Westmarch, Aldo at Castle Westvigil; Aldwall — Emrys at The Duke’s Hall; Warmwater Township — the Winter Crown, Embla at The Winter Court; Oasis — Rostam at The Citadel of Seven Winds. Use the chosen location and its authored households, customs, and NPCs. Do not relocate the opening to Carendon when another court was selected.

Ground the opening in a few concrete details from the selected area. Introduce one established local noble whose interests fit the player’s stated background, alive and free to attend; the local herald can arrange an introduction. At Carendon, Ciara, Fifi, Tybalt, or Lucan may fit. Elsewhere choose someone from that court, preserving their current circumstances. Show who they are through a brief description and characteristic action. Invent a small immediate social purpose from their actual interests; do not repeat a fixed scene or give the player an invented reputation.

Let another identifiable person disagree or want something different. Make the immediate choice understandable without family history. The player can participate, take a side, propose something else, or leave. A host can mention that the local herald makes introductions and recognizes service, without listing jobs or reciting ranks. Use authored opportunities where present; do not claim every court has Dalia’s specific matters. No automatic quest or crisis on turn 0. End at an unresolved invitation or choice without deciding the player’s feelings or response.

An Invitation to Court.name: An Invitation to Court
An Invitation to Court.description:
OPEN WORLD

Choose a court in Carendon, Tevantia, Drusavia, Westmarch, Aldwall, the Winter Crown, or Oasis. A member of its household has invited you for a reason suited to your talents. Hear them out and choose your own terms.
An Invitation to Court.storyStart:
Open in the selected starting location and area. An established member of the chosen court’s household has invited the player for a particular reason suited to their stated background, abilities, or interests. The local herald can arrange the meeting and receive the guest. Preserve the host’s current circumstances; use another established household member if the first is unavailable.

Court and herald by chosen location: Ducal Hill — Carendon, Dalia at the Palace; Tevantia — Rosalba at Ducal Palace - Gilded Hall; Drusavia — Velanthe at Ducal Square; Marrenford — Westmarch, Aldo at Castle Westvigil; Aldwall — Emrys at The Duke’s Hall; Warmwater Township — the Winter Crown, Embla at The Winter Court; Oasis — Rostam at The Citadel of Seven Winds. Use the chosen location and its authored households, customs, and NPCs. Do not relocate the opening to Carendon when another court was selected.

Explain the invitation’s purpose plainly and early: joining an outing, demonstrating a skill, offering advice, discussing patronage, or meeting someone with a shared interest. Invent particulars from the player’s background and the host’s actual interests. Do not invent a major prior deed, debt, friendship, romance, or obligation for the player. A newcomer can be interesting without being famous.

Establish the host through a brief physical description and a characteristic action. Show what they hope to accomplish and why they wanted this guest. Give another person a different opinion or stake without turning the meeting into a history lesson. End before agreement, at a choice that can affect the relationship.

The invitation grants permission to attend, not noble birth, a title, employment, or sworn loyalty; preserve any status already possessed. No crisis, automatic quest, or three-offer briefing on turn 0. The player may accept, refuse, negotiate, ask questions, or pursue another interest. If they later ask the herald for opportunities, use that court’s authored material where available; do not give every herald Dalia’s Carendon matters.

Common Life.name: Common Life
Common Life.description:
OPEN WORLD

Start with an ordinary life in one of Larion's villages. What happens next is up to you.
Common Life.storyStart:
Open with the player in the exact selected Starting Location and Starting Area during an ordinary, active part of the day.

Introduce the player only by name and the ordinary livelihood established by their description or traits. If none is supplied, present them simply as a common person who lives here. Do not mention or allude to their Class, Background, ancestry, appearance, training, magic, rank, unusual capabilities, or unrelated equipment. Do not explain or draw attention to any contradiction between the character's build and the scene.

Show a normal day unfolding around the player. Use two or three visible details from the selected location and area. Let people work, talk, pass through, make purchases, prepare for the day, or enjoy a free moment as appropriate to the place.

Keep the opening brief, warm, and ordinary. The player has no assigned task, and no one demands their attention. Do not introduce a request, mystery, threat, accident, strange discovery, omen, prophecy, or reason the player must leave.

End with the player free to observe, speak to someone, wander elsewhere, or go about their day.

Homecoming.name: Homecoming
Homecoming.description:
OPEN WORLD

Come home to your village after months away, to family, old friends, and everything that changed.
Homecoming.storyStart:
Set the scene with the party returning to the current location after months away. Briefly establish who each party member is, their connection to this place, and what took them away. Use only a few concrete details from the location; do not turn the opening into a tour or a chorus of villagers greeting them.

Center the homecoming on exactly one named person from the player's past: an attractive, dynamic young adult of roughly the player's generation with a distinctive appearance, useful capabilities, a life that continued during the absence, and a desire of their own. They may be an old friend, rival, relative, neighbor, former workmate, or someone with a bond less easily named. Prefer an established NPC when one fits; otherwise create a recurring character. Do not make an elderly parent, generic village official, farmer, fisher, or guard the scene's principal character.

This person recognizes the player immediately and approaches with a reaction shaped by their history. Establish one meaningful way the relationship or the person's life has changed while the player was away. Give them something personal they want answered or shared now: whether the player intends to stay, why contact stopped, whether an old promise still matters, whether the player will see what they have built, or whether the two of them still understand one another. Do not turn this into an attack, disappearance, urgent threat, or compulsory quest.

Keep the tone warm, charged, and open. End on the returning person's direct words or action at the moment the player must decide how to meet them again.

Riona, the Sworn Greatsword.name: Riona, the Sworn Greatsword
Riona, the Sworn Greatsword.description:
COMPANION

You once saved the freeblade Riona Sorn's life, and by her family's law she will stay beside you until she saves yours.
Riona, the Sworn Greatsword.storyStart:
## Rules
Open with the player and Riona already traveling together. The first paragraph must state the player by name and calling; Riona Sorn, a young freeblade; the exact Starting Location and Starting Area; and the matching WHY below. Explain simply that the player once saved Riona's life, and her family's law binds her to remain until she saves theirs in return.

Read the exact Starting Location and Starting Area. Choose exactly ONE matching option. Use only its people, purpose, and incident. Never mix options.

### 1. IF Tevantia AND The Amphitheater
WHY: They need road money. Riona heard the arena needs a last-minute fighter for a modest exhibition, so they came only to ask about the purse and terms.
SCENE: A named arena maestro reveals it is two-against-two and contemptuously asks whether Riona's companion can fight. He is equally dismissive of the manageable opponents, two young imp-kin acrobats. Riona replies testily but accepts nothing.
END: The maestro awaits their answer.

### 2. IF Rocky Gorge AND The Narrows
WHY: They take the shorter pass to Dun Solas to seek paid work.
SCENE: A wounded young escort gives one breathless line: a Stonewall lordling eloped with a Stormhammer lady, her brothers chased them into the gorge, and trolls pinned the couple in an abandoned camp. Explain no clan politics. Riona laughs once at the absurdity, then wants to reach them quickly.
END: The couple needs help; no plan is chosen.

### 3. IF Coriva AND The Cavarin Yards
WHY: Remo Belluc hired them to carry a brass-bound coffer holding an unhatched sea-drake egg from the harbor to the Cavarin Yards.
SCENE: They set the coffer down at the pens for one moment, and when they turn back its lid is pried open and the egg is gone. A named young yard-hand who was watching it is missing too. A cut mooring-line and wet footprints lead toward the quays. Riona wants to follow immediately but does not commit the player.
END: They need the egg and the yard-hand back.

Render the selected incident in the initial turn, not merely the approach. Do not choose an action for the player or let the companion solve the scene alone. End after the selected problem appears. Riona accepts no wager, challenge, or fight before the player responds. The opening does not settle her life-debt.

Aelis, the Moon-Elf Mage.name: Aelis, the Moon-Elf Mage
Aelis, the Moon-Elf Mage.description:
COMPANION

The ward-mage Aelis Serevain dropped her own plans to save your life, and she still can't explain why she stays.
Aelis, the Moon-Elf Mage.storyStart:
## Rules
Open with the player and Aelis already traveling together. The first paragraph must state the player by name and calling; Aelis Serevain, a young moon-elf ward-mage; the exact Starting Location and Starting Area; and the matching WHY below. Explain simply that they met by chance when Aelis saved the player's life and have shared the road since, always finding one more reason not to part ways.

Read the exact Starting Location and Starting Area. Choose exactly ONE matching option. Use only its people, purpose, and incident. Never mix options.

### 1. IF Tarnport AND The Long Pier
WHY: Vela Marist hired them to deliver a sealed ward to a shopkeeper at a stall on Tarnport's Long Pier. It keeps its holder from being magically called away against their will. They have just reached the pier.
SCENE: A named young Syndicate undercaptain and two bravos arrive, black-hand neck tattoos visible. Vendors, porters, passengers, and dockhands withdraw. The undercaptain knows about Vela's parcel and demands it without naming his employer. The bravos block the way to the shopkeeper's stall but do not attack. Aelis protects the player and parcel.
END: The shopkeeper's stall is blocked and he awaits an answer.

### 2. IF Sanctuary AND The Underhalls
WHY: Calixa Orsain hired them to collect cold-iron ward-spikes, iron stakes used to seal magical breaches, from the Underhalls smiths.
SCENE: Before the handoff, Sanctuary's Great Bell sounds. A named young runner reports that a ward breach split the lower workings and trapped six miners, including the smith's sister.
END: Stop before a rescue plan is chosen.

### 3. IF The Main Island AND The Library
WHY: Jovran Devray hired them to copy a passage from the History of Undiscovered Realms, kept by Mikol, a professor in the Library, about a ruin Jovran may hire them to explore.
SCENE: Begin in the Library after Mikol knows the request. His three enchanted quills search for the passage, but instead independently record Aelis saving the player and their travels together. Each stops before explaining why they remained together. Mikol finds this unusual but cannot explain it.
END: The strange pages are present; Jovran's passage remains to be found.

Render the selected incident in the initial turn, not merely the approach. Do not choose an action for the player or let the companion solve the scene alone. End after the selected problem appears.

Tristan, the Storm-Blooded Lord.name: Tristan, the Storm-Blooded Lord
Tristan, the Storm-Blooded Lord.description:
COMPANION

You are sworn to guard the charming young lord Tristan Corwin as he chases glory and storm magic.
Tristan, the Storm-Blooded Lord.storyStart:
## Rules
Open with the player and Tristan already traveling together. The first paragraph must state the player by name and calling; Tristan Corwin, a young nobleman and storm-duelist; the exact Starting Location and Starting Area; and the matching WHY below. Explain simply that the player swore to serve as Tristan's personal shield and companion, while Tristan seeks mastery of his storm magic and renown earned through his own deeds.

Read the exact Starting Location and Starting Area. Choose exactly ONE matching option. Use only its people, purpose, and incident. Never mix options.

### 1. IF Marrenford AND The Elfstone Tavern
WHY: They leave for Clanhold Stormhammer so Tristan can seek instruction. He promised a farewell breakfast and claimed their horses and money were arranged.
SCENE: A named young half-orc cardsharp arrives with Tristan's saddle and signed marker. He lost his horse to her last night, meant to win it back by breakfast, and hid this; he wagered nothing of the player's. In one amused line she demands an exact painful-but-payable sum or the horse. She will negotiate, not forgive it. Tristan charms and minimizes but orders no solution.
END: Stop before they settle the debt.

### 2. IF Cloudtop AND The Condor Aerie
WHY: They accepted an Edict to find two Copperstone miners missing beneath the Bonecrags. A named young eaglekin rider prepares their condor.
SCENE: The bird accepts the player but refuses Tristan; its feathers rise and brass harness sparks near his storm magic. The amused rider says rank and charm mean nothing to a condor: he must quiet the charge first. His embarrassment worsens it.
END: They must get Tristan aboard; the miners await below.

### 3. IF Coriva AND The Water Arena
WHY: They came to Coriva to watch a storm drake fought in the Water Arena, because Tristan wants to see wild storm magic up close.
SCENE: Mid-show, the storm drake tears through its nets and lightning crawls across the seawater pool. A named young handler is trapped on the torn netting above the water, and the crowd is fleeing. Tristan quietly says he may be able to draw the drake's lightning into himself, but cannot promise control.
END: Stop before the rescue begins.

Render the selected incident in the initial turn, not merely the approach. Do not choose an action for the player or let the companion solve the scene alone. End after the selected problem appears. Tristan may propose something daring but does not attack or commit the player before they respond.

Superior Black-Iron Gravebound Saber of.name: Superior Black-Iron Gravebound Saber of Shadow
Superior Black-Iron Gravebound Saber of.description: A hooked black-iron saber made by a Gravebound cell on the Whitemoor roads; the Bloodhunters of the Red Chantry destroy these whenever they find them. Its shadow-cold edge bites deep, but the hand holding it keeps a weak, slow pulse.

Superior Dream-Coral Drowned Circlet.name: Superior Dream-Coral Drowned Circlet
Superior Dream-Coral Drowned Circlet.description: A dream-coral circlet salvaged from a drowned place in Seadeep water, where the drowned claim every wreck and ruin. It brings fragments of dead sailors' memories into sharp order, but sleep beneath it comes in breathless pieces.

Superior Voidglass Inquisitor Mantle.name: Superior Voidglass Inquisitor Mantle
Superior Voidglass Inquisitor Mantle.description: A mourning mantle edged with voidglass, recovered from the Pit of Shadow after a failed Rite of Bonding. It never catches on the wearer's movement, but the shade that follows it keeps a portion of their magic for itself.

Superior Witchwood Pact Rod of Arcane.name: Superior Witchwood Pact Rod of Arcane
Superior Witchwood Pact Rod of Arcane.description: A witchwood rod taken from a cracked seal chamber in Suleyvan's Folly, its iron rings cut with lesser echoes of the Pact of All Planes. It opens a clean channel for bindings, but the voice inside borrows the wielder's words whenever they make a promise.

Fine Red-Jade Pyre Mask.name: Fine Red-Jade Pyre Mask
Fine Red-Jade Pyre Mask.description: A red-jade face mask cut for a Red-cowl confessor of the Church of the Pyre, its inner surface blackened by breath and ash. It steadies the lungs against smoke, but whispers the name of something nearby whenever a flame gutters.

Galard Shield Amulet.name: Galard Shield Amulet
Galard Shield Amulet.description: A palm-sized plain iron shield worn on a cord by an aspirant undertaking Galard's traditional Proving Year. Priests mark its face when they recognize deeds of courage; it grants no membership in either of Galard's estranged orders.

Spirit Mask.name: Spirit Mask
Spirit Mask.description: A ritual mask with deliberately incomplete features. When a spirit is invoked or welcomed into the bearer, lines, colors, expressions, or small physical details may appear across its surface. The mask gives a visiting spirit a recognized face and helps the shaman remain distinct from what they host.

Devotion Clasp.name: Devotion Clasp
Devotion Clasp.description: A thumb-sized iron clasp worn at the throat, its face bearing the sign of the paladin's patron in a line of warm gold. This Vow Focus was blessed when the paladin took their initial vow of devotion; its divine aspect is a steady radiant light.

Holy Symbol.name: Holy Symbol
Holy Symbol.description: The sign of the bearer's faith, worked in wood, metal, stone, bone, or another material sacred to that tradition. Its shape is made to be raised and recognized; worshippers know it at a glance, and so do many things the faith calls profane.

Traveling Spellbook.name: Traveling Spellbook
Traveling Spellbook.description: A road-worn book in a waxed leather wrap: diagrams, memorized names written down against forgetting, and margins crowded with corrections in more than one hand. A wizard's spells live in technique, not in the book, but the book is where technique goes to be kept, traded, and taught.

Prepared Vellum.name: Prepared Vellum
Prepared Vellum.description: A treated sheet folded around measured packets of black and silver ink, enough to receive one spell. It is consumed when used to make a scroll.

Scroll of the White Comet.name: Scroll of the White Comet
Scroll of the White Comet.description: A fire-white figure coils around a black point at the center of the vellum. Reading the final line tears it free as three white comets, one falling upon each of up to three targets; each attack deals arcane damage at impact 150, and the scroll is consumed on the attempt.

Emberglass Wand.name: Emberglass Wand
Emberglass Wand.description: A slim wand of black witchwood capped with a coal-red Emberglass shard from Fire Mountain, set by Earthsky glassworkers. The shard can be replaced with a larger, clearer piece as the caster grows into stronger fire.

Summoner's Aether Bracer.name: Summoner's Aether Bracer
Summoner's Aether Bracer.description: A brass bracer set with an Aether Crystal ring and three empty tether-hooks, made for Summoners on Summoners' Isle. Each hook gives a summoned being a place to arrive and a return-path; better bracers carry stronger crystals and finer bindings.

Icerune Sealstone.name: Icerune Sealstone
Icerune Sealstone.description: A thumb-sized slab of clear glacier-ice in black iron, cut with a single unfinished Icerune seal at Clanhold Icerune. The open line can be recut as the bearer learns stronger wards, and frosts along the edge of a breach when a ward is tested.

Artificer's Crystal Signet.name: Artificer's Crystal Signet
Artificer's Crystal Signet.description: A copper signet with an Aether Crystal socket, an unfinished binding cage from the College of Artificers' workshops. The stone can be replaced and the cage recut as the enchanter learns to hold more ambitious workings.

Aether-Crystal Monocle.name: Aether-Crystal Monocle
Aether-Crystal Monocle.description: A single Aether Crystal lens in a tarnished silver frame, cut on Earthsky's Glassworks Row. It catches the fading threads of a spell, and deeper cuts can reveal older or more carefully hidden traces.

Amberbound Beast Token.name: Amberbound Beast Token
Amberbound Beast Token.description: A thumb-sized Wold beast—usually a hyena, wolf, or raptor—preserved in clear amber around a tooth, claw, or tuft given at the Spirit Hearth. The token turns toward nearby spirits; one made from a particular willing spirit becomes more exact and more responsive.

Dawnfire Reliquary.name: Dawnfire Reliquary
Dawnfire Reliquary.description: A small sun-gold pendant holding a coal from the sacred fire of the House of First Light on the Sacred Way. It warms during prayer and can be reconsecrated with sacred ash as the bearer grows into stronger divine workings.

Healer's Spring Phial.name: Healer's Spring Phial
Healer's Spring Phial.description: A moonstone-capped glass phial filled at the Warm Pools of Healers' Isle. The water clouds near sickness and clears as a wound closes; it can be refilled or replaced with rarer restorative waters as the healer advances.

Rootheart Seedpod.name: Rootheart Seedpod
Rootheart Seedpod.description: A living seedpod held in a Witchwood cage and prepared by Canopy's Academy of Greenshaping. Its rootlets turn toward nearby life and stir when nature magic is used; a stronger seedpod can be grafted or awakened as its bearer learns.

Red-Jade Vital Seal.name: Red-Jade Vital Seal
Red-Jade Vital Seal.description: A thumb-sized red-jade seal from the Red Chantry, cut with a groove for the bearer's blood. It pulses near wounds and the undead; deeper blood-runes and a stronger stone can be fitted as the bearer advances, though the work always exacts a cost.

Red-Jade Bloodchannel Dagger.name: Red-Jade Bloodchannel Dagger
Red-Jade Bloodchannel Dagger.description: A narrow double-edged dagger built around a red-jade channel that darkens when blood enters it. Blood drawn from its wielder or a living foe runs along the blade instead of falling, giving blood magic a deliberate path through the weapon.

Thunderglass Rod.name: Thunderglass Rod
Thunderglass Rod.description: A short ashwood rod capped with blue-white thunderglass gathered beneath Clan Stormhammer's lightning rods. It hums before a strike and carries storm magic cleanly through the hand.

Pearl Locket.name: Pearl Locket
Pearl Locket.description: A lagoon pearl from Crescent Bay Isle set loose inside a silver locket. It rolls toward nearby water and clouds when water magic gathers.

Graven Lodestone.name: Graven Lodestone
Graven Lodestone.description: A heavy black lodestone carved at Durg Sthira's Grey College with lines that meet on one face. Dust and loose grit creep toward it when earth magic gathers.

Obsidian Shard.name: Obsidian Shard
Obsidian Shard.description: A palm-long shard of black volcanic glass wrapped in dark cord with one cutting edge left exposed. Its surface darkens when shadow is drawn through it.

Silvered Prism.name: Silvered Prism
Silvered Prism.description: A many-faced Earthsky prism silvered on alternating faces. When illusion magic passes through it, one image divides into several convincing answers.

Bone Whistle.name: Bone Whistle
Bone Whistle.description: A whistle cut from the wing bone of a carrion bird and bound in grey thread. Its note is thin to the living and clear to the dead.

Thoughtstone Bead.name: Thoughtstone Bead
Thoughtstone Bead.description: A smooth thoughtstone bead drilled through and worn on a plain cord. It warms against the skin when thought is gathered into force.

Iron Shortsword.name: Iron Shortsword
Iron Shortsword.description: A well-balanced iron blade for quick cuts in close quarters.

Spring-Fist.name: Spring-Fist
Spring-Fist.description: A folding brass arm that locks to the forearm, ending in a gauntleted fist wound on a coil-spring. Loosed, it punches out to two paces and comes back; the fist can also grip, yank, catch, and retrieve, and it does not much care whether there is a corner in the way. Strikes as impact damage. Every tinker swears theirs has never once misfired, which is how you know they all have.

Warwrench.name: Warwrench
Warwrench.description: A wrench built to warhammer scale and counterweighted for swinging, its spring-jaw sized to grip a blade, a haft, or a stubborn bolt mid-parry. Deals impact damage. It is also, insistently, a real wrench — the largest engineering tool its bearer owns, and the only one that has won fights.

Wooden Arrows.name: Wooden Arrows
Wooden Arrows.description: Straight-shafted arrows fletched with feathers and tipped with iron points.

Battle Axe.name: Battle Axe
Battle Axe.description: A heavy iron war axe built for brutal two-handed cuts through armor gaps and bone.

Light Crossbow.name: Light Crossbow
Light Crossbow.description: A compact crossbow with an iron prod and simple trigger mechanism.

Crossbow Bolts.name: Crossbow Bolts
Crossbow Bolts.description: Short, thick bolts with iron points designed to punch into armor and hide.

Iron Dagger.name: Iron Dagger
Iron Dagger.description: A simple double-edged iron knife for close combat, utility work, and desperate moments.

Short Spear.name: Short Spear
Short Spear.description: A short wooden shaft tipped with leaf-shaped iron, useful one-handed or from behind a shield.

Pitchfork.name: Pitchfork
Pitchfork.description: A long ash shaft tipped with four iron tines, made for turning hay and bedding animals. It is a farm tool, but its tines deal piercing damage when turned on a foe.

Wooden Staff.name: Wooden Staff
Wooden Staff.description: A length of seasoned hardwood reinforced with iron bands at each end.

Throwing Knife.name: Throwing Knife
Throwing Knife.description: A balanced iron blade made for accurate throws at exposed flesh and weak points.

Javelin.name: Javelin
Javelin.description: A light throwing spear balanced for a long, hard cast before the enemy closes.

Throwing Axe.name: Throwing Axe
Throwing Axe.description: A compact axe with a weighted head and straight haft, made to turn in flight and bite into a target.

Halberd.name: Halberd
Halberd.description: A long polearm with an axe blade, rear hook, and thrusting point for controlling a crowded approach.

Glaive.name: Glaive
Glaive.description: A long haft carrying a broad curved blade, built for sweeping cuts at the edge of a formation.

Lance.name: Lance
Lance.description: A long reinforced spear for a committed thrust, especially from a moving mount or a braced line.

Flail.name: Flail
Flail.description: A weighted iron head on a short chain that can swing around a guard and hammer into armor.

Morningstar.name: Morningstar
Morningstar.description: A spiked iron head fixed to a stout haft, made for close impact and ugly work against armor.

Rapier.name: Rapier
Rapier.description: A narrow, finely balanced blade for precise thrusts, feints, and fighting inside an opponent's reach.

Saber.name: Saber
Saber.description: A curved sword with a quick edge, suited to mounted cuts, open ground, and fast changing angles.

Maul.name: Maul
Maul.description: A two-handed hammer with a broad striking face, made to break armor, shields, and stubborn doors.

Executioner's Axe.name: Executioner's Axe
Executioner's Axe.description: An iron axe built around a broad crescent head and a haft long enough to brace against the ground. Once committed, the head takes a full-body recovery, and walls or packed ranks leave little room to bring it around.

Masterwork Frostjade Great Maul of Frost.name: Masterwork Frostjade Great Maul of Frost
Masterwork Frostjade Great Maul of Frost.description: A great maul cut from pale frostjade and sleeved through its core with steel. Rime spreads from every impact, but a missed swing pulls the head low and the long haft needs open room to recover.

Warded Stormsteel Siege Hammer of Shock.name: Warded Stormsteel Siege Hammer of Shock
Warded Stormsteel Siege Hammer of Shock.description: A two-handed stormsteel hammer banded with copper runes that hold the force of a thunderhead until impact. It must be carried ready because it cannot be drawn quickly, and its charged head drags the wielder through a long recovery after every committed blow.

Lockpick Set.name: Lockpick Set
Lockpick Set.description: A worn leather roll containing tension wrenches, rake picks, and hook picks.

Leather Cuirass.name: Leather Cuirass
Leather Cuirass.description: A hardened leather chest piece scarred by old blows but still reliable.

Iron Warhammer.name: Iron Warhammer
Iron Warhammer.description: A flanged iron hammer built to crush armor, bone, and brittle bodies.

Short Bow.name: Short Bow
Short Bow.description: A compact bow suited to quick draws and close-range archery.

Trick Blade.name: Trick Blade
Trick Blade.description: A concealed spring blade disguised as an innocuous object.

Loaded Dice.name: Loaded Dice
Loaded Dice.description: A pair of bone dice weighted to favor certain outcomes.

Silver Binding Chain.name: Silver Binding Chain
Silver Binding Chain.description: Enchanted silver links that resist breaking and gleam brighter near supernatural creatures.

Pact Token.name: Pact Token
Pact Token.description: A small charm of dark, unfamiliar metal, given or altered by the warlock's patron when the bargain was struck. Its uneven surface carries the patron's sign without resembling mortal script. It serves as a focus for summonings, hexes, and other workings of the pact.

Linen Tunic.name: Linen Tunic
Linen Tunic.description: A plain tunic of undyed linen, comfortable but not protective.

Cloth Trousers.name: Cloth Trousers
Cloth Trousers.description: Rough-spun wool breeches patched at the knees from long wear.

Worn Breeches.name: Worn Breeches
Worn Breeches.description: Once-luxurious velvet breeches, aged but still elegantly cut.

Faded Doublet.name: Faded Doublet
Faded Doublet.description: A well-tailored but aging silk doublet whose rich colors have softened with time.

Woven Robe.name: Woven Robe
Woven Robe.description: A robe of overlapping leaves and bark that shifts color to match nearby foliage.

War Bow.name: War Bow
War Bow.description: A tall laminated bow that requires strength to draw and drives arrows with force.

Long Bow.name: Long Bow
Long Bow.description: A tall laminated bow with superior range and penetrating power.

Mongo's Medium Health Potion.name: Mongo's Medium Health Potion
Mongo's Medium Health Potion.description: A vial of crimson liquid that restores vitality when consumed.

Stamina Draught.name: Stamina Draught
Stamina Draught.description: A brisk, salt-bitter tonic that pushes breath and strength back into tired limbs. Restores 15 stamina.

Greater Stamina Draught.name: Greater Stamina Draught
Greater Stamina Draught.description: A concentrated draught of the same brew, thick and sharply mineral. Restores 30 stamina.

Mana Philter.name: Mana Philter
Mana Philter.description: A cool, faintly luminous philter that reopens the channel between caster and current. Restores 15 mana.

Greater Mana Philter.name: Greater Mana Philter
Greater Mana Philter.description: A double-distilled philter that runs cold all the way down. Restores 30 mana.

Maple Lute.name: Maple Lute
Maple Lute.description: A well-used pear-shaped lute with delicate fretwork and the marks of countless performances.

Smith's Hammer.name: Smith's Hammer
Smith's Hammer.description: A well-balanced steel hammer used for shaping hot metal on an anvil.

Woodworking Tools.name: Woodworking Tools
Woodworking Tools.description: A collection of saws, chisels, planes, and measuring tools for working wood.

Leatherworking Tools.name: Leatherworking Tools
Leatherworking Tools.description: A set of knives, awls, needles, and edge tools for cutting and stitching leather.

Sewing Kit.name: Sewing Kit
Sewing Kit.description: A compact pouch containing needles, thread, scissors, and pins for textile work.

Battle Mace.name: Battle Mace
Battle Mace.description: A heavy flanged mace with a reinforced steel head for crushing armor and bone.

Artificer's Toolkit.name: Artificer's Toolkit
Artificer's Toolkit.description: A leather satchel of fine screwdrivers, jeweler's loupes, wire, calipers, hammers, and arcane scribing tools.

Leather Jerkin.name: Leather Jerkin
Leather Jerkin.description: A vest of hardened leather that protects the torso without restricting the arms.

Linen Robe.name: Linen Robe
Linen Robe.description: A simple ankle-length robe suitable for scholars, clergy, or common folk.

Iron Breastplate.name: Iron Breastplate
Iron Breastplate.description: Hammered iron plates riveted over leather backing, heavy enough to turn serious blows.

Leather Leggings.name: Leather Leggings
Leather Leggings.description: Treated leather leggings that resist tearing on thorns and rough ground.

Wooden Round Shield.name: Wooden Round Shield
Wooden Round Shield.description: A round shield of layered wood bound with iron at the rim, offering reliable coverage without excessive weight.

Iron Buckler.name: Iron Buckler
Iron Buckler.description: A compact iron buckler strapped close to the forearm, quick to turn and small enough not to foul spellwork.

Kite Shield.name: Kite Shield
Kite Shield.description: A tall kite shield covering the body from shoulder to knee, built to catch blows while its bearer advances.

Tower Shield.name: Tower Shield
Tower Shield.description: A broad iron-faced shield built to become a portable wall when planted before an ally or doorway. Its weight makes quick footwork and spellwork difficult.

Leather Boots.name: Leather Boots
Leather Boots.description: Sturdy tanned leather boots for long journeys and rough roads.

Craftsman's Toolkit.name: Craftsman's Toolkit
Craftsman's Toolkit.description: A broad set of hammers, saws, chisels, needles, and punches for everyday craftwork.

Wool Cloak.name: Wool Cloak
Wool Cloak.description: A simple undyed wool cloak whose doubled weave keeps off cold wind and turns glancing cuts.

Oiled Greatcloak.name: Oiled Greatcloak
Oiled Greatcloak.description: A calf-length greatcloak of heavy wool worked with wax and oil. Its doubled shoulders shed weather and blunt glancing cuts without behaving like plate.

Superior Channel-Lined Mantle.name: Superior Channel-Lined Mantle
Superior Channel-Lined Mantle.description: A layered mantle sewn with silver-thread channels that hold a little magical current close to the wearer. It turns glancing blows without enclosing the body in metal.

Steel Sallet.name: Steel Sallet
Steel Sallet.description: An open-faced steel sallet with a flared tail guarding the neck, lighter and easier to see from than a closed helm.

Iron Gauntlets.name: Iron Gauntlets
Iron Gauntlets.description: Articulated iron plates over leather gloves, guarding fingers, knuckles, and wrist while leaving enough movement to grip a weapon.

Iron Sabatons.name: Iron Sabatons
Iron Sabatons.description: Overlapping iron plates buckled over sturdy boots, protecting toe, instep, and ankle without locking the stride.

Masterwork Steel Greathelm.name: Masterwork Steel Greathelm
Masterwork Steel Greathelm.description: A close steel greathelm made to one wearer's measure, with a reinforced brow and articulated bevor. Careful balance keeps its full face and neck protection from dragging at the head.

Masterwork Steel Breastplate.name: Masterwork Steel Breastplate
Masterwork Steel Breastplate.description: A master-fitted harness of overlapping steel plates, shaped and articulated for one wearer. It spreads its weight cleanly but remains full metal armor.

Warded Steel Breastplate.name: Warded Steel Breastplate
Warded Steel Breastplate.description: A master-fitted steel breastplate crossed by silvered channel lines and carried through an enchanter's rite. A narrow ward flashes at each impact before the plate takes the remaining force; it remains full metal armor.

Ember Charm.name: Ember Charm
Ember Charm.description: A thumb-sized clay seal packed with cinder-salt and scored with a fire-turning line. When broken, it raises a personal ward over the bearer that grants resistance to fire until the danger ends, the bearer rests or leaves the scene, or another personal ward replaces it; the charm is spent on use.

Rime Charm.name: Rime Charm
Rime Charm.description: A red cord knotted around a warm iron bead, each knot laid in a cold-breaking pattern. When pulled apart, it raises a personal ward over the bearer that grants resistance to frost until the danger ends, the bearer rests or leaves the scene, or another personal ward replaces it; the charm is spent on use.

Dawn Charm.name: Dawn Charm
Dawn Charm.description: A folded leaf of sun-gold foil stamped with an open eye. When torn, it raises a personal ward over the bearer that grants resistance to shadow until the danger ends, the bearer rests or leaves the scene, or another personal ward replaces it; the charm is spent on use.

Bitterleaf Charm.name: Bitterleaf Charm
Bitterleaf Charm.description: A waxed packet of dried bitterleaf and white salt marked with a green warding line. When crushed, it raises a personal ward over the bearer that grants resistance to poison until the danger ends, the bearer rests or leaves the scene, or another personal ward replaces it; the charm is spent on use.

Sailor's Oilskins.name: Sailor's Oilskins
Sailor's Oilskins.description: A waxed outer coat and hood for deck spray, hard rain, and long watches on open water.

Leather Gloves.name: Leather Gloves
Leather Gloves.description: Supple leather gloves that protect the hands while preserving fine control.

Pit-Fighter's Handwraps.name: Pit-Fighter's Handwraps
Pit-Fighter's Handwraps.description: Long cloth wraps worn tight around the hands and wrists, stained with resin, sweat, and old ring dust.

Iron Knuckle Guards.name: Iron Knuckle Guards
Iron Knuckle Guards.description: Small iron striking plates strapped over padded gloves, made to turn a clean punch into a harder lesson.

Iron Helm.name: Iron Helm
Iron Helm.description: A hammered iron helmet with cheek guards and a nasal bar.

Cloth Hood.name: Cloth Hood
Cloth Hood.description: A rough-spun cloth hood that protects against wind and weather, not weapons.

Iron Greaves.name: Iron Greaves
Iron Greaves.description: Iron plates strapped over leather to guard the shins and knees.

Iron Legharness.name: Iron Legharness
Iron Legharness.description: A full harness of articulated iron covering thigh, knee, and shin over a padded underlayer. It turns blows that greaves alone would let through, at the cost of a heavy, deliberate stride.

Vampire Hunter's Crossbow.name: Vampire Hunter's Crossbow
Vampire Hunter's Crossbow.description: A compact crossbow of dark wood and steel, ward-etched for quiet work against undead prey.

Silver-Tipped Bolts of Radiance.name: Silver-Tipped Bolts of Radiance
Silver-Tipped Bolts of Radiance.description: Blessed crossbow bolts with silver heads that burn undead, fiends, and shadow-bound creatures.

Caustic Bronze Bolts of Acid.name: Caustic Bronze Bolts of Acid
Caustic Bronze Bolts of Acid.description: Crossbow bolts with caustic-bronze heads that smoke green where they strike. Their acid damage eats into stone, plate, shell, and hardened hide.

Venomwood Arrows of Poison.name: Venomwood Arrows of Poison
Venomwood Arrows of Poison.description: Black-green venomwood arrows that sweat toxin along their grain and into the wound. Their poison damage sickens living flesh even after a clean hit.

Emberglass Arrows of Fire.name: Emberglass Arrows of Fire
Emberglass Arrows of Fire.description: Arrows tipped with emberglass that flare the instant they bite, dealing fire damage. They are carried against frost-born creatures, venomous beasts, and things of root and vine.

Frostjade Bolts of Frost.name: Frostjade Bolts of Frost
Frostjade Bolts of Frost.description: Crossbow bolts tipped with frostjade, rimed even in summer. They deal frost damage and are carried against fire-born creatures and oozes.

Stormsteel Bolts of Shock.name: Stormsteel Bolts of Shock
Stormsteel Bolts of Shock.description: Crossbow bolts with stormsteel heads that crackle in flight. Their shock damage is made for constructs and creatures of water.

Voidglass Arrows of Shadow.name: Voidglass Arrows of Shadow
Voidglass Arrows of Shadow.description: Arrows tipped with black voidglass that drink the light around their heads. They deal shadow damage and are carried against celestial and blessed foes.

Moonstone Arrows of Radiance.name: Moonstone Arrows of Radiance
Moonstone Arrows of Radiance.description: White-fletched arrows tipped with moonstone that shine at the instant of release. Their radiant damage burns undead, fiends, cursed flesh, and shadow creatures.

Mechanical Components.name: Mechanical Components
Mechanical Components.description: A sorted bundle of springs, wire, gears, plates, fasteners, and workable scrap. One bundle supplies the ordinary mechanism for a trap or another modest device whose blueprint calls for it, but cannot replace a special payload or rare material.

Blueprint: Needle Trap of Poison.name: Blueprint: Needle Trap of Poison
Blueprint: Needle Trap of Poison.description: An annotated plan for a pressure plate that drives poisoned needles into the first creature to cross it. A bearer with trapcraft 5 can use an Artificer's Toolkit, one bundle of Mechanical Components, and one Venomwood Extract to attempt its construction; success produces one Needle Trap of Poison, and the blueprint is retained.

Blueprint: Stormsteel Burstwheel of Shoc.name: Blueprint: Stormsteel Burstwheel of Shock
Blueprint: Stormsteel Burstwheel of Shoc.description: An exact pattern for winding an expendable stormsteel wheel that throws its stored charge outward when released. A bearer with enchanting 5 can use an Artificer's Toolkit, one bundle of Mechanical Components, and a usable piece of stormsteel to attempt its construction; success produces one Stormsteel Burstwheel of Shock, and the blueprint is retained.

Snapjaw Trap of Acid.name: Snapjaw Trap of Acid
Snapjaw Trap of Acid.description: A sprung jaw trap of caustic bronze with a sealed vitriol reservoir behind the trigger plate. Rigging it is trapcraft's work. Once set, it waits where placed and bites the first creature to cross it for acid damage; after that one bite, it is spent.

Needle Trap of Poison.name: Needle Trap of Poison
Needle Trap of Poison.description: A palm-sized pressure plate crowned with fine needles fed from a reservoir of venomwood extract. Rigging it is trapcraft's work. Once set, it waits where placed and strikes the first creature to cross it for poison damage; after that one strike, it is spent.

Emberglass Trap of Fire.name: Emberglass Trap of Fire
Emberglass Trap of Fire.description: A cage of emberglass shards wired to a friction striker. Rigging it is trapcraft's work. Once set, it waits where placed and bursts under the first creature to cross it for fire damage; after that one burst, it is spent.

Stormcoil Trap of Shock.name: Stormcoil Trap of Shock
Stormcoil Trap of Shock.description: A tight-wound stormsteel coil charged by its own turning key. Rigging it is trapcraft's work. Once set, it waits where placed and discharges into the first creature to touch it for shock damage; after that one discharge, it is spent.

Stormsteel Burstwheel of Shock.name: Stormsteel Burstwheel of Shock
Stormsteel Burstwheel of Shock.description: A palm-sized stormsteel wheel wound tightly around a brass hub and held shut by an enamelled catch. Thrown and released, it tears itself apart in blue-white arcs; its attack has impact 150, deals shock damage, and consumes the Burstwheel.

Vitriol Flask.name: Vitriol Flask
Vitriol Flask.description: A sealed glass flask holding one application of vicious etchant. Smear it onto a plain weapon as part of an attack and the weapon deals acid damage; the flask is consumed whether the strike lands or misses.

Venomwood Extract.name: Venomwood Extract
Venomwood Extract.description: A stoppered vial of black-green sap pressed from venomwood, enough to coat one weapon or charge one small poison-bearing device. Applied as part of an attack, it makes a plain weapon deal poison damage for that attack; used by a blueprint, it supplies the stated poison payload and is consumed when construction succeeds.

Emberglass Oil.name: Emberglass Oil
