dagger.description: Daggers and knives at a range most people fear. Deals piercing damage. Signature work: fighting inside a foe's guard, the grapple-and-blade, the strike before the draw.

archery.name: archery
archery.description: Bows and crossbows. Deals piercing damage. Signature work: the long shot, the moving target, the arrow through a gap in armor.

throwing.name: throwing
throwing.description: Thrown knives, axes, javelins, stones, and slings. Damage by what's thrown — piercing for points, impact for weight. Signature work: the turning throw, two targets in a breath, pinning a sleeve to a door.

shield.name: shield
shield.description: Bucklers to tower shields: turning blows, covering others, striking with the rim. Bashes deal impact damage. Signature work: holding a doorway, covering an ally under volley, the shield-wall.

unarmed combat.name: unarmed combat
unarmed combat.description: Fists, elbows, knees, headbutts, grapples. Deals impact damage. Signature work: disarming a blade barehanded, the chokehold, ending a fight in one motion.

riding.name: riding
riding.description:
Mounts under saddle: riding hard, fighting mounted, staying on when others come off.
Easy: ride a trained horse at a walk, stay seated at a canter, lead a pack animal.
Medium: gallop rough ground, jump a fence, calm a mount that's caught a bad scent.
Hard: fight from the saddle, ride down a fleeing man, stay on through panic.
Extreme: leap a chasm mounted, ride an unbroken stallion to a standstill, thread a battlefield at full gallop.
Taming and bonding wild beasts is animal handling; exotic mounts ride harder by their nature.

sailing.name: sailing
sailing.description:
Boats and ships: handling, navigation at sea, reading weather and water.
Easy: row a calm harbor, trim a sail in fair wind, tie off properly.
Medium: sail a coastal run, hold course in chop, bring a boat alongside clean.
Hard: ride out a storm, navigate by stars on open water, thread a reef passage.
Extreme: sail through a hurricane's edge, run a blockade at night, bring a crippled ship home.
Navigation on land is survival.

stealth.name: stealth
stealth.description:
Moving unseen and unheard: hiding, sneaking, shadowing, and breaking attention. To become Hidden, describe a plausible means of concealment—cover, darkness, silence, smoke, crowds, confusion, misdirection, or a broken sightline—and make a Stealth check. Failure leaves you exposed; active opposition always makes this a check.
Easy: leave casual notice using good cover, drift out of a crowd, or follow someone down a busy street.
Medium: become Hidden amid a confused fight using real cover, cross a guarded yard in shadow, or hide while searchers are nearby.
Hard: break the attention of enemies actively watching for you, slip past an alert sentry at close range, or vanish from a close pursuit.
Extreme: disappear under concentrated observation, cross open torchlit ground unseen, or shadow a trained spy who expects pursuit.
Hidden is concealment, not invisibility. An attack or another obvious action ends it after that action resolves unless an ability says otherwise. Wearing a false face is performance; locks are lockpicking.

lockpicking.name: lockpicking
lockpicking.description:
Opening locks and sealed mechanisms without the key.
Easy: a crude padlock, a jammed latch, a strongbox with a worn-out lock.
Medium: a house door, a merchant's chest, working by feel in the dark.
Hard: a guildmaster's safe, a prison cell under time pressure, a lock built to break picks.
Extreme: a master locksmith's life's work, a vault door, a lock picked silently an arm's length from its guard.
Traps on the lock are trapcraft; magical seals are warding's to break.

trapcraft.name: trapcraft
trapcraft.description:
Traps and snares: spotting them, disarming them, setting them.
Easy: spot a tripwire in good light, rig a simple snare, disarm a known trap at leisure.
Medium: sweep a corridor for pressure plates, set a trap that takes a wolf, disarm a dart trap cleanly.
Hard: disarm a trap mid-mechanism, find the trap hidden by a professional, rig a trap that takes an armed man.
Extreme: unmake a master trapwright's gauntlet, disarm by touch in pitch dark, trap a corridor so well it ends a pursuit.
Game snares are also tracking's country. Larger contraptions and devices are engineering; magical wards are warding magic.

pickpocketing.name: pickpocketing
pickpocketing.description:
Light hands: lifting, palming, planting, sleight of hand.
Easy: palm a coin, lift an unwatched purse, swap two similar objects on a table.
Medium: cut a purse in a market crowd, slip a ring off a distracted hand, plant a token in a pocket.
Hard: lift a key from a guard's belt, work a wary mark, take something the owner checks often.
Extreme: lift a blade from its sheath, rob a man mid-conversation with you, plant evidence on a spymaster.
Crowds and distraction make it easier; watchful marks and quiet rooms make it harder.

leadership.name: leadership
leadership.description:
Command: rallying, coordinating, being followed.
Easy: organize willing hands, keep a small group on task, settle a minor dispute.
Medium: steady nervous recruits, coordinate a search, be obeyed by people who don't know you.
Hard: rally a breaking line, command veterans older than you, hold a crowd at the edge of panic.
Extreme: turn a rout, lead strangers through fire, take command of those sworn to someone else.
Inspiring through art is performance; the clever plan itself is tactics.

tracking.name: tracking
tracking.description:
Following sign to find and close on a quarry, animal or person: trail, spoor, blood, and the age and direction of passage.
Easy: follow fresh tracks in soft ground, follow a blood trail, tell a horse passed from a cart.
Medium: follow a day-old trail over mixed ground, count a party from its camp, stalk within bowshot of wary game.
Hard: track over rock, through water, or along a crowded street, tell a laid false trail from a real one, track by night.
Extreme: follow a week-old trail after rain, track a creature hiding its trail, name what killed something from the kill alone.
This finds and follows; the shot itself is archery, spear, or throwing. Living off the land, weather, and shelter are survival. Snares are shared country with trapcraft. Reading a person's intent is insight; befriending a beast is animal handling.

animal handling.name: animal handling
animal handling.description:
Winning beasts over: calming, training, bonding.
Easy: calm a nervous dog, approach a skittish horse, quiet hens at night.
Medium: calm a spooked horse mid-panic, teach a dog real commands, handle an animal that's been mistreated.
Hard: approach a wild predator without violence, train a hunting hawk, steady animals as fire spreads.
Extreme: befriend a creature that's killed men, calm a war-maddened beast, earn a wild animal's lasting loyalty.
Riding trained mounts is riding; speaking with beasts in words is nature magic.

farming.name: farming
farming.description:
The homestead: crops, livestock, orchards, fishponds, hives, and the turning of seasons.
Easy: plant a kitchen garden, milk and muck without trouble, judge ripe from not.
Medium: bring in a harvest before the rain, pull a difficult lambing through, read blight early enough to act.
Hard: save a crop the frost should have taken, nurse a prize animal back from the brink, make poor soil yield.
Extreme: bring a harvest out of drought, save a herd from a spreading murrain, turn waste ground into a working farm inside a year.
Includes fishing, beekeeping, and husbandry. Bonding and training beasts is animal handling; quickening growth by magic is nature magic.

lore.name: lore
lore.description:
Knowing things: history, legend, heraldry, custom, and what things are worth.
Easy: name the local lord, recall a famous battle, spot a fake coin.
Medium: read an old map's conventions, place a stranger by dress and speech, appraise a merchant's stock fairly.
Hard: identify an ancient ruin's builders, recall the weakness in a monster's legend, value a relic no market has priced.
Extreme: piece together a forgotten dynasty from fragments, know the true name behind a myth, read the meaning of a dead language's inscription.
Knowing is lore; finding is investigation. Appraisal and street-knowledge live here.

tactics.name: tactics
tactics.description:
Reading and shaping a fight: positioning, plans, the moment to press.
Easy: pick the defensible corner, spot the obvious flank, know when to back off.
Medium: set a simple ambush, read which foe leads, position a small group well.
Hard: turn bad ground to advantage, predict the enemy's plan in motion, coordinate a fight on two fronts.
Extreme: beat numbers with ground and timing, read a master commander's trap before it closes, win the battle in the placement.
The plan is tactics; being followed is leadership.

medicine.name: medicine
medicine.description:
Healing without magic: wounds, bones, sickness, poison.
Easy: clean and bind a cut, splint a finger, dose a fever with the right herb.
Medium: stitch a deep wound, set a broken arm, recognize a poison by its signs.
Hard: stop bleeding that should be fatal, treat a crushed limb so it heals straight, pull someone through a killing fever.
Extreme: surgery by lamplight that saves a life, identify and counter a rare poison in time, keep the dying alive until real help comes.
Slower and humbler than healing magic, and works where magic is spent or absent. Brewing remedies at a bench is alchemy.

alchemy.name: alchemy
alchemy.description:
The bench arts: potions, poisons, reagents, transformations of matter.
Easy: brew a simple remedy, render fat to tallow, identify a common reagent.
Medium: brew a healing draught, distill a clean poison, stabilize a volatile mixture.
Hard: brew from a formula half-lost, counter a poison from its symptoms alone, work with reagents that punish mistakes.
Extreme: create a draught no recipe describes, refine a legendary reagent without ruining it, brew under fire with a field kit.
Easier in a proper laboratory; harder with improvised tools. Binding magic into objects is enchanting.

engineering.name: engineering
engineering.description:
Making things work: contraptions, machines, siegeworks, and clever construction.
Easy: fix a wagon wheel, rig a pulley, judge whether a floor will hold.
Medium: repair a mill mechanism, rig a hoist for a heavy load, brace a failing tunnel.
Hard: build a working siege engine from parts, divert a stream through a camp, understand an ancient mechanism by inspection.
Extreme: crack the workings of old-world magitek, bridge a gorge with what's on hand, build a machine no one's seen before.
Traps and snares as such are trapcraft; lasting magic in the work is enchanting.

smithing.name: smithing
smithing.description:
Metalwork: forging, repairing, and finishing — from horseshoes to blades to jewelry.
Easy: mend a hinge, sharpen a blade true, judge good ore from bad.
Medium: forge a serviceable sword, repair mail, set a stone in a simple ring.
Hard: forge a fine weapon worth a name, work a difficult metal clean, finish jewelry a noble would wear.
Extreme: forge a masterwork blade, rework an ancient piece without ruining it, smith a thing other smiths come to study.
Jewelry and ore-sense live here. Enchanting the work is enchanting. Forging a weapon or a piece of armor away from a proper forge is Impossible.

mining.name: mining
mining.description:
Finding and working ore and stone underground: reading a seam, cutting it cleanly, shoring a working, and knowing bad air and bad rock before they kill you.
Easy: pick surface ore from a spoil heap, tell iron ore from worthless rock, crawl a dry old tunnel safely.
Medium: follow a vein through a working, cut ore without bringing the roof down, judge a seam's worth by eye.
Hard: work a rich seam under pressure, mine silver or cold iron without spoiling it, shore a collapsing drift.
Extreme: cut frostjade from a glacier vein, find a lost seam in dead workings, bring a crew out of a cave-in alive.
Cutting ore worth keeping is never Simple. Smelting and working the metal is smithing. Finding ground worth digging is survival.

carpentry.name: carpentry
carpentry.description:
Building in wood and stone: framing, joinery, masonry.
Easy: mend a fence, hang a true door, lay a straight course of brick.
Medium: frame a shed that stands square, repair a roof properly, build solid furniture.
Hard: raise a house from foundation to ridgepole, repair a bridge that carries carts, vault a stone ceiling.
Extreme: build what masters would sign, restore ancient stonework seamlessly, raise a hall in a season.
Masonry and building live here; machines and mechanisms are engineering. Making a bow, shield, or staff away from a proper workbench is Impossible.

leatherworking.name: leatherworking
leatherworking.description:
Hide and leather: tanning, cutting, stitching, armoring.
Easy: patch a boot, oil and mend tack, cut a clean strap.
Medium: make good boots to measure, craft a sturdy pack, repair leather armor properly.
Hard: craft armor that turns a blade, work an exotic hide without waste, finish goods a guild would stamp.
Extreme: armor from a creature's hide that keeps its virtue, masterwork a guild would display, restore a relic of old leather. Making armor away from a proper workshop is Impossible.

tailoring.name: tailoring
tailoring.description:
Cloth and thread: cutting, sewing, fitting, finery.
Easy: hem and mend, patch invisibly enough, take in a coat.
Medium: sew a garment to measure, copy a fashionable cut, repair fine cloth without a trace.
Hard: dress someone for court, work silk and cloth-of-gold, fit armor's padding so it saves lives.
Extreme: a gown that sets the season's fashion, recreate a lost weave, finery fit for a coronation. Making garments meant as armor away from a proper workshop is Impossible.

cooking.name: cooking
cooking.description:
The kitchen and the kettle: meals, preserving, brewing.
Easy: a solid camp meal, bake honest bread, brew passable ale.
Medium: feed a full table well, preserve a harvest through winter, brew ale people ask for by name.
Hard: a feast that honors a hall, cook a memorable meal from poor stores, brew a batch worth trading.
Extreme: a dish spoken of for years, feed an army from a moving kitchen, brew what connoisseurs travel for.
Brewing and preserving live here. Remedies and poisons are alchemy.

spirit magic.name: spirit magic
spirit magic.description:
Perceiving, addressing, bargaining with, invoking, warding, and driving out spirits connected to ancestors, elements, places, objects, and strong memories.
Easy: sense a nearby spirit, recognize spiritual disturbance, offer a respectful greeting, hear a faint ancestral warning.
Medium: converse with a nearby spirit, learn what holds it to a place, ask a known spirit for direct practical aid, ward a doorway against lesser spirits.
Hard: drive a hostile spirit from a person or place, call an ancestor into visible presence, negotiate meaningful aid from a powerful local spirit, break a spiritual curse.
Extreme: bargain with a great spirit, cross bodily into the spirit world, end possession by an ancient power, establish a lasting covenant between a spirit and a people or place.
Spirits have wills. Success secures attention, communication, a fair bargain, or aid within a spirit's nature; it does not make every spirit obedient. Familiar spirits and fitting offerings make workings easier. Hostility, violated taboos, alien places, and requests against a spirit's nature make them harder. Elemental manifestations use their element's damage type; direct spiritual assaults deal psychic damage; ancestors acting through weapons use the weapon's damage type.
Its Extreme bodily crossing is one crossing through a rite, thin place, gate, or guide. The Graywalk permits an unaided crossing made at will. Being ridden by a spirit is spirit channeling.

Psionicist.name: Psionicist
Psionicist.description:
Main Attributes: Attunement, Wisdom, and Charisma

Psionicists train the mind to act beyond the body. They move objects without touching them, reach into other minds, and perceive things ordinary senses cannot reveal. Some become warriors who wield invisible force; others become investigators, advisers, spies, or masters of mental influence.

Their disciplines often overlap. A psionicist might read an opponent’s intentions before striking, sense the fear beneath a confident answer, or turn a nearby object into a weapon. Their strength lies in knowing what to attempt as much as in the power of the attempt.

Psionicists are often associated with the feared practice of mind-puppeteering. Public practice of psionic magic is not permitted everywhere in Larion.
abilities: Forceful Hand
Touch of Feeling
Second Sight
Second Wind
Draw Power
Psionicist.traitNarrativeEffects: A psionicist can seek teachers and study unfamiliar feats of thought, perception, and mental influence.

Tarnished.name: Tarnished
Tarnished.description: The dead country has left its first mark on them—through a bargain, an unwarded crossing, necromantic overreach, or the power of one of its creatures. The mark is faint but real, and further dealings can deepen it.

Tarnish-Marked.name: Tarnish-Marked
Tarnish-Marked.description: The grey-rot has become visible at the temples, beneath the nails, and around the irises. Priests, animals, and those familiar with the Reaches can recognize it.
Tarnish-Marked.traitNarrativeEffects: Grey shows at the temples and beneath the nails, and a pale ring circles the irises. Surface one of these signs when someone examines the character closely, a priest or consecrated servant meets them, an animal catches their scent, or a veteran of the Reaches, spirit-worker, shade, or desperate petitioner has reason to recognize the mark. Let the reaction follow the observer: suspicion or guarded refusal from the pious; wary respect or opportunity from those accustomed to the dead country. Do not make every stranger react.

Tarnish-Ridden.name: Tarnish-Ridden
Tarnish-Ridden.description: The grey country counts them nearly its own. Their shadow thins in direct daylight, and radiant power burns them more deeply.
Tarnish-Ridden.traitNarrativeEffects: Their shadow is visibly thin in direct daylight, and an active consecration may answer their presence—a shrine flame guttering, blessed water stirring, or a ward-bell sounding without wind. Surface this only when daylight, a rite, a shrine, clergy, spirits, necromancers, or frightened witnesses are directly involved. The pious may refuse ordinary welcome or impose terms; shades and dark practitioners may recognize someone they can approach. Do not make every bystander recoil, and do not grant automatic fame.

Determined.name: Determined
Determined.description:
You don't go down easy.

Constitution makes you harder to kill and keeps you going when others drop. It carries your health and boosts Riding, Sailing, Farming, Mining, and Shield use.

Graceful.name: Graceful
Graceful.description:
You move well and your hands are quick.

Dexterity governs agility and fine control. It carries your stamina and boosts Stealth, Acrobatics, Archery, Throwing, and fast weapons like Daggers, Spears, and Staves. Also helps with Lockpicking, Pickpocketing, and Trapcraft.
Graceful.traitNarrativeEffects: You move well and your hands are quick.

Strong.name: Strong
Strong.description:
You've always had a powerful build.

Strength governs raw physical power. It boosts Athletics and heavy weapons like Swords, Axes, Blunt Weapons, Warhammers, and Unarmed Combat.
Strong.traitNarrativeEffects: You've always had a powerful build.

Charming.name: Charming
Charming.description:
People like to be around you.

Charisma governs social influence and force of personality. It boosts Persuasion, Intimidation, Leadership, and Performance.
Charming.traitNarrativeEffects: People like to be around you.

Intelligent.name: Intelligent
Intelligent.description:
You're a quick study and knowledge comes easily.

Intelligence governs study, design, and making. It boosts Lore, Tactics, Alchemy, Engineering, Enchanting, and every craft — Smithing, Carpentry, Leatherworking, and Tailoring. If you intend to make things, this is the attribute you buy. Casting is still governed by Attunement, so this makes you a scholar of magic and a maker of magic items rather than a stronger caster.
Intelligent.traitNarrativeEffects: You're a quick study and knowledge comes easily.

Wise.name: Wise
Wise.description:
You're wise beyond your years.

Wisdom governs perception and judgment. It boosts Investigation, Insight, Tracking, Medicine, Survival, Animal Handling, Cooking, and Shape Shifting.

Attuned.name: Attuned
Attuned.description:
Magic answers you before you ask.

Attunement is the capacity to channel Larion's magic, and it governs every school: Fire, Storm, Water, Earth, Divine, Dark, Illusion, Necromancy, Conjuration, Divination, Nature, Spirit, Blood, Healing, Warding, and Psionics. It also carries your mana.
Attuned.traitNarrativeEffects: Wards, currents, and worked magic register early and clearly, and channelling costs them less than it costs others.

Friendly Face.name: Friendly Face
Friendly Face.description: People like you. They can't always explain why. You have a way of saying things that makes people want to agree, and a smile that makes them forget they weren't going to.

Peasant.name: Peasant
Peasant.description: You were raised to the work of fields, livestock, and the farmyard. You know crops, animals, weather, and the ordinary jobs that keep a household running.

Tavern Worker.name: Tavern Worker
Tavern Worker.description: You grew up in common rooms and kitchens, carrying trays, pouring drinks, keeping orders straight, and learning when to charm a guest or step around trouble. You know how taverns work and how quickly news travels through one.

Noble Heritage.name: Noble Heritage
Noble Heritage.description: You were born into a family with a name, a crest, and expectations. You learned to lead, to speak to power, and to carry yourself like someone who belongs at the high table. Your family name opens doors in places where it's recognized.
Noble Heritage.traitNarrativeEffects: This character is Noble-born: their family is known to the heralds of every court of the Greater Duchies. Heralds, stewards and hosts of the Greater Duchies receive them with the courtesy owed to gentle birth, admit them to noble company, and seat them below knights and titled nobles. A court of the Greater Duchies may knight them or raise them to a title for their service.

Craftsman.name: Craftsman
Craftsman.description: You apprenticed with tools in your hands — forge, workbench, needle, awl. You know how things are made, how they break, and how to put them back together. Give you the right materials and you can make almost anything.

Trade Contacts.name: Trade Contacts
Trade Contacts.description: You've worked the trade roads long enough to know people in most towns — merchants, innkeepers, caravan masters, the sort of folk who can find you a bed, a ride, or a deal. You know how to haggle and how to lean on someone when haggling doesn't work.

Athlete.name: Athlete
Athlete.description: You've always been fast, strong, and hard to keep up with. Running, climbing, jumping, swimming — whatever the obstacle, you go over it, under it, or through it.

Sword.name: Sword
Sword.description: You've put in the hours with a blade. Drawing, cutting, parrying — the fundamentals that keep you alive when someone else has a weapon too.

Fencing.name: Fencing
Fencing.description: You learned the light blade: footwork, feints, and a point that arrives before the other fighter has finished deciding.

Gadgetry.name: Gadgetry
Gadgetry.description: Trained to fight with made weapons: spring-arms, wound wheels, sparkers, and the bench's newest idea.

Shield.name: Shield
Shield.description: A shield is more than something to hide behind. You know how to turn blows, cover the person next to you, and slam the rim into someone's face when they get too close.

Staff.name: Staff
Staff.description: A length of hardwood and two ends to hit with. Simple, versatile, and brutal when you know the angles.

Archery.name: Archery
Archery.description: You can put an arrow where you want it at distance. Draw, aim, loose — the rhythm is second nature.

Throwing.name: Throwing
Throwing.description: You know how to put a weapon into motion and have it arrive before the target expects it. Knives, axes, javelins, stones, and slings all become dangerous in a practiced hand.

Axe.name: Axe
Axe.description: You know how to put an axe where it hurts. Heavy, committed swings that split shields and don't stop at leather.

Spear.name: Spear
Spear.description: Reach wins fights. You know how to keep enemies at the pointy end and control the space between you and them.

Blunt Weapons.name: Blunt Weapons
Blunt Weapons.description: A mace is a soldier's best friend — simple, cheap, and it doesn't care what the other person is wearing. You know how to swing one fast and put it where it counts.

Dagger.name: Dagger
Dagger.description: Close, fast, and ugly. You fight at a range most people aren't comfortable with and you're very comfortable there.

Unarmed Combat.name: Unarmed Combat
Unarmed Combat.description: Fists, elbows, knees, headbutts — you fight with what you were born with and you've learned to make it count.

Called to the Divine.name: Called to the Divine
Called to the Divine.description: You have a connection to a benevolent divine power.
abilities: Sacred Word
Called to the Divine.traitNarrativeEffects: You have a connection to a benevolent divine power.

Human.name: Human
Human.description:
Humans live fast and refuse to accept it. Where longer-lived races measure ambition in centuries, humans measure it in decades — and somehow get more done. They fill every role, chase every calling, and build kingdoms in a single generation through sheer restless drive. What they lack in raw power or ancient wisdom, they make up for with stamina, charm, and a refusal to stay down. No race in Larion is more varied in temperament or talent, and none spreads faster.

The most physically diverse people in Larion. Skin from pale to deep brown, hair from flaxen to black, builds from slight to broad. Heights range from just over five feet to well past six. No single look defines them — a human from the Bright Kingdoms and a human from Aurora might not recognize each other as kin.

Common enough in every corner of Larion that a human face rarely draws a second glance. They walk into taverns, trading posts, and throne rooms without raising eyebrows — a convenience that rarer folk don't enjoy. Other races find them ambitious to a fault, always building something new before the last thing is finished. Respected for their energy. Exhausting to keep up with.
Human.traitNarrativeEffects: Human race draws no special attention in most settlements across Larion.

Dwarf.name: Dwarf
Dwarf.description:
Built for stone and deep places. Dwarves live in clan-holds carved into mountain roots, bound by ties of kinship, craft, and duty that outlast human kingdoms. They measure worth by what you make and whether you keep your word. A dwarf who breaks an oath is already dead to their clan — and most would rather die than prove it true. They live two centuries or more, and every year makes them more stubborn.

Broad and dense-boned, rarely more than five feet tall but often nearly as wide at the shoulder. Thick-fingered hands built for hammer and chisel. Skin tones from ruddy bronze to deep granite-grey. Hair worn long and often braided — copper, black, iron-grey, or stark white regardless of age. Heavy brows, deep-set eyes, and defined jawlines.

A dwarf's word is taken seriously everywhere in Larion, and so is their coin. Merchants offer fair prices, smiths acknowledge a peer, and strangers assume competence. But no one expects a dwarf to be flexible, funny, or fast. Seen as reliable, immovable, and predictable — which suits most dwarves just fine.
Dwarf.traitNarrativeEffects: A dwarf can usually identify the maker, age, alteration, and likely failure of worked stone or metal.

Halfling.name: Halfling
Halfling.description:
Small, quick, and easy to underestimate: just how most halflings like it. They stand about three feet tall and make up for it with fast hands, sharp instincts, and more charm than anyone expects. Halflings turn up everywhere: running market stalls, cooking for mercenary companies, scouting for armies, or quietly running the best tavern in town. They prize comfort, good food, and good company, but don't mistake that for softness. A halfling who's survived the road has done it by being quicker, cleverer, and more likeable than whatever was trying to kill them.

Small and slight with nimble builds. Round faces, bright eyes, and curly hair in shades of brown, auburn, copper, or straw-blond. Bare feet by preference — the soles toughen like leather — though boots are worn when the terrain demands it. Halfling hands are deft and nimble, a boon for locksmiths, tailors, and thieves alike. 

People like halflings. They can't help it. A halfling in the room lowers the tension, and most folk are disarmed before they realize they've let their guard down. The flip side: nobody takes them seriously at first. Guards look past them, warlords dismiss them, and shopkeepers assume they can't afford the good stock. Halflings who've learned to use that blind spot tend to do very well for themselves.
abilities: A Fortunate Disaster
Halfling.traitNarrativeEffects: A halfling's size and balance make low cover, crowded rooms, narrow gaps, and overlooked routes naturally usable.

Orc.name: Orc
Orc.description:
Orcs are a people of witnessed oaths, clan memory, fierce competition, and blunt affection. Their homeland is the Orc Wolds, where Clan Drokash rides the open steppe and Clan Vorren builds in the iron hills, but generations of war scattered orc communities across Larion. Strength earns respect; keeping your word earns trust. An oath spoken before an elder is sacred, and an orc who breaks one loses more than reputation. Orcs mock the people they love, eat from shared platters, argue loudly, and find polite evasions far more insulting than an honest challenge.

Tall, broad, and heavy with muscle. Green or brown skin, prominent lower tusks, and deep-set eyes in shades of amber, black, or copper. Thick jaws, heavy brows, and builds that run to powerful rather than lean. Most stand over six feet. Hair is worn in braids, topknots, or shaved close, often decorated with clan tokens or bone rings.

Within the Orc Wolds, tusks, clan tokens, contests, and hard truths are ordinary. Elsewhere, strangers often see a fighter first and ask questions second. Guards watch orcs a little longer and merchants speak a little more carefully, but those who have lived or worked beside them know the other reputation: fierce loyalty, communal generosity, cheerful insult, and a promise that means exactly what it says.
abilities: Old Blood Rises
Orc.traitNarrativeEffects: Those familiar with orc tradition treat a witnessed oath seriously; orcs can call on a named ancestral memory through Old Blood Rises.

Dragonkin.name: Dragonkin
Dragonkin.description:
Descended from true dragons through bloodlines no one fully understands. Dragonkin carry that heritage in their bones — the scales, the horns, the elemental fire in their veins, and the instinct to dominate any room they enter. They're drawn to power the way their ancestors were drawn to hoards, though what a dragonkin hoards varies: gold, followers, knowledge, territory. Most feel the pull of elemental magic whether they train in it or not. A dragonkin who ignores their draconic nature entirely is rare and usually unhappy.

Large and powerfully built, standing six to seven feet tall with dense, scaled skin in shades of bronze, crimson, obsidian, emerald, or pale silver. Pronounced horns curve back from the skull — shape and size vary by lineage. Vertical-slit pupils, heavy clawed hands, and a broad chest built for the deep breath that precedes something terrible. Tails are common but not universal. Some lineages show more human features, others look barely humanoid at all.

Dragonkin don't walk into a room unnoticed. This isn't fear exactly — it's the recognition that something powerful just arrived. In the Bright Kingdoms and Westmarch, dragonkin often find doors opened for them simply because no one wants to be the one who said no. The assumption is always strength first, subtlety never. Dragonkin who prefer books to battlefields spend a lot of time correcting first impressions.
abilities: Dragon Breath
Dragonkin.traitNarrativeEffects: Dragonkin scales provide natural physical protection, and each dragonkin has one established breath lineage: fire, acid, frost, or shock.

Moon elf.name: Moon elf
Moon elf.description:
Moon elves withdrew from the world after the Kindred War split elvenkind, and they've spent the centuries since accumulating knowledge the way other races accumulate coin. They live five hundred years or more, and it shows in everything they do. They take the long view on matters other races consider urgent, and the very long view on everything else. Magic comes to them as naturally as breathing, and most moon elf children can read a ward before they can read a book.

Tall and slender with silver-pale skin. Hair ranges from white-platinum to deep blue-black, worn long. Eyes are large and luminous — silver, violet, pale gold, or solid black — adapted for perfect vision in darkness. Their features are angular and fine-boned, with a stillness to their expressions that other races often misread as coldness.

Moon elves are treated as authorities on magic and history whether they've earned it or not. A moon elf who walks into a library or academy is assumed to belong there. A moon elf who walks into a tavern gets watched — not because anyone necessarily minds, but because everyone assumes the moon elf is sizing them up. The reputation for arrogance isn't entirely unfair. Some moon elves may be patient with ignorance, but they rarely bother to hide that they consider it ignorance.
abilities: Yearfold
Moon elf.traitNarrativeEffects: Moon elves read comfortably by moonlight and starlight and may call on the accumulated precision of a long life through Yearfold.

High elf.name: High elf
High elf.description:
High elves are the surface kindred of the Everwood and the people of Canopy, heirs to the silverleaf cities and the long peace called the Sundering. They build in living wood, preserve the old arts of greenshaping and wardcraft, and believe a good life should show discipline, beauty, and care for what must last. They are not all nobles or Wardens: high elves include scholars, artisans, rangers, soldiers, traders, and exiles from the Council's slow politics.

Tall and slender, with fine-boned faces and long pointed ears. Skin ranges from ivory and rose-gold through olive and warm brown; hair from silver, pale gold, copper, chestnut, or black; eyes are often green, gold, grey, or clear blue. Their clothing favors layered cloth, worked wood, leaf-metal, house colors, and practical gear suited to the heights of Canopy.

A high elf is recognized as one of the forest's people even far from Elfwood. In Canopy, lineage and bearing carry weight; elsewhere, strangers may read their poise as refinement or condescension. They are expected to understand old obligations and the Sundering, but an adventuring high elf may uphold that inheritance, question it, or simply want to see the world below the branches.
abilities: The Ward Advances
High elf.traitNarrativeEffects: High elves treat branches, railings, ropes, and narrow elevated footing as familiar roads and know the old laws of Elfwood and Canopy.

Wood elf.name: Wood elf
Wood elf.description:
Wood elves never left the forests. When the Kindred War tore elvenkind apart, they chose neither side — they chose the trees. They live in scattered communities through the deep woodlands of Larion, particularly the Everwood, building with living wood and answering to councils of elders rather than kings. Where moon elves hoard knowledge and dark elves prize cleverness, wood elves value connection — to the land, the seasons, the signs that something is wrong before anyone else notices. They live as long as their moon elf cousins, but count their years in seasons and harvests rather than books read.

Lean and long-limbed with sun-darkened skin in shades of brown, olive, and weathered bronze. Hair tends toward earth tones — chestnut, deep red, black, mossy green — often worn loose or tied back for practicality. Their eyes are bright and watchful: green, amber, hazel, or deep brown. They move quietly by habit, and most have the kind of stillness that lets them disappear into a treeline without trying.

Wood elves are trusted in wild places and treated as outsiders in cities. Farmers and villagers on the forest edge welcome them as trading partners and wardens. In larger towns, they're regarded as capable but odd — people who could live comfortably but choose bark and rain instead. Most folk assume a wood elf knows the answer to any question about weather, beasts, or which mushrooms will kill you.
Wood elf.traitNarrativeEffects: Wood elves read woodland routes, animal warning, wind, and broken growth as naturally as city folk read streets and signs.

Catkin.name: Catkin
Catkin.description:
Feline folk with the reflexes and restlessness to match. Catkin are found across Larion but never in large numbers — they don't build cities or hold territory the way other races do. They drift, settle for a while, drift again. Most are drawn to work that rewards quick reflexes and independent judgment: scouting, hunting, rooftop courier work, the kind of job where being able to land on your feet matters literally. They're social on their own terms, affectionate when they choose to be, and gone without warning when they don't.

Lithe builds covered in short fur ranging from tawny gold to charcoal, tabby-striped, calico, or solid black. Cat-shaped ears sit high on the head and move independently, tracking sound before the catkin consciously reacts. Eyes are large with vertical pupils — green, gold, copper, or pale blue — and see well in near-darkness. Retractable claws on both hands and feet. Tails are expressive and hard to control, giving away mood even when the face stays composed.

People find catkin charming in small doses and unsettling in large ones. The way they watch, the way they go still before they move, the fact that they're always closer than you thought — it reads as predatory even when it isn't. Most folk enjoy a catkin's company but wouldn't trust one with a key to the shop. Whether that caution is earned depends entirely on the catkin.
Catkin.traitNarrativeEffects: Catkin have functional claws, feline balance, and a strong instinct for turning falls and narrow footing into controlled landings.

Demonborn.name: Demonborn
Demonborn.description:
Demonborn descend from the people who escaped Ur during the Excession and made a new life in Larion. Their greatest communities stand in Ntar Vanna, especially New Anthara, with others across the southern isles, eastern deserts, and every port where trade carries them. Otherworldly power still answers readily through their blood, but demonborn culture is built around freedom from Ur: passionate, direct, fiercely hospitable, and committed to the deliberate self-mastery that keeps power from becoming another master. The Children of Ur reject that freedom; they are a proscribed cult, not the measure of the people they betray.

Demonborn vary dramatically in appearance. Horns range from small nubs to sweeping curves. Skin may be deep crimson, ashen grey, bruise-purple, or other unnatural colors, sometimes patterned or faintly luminous. Clawed fingers, pointed teeth, tails, and eyes of solid gold, red, black, or silver are common, while builds vary as widely as those of other peoples. No demonborn passes wholly for human — something about them is always visibly, unmistakably other.

In Ntar Vanna and many southern ports, demonborn features are ordinary and their traditions are understood. Elsewhere, horns and glowing eyes still draw stares, superstition, fascination, or suspicion. Demonborn learn to read that first look quickly, but they do not define themselves by it: they are the descendants of people who escaped the demon princes and chose their own future.
abilities: Black Edict
Demonborn.traitNarrativeEffects: A demonborn can deliberately color their presence with infernal beauty, menace, or temptation and may release precisely bounded infernal shadow through Black Edict.

Giantborn.name: Giantborn
Giantborn.description:
Giantborn trace their ancestry to the ur-giants said to have shaped Larion's northern mountains. They stand head and shoulders above most other peoples, with the size, strength, and valley-carrying voices of that old blood. Their strongest communities live in Highheath's cattle-vales, where families such as Tuskhollow raise enormous herds, settle pride through feats of strength, and remember favors and insults for generations. Giantborn are not all warriors: their size also makes them prized as herders, porters, smiths, builders, and anyone who can turn a two-person task into a one-person job. Their joy tends to be loud, their hospitality generous, and their anger hard to miss.

Massive. Seven feet is average, eight not unusual. Thick-limbed and heavy-boned with broad hands that make human weapons look undersized. Skin tones mirror human ranges but often carry a stony undertone — slate-grey, ruddy granite, pale quartz. Hair is coarse and heavy, ranging from black and brown to stone-white. Their features are blunt and strong, with heavy brows and deep-set eyes.

Giantborn are impossible to miss. People step aside, perhaps less from fear than from simple necessity — a giantborn in a crowded space parts the crowd without trying. Stools buckle, market awnings catch on shoulders, and every doorway is a reminder to duck. People remember a giantborn: they are the easiest witness to recall, the hardest person to lose in a crowd, and often the first person asked to lift, carry, fight, or take the blame.
abilities: Weightfall
Giantborn.traitNarrativeEffects: Giantborn size and mountain-blooded mass make heavy lifting, high reach, and taking up physical space natural facts of the scene.

Dark Elf.name: Dark Elf
Dark Elf.description:
Driven into the Rootdark after the Kindred War, dark elves built Maanvalta into a wealthy realm beneath the Elfwood and made exile look enviable. Within Elfwood, the Sundering confines them to the deep and to Ilunethel on the surface; beyond the high elves' realm, their houses reach the wider world through tunnel-roads, trade, agents, and coin. Dark elves prize velesse — the art of getting exactly what you want while making it look effortless. Wit, craft, style, illusion, and a useful lie all earn respect; being dull is often treated as a worse failure than being wrong.

Silver-white or blue-black hair contrasts with skin ranging from charcoal grey to deep obsidian. Eyes adapted for total darkness may be pale violet, silver, amber, or faintly luminous red. Dark elves tend to be lean and sharp-featured, and they dress with intention even when they own very little. The way they carry themselves often suggests they know something you do not.

Dark elves carry a reputation for beautiful craft, dangerous charm, illusion, theft, and intrigue, and many of them enjoy keeping the stories alive. Cosmopolitan cities hire them as spies, enchanters, entertainers, and negotiators; Ilunethel openly trades in their work; Nocturne's outcasts in the Shadow Summits rarely object to another elegant danger. More conservative communities remain suspicious, and anyone who assumes charm and danger are separate qualities tends to learn otherwise.
abilities: Shadow Wound
Dark Elf.traitNarrativeEffects: Dark elves are practiced with shadow, misdirection, and dramatic movement; they can carry a deliberate attack through a target's shadow with Shadow Wound.

Construct.name: Construct
Construct.description:
Made, not born. Constructs are artificial beings — bodies of stone, metal, wood, or ceramic animated by a soul bound through enchantment. Who made them and why varies: some were forged as laborers, some as guardians, some as experiments. Whatever the original purpose, the art of making them is believed to be lost, and their kind is rarer by the day. Every construct faces the same question sooner or later — what am I for now? The answer is theirs to decide, which may be more freedom than most of their creators intended.

No two constructs look alike. A body of riveted iron plates moves differently from one carved in smooth granite or assembled from lacquered hardwood. Some are roughly humanoid, others only approximate it. Eyes glow or don't. Joints click or hum or grind. Faces range from expressive carved features to featureless masks to bare metal with nothing resembling a face at all. Size varies with construction but most fall within human range. They don't need to breathe, eat or sleep, though some learn to mimic such behaviors for the peace of mind of those around them. But, like the other races, they can be hurt and die when their bodies sustain too much damage.

People don't know what to make of constructs, and it shows. Are you a person or a thing? Most folk land on person eventually, but the hesitation is always there. In big cities, they're rare but common enough to be accepted without open fear. In rural places, where most people have never seen one, reactions may be more varied and extreme: fear, revulsion, or even worship.
abilities: Soul Flare
Construct.traitNarrativeEffects: A construct's built body may be stone, metal, wood, porcelain, or mixed artifice; its joints and shell do not behave like ordinary flesh.

Serpentkin.name: Serpentkin
Serpentkin.description:
Cold-blooded in more senses than one. Serpentkin are reptilian humanoids with snake-like heads, fanged jaws, and a way of thinking that other races find alien and a little frightening. They don't rush. They don't panic. They let a situation play out before they move, and when they move, they don't miss. Serpentkin societies in Ntar Vanna are ancient and layered — built on obligation, hierarchy, and the understanding that venom is only one of several tools available. Outside their homeland, most serpentkin operate alone or in small enclaves, and they prefer it that way.

Scaled skin in patterns of jade, amber, obsidian, sand-brown, or deep emerald, sometimes banded or diamond-patterned. Serpentine heads with lidless eyes — gold, slit-pupiled, unblinking. Forked tongues that read scent the way others read expressions. Lean, flexible builds with deceptive strength in the grip. Fangs carry mild venom in most bloodlines, though potency varies. They move with an unsettling smoothness — no wasted motion, no fidgeting, no tells.

Serpentkin make people nervous. The unblinking stare, the tongue-flick, the absolute stillness before they speak — it all reads as predatory even in friendly conversation. Merchants deal with them fairly because serpentkin have long memories and longer grudges. Alchemists and poisoners seek them out for their expertise. Most folk are polite, careful, and quietly relieved when they leave. Serpentkin are aware of this effect and few go out of their way to soften it.
abilities: The Far Fang
Serpentkin.traitNarrativeEffects: Serpentkin possess functional venom that can be delivered by bite, spit, scratch, or a prepared cut; The Far Fang concentrates it into an exceptional ranged attack.

Wolfpack Trial-Hunter.name: Wolfpack Trial-Hunter
Wolfpack Trial-Hunter.description: An outsider accepted by Wolfpack Lodge to attempt one witnessed proving deed. A Trial-Hunter is not yet a Packmate and does not bear the pack clasp.
Wolfpack Trial-Hunter.traitNarrativeEffects: Wolfpack members recognize this character as a Trial-Hunter permitted to undertake one witnessed proving deed, but not yet as a full Packmate. This standing changes only when the Great Lodge names the next standing; until then, no slip, token, badge, or partial title stands in for it.

Wolfpack Packmate.name: Wolfpack Packmate
Wolfpack Packmate.description: A full member of Wolfpack Lodge who completed a witnessed proving deed and received the pack clasp. Packmates may take ordinary lodge contracts and earn recognized deeds.
Wolfpack Packmate.traitNarrativeEffects: The pack clasp and the lodge's recognition mark this character as a full Packmate trusted with ordinary Wolfpack contracts. This standing changes only when the Great Lodge names the next standing; until then, no slip, token, badge, or partial title stands in for it.

Wolfpack Proven Hunter.name: Wolfpack Proven Hunter
Wolfpack Proven Hunter.description: A Wolfpack hunter recognized after three Packmate deeds and trusted with the lodge's harder independent work. Proven Hunters may voluntarily seek the Beast Bond at the Spirit Hearth.
Wolfpack Proven Hunter.traitNarrativeEffects: Wolfpack members recognize this character as a Proven Hunter trusted with difficult independent work. The Beast Bond is available but remains voluntary. This standing changes only when the Great Lodge names the next standing; until then, no slip, token, badge, or partial title stands in for it.

Wolfpack Pack-Captain.name: Wolfpack Pack-Captain
Wolfpack Pack-Captain.description: A trusted Wolfpack field leader acclaimed after serious Beast-Bonded deeds. Pack-Captains may lead lodge contracts and willing packmates without replacing the singular Pack-Leader.
abilities: Run Them Down
Wolfpack Pack-Captain.traitNarrativeEffects: Wolfpack members recognize this character as a Pack-Captain with authority to lead serious lodge contracts and any packmates who willingly ride under them.

Beast-Bonded.name: Beast-Bonded
Beast-Bonded.description: A beast-spirit freely chose you at the Wolfpack's Spirit Hearth, and you freely chose it. The bond shares instinct, senses, protection, and flashes of physical nature without erasing either mind. Wolf is traditional, not mandatory; the specific spirit and its nature are whatever the rite established in the story.
abilities: Bond Incarnate
Beast-Bonded.traitNarrativeEffects: The specific bonded beast-spirit may lend senses, warning, and limited guidance when deliberately invoked. Bond Incarnate is its exceptional physical manifestation. This standing changes only when the Great Lodge names the next standing; until then, no slip, token, badge, or partial title stands in for it.

Berserker.name: Berserker
Berserker.description:
Main Attributes: Strength and Constitution

Berserkers turn danger into motion. They learn to enter and steer a battle-fury that carries them through pain, fear, and exhaustion without taking away their judgment. In a fight, a berserker is the one who closes the distance, breaks the line, drags an ally clear with one hand, and keeps moving while the body is still deciding whether it is hurt.

Fury is physical discipline and instinct, not spellcraft. Some individual berserkers also practice blood rites, spirit-binding, or other magic, but none of these are required by the class. The good ones know when to let fury loose, where to drive it, and how much the body will owe when it ends.
abilities: Break the Line
Let Fury Loose
Second Wind
Draw Power
Berserker.traitNarrativeEffects: A berserker can deliberately enter and steer a controlled physical battle-fury. Let Fury Loose is the explicit entry technique. Fury sharpens action under pain and fear without taking away judgment or control.

Hidden.name: Hidden
Hidden.description: This character is concealed from anyone who has not specifically found or sensed them. Attacks made by this character while Hidden deal twice the damage. After an attack or another obvious action resolves, the character loses Hidden unless an ability explicitly says otherwise.
Hidden.traitNarrativeEffects: This character is concealed from anyone who has not found or sensed them. Their attacks have impact 200.

Warded Against Fire.name: Warded Against Fire
Warded Against Fire.description: A personal ward bends flame and heat away from you. You have resistance to fire damage while the ward stands. It ends when broken or dispelled, when the danger passes, when the company completes a rest or leaves the scene, or when another personal ward replaces it.
Warded Against Fire.traitNarrativeEffects: When fire reaches them, a thin ward-circle flashes over skin or gear and shears part of the flame aside. The sign remains visible only at contact and lapses with the ward.

Warded Against Frost.name: Warded Against Frost
Warded Against Frost.description: A personal ward breaks supernatural cold against an unseen shell around you. You have resistance to frost damage while the ward stands. It ends when broken or dispelled, when the danger passes, when the company completes a rest or leaves the scene, or when another personal ward replaces it.
Warded Against Frost.traitNarrativeEffects: When frost reaches them, rime webs across an unseen ward-circle and cracks before the worst cold crosses it. The sign lapses with the ward.

Warded Against Shadow.name: Warded Against Shadow
Warded Against Shadow.description: A personal ward blunts shadow-force before it reaches you. You have resistance to shadow damage while the ward stands. It ends when broken or dispelled, when the danger passes, when the company completes a rest or leaves the scene, or when another personal ward replaces it.
Warded Against Shadow.traitNarrativeEffects: When shadow-force reaches them, it pales and recoils where it meets a narrow line of ward-light. The sign lapses with the ward.

Warded Against Poison.name: Warded Against Poison
Warded Against Poison.description: A personal ward takes the edge from venom and poisonous vapors before they reach you. You have resistance to poison damage while the ward stands. It ends when broken or dispelled, when the danger passes, when the company completes a rest or leaves the scene, or when another personal ward replaces it.
Warded Against Poison.traitNarrativeEffects: Venom, tainted vapor, and sickly droplets bead against a ward-sign and lose part of their force before crossing it. The sign lapses with the ward.

Fury.name: Fury
Fury.description: A controlled physical battle-fury that increases strength for a short, exhausting burst.
Fury.traitNarrativeEffects: ACTIVE BATTLE-FURY. Narrate the berserker's chosen physical combat actions at an exaggerated, full-body scale: violent charges, hard stops, collisions, wrestling, shield-breaking blows, and committed weapon swings. These actions are exceptionally demanding and should incur substantial stamina costs under the normal stamina rules. Fury is physical discipline, not magic, and does not compel behavior the player did not choose.

Deep Fury.name: Deep Fury
Deep Fury.description: A practiced battle-fury that drives greater strength and endurance for a short, exhausting burst.
Deep Fury.traitNarrativeEffects: ACTIVE DEEP BATTLE-FURY. Narrate the berserker's chosen physical combat actions at an exaggerated, full-body scale: violent charges, hard stops, collisions, wrestling, shield-breaking blows, and committed weapon swings. These actions are exceptionally demanding and should incur substantial stamina costs under the normal stamina rules. Fury is physical discipline, not magic, and does not compel behavior the player did not choose.

Unbroken Fury.name: Unbroken Fury
Unbroken Fury.description: A mastered battle-fury that drives extraordinary strength and endurance for a short, exhausting burst.
Unbroken Fury.traitNarrativeEffects: ACTIVE MASTERED BATTLE-FURY. Narrate the berserker's chosen physical combat actions at an exaggerated, full-body scale: violent charges, hard stops, collisions, wrestling, shield-breaking blows, and committed weapon swings. These actions are exceptionally demanding and should incur substantial stamina costs under the normal stamina rules. Fury is physical discipline, not magic, and does not compel behavior the player did not choose.

Fury Crash.name: Fury Crash
Fury Crash.description: The crash after battle-fury leaves strength and endurance temporarily depleted.
Fury Crash.traitNarrativeEffects: POST-FURY CRASH. The berserker is breathless, shaking, and physically spent as deferred strain catches up. They cannot enter Fury during the Fury Crash. Do not prescribe their mood or decisions; show the temporary physical cost.

Fury Active.name: Fury Active
Fury Active.description: Internal marker for an active Berserker Fury state.

Cleric.name: Cleric
Cleric.description:
Main Attributes: Attunement and Wisdom

Clerics are people who answer a call and learn the rites that let that call act through them. Their power lives in prayers, hands, vows, symbols, water, oil, bells, salt, fire, scripture, and the stubborn work of care. A cleric can close a wound, steady the dying, bless a road, name a curse, turn the profane, or make a frightened room remember what it believes.

Clerics serve temples, shrines, orders, battlefields, villages, roads, or a faith they carry without walls. Some are gentle healers, some hard-eyed exorcists, some battlefield priests, some keepers of burial rites. What they share is presence under pressure: they bring mercy where bodies break, judgment where corruption festers, and ritual where chaos wants to make people forget themselves.

Special Starting Gear: Holy Symbol
abilities: The Sign Descends
Second Wind
Draw Power
Ask in Need
Cleric.traitNarrativeEffects: A cleric is a keeper of a faith's rites and responsibilities. They know the ordinary forms of its prayers, blessings, funerary rites, and consecrations; recognize its sacred signs and profanations; and may speak for its temple or tradition where that standing is acknowledged. Meaningful service may earn access to a guarded rite, a sacred place, or an object entrusted by the faith.

Half-elf.name: Half-elf
Half-elf.description:
Caught between two worlds and at home in both — or neither, depending on who you ask. Half-elves carry enough of each parent's blood to belong everywhere and nowhere. Among humans they're exotic, graceful, touched by something older. Among elves they're blunt, hasty, burning through a life that's long by human measure and embarrassingly short by elven. Most half-elves stop trying to pick a side early and learn to be whatever the room needs instead. It makes them very good with people.

Elven heritage softens human features without replacing them. Pointed ears, slightly angular bone structure, and eyes a shade too bright to be fully human. They age slowly — a half-elf at sixty might pass for a human at thirty — but they do age, visibly, which sets them apart from their elven parent's people. Builds vary widely depending on the human side. Hair and coloring tend toward the elven parent but nothing is guaranteed.

Half-elves fit in. That's the short version. They pick up local customs fast, adjust their manner to match their company, and rarely give offense without meaning to. People find them easy to talk to and hard to pin down — friendly without being fully knowable. Elves consider them charming but shallow. Humans consider them elegant but distant. Half-elves have heard both opinions enough times to stop caring, or at least to fake it convincingly.
Half-elf.traitNarrativeEffects: Half-elves move easily between human and elven communities and can usually recognize and adopt the local manners of either.

Ratkin.name: Ratkin
Ratkin.description:
Survivors first, everything else second. Ratkin are small, quick, and very hard to get rid of — a description they'd take as a compliment. They live in the spaces other races overlook: crawlways, storm drains, wall cavities, the gaps between buildings where the light doesn't reach. Most cities have a ratkin population whether they know it or not. They're scavengers, informants, couriers, fixers — people who make a living in the margins and know more about how a city actually works than anyone sitting in a guildhall. Ratkin don't build empires. They outlast them.

Small and lean, standing three and a half to four feet tall. Coarse fur in shades of brown, grey, black, or dull tawny. Pointed faces with bright dark eyes, prominent front teeth, and round ears that swivel toward sound. Hairless tails as long as their bodies, used for balance in tight spaces. Narrow builds that can squeeze through gaps that look impossible. Their hands are small but extraordinarily quick — a ratkin can strip a lock, re-stitch a seam, or empty a pocket faster than most people can follow.

Nobody trusts a ratkin on sight. That's the reality, and most ratkin stopped being hurt by it a long time ago. Merchants watch them, guards move them along, and polite company pretends they aren't there. In the underworld they're valued — good ratkin informants and couriers are worth their weight in coin. Above ground, earning trust takes time and proof. Ratkin who've done it tend to inspire fierce loyalty precisely because everyone knows what it cost them to be taken seriously.
Ratkin.traitNarrativeEffects: In any city or large town, a ratkin can usually find the local ratkin community, its hidden routes, or someone who knows the roads beneath the roads. Ratkin bodies tolerate spoiled food and urban foulness unusually well.

Lizardfolk.name: Lizardfolk
Lizardfolk.description:
Older than the elves and unimpressed by the fact. Lizardfolk have lived in the marshes, rivers, and coastal shallows of Larion since before anyone started writing things down, and they regard the rise and fall of kingdoms with the polite disinterest of someone watching weather pass. They're not primitive — they build, trade, worship, and wage war — they just don't see the point of doing any of it faster than necessary. A lizardfolk hunts when hungry, fights when threatened, and rests without guilt. Other races call this lazy. Lizardfolk call it sane.

Broad and solid, standing five and a half to six and a half feet tall with dense, scaled hide in shades of green, brown, slate-grey, or muddy gold. Blunt snouts, heavy jaws, and eyes set wide on the skull — amber, yellow, or dark brown with horizontal pupils. Thick tails used for balance and swimming. Clawed hands and feet. Their faces are largely unreadable to mammalian eyes — the muscles aren't built for the same expressions, and most lizardfolk don't bother learning to fake them.

Lizardfolk confuse people. They're not hostile, not friendly, not rude, not polite — they're just there, watching with those flat unblinking eyes, saying exactly what they mean in as few words as possible. Most folk find the honesty refreshing for about ten minutes and then deeply unsettling. Lizardfolk don't do small talk, don't feign interest, and won't laugh at a joke they don't find funny. In the Great Lagoon and Ntar Vanna this is understood. Elsewhere, people assume they're either stupid or angry. They're usually neither.
Lizardfolk.traitNarrativeEffects: Lizardfolk scales take ordinary scrapes well, and their stillness and flat affect make them difficult to read under pressure.

Goblin.name: Goblin
Goblin.description:
Goblins are small, wiry people of volcanic forge-towns, independent caravans, border camps, and raiding bands. The Black Fells hold their largest settlements, where goblin makers work obsite, metal, dragonfire, and whatever a clever hand can keep alive. Some serve the Greater Goblinate; many do not. Goblin life prizes quick judgment, useful craft, and knowing when a fair fight is a stupid one.

Most goblins stand well below human height, with wiry builds, pointed ears, sharp features, and skin ranging from sallow green to grey-brown. Their hands are quick, their eyes watchful, and their tools are often repaired more times than anyone can count. A goblin's best possession is usually the thing they can make work when it should have failed.

In most settled communities, people do not welcome a goblin by default. Guards may assume raider or Goblinate agent, innkeepers may ask who vouches for you, and strangers may watch your hands. This is not universal hostility: Black Fells communities, independent caravans, craft circles, people who need a fixer, and people who know your deeds may offer conditional respect.
Goblin.traitNarrativeEffects: A goblin can turn scrap, wire, cloth, clutter, and broken parts into temporary tools, routes, braces, and practical distractions.

Vanarin.name: Vanarin
Vanarin.description:
The Vanarin—High Vanarin to themselves—hold Citadel Uchaghar in the southern jungles of Ntar Vanna. They are quick, agile, canopy-dwelling people who fight in three dimensions, launch from ropes and branches, and treat boldness as a form of good manners. Their pride is enormous, their generosity is real, and their loyalty is fierce once earned.

Vanarin have expressive monkeylike faces, short fur in dark, copper, russet, or gold-brown shades, long arms, nimble hands, rounded ears, and powerful prehensile tails. They move as comfortably above a river or street as most people move across level ground. A Vanarin warrior is expected to see the route nobody else can reach.

Outside Ntar Vanna, Vanarin are rare and conspicuous. Strangers may stare, misunderstand Vanarin customs around generosity and possession, or distrust quick hands near valuables. In Uchaghar and other southern communities, boldness, generosity, and courage can earn recognition quickly; elsewhere, trust usually begins with a demonstration rather than an assumption.
Vanarin.traitNarrativeEffects: A vanarin's tail, hands, and momentum make branches, ropes, rails, gaps, and sudden changes of elevation natural routes.

Gnoll.name: Gnoll
Gnoll.description:
Gnolls are hyena-headed people of packs, caravan roads, and the burnt cities of lower Redrock. Their princes build power through raids, tribute, captives, and public contests of strength, but not every gnoll accepts a prince's rule. Packs break, exiles travel, and a gnoll who refuses a bad alpha may become a hunter, guard, guide, or rebel far from the people who named them.

Gnolls are tall and powerful, with long arms, sloping shoulders, coarse fur marked in ochre, brown, grey, or black, rounded ears, broad jaws, and teeth made for tearing. Their senses and pack habits make them dangerous trackers and ambushers. A gnoll who chooses a different life still carries the body and reputation of the pack.

Most settled people read a gnoll as a raider or pack enforcer. Guards, merchants, and caravan towns may demand proof, toll, or distance. A gnoll who breaks with a prince can also be treated as a traitor by gnoll powers. This is suspicion and political danger, not automatic violence: independent caravan folk, rebels, and people defended by the character may become allies.
Gnoll.traitNarrativeEffects: Gnolls read scent, spoor, fear, and group movement instinctively and know how to make a refusal or challenge legible to pack-minded people.

Empyrean.name: Empyrean
Empyrean.description:
Empyreans are rare, scattered winged people whose ancestors ruled land, sea, and sky in the Empyrean Empire. The old empire was proud and tyrannical; the empyreans alive today are not responsible for it, though their height, wings, inner-lit eyes, and ancient names make the history difficult to forget. The Empire of Light at Caranthoria claims the old crown's foundations while opening citizenship to every people, and an empyrean may be welcomed there, recruited, watched, or all three.

Empyreans stand taller than most humans and are built on a grander scale, with strong features, broad feathered wings, and skin and feathers ranging from white through red, black, bronze, and shades between. Their eyes hold a faint steady light. Wings are part of their body and identity, not proof of holiness.

An empyrean is rare and impossible to ignore. People may assume imperial, celestial, or ancient tyrant ancestry; the Empire of Light may expect service or loyalty. In Caranthoria and among people who know modern empyreans, recognition can open doors, but most settlements begin with attention and assumptions rather than easy trust.
Empyrean.traitNarrativeEffects: Broad feathered wings permit controlled ascent, gliding, aerial observation, and crossings appropriate to the available space and weather.

Bard.name: Bard
Bard.description:
Main Attributes: Attunement and Charisma

Bards are specialists in attention, mood, story, and access. A good bard can turn a room before anyone admits the room has turned: a song at the right time, a joke that lands too sharply, a rumor carried to the right ear, a silence that makes everyone lean in. Performance is their craft, but the real talent is knowing what people want to believe and giving it shape.

Bards move through taverns, courts, camps, ships, guildhalls, underworld dens, and noble salons because people open doors for entertainment, gossip, comfort, and spectacle. That access is power. A bard can lift allies, expose fools, start trouble, end trouble, and make a dangerous moment follow their tempo long enough to matter.

Special Starting Gear: Maple Lute
abilities: Walking Lie
Second Wind
Draw Power
Cutting Verse
Make a Song of It
Bard.traitNarrativeEffects: Bards are in demand as entertainers. A notable performance may earn an invitation from a wealthy patron or other person of consequence, opening rooms and company usually closed to strangers.

Blood Dancer.name: Blood Dancer
Blood Dancer.description:
Main Attributes: Attunement, Constitution, and Dexterity

Blood dancers turn bloodletting, pulse, pain, and blade-work into a disciplined fighting art. Their scars are practiced channels that make fresh blood easier to focus, clot, read, and spend. They learn to open themselves for sudden power, leave a foe’s wound working after the blade has passed, and draw that failing strength back into their own body.

The style is acrobatic, intimate, and costly. A good blood dancer knows what each cut buys, when to let a wound keep bleeding, when to take its power, and when the price in their own body has become too high.

Special Starting Gear: Red-Jade Bloodchannel Dagger.
abilities: Bloodstep
First Cut
Second Wind
Draw Power
A New Movement
Blood Dancer.traitNarrativeEffects: A blood dancer reads pulse, blood heat, bleeding, tremor, and fresh wounds as practical information and understands the bodily cost of bloodcraft.

Druid.name: Druid
Druid.description:
Main Attributes: Attunement and Wisdom

Druids work with the living world as it is: root, rain, rot, thorn, soil, animal sign, river mud, bark, hunger, shelter, and blight. Their magic is not a lecture from nature. It is a practiced relationship with land that answers in useful ways when danger comes. A druid knows when a forest has gone too quiet, when a field is sick, when water has been fouled, and when a path is trying to close behind someone.

In Larion, druids protect wild places, guide settlements through weather and plague, read the health of farms and forests, and make the terrain itself part of the answer. They can call roots around an enemy's feet, wrap an ally in bark and bramble, borrow a beast's sense or a tree's patience, and help living things hold together when poison, panic, or violence would tear them apart.
abilities: Greenbreak
No Shape Forgotten
Second Wind
Draw Power
Druid.traitNarrativeEffects: Druids read the health and recent disturbance of land, water, plants, animals, and weather.

Fighter.name: Fighter
Fighter.description:
Main Attribute: Strength

Fighters are not just people with weapons. They are the ones who know where to stand, when to move, how to read a grip, how to punish bad footing, and how to make a chaotic fight obey them for one more breath. A fighter can be an academy duelist, mercenary veteran, pit champion, guard captain, caravan blade, village defender, or self-taught survivor, but the core is the same: practiced violence under pressure.

In Larion, fighters keep roads open, hold doors while others run, break charges before they land, and turn ugly brawls into winnable exchanges. Magic can fail, bargains can sour, courage can crack. A trained fighter still knows how to put steel, shield, armor, body, and timing between danger and the people or prize that matter.

A fighter can bring practiced control to any weapon, even one snatched from an enemy or improvised from what lies at hand. They may use a trained weapon skill of their choice instead of the weapon's matching skill. Before level 10, doing so carries a -5 modifier; at level 10, that modifier disappears.
abilities: Turn the Exchange
Second Wind
Draw Power
Make It Mine
Fighter.traitNarrativeEffects: A fighter reads stance, grip, armor, breath, weapon angle, spacing, and bad footing as practical information during a dangerous exchange.

Hammerdwarf.name: Hammerdwarf
Hammerdwarf.description:
Main Attributes: Strength and Intelligence

Hammerdwarves are armored warriors who fight the way dwarves build — heavy, precise, and methodical. They know how things are put together, which makes them very good at taking things apart.
abilities: Flying Headbutt
Everything Is a Nail
Second Wind
Draw Power
Hammerdwarf.traitNarrativeEffects: A Hammerdwarf can read how a worked object or structure was made, what strain it carries, and where repair or dismantling should begin.

Monk.name: Monk
Monk.description:
Main Attributes: Attunement, Wisdom, Dexterity, and Strength

Monks train until breath, balance, attention, and motion answer as one. Some orders teach through meditation and prayer, some through endurance, some through repeated movement until the body learns before thought can interfere. The result is not serenity as decoration. It is practical control: a hand in the right place, a step taken at the right time, a body that refuses to be hurried by fear.

A trained monk can fight unarmed because every joint, breath, stance, and fall has been made useful. They close gaps, redirect force, read tension, and strike where balance fails. Outside combat, that same discipline lets them climb, wait, listen, endure, and act cleanly when everyone else is reacting. The most dangerous monks are not the loudest ones. They are the ones who arrive already centered.

Monks teach that the body has more answers than habit permits. Through Forms—commands perfected until breath, flesh, bone, balance, and sense answer the will—they make their own bodies exceed ordinary mortal limits for a single deed. Different orders pursue different limits: impossible weight or lightness, hardness or suppleness, sense without sight, perfect timing, endurance, or swift mending.
abilities: Form: Three Before Thunder
Second Wind
Draw Power
Monk.traitNarrativeEffects: A monk can command their own living body beyond ordinary mortal limits: change how it bears weight and force, harden or loosen it, act without sight, bring impossible timing to a movement, hold breath or poison at bay, or urge a fresh wound to close. A learned Form perfects one such command into a repeatable technique.

Paladin.name: Paladin
Paladin.description:
Main Attributes: Attunement, Strength, Wisdom, and Charisma

Paladins turn divine service into vows and vows into action. Each serves one or more patron divinities, pledging to carry divine will into the world through action. A vow may bind a paladin to defend a temple, order, homeland, company, cause, or sacred ideal, but the patron divinity is the power that witnesses and answers it. It is a promise with armor on: the paladin names what they will do, fulfills it under pressure, and returns in prayer for the patron's answer.

Some paladins guard pilgrims and sanctuaries. Some hunt undead, fiends, tyrants, oathbreakers, or monsters that prey on the helpless. Some serve old orders, and some carry a vow no institution fully understands. What they share is not softness or certainty, but commitment under pressure: the courage to stand between danger and the vulnerable, and the authority to make a fight about more than survival.

Special Starting Gear: Devotion Clasp
abilities: Oathbound Smite
Second Wind
Draw Power
Answer the Oath
Paladin.traitNarrativeEffects: A paladin serves one or more patron divinities through vows that carry divine will into the world. Leave every vow and its terms to the player. After a paladin fulfills a vow and returns to prayer, their patron may bless an object tied to the deed as a Vow Focus.

Ranger.name: Ranger
Ranger.description:
Main Attributes: Dexterity and Wisdom

Rangers are scouts, hunters, guides, wardens, and ambushers who understand how movement works when roads end and sightlines lie. They read tracks, weather, cover, water, animal sign, patrol habits, and bad footing as quickly as other people read faces. A ranger does not need a fair fight. A ranger needs the right ground, the right route, and one clean moment when the target steps where they should not.

Every frontier settlement, logging camp, border fort, and trade caravan knows the value of a good ranger. They find the pass before snow closes it, spot the raiders before the horn sounds, guide travelers around danger, and put an arrow or blade into trouble from the angle it forgot to guard. The best rangers make the world feel larger to their allies and much smaller to anything being hunted.

Rangers can tame and train wild beasts, and one that comes to lasting trust may become an enduring companion in travel and battle. Their finest shots can follow trajectories no ordinary archer could make.
abilities: Crooked Flight
Second Wind
Draw Power
Ranger.traitNarrativeEffects: A ranger belongs in the wilds. They read tracks, weather, cover, water, animal sign, patrol habits, routes, and terrain, and understand the needs and temperaments of wild beasts. In new country, occasionally establish a distinctive local beast through its signs before the encounter; it may be hunted, avoided, aided, calmed, trained, or befriended according to its nature. A beast that comes to lasting trust may choose to travel with the ranger as a companion.

Beastmaster.name: Beastmaster
Beastmaster.description: You can guide several beasts as one hunting company. You may have up to three active Beast Companions.

Rogue.name: Rogue
Rogue.description:
Main Attribute: Dexterity

Rogues are specialists in attention, access, timing, and exits. They notice the loose latch, the bored guard, the false smile, the loaded purse, the hidden pocket, the crowded doorway, and the one second when everyone looks somewhere else. Some are thieves, spies, burglars, smugglers, assassins, scouts, or professional problem-solvers, but the shared talent is simple: get in, get what matters, and get out with the room still arguing about what happened.

A rogue does not need the cleanest fight or the honest path. They need a blind spot, a useful lie, a misplaced key, a moving crowd, a hand already in motion, or an exit nobody else counted. In Larion's cities, ruins, courts, underworlds, and locked places, that skill set opens doors steel cannot break and survives dangers armor cannot solve.

Special Starting Gear: Loaded Dice
abilities: Melt Away
Second Wind
Draw Power
Under the Guard
Worked It Out
Rogue.traitNarrativeEffects: A rogue notices exits, security habits, underworld signs, valuables, blind spots, loose latches, and moments when attention moves elsewhere.

Warlock.name: Warlock
Warlock.description:
