Main Attributes: Attunement, Intelligence, and Charisma

Warlocks hold power through a living pact with a patron beyond the mortal world. The bargain may be written, sworn, inherited, stolen, misunderstood, or struck in desperation. It grants specific powers through signs, servants, hexes, summonings, sudden doors, and other workings marked by the patron.

A warlock's existing powers are settled clauses of the bargain, not a new negotiation each time they are used. A practiced warlock learns to call on those powers cleanly, read what the patron wants, find leverage, and negotiate new clauses without yielding more than they intend.

Special Starting Gear: Pact Token
abilities: Handspan Gate
Second Wind
Draw Power
Warlock.traitNarrativeEffects: A warlock may deliberately use the established sign, token, name, or custom of their pact to seek an audience, answer, or omen from the patron. The patron may answer, refuse, or name terms, but no response accepts a bargain or obligation for the player.

Wizard.name: Wizard
Wizard.description:
Main Attributes: Attunement and Intelligence

Wizards are the people who learned how magic is built, then learned where to put pressure until it obeys. No bloodline gift, no patron's bargain: just hard-won technique, exact hands, prepared marks, and the nerve to use them under threat. A good wizard does not merely throw fire. They read the shape of a curse, cut a summoning loose, fold a ward into a cuff, and turn a bad battlefield into a problem they have already solved.

Their tools are spellbooks, chalk, thread, ink, rings, diagrams, and memorized names, but the point is not study for its own sake. The point is control. Wizardry in Larion is precise, dangerous work practiced in academies, towers, courts, ruins, and on roads where theory has to survive teeth, steel, weather, and hostile magic.

Special Starting Gear: Traveling Spellbook, two sheets of Prepared Vellum, and a Scroll of the White Comet.
abilities: Magebolt
The Unwritten Spell
Second Wind
Draw Power
Wizard.traitNarrativeEffects: A wizard sees spells, wards, curses, rituals, magical traps, and other formal magic as things made from parts. When a wizard studies unfamiliar magic, reveal a specific principle they can pursue: an inscription, residue, repeated gesture, material, name, or flaw. Understanding the principle may seed a spell, but does not finish one.

Tinker.name: Tinker
Tinker.description:
Main Attributes: Intelligence and Dexterity

Tinkers solve problems with kit, nerve, and hands that keep moving: clamps, springs, wire, lenses, vials, gears, oil, chalk marks, tiny charms, and field repairs that hold exactly long enough. Some build companions or elaborate constructs, but the core trade is more immediate than that. A tinker sees where pressure goes, where a mechanism wants to fail, and what small device can make the next few seconds belong to them.

In Larion, tinkers fix wagons, open old locks, read broken mechanisms, rig traps, patch armor, tune spellgear, and make dangerous little tools from whatever is on hand. In a fight, they do not need to be the strongest person in the room. They need a hinge, a wire, a weak plate, a vial, a spark, and one good moment when the device works.

Special Starting Gear: Artificer's Toolkit; a Spring-Fist; a Needle Trap of Poison and its blueprint; a Stormsteel Burstwheel of Shock and its blueprint; two bundles of Mechanical Components; and one Venomwood Extract.
abilities: Disaster in Three
Everything Has Parts
Second Wind
Draw Power
Tinker.traitNarrativeEffects: A tinker can identify mechanical faults, produce ordinary pocket tools, and make temporary field repairs when kit and material allow.

Sorcerer.name: Sorcerer
Sorcerer.description:
Main Attributes: Attunement and Intelligence

Sorcerers carry magic inside the body before they ever learn what to call it. Its origin may be an inheritance, curse, old ritual, magical accident, strange birth, or mystery no one has answered, but it is not borrowed and it is not built from notes. It lives in breath, temper, pulse, skin, voice, and instinct. Training teaches a sorcerer how not to burn down the room every time fear or anger reaches for the power.

That rawness is both gift and danger. A sorcerer can release power faster than a careful caster can prepare for it, shape a surge into something useful, and survive moments where the magic almost gets away. The best ones are not calm because the power is gentle. They are calm because they have learned exactly how much of themselves to let out.
abilities: Power Breaks Loose
No One Taught You This
Second Wind
Draw Power
Sorcerer.traitNarrativeEffects: A sorcerer may deliberately let their inborn magic show through their body or the nearby world. Reuse a recurring appearance only when background or story has already established it.

Vampire.name: Vampire
Vampire.description: You have become a vampire, gaining supernatural power at the cost of a bestial hunger for blood and vulnerability to sunlight.
Vampire.traitNarrativeEffects: Possesses dark sight and blood sense. Extremely vulnerable to sunlight and weak by holy symbols. Must regularly consume fresh blood or grow weak and lose self-control.

Lycanthrope.name: Lycanthrope
Lycanthrope.description: You have been cursed with the affliction of the werewolf. Under the full moon, you transform into a powerful beast, gaining supernatural strength and senses at the cost of feral rage and loss of self-control.
Lycanthrope.traitNarrativeEffects: Can transform into a werewolf, gaining enhanced strength, speed, and senses. Heightened senses of smell and hearing. Vulnerable to silver weapons.

Fire Magic.name: Fire Magic
Fire Magic.description: You can call fire from your hands and bend it where you want it. A spark, a bolt, a wall of flame. (Attunement)
abilities: Firebrand Charge

Water Magic.name: Water Magic
Water Magic.description: You can pull water from the air, shape it, freeze it, drive it forward like a fist. Where there's moisture, you have a weapon. (Attunement)
abilities: Winter's Grasp

Earth Magic.name: Earth Magic
Earth Magic.description: Stone listens to you. You can crack rock, raise walls from bare ground, and make the earth move under someone's feet. (Attunement)
abilities: Earthfist

Divine Magic.name: Divine Magic
Divine Magic.description: You can wield holy power — a smite that burns the unholy, a ward that holds evil at bay, a blessing that strengthens the faithful. (Attunement)
abilities: Sacred Word

Dark Magic.name: Dark Magic
Dark Magic.description: You've learned to wield shadow, decay, and worse. It's dangerous, it's forbidden in most places, and it works. (Attunement)
abilities: Night Talon

Illusion Magic.name: Illusion Magic
Illusion Magic.description: You can make people see things that aren't there and miss things that are. A useful trick that scales as far as your imagination does. (Attunement)
abilities: Mirrorstep

Necromancy.name: Necromancy
Necromancy.description: You can speak to the dead and, when needed, make them get back up. Most people find this unsettling. The dead don't seem to mind. (Attunement)
abilities: Loose the Shade-Hound

Conjuration.name: Conjuration
Conjuration.description: You can reach across the veil and pull something through — a servant, a beast, a thing that follows your commands. What comes depends on what you call. (Attunement)
abilities: Swift Circle

Divination.name: Divination
Divination.description: You can see what others can't — glimpses of what's coming, traces of what's hidden, the thread connecting a question to its answer. (Attunement)
abilities: See It Coming

Nature Magic.name: Nature Magic
Nature Magic.description: You can coax a seed to sprout in seconds, command roots to bind, and call on the green world to fight for you. (Attunement)
abilities: Wyrmseed

Blood Magic.name: Blood Magic
Blood Magic.description: You can turn living blood into power — your own or someone else's. It costs something every time. It's always worth it in the moment. (Attunement)
abilities: The Red Price

Healing Magic.name: Healing Magic
Healing Magic.description: You can close wounds, purge poison, and mend what's broken. In a world full of things that hurt people, you're the one who puts them back together. (Attunement)
abilities: Golden Stitches

Warding Magic.name: Warding Magic
Warding Magic.description: You have trained in barriers, seals, and the unmaking of hostile magic. You can raise temporary protections, unravel spells, and hold supernatural forces at bay. (Attunement)

Psionics.name: Psionics
Psionics.description: You have trained thought and will into force without hands: lifting objects, speaking mind to mind, and striking directly at another will. (Attunement)
abilities: Psychic Lance

Enchanting.name: Enchanting
Enchanting.description: You can pour magic into an object and make it hold. A blade that glows hot, a lock that won't open, a shield that turns spells. (Attunement)
abilities: Living Sigil

Tactics.name: Tactics
Tactics.description: You read a fight before it starts — who's exposed, where the line will break, when to press. You make everyone around you more dangerous. (Intelligence)
abilities: Take the Ground

Medicine.name: Medicine
Medicine.description: You know how to stop bleeding, set bones, and brew a poultice from roadside plants. Steady hands, hard-won knowledge, and no magic required. (Wisdom)
abilities: Blood, Bone, Breath

Insight.name: Insight
Insight.description: You read people the way others read weather — the rehearsed answer, the grief that is performed, the person in the room who actually decides. (Wisdom)
abilities: Inside Their Guard

Investigation.name: Investigation
Investigation.description: You notice what other people walk past — the scratches on the lock, the footprint under the window, the thing that doesn't belong. (Wisdom)
abilities: Retrace Their Steps

Animal Handling.name: Animal Handling
Animal Handling.description: Animals trust you. You can calm a spooked horse, read a dog's warning, and earn the loyalty of creatures most people can't get near. (Wisdom)
abilities: Run Beside Me

Riding.name: Riding
Riding.description: You're at home in the saddle — riding hard, fighting mounted, and handling beasts that throw anyone else. (Constitution) Your training includes a named ordinary mount appropriate to your history and premise; establish its name and nature when it first matters.
abilities: No Road Needed

Warhammer.name: Warhammer
Warhammer.description: Two hands, a long haft, and an iron head that turns plate armor into a coffin. Warhammers are specialist weapons for people who like to solve problems in one swing.

Criminal.name: Criminal
Criminal.description: You grew up on the wrong side of the law — picking pockets, running jobs, learning which alleys go through and which ones are traps. You know how the underworld works because you worked in it.

Soldier.name: Soldier
Soldier.description: You did a stint in a company, a garrison, or a lord's retinue. Long enough to learn camp discipline, formation drill, and how to sleep in the rain. Short enough that you're nobody's sergeant.

Outlaw.name: Outlaw
Outlaw.description: You lived outside the law and outside the walls — in the hills, the forest, the places where the king's writ doesn't reach. Banditry, smuggling, poaching, whatever kept you fed. You know how to survive and how to make people do what you want when asking nicely isn't an option.

Herbalist.name: Herbalist
Herbalist.description: You learned which plants close wounds and which ones stop hearts. Village healer, roadside apothecary, hedge-doctor — whatever the title, people came to you when they were hurt and the nearest temple was three days' ride away.

Hunter.name: Hunter
Hunter.description: You fed your family from the forest. Tracks, traps, patience, and a clean kill. You know animal behavior the way a merchant knows prices — instinct backed by experience.

Acolyte.name: Acolyte
Acolyte.description: You were raised in a temple or monastery. Maybe you believed, maybe you just needed a roof. Either way, you learned to read, studied history and scripture, and came out knowing more about the world than most people who've actually seen it.

Entertainer.name: Entertainer
Entertainer.description: You've worked stages, tavern floors, and street corners. Singing, juggling, acting, telling stories — whatever held the crowd. You know how to walk into a room full of strangers and leave with their attention, their coin, or both.

Templar Initiate.name: Templar Initiate
Templar Initiate.description: A newly sworn Shieldbearer admitted to the Templars Adamant after completing Galard's Proving Year. An Initiate undertakes one supervised shield-work before receiving full Templar standing.
Templar Initiate.traitNarrativeEffects: The Templars Adamant recognize this character as a newly sworn Initiate who must complete one supervised shield-work before receiving full standing. This standing changes only when the order names the next rank in the Hall of Shields; until then, no slip, token, badge, or partial title stands in for it.

Templar Adamant.name: Templar Adamant
Templar Adamant.description: A full member of the Templars Adamant trusted to undertake independent protection, purging, warding, and sealing works in Galard's name.
Templar Adamant.traitNarrativeEffects: The order recognizes this character as a full Templar Adamant trusted with independent shield-works and access appropriate to ordinary membership. This standing changes only when the order names the next rank in the Hall of Shields; until then, no slip, token, badge, or partial title stands in for it.

Templar Captain.name: Templar Captain
Templar Captain.description: A proven Templar Adamant authorized to direct field wards, sealing rites, and willing Templars during serious operations.
abilities: Take the Blow
Templar Captain.traitNarrativeEffects: The order recognizes this character as a Templar Captain with authority to direct field wards, sealing rites, and Templars who serve under the operation. This standing changes only when the order names the next rank in the Hall of Shields; until then, no slip, token, badge, or partial title stands in for it.

Templar Champion.name: Templar Champion
Templar Champion.description: A senior champion of the Templars Adamant trusted with the order's largest purges, defenses, breaches, and strategic sealing campaigns.
abilities: The Wall Holds
Templar Champion.traitNarrativeEffects: The order recognizes this character as a Templar Champion empowered to direct its largest field responses, judge recognized works, and lead strategic campaigns. First Sword and temple leadership remain appointed offices.

Shieldbearer Oath.name: Shieldbearer Oath
Shieldbearer Oath.description: You freely swore Galard's Shieldbearer oath before the Hall of Shields and entered the Templars Adamant. Its courage is the courage to become the wall: protect the living, hold while necessary work is done, purge what violates sanctuary, destroy the anchors of the hostile dead, and close the breach behind them. The oath does not require a literal shield, heavy armor, Paladin training, or any particular weapon.
abilities: Shieldfall
Shieldbearer Oath.traitNarrativeEffects: This character has chosen Galard's Shieldbearer way and is recognized as a Templar of the appropriate stored rank. Their oath supports weapons, shields, magical foci, spells, mobility, healing, and other builds; never assume plate armor or a literal shield. Their standing comes from Templar state, not from this trait alone.

Swordbearer Oath.name: Swordbearer Oath
Swordbearer Oath.description: You freely swore Galard's Swordbearer oath and entered the Knights Vigilant. Its courage is the courage to carry the fight to the dark: ride toward threatened people, confront what hunts them, break its advantage, and refuse to leave companions behind. The oath does not require a sword, a mount, Paladin training, or any particular weapon.
abilities: Advancing Dawn
Swordbearer Oath.traitNarrativeEffects: This character has chosen Galard's Swordbearer way and is recognized as a Knight Vigilant of the appropriate stored rank. Their oath supports weapons, bows, magical foci, spells, mobility, healing, and other builds; never assume a sword or mount. Their standing comes from Knights Vigilant state, not from this trait alone.

Proving-Year Aspirant.name: Proving-Year Aspirant
Proving-Year Aspirant.description: You are undertaking Galard's traditional Proving Year: traveling beyond the shelter of family and temple, facing worthy dangers, and learning through deeds whether the Shieldbearer oath, the Swordbearer oath, or neither should be yours. You belong to neither estranged order yet.
Proving-Year Aspirant.traitNarrativeEffects: This character is publicly recognizable to Galard's faithful as a Proving-Year Aspirant if they show the Road-Shield. They are not a Templar Adamant, Knight Vigilant, Shieldbearer, or Swordbearer and possess no authority from either order. Their three recognized deeds and eventual oath remain player choices. This standing changes only when the character swears their chosen oath at the end of the Proving Year; until then, no slip, token, badge, or partial title stands in for it.

Mark of Rhadan.name: Mark of Rhadan
Mark of Rhadan.description: You have been accepted into the Shadow Inquisition at the Black Tower in Drusavia. The Mark of Rhadan is the order's oath-mark, carried by Initiates as well as full Inquisitors. It identifies you to the Tower and anchors you to the living world during authorized contact with the Shadelands, but it does not by itself make you Shade-Bonded or grant full Inquisitor rank.
Mark of Rhadan.traitNarrativeEffects: This character bears the Mark of Rhadan and is recognized as a member of the Shadow Inquisition. The Shadow Inquisition is a heroic and prestigious institution in Drusavia. Its Inquisitors protect the living from ghosts, necromancers, vampires, ghouls, and other threats from the dead. The Mark is a sanctioned sign of service, not a curse or proof of evil. Drusavian rulers, guards, and citizens generally respect the order's authority and do not interfere with its work lightly. The Mark anchors authorized crossings and keeps the Shadelands from rejecting them outright. It does not establish their rank: an Initiate remains a candidate, cannot undertake an unsanctioned descent, and is not Shade-Bonded until completing the Rite of Bonding.

Shade-Bonded.name: Shade-Bonded
Shade-Bonded.description: Through the authorized Rite of Bonding at the Pit of Shadow, you knowingly accepted a permanent bond with a Shade — a spirit drawn from the Shadelands, the grey country of the dead. It stands with you as supernatural partner and shield: a figure almost a person, the shape right but the details wrong, like a reflection in dark water. Through the bond you feel the dead and the Shadelands pressing into the living world.
abilities: Send the Shade
Shade-Bonded.traitNarrativeEffects: The bonded Shade can help perceive the dead, confront restless spirits and their anchors, and recognize places where the Shadelands press against the living world. Its personality and relationship emerge through play.

Path of the Blade.name: Path of the Blade
Path of the Blade.description:
You are trained in serious weapon combat. This Path covers soldiers, duelists, guards, mercenaries, knights, pit fighters, and anyone who has learned to stay alive when steel comes out. The Order of the Silver Sword and other martial schools can give this beginning a place in the world, but the Path is broader than any one order. Its foundation is the body that carries the weapon: footwork, wind, balance, and the conditioning that decides who is still standing in the third minute.

You have: +2 athletics and +1 strength.

Power, Momentum: each attack or defence of yours that lands in a fight climbs a step of impact; at this rank up to In Stride (125).

Next: Novice of the Blade, open to anyone on this Path. To pursue Novice rank, first declare a concrete martial feat before attempting it, explicitly naming Novice of the Blade as the rank you seek. Enact the declaration as a vow, promise, pledge, or sworn undertaking to a god, master, witness, opponent, institution, or yourself. Name the feat, a meaningful danger or constraint, and a clear success condition. A suitable Novice feat requires disciplined weapon use under genuine danger; for example, swear to disarm a dangerous opponent without killing them or hold a named position until others escape. A win or a kill does not count by itself: the vow must hold you to a limit you chose, such as sparing the foe or holding a place, and the feat must keep it.

The Path: Path of the Blade (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Blade from level 50). Rank skill counts in a weapon skill (any weapon, shield, or unarmed combat). Each rank adds 1 to your strength.

Vowed Blade Feat.name: Vowed Blade Feat
Vowed Blade Feat.description: You have deliberately vowed to complete a specific martial feat as proof that you are ready to advance on the Path of the Blade. The feat must be completed as declared, including its named danger, constraints, and success condition. This undertaking remains until it is fulfilled or you explicitly relinquish it. Relinquish the current undertaking before declaring a different one.

Path of the Cloak.name: Path of the Cloak
Path of the Cloak.description:
You are trained in quiet work: moving unseen, opening what is locked, scouting danger, following without being seen, reading exits, handling secrets, and wearing a false face when needed. This path covers thieves, spies, scouts, infiltrators, trap-breakers, rebel couriers, noble agents, guild hands, and careful survivors.

You have: +2 stealth and +1 dexterity.

Power, Unseen Strikes: an attack from hiding that rolls a Great Success or better keeps you Hidden and climbs a step of impact; at this rank up to Unseen Strike I (225).

Next: Novice of the Cloak, open to anyone on this Path. To become a Novice of the Cloak, find a suitable contact or patron, take a small quiet job, return with proof, and show that you can work with discretion.

The Path: Path of the Cloak (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Cloak from level 50). Rank skill counts in stealth, lockpicking, pickpocketing, or acrobatics. Each rank adds 1 to your dexterity.

Novice of the Blade.name: Novice of the Blade
Novice of the Blade.description:
You have deliberately tested your weapon discipline under genuine danger and fulfilled the feat exactly as you vowed it. Fear, resistance, and consequence are no longer abstractions to you.

You have: +5 maximum stamina; +1 strength from your ranks so far.

Power, Momentum: each attack or defence of yours that lands in a fight climbs a step of impact; at this rank up to In Stride (125).

Next: Adept of the Blade, once you have 15 in a weapon skill (any weapon, shield, or unarmed combat). "Ready for Adept of the Blade" appears on your sheet when you do. To pursue Adept rank, first vow a concrete feat that explicitly names Adept of the Blade as the rank you seek and demonstrates a named martial technique or controlled result against capable resistance. Declare the technique, a meaningful constraint, and a clear success condition before attempting it. For example, swear to take a weapon from a veteran without drawing blood, or defeat a shield fighter without yielding the center of a marked circle. Simply beating or killing a dangerous enemy does not count: the feat must show the technique you named, within the constraint you declared.

The Path: Path of the Blade (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Blade from level 50). Rank skill counts in a weapon skill (any weapon, shield, or unarmed combat). Each rank adds 1 to your strength.

Adept of the Blade.name: Adept of the Blade
Adept of the Blade.description:
You have demonstrated deliberate technique against capable resistance while holding yourself to a declared constraint. Your weapon work is measured by control, not merely by victory.

You have: +5 maximum stamina; +2 strength from your ranks so far; Set the Terms.

Power, Momentum: each attack or defence of yours that lands in a fight climbs a step of impact; at this rank up to In Full Stride (150).

Next: Expert of the Blade, once you have 25 in a weapon skill (any weapon, shield, or unarmed combat). "Ready for Expert of the Blade" appears on your sheet when you do. To pursue Expert rank, first vow a concrete feat that explicitly names Expert of the Blade as the rank you seek and in which you take responsibility for a dangerous engagement beyond your own survival. Declare the people or larger objective you will safeguard, the tactical constraint you will uphold, the real opposition, and a clear success condition. For example, swear to hold a gate alone until every civilian has crossed without allowing an enemy through. Surviving or fighting bravely does not count: you must control the fight while carrying the lives or objective you named.

The Path: Path of the Blade (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Blade from level 50). Rank skill counts in a weapon skill (any weapon, shield, or unarmed combat). Each rank adds 1 to your strength.
abilities: Set the Terms

Expert of the Blade.name: Expert of the Blade
Expert of the Blade.description:
You have controlled a dangerous engagement while carrying responsibility for lives or an objective beyond yourself. You understand how position, timing, nerve, and force decide what happens to everyone around you.

You have: +10 maximum stamina; +3 strength from your ranks so far; Set the Terms and Answer in Kind.

Power, Momentum: each attack or defence of yours that lands in a fight climbs a step of impact; at this rank up to Relentless (175).

From level 30, you can take one Discipline as a level-up pick: Discipline of Measure, Discipline of the Line, or Discipline of Command.

Next: Master of the Blade, once you have 40 in a weapon skill (any weapon, shield, or unarmed combat). "Ready for Master of the Blade" appears on your sheet when you do. To pursue Master rank, first vow an exceptional martial capstone that explicitly names Master of the Blade as the rank you seek. Declare the extreme opposition or stakes, an exacting constraint, and a decisive success condition worthy of a life's discipline. For example, swear to end a renowned champion's undefeated run using no weapon but the one they choose for you, while sparing their life. A hard victory or a famous kill does not count unless it meets the exact vow.

The Path: Path of the Blade (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Blade from level 50). Rank skill counts in a weapon skill (any weapon, shield, or unarmed combat). Each rank adds 1 to your strength.
abilities: Set the Terms
Answer in Kind

Master of the Blade.name: Master of the Blade
Master of the Blade.description:
You have fulfilled an exceptional martial undertaking under exacting constraints and against extreme stakes or opposition. Your mastery lies not simply in defeating danger, but in carrying contact, recovery, position, and force as one unbroken discipline.

You have: +10 maximum stamina; +4 strength from your ranks so far; Set the Terms, Answer in Kind, and No Motion Wasted; resistance to piercing, slashing, and impact damage.

Power, Momentum: each attack or defence of yours that lands in a fight climbs a step of impact; at this rank up to Unstoppable (200).

From level 30, you can take one Discipline as a level-up pick: Discipline of Measure, Discipline of the Line, or Discipline of Command.

Next: from level 50, Legend of the Blade as a level-up pick: +5 strength and One True Blow.

The Path: Path of the Blade (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Blade from level 50). Rank skill counts in a weapon skill (any weapon, shield, or unarmed combat). Each rank adds 1 to your strength.
abilities: Set the Terms
Answer in Kind
No Motion Wasted

Discipline of Measure.name: Discipline of Measure
Discipline of Measure.description: You specialize in reading one opponent, controlling the geometry of an exchange, and choosing exact outcomes. This permanent Expert specialization grants +5 tactics and makes The Fourth Strike available for purchase with ability points.

Discipline of the Line.name: Discipline of the Line
Discipline of the Line.description: You specialize in holding consequential ground and carrying other people through danger. This permanent Expert specialization grants +20 maximum stamina and makes Carve the Lane available for purchase with ability points.

Discipline of Command.name: Discipline of Command
Discipline of Command.description: You specialize in identifying what will decide a battle and seizing it at the critical moment. This permanent Expert specialization grants +5 leadership and makes Turning Point available for purchase with ability points.

Novice of the Wild.name: Novice of the Wild
Novice of the Wild.description:
The land has taught you something you did not bring with you. You read weather before it arrives, you camp where camping works, and the country stops being scenery.

You have: +5 maximum stamina; +1 wisdom from your ranks so far.

Power, Aspects of the Wild: call an aspect on your ability list in a fight, for mana. It holds until the fight ends, one at a time, and grows with your rank.

Next: Adept of the Wild, once you have 15 in survival, tracking, animal handling, nature magic, or shape shifting. "Ready for Adept of the Wild" appears on your sheet when you do. To become an Adept of the Wild, bring yourself or others through country that could have killed you: bad weather, a hard crossing, a lean season, hostile ground, or a route nobody sensible takes.

The Path: Path of the Wild (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Wild from level 50). Rank skill counts in survival, tracking, animal handling, nature magic, or shape shifting. Each rank adds 1 to your wisdom.

Adept of the Wild.name: Adept of the Wild
Adept of the Wild.description:
You have brought people through country that should have stopped them. Not survival by luck — you chose the route, read the season, and were right.

You have: +5 maximum stamina; +2 wisdom from your ranks so far; Read the Ground and Aspect of the Serpent.

Power, Aspects of the Wild: call an aspect on your ability list in a fight, for mana. It holds until the fight ends, one at a time, and grows with your rank.

Next: Expert of the Wild, once you have 25 in survival, tracking, animal handling, nature magic, or shape shifting. "Ready for Expert of the Wild" appears on your sheet when you do. To become an Expert of the Wild, take responsibility for wild places or the people crossing them: guide a party through real danger, hold a frontier route open, tend sick land, or stand between a settlement and what the wild sent at it.

The Path: Path of the Wild (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Wild from level 50). Rank skill counts in survival, tracking, animal handling, nature magic, or shape shifting. Each rank adds 1 to your wisdom.
abilities: Read the Ground
Aspect of the Serpent

Expert of the Wild.name: Expert of the Wild
Expert of the Wild.description:
Wild places and the people crossing them are trusted to you. When a road closes, a season turns bad, or something comes out of the trees, you are who gets sent.

You have: +10 maximum stamina; +3 wisdom from your ranks so far; Read the Ground, Run It to Ruin, Aspect of the Serpent, and Aspect of the Oak.

Power, Aspects of the Wild: call an aspect on your ability list in a fight, for mana. It holds until the fight ends, one at a time, and grows with your rank.

From level 30, you can take one Discipline as a level-up pick: Discipline of the Pack or Discipline of the Green.

Next: Master of the Wild, once you have 40 in survival, tracking, animal handling, nature magic, or shape shifting. "Ready for Master of the Wild" appears on your sheet when you do. To become a Master of the Wild, do something for the wild, or against what threatens it, that frontier folk repeat afterwards, and be named, sought out, or openly acknowledged for it.

The Path: Path of the Wild (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Wild from level 50). Rank skill counts in survival, tracking, animal handling, nature magic, or shape shifting. Each rank adds 1 to your wisdom.
abilities: Read the Ground
Run It to Ruin
Aspect of the Serpent
Aspect of the Oak

Master of the Wild.name: Master of the Wild
Master of the Wild.description:
Frontier folk speak your name as the reason a road is passable, a season was survived, or something that came out of the wild did not reach them.

You have: +10 maximum stamina; +4 wisdom from your ranks so far; Read the Ground, Run It to Ruin, Wear the Wild, Aspect of the Serpent, Aspect of the Oak, and Aspect of the Wolf; resistance to frost damage.

Power, Aspects of the Wild: call an aspect on your ability list in a fight, for mana. It holds until the fight ends, one at a time, and grows with your rank.

From level 30, you can take one Discipline as a level-up pick: Discipline of the Pack or Discipline of the Green.

Next: from level 50, Legend of the Wild as a level-up pick: +5 wisdom and The Weather Turns.

The Path: Path of the Wild (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Wild from level 50). Rank skill counts in survival, tracking, animal handling, nature magic, or shape shifting. Each rank adds 1 to your wisdom.
abilities: Read the Ground
Run It to Ruin
Wear the Wild
Aspect of the Serpent
Aspect of the Oak
Aspect of the Wolf

Novice of the Song.name: Novice of the Song
Novice of the Song.description:
You can read a room and hold it. You know when to start, when to stop, and what a crowd is actually asking for underneath what it says it wants.

You have: +5 maximum mana; +1 charisma from your ranks so far.

Power, the Big Performance and Battle Songs: one big performance can win over a whole room (then about 50 turns before the next), and the battle songs on your ability list lift your whole party in a fight, one song at a time.

Next: Adept of the Song, once you have 15 in performance, persuasion, intimidation, or insight. "Ready for Adept of the Song" appears on your sheet when you do. To become an Adept of the Song, carry a hard occasion: a hostile court, a funeral, a riot on the turn, a mutinous camp, or a crowd that came to see someone else.

The Path: Path of the Song (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Song from level 50). Rank skill counts in performance, persuasion, intimidation, or insight. Each rank adds 1 to your charisma.

Adept of the Song.name: Adept of the Song
Adept of the Song.description:
You have carried an occasion that could have gone badly and did not, because of how you handled it. A room that was going one way went another.

You have: +5 maximum mana; +2 charisma from your ranks so far; Hold the Room and Hymn of the Deep.

Power, the Big Performance and Battle Songs: one big performance can win over a whole room (then about 50 turns before the next), and the battle songs on your ability list lift your whole party in a fight, one song at a time.

Next: Expert of the Song, once you have 25 in performance, persuasion, intimidation, or insight. "Ready for Expert of the Song" appears on your sheet when you do. To become an Expert of the Song, be trusted with something that matters to other people: a story they need told right, a message that must land, a grief that must be given shape, or a peace that depends on how it is said.

The Path: Path of the Song (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Song from level 50). Rank skill counts in performance, persuasion, intimidation, or insight. Each rank adds 1 to your charisma.
abilities: Hold the Room
Hymn of the Deep

Expert of the Song.name: Expert of the Song
Expert of the Song.description:
People hand you their story to carry, knowing you will carry it right. That trust is the whole trade, and it is not given to entertainers.

You have: +10 maximum mana; +3 charisma from your ranks so far; Hold the Room, Turn the Crowd, Hymn of the Deep, and Steady Breath.

Power, the Big Performance and Battle Songs: one big performance can win over a whole room (then about 50 turns before the next), and the battle songs on your ability list lift your whole party in a fight, one song at a time.

From level 30, you can take one Discipline as a level-up pick: Discipline of the Battle-Song or Discipline of the Lullaby.

Next: Master of the Song, once you have 40 in performance, persuasion, intimidation, or insight. "Ready for Master of the Song" appears on your sheet when you do. To become a Master of the Song, make something other performers take up, or move an occasion so completely that people repeat it afterwards.

The Path: Path of the Song (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Song from level 50). Rank skill counts in performance, persuasion, intimidation, or insight. Each rank adds 1 to your charisma.
abilities: Hold the Room
Turn the Crowd
Hymn of the Deep
Steady Breath

Master of the Song.name: Master of the Song
Master of the Song.description:
You are in someone else's repertoire. Performers you have never met know a piece of yours, or a night you carried, and use your name to explain what they are trying to do.

You have: +10 maximum mana; +4 charisma from your ranks so far; Hold the Room, Turn the Crowd, The Voice Between Blades, Hymn of the Deep, Steady Breath, The Deep Well, and Rout; resistance to psychic damage.

Power, the Big Performance and Battle Songs: one big performance can win over a whole room (then about 50 turns before the next), and the battle songs on your ability list lift your whole party in a fight, one song at a time.

From level 30, you can take one Discipline as a level-up pick: Discipline of the Battle-Song or Discipline of the Lullaby.

Next: from level 50, Legend of the Song as a level-up pick: +5 charisma and Everyone Sings.

The Path: Path of the Song (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Song from level 50). Rank skill counts in performance, persuasion, intimidation, or insight. Each rank adds 1 to your charisma.
abilities: Hold the Room
Turn the Crowd
The Voice Between Blades
Hymn of the Deep
Steady Breath
The Deep Well
Rout

Novice of the Work.name: Novice of the Work
Novice of the Work.description:
Your repairs hold and your devices do what you said they would. That sounds small until you meet the many makers of whom it is not true.

You have: +5 maximum stamina; +1 intelligence from your ranks so far.

Power, The Gadget Belt: each gadget on your ability list works once per fight.

Next: Adept of the Work, once you have 15 in engineering, gadgetry, trapcraft, smithing, alchemy, enchanting, carpentry, leatherworking, or tailoring. "Ready for Adept of the Work" appears on your sheet when you do. To become an Adept of the Work, have your work hold when it mattered: under load, in the field, in weather, in a fight, or with someone's life resting on it.

The Path: Path of the Tinker (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Work from level 50). Rank skill counts in engineering, gadgetry, trapcraft, smithing, alchemy, enchanting, carpentry, leatherworking, or tailoring. Each rank adds 1 to your intelligence.

Adept of the Work.name: Adept of the Work
Adept of the Work.description:
Your work held when it mattered, in the field, under load, with consequences attached. You build for the moment it is tested, not for the bench.

You have: +5 maximum stamina; +2 intelligence from your ranks so far; Make It Hold and Spring Shields.

Power, The Gadget Belt: each gadget on your ability list works once per fight.

Next: Expert of the Work, once you have 25 in engineering, gadgetry, trapcraft, smithing, alchemy, enchanting, carpentry, leatherworking, or tailoring. "Ready for Expert of the Work" appears on your sheet when you do. To become an Expert of the Work, be brought dangerous work: a mechanism that has already hurt someone, a device nobody else will touch, a repair that has to hold first time, or a commission with real consequences.

The Path: Path of the Tinker (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Work from level 50). Rank skill counts in engineering, gadgetry, trapcraft, smithing, alchemy, enchanting, carpentry, leatherworking, or tailoring. Each rank adds 1 to your intelligence.
abilities: Make It Hold
Spring Shields

Expert of the Work.name: Expert of the Work
Expert of the Work.description:
People bring you dangerous work because you are the one who will not botch it. The jobs that arrive at your bench are the ones that already went wrong somewhere else.

You have: +10 maximum stamina; +3 intelligence from your ranks so far; Make It Hold, See the Flaw, Spring Shields, and Spark Coil.

Power, The Gadget Belt: each gadget on your ability list works once per fight.

From level 30, you can take one Discipline as a level-up pick: Discipline of the Siege or Discipline of the Snare.

Next: Master of the Work, once you have 40 in engineering, gadgetry, trapcraft, smithing, alchemy, enchanting, carpentry, leatherworking, or tailoring. "Ready for Master of the Work" appears on your sheet when you do. To become a Master of the Work, build or repair something other makers come to study, and be named, commissioned, sought out, or openly acknowledged for it.

Novice of Blood.name: Novice of Blood
Novice of Blood.description:
You have learned the craft's first discipline: it costs, and you pay knowingly. Blood answers, and you have stopped pretending it does not take something back.

You have: +5 maximum health; +1 attunement from your ranks so far.

Power, Blood Calls: spend your own blood in an attack, and your next attack that lands hits at impact 175 and draws health back from a living foe.

Next: Adept of Blood, once you have 15 in blood magic or dagger. "Ready for Adept of Blood" appears on your sheet when you do. To become an Adept of Blood, use the craft under real stakes and stop when you meant to — no slide, no overreach, and nothing taken that you did not intend to take.

Adept of Blood.name: Adept of Blood
Adept of Blood.description:
You used it under real stakes and did not slide. The Gravebound are what happens to people who could not say that, and everyone in this craft knows it.

You have: +5 maximum health; +2 attunement from your ranks so far; Open Vein.

Power, Blood Calls: spend your own blood in an attack, and your next attack that lands hits at impact 200 and draws health back from a living foe.

Next: Expert of Blood, once you have 25 in blood magic or dagger. "Ready for Expert of Blood" appears on your sheet when you do. Power, Blood Calls: spend your own blood in an attack, and your next attack that lands hits at impact 225 and draws back more.

Novice of the Cloak.name: Novice of the Cloak
Novice of the Cloak.description:
You have shown practical competence in quiet work. You are not merely sneaky. You understand how to move, watch, open, follow, listen, retrieve, and leave without turning every problem into a fight.

You have: +5 maximum stamina; +1 dexterity from your ranks so far.

Power, Unseen Strikes: an attack from hiding that rolls a Great Success or better keeps you Hidden and climbs a step of impact; at this rank up to Unseen Strike I (225).

Next: Adept of the Cloak, once you have 15 in stealth, lockpicking, pickpocketing, or acrobatics. "Ready for Adept of the Cloak" appears on your sheet when you do. To become an Adept of the Cloak, complete quiet work cleanly enough that a credible contact, scoutmaster, fixer, handler, League officer, rebel agent, noble agent, guild contact, or underworld patron is willing to put their name behind you.

Adept of the Cloak.description:
Someone credible has put their word behind you. In the quiet trades, that matters more than boasting. A contact, handler, officer, patron, or guild name now says you can be trusted with work that needs proof and discretion.

You have: +5 maximum stamina; +2 dexterity from your ranks so far; Melt Away.

Power, Unseen Strikes: an attack from hiding that rolls a Great Success or better keeps you Hidden and climbs a step of impact; at this rank up to Unseen Strike II (250).

Next: Expert of the Cloak, once you have 25 in stealth, lockpicking, pickpocketing, or acrobatics. "Ready for Expert of the Cloak" appears on your sheet when you do. Path of the Vessel.name: Path of the Vessel
Path of the Vessel.description:
You are learning to channel magic through your body and will. In Larion, the vessel is the capacity of body and will that lets someone safely carry magic. This Path covers studied mages, bloodline casters, pact-bound spellworkers, hedge witches, temple miracle-workers, spirit-carriers, druids, clerics, and anyone whose power depends on disciplined internal capacity.

You have: +2 lore and +1 attunement; Steady Overchannel.

Power, Overchannel: use your strongest Overchannel ability on a spell for more power. It costs extra mana unless the casting is a Great Success, and a failure burns you.

Next: Novice of the Vessel, open to anyone on this Path. To pursue Novice rank, first declare a concrete magical feat before attempting it, explicitly naming Novice of the Vessel as the rank you seek. Enact the declaration as a vow, promise, pledge, or sworn undertaking to a god, master, witness, spirit, institution, or yourself. Name the working, a meaningful limit or pressure, and a clear success condition. A suitable Novice feat deliberately tests controlled magical capacity; for example, swear to hold a ward steady through a dangerous disturbance without letting its force touch those inside. Ordinary spellcasting, study, or surviving by luck does not count: the working must keep the limit you declared.

The Path: Path of the Vessel (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Vessel from level 50). Rank skill counts in a school of magic, divine channeling, or spirit channeling. Each rank adds 1 to your attunement.
abilities: Steady Overchannel

Vowed Vessel Feat.name: Vowed Vessel Feat
Vowed Vessel Feat.description: You have deliberately vowed to complete a specific magical feat as proof that you are ready to advance on the Path of the Vessel. The feat must be completed as declared, including its named pressure, limits, and success condition. This undertaking remains until it is fulfilled or you explicitly relinquish it. Relinquish the current undertaking before declaring a different one.

Novice of the Vessel.name: Novice of the Vessel
Novice of the Vessel.description:
You have deliberately carried or shaped magic under a declared limit and maintained enough control to fulfill the feat exactly as vowed. You have begun to understand magical capacity as something practiced from within rather than merely spent.

You have: +5 maximum mana; +1 attunement from your ranks so far.

Power, Overchannel: use your strongest Overchannel ability on a spell for more power. It costs extra mana unless the casting is a Great Success, and a failure burns you.

Next: Adept of the Vessel, once you have 15 in a school of magic, divine channeling, or spirit channeling. "Ready for Adept of the Vessel" appears on your sheet when you do. To pursue Adept rank, first vow a feat that explicitly names Adept of the Vessel as the rank you seek and sustains a named magical working safely under meaningful pressure. Declare the working, the pressure or limitation, what control requires, and a clear success condition before attempting it. For example, swear to maintain a healing current through pain and distraction without allowing it to falter or draw strength from the patient. Routine casting, a finished lesson, or praise does not count: you must sustain the working under pressure within your limit.

The Path: Path of the Vessel (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Vessel from level 50). Rank skill counts in a school of magic, divine channeling, or spirit channeling. Each rank adds 1 to your attunement.

Adept of the Vessel.name: Adept of the Vessel
Adept of the Vessel.description:
You have sustained a deliberate magical working under pressure while preserving the control you promised. You can distinguish strain from failure and adjust how power moves through body and will before it escapes you.

You have: +5 maximum mana; +2 attunement from your ranks so far; Hold the Spell and Deep Overchannel.

Power, Overchannel: use your strongest Overchannel ability on a spell for more power. It costs extra mana unless the casting is a Great Success, and a failure burns you.

Next: Expert of the Vessel, once you have 25 in a school of magic, divine channeling, or spirit channeling. "Ready for Expert of the Vessel" appears on your sheet when you do. To pursue Expert rank, first vow a difficult magical feat that explicitly names Expert of the Vessel as the rank you seek and takes place under serious adverse conditions. Declare the working, the opposition or strain, what must remain controlled or protected, and a clear success condition. For example, swear to close a hostile breach while wounded without allowing its magic to strike anyone behind you. Surviving strain or recovering afterward does not count: you must keep control through it.

The Path: Path of the Vessel (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Vessel from level 50). Rank skill counts in a school of magic, divine channeling, or spirit channeling. Each rank adds 1 to your attunement.

Expert of the Vessel.name: Expert of the Vessel
Expert of the Vessel.description:
You have controlled difficult magic through serious opposition or strain while preserving what you vowed to protect. Your capacity is expressed through discipline: pressure can rise without deciding the shape of the working for you.

You have: +10 maximum mana; +3 attunement from your ranks so far; Hold the Spell, Wear the Working, Full Overchannel, and Deep Overchannel.

Power, Overchannel: use your strongest Overchannel ability on a spell for more power. It costs extra mana unless the casting is a Great Success, and a failure burns you.

From level 30, you can take one Discipline as a level-up pick: Discipline of the Anchor, Discipline of the Conduit, or Discipline of the Crucible.

Next: Master of the Vessel, once you have 40 in a school of magic, divine channeling, or spirit channeling. "Ready for Master of the Vessel" appears on your sheet when you do. To pursue Master rank, first vow a large, complex, or opposed magical capstone that explicitly names Master of the Vessel as the rank you seek. Declare the exceptional stakes, an exacting limit on control or harm, and a decisive success condition worthy of a life's discipline. For example, swear to bind a raging ley rupture before dawn without letting its force take a life or permanently scar the surrounding land. Recognition or surviving great power does not count: the working must keep the exact limit you vowed.

The Path: Path of the Vessel (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Vessel from level 50). Rank skill counts in a school of magic, divine channeling, or spirit channeling. Each rank adds 1 to your attunement.

Master of the Vessel.name: Master of the Vessel
Master of the Vessel.description:
You have completed an exceptional magical undertaking while holding power to an exacting limit and preserving control through extreme stakes. Great capacity no longer means surrendering the shape or consequence of the working.

You have: +10 maximum mana; +4 attunement from your ranks so far; Hold the Spell, Wear the Working, Two Spells at Once, Great Overchannel, Deep Overchannel, and Full Overchannel; resistance to arcane damage.

Power, Overchannel: use your strongest Overchannel ability on a spell for more power. It costs extra mana unless the casting is a Great Success, and a failure burns you.

Discipline of the Anchor.name: Discipline of the Anchor
Discipline of the Anchor.description: You specialize in making magic briefly solid enough to bear physical consequence. This permanent Expert specialization grants +5 warding magic and makes Give Magic Weight available for purchase with ability points.

Discipline of the Conduit.name: Discipline of the Conduit
Discipline of the Conduit.description: You specialize in carrying magical force cleanly from one point of impact to another. This permanent Expert specialization grants +5 lore and makes The Second Arc available for purchase with ability points.

Discipline of the Crucible.name: Discipline of the Crucible
Discipline of the Crucible.description: You specialize in containing and refining magic until its original form burns away. This permanent Expert specialization grants +20 maximum mana and makes Naked Magic available for purchase with ability points.

Path of the Oath.name: Path of the Oath
Path of the Oath.description:
You are bound to a vow, order, god, cause, or sacred duty. This path covers temple guardians, sworn healers, paladins, exorcists, holy knights, and grim protectors who draw strength from what they have promised.

You have: +2 leadership and +1 charisma.

Power, Shelter: a Great Success or better on a blow or a guard in a fight heals the whole party by 25 and gives you Bulwark I.

Next: Novice of the Oath, open to anyone on this Path. To become a Novice of the Oath, swear, renew, accept, or dedicate yourself to a solemn vow before a sacred witness: a temple, shrine, chapel, holy order, grave, community, god, saint, spirit, or power.

The Path: Path of the Oath (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Oath from level 50). Rank skill counts in divine magic, divine channeling, healing magic, leadership, or shield. Each rank adds 1 to your charisma.

Novice of the Oath.name: Novice of the Oath
Novice of the Oath.description:
You have made or renewed a vow before a sacred witness, sworn order, community, shrine, temple, grave, or power. Your word has weight now, and breaking it should matter.

You have: +5 maximum health; +1 charisma from your ranks so far.

Power, Shelter: a Great Success or better on a blow or a guard in a fight heals the whole party by 25 and gives you Bulwark I.

Next: Adept of the Oath, once you have 15 in divine magic, divine channeling, healing magic, leadership, or shield. "Ready for Adept of the Oath" appears on your sheet when you do. To become an Adept of the Oath, uphold your vow under pressure, then report, pray over, present proof of, ask judgment about, or receive recognition for the deed from someone or something that matters.

The Path: Path of the Oath (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Oath from level 50). Rank skill counts in divine magic, divine channeling, healing magic, leadership, or shield. Each rank adds 1 to your charisma.

Adept of the Oath.name: Adept of the Oath
Adept of the Oath.description:
Your vow has been tested by action. Someone or something that matters has recognized that you kept faith when it would have been easier to turn away.

You have: +5 maximum health; +2 charisma from your ranks so far; Between Them and Harm.

Power, Shelter: a Great Success or better on a blow or a guard in a fight heals the whole party by 35 and gives you Bulwark I.

Next: Expert of the Oath, once you have 25 in divine magic, divine channeling, healing magic, leadership, or shield. "Ready for Expert of the Oath" appears on your sheet when you do. To become an Expert of the Oath, accept greater sacred duty from a temple, shrine, holy order, priest, paladin, village, rescued community, sacred witness, or oath-bound authority.

The Path: Path of the Oath (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Oath from level 50). Expert of the Oath.description:

The Path: Path of the Oath (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Oath from level 50). Master of the Oath.name: Master of the Oath
Master of the Oath.description:
You are known as a living example of your vow. When corruption spreads, the dead stir, fiends walk, or frightened people need someone to stand firm, your name may be spoken as an answer.

You have: +10 maximum health; +4 charisma from your ranks so far; Between Them and Harm, Lamp of the Vow, and Every Oath Kept; resistance to shadow damage.

Power, Shelter: a Great Success or better on a blow or a guard in a fight heals the whole party by 75 and gives you Bulwark III.

From level 30, you can take one Discipline as a level-up pick: Discipline of the Shelter or Discipline of Judgment.

Next: from level 50, Legend of the Oath as a level-up pick: +5 charisma and Not While I Stand.

The Path: Path of the Oath (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Oath from level 50). Rank skill counts in divine magic, divine channeling, healing magic, leadership, or shield. Each rank adds 1 to your charisma.
abilities: Between Them and Harm
Lamp of the Vow
Every Oath Kept

Path of the Wild.name: Path of the Wild
Path of the Wild.description:
You are trained to live with the wild world rather than merely pass through it. This path covers rangers, druids, beast-speakers, wardens, herbalists, trackers, and wanderers who know that every forest, marsh, hill, and desert has rules.

You have: +2 survival and +1 wisdom; Aspect of the Hawk and Aspect of the Bear.

Power, Aspects of the Wild: call an aspect on your ability list in a fight, for mana. It holds until the fight ends, one at a time, and grows with your rank.

Next: Novice of the Wild, open to anyone on this Path. To become a Novice of the Wild, live with wild country rather than passing through it: read weather before it arrives, choose a camp or route that works, forage or shelter through a bad night, or handle terrain that would have stopped an untrained traveller.

The Path: Path of the Wild (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Wild from level 50). Rank skill counts in survival, tracking, animal handling, nature magic, or shape shifting. Each rank adds 1 to your wisdom.
abilities: Aspect of the Hawk
Aspect of the Bear

Path of the Song.name: Path of the Song
Path of the Song.description:
You are trained to move hearts, steady allies, twist a room, carry stories, and turn performance into power. This path covers bards, heralds, court players, tavern heroes, battle-singers, and silver-tongued wanderers.

You have: +2 performance and +1 charisma; March of Iron and Quickstep Reel.

Power, the Big Performance and Battle Songs: one big performance can win over a whole room (then about 50 turns before the next), and the battle songs on your ability list lift your whole party in a fight, one song at a time.

Next: Novice of the Song, open to anyone on this Path. To become a Novice of the Song, read a room and turn it: start, stop, or shift a performance, speech, toast, story, or song so that the mood of the people present visibly changes.

The Path: Path of the Song (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Song from level 50). Rank skill counts in performance, persuasion, intimidation, or insight. Each rank adds 1 to your charisma.
abilities: March of Iron
Quickstep Reel

Path of the Tinker.name: Path of the Tinker
Path of the Tinker.description:
You are trained to solve problems with tools, craft, alchemy, small devices, traps, repairs, and clever hands. This path covers tinkers, artificers, smiths, alchemists, siege-workers, locksmiths, and practical makers.

You have: +2 engineering and +1 intelligence; Smoke Pot and Patch Kit.

Power, The Gadget Belt: each gadget on your ability list works once per fight.

Next: Novice of the Work, open to anyone on this Path. To become a Novice of the Work, make or repair something that then does exactly what you said it would: a device that works, a lock that opens, a mechanism that runs, or a repair that holds under use.

The Path: Path of the Tinker (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Work from level 50). Rank skill counts in engineering, gadgetry, trapcraft, smithing, alchemy, enchanting, carpentry, leatherworking, or tailoring. Each rank adds 1 to your intelligence.
abilities: Smoke Pot
Patch Kit

Path of the Will.name: Path of the Will
Path of the Will.description:
You are learning to make breath, balance, attention, and motion answer as one. This path covers monks, disciplined fighters, ascetics, meditative healers, bodyguards, climbers, and anyone who treats control as a craft rather than a mood. The Sky Temple of the Ascension in Redrock is one place where outsiders may learn the deeper work, but the Path is not owned by one monastery.

You have: +2 acrobatics and +1 dexterity.

Power, The Center: each defence or evade of yours that lands in a fight climbs a step of protection and impact; at this rank up to Centered.

Next: Novice of the Will, open to anyone on this Path. To become a Novice of the Will, find stillness and control deliberately — breath, balance, or attention — at a moment when it is difficult, and have it hold.

The Path: Path of the Will (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of the Will from level 50). Rank skill counts in unarmed combat, acrobatics, athletics, psionics, or staff. Each rank adds 1 to your dexterity.

Path of Blood.name: Path of Blood
Path of Blood.description:
You are learning the disciplined art of blood, pulse, pain, and blade-work. The Bloodhunters of the Red Chantry teach that blood is a dangerous craft to master and a duty to turn against the dead; this Path is distinct from the Gravebound, the corrupted offshoot that raises and binds the dead.

You have: +2 blood magic and +1 attunement.

Power, Blood Calls: spend your own blood in an attack, and your next attack that lands hits at impact 175 and draws health back from a living foe.

Next: Novice of Blood, open to anyone on this Path. To become a Novice of Blood, use blood, pulse, pain, or blade-discipline knowingly and pay its cost deliberately rather than being surprised by it.

The Path: Path of Blood (a level-up pick from level 5) → Novice → Adept (skill 15) → Expert (skill 25; a Discipline from level 30) → Master (skill 40; Legend of Blood from level 50). Rank skill counts in blood magic or dagger. Each rank adds 1 to your attunement.

Shaman.name: Shaman
Shaman.description:
Main Attributes: Attunement, Wisdom, and Constitution

Shamans deal with the unseen inhabitants of the world. Spirits gather in wind and flame, earth and water, old roads, homes, battlefields, treasured objects, strong memories, and the honored dead. They are not gods, and they are not creatures dragged from elsewhere and bound like conjured servants. They have their own natures, desires, loyalties, and grudges.

A shaman learns to perceive them, address them, bargain for their aid, ward against them, challenge them, and sometimes welcome them into the body. Every shaman gradually gathers a spirit court: the ancestors and other powers that know their name and may answer when called. A novice has only a few such relationships. A great shaman can open the way for many spirits to act together.

In danger, spirits strike through wind, flame, stone, water, weapon, and voice. They guard boundaries, expose what is hidden, lend their nature to a shaman's body, and take form beside the living. Spirit Magic is not Conjuration: conjurers call and bind creatures from elsewhere, while shamans deal with spirits connected to this world and must reckon with why they answer.

Special Starting Gear: Spirit Mask
abilities: Soulstrike
Second Wind
Draw Power
Let a Spirit In
Shaman.traitNarrativeEffects: A shaman is a spirit-worker who can see and speak with the unseen inhabitants of the world: spirits of places, objects, and elements; ancestors; and presences born from powerful memories. They read the signs spirits leave, learn their wants and taboos, and win their aid through respect, offerings, shared purpose, leverage, or bargains. A shaman’s spirit court is the circle of named spirits that have chosen lasting bonds with them and may answer when called. A spirit enters that court through a bond formed in the character’s past or during play. After a meaningful victory or discovery, a local spirit may make its notice concrete—a voice from an object, an element taking a face, an ancestor stepping into view—leaving the player to approach, answer, or walk away. If a lasting bond forms, the spirit may mark it with a physical token.

Spirit Magic.name: Spirit Magic
Spirit Magic.description: You can perceive and address spirits connected to ancestors, elements, places, objects, and strong memories. You can bargain for their intervention, ward against hostile influence, and build relationships with spirits that may answer you again. Spirit Magic uses Attunement.
abilities: The Deed Walks

Prizefighter.name: Prizefighter
Prizefighter.description: A recognized Prizefighter on the Grand Arena Circuit, proven capable of drawing a crowd and completing sanctioned bouts for real purses.
Prizefighter.traitNarrativeEffects: Arena officials, promoters, bettors, and fighting crowds recognize this character as a Prizefighter and offer established professional bouts rather than debuts.

Arena Contender.name: Arena Contender
Arena Contender.description: A proven Contender on the Grand Arena Circuit, trusted with difficult marquee bouts and able to earn a challenge for a local championship.

Arena Contender.traitNarrativeEffects: Arena officials and promoters recognize this character as a serious Contender whose matches deserve skilled opposition, substantial purses, and a path toward championship bouts.

Circuit Champion.name: Circuit Champion
Circuit Champion.description: A Champion who has won at least one formally declared title at an eligible Grand Arena Circuit venue.
Circuit Champion.traitNarrativeEffects: Crowds, promoters, patrons, fighting schools, and other competitors recognize this character as a circuit Champion. Other eligible venues may offer championship challenges and marquee purses.

Grand Champion of the Arenas.name: Grand Champion of the Arenas
Grand Champion of the Arenas.description: The victor of the Grand Champion's Contest at the Field of Valor, holding the highest recognized standing on Larion's Grand Arena Circuit.
abilities: Finishing Blow
Grand Champion of the Arenas.traitNarrativeEffects: Throughout Larion, arena officials, crowds, patrons, and fighting schools recognize this character as Grand Champion of the Arenas, entitled to headline, choose challengers, command the greatest purses, or establish a stable.

Initiate of the Silver Sword.name: Initiate of the Silver Sword
Initiate of the Silver Sword.description: A candidate of the Order of the Silver Sword undertaking a supervised trial hunt. An Initiate belongs to the Order but has not yet been sworn as a Silverblade, and carries neither an Order horn nor Order silver.
Initiate of the Silver Sword.traitNarrativeEffects: Members of the Order recognize this character as an Initiate under a Veteran Silverblade. They may undertake a supervised trial hunt, but cannot claim independent Order contracts or Silverblade authority. An Initiate is sworn as a Silverblade only at Taking the Silver in the Great Hall at Castle Harstone, after one supervised trial hunt, where they swear the Order's oath and receive an Order horn and Order silver. Not yet.

Silverblade.name: Silverblade
Silverblade.description: A full sworn member of the Order of the Silver Sword, sworn at Castle Harstone after a supervised trial hunt. A Silverblade carries an Order horn handed down from a fallen hunter and may take monster contracts independently.
Silverblade.traitNarrativeEffects: Order members, knowledgeable monster-hunters, and those who know the Order horn recognize this character as a full Silverblade trusted with independent monster contracts. Veteran rank is named only at Tempering the Silver in the Great Hall at Castle Harstone, after four recognized hunts as a Silverblade. Not yet.

Veteran Silverblade.name: Veteran Silverblade
Veteran Silverblade.description: A proven senior hunter of the Order of the Silver Sword, trusted to lead difficult hunts, supervise Initiates, attest trial hunts, and direct junior Silverblades in the field.
abilities: Find the Seam
Veteran Silverblade.traitNarrativeEffects: The Order recognizes this character as a Veteran Silverblade with authority to lead difficult hunts, supervise Initiates, attest trials, and direct less experienced hunters. Masters of the Hunt are raised only at Mastering the Silver in the Great Hall at Castle Harstone, after five recognized hunts as a Veteran. Not yet.

Master of the Hunt.name: Master of the Hunt
Master of the Hunt.description: A Master of the Hunt of the Order of the Silver Sword, seated at the high table in Castle Harstone's Great Hall. Masters judge admissions and promotions, give out the hunts too grave for the open board, may call Silverblades to ride under them, and keep the Hornwall.
abilities: Silver Dust

They haven't joined a College yet: the Colleges claim the First-Years at Colors Night, at the end of the First Year, after three Practica and a year-end mission. Not yet.

Second-Year Student.name: Second-Year Student
