Win a Sponsor.questStatement: Only the Black Gate makes a lord, and no aspirant passes it without a house spending its name on them in front of its rivals. Find something a house needs badly enough that an outsider holding a valley becomes the cheaper problem, do it, and have a lord announce your sponsorship in the Hall of Witnesses at the Black Gate.
Win a Sponsor.mainObjective: Earn a house's sponsorship and have it announced at the Hall of Witnesses

completionCondition.query: A vampire lord or house of the Shadow Summits has formally sponsored the party as an aspirant at the Black Gate, announced before the other houses in the Hall of Witnesses. Do not match a private promise, a lord merely expressing interest, an offer conditional on work not yet done, or a sponsorship discussed anywhere other than the Hall of Witnesses.

Graduate from Tarnholme.name: Graduate from Tarnholme
Graduate from Tarnholme.questStatement: Finish three Fourth-Year Practica, then pass the Final Trial. At Commencement on the Muster Court, graduates swear the oath and leave Tarnholme as mages.
Graduate from Tarnholme.mainObjective: Finish three Practica, pass the Final Trial, and graduate at Commencement

completionCondition.query: A party member swears the oath and graduates at Commencement on the Muster Court.

The Black Fortress.name: The Black Fortress
The Black Fortress.questStatement: For the League of Adventurers: the Black Fortress at the heart of burned Gesenthame still stands shut under the Azhakid princes' fire-wards, which burn whoever forces the gates, and the Church of the Pyre is close to breaking them for the princes' burning crowns. A jackalkin dig-boss who has watched every attempt from the ruins knows where the wards are weakest. Get through the wards and into the fortress before the Pyre does, and keep the crowns out of the Church's hands.
The Black Fortress.mainObjective: The party is inside the Black Fortress, and the Church of the Pyre does not get the Azhakid crowns.

completionCondition.query: The party has completed the legendary deed The Black Fortress: The party is inside the Black Fortress, and the Church of the Pyre does not get the Azhakid crowns.

The White Eye.name: The White Eye
The White Eye.questStatement: For the Order of the Silver Sword, the monster-hunters of Castle Harstone: the White Eye, eldest of the ice drakes of the White Wyrmspire, has outlived every hunter who ever climbed against it and now hunts the north road itself, one sled-team at a time. The frost giants of Whitefang Hold will send their best hunter to climb with the party. Kill the White Eye, or beat it so badly it never comes down to the road again.
The White Eye.mainObjective: The White Eye is dead, or so badly beaten that it abandons the north road for good.

completionCondition.query: The party has completed the legendary deed The White Eye: The White Eye is dead, or so badly beaten that it abandons the north road for good.

The Old Bull Beithir.name: The Old Bull Beithir
The Old Bull Beithir.questStatement: For the Order of the Silver Sword, the monster-hunters of Castle Harstone: the oldest bull beithir anyone at Dun Beithir has seen has come up the lake to the cutting ice, a cold sea-serpent grown far too big for the village's harpoon-lines, and it takes fishers through the ice every week. The harpoon-mistress who leads the village hunt will put every line and hand at the party's command. Kill it, or drive it back to the open sea for good.
The Old Bull Beithir.mainObjective: The old bull beithir is dead or driven back to the open sea.

completionCondition.query: The party has completed the legendary deed The Old Bull Beithir: The old bull beithir is dead or driven back to the open sea.

The Frozen Colossus.name: The Frozen Colossus
The Frozen Colossus.questStatement: For the League of Adventurers: the Frozen Colossus, greatest of the coldstone guardians left by the builders of the white city, has turned its head a hand's width in a month, and the ice is cracking for miles around it. A meticulous dwarf loremaster camped at its feet says it has a heartbeat now, slow as the seasons and getting faster. Climb into the cracks at its chest and put it back to sleep, or bring it down before it rises and walks.
The Frozen Colossus.mainObjective: The Frozen Colossus is put back to sleep or destroyed before it wakes and walks.

completionCondition.query: The party has completed the legendary deed The Frozen Colossus: The Frozen Colossus is put back to sleep or destroyed before it wakes and walks.

The Mother of Serpents.name: The Mother of Serpents
The Mother of Serpents.questStatement: For the Order of the Silver Sword, the monster-hunters of Castle Harstone: the Mother of Serpents, the pearl-white serpent as big as a fleet, has turned on the southern shipping lanes since a harpoon was left festering behind her crest, and three ships went down this season. The hunting houses of Coriva want her gone from the lanes. An old harpooner who has watched her spare whole crews swears that drawing the barb would calm her. Make her leave the lanes, by the barb or by force.
The Mother of Serpents.mainObjective: The Mother of Serpents no longer hunts the shipping lanes.

completionCondition.query: The party has completed the legendary deed The Mother of Serpents: The Mother of Serpents no longer hunts the shipping lanes.

The Door in the Third Pyramid.name: The Door in the Third Pyramid
The Door in the Third Pyramid.questStatement: For the League of Adventurers: the New Sun has dug the broken Third Pyramid down to the door of a Sun King's burial chamber, and the dead across the necropolis stir with every blow of their picks. A quiet goliath dig-foreman among the converts has begun to doubt and could help turn the dig. Stop the door from opening, or if it opens, face the god-king who walks out before he goes to claim his kingdom.
The Door in the Third Pyramid.mainObjective: The burial chamber in the Third Pyramid stays shut, or the Sun King who woke there is destroyed.

completionCondition.query: The party has completed the legendary deed The Door in the Third Pyramid: The burial chamber in the Third Pyramid stays shut, or the Sun King who woke there is destroyed.

The Laughing Jarl.name: The Laughing Jarl
The Laughing Jarl.questStatement: For the League of Adventurers: the Laughing Jarl, the rogue storm giant who holds Storm Crag, breaks bridges, crushes caravans and sets the dwarf clans of Highheath at each other's throats for his own amusement. An envoy of the stone giants, still battered from her own failed climb, wants him ended and will tell the party everything she learned. Kill him, drive him off the mountain, or beat him at his own game; he bargains in bad faith, and he laughs loudest right before he kills.
The Laughing Jarl.mainObjective: The Laughing Jarl is dead, driven from Storm Crag, or beaten at his own game and bound to leave the clans alone.

completionCondition.query: The party has completed the legendary deed The Laughing Jarl: The Laughing Jarl is dead, driven from Storm Crag, or beaten at his own game and bound to leave the clans alone.

The Old One of the Crags.name: The Old One of the Crags
The Old One of the Crags.questStatement: For the Order of the Silver Sword, the monster-hunters of Castle Harstone: the old troll of the Argenval Crags, the ancient one Argenval's tribute was always meant for, has woken hungry since the town stopped paying, and silver no longer bites the trolls bred in that silver-veined rock. The tribute-shrine's last keeper will show the way up past the trow-warren to its den. End the Old One, or drive it so deep into the crags it never comes down again.
The Old One of the Crags.mainObjective: The Old One is dead or driven deep into the crags for good, and Argenval owes it nothing.

completionCondition.query: The party has completed the legendary deed The Old One of the Crags: The Old One is dead or driven deep into the crags for good, and Argenval owes it nothing.

The Behemoth of the Greatwild.name: The Behemoth of the Greatwild
The Behemoth of the Greatwild.questStatement: For the Order of the Silver Sword, the monster-hunters of Castle Harstone: a behemoth the size of a hill has come down out of the deep jungle to wallow on the Open River's sandbars, crushing every boat that passes, and the river is the only road through Ntar Vanna. A monkeyfolk river-raider who has outrun it twice knows where it feeds. Kill it, or turn it back to the deep jungle for good.
The Behemoth of the Greatwild.mainObjective: The behemoth is dead or has gone back into the deep jungle, and the Open River is passable again.

completionCondition.query: The party has completed the legendary deed The Behemoth of the Greatwild: The behemoth is dead or has gone back into the deep jungle, and the Open River is passable again.

The Pens at the Brood-Mounds.name: The Pens at the Brood-Mounds
The Pens at the Brood-Mounds.questStatement: For the League of Adventurers: the lizardfolk of the Reedmoot Fens have taken a whole fen village and penned them at the Dragon-Brood Mounds to be fed to the drakes at the great feast. The captives are kept alive until then. A marsh-guide whose whole family is in the pens will lead the party in by the reed paths. Every warrior, priest-king and drake on the mounds will rise at the first alarm. Bring everyone home.
The Pens at the Brood-Mounds.mainObjective: The captives from the pens at the Dragon-Brood Mounds are brought out of the Fens alive.

completionCondition.query: The party has completed the legendary deed The Pens at the Brood-Mounds: The captives from the pens at the Dragon-Brood Mounds are brought out of the Fens alive.

What the Sea Keeps.name: What the Sea Keeps
What the Sea Keeps.questStatement: For the League of Adventurers: the drowned of the deep kingdoms took a whole crew down alive at Manywrecks for touching a wreck, and by their law what the sea takes, the sea keeps. A shipwright widow who will not believe her crew is dead wants them back. Bargain with the drowned, outwit them, or take the crew back by force.
What the Sea Keeps.mainObjective: The taken crew is brought back up alive.

completionCondition.query: The party has completed the legendary deed What the Sea Keeps: The taken crew is brought back up alive.

Lady Sable.name: Lady Sable
Lady Sable.questStatement: For the Order of the Silver Sword, the monster-hunters of Castle Harstone: the vampire lords walled up the Vale Sable when its house went feral, and strigoi packs have held it ever since under the ancient, mindless Lady Sable in her inner keep. A priest-warden of the lords, ashamed of the sealed pass, will open it for hunters who mean to finish what the lords would not. End Lady Sable and break the packs.
Lady Sable.mainObjective: Lady Sable is destroyed and the strigoi packs of the vale are broken.

completionCondition.query: The party has completed the legendary deed Lady Sable: Lady Sable is destroyed and the strigoi packs of the vale are broken.

A Place at the Table.name: A Place at the Table
A Place at the Table.questStatement:
Tybalt and his friends have been banned from Greenwood Lodge on Ducal Hill after he laughed at an insult to their host. Go with him and help him put things right so his friends can return.

Reward: 80 florins from Tybalt and a standing invitation to join his company.

Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition.
A Place at the Table.mainObjective: Help Tybalt settle the quarrel and get his friends welcomed back to Greenwood Lodge.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter A Place at the Table has been resolved: After the player helps Tybalt address the quarrel, the host explicitly welcomes his friends back to Greenwood Lodge with no apology or other condition still outstanding. If the host says they may return AFTER Tybalt does something, that condition must actually be fulfilled and the host must then confirm they are welcome. An agreement to apologize later, a plan, Tybalt's unsupported claim, or merely attending does not complete the matter. Do not count a fabricated claim.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. When it fits, the people involved acknowledge the actual outcome and remind the participants that Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill can recognize their service. Do not force an immediate return or grant a title yet.

A Place at the Table.questDesignBrief:
Tybalt laughed when a friend insulted their host at Greenwood Lodge; now his whole company is unwelcome, including innocent friends. He has asked Dalia to introduce someone who can help him repair the quarrel. Meet Tybalt, hear him out, and help him secure another invitation for his friends. He comes with you and must address his own behavior. Dalia offers an introduction, not a claim that you are uniquely qualified; she mentions your reputation only if established. 80 florins from Tybalt and a standing invitation to join his company. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of helping mend a quarrel within the household.

Completion details: After the player helps Tybalt address the quarrel, the host explicitly welcomes his friends back to Greenwood Lodge with no apology or other condition still outstanding. If the host says they may return AFTER Tybalt does something, that condition must actually be fulfilled and the host must then confirm they are welcome. An agreement to apologize later, a plan, Tybalt's unsupported claim, or merely attending does not complete the matter.

A Partner for Peregrine.name: A Partner for Peregrine
A Partner for Peregrine.questStatement:
Peregrine needs a new partner after insulting his last one. Join him at the Coronet Club on Ducal Hill and win one doubles fencing match. Bouts use blunted blades and scored touches; winning the whole tournament is optional.

Reward: 90 florins in match winnings for the player and an invitation to practice with Peregrine.

Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition.
A Partner for Peregrine.mainObjective: Win one doubles fencing match with Peregrine.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter A Partner for Peregrine has been resolved: The player and Peregrine enter the doubles fencing tournament as partners and win at least one match together. Do not count practice, an intention, merely entering, or a fabricated claim.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. When it fits, the people involved acknowledge the actual outcome and remind the participants that Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill can recognize their service. Do not force an immediate return or grant a title yet.

A Partner for Peregrine.questDesignBrief:
Peregrine Ashcombe, a brilliant but insufferable young noble, needs a partner for the Coronet Club's next doubles fencing tournament. His last partner walked out after one insult too many, so he asked Dalia to find a replacement. Meet him, enter together, and win a match. The bouts use blunted blades and end on scored touches. He criticizes your footwork but fights fiercely beside you, driving opponents back and breaking their attacks when they corner you. Winning the whole tournament is optional. 90 florins in match winnings for the player and an invitation to practice with Peregrine. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of helping a court household compete. Peregrine privately needs the prize money to support his old servants; reveal this through interaction, not in the public offer.

Completion details: The player and Peregrine enter the doubles fencing tournament as partners and win at least one match together.

Borrowed Brilliance.name: Borrowed Brilliance
Borrowed Brilliance.questStatement:
An attendant at the Coronet Club on Ducal Hill is accused of stealing a jeweled clasp. Find and return it, and get its owner to withdraw the accusation before the attendant loses their job.

Reward: 70 florins from the grateful owner and admission as a guest at the Coronet Club.

Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition.
Borrowed Brilliance.mainObjective: Return the clasp and clear the attendant’s name.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter Borrowed Brilliance has been resolved: The owner receives the missing clasp and explicitly withdraws the accusation against the attendant. Do not count locating the clasp alone, a promise to return it, or a fabricated claim.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. When it fits, the people involved acknowledge the actual outcome and remind the participants that Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill can recognize their service. Do not force an immediate return or grant a title yet.

Borrowed Brilliance.questDesignBrief:
A jeweled clasp has disappeared at the Coronet Club. Its owner accuses an attendant of stealing it and demands their dismissal. The attendant has asked Dalia for help. Visit the club, question the guests, find the clasp, and clear the attendant's name. Fifi Dauvigne, a mischievous young noble, is among the guests; she wears a clasp suspiciously like the missing one. 70 florins from the grateful owner and admission as a guest at the Coronet Club. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of clearing the attendant's name. Fifi took the clasp. When confronted she tries an outrageous excuse, then realizes the attendant could lose their livelihood and seeks help putting it right. She prefers to avoid a public confession. Allow a private admission and return, persuasion to confess, or public exposure; her response depends on how the player treats her. Do not disclose the culprit in the herald’s offer.

Completion details: The owner receives the missing clasp and explicitly withdraws the accusation against the attendant.

The Wager on Lucan.name: The Wager on Lucan
The Wager on Lucan.questStatement:
A dire wolf is attacking woodcutters. Meet Lucan Valcourt at the Coronet Club on Ducal Hill, then hunt it together from the Woodsman’s Hut in the Wolvesholt Range. Kill it, capture it, or drive it somewhere it cannot threaten the settlement.

Reward: 90 florins from the ducal household and an invitation to fence or hunt with Lucan.

Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition.
The Wager on Lucan.mainObjective: Hunt with Lucan and stop the dire wolf’s attacks.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Wager on Lucan has been resolved: With Lucan participating in the hunt, the party stops the dire wolf's attacks by killing it, securely capturing it, or driving it somewhere it cannot threaten the settlement. Do not count merely frightening it away for a night, moving the danger onto other people, a promise, or a fabricated claim.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. When it fits, the people involved acknowledge the actual outcome and remind the participants that Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill can recognize their service. Do not force an immediate return or grant a title yet.

The Wager on Lucan.questDesignBrief:
Lucan Valcourt, the duke's younger son, has asked Dalia for capable hunting companions. A dire wolf is attacking woodcutters on his family's land at the edge of the Wolvesholt Range. Meet Lucan at the Coronet Club, then track it from the Woodsman's Hut and stop its attacks together. Courtiers are betting he will fail; one offers you money to bring him home before he succeeds. Lucan wants to learn, takes his share of the fighting, and protects companions in danger. 90 florins from the ducal household and an invitation to fence or hunt with Lucan. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of protecting the woodcutters. Lucan intercepts charges, tears open a flank with rapid sword strikes, and fights his way to companions in trouble. His usual strengthening draughts let him fight effectively; do not turn this hunt into babysitting. The bet is optional social friction, not a second completion requirement.

Completion details: With Lucan participating in the hunt, the party stops the dire wolf's attacks by killing it, securely capturing it, or driving it somewhere it cannot threaten the settlement.

Who May Ride the Wood?.name: Who May Ride the Wood?
Who May Ride the Wood?.questStatement:
A lord has blocked the road villagers use to reach their homes. Meet Ciara Valcourt at the Palace on Ducal Hill and ride out together. Get the road reopened for regular use through an agreement or ruling; pulling down the gate alone will not settle it.

Reward: 100 florins from the ducal household and access to the household stables for local rides.

Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition.
Who May Ride the Wood?.mainObjective: Help Ciara secure regular access to the villagers’ road.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter Who May Ride the Wood? has been resolved: The forest road reopens under an agreement or enforceable ruling that lets villagers use it regularly. Do not count merely breaking the gate, a single passage, a promise to negotiate, or a fabricated claim.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. When it fits, the people involved acknowledge the actual outcome and remind the participants that Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill can recognize their service. Do not force an immediate return or grant a title yet.

Who May Ride the Wood?.questDesignBrief:
A lord has locked a gate across the forest road villagers use to reach their homes, claiming they frighten his game. The villagers complained to court. Ciara Valcourt, the duke's cousin, volunteered to help but has already exchanged insults with him; she asked Dalia for someone to accompany her. Meet Ciara at the Palace, ride to the gate, and get the road reopened for regular village use. Persuasion, an agreement, or a ducal ruling can work; tearing it down alone lets the lord rebuild it. 100 florins from the ducal household and access to the household stables for local rides. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of restoring the villagers' road. Ciara first suggests pulling the gate down. She helps and argues rather than leaving the work to the player. The lord wants uninterrupted hunting; the villagers need a usable route home. Allow a challenge to his right to close it, negotiated access hours that meet village needs, or an order from the ducal household. The gate is on an ordinary forest road on Valcourt land, not a new named destination. Schedule the ride by day and respect Ciara’s existing dusk transformation.

Completion details: The forest road reopens under an agreement or enforceable ruling that lets villagers use it regularly.

A Toast to Harstone.name: A Toast to Harstone
A Toast to Harstone.questStatement:
A Harstone noble insulted a Silverblade monster-hunter at Greenwood Lodge on Ducal Hill. A duel is about to follow. Get the noble to withdraw the insult and the hunter to accept the apology and call off the duel.

Reward: 110 florins from the grateful host and introductions among the lodge's hunters and patrons.

Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition.
A Toast to Harstone.mainObjective: Settle the insult and stop the duel.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter A Toast to Harstone has been resolved: The Harstone noble withdraws the insult, and the hunter accepts the apology and calls off the duel. Do not count a temporary postponement, a promise to apologize, killing either disputant, or a fabricated claim.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. When it fits, the people involved acknowledge the actual outcome and remind the participants that Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill can recognize their service. Do not force an immediate return or grant a title yet.

A Toast to Harstone.questDesignBrief:
At Greenwood Lodge, a young noble of House Harstone called a visiting Silverblade monster-hunter the family's kennel dog. The hunter demanded an apology; the noble refused before their friends, and a duel threatens. The supper's host asked Dalia for help. Visit the lodge and get the noble to withdraw the insult so the hunter will call off the duel. Private persuasion, challenging the friends egging them on, or helping the noble apologize publicly can work. 110 florins from the grateful host and introductions among the lodge's hunters and patrons. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of settling the quarrel. The hunter wants their dignity restored, not a groveling performance. The noble fears looking weak before their friends. House Harstone gave the Order its castle generations ago; some descendants still behave as though they own the independent hunters. Reveal this history if relevant or asked, rather than making it required knowledge. The duel has not happened when the party arrives; give them an opportunity to intervene without prescribing dialogue or their choices.

Completion details: The Harstone noble withdraws the insult, and the hunter accepts the apology and calls off the duel.

A Song for the Court.name: A Song for the Court
A Song for the Court.questStatement:
Help a young silversmith sell their singing silver nightingale. Meet them on Silver Row in Carendon, then demonstrate it together at a Palace supper on Ducal Hill. It copies voices and songs: choose how to show it off and win a noble customer who pays a deposit.

Reward: 100 florins, the maker’s friendship, and a small enchanted songbird that remembers and repeats one tune, replacing it when taught another. The bird is a keepsake, not a combat summon.

Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition.
A Song for the Court.mainObjective: Demonstrate the nightingale with its maker and secure a paid commission.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter A Song for the Court has been resolved: After the player and silversmith demonstrate the nightingale at the palace supper, a guest commissions a piece from the maker and pays a deposit. Applause, a demonstration alone, a promise to commission later, or a fabricated claim does not count.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. When it fits, the people involved acknowledge the actual outcome and remind the participants that Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill can recognize their service. Do not force an immediate return or grant a title yet.

A Song for the Court.questDesignBrief:
Dalia has offered a young silversmith a place to demonstrate their singing silver nightingale at a palace supper. They want help presenting it. Meet them on Silver Row, try the bird, then show it off together at the Palace on Ducal Hill and win their first noble customer. It imitates voices and sings anything it hears: perform, impersonate a courtier, or invite song challenges. An established court jeweler calls it an expensive toy; the maker knows the craft but needs help winning the room. 100 florins from the household's demonstration fund, the maker's friendship, and a small silver songbird that remembers and repeats one tune. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of helping a Carendon craftsperson win a patron. Dalia arranges demonstrations of Carendon craftsmanship; the maker earned this place and asked for someone comfortable with an audience. Let the player choose the presentation. The maker answers technical questions and participates throughout. The reward bird is a small enchanted keepsake, not a combat summon: it remembers and repeats one tune, replacing that tune when taught another. Award it once through ordinary in-world item handling after success.

Completion details: After the player and silversmith demonstrate the nightingale at the palace supper, a guest commissions a piece from the maker and pays a deposit.

The Hounds Choose.name: The Hounds Choose
The Hounds Choose.questStatement:
A kennel-master needs help handling a scruffy rescue dog at Greenwood Lodge on Ducal Hill. Practice together, then win one scent-trail or obstacle trial. Winning the whole championship is optional.

Reward: 80 florins in prize money, the kennel-master's help training an animal companion, and the option to adopt the rescue dog.

Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition.
The Hounds Choose.mainObjective: Help the kennel-master and rescue dog win one hound trial.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Hounds Choose has been resolved: The player and kennel-master handle the rescue dog together and win at least one official hound trial at Greenwood Lodge. Practice, entering, adopting the dog, or a fabricated claim does not count; winning the overall championship is not required.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. When it fits, the people involved acknowledge the actual outcome and remind the participants that Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill can recognize their service. Do not force an immediate return or grant a title yet.

The Hounds Choose.questDesignBrief:
A young kennel-master needs a second handler for Greenwood Lodge's hound trials and has asked Dalia for help. Meet their scruffy rescue dog, practice together, and win one trial: a scent trail or obstacle course. The dog is clever but loves food and jumping on finely dressed guests. A rival with immaculate pedigree hounds calls it a kitchen mongrel; the kennel-master takes the insult personally and pushes too hard. Help them and the dog show what they can do. The overall championship is optional. 80 florins in prize money, the kennel-master's help training an animal companion, and the option to adopt the rescue dog. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of helping a local trainer compete. Dalia wants capable local trainers included in the court contest and offers this to players interested in animals, without inventing their preferences. The kennel-master takes in strays to find them homes. Practice lets the player learn the dog’s strengths and distractions before the trials; let handling choices matter. The player can encourage the kennel-master or challenge them for taking embarrassment out on the dog. Adoption is optional and requires the player to accept; declining leaves the dog cared for and does not affect completion. Do not require the whole championship or turn the trials into combat.

Completion details: The player and kennel-master handle the rescue dog together and win at least one official hound trial at Greenwood Lodge.

The Voices in the Preserve.name: The Voices in the Preserve
The Voices in the Preserve.questStatement:
Gamekeepers have vanished from Dauvigne Preserve, and their voices now call from the woods. Meet the surviving keepers at the Preserve Gate. Find the missing people, rescue anyone alive, bring back identifiable belongings of the dead, and stop the attacks.

Reward: 140 florins from House Dauvigne, a welcome at its hunts, and friendship with the surviving gamekeepers.

Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition.
The Voices in the Preserve.mainObjective: Find the missing keepers and stop whatever is taking them.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Voices in the Preserve has been resolved: The voice-mimicking predator can no longer prey on people in the preserve, the missing gamekeepers' fates are established, any survivors are rescued, and identifiable belongings of those who died are brought back. Do not count hearing a voice, a temporary retreat by the creature, a promise to investigate, or a fabricated claim.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. When it fits, the people involved acknowledge the actual outcome and remind the participants that Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill can recognize their service. Do not force an immediate return or grant a title yet.

The Voices in the Preserve.questDesignBrief:
Gamekeepers have disappeared in House Dauvigne's hunting preserve. Now their voices call for help from the woods. The household has asked Dalia to find hunters; Fifi Dauvigne, a young noble of the family, can introduce you to its people. Meet the surviving keepers at the Preserve Gate, find the missing men, and stop whatever is taking them. Rescue anyone still alive and bring back identifiable belongings for those who died. 140 florins from House Dauvigne, a welcome at its hunts, and friendship with the surviving gamekeepers. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of your service. Use the leucrotta already established in the preserve: a stag-bodied predator that copies voices it has heard, lairing in the ravine cave among its victims’ bones and gear. It calls from cover in a missing keeper’s voice to draw someone away from the group, then charges to knock them down and drag them away. Describe the creature clearly without requiring players to know its name. Let players discover the mimicry, bait it themselves, or confront it in the lair; do not force separation or surprise. Respect established deaths and rescue anyone still alive in the game’s actual state. Fifi’s introduction is optional and grants no automatic friendship or knowledge of the culprit.

Completion details: The voice-mimicking predator can no longer prey on people in the preserve, the missing gamekeepers' fates are established, any survivors are rescued, and identifiable belongings of those who died are brought back.

Guests of the Reavers.name: Guests of the Reavers
Guests of the Reavers.questStatement:
Bandits on Reaver Road have captured a young noble and a groom from rival households. Find their camp and get both prisoners to safety. Fight, sneak, bluff, negotiate, or try another plan.

Reward: 160 florins from the court and a welcome in both households.

Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition.
Guests of the Reavers.mainObjective: Rescue both the noble and the groom.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter Guests of the Reavers has been resolved: Both the young noble and the groom are free of their captors and have reached safety. Freeing only one, agreeing to a ransom without release, or a fabricated claim does not count. Resolving the households’ feud is not required.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. When it fits, the people involved acknowledge the actual outcome and remind the participants that Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill can recognize their service. Do not force an immediate return or grant a title yet.

Guests of the Reavers.questDesignBrief:
Bandits have captured a young noble and a groom from a rival household on Reaver Road. Both households appealed to Dalia and blame each other. Find the camp and get both prisoners safely out by force, stealth, bluff, negotiation, or another workable plan. The noble's family will ransom only their child, but the noble refuses to abandon the groom who protected them. The groom knows the guards' movements; the noble can create a distraction. 160 florins from the court and a welcome in both households. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of rescuing both captives. Investigating the ambush on the Road can lead to the existing Reaver Camp. Use households consistent with the game’s established relationships, without overwriting a named character’s history. Before the ambush the noble barely considered the groom worth speaking to. Both captives are frightened and argumentative but actively seek escape; let their observations and distractions help when an opportunity arises. They can tell their own households what happened after rescue; mediating the family quarrel is not required. Their unlikely friendship can continue on later visits. The court’s bounty covers rescuing both people, regardless of the family’s narrow ransom offer.

Completion details: Both the young noble and the groom are free of their captors and have reached safety.

The Boats Under the Reeds.name: The Boats Under the Reeds
The Boats Under the Reeds.questStatement:
A hydra is overturning fishing boats in Drowner’s Deep. Meet the boat-builder at the Fen-Edge and take their boat into the reeds. Make the landing and fishing routes safe without driving the threat onto another settlement.

Reward: 180 florins from the sponsoring household, a standing welcome among the river families, and use of the boat for future local outings by arrangement with its builder.

Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition.
The Boats Under the Reeds.mainObjective: Stop the hydra’s attacks so the fishing crews can return to work.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Boats Under the Reeds has been resolved: The hydra can no longer attack the landing or its fishing routes, and the crews can resume work without the threat being moved onto another settlement. A temporary retreat, one successful crossing while the threat remains, a promise, or a fabricated claim does not count. Killing the hydra is not required if another durable solution works.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. When it fits, the people involved acknowledge the actual outcome and remind the participants that Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill can recognize their service. Do not force an immediate return or grant a title yet.

The Boats Under the Reeds.questDesignBrief:
A marsh hydra is overturning fishing boats at the edge of Drowner's Deep. The fishing families petitioned the court, and a noble household has funded a bounty. Meet a young boat-builder at the Fen-Edge, take their shallow-draft boat into the reeds, and stop the hydra so crews can use their landing and fishing routes again. The builder wants to come: they know the channels, steer through narrow gaps, haul people aboard, and fight off snapping heads with a boat-hook. 180 florins from the sponsoring household, a standing welcome among the river families, and use of the boat for future local outings by arrangement with its builder. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of restoring safe access to the water. Heads rise on opposite sides of the boat: one snaps at the crew while another tries to overturn it. Let the party fight afloat, lure it onto a mudbank, set an ambush, or devise another way to remove the threat. The builder insists they can help but does not override the party’s choices; when accompanying them, they steer, rescue people, and drive a boat-hook into an attacking mouth on their own initiative. Respect resolved combat outcomes instead of forcing a capsize. The builder dreams of designing boats for difficult waters rather than only repairing leaking hulls; let this relationship continue on later visits. Boat access is a recurring local favor, not transfer of ownership or a required funding negotiation.

Completion details: The hydra can no longer attack the landing or its fishing routes, and the crews can resume work without the threat being moved onto another settlement.

The Hunt Comes Home.name: The Hunt Comes Home
The Hunt Comes Home.questStatement:
A hunter at the Hound and Horn in Vaudania has been bitten by a wereboar. Help him survive his next transformation without anyone being killed or infected. Arrange protection for future changes too; a cure is optional.

Reward: 150 florins from the court, the innkeeper's hospitality, and the grateful hunter's friendship.

Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition.
The Hunt Comes Home.mainObjective: Keep the hunter and others safe through his next change, and make a workable plan for future changes.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Hunt Comes Home has been resolved: The hunter survives the transformation, nobody is killed or infected during the attempt, and a workable arrangement protects him and others during future changes. Do not count killing the hunter, postponing the change, a single restraint without provision for future changes, or a fabricated claim. A cure is not required.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. When it fits, the people involved acknowledge the actual outcome and remind the participants that Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill can recognize their service. Do not force an immediate return or grant a title yet.

The Hunt Comes Home.questDesignBrief:
A young hunter at Vaudania's Hound and Horn has been bitten by a wereboar. The innkeeper who raised him asked the court for help after his last transformation broke his restraints. Meet him while human and help him survive his next change without hurting anyone. Agree on containment, available treatment, or a plan to subdue him; he helps prepare and explains his last escape. Visiting trophy-hunters want to turn your effort into their hunt. Arrange safety for future changes too. 150 florins from the court, the innkeeper's hospitality, and the grateful hunter's friendship. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of protecting the hunter and village. The hunter is frightened and ashamed but participates: he knows the woods, helps build restraints, explains exactly how he escaped last time, and asks the party to stop him if he attacks someone. His transformed body hits like a battering ram, splintering timber, tossing obstacles aside, and charging through a blocked doorway. Resolve these attempts through combat outcomes; do not automatically defeat a sound containment plan. The visiting hunters seek a trophy and can be confronted, persuaded, deceived, or otherwise prevented from killing him. A cure is optional and only available if supported by established world magic. Effective containment, treatment, or another credible ongoing arrangement can succeed; a promise to find a solution later cannot. This accepted matter creates the local crisis; do not make ordinary visits to Vaudania start with this event.

Completion details: The hunter survives the transformation, nobody is killed or infected during the attempt, and a workable arrangement protects him and others during future changes.

A Voice at Westvigil.name: A Voice at Westvigil
A Voice at Westvigil.questSource: Dalia and Aldo, heralds of Carendon and Westmarch
A Voice at Westvigil.questStatement:
Aldo invites you to supper at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford. The household wants engineer Fennick Corwin to demonstrate his work but denies him a seat at the high table. Hear both sides and help settle how he will take part. You can challenge your hosts or decline.

Reward: future hospitality at Castle Westvigil. Helping does not change your allegiance.
A Voice at Westvigil.mainObjective: Help Fennick and the household freely agree on his part in the gathering, with Aldo acknowledging your help.

completionCondition.query: The accepted invitation A Voice at Westvigil is resolved: Fennick and the household have freely settled his participation and standing at this gathering, and Aldo acknowledges the visitor's contribution. Arrival, a demonstration alone, or a forced capitulation is not completion.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Aldo recognizes the visitors' contribution and offers future hospitality at Castle Westvigil. Their titles remain recognized, and neither hospitality nor helping here changes their allegiance or compels further work. Dalia will be glad to hear how it went. Do not grant another title or repeat the invitation as a new task.

A Voice at Westvigil.questDesignBrief:
Aldo, Duke Corwin's herald at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford, invites a proven guest from Carendon to a household supper. Fennick Corwin, the engineer of the Greatwall's defenses, is being asked to demonstrate his work while still denied a place at the high table. Hear Fennick and the household, then help them reach an honest arrangement about his place and voice. You may challenge your hosts, back Fennick, negotiate or decline; Carendon asks for your judgment, not obedience. Travel is simply how you reach the people involved.

Completion details: At Castle Westvigil, Fennick and the household settle the invitation and his place in the discussion without coercing him into a humiliating performance. Aldo acknowledges what the visitor contributed.

The Price of a Discovery.name: The Price of a Discovery
The Price of a Discovery.questStatement:
Shirin Serayaf needs companions for the First Pyramid. She has found carvings about the djinn, but Khenret’s Company demands her flying carpet to let her reach them. She refuses. Join her at the Citadel of Seven Winds, help her reach and examine the chamber, and return safely. She brings wind and flame magic and knowledge of the tombs; bargain, sneak, fight, or find another approach. The court offers 180 florins.

Return to Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds for recognition.
The Price of a Discovery.mainObjective: Shirin has examined the chamber’s carvings and the expedition has returned safely.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Price of a Discovery has been resolved: Shirin has examined the chamber’s carvings and the expedition has returned safely. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

The Price of a Discovery.questDesignBrief:
Shirin Serayaf has found a chamber beneath the First Pyramid with carvings showing how the Sun Kings dealt with djinn. Khenret’s Company holds the passages above it and demands her flying carpet as the price of entry. She refuses to surrender it or abandon the discovery.

Shirin has asked Rostam for capable companions. He hopes someone will help her find a workable approach before pride makes her storm the entrance.

Shirin hopes the carvings illuminate her family’s djinn ancestry.

Join Shirin to reach the chamber and uncover its history through bargaining, deception, stealth, fighting, or another workable approach. Shirin contributes magic and knowledge, has strong opinions, and listens to better plans.

Meet Shirin at the Citadel of Seven Winds before traveling to the First Pyramid. The mapped destination is the tomb.

The Serayafs inherit actual djinn ancestry; there is no demonic bargain. Leave the carvings’ specific content to narration, consistent with that lore.

The approved extortion demand precedes hostilities: Khenret’s Company demands Shirin’s carpet, allowing bargaining or another approach despite the location’s general hostility toward rival crews.

Use the premise as a narrative seed. Leave incidental names, scene details and workable solutions to play; no mandatory scene sequence. Return to Rostam for recognition after resolving the matter. Pay the stated coin reward once, not again during recognition.

The Gold on Her Wrists.name: The Gold on Her Wrists
The Gold on Her Wrists.questStatement:
At the Rosewater Baths, a young noblewoman has recognized her mother’s burial bracelets on a wealthy widow from a rival house. The widow says she bought them innocently and resents the accusation. Rostam wants the bracelets recovered and the trade in goods stolen from Oasis’s dead stopped. Speak with both women and trace the seller through the Great Serpent Market. The court offers 160 florins.

Return to Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds for recognition.
The Gold on Her Wrists.mainObjective: Recover the mother’s bracelets and stop the broker’s trade in goods stolen from the city’s graves.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Gold on Her Wrists has been resolved: Recover the mother’s bracelets and stop the broker’s trade in goods stolen from the city’s graves. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

The Gold on Her Wrists.questDesignBrief:
A young noblewoman recognizes her mother’s burial bracelets on a wealthy widow from a rival house. The widow bought them innocently and resents being accused of grave-robbing.

Rostam seeks the truth: an unfounded accusation against a rival would harm House Serayaf, while ignoring robbery of the city’s dead would betray its law.

A tomb broker mixes jewelry stolen from Oasis’s dead into legitimate Sun-King treasure. The operation already exists. The widow can become a formidable ally when convinced the broker used her to sell stolen burial goods.

Question both women, examine the jewelry, trace the seller through the Great Serpent Market, and confront the supplier. Investigation, infiltration, exposure, and force are available.

Robbing Oasis’s own dead is forbidden; treasure from the Sun Kings is openly traded. Leave the evidence and investigation’s course to narration.

Use the premise as a narrative seed. Leave incidental names, scene details and workable solutions to play; no mandatory scene sequence. Return to Rostam for recognition after resolving the matter. Pay the stated coin reward once, not again during recognition.

The Favorite Must Lose.name: The Favorite Must Lose
The Favorite Must Lose.questStatement:
Omid’s sponsored camel racer refuses to throw a race. The patron demanding it has hired fighters occupying her training yard and controlling her camels. Meet her at the Caravanserai of the Thousand Roads and help her regain control so she can race freely. She is outspoken and wants credit for her own courage; Omid brings money and fighting skill but tends to take over. Winning the race is not required. Omid offers 140 florins.

Return to Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds for recognition.
The Favorite Must Lose.mainObjective: Her yard and camels are under her control again, the patron’s coercion has ended, and she has raced freely. Winning is not required.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Favorite Must Lose has been resolved: Her yard and camels are under her control again, the patron’s coercion has ended, and she has raced freely. Winning is not required. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

The Favorite Must Lose.questDesignBrief:
Omid backs a fast, outspoken young camel racer who resents claims that Serayaf money bought her victories. A wealthy race patron orders her to lose; his hired fighters already occupy her training yard, control access to her camels, and rough up helpers. She refuses to withdraw.

Omid has asked Rostam for help and House Serayaf has publicly sponsored her entry.

The racer wants her yard back without becoming the helpless girl Omid rescued in every retelling. Omid wants to throw the occupiers out himself.

End the occupation by force, turn the patron’s people against him, expose his interference to the other owners, or find another workable solution. The racer contributes her knowledge and contacts; Omid contributes money, influence, and effective fighting but tends to take over.

Use the premise as a narrative seed. Leave incidental names, scene details and workable solutions to play; no mandatory scene sequence. Return to Rostam for recognition after resolving the matter. Pay the stated coin reward once, not again during recognition.

Supper Above the City.name: Supper Above the City
Supper Above the City.questStatement:
Join Shirin at the Citadel of Seven Winds for supper on a broad flying carpet. Each guest chooses a sight below and tells a true or invented story. The hostess loves outrageous tales and awards a golden cup to her favorite; a pompous rival insists on celebrating his ancestors. Tell a story, alone or with Shirin, and win the cup. Rostam will recognize the achievement.

Return to Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds for recognition.
Supper Above the City.mainObjective: Win the hostess’s golden cup, alone or jointly with Shirin. The hostess judges daring, humor, or ingenuity.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter Supper Above the City has been resolved: Win the hostess’s golden cup, alone or jointly with Shirin. The hostess judges daring, humor, or ingenuity. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

Supper Above the City.questDesignBrief:
Shirin attends a young noblewoman’s supper on a broad flying carpet above Oasis. Each guest chooses a sight below and tells a true or invented story about it. The hostess awards a golden cup to her favorite.

The hostess loves outrageous tales. A pompous rival noble insists every story must celebrate his ancestors. Shirin contributes dry humor and tomb discoveries, and can collaborate or compete.

Enjoy supper, choose a sight below, and tell a story; embellish an adventure, invent a tale, or involve another guest. A polished player-written speech is not required.

Meet at the Citadel’s existing carpet launch platform. The supper takes place aboard a broad flying carpet above Oasis.

Use the premise as a narrative seed. Leave incidental names, scene details and workable solutions to play; no mandatory scene sequence. Return to Rostam for recognition after resolving the matter. Pay the stated coin reward once, not again during recognition.

The Prisoners Below Hillwatch.name: The Prisoners Below Hillwatch
The Prisoners Below Hillwatch.questStatement:
A merchant passing through Hillwatch saw prisoners being taken beneath the town. The New Sun keeps people down there who’ve crossed its priests. We’ll pay 200 florins to anyone who gets them out.

Return to Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds for recognition.
The Prisoners Below Hillwatch.mainObjective: Free the prisoners held in the Undertemple and get them safely out of Hillwatch.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Prisoners Below Hillwatch has been resolved: Free the prisoners held in the Undertemple and get them safely out of Hillwatch. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

The Prisoners Below Hillwatch.questDesignBrief:
The New Sun cult holds travelers and dissenters in the Undertemple. This is an established situation, not an emergency or timed rescue. Hillwatch admits peaceful visitors.

A proud caravan owner refused to surrender a companion. A former cult believer knows the underground chambers. Both prisoners can help with the escape.

Enter openly and find a way below, bluff guards, bargain, sneak in, attack, or pursue another workable approach.

Use the premise as a narrative seed. Leave incidental names, scene details and workable solutions to play; no mandatory scene sequence. Return to Rostam for recognition after resolving the matter. Pay the stated coin reward once, not again during recognition.

A Collar Fit for a King.name: A Collar Fit for a King
A Collar Fit for a King.questStatement:
A noble collector wants one of the sun-gold collars from the Tomb of the Beast-King. Unfortunately, the dead king’s hunting cats are still wearing them. Bring her one and she’ll pay 250 florins—and insist you tell her supper guests how you got it.

Return to Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds for recognition.
A Collar Fit for a King.mainObjective: Bring the collector an intact sun-gold hunting-cat collar from the tomb.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter A Collar Fit for a King has been resolved: Bring the collector an intact sun-gold hunting-cat collar from the tomb. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

A Collar Fit for a King.questDesignBrief:
A lavish, enthusiastic noble hostess who keeps ordinary cats and admires the dead king’s taste wants the collar for display and wants to meet someone who faced its owner.

Enter the Beast-Halls and remove a sun-gold collar from a prowling mummified great cat through fighting, trapping, immobilization, or another workable approach. The hostile beast already guards the tomb.

Rostam arranges the collector’s introduction and receipt of the collar through the Citadel; no new permanent residence is required.

Use the premise as a narrative seed. Leave incidental names, scene details and workable solutions to play; no mandatory scene sequence. Return to Rostam for recognition after resolving the matter. Pay the stated coin reward once, not again during recognition.

The Merchant’s Little Book.name: The Merchant’s Little Book
The Merchant’s Little Book.questStatement:
A wealthy merchant has been buying servants’ gossip and using it to blackmail their employers. He keeps his little book locked in his study, and the key on his belt. He’s hosting a feast, and I can get you invited. Bring me that book. The court offers 180 florins. Collect the invitation from Rostam at the Citadel.

Return to Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds for recognition.
The Merchant’s Little Book.mainObjective: Bring the blackmail book to Rostam.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Merchant’s Little Book has been resolved: Bring the blackmail book to Rostam. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

The Merchant’s Little Book.questDesignBrief:
The merchant’s blackmail is an established fact, not a mystery to prove. He hosts a feast while guards protect his private rooms.

Attend the feast, gain access to the study and steal the book. Lift the belt key while dancing, lure the merchant away, enlist another guest, pick the lock or use another workable approach. Force can cause a fight with guests and guards; this is a consequence rather than an arbitrary game prohibition.

Rostam supplies the invitation and directions at the Citadel. Narration establishes the merchant’s private house, feast and study within Oasis; these are incidental rooms, not new permanent map areas.

Use the premise as a narrative seed. Leave incidental names, scene details and workable solutions to play; no mandatory scene sequence. Return to Rostam for recognition after resolving the matter. Pay the stated coin reward once, not again during recognition.

A Piece of the Sun.name: A Piece of the Sun
A Piece of the Sun.questStatement:
A young sorceress of the court wants a focusing lens from the Tomb of the Sun’s Eye. She’s spent a fortune collecting ancient magical weapons and is desperate to fire one herself. She’s offering 250 florins, and she’s coming with you—she refuses to hear about the interesting part afterward.

Return to Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds for recognition.
A Piece of the Sun.mainObjective: Return from the tomb with an intact focusing lens for the sorceress.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter A Piece of the Sun has been resolved: Return from the tomb with an intact focusing lens for the sorceress. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

A Piece of the Sun.questDesignBrief:
Explore the Mirror Halls, redirect burning beams using movable mirrors, fight flying brass scarab guardians, and extract an intact focusing lens. The patron contributes powerful magic and fights effectively; this is not an escort or babysitting task.

Use the premise as a narrative seed. Leave incidental names, scene details and workable solutions to play; no mandatory scene sequence. Return to Rostam for recognition after resolving the matter. Pay the stated coin reward once, not again during recognition.

Her Own Applause.name: Her Own Applause
Her Own Applause.questStatement:
A young noblewoman who hunts tombs has entered the paired fights at the Red Sands. She’s bold, boastful, and spends her treasure as quickly as she finds it. Her brother is an arena favorite; she insists fighting things that actually want to eat you is better training. Now she wants a partner to help prove it. Half the purse is yours.

Return to Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds for recognition.
Her Own Applause.mainObjective: Win the paired bout together. Changing the crowd’s opinion or resolving the sibling rivalry is not required.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter Her Own Applause has been resolved: Win the paired bout together. Changing the crowd’s opinion or resolving the sibling rivalry is not required. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

Her Own Applause.questDesignBrief:
She has money, leisure and actual fighting experience, and wants public glory to rival her famous brother.

Fight beside the noblewoman against two arena veterans. She contributes spear-and-shield fighting and an aggressive style learned in the tombs.

Use the premise as a narrative seed. Leave incidental names, scene details and workable solutions to play; no mandatory scene sequence. Return to Rostam for recognition after resolving the matter. Pay the stated coin reward once, not again during recognition.

The Guest Who Stayed.name: The Guest Who Stayed
The Guest Who Stayed.questStatement:
A young nobleman broke open a sealed brass vessel in a tomb and freed a djinn. Delighted with his rescuer, it followed him home—and now throws thunderous feasts in his roof garden every night. The young man loves boasting about the rescue, but he’s sleeping at his aunt’s. Get his guest to leave, and he’ll pay 200 florins. Meet him at the Citadel of Seven Winds.

Return to Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds for recognition.
The Guest Who Stayed.mainObjective: The djinn relinquishes the house and leaves, allowing its owner to move back in.

The Guest Who Stayed.questDesignBrief:
The freed djinn considers its company a magnificent reward. It knows the nobleman wants quiet, but finds that an absurd way to live. It is proud, pleasure-loving and powerful in wind magic.

Persuade, trick or force the djinn to relinquish the house and leave. Bargain or offer something worth leaving for; combat is possible.

Meet the nobleman at the Citadel; he gives directions to his private house within Oasis. Its roof garden is an incidental setting, not an existing household repurposed for this matter.

Use the premise as a narrative seed. Leave incidental names, scene details and workable solutions to play; no mandatory scene sequence. Return to Rostam for recognition after resolving the matter. Pay the stated coin reward once, not again during recognition.

The Laughing Hunters.name: The Laughing Hunters
The Laughing Hunters.questStatement:
A pack of giant hyenas has made its den among the wrecks on Widow’s Way. A young noblewoman who breeds racing camels has lost three of her finest animals to them. She’s furious, knows their hunting grounds, and wants to come along with her bow. Break up that pack, and her household will pay 250 florins.

Return to Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds for recognition.
The Laughing Hunters.mainObjective: The pack is killed or driven out of the area, and its den no longer threatens the road. Briefly scattering it does not count.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Laughing Hunters has been resolved: The pack is killed or driven out of the area, and its den no longer threatens the road. onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

The Laughing Hunters.questDesignBrief:
Track the established pack to its den, lure it into an advantageous fight, or drive it away from the road. The noblewoman knows animals, shoots well and contributes without needing protection.

Use the premise as a narrative seed. Leave incidental names, scene details and workable solutions to play; no mandatory scene sequence. Return to Rostam for recognition after resolving the matter. Pay the stated coin reward once, not again during recognition.

The Lion in the Garden.name: The Lion in the Garden
The Lion in the Garden.questStatement:
A young nobleman brought a mummified lion home from a tomb to display at his garden parties. It woke up. Now it prowls the grounds, and he’s too proud to abandon the house his friends warned him against filling with tomb treasures. Destroy the beast, and he’ll pay 200 florins. Meet him at the Citadel of Seven Winds.

Return to Rostam at the Citadel of Seven Winds for recognition.
The Lion in the Garden.mainObjective: Destroy the lion so the household can safely use the garden again.

The Lion in the Garden.questDesignBrief:
Hunt the hostile undead lion through an established occupied walled pleasure garden with palms, fountains, shaded galleries and roof terraces. The owner knows the garden entrances and the beast’s movements.

Meet the collector at the Citadel; he gives directions to his private house and walled garden within Oasis. This is an incidental household, not a player estate or an established NPC’s home.

Use the premise as a narrative seed. Leave incidental names, scene details and workable solutions to play; no mandatory scene sequence. Return to Rostam for recognition after resolving the matter. Pay the stated coin reward once, not again during recognition.

A Hall Worth Keeping.name: A Hall Worth Keeping
A Hall Worth Keeping.questSource: Embla, herald of the Winter Crown
A Hall Worth Keeping.questStatement:
Thyra Ormsvald wants to reclaim an old Northrealm hunting hall as a refuge for woodcutters. Meet her at the Logging Steads and take the troll-held hall together. Haldor has joined the effort to make sure the workers get their shelter. Embla introduces volunteers at Thyra’s request.

Reward: 150 florins from the court, standing welcome at the hall, and Embla’s recognition once per participant.

Return to Embla at the Winter Court in Warmwater Township for recognition.
A Hall Worth Keeping.mainObjective: Reclaim the hunting hall with Thyra and Haldor so woodcutters can safely use it.

Embla introduces Thyra’s effort to reclaim an old Northrealm hunting hall in the Firwood as a refuge for the woodcutters. Meet Thyra at The Logging Steads and take the troll-held hall together.

Thyra sees a first step toward reclaiming the kingdom. Haldor joins to secure shelter for woodcutters. Both fight effectively. Player may support either, challenge both, or prioritize the people using the hall.

Trolls dead or permanently driven away; woodcutters can safely occupy the hall.

150 florins from the court, standing welcome at the hall, and Embla’s recognition once per participant.

The Guests in the Glass.name: The Guests in the Glass
The Guests in the Glass.questSource: Embla, herald of the Winter Crown
The Guests in the Glass.questStatement:
Sanna Rimedal, the frost-mage of the Ice Gardens, wants help freeing icelings kept in a Pearl House collector’s glass cabinets. The spirits want to return to the gardens; the collector claims they came with his purchases. Embla can introduce you as court guests.

Reward: 100 florins from Sanna, an invitation into her studio to learn ice magic or commission a work, and Embla’s recognition once per participant.

Return to Embla at the Winter Court in Warmwater Township for recognition.
The Guests in the Glass.mainObjective: Free the captive icelings and return them safely to the Ice Gardens.

The Guests in the Glass.questDesignBrief:
Sanna Rimedal asks for help freeing icelings held in chilled glass cabinets by a Pearl House collector at The Glasshouses. Embla can introduce court guests to him.

Sanna wants to smash the cabinets. The collector considers his beautifully displayed captivity generous protection and claims the icelings came with the purchased sculptures. The icelings want to return to the Ice Gardens and express their own opinions.

Persuasion, bargaining, public exposure to his guests, or escape.

The captive icelings are free and safely back in the Ice Gardens.

100 florins from Sanna, an invitation into her studio to learn ice magic or commission a work, and Embla’s recognition once per participant.

The Ship Beneath the Ice.name: The Ship Beneath the Ice
The Ship Beneath the Ice.questSource: Embla, herald of the Winter Crown
The Ship Beneath the Ice.questStatement:
Margit Ismark’s expedition found a Northrealm ship and glimpsed a painted chart of the coast before the freeze, then narrowly escaped a rimewyrm. She wants companions to return with her. Meet her at the Glasshouses, explore the wreck in the Underfloes, and bring back the chart or a usable copy for the court.

Reward: 180 florins from Margit, her backing for a future expedition, and Embla’s recognition once per participant.

Return to Embla at the Winter Court in Warmwater Township for recognition.
The Ship Beneath the Ice.mainObjective: Explore the wreck with Margit and bring the old coastal chart or a faithful usable copy to the court.

The Ship Beneath the Ice.questDesignBrief:
Margit Ismark seeks companions to revisit a Northrealm ship exposed in the Underfloes, explore it, and recover its painted coastal chart. Her previous expedition narrowly escaped a rimewyrm. Embla sees useful knowledge for the court.

An intact painted cabin contains a chart of the Northrealm before the freeze, including settlements absent from court maps. The rimewyrm already hunts this stretch of broken ice.

Margit wants to see the discovery herself and earn serious recognition. The expedition leader will guide another attempt but insists on withdrawing if danger becomes untenable. Funding does not purchase unlimited risk. Margit contributes frost magic.

Fight or divert the wyrm, or find a protected way into the wreck.

Recover the chart or a faithful usable copy and bring it back for the Winter Court to examine.

180 florins from Margit, her backing for a future expedition, and Embla’s recognition once per participant.

The Crown on Runners.name: The Crown on Runners
The Crown on Runners.questSource: Embla, herald of the Winter Crown
The Crown on Runners.questStatement:
Haldor has beaten the Winter Court’s sled in every race this season. Aksel Ormsvald has asked Embla to find a partner who will enter with him. Meet Aksel at the Kennels and beat Haldor in one race on the frozen lake; you may drive or ride alongside him, and practice is available.

Reward: 100 florins in prize money, standing invitation to use Aksel’s racing sled and team at the Kennels, and Embla’s recognition once per participant.

Return to Embla at the Winter Court in Warmwater Township for recognition.
The Crown on Runners.mainObjective: Win one sled race against Haldor with Aksel as your teammate.

Aksel is an excellent daring driver who loves an audience. Haldor knows the ice better and delights in making him chase. Both want an honest win; their rivalry concerns whom the north ought to follow.

Player drives or rides alongside Aksel, helping choose the route, manage the team and overcome obstacles. Practice available. Rivalry responds to participant behavior.

Win one race against Haldor with Aksel as teammate. Losing permits another attempt.

100 florins in prize money, standing invitation to use Aksel’s racing sled and team at the Kennels, and Embla’s recognition once per participant.

The Private Spring.name: The Private Spring
The Private Spring.questSource: Embla, herald of the Winter Crown
The Private Spring.questStatement:
A Pearl House owner has enclosed a bathing pool used for generations by his neighbors. The displaced bathers have petitioned the court. Embla introduces you to Emil Goldveik at the Glasshouses, who knows the owner and has offered to help. Restore regular free access acceptable to the neighbors.

Reward: 100 florins from the court, a standing invitation to Emil’s Glasshouse suppers, and Embla’s recognition once per participant.

Return to Embla at the Winter Court in Warmwater Township for recognition.

A Pearl House owner has enclosed a spring-fed bathing pool used for generations by neighbors, with guards excluding them. The bathers petitioned the court. Embla introduces the party to Emil Goldveik at the Glasshouses to approach the owner.

Emil knows the owner socially and initially offers to pay for occasional visits elsewhere. The bathers’ outspoken representative wants their pool back. The young owner enjoys hosting friends but considers neighbors intrusive. Emil can learn what the bathers actually seek and become a useful ally.

Persuade the owner, negotiate shared use acceptable to bathers, enlist social pressure from fellow hosts, or challenge his claim to exclude neighbors.

Neighbors regain regular free access they accept and actually return to use the pool; a future promise alone is insufficient.

100 florins from the court, a standing invitation to Emil’s Glasshouse suppers, and Embla’s recognition once per participant.

Cold Pearls.questStatement:
Aksel bought hearthpearls at the Frost Fair as gifts for northern households, but recipients say they go cold overnight. Embla asks you to investigate the merchant’s stock, stop any fraudulent sales, and secure genuine replacements for the affected households.

Reward: 120 florins from Aksel, a genuine hearthpearl for travel, and Embla’s recognition once per participant.

Return to Embla at the Winter Court in Warmwater Township for recognition.

At the Frost Fair a merchant sells exhausted hearthpearls as fresh, warming them before demonstrations. Aksel bought gifts for northern households whose pearls go cold overnight. Embla asks the party to investigate, stop fraudulent sales, and secure genuine replacements.

The charming merchant feigns indignation and blames owners. A sharp-eyed older fisher refuses to leave his stall after returning a cold pearl. Aksel wants to make recipients whole; his willingness to pay again creates another opening for the merchant.

Test stock, question customers, catch demonstration preparation, force admission; persuasion, exposure, intimidation, or recovering remaining proceeds.

Fraudulent sales stopped and affected households receive genuine replacements. Aksel can cover a shortfall; recovering every coin is optional.

120 florins from Aksel, a genuine hearthpearl for travel, and Embla’s recognition once per participant.

The Volunteers.name: The Volunteers
The Volunteers.questSource: Embla, herald of the Winter Crown
The Volunteers.questStatement:
Snowlanders who joined Raphael ni Monbrume’s recruiting party want to leave after seeing a recruit beaten for trying. Their captain confines them in rented quarters near the Frost Fair. Their families have asked the court for help; Embla asks you to secure their release.

Reward: 150 florins from court and Embla’s recognition once per participant. Approach changes Raphael’s opinion.

Return to Embla at the Winter Court in Warmwater Township for recognition.
The Volunteers.mainObjective: Free the unwilling recruits, reunite them with their families and end their pursuit.

The captain confines them in rented quarters near the Frost Fair. Their families approach the court; Embla asks the party to secure release.

The captain treats enlistment as permanent obedience. Raphael values him but recognizes the threat to his cultivated welcome. He may arrange release in exchange for a personal favor.

Confront captain, pressure through Raphael or court, help recruits escape, or fight. Raphael’s bargain is optional.

Unwilling recruits free, reunited with families, and no longer pursued by recruiting party.

150 florins from court and Embla’s recognition once per participant. Approach changes Raphael’s opinion.

The Unwelcome Guest.name: The Unwelcome Guest
The Unwelcome Guest.questSource: Embla, herald of the Winter Crown
The Unwelcome Guest.questStatement:
A young noblewoman’s winter guest, a celebrated hunter, has taken over her home near the Ice Gardens with his companions. He refuses to leave and has threatened her friends away. She is staying elsewhere and has asked Embla for help getting her home back.

Reward: 120 florins, welcome at her future gatherings, and Embla’s recognition once per participant.

Return to Embla at the Winter Court in Warmwater Township for recognition.
The Unwelcome Guest.mainObjective: Remove the unwanted hunter and his companions so the owner can return in control of her home.

The Unwelcome Guest.questDesignBrief:
A young noblewoman hosted a celebrated northern hunter for winter. He brought companions, took over her best rooms, threatened away her friends and laughed at her demand to leave. She is staying elsewhere. Embla introduces her request to reclaim her house.

The owner admired him and is humiliated by what happened. The hunter thinks his fame makes him more valuable than the owner. He has powerful Pearl House friends but no right to remain. Some companions do not know they were ordered out.

Turn companions against him, confront him before admirers, persuade a patron to withdraw protection, or physically eject him.

Hunter and unwanted companions leave; owner returns with control of her home.

120 florins, welcome at her future gatherings, and Embla’s recognition once per participant.

The Dark Watchfire.questSource: Embla, herald of the Winter Crown
The Dark Watchfire.questStatement:
Hakon Falk, a knight of the Long Watch, wants companions to reclaim a signal-tower on the Aurora Icefields. An ice drake nests there and hunts the old winter road. Meet Hakon at the Lamp-Tower, then make the tower safe and restore its willing hearth-spirit’s signal-fire. The court funds the attempt.

Reward: 180 florins, welcome at Long Watch shelters, and Embla’s recognition once per participant.

Return to Embla at the Winter Court in Warmwater Township for recognition.
The Dark Watchfire.mainObjective: Reclaim the tower with Hakon and restore a safe refuge and signal-fire.

Hakon saved the tower’s hearth-spirit when its last keeper died. It lives in a lantern at the Lamp-Tower, remembers generations of travelers, takes pride in sheltering them, and wants to return. Hakon wants the road reopened but has grown attached to its company.

Accompany Hakon, kill the drake, drive it to uninhabited hunting grounds, or find another lasting solution; restore the tower as refuge.

Drake no longer threatens tower or road; hearth-spirit’s signal-fire burns in a refuge travelers can safely use.
