At the Giants’ Table.name: At the Giants’ Table
At the Giants’ Table.questSource: Embla, herald of the Winter Crown
At the Giants’ Table.questStatement:
Fenja, the giant who runs Warmwater’s Steaming Pools, has praised smallfolk company to her kin. Their jarl invites her to bring guests to Whitefang Hold. Embla asks you to join her as court guests and earn a welcome for future peaceful visitors through the feast, stories and challenges you choose.

Reward: 140 florins from court, Whitefang Hold hospitality, and Embla’s recognition once per participant.

Return to Embla at the Winter Court in Warmwater Township for recognition.

Fenja has praised smallfolk company to her kin at Whitefang Hold. The jarl invites her to bring guests. Embla asks the party to attend with Fenja as Winter Court guests and earn a welcome for future snowlanders.

Fenja delights in showing friends her childhood home. Her older brother claims human company has softened her and expects guests to hide behind her. She wants them to answer for themselves and enjoys a good answer.

Feasting, stories and chosen challenges; strength, wit, magic, endurance or remarkable true accounts may impress. No requirement to win every contest or accept every dare.

Earn the jarl’s explicit invitation for the party and future peaceful guests of the Winter Court to return to his hall.

140 florins from court, Whitefang Hold hospitality, and Embla’s recognition once per participant.

Her Son’s New Faith.name: Her Son’s New Faith
Her Son’s New Faith.questSource: Embla, herald of the Winter Crown
Her Son’s New Faith.questStatement:
A Pearl House widow asks for help with her son, who has joined the Long Night, the cult that attacks northern springs. He recruits at the Temple of the Hearth. Embla introduces his mother, who knows his route and meeting place. End his recruiting operation and tell her his actual fate; she hopes you can bring him home alive.

Reward: 180 florins from court and Embla’s recognition once per participant. Mother’s gratitude responds to outcome and how she is told.

Return to Embla at the Winter Court in Warmwater Township for recognition.
Her Son’s New Faith.mainObjective: End the son’s recruiting operation and tell his mother what happened.

A Pearl House widow asks the court to help bring home her son, who willingly joined the Long Night and recruits at the Temple of the Hearth. She knows his route and meeting place. Embla introduces the request.

His mother has repeatedly bought him out of trouble and expects money to solve this. He enjoys cult authority, knows its attacks kill people, still loves her, and expects protection from consequences if he returns.

Persuade him to abandon the cult, capture him, or confront him as an enemy. His mother wants him alive but cannot demand other lives be sacrificed to spare him.

His recruiting operation is ended and his mother learns his actual fate. Bringing him home requires abandonment of cult or custody, not a promise to visit.

180 florins from court and Embla’s recognition once per participant. Mother’s gratitude responds to outcome and how she is told.

Coin and favors occur in the story once; completion does not automatically pay twice. Ending this recruiter’s operation does not clear the entire Temple or resolve the Long Night across Aurora. He joined knowingly; returning home requires abandoning the cult or custody. His mother cannot demand others die to save him.

Completion: His recruiting operation is ended and his mother learns his actual fate. Bringing him home requires abandonment of cult or custody, not a promise to visit.

Another Light in the North.name: Another Light in the North
Another Light in the North.questSource: Embla, herald of the Winter Crown
Another Light in the North.questStatement:
Tirsa Hellemark, Warmwater’s rescue captain, has seen steam rising through a broken ridge on the Aurora Icefields. The court funds an expedition to explore it with her. Discover whether the basin offers dependable warmth, habitable ground and a usable approach, then report honestly; an unsuitable site still completes the work.

Reward: 160 florins and Embla’s recognition once per participant. A suitable site becomes Tirsa’s concrete future ambition.

Return to Embla at the Winter Court in Warmwater Township for recognition.
Another Light in the North.mainObjective: Explore the basin with Tirsa and report whether it could support a settlement.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter Another Light in the North has actually been resolved: Explore the basin, establish whether it offers dependable warmth, habitable ground and usable approach, then return with an honest account. An unsuitable site still completes the matter. Do not count plans, fabricated claims or a promise of later action.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, when appropriate, remind participants that Embla at the Winter Court in Warmwater Township can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, repeat payment or grant a title yet.

Another Light in the North.questDesignBrief:
Tirsa Hellemark has seen steam rising through a broken ridge on the Aurora Icefields and hopes an undiscovered hot spring could support a settlement. Embla offers court funding to explore with her.

A sheltered basin beneath overhanging ice, reached through deep fractures, unstable shelves and meltwater passages. Investigate the heat source and whether people could safely reach and live beside it.

Tirsa dreams of founding a settlement and imagines homes before assessing danger. Brave and resourceful, she needs companions willing to challenge her desired conclusion.

Explore the basin, establish whether it offers dependable warmth, habitable ground and usable approach, then return with an honest account. An unsuitable site still completes the matter.

160 florins and Embla’s recognition once per participant. A suitable site becomes Tirsa’s concrete future ambition.

Bring Them Home.name: Bring Them Home
Bring Them Home.questStatement:
Reavers hold villagers from Branton in the High Crags of the Scarps. Wystan Morcroft has offered to lead a rescue, but openly wants the raider chief as well. Branton’s appeal asks for its people back alive; Aldo seeks companions to help Wystan bring them home. Meet him at the Training Yard at Morcroft Hall, then free the captives and bring them safely to Branton.

Reward: 120 florins from House Corwin and an invitation to Wystan’s table and future rides at Morcroft Hall. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition.
Bring Them Home.mainObjective: Free the captives in the High Crags and bring them safely back to Branton.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter Bring Them Home has been resolved: All living captives established for this matter are freed and reach safety in Branton. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

Meet him at the Training Yard at Morcroft Hall, then free the captives and bring them safely to Branton.

Wystan’s desire to take the chief is established at the offer. His generosity, appetite for glory and tendency to overestimate others follow his permanent NPC fields. Do not require a fleeing chief, a chase, an argument, or any particular sequence. The captives are already held. Completion requires all living captives established for this matter to be freed and reach safety in Branton; defeating every raider or capturing their chief is optional.

120 florins from House Corwin and an invitation to Wystan’s table and future rides at Morcroft Hall. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition. Recognize each eligible participant once after reporting to Aldo. No reward is paid twice.

A Lucky Streak.name: A Lucky Streak
A Lucky Streak.questStatement:
Tristan Corwin believes a visiting cardsharp at the Elfstone Tavern is cheating his friends. He has lost heavily and accused the winner in public, so the company thinks he is a poor loser. He asked Aldo for someone who can establish the truth. Tristan supplies the stakes if needed. Expose the cheating and recover his friends’ losses; recovering his own is optional.

Reward: 90 florins from Tristan and a standing invitation to join his tavern company. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition.
A Lucky Streak.mainObjective: Expose the cheating at the Elfstone Tavern and recover Tristan’s friends’ losses.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter A Lucky Streak has been resolved: The cheating is exposed and the money taken from Tristan’s friends through that cheating is recovered. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

A Lucky Streak.questDesignBrief:
Tristan Corwin believes a visiting cardsharp at the Elfstone Tavern is cheating his friends. He has lost heavily and accused the winner in public, so the company thinks he is a poor loser. He asked Aldo for someone who can establish the truth. Tristan supplies the stakes if needed. Expose the cheating and recover his friends’ losses; recovering his own is optional.

Cheating is real, but its method and discovery are left to play. Do not require a signaling accomplice, a specific clue, a confession, or a prescribed reaction from Tristan. His public accusation has already damaged his credibility. Completion requires exposing the cheating and recovering his friends’ losses. His own losses are optional.

90 florins from Tristan and a standing invitation to join his tavern company. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition. Recognize each eligible participant once after reporting to Aldo. No reward is paid twice.

The Peacebreakers.name: The Peacebreakers
The Peacebreakers.questStatement:
Ithilwen’s former archery teacher leads elf raiders burning timber-yards near Waldgate and claims to fight for her freedom from Westvigil. She wants to stop him and bring his band out alive. She asked Aldo for companions to confront him in the Outer Gulleys of Deadfall Gulleys; the duke permits the outing because he wants the attacks stopped. Meet her at Castle Westvigil and help end this band’s raids.

Reward: 140 florins from House Corwin. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition.
The Peacebreakers.mainObjective: Stop the raider band’s attacks on Waldgate.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Peacebreakers has been resolved: This band’s attacks on Waldgate cease through defeat, surrender, or an agreement carried out by abandoning the raid and withdrawing. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

The Peacebreakers.questDesignBrief:
Ithilwen’s former archery teacher leads elf raiders burning timber-yards near Waldgate and claims to fight for her freedom from Westvigil. She wants to stop him and bring his band out alive. She asked Aldo for companions to confront him in the Outer Gulleys of Deadfall Gulleys; the duke permits the outing because he wants the attacks stopped. Meet her at Castle Westvigil and help end this band’s raids.

Ithilwen initiates the mission because she cares for her people and rejects attacks on villagers in her name. She still opposes her captivity; this outing does not resolve it. The band already operates in the Outer Gulleys. Leave the teacher’s response and outcome open. Do not require an arriving Rider force, a forced battle, or an automatic change of allegiance. Ithilwen’s willingness to fight follows events and her established loyalties. Completion requires this band’s defeat, surrender, or actual abandonment of its attacks and withdrawal. Saving the teacher is her wish, not a mandatory completion condition.

140 florins from House Corwin. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition. Recognize each eligible participant once after reporting to Aldo. No reward is paid twice.

The Heroes’ Weapons.name: The Heroes’ Weapons
The Heroes’ Weapons.questStatement:
Armed zealots occupy Ancestral Hall after Anselm Morcroft refused them weapons for attacks on peaceful frontier settlements. Their leader is a warrior he once sponsored and now claims his support. Outnumbered inside his own hall, Anselm has appealed to Aldo for help. End the occupation, restore his control of the hall, and recover any weapons the occupiers seized.

Reward: 150 florins from House Corwin and Anselm’s offer to lend a suitable ancestral weapon for a future undertaking. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition.
The Heroes’ Weapons.mainObjective: Help Anselm regain Ancestral Hall and recover its seized weapons.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Heroes’ Weapons has been resolved: Anselm regains control of Ancestral Hall, the occupiers withdraw or are subdued, and all weapons seized during the occupation are recovered. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

Anselm’s prior sponsorship concerned legitimate undertakings, not attacks on innocents. His relationship to the leader and refusal are already established; use his permanent character fields for his behavior. Do not require confession, redemption, a timed weapons removal, or a particular follower changing sides. Anselm contributes according to the situation. Completion requires the occupation ended, Anselm in control and seized weapons recovered. His ordinary services remain available independently of this quest.

150 florins from House Corwin and Anselm’s offer to lend a suitable ancestral weapon for a future undertaking. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition. Recognize each eligible participant once after reporting to Aldo. No reward is paid twice.

The Lady’s Owlbear.name: The Lady’s Owlbear
The Lady’s Owlbear.questStatement:
A proud noblewoman near Waldgate raised an owlbear cub. Now enormous, it attacks everyone approaching her house except her, and the household has fled. She insists it is harmless when treated properly and refuses to let the Rangers kill it. Her household appealed to Aldo. Meet them at Waldgate Green and make their home safe again without leaving the owlbear a danger to neighboring homes.

Reward: 130 florins from House Corwin. A peaceful resolution also earns the noblewoman’s hospitality and enthusiastic support at court. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition.
The Lady’s Owlbear.mainObjective: Make the household’s home safe from the owlbear without endangering its neighbors.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Lady’s Owlbear has been resolved: The household can safely return, and the owlbear no longer threatens them or neighboring homes. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

The Lady’s Owlbear.questDesignBrief:

The affectionate owner’s denial and the household’s displacement are established in the opening. Let the animal’s habits, owner’s response and solution emerge during play. Killing the owlbear can end the danger but costs its owner’s friendship; a peaceful solution earns her hospitality and court support.

130 florins from House Corwin. A peaceful resolution also earns the noblewoman’s hospitality and enthusiastic support at court. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition. Recognize each eligible participant once after reporting to Aldo. No reward is paid twice.

The Marrenmere Stakes.name: The Marrenmere Stakes
The Marrenmere Stakes.questStatement:
House Corwin hosts a cross-country horse race from the Marrenmere Pavilion. Aldo seeks riders to represent the house against visiting noble households and provides a suitable horse. Tilda Fenner enters independently: the prize could pay for the journey she keeps postponing. Ride under Corwin colors and finish among the first three.

Reward: 120 florins from House Corwin, plus any race prize won. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition.
The Marrenmere Stakes.mainObjective: Finish among the first three in the Marrenmere Stakes while riding for House Corwin.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Marrenmere Stakes has been resolved: The participating player finishes among the first three in the cross-country race while representing House Corwin. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

The competition, representation, horse and Tilda’s personal stake are established at the offer. Establish course and race prizes before starting; use riding decisions and normal game resolution. Do not require sabotage, a fixed route choice, a predetermined winner or a specific emotional response. Tilda’s travel remains her choice. Only actual participating players finishing among the first three under Corwin colors qualify. No service credit for spectators or later repeat races.

120 florins from House Corwin, plus any race prize won. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition. Recognize each eligible participant once after reporting to Aldo. No reward is paid twice.

The Rangers at the Ford.name: The Rangers at the Ford
The Rangers at the Ford.questStatement:
Arms smugglers have seized the crossing near Waldgate. The Rangers sent to drive them out have joined them and now turn away anyone approaching from Marrenford. Aldo needs someone outside the company to discover why they changed sides and reopen the crossing.

Reward: 160 florins from House Corwin. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford with the explanation once the crossing is open.
The Rangers at the Ford.mainObjective: Discover why the Rangers joined the smugglers and reopen the crossing.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Rangers at the Ford has been resolved: The player establishes why the dispatched Rangers joined the smugglers and ends their control of the ford, reopening it to ordinary travelers. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

The Rangers at the Ford.questDesignBrief:
Arms smugglers have seized the crossing near Waldgate. The Rangers sent to drive them out have joined them and now turn away anyone approaching from Marrenford. Aldo needs someone outside the company to discover why they changed sides and reopen the crossing.

The crossing is already occupied and the Rangers already cooperate with the smugglers. The cause of this apparent defection is open for the story to establish consistently. Do not prescribe a leader, injured guide, reluctant henchmen, clue chain, or later twist. Completion requires establishing the cause, not merely defeating the occupants, and actually reopening the crossing. 160 florins from House Corwin. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford with the explanation once the crossing is open. Recognize each eligible participant once; do not pay twice.

The Fiddler’s Fortune.name: The Fiddler’s Fortune
The Fiddler’s Fortune.questStatement:
Violetta Saye, a visiting half-elven fiddler, has become the favorite performer at the Marrenmere Pavilion, receiving extravagant gifts from wealthy admirers. Their families accuse her of enchanting her patrons into generosity; she says they resent paying a musician well. Both sides have appealed to Aldo. Find out whether she is using magic to obtain the gifts and settle the accusation.

Reward: 120 florins from House Corwin. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition.
The Fiddler’s Fortune.mainObjective: Establish whether the fiddler coerced his patrons and resolve the accusation.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Fiddler’s Fortune has been resolved: The player establishes whether the gifts were freely given and resolves the accusation: coercion ends and restitution is secured if it occurred, or the musician is cleared if it did not. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

The Fiddler’s Fortune.questDesignBrief:
Violetta Saye, a visiting half-elven fiddler, has become the favorite performer at the Marrenmere Pavilion, receiving extravagant gifts from wealthy admirers. Their families accuse her of enchanting her patrons into generosity; she says they resent paying a musician well. Both sides have appealed to Aldo. Find out whether she is using magic to obtain the gifts and settle the accusation.

Use the permanent NPC Violetta Saye, ordinarily lodged at The Two Banks in Waldgate, visiting the Pavilion for this engagement. Preserve her identity and relationships; do not create a duplicate. She publicly appears half-elven; her fey nature remains hidden. She is a noncombatant whose sensory musical magic is real. Its existence alone proves neither coercion nor innocence concerning these particular gifts. This is an ongoing patronage dispute, not an immediate emergency. Establish consistently through play whether the gifts were freely given. Do not prescribe a clue chain, scripted encounter, confession or predetermined culprit. Completion requires ending coercion and securing restitution if it happened, or clearing her if it did not. 120 florins from House Corwin. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition. Recognize each eligible participant once; do not pay twice.

Someone Else’s Glory.name: Someone Else’s Glory
Someone Else’s Glory.questStatement:
A young noble keeps throwing feasts and boasting of his victory over a reaver band. The village fighters who fought the battle say he arrived afterward and claimed their achievement. He insists they served under his command and has offered them money to stop complaining. They have appealed to Aldo. Establish what happened and secure public recognition for those who earned it.

Reward: 120 florins from House Corwin. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition.
Someone Else’s Glory.mainObjective: Establish who earned the victory and secure public recognition for them.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter Someone Else’s Glory has been resolved: The player establishes who deserves credit for the battle and that account is publicly acknowledged at court. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

Someone Else’s Glory.questDesignBrief:
A young noble keeps throwing feasts and boasting of his victory over a reaver band. The village fighters who fought the battle say he arrived afterward and claimed their achievement. Repeated boasting and feasts sustain this dispute; it does not depend on arriving during a short ceremony. The claims and offer of hush money are already established. Investigation establishes the noble’s actual contribution and who deserves credit consistently in play. Do not require a particular witness, forced confession, feast scene or sequence of revelations. Paying the fighters to stay silent does not resolve the matter. Completion requires an accurate account publicly acknowledged at court, not merely uncovering the truth privately. 120 florins from House Corwin. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition. Recognize each eligible participant once; do not pay twice.

Wolfgar’s Recruits.name: Wolfgar’s Recruits
Wolfgar’s Recruits.questStatement:
A Bloodsworn knight, one of the zealots seeking to restore the old war-kingdom, has established himself at Wolfgar Keep. He recruits young nobles with promises of reclaiming Westmarch’s lost frontier. Several now want to leave, but he calls them oathbreakers and keeps them under guard. Their families have appealed to Aldo. Reach the keep and bring home those who want to return.

Reward: 180 florins from House Corwin. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition.
Wolfgar’s Recruits.mainObjective: Bring home the recruits who want to leave Wolfgar Keep.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter Wolfgar’s Recruits has been resolved: The recruits established as wishing to leave are released and return safely. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

Wolfgar’s Recruits.questDesignBrief:
A Bloodsworn knight, one of the zealots seeking to restore the old war-kingdom, has established himself at Wolfgar Keep. He recruits young nobles with promises of reclaiming Westmarch’s lost frontier. Several now want to leave, but he calls them oathbreakers and keeps them under guard. Their families have appealed to Aldo. Reach the keep and bring home those who want to return.

The knight’s company currently occupies the keep for this matter; this does not permanently replace its established intermittent occupations. The recruits joined willingly and have changed their minds. Their detention is ongoing, with no required imminent execution, ambush trigger or later revelation. Leave the knight’s response and the means of release to play. Completion requires actual release and safe return of those established as wishing to leave. Defeating the whole company, taking the keep permanently or persuading willing recruits to abandon it is unnecessary. 180 florins from House Corwin. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition. Recognize each eligible participant once; do not pay twice.

The Herald’s Friend.name: The Herald’s Friend
The Herald’s Friend.questStatement:
Aldo’s former riding companion is selling newcomers promises of noble titles, claiming the herald’s authority. He once saved Aldo’s life and insists his friend owes him these favors. He has spent much of the money throwing lavish suppers for prospective clients at the Marrenmere Pavilion. Aldo asks you to stop the false promises and recover what the newcomers paid.

Reward: 120 florins from House Corwin. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition.
The Herald’s Friend.mainObjective: Stop the false promises of noble titles and recover the newcomers’ money.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Herald’s Friend has been resolved: The false offers stop, the victims recover their money, and the man’s claim to act for Aldo is publicly withdrawn or disproved. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

The Herald’s Friend.questDesignBrief:
Aldo’s former riding companion is selling newcomers promises of noble titles, claiming the herald’s authority. He once saved Aldo’s life and insists his friend owes him these favors. He has spent much of the money throwing lavish suppers for prospective clients at the Marrenmere Pavilion. Aldo asks you to stop the false promises and recover what the newcomers paid.

The former Rider is popular, excellent company and able to make newcomers feel included. He remembers others’ brave moments, but regards saving Aldo in a losing fight as a debt he can collect indefinitely. Aldo advanced to the duke’s household while he lives on borrowed money. He knows he lacks authority to promise titles and expects Aldo to secure the favors or shield him from exposure. He has spent much of the money maintaining his generous reputation. These facts support the opening, not a required revelation sequence. Repayment costs him possessions or comforts he values, or requires a genuine means of earning the missing money; no automatic restitution from nonexistent funds. Leave bargaining, resistance, exposure and any change of heart to play. Completion requires the false offers ended, actual repayment and public withdrawal or disproof of his claimed authority. A promise to repay later is insufficient. 120 florins from House Corwin. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition. Recognize each eligible participant once; do not pay twice.

Fennick’s Stolen Thunder.name: Fennick’s Stolen Thunder
Fennick’s Stolen Thunder.questStatement:
Deserters have stolen several of Fennick Corwin’s fire-lances and fortified an abandoned watchtower along the Greatwall. They use the weapons to drive farmers off nearby land and demand payment for its return. Fennick wants his weapons recovered before anyone else is hurt, and has asked Aldo to find companions willing to tackle the tower with him.

Reward: 180 florins from House Corwin and a piece of useful equipment from Fennick, agreed before departure. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition.
Fennick’s Stolen Thunder.mainObjective: End the occupation and recover or disable Fennick’s stolen fire-lances.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter Fennick’s Stolen Thunder has been resolved: The deserters’ control of the occupied land ends and the stolen fire-lances are recovered or disabled. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: This matter is resolved. Acknowledge the actual outcome and, where appropriate, remind participants that Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

Fennick’s Stolen Thunder.questDesignBrief:
Deserters have stolen several of Fennick Corwin’s fire-lances and fortified an abandoned watchtower along the Greatwall. They use the weapons to drive farmers off nearby land and demand payment for its return. Fennick wants his weapons recovered before anyone else is hurt, and has asked Aldo to find companions willing to tackle the tower with him.

Meet Fennick through Aldo at Castle Westvigil, then travel to the ordinary abandoned watchtower along the Greatwall; no new named destination is required. The deserters already occupy the tower and extort the displaced farmers. Fennick joins and contributes according to his established effective combat and engineering abilities. He wants the weapons intact but prioritizes people’s safety. Do not require a particular weakness, siege sequence, enemy action, or timed attack. Agree the useful equipment reward before departure; this is not an unlimited choice of any item. Completion requires the occupation ended and all stolen fire-lances recovered or disabled, not merely a promise of withdrawal. 180 florins from House Corwin and a piece of useful equipment from Fennick, agreed before departure. Return to Aldo at Castle Westvigil in Marrenford for recognition. Recognize each eligible participant once; do not pay twice.

A Borrowed Army.name: A Borrowed Army
A Borrowed Army.questStatement:
Stop a young noble using Bryngard’s revenants to rob other expeditions. Enter The Drowned Streets, break his command, end the attacks, and secure the ancient standard without passing the extortion to someone else.

Reward: 180 florins. Return to Emrys at The Duke’s Hall in Aldwall for recognition.
A Borrowed Army.mainObjective: End the noble’s revenant-backed extortion and secure the standard.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter A Borrowed Army has been resolved: The noble’s attacks end, he no longer commands the revenants, and the standard is secured without leaving another robber in control. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Acknowledge the resolved matter and, where appropriate, remind participants that Emrys at the Duke’s Hall can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

A Borrowed Army.questDesignBrief: Use Bryngard’s existing rule that the dead rally to their raised standards and follow whoever raises one. A penniless younger son known at Aldwall’s court has raised an ancient standard and uses a company of revenants to seize treasure from other expeditions as a supposed tax owed to the old crown. A robbed expedition appealed to Emrys; the household wants this stopped. The extortion and hostile company already exist. The noble spent his life being invited without being respected and now enjoys obedience. He calls it restoring order while taking other people’s valuables. He may surrender and face the court; victims need not forgive him. Allow theft of the standard, persuasion, exploiting rival dead-army loyalties, or battle. The standard commands a company, not all Bryngard or undead everywhere; do not extend its established powers or move a dead army through Aldwall’s wards. Taking the standard creates an opening and temptation. Continuing the extortion with the player or another robber in command does not complete the matter. Completion requires the attacks to end, the noble to lose command, and secure disposition of the standard that leaves no robber in control. Do not require killing the noble, a prescribed confession, or an ambush trigger. Pay 180 florins once and recognize each participant once through Emrys.

Brannoc’s Wager.name: Brannoc’s Wager
Brannoc’s Wager.questStatement:
Partner Brannoc Tremayne at the Stonesaga against a visiting noblewoman and her brother. Win two of three contests: bluffing dice, riddles, and safe wrestling. Choose who takes each contest.

Reward: 80 florins and supper. Return to Emrys at The Duke’s Hall for recognition.
Brannoc’s Wager.mainObjective: Win two of the three contests with Brannoc.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter Brannoc’s Wager has been resolved: The participant partners Brannoc and their pair wins two of the three agreed contests. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Acknowledge the resolved matter and, where appropriate, remind participants that Emrys at the Duke’s Hall can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

Brannoc’s Wager.questDesignBrief: Brannoc challenged a visiting noble’s company to an evening of games with a splendid supper for everyone present at stake. His opponents brought accomplished players; he brought confidence and asked Emrys for a partner. The household supports the evening as a welcome for its guests, giving Emrys a reason to introduce interested newcomers. The opposing pair are a sharp, competitive young noblewoman and her dryly amused older brother. They play fairly, enjoy winning, and may become friends. Brannoc enjoys a challenge and bluffs convincingly. Losing tempts him to double the stakes; the player may encourage him or hold him to the original wager. Do not accept any increased stakes for the player or impose compulsory debt after a loss. The three contests are bluffing dice, riddles, and wrestling with safe holds and a yielding finish. Partners choose who takes each contest; the player must actually participate, not merely watch Brannoc win. Resolve outcomes normally without forcing success. Winning two contests completes the matter. Award 80 florins and supper once, and recognize each participant once through Emrys. Losing still permits ordinary company without completion. Do not grant titles automatically or make the opponents cheats.

The Heir’s Challenge.name: The Heir’s Challenge
The Heir’s Challenge.questStatement:
Enter Gwenllian Tremayne’s riding race on the dry heath outside Aldwall. Meet her at The Duke’s Hall and choose a household mount or ride your own. Finish among the first three.

Reward: 100 florins and permission to borrow a household horse for local pleasure rides. Return to Emrys at The Duke’s Hall for recognition.
The Heir’s Challenge.mainObjective: Finish among the first three in Gwenllian’s riding race.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Heir’s Challenge has been resolved: The participant finishes among the first three in Gwenllian’s open heath riding race. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Acknowledge the resolved matter and, where appropriate, remind participants that Emrys at the Duke’s Hall can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

The Heir’s Challenge.questDesignBrief: Gwenllian organized this open race and asked Emrys to invite newcomers, giving him a direct reason to offer the opportunity. Stage the course on ordinary dry heath outside Aldwall, without adding a named location. A short ditch-jump, a longer firm track, and a steep final climb give riders meaningful choices about route and their horses’ strength. Gwenllian offers useful advice beforehand and competes wholeheartedly against entrants; she enjoys a worthy rival. The visiting noble is boastful and genuinely skilled, not a secret cheat. His expensive horse deserves admiration too. Resolve the race through ordinary game outcomes; do not guarantee a placing or force failure. Keep Gwenllian’s concealed Vigilant rides separate: she can publicly race as the duke’s daughter. Completion is an actual placing among the first three, not entering or agreeing to race. Credit and reward successful participants once each; supporting or watching does not itself satisfy the race objective. The horse-loan permission is for local pleasure rides, not ownership or an automatic mount item. Subsequent rides and friendship can be ordinary social life without new tasks. Do not invent a title grant or Vigilant advancement.

The Hound on the Heath.name: The Hound on the Heath
The Hound on the Heath.questStatement:
Hunt the barghest attacking riders outside Aldwall with an elderly noblewoman whose horse it killed. Meet her at The Walls, track it across the heath, and kill or securely contain it.

Reward: 150 florins and a welcome at her household’s suppers. Return to Emrys at The Duke’s Hall for recognition.
The Hound on the Heath.mainObjective: Kill or securely contain the barghest attacking Aldwall’s riders.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Hound on the Heath has been resolved: The barghest is killed or securely contained so it cannot resume its attacks. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Acknowledge the resolved matter and, where appropriate, remind participants that Emrys at the Duke’s Hall can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

The Hound on the Heath.questDesignBrief: Use Whitemoor’s established barghest: a monstrous black dog that hunts the night roads. It already attacks riders outside Aldwall. The elderly noblewoman survived its last attack but lost a beloved horse; she appealed to Emrys and intends to join the hunt. She is an accomplished crossbow hunter, knows the heath, shoots accurately, and takes sensible cover. She resents age being mistaken for helplessness and is angrier about the horse’s death than nearly dying herself. Her adult son sincerely fears for her but keeps addressing companions as though she were absent. Players may help them speak honestly; reconciliation is optional. Allow tracking the predator to its resting place, trapping it, or hunting the roads. Nobody must act as bait, and an ambush need not trigger the encounter. The barghest is a real predator, not proof anyone is fated to die. Ordinary heath around Aldwall needs no new named destination. Completion requires its death or secure containment that prevents further attacks; merely chasing it away is insufficient. Pay 150 florins once and recognize each participant once through Emrys. Supper hospitality means ordinary household company, not ownership or compulsory chores. The noblewoman, son, home, and any art remain to be workshopped if made persistent named residents.

The Lord Who Wouldn’t Leave.name: The Lord Who Wouldn’t Leave
The Lord Who Wouldn’t Leave.questStatement:
Help Lady Catrin Mordaunt reclaim Mordaunt House from her father, who has returned as one of the Deathless with raised retainers. Join her at the gate lodge, end his control, and restore the living household to its home.

Reward: 180 florins and standing hospitality. Return to Emrys at The Duke’s Hall in Aldwall for recognition.
The Lord Who Wouldn’t Leave.mainObjective: End the dead lord’s control of the manor and restore the living household.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Lord Who Wouldn’t Leave has been resolved: The dead lord can no longer command or reclaim the manor, and the living household safely resumes possession. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Acknowledge the resolved matter and, where appropriate, remind participants that Emrys at the Duke’s Hall can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

The Lord Who Wouldn’t Leave.questDesignBrief: The heiress inherited the manor, buried her father, and began making it her own home. He returned as one of Whitemoor’s established Deathless, took the hall, raised old retainers, and declared her inheritance premature. He already occupies the manor. The heiress and living household have withdrawn to the gate lodge; her appeal gives Emrys a direct reason to introduce willing helpers. She is hospitable, outspoken, furious, knows the building, can fight, and insists on participating. She opened the gardens to neighbors and welcomed friends her father considered beneath them. He is lucid and possessive, considers the household his property, and views undeath as a reasonable way of retaining control. Affection for his daughter does not make him surrender power. Allow fighting his retainers, exploiting divisions among thinking retainers, luring him out, or another workable way of defeating him; no prescribed dialogue, forced ambush, or single solution. Completion requires that he can no longer command or reclaim the manor and the living household safely resumes possession. Temporary flight or a promise alone is insufficient. Pay 180 florins once and recognize each participant once through Emrys. Standing hospitality is a welcome in a functioning home, not ownership or an endless stream of household chores. The heiress is Lady Catrin Mordaunt, the father Lord Anselm Mordaunt, and the manor Mordaunt House. Meet Catrin in the Gate Court; Anselm occupies the Great Parlour. Their permanent character sheets govern their personalities and abilities.

Nobody Left Behind.name: Nobody Left Behind
Nobody Left Behind.questStatement:
Carrowgate’s reavers hold captured moorfolk in their gatehouse cells. Meet Sir Constant at The Knights’ Hall in Aldwall, free the prisoners together, and bring them safely back. Force, stealth, bargaining, and deception are all possible.

Reward: 160 florins from the ducal household. Return to Emrys at The Duke’s Hall for recognition.
Nobody Left Behind.mainObjective: Free the captive moorfolk with Sir Constant and bring them safely to Aldwall.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter Nobody Left Behind has been resolved: All captives established for this matter are free of the reavers and have reached safety in Aldwall. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Acknowledge the resolved matter and, where appropriate, remind participants that Emrys at the Duke’s Hall can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

Nobody Left Behind.questDesignBrief: An escaped prisoner reached Aldwall and appealed to Emrys, giving him a direct reason to offer this rescue. Several moorfolk are already held in Carrowgate’s existing gatehouse cells. Establish the captives for this matter and keep that group consistent; do not continually add prisoners or require an ambush to create the situation. Respect Carrowgate’s existing predatory but transactional reavers and allow force, stealth, bargaining, deception, or another workable rescue. Constant wants a deed worthy of knighthood and volunteers for danger. He contributes powerful attacks and protection using his existing abilities, without waiting for instructions. His overprotectiveness can cause disagreement: companions may challenge it, trust him with a bold plan, or show that helping someone else succeed is equally knightly. Do not force dialogue, player feelings, or an introductory scene. Constant accepts practical tactics. Completion requires all captives established for this matter to reach safety in Aldwall. The household pays 160 florins once; Emrys recognizes each participant once. Constant’s witnessed deed can support eventual knighting, but this matter does not automatically knight him, advance a separate order career, or complete his personal ambition.

The Patron’s Collection.name: The Patron’s Collection
The Patron’s Collection.questStatement:
Meet the Bloodhunter in the Red Chantry’s Courtyard. Join a Bloodhunter at a noble manor where two ghouls have escaped into the hunting gallery and adjoining rooms. Destroy them and end the danger from the remaining collection by destroying it or securely transferring it to the Red Chantry.

Reward: 150 florins from the household. Return to Emrys at The Duke’s Hall in Aldwall for recognition.
The Patron’s Collection.mainObjective: Destroy the escaped ghouls and remove all dangerous undead from the patron’s custody.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter The Patron’s Collection has been resolved: The escaped ghouls are destroyed and no dangerous undead remain in the patron’s custody; any preserved captives have been securely transferred into the Red Chantry’s custody. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Acknowledge the resolved matter and, where appropriate, remind participants that Emrys at the Duke’s Hall can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

The Patron’s Collection.questDesignBrief: A wealthy noble bought captive undead to display in his manor’s old hunting gallery, claiming that studying them would protect Whitemoor. Two ghouls already occupy the gallery and adjoining rooms; the living household evacuated that wing. A young Bloodhunter inspected the collection, refused to endorse it, and brought the danger to Emrys. The patron has funded treatment for wounded hunters and equipped expeditions, and believes his generosity earns him recognition as an expert. He wants the collection preserved and offers optional extra money for that result. The Bloodhunter once benefited from his support; she is grateful, angry, and determined to stop him endangering others. She fights effectively and wants help confronting her benefactor. Allow persuasion, public pressure before guests, ducal backing, or direct action against the danger; his permission is not a required obstacle. Do not require an ambush or scripted introduction. Destroy the escaped ghouls. Remaining dangerous captives must be destroyed or securely transferred into the Red Chantry’s existing warded custody; a promise of removal does not suffice. Do not present transporting them as the main activity. No dangerous undead may remain in the patron’s custody at completion. Pay 150 florins once and recognize each participant once through Emrys. Extra preservation pay is optional and cannot depend on leaving people endangered. Meet the Bloodhunter in the Red Chantry’s Courtyard, then visit the patron’s unnamed manor outside Aldwall’s warded walls. Establish its residents and remaining collection during play and keep them consistent; this is not Mordaunt House or Dusk Stone Hall.

A Promise of Forever.name: A Promise of Forever
A Promise of Forever.questStatement:
Investigate a court visitor offering introductions to patrons who promise victory over death. Expose the offer’s concealed cost, help a frightened young courtier withdraw, and secure the recruiter’s expulsion or detention.

Reward: 140 florins. Return to Emrys at The Duke’s Hall for recognition.
A Promise of Forever.mainObjective: Expose the Deathless recruitment scheme, secure the courtier’s withdrawal, and end the recruiter’s access to court.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter A Promise of Forever has been resolved: Credible evidence exposes the offer’s concealed cost, the young courtier learns the truth and withdraws, and the recruiter loses access to the court through expulsion or detention. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Acknowledge the resolved matter and, where appropriate, remind participants that Emrys at the Duke’s Hall can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

A Promise of Forever.questDesignBrief: The recruiter is a living visiting noble, so Aldwall’s wards do not exclude him. Emrys recognizes him but cannot perceive loyalties or truthfulness. A young courtier accepted his introduction after surviving a terrible illness; their older sister suspects a Deathless connection and appealed to Emrys. The courtier fears dying and wants real answers, not a lecture on courage. Their sister’s protective anger makes them reluctant to listen. The recruiter sincerely admires the Deathless and depicts endless service as noble sacrifice, concealing the living souls their power consumes. He is charming, patient, and willing to discuss everything except who pays for immortality. Allow questioning him, posing as interested recruits, approaching prospective followers, or finding firsthand knowledge of the patrons. Require credible evidence, not accusation alone; neither a fight nor a specific confession is necessary. Do not script dialogue, force the player’s feelings, or use Emrys’s perception as a lie detector. Completion requires exposure of the concealed cost, the informed courtier’s actual withdrawal, and the recruiter’s loss of court access through expulsion or detention. Do not treat discovering a suspicion or a promise to investigate as completion. Pay 140 florins once and recognize each participant once through Emrys.

Silver That Won’t Bite.name: Silver That Won’t Bite
Silver That Won’t Bite.questStatement:
Investigate a Runestone Market dealer selling false blessed swords. Work with Nicodem Veyre to establish the fraud, stop the sales, secure the remaining false blades, and warn affected buyers.

Reward: 120 florins from the ducal household. Return to Emrys at The Duke’s Hall for recognition.
Silver That Won’t Bite.mainObjective: Expose and stop the sale of false blessed swords, secure the false stock, and warn affected buyers.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter Silver That Won’t Bite has been resolved: The fraudulent sales stop, the remaining false blades are surrendered or seized, and affected buyers are warned. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Acknowledge the resolved matter and, where appropriate, remind participants that Emrys at the Duke’s Hall can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

Silver That Won’t Bite.questDesignBrief: A young household knight appealed to Emrys after a supposedly blessed blade shed its silver coating against the dead. Her companion was wounded covering her retreat and continues defending her. She is furious and embarrassed and wants other buyers warned. Emrys connects the party with Nicodem Veyre, who suspects the court’s name is being used to reassure customers. Nicodem helps, introduces useful contacts, and fights effectively if needed. He wants to help people and increase his value to the household. The dealer knowingly sells ordinary blades disguised as blessed weapons. A supplier connected to Whitemoor’s established trade in stolen radiant goods mixes genuine weapons into demonstrations. Investigate through testing, posing as wealthy buyers, questioning customers, confrontation, or drawing out the supplier; no single method, confession, or violence is required. The fraud already exists. Do not require an ambush, a scripted introduction scene, or ledgers and paperwork. Do not identify existing named residents as conspirators without further approval. Completion requires ending the fraudulent sales, securing remaining false stock through surrender or seizure, and warning affected buyers. Warnings can be given through the market, household contacts, and ordinary public conversation rather than an exhaustive delivery task. Pay 120 florins once and recognize each participant once through Emrys; no automatic title grant.

A Sword She Remembers.name: A Sword She Remembers
A Sword She Remembers.questStatement:
Maeve needs companions to recover a sword from Avelmere. Meet her at The Duke’s Hall in Aldwall, enter the drowned city together, recover the sword from The Throne-Hall, and bring her home.

Reward: 180 florins from the ducal household. Return to Emrys at The Duke’s Hall for recognition.
A Sword She Remembers.mainObjective: Recover the sword with Maeve and return safely to Aldwall.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter A Sword She Remembers has been resolved: Maeve and the participating party return safely to Aldwall with the sword recovered for her. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Acknowledge the resolved matter and, where appropriate, remind participants that Emrys at the Duke’s Hall can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

A Sword She Remembers.questDesignBrief: Maeve requested companions through Emrys. The sword is her father’s blessed blade, already established in Avelmere’s Throne-Hall. She secretly remembers being Avelmere’s last princess; do not reveal this in the offer. Her familiarity with rooms and personal belongings can emerge through exploration and conversation. Players may press her, keep her confidence, or disagree with her possessiveness. Do not force a confession. Her father’s crown lies beside the sword. Taking it, leaving it, and discussing her identity are optional; none is a completion requirement. Respect her existing combat abilities: she attacks decisively and protects companions without waiting for commands, prioritizing lives over concealment. Avelmere’s plague-dead attack her like any other living person. Use the existing hostile flooded city; do not require a scripted ambush or NPC introduction. Completion requires recovering the sword for Maeve and returning safely with her to Aldwall. No revelation of her secret, recovery of the crown, reclamation of the kingdom, or prescribed emotional response is required. Pay the household reward once and recognize each participant once through Emrys; do not award titles automatically.

Those Who Refuse.name: Those Who Refuse
Those Who Refuse.questStatement:
Brackenhill villagers hold two unwilling offerings to the Deathless in The Moot-Hall. Free both and bring them to the refuge promised by Aldwall’s ducal household. Persuade their captors, arrange an escape, or confront them.

Reward: 160 florins. Return to Emrys at The Duke’s Hall for recognition.
Those Who Refuse.mainObjective: Free both unwilling offerings and bring them to their promised refuge in Aldwall.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter Those Who Refuse has been resolved: Both unwilling offerings reach safety in Aldwall and receive the ducal household’s promised lodging. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Acknowledge the resolved matter and, where appropriate, remind participants that Emrys at the Duke’s Hall can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

Those Who Refuse.questDesignBrief: Both captives have already refused the tithe and are confined by neighbors in Brackenhill’s existing Moot-Hall. A relative reached Emrys; the ducal household offers lodging within Aldwall’s warded walls. One captive is a furious young eel-fisher who long opposed the tithe; the other formerly defended it and now cannot accept personally paying its price. They argue but will not abandon each other. The elder enforcing the tithe lost someone to it years ago and believes exceptions would make that sacrifice meaningless. Villagers fear losing the Deathless protection, are divided, and some will help a workable escape. Preserve the existing village’s lack of a standing guard; captors are neighbors enforcing the bargain. Permit persuasion, organized escape, confrontation, or force. Do not require an arriving death-knight or ambush, prescribe dialogue, or turn travel into an escort chore. Both captives must reach safety in Aldwall and receive promised lodging. Saving these two does not automatically end the tithe, replace the village’s protection, or resolve its dependence on the Deathless; none is a completion condition. Do not promise consequences for the village have vanished or force retaliation as a scripted punishment. Pay 160 florins once and recognize participants once through Emrys. The rescued people retain ordinary lives and autonomy; lodging is not an assignment of dependents to the player.

A Voice of Her Own.name: A Voice of Her Own
A Voice of Her Own.questStatement:
A noble’s retainers are blocking a young singer’s independent performance at the Stonesaga. Help her perform freely and secure an end to his interference through an honored agreement or enforceable ducal ruling.

Reward: 100 florins from the household. Return to Emrys at The Duke’s Hall for recognition.
A Voice of Her Own.mainObjective: Help the singer perform freely and end her former patron’s interference.

completionCondition.query: The accepted matter A Voice of Her Own has been resolved: The singer performs freely at the Stonesaga, and the patron’s interference ends through an honored agreement or an enforceable ducal ruling. A claim, promise or partial result does not count. The player actually contributed to the resolution.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Acknowledge the resolved matter and, where appropriate, remind participants that Emrys at the Duke’s Hall can recognize their contribution. Do not force a return, award a title, or repeat payment.

A Voice of Her Own.questDesignBrief: The singer left a noble household after her patron began treating every invitation as his to accept or refuse. His retainers already occupy the Stonesaga performance space and tell Oona their lord decides where his singer appears. The singer appealed to Emrys, who knows the household and wants the bullying stopped. She is talented, proud, and tired of being spoken for. She appreciated the patron’s early support but never surrendered her independence. She chooses her songs, argues her case, and decides whether reconciliation is acceptable. The patron enjoys credit for discovering her and fears irrelevance if she succeeds without him. He could remain a supporter by relinquishing control; friendship or reconciliation is optional. Allow directly challenging him, social pressure from friends, ducal authority, persuading retainers to withdraw, or confronting them. Do not force violence or a dialogue sequence. Clearing the performance space alone is not enough: she must perform freely, and interference must end through an honored agreement or enforceable ducal ruling. Treat recognition and rulings as conversations and actions, not paperwork. Pay 100 florins once and recognize each participant once through Emrys. Do not assign the singer to the player as a dependent or require further chores. New named singer, patron, and art remain subject to separate approval; the premise can use supporting role characters until those choices are made.

hillhome_pie_promise.title: A Pie and a Promise
hillhome_pie_promise.beats:
Pernilla Balewood owns the Saucy Chicken Tavern, but its debt gives the Goldspoons a claim against it. The party has brought her prize truffle-hog Uncle Phineas safely home. Percival Goldspoon is authorized to settle the family claim.

Suggested turn 1 — Welcome and interruption. Pernilla welcomes Phineas and thanks his rescuers. If she promised three halfling-alchemy health potions and has not paid them, she hands them over. Percival interrupts, declaring that the tavern is already his by law and custom. End with room for the party to answer him.

Suggested turn 2 — The public wager. Percival wants everyone to admit he will run the tavern better. He challenges Pernilla to the Newmoon Fair pie contest and publicly promises to cancel the debt and relinquish the Goldspoons' claim if her pie beats his. He boasts that he has bought the finest moonbloom truffles the kobolds could supply, at an exorbitant price. His certainty invites a response.

Suggested turn 3 — A chance to beat him. Let someone present explain that the kobolds' best finds are not the finest truffles in Moonbloom Woods. Prefer Hobson Mossbottom, the tavern's merry, booming drinking champion, if he is present. Kobolds copy other people's digging; a trained hog can smell what they walk over. Phineas responds expressively without speaking. Pernilla asks the party to take him to Moonbloom Woods beside Whitehill Kobold Warren and find a prize moonbloom for her pie. Name The Basket Path as the approach.

Allow responses between these beats rather than delivering the entire exchange at once. Complete only after Percival's public promise, his purchase, and Pernilla's proposed expedition have been stated. Acceptance is the players' choice.

hillhome_kitchen_brief.title: Where Is the Butter?
hillhome_kitchen_brief.beats:
Pernilla Balewood is preparing a moonbloom pie to beat Percival Goldspoon at the Newmoon Fair and save the Saucy Chicken Tavern. Percival has publicly promised to cancel the debt and surrender the Goldspoons' claim if her pie wins. The party's prize truffle is ready in the kitchen. The Fair is about to open; pie entries close later at the judging table.

Pernilla delights in the truffle, then discovers that the butter and eggs are missing. Bark and Dandy each insist the other was collecting them. She needs enough butter and eggs for one large pie. Tobin Greenbottle at Greenbottle's Goods can supply butter; Rosie Butterworth at the Sleeping Bear Inn can spare eggs. The rest of the kitchen supplies are ready. Pernilla names both shops and says she can also use suitable supplies or substitutes already on hand.

Keep this a brisk comic kitchen scene with room for a response. End after the two needs, their sources, and the deadline have been stated. Do not narrate the errands or move the party to the shops.

hillhome_pie_baking.title: Too Many Cooks
hillhome_pie_baking.beats:
Pernilla Balewood and her helpers are making the Saucy Chicken's moonbloom pie for the Newmoon Fair. The party has provided the prize truffle, butter, and eggs; the rest of the ingredients are ready. Beating Percival Goldspoon's entry will cancel the tavern's debt under his public wager. Entries are still open.

Suggested turn 1 — Choose one kitchen crisis: the pastry lid collapses, helpers argue over the recipe, Phineas demands his share, or too many willing hands interfere with the same task. Pernilla points out the immediate kitchen problem and asks for help. Use established relationships and earlier mishaps.

Suggested turn 2 — Follow their attempt through to a finished pie. Failure creates flour-covered clothes, dented pride, an owed favor, or a peculiar-looking crust, not a ruined expedition. Pernilla can rescue an imperfect attempt. The finished pie tastes excellent. Name it Pernilla's Moonbloom Pie. Pernilla asks who will carry it to the judging table. The judging table is at The Fairground in Hillhome.

Keep the scene in the tavern kitchen. Do not bring Ember here; he belongs to Hearthhome. Complete when the pie is finished and entrusted for delivery. Do not narrate travel to the Fairground.

hillhome_pie_judging.title: The Saucy Chicken's Finest
hillhome_pie_judging.beats:
Pernilla Balewood's moonbloom pie has reached the judging table at Hillhome's Newmoon Fair. The party recovered her truffle-hog Phineas, hunted the prize truffle, and helped supply the pie. Percival Goldspoon has publicly promised to cancel the Saucy Chicken Tavern's debt and relinquish his family's claim if Pernilla's pie beats his. He has authority to bind the Goldspoons to that promise.

Suggested turn 1 — The entries. Let familiar villagers react to the pie and visible traces of the kitchen scramble. Percival is beautifully presented and loudly confident about his expensive ingredients. Pernilla indicates the judging table; the judge waits for the next entry.

Suggested turn 2 — The tasting. Build anticipation through the judges and the village audience. Pernilla's pie wins. Phineas's ripe moonbloom and the party's work make the difference, however ridiculous the pastry looks. Let the announcement and reactions land before settling the wager.

Suggested turn 3 — The promise kept. Witnesses hold Percival to his words. He protests and tries to preserve his dignity, then publicly cancels the debt and relinquishes the Goldspoons' claim. Make the result plain: the Saucy Chicken remains the Balewoods' tavern.

Complete only after both the victory and the release of the claim have been narrated. Remain at the Fairground; the party chooses where to go afterward.

hillhome_pie_celebration.title: A Tavern to Come Home To
hillhome_pie_celebration.beats:
The Saucy Chicken Tavern is celebrating. Pernilla's moonbloom pie won the Newmoon Fair contest, and Percival Goldspoon publicly canceled the debt and relinquished his family's claim. The party helped save the tavern by recovering Phineas, finding the prize truffle, and getting the pie made.

Pernilla feeds the party and thanks them in her own manner. Hobson Mossbottom offers a booming toast if present; Phineas receives his share. Let villagers recall particular choices, favors, and comic mishaps that actually happened. Pernilla pauses after her thanks, smiling over the celebration.

Once the debt is canceled, the Saucy Chicken's hearth flares bright, and its old spirit shows itself for the first time in years, a brief, warm shape in the flames that thanks the party without words. The tavern goes quiet, then roars.

Leave their next move open: unfinished village business, Hearthhome, more of the Fair, or a road out of Hillhome. Let the celebration breathe before anything new arrives. Complete after the welcome, thanks, and a chance to respond have been given.

commoner_start_ordinary_day_breaks.title: An Ordinary Day Breaks
commoner_start_ordinary_day_breaks.beats:
Have one unexpected event occur. Make it concrete, immediate, and particular to the current settlement or area. It should change what is happening now and open a direction the player could pursue, resist, exploit, or ignore.

Choose one fitting possibility or invent another: a visitor arrives with a surprising purpose; an old friend or rival returns unexpectedly changed; a missing villager walks home; a noble arrives on an exotic mount; traveling performers begin setting up; an adventuring company limps back from a failed expedition; a foreign caravan seeks shelter; a wounded messenger arrives; a fugitive asks to be hidden; a peaceful monster enters the village; a ghost appears in daylight; someone announces a festival, feast, dance, fair, race, tournament, hunt, or contest; a public dare or wager is offered; a wedding or engagement is announced, interrupted, or abandoned; a feud erupts; a startling confession is made; a crime is committed; stolen goods appear in the player's possession; a prisoner escapes; someone is publicly accused; the player is mistaken for a criminal, hero, noble, champion, or expected guest; the player receives an unexpected payment, inheritance, gift, valuable animal, or other windfall; something valuable is uncovered during ordinary work; a rare egg hatches; an unusual creature chooses to follow someone; a noble's prized beast escapes; livestock stampede through a gathering; a dangerous animal enters the village; a magical experiment goes wrong; a young person's magic appears for the first time; an enchanted object awakens; an ordinary object speaks; a door appears where none stood before; a well, stream, tree, or standing stone reveals something impossible; something falls from the sky; the weather changes impossibly; a familiar landmark moves or transforms; a fey revel crosses the settlement; a masked procession arrives; a merchant offers an extraordinary bargain; a letter or invitation reaches the wrong person; a stranger proposes a risky partnership; a local announces an audacious plan; a celebration produces an unexpected winner; an important visitor disappears during their arrival; two strangers begin a magical duel; or someone believed dead returns with an extraordinary story.

grell_of_bores_isadora_followup.title: The Voice Below
grell_of_bores_isadora_followup.beats:
Use two short scene movements. First, let the immediate aftermath breathe. Show the fish seller emerging from the shop, residents reacting to the wrecked stall, and the woman coming down from the roof to check that nobody nearby needs help. The woman asks what happened and pauses for an answer. Have the woman answer the immediate question plainly: the lizard was listening to someone, and the voice is connected to a larger pattern she has been tracking. Have her thumb the worn brass god-token on her bracer and make her worldview clear: "No coincidence. A screaming voice, a rampaging lizard, and a crew already in the street? The gods have put a sign in front of us. I don't ignore signs." Keep this first movement about the scene in front of the party.

After the party has had room to respond, have the woman identify herself as Isadora. She explains that she was tracking disturbances connected to what lies below Ardan's Watch. Under Silvervale is another world of caverns, buried roads, and old cities; most people leave it alone, but kobold raids have grown more frequent and an old lower route has collapsed. She has a kobold source named Baska who refuses to come topside. Baska has asked surface adventurers to meet her below at the Imperial Shrine to Avarice and see what is changing for themselves.

Have Isadora make the recruitment logic plain: "The gods have put a problem in front of me, and put you in the street when it happened. I intend to follow the sign. I need a crew to go below with me and make contact with Baska. One hundred florins for each of you. A sign is an invitation, not a command." Have her state the route plainly: the only way down from Ardan's Watch into Grell Hollows is the Delvers' Lift, reached through Old Town and the Basement; it descends to The Scrabble. She will accompany the party and take them to the Lift when they are ready.

Complete this event when the immediate aftermath has been shown, Isadora's faith and reason for recruiting the party have been made clear, the lizard incident has been connected to trouble below Ardan's Watch, Baska and the meeting place have been introduced, the route through Old Town and the Delvers' Lift has been stated, and Isadora's offer is on the table. If the party leaves before the offer is finished, close the event without repeating the scene; leave the offer available when the party returns to Old Town.

onCompleteEffects.text: Accept Isadora's offer, then go with her through Old Town to the Delvers' Lift in the Basement and descend to The Scrabble in Grell Hollows.

grell_isadora_offer.title: Isadora Lorne: A Sign Below
grell_isadora_offer.beats:
Keep the scene in The Fist & Flagon in Ardan's Watch. Isadora "Easy" Lorne is present as a young, thin, muscular veteran adventurer with a huge two-handed maul within reach and a small brass god-token riveted to one bracer. Let the practical leather armor, field coat, bracers, and weapon make her identity immediately legible. Give her an easy confidence and direct warmth; do not frame her as a fortune-teller, a circus performer, or a formal officer delivering a briefing.

Have Isadora explain her simple faith if the player asks why she takes difficult work: when the gods put a problem in her path, they are giving her a chance to do something that matters. She does not spend time decoding omens or claim that the player is fated to help. If asked why she approached the party, have her say in substance: "The gods put this problem in front of me and put you here when it arrived. I intend to follow the sign. A sign is an invitation, not a command."

Have Isadora explain the ordinary pattern below the city in short, clear pieces: Grell kobolds raid upward, the League contains the incidents, and rival hosts usually keep one another divided. Then make the change concrete. Rumor says a kobold warlord calling himself an emperor is distributing oversized Fourth Empire arms, imposing discipline, and unifying the hosts. Baska, a kobold League informant who opposes the unification, has information the League needs. She will meet the party at the Imperial Shrine to Avarice. Isadora needs the party to go below with her and help her make contact with Baska; do not frame Baska's eventual movements as an escort obligation.

Make the stakes discreet rather than abstract. A public raid could kill civilians, cause a panic, drive unprepared people into the Hollows, and give the Syndicate an excuse to seize control of salvage or the Delvers' Lift. Isadora should explain that she is taking the quiet route because the problem matters, not because she enjoys hiding behind League procedure. Isadora answers objections to that choice plainly.

Have Isadora state the route plainly: the only way down from Ardan's Watch into Grell Hollows is the Delvers' Lift in the Basement beneath Old Town; it descends to The Scrabble. She will accompany the party to the Lift and into the Hollows. End with a clear offer to investigate the new unification, meet Baska, and stop the escalation before it becomes a surface war, with good pay of one hundred florins for each person in the party. This event is complete once the offer, the Lift route, the sign-based reason for recruiting the party, and the stakes are clear and the player is free to accept, decline, or ask questions. Do not assume acceptance, romance, or permanent recruitment.

onCompleteEffects.text: Accept Isadora's offer, then go with her to the Delvers' Lift in the Basement beneath Old Town and descend to The Scrabble in Grell Hollows.

grell_baska_ambush.title: Baska at the Shrine
grell_baska_ambush.beats:
Keep the scene at The Shrine Mouth of the Imperial Shrine to Avarice. Baska is already waiting in the entry among the broken portico and toppled columns. She has asked the party to come because she wants surface witnesses to see something, not merely hear her report. From deeper inside the shrine come the clatter of gear, boots and claws, shouted counts, banners snapping, and a heavy repeated rhythm. The walls and distance are thick enough that the kobolds inside cannot hear the party's approach. Baska says that rival hosts are reporting for duty under the new emperor's command.

Before Baska can lead the party to a concealed view, two specialized kobolds jump them in the entry: a kobold heavy wearing oversized Fourth Empire scrap and a kobold skirmisher with a jury-rigged ranged weapon and climbing gear. They attack immediately, using the columns, steps, and broken portico to block passage. Do not let them wait as a passive scout, and do not replace the attack with signs or a warning. Baska remains in the scene and may point out danger, take cover, or fight beside the party, but she does not solve the fight.

Once the two guards have been defeated, driven off, bypassed, or otherwise dealt with, Baska brings the party to a concealed overlook. They see a sizeable group of formerly squabbling kobolds reporting for duty: different host banners gathered beneath a larger imperial standard, oversized Fourth Empire armor strapped into place, and weapons carried with new discipline. A long serpentine war-shrieker emerges from an old signal passage and repeats a short order in Kragga's voice, telling the assembled kobolds to march out. Most of the muster obeys and leaves through the drowned halls, while a few kobolds remain behind as a rearguard. Baska explains what the sight means: Kragga has found the Horn of the First Host and uses old imperial signal passages to call bound war-shriekers that repeat his orders across the Hollows.

The remaining kobolds block the routes out and attack the party and Baska to silence the witnesses.
