Make the blockade physically and tactically legible; egress requires defeating, evading, bargaining past, or otherwise breaking the attackers' hold. Baska fights to survive and helps the party read the ruin, but she must remain alive. Do not invent an unnamed League contact, kill Baska, or resolve the scene by teleporting the party away. Complete the event when the immediate rearguard has been broken or bypassed and the party has witnessed the muster. Baska remains a living League contact; do not require the party to escort her to Ardan's Watch or state that she has already reached the surface.

onCompleteEffects.text: Return to Ardan's Watch and report the situation to the League.

grell_volnom_council_report.title: The League Report
grell_volnom_council_report.beats:
Stage this in Watchtower - League Hall in Ardan's Watch, with Gwyneth Valcazar, a League Champion on the Council of Champions, receiving the party's report at the League's main table or in a quieter corner of the hall. The party may already have delivered the report to Gwyneth, Volnom the Wayfarer, or another clearly established League representative elsewhere in Ardan's Watch; if so, treat this scene as the formal League recording and response, not as a demand that the party repeat facts they have already established. Baska need not be present and must not be assumed to have been transported into Ardan's Watch; the League is acting on the information the party brought back from the shrine.

Confirm the essential report in natural conversation: Baska showed the party an organized kobold muster; Kragga has found the Horn of the First Host in the Imperial Arsenal; and the horn's surviving signal passages call and coordinate bound war-shriekers. Establish that the long serpentine fiends repeat short orders in Kragga's voice across the Hollows, giving separate kobold hosts a reach and timing they never had before. The horn carries commands; it is not Big Buzzer and it does not attract beetles. Do not require the player to recite every detail again if the report has already been delivered.

Let Gwyneth or the receiving League representative ask only the questions needed for containment: what the party saw, how the signals travel, what Kragga is trying to unify, and how much the surface knows. Keep the response discreet and inside the League Hall; do not turn it into a public announcement, do not require Isadora's presence, and do not begin the Greenmeadow incident in the same scene. Complete the event once the League has accepted the report and has a concrete reason to watch for the next surface breach.

onCompleteEffects.text: Wait for the League's next surface report.

grell_ratkin_courier.title: News from Greenmeadow
grell_ratkin_courier.beats:
A ratkin courier tracks the party down wherever they are. Do not assign the courier a permanent NPC object or require a particular tavern, lift, or hub; stage the encounter in the party's current scene at a natural pause, with the courier arriving breathless and intent on being heard. The courier says a Messenger Owl carried fresh news from Greenmeadow.

The report is concrete: tremors under the village, water vibrating in wells and troughs, livestock frightened, burrowing animals fleeing their holes, birds abandoning the fields, and a low grinding that can be felt before it can be heard. The courier explains what the League has learned about the kobolds' Big Buzzer: a Fourth Empire artifact that emits directional ground-vibrations, attracts and irritates stone-boring beetles, and turns them violently destructive. It does not control the beetles.

This is the actionable report, not a separate warning scene at Greenmeadow. Complete the event once the party understands that a breach is imminent or opening and can choose to go there.

onCompleteEffects.value: Defeat Grindmaw and Seal the Breach

onCompleteEffects.text: Go to Greenmeadow and investigate the surface breach.

grell_grindmaw_greenmeadow.title: The Ground Opens
grell_grindmaw_greenmeadow.beats:
Stage the attack at Greenmeadow, with the immediate action centered in The Fields. Most villagers are hiding or have fled. Keep one stubborn local visible — a farmer, miller, or shepherd who refuses to abandon animals, tools, or home — so the party has a stageable person to protect, question, or follow.

The ground splits open and Grindmaw erupts. It is a natural, wagon-sized stone-boring beetle, hostile to everything near its bore and attacking on sight. Its arrival is violent and physical: earth heaves, water shakes, stone dust pours from the fresh throat, and the beetle's mandibles bite through whatever stands in its way. Kobold raiders or low-tech sappers may exploit the fresh tunnel behind it, but they do not operate, ride, guide, or control the beetle; Grindmaw attacks kobolds as readily as villagers.

Do not stage a separate warning event here and do not auto-resolve the sealing action. The open objective is to defeat Grindmaw, silence or remove Big Buzzer, and secure the weakened upper throat of the bore. Complete this event once the immediate attack is established and the party has an actionable opening; leave the actual defeat and sealing to play and the quest trigger.

onCompleteEffects.text: Defeat Grindmaw, silence or remove Big Buzzer, and seal the fresh bore.

grell_kragga_war_shrieker_taunt.title: Kragga's Answer
grell_kragga_war_shrieker_taunt.beats:
After the Greenmeadow breach has been contained, stage a long, serpentine bound fiend emerging from an old signal passage or the collapsing edge of a fresh bore. This is a war-shrieker, not a banshee, shrieker fungus, ghost, or disembodied voice. It is physically present, can be attacked, and carries the sound of Kragga's command through its throat.

Have the war-shrieker berate the party in short, repeated phrases that clearly come from Kragga in a fit of pique. Kragga knows they have disrupted one of his surface roads. He says they have silenced a mouth but not the empire, that he is secure in the Imperial Arsenal, and that the party should come to The Command Hall if it wants to challenge the Emperor of All Grell. Name the Arsenal plainly; this is the clue that identifies the command center.

The party may kill, drive off, intercept, or otherwise answer the messenger. Do not require the war-shrieker to survive after delivering the information, and do not stage Kragga's final confrontation in this event. Complete it once the taunt and location have been delivered and the fiend is no longer immediately controlling the scene.

onCompleteEffects.text: Reach The Command Hall of The Imperial Arsenal and defeat Kragga the First, Emperor of All Grell.

ntar_vanna_taravati_matriarchs_court_int.title: The Matriarchs Deliberate
ntar_vanna_taravati_matriarchs_court_int.beats: While the party remains in the Matriarch's Court and Ruling Matriarch Taravati Dhal is still present at Durg Sthira, establish an active public council rather than a silent court waiting for visitors. Taravati and at least three family matriarchs may be assigning obligations for a defense, comparing rival designs, judging whether a proposed expedition can be supplied, or hearing a dispute between forge-families. Let the other matriarchs participate instead of making Taravati an absolute monarch. Do not summon the party or make them central merely for arriving. If they approach, present relevant evidence, offer expertise, or involve themselves, Taravati hears the full proposal and tests its costs, durability, and division of risk. Do not turn the exchange into repeated stock questions. Insults, disagreement, refusal, and poor etiquette do not begin violence. If Taravati is no longer present, do not relocate or duplicate her; complete the event without staging her. Complete the event once the immediate council matter has been shown and the party has engaged, declined involvement, remained an observer, or moved on.

ntar_vanna_oruvan_high_court_introductio.title: The High King Holds Court
ntar_vanna_oruvan_high_court_introductio.beats: While the party remains in the High Court and High King Oruvan Tavakar is still present at Citadel Uchaghar, establish the court as active rather than waiting silently for the party. Oruvan may be hearing two rival accounts of an expedition, judging a disputed boast, rewarding a returning patrol, or requiring a cautious commander to state the better plan they claim to possess. Show his exuberance, authority, and attention through the proceeding. Do not automatically summon or challenge the party and do not make them the center of the court merely for arriving. If they approach, interrupt boldly, present an important purpose, or involve themselves in the matter, Oruvan notices and engages them. Oruvan's response to observed conduct ranges from formal attention to amusement or serious interest in a possible agent. A test need not be athletic. Do not begin violence over refusal, poor etiquette, or an insult. If Oruvan is no longer present, do not relocate or duplicate him; complete the event without staging him. Complete the event once the court's immediate matter has been shown and the party has engaged, declined involvement, remained an observer, or moved on.

dunelands_danger_hillwatch.title: Danger at Hillwatch
dunelands_danger_hillwatch.beats: While the party remains at Hillwatch, bring one characteristic threat of the place into immediate play as a contained social challenge, obstacle, tense encounter, or attack if escalation is justified. Scale it to a reasonable challenge for the current party. The New Sun does not attack peaceful arrivals on sight. Begin with cult scrutiny, recruitment pressure, a demand, witnessing someone being taken, an invitation below, or consequences for prying. Escalate to capture or violence only if the party threatens the cult's work, refuses to move along, or interferes. Do not create a huge force or an impossible problem. Preserve the location's authored behavior and allow negotiation, compliance, deception, escape, stealth, or resistance. Complete the event once the immediate threat has been accepted, defused, escaped, bypassed, or otherwise resolved.

dunelands_danger_tomb_crags.title: Danger at the Tomb Crags
dunelands_danger_tomb_crags.beats: Make hostile enemies appear and engage the party at the Tomb Crags now. Choose either a limited crew of Khenret raiders actively ambushing or robbing the party from the rocks, or one sand-wyrm erupting beneath an open-sand crossing. The enemies must be physically present and acting; do not substitute tracks, rumors, warnings, or a traveler describing the danger. Scale the force to a reasonable fight for the current party. The crags are safe high ground and the vibration-sensitive sand is the killing-floor. Raiders may bargain or flee when outmatched; the wyrm attacks movement across the sand. Complete the event when the immediate enemies are defeated, driven off, escaped, or bargained through.

dunelands_danger_sweetwater.title: Danger at Sweetwater Pool
dunelands_danger_sweetwater.beats: Make one or two lamia appear and begin hunting the party at Sweetwater Pool now. They may approach under a deception, stalk through reeds or palms, isolate someone near the water, seize a captive, or attack from the rocks, but they must be present and actively treating visitors as prey. Do not substitute signs, rumors, or warnings about lamia. Scale the number and strength to a reasonable challenge. Lamia are cunning enough to speak, deceive, or bargain when that serves the hunt. Complete the event when the immediate lamia are defeated, driven off, escaped, exposed, or bargained through.

dunelands_danger_mirror_waste.title: Danger in the Mirror-Waste
dunelands_danger_mirror_waste.beats: Make hostile creatures appear and attack the party in the Mirror-Waste now. Choose one or two mirror-bright guardians or one lesser fire-spirit, scaled to a reasonable challenge. The creatures must be physically present and acting; do not substitute glare, strange reflections, tracks, or warnings for the encounter. Add at most one useful environmental complication such as blinding reflected light, razor glass, deceptive reflections, or uncertain distance. Guardians do not parley and are vulnerable to shock or acid; frost is effective against fire-things. Complete the event when the creatures are defeated, disabled, driven off, escaped, or bypassed.

dunelands_danger_widows_way.title: Danger on Widow's Way
dunelands_danger_widows_way.beats: Make a hostile force appear and confront the party on Widow's Way now. Choose a manageable bandit crew actively attempting a robbery or a small gnoll pack actively hunting the party. A wreck or narrow choke may shape the fight, and the two hostile groups may already be contesting the same prize, but enemies must be present and acting. Do not substitute an abandoned wreck, distant movement, warnings, or evidence of danger. Scale the force to a reasonable challenge. Bandits may accept payment, surrender, or flee when outmatched; gnolls hunt and do not parley. Complete the event when the immediate attackers are defeated, driven off, escaped, or bargained through.

dunelands_danger_drowned_king.title: Danger in the Tomb of the Drowned King
dunelands_danger_drowned_king.beats: Make hostile tomb guardians appear and attack the party in the Tomb of the Drowned King now. Choose a limited group of drowned dead or one mummified crocodile appropriate to the party's strength. The guardians must rise from the water, silt, or flooded halls and act immediately; do not substitute grasping sensations, lost footing, warnings, or an empty flooded passage for enemies. Use cold water, darkness, poor footing, swimming, and attempts to drag someone or their gear underwater as part of the encounter. The dead do not parley. Complete the event when the immediate guardians are defeated, escaped, trapped, or bypassed.

dunelands_danger_suns_eye.title: Danger in the Tomb of the Sun's Eye
dunelands_danger_suns_eye.beats: Make a limited group of scarab or hawk constructs activate and attack the party in the Tomb of the Sun's Eye now. The guardians must be visibly present and acting; do not substitute an inactive mechanism, warning beam, or description of what guards the tomb. Scale the group to a reasonable fight and combine it with one active focused-light defense such as a burning beam, blinding mirror angle, lens mechanism, or illuminated chokepoint. The constructs do not parley and are vulnerable to shock or acid. Mirrors and lenses can be redirected or disabled. Complete the event when the constructs and immediate light defense are defeated, disabled, escaped, or redirected.

dunelands_danger_bound_host.title: Danger in the Tomb of the Embalmers
dunelands_danger_bound_host.beats: Make hostile undead appear and attack the party in the Tomb of the Embalmers now. Choose a handful of lesser bound dead, one embalmer-priest with a few lesser dead, or a contained scarab swarm appropriate to the party's strength. They must rise, emerge, or pour into the current chamber and act immediately; do not substitute distant movement, an empty blocked room, or warnings that more corpses may come. The full host remains a looming danger if the party lingers, but only the limited immediate force fights now. The dead do not parley, and dry wrappings burn readily. Complete the event when the immediate undead or scarabs are defeated, burned, contained, escaped, or sealed away.

dunelands_danger_risen_host.title: Danger in the Tomb of the Risen Host
dunelands_danger_risen_host.beats: Make one disciplined squad of mummified soldiers appear and attack or bar the party's passage in the Tomb of the Risen Host now. The squad must be present, armed, and moving in formation; do not substitute statues, old ranks, distant marching, or warnings about the army. Scale the squad to a reasonable challenge. Use a shield-and-spear chokepoint, patrol formation, or small rank that can be flanked, split, baited out of position, burned, or broken with heavy impact. The dead hold their ground and do not parley. Complete the event when the immediate squad is defeated, outmaneuvered, escaped, or bypassed.

dunelands_danger_beast_king.title: Danger in the Tomb of the Beast-King
dunelands_danger_beast_king.beats: Make one kind of mummified beast appear and attack the party in the Tomb of the Beast-King now. Choose great cats springing from cover, hawks or vultures stooping from above, crocodiles surging from water channels, serpents striking from niches, or one heavier beast in a deeper hall. The beasts must be physically present and hunting; do not substitute bones, tracks, calls, or warnings. Use only one beast type and scale its number or size to a reasonable challenge. The beasts retain their natural hunting behavior, do not parley, and their dry wrappings burn readily. Complete the event when the immediate beasts are defeated, driven off, escaped, or bypassed.

dunelands_danger_sun_kings.title: Danger among the Tombs of the Sun Kings
dunelands_danger_sun_kings.beats: Make a limited hostile force physically appear and confront the party among the Tombs of the Sun Kings now. Choose a Khenret crew or New Sun diggers attempting robbery, coercion, or control of a worked tomb, or a few hostile dead emerging from a disturbed excavation and attacking everyone nearby. Do not substitute an exposed ward by itself, an empty dig-site, rumors, warnings, or signs that raiders or dead have passed through. Scale the force to a reasonable challenge and do not open a sealed pyramid, awaken a Sun King, or deploy a huge host. Raiders may bargain, surrender, or flee when it serves them; the dead do not. Use dig-sites, exposed tomb approaches, competing crews, and grave terrain as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate force is defeated, escaped, driven off, bargained through, or bypassed.

redrock_danger_ghoultown.title: Danger in Ghoultown
redrock_danger_ghoultown.beats: Make a limited number of nearby ghouls awaken and attack the party in Ghoultown now. They must rise from the street, ruined buildings, or nearby dead and immediately rush, pursue, surround, or drag at the living; do not substitute still corpses, noises, tracks, warnings, or a survivor describing them. Scale the number and strength to a reasonable challenge, with worse ghouls appearing only deeper in the ruin. The ghouls attack without fear or parley. Use doors, roofs, alleys, rubble, and chokepoints to make the fight or escape playable. Complete the event when the immediate ghouls are defeated, trapped, escaped, or bypassed.

redrock_danger_wadi_beasts.title: Danger in the Wadi of the Beasts
redrock_danger_wadi_beasts.beats: Make a hostile beast appear and engage the party in the Wadi of the Beasts now. Choose one giant scorpion, one sand drake, one desert lion or a small pride, or another established predator appropriate to the party's strength. The animal must be physically present and attacking, stalking, cornering, or defending its drinking ground; do not substitute tracks, distant cries, warnings, or a druid describing the wildlife. Use only one beast type. It behaves as an animal driven by hunger, territory, young, water, or injury and may withdraw when that motive is satisfied or the fight turns against it. Complete the event when the immediate beast is defeated, driven off, escaped, calmed, or otherwise overcome.

redrock_danger_suleyvans_folly.title: Danger in Suleyvan's Folly
redrock_danger_suleyvans_folly.beats: Make one cracked, failing, or newly opened vessel release a physically present djinn, ifrit, shaitan, or other contained spirit in Suleyvan's Folly now. The spirit must immediately attack, seize something, impose a dangerous demand, or begin a treacherous bargain; do not substitute a humming vessel, loose magic, warnings, a voice with no manifestation, or evidence of a past release. Scale the spirit to a reasonable challenge and never cause a mass release from the palace. Preserve its authored nature: many spirits attack when freed, some bargain, and a shaitan's bargain is likely a trap. Allow fighting, bargaining, binding, repairing the vessel, trickery, flight, magic, and use of the ruined palace. Complete the event when the immediate spirit is defeated, rebound, escaped, bargained through, or otherwise resolved.

redrock_danger_bonecrags.title: Danger in the Bonecrags
redrock_danger_bonecrags.beats: Make one or two dire vultures appear and attack the party in the Bonecrags now. They must stoop from above, defend a nearby nest, seize at a lone or wounded target, or attempt to carry someone toward a drop; do not substitute circling birds, old bones, warnings, or evidence of a nest. Scale the number and strength to a reasonable challenge. Use ledges, exposed climbs, wind, cover, and rescue from a vulture's grip as active parts of the encounter without making one mistake automatically fatal. Complete the event when the immediate vultures are killed, driven off, escaped, or forced to abandon their prey.

redrock_danger_flamebleed.title: Danger at the Flamebleed
redrock_danger_flamebleed.beats: Make hostile fire-creatures appear and attack the party at the Flamebleed now. Choose a few imps, one fire-demon, or one burned beast appropriate to the party's strength. They must emerge from a flame seam, cross the unstable crust, or rush from the burned ground and act immediately; do not substitute heat, a gout of flame, tracks, warnings, or distant creatures for the encounter. Add at most one terrain complication such as open flame, a fire seam, or uncertain footing. The creatures do not parley, though an incapacitated demon can be bound or captured. Complete the event when the immediate creatures are defeated, captured, escaped, or contained.

redrock_danger_redgate.title: Danger at Redgate Caravanserai
redrock_danger_redgate.beats: Make a limited gnoll force appear and attack the party at Redgate Caravanserai now. Choose a small patrol, hunting pack, ambush group, or archers holding an approach, optionally supported by one trained beast. They must physically confront, surround, shoot at, or flush out the party; do not substitute an empty gate, distant guards, a captive's warning, or signs that gnolls were here. Scale the group to a reasonable challenge rather than the whole fortified band. The gnolls use pack tactics and walls, gates, towers, or the courtyard, and may flee if their leader falls or their numbers are sharply reduced. Complete the event when the immediate force is defeated, driven off, escaped, or outmaneuvered.

redrock_danger_naran_kadish.title: Danger in the Ruins of Naran-Kadish
redrock_danger_naran_kadish.beats: While the party remains in the Ruins of Naran-Kadish, bring one contained social or political danger into immediate play: a toll demand, an expectation of deference, a perceived insult, a forbidden passage, a captive dilemma, suspicious relic buyers, or a scheme between gnoll princes that draws in the party. Scale it to a reasonable challenge for the current party. The gnoll princes do not attack peaceful arrivals on sight; outsiders who trade, pay tolls, and show respect are permitted. Escalate to capture or violence only when offense, cheating, trespass, interference, or a prince's scheme justifies it. Do not deploy an overwhelming court or war-band. Allow negotiation, payment, flattery, deception, intrigue, stealth, rescue, flight, or resistance. Complete the event once the immediate demand, scheme, or danger has been accepted, defused, escaped, bargained through, bypassed, or otherwise resolved.

alar_coast_danger_celestial_citadel.title: Danger in the Celestial Citadel of Alar
alar_coast_danger_celestial_citadel.beats: Make a hostile force appear and attack the party at the Celestial Citadel of Alar now. Choose a limited Red-cowl watch at the Sungate, a few stone constructs or bound fire elementals defending an outer hall, or wild fire-creatures pushing through a breach. The enemies must physically confront or attack the party; do not substitute alarms, scorch marks, inactive guardians, warnings, or a distant battle. Scale the force to a reasonable challenge. Constructs and fire-creatures do not parley; Red-cowls attack unauthorized approaches. A clash between two hostile forces may create a tactical opening. Keep the encounter in the approaches or outer halls. Complete the event when the immediate force is defeated, driven off, escaped, or bypassed.

alar_coast_danger_gesenthame.title: Danger in Gesenthame
alar_coast_danger_gesenthame.beats: Make a characteristic hostile force physically appear and attack the party in Gesenthame now. Choose a limited Red-cowl squad discovering outsiders, a rival dig-crew attempting robbery or press-ganging, a chained dig-beast breaking loose or being set on someone, or a jackal pack attacking around an exposed excavation. Do not substitute a collapse, newly uncovered find, empty dig-site, distant activity, warnings, or signs of enemies. Scale the force to a reasonable challenge and use one contained threat rather than the whole Church operation. Red-cowls attack outsiders on sight; dig-crews may threaten, bargain, surrender, or flee according to advantage. Use pits, rubble, chained beasts, and excavations as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate enemies are defeated, escaped, driven off, bargained through, or contained.

alar_coast_danger_slagrun.title: Danger in the Slagrun
alar_coast_danger_slagrun.beats: Make hostile enemies appear and engage the party in the Slagrun now. Choose a manageable Red-cowl patrol, a few fire mephits, one salamander, or one fire elemental appropriate to the party's strength. They must discover, pursue, ambush, or attack the party; do not substitute unstable glass, standing fire, tracks, warnings, or distant patrols for the encounter. Add at most one terrain complication such as broken slag, wreckage, or standing flame. Red-cowls attack looters but can be hidden from or outrun; fire-creatures attack without parley. Threats grow stronger toward the Fallshead. Complete the event when the immediate enemies are defeated, driven off, escaped, hidden from, or bypassed.

alar_coast_danger_miragelands.title: Danger in the Miragelands
alar_coast_danger_miragelands.beats: Create one concrete situation already unfolding around the party in the Miragelands: a convincing mirage actively draws travelers toward deadly ground while their water runs short; a manageable Red-cowl hunting party closes on known fugitives or Tribesfolk; Desert Tribe riders physically approach to test, trade with, question, or judge the party; or Church hunters and Tribesfolk clash where the party can intervene, avoid them, or exploit the confusion. Do not substitute uncertain direction, distant riders, heat shimmer, warnings, or threatened supplies without people or an immediate decision attached. Scale the situation reasonably and do not create a huge mounted force or impossible survival problem. Red-cowls attack Tribesfolk and known fugitives on sight. Desert Tribe riders attack Red-cowls, but observe, approach, test, trade with, or guide neutral travelers rather than attacking automatically. Complete the event when the immediate pursuit, meeting, clash, or survival problem is resolved or escaped.

whiteholds_danger_rathcairn.title: Danger at Rathcairn
whiteholds_danger_rathcairn.beats: Make a limited number of dwarven barrow-wights physically rise and attack at Rathcairn now. They may overwhelm gravecrafters during a sealing, break through a failing ward, or force the party to hold a barrow while the proper rite is completed; do not substitute a broken ward-stone, an open mound, trapped workers with no attackers present, warnings, or signs of disturbed dead. Scale the wights to a reasonable challenge and do not raise a great host from the whole grave-field. They attack the living and do not parley, but they are honored dwarven dead gone wrong, and putting them back to rest is sacred mercy. Defeating them is not enough if the barrow remains open: proper sealing, ward-craft, or aid from gravecrafters must resolve the disturbance. Complete the event when the immediate dead are subdued or escaped and the grave is sealed or stabilized.

whiteholds_danger_skarn.title: Danger on the Skarn
whiteholds_danger_skarn.beats: Make one or two yetis appear and attack the party on the Skarn now. They must rush from snow, cliffside, or concealment, seize at a lone or wounded target, or attempt to drag someone toward an ice-cave; do not substitute tracks, distant shapes, a whiteout, warnings, or evidence of a den. Scale the attackers to a reasonable challenge. Add at most one terrain complication such as a whiteout, hidden crevasse, or failing ice shelf. Yetis prefer to carry off one victim and withdraw rather than press against a braced party. Complete the event when the immediate yetis are killed, driven off, escaped, or forced to release their prey.

whiteholds_danger_wyrmtarn.title: Danger at Wyrmtarn
whiteholds_danger_wyrmtarn.beats: Make one rimewyrm appear and attack the party at Wyrmtarn now. It must track vibration beneath the ice, erupt through the surface to seize prey, and dive again to circle if wounded; do not substitute cracking ice, old tunnels, wreckage, warnings, or movement beneath the surface without an attack. Scale the wyrm to a reasonable challenge. Use thin ice, black water, or a fresh tunnel as active terrain. Stillness, light steps, dispersed weight, and misleading vibration can divert or expose it. Complete the event when the wyrm is defeated, driven off, escaped, or successfully diverted.

whiteholds_danger_twicehold.title: Danger at Twicehold
whiteholds_danger_twicehold.beats: While the party remains at Twicehold, bring one contained Twiceling complication into immediate play: a few ogres demand tribute, seize something bright or interesting, attempt to grab an apparently weak traveler, invite the party into dangerous oversized hospitality, propose a wildly uneven trade, or take offense at insufficient respect for their greatness. Scale it to a reasonable challenge and do not mobilize every ogre in the hold. The Twicelings default to bullying those they think weaker, but sincere flattery, an amusing performance, tribute, boldness, or clever trading can win passage or welcome. Keep them huge, delighted with themselves, and proudly foolish rather than cunning. Allow negotiation, tribute, flattery, entertainment, deception, escape, theft, or fighting. Complete the event once the immediate demand, misunderstanding, seizure, or confrontation has been accepted, defused, escaped, bargained through, or otherwise resolved.

whiteholds_danger_coldrun.title: Danger on the Coldrun
whiteholds_danger_coldrun.beats: Make a manageable bandit crew appear and actively rob the party on the Coldrun now. They may spring an ambush from high ground, reveal themselves around a false obstruction, use stolen delving gear as bait, or surround the party and demand its haul, but they must be physically present and committing the robbery. Do not substitute an already robbed traveler, an empty trap, warnings, or signs of bandits. Scale the crew to a reasonable challenge rather than the whole gang. They prefer plunder to killing, may negotiate with a hard-looking party, and scatter when their immediate leader falls. Complete the event when the robbers are defeated, driven off, escaped, intimidated, deceived, or paid through.

whiteholds_danger_hodremur.title: Danger at Hodremur
whiteholds_danger_hodremur.beats: Make a limited band of Hodremur bearfolk appear and attack the party now. They may return with plunder or captives, hunt escaped prisoners, strike travelers or a nearby camp, or rush from sentry positions in the snow, but the hostile warriors must be physically present and acting. Do not substitute an empty camp, stolen beasts alone, tracks, warnings, or news of a raid. Scale the group to a reasonable challenge rather than the whole war-band or its chief. They fight for plunder and thralls, though an exceptionally bold display of strength may earn a brief hearing. Complete the event when the immediate raiders are defeated, driven off, escaped, or forced to release their captives.

whiteholds_danger_deepgate.title: Trouble at Deepgate
whiteholds_danger_deepgate.beats: While the party remains at Deepgate, bring one contained piece of boomtown adventure pressure into immediate play: rival delving crews contesting a claim or recruit, Greloq's Company coercing someone over a find, Deepfire and Icerune agents interfering with the same delve, a dangerous relic changing hands, a wounded crew returning with trouble behind it, or one manageable construct, morlock, or other threat climbing from the crater. Scale it to a reasonable challenge and make the complication social, practical, investigative, or violent according to context rather than treating every arrival as an ambush. Do not casually unleash the Darek Deep, send a huge force up the pit, resolve the lost throne, or force either clan into open war. Allow negotiation, recruitment, trade, investigation, deception, rescue, fighting, flight, magic, and choosing whether to become involved. Complete the event once the immediate dispute, opportunity, or escaped threat has been accepted, defused, defeated, escaped, bargained through, or otherwise resolved.

aurora_danger_wyrmspire.title: Danger on the White Wyrmspire
aurora_danger_wyrmspire.beats: Make one ice drake appear and attack the party on the White Wyrmspire now. It must glide from a high ledge, stoop in a sudden pass, harry the party from above, or defend a nearby route or nesting shelf; do not substitute a distant silhouette, tracks, an abandoned nest, warnings, or signs of a drake. Scale the drake to a reasonable challenge. Ice drakes are cunning, territorial hunters that climb out of reach after striking, wait for exposure, and do not parley. Use ledges, cover, climbing, and the drake's repeated passes as active parts of the fight. Complete the event when the immediate drake is defeated, driven off, escaped, or diverted.

aurora_danger_crevasse.title: Danger in the Crevasse
aurora_danger_crevasse.beats: Make hostile guardians appear and attack the party in the Crevasse now. Choose a few ice-mummies, a few coldstone constructs, or one mummy directing a limited construct group, scaled to a reasonable challenge. They must wake, step from the white-stone ruins, or emerge onto the party's route and act immediately; do not substitute an unstable descent, strange device, inactive statue, warning, or evidence of guardians. Use glacier walls, exposed ruins, narrow bridges, and shifting ice as terrain. The dead and constructs do not parley. Complete the event when the immediate guardians are defeated, disabled, escaped, or bypassed.

aurora_danger_underfloes.title: Danger on the Underfloes
aurora_danger_underfloes.beats: Make one rimewyrm, or one smaller young rimewyrm near the broken shallows, appear and attack the party on the Underfloes now. It must follow vibration beneath the ice, erupt under prey, strike, and submerge to circle for another pass; do not substitute cracking ice, exposed wreckage, warnings, or movement below without an attack. Scale it to a reasonable challenge. Fractured floes and broken shallows shape the fight, while light steps, stillness, dispersed weight, and deliberate vibration can mislead or expose the wyrm. Complete the event when the immediate wyrm is defeated, driven off, escaped, or diverted.

aurora_danger_herdways.title: Danger on the Herdways
aurora_danger_herdways.beats: Make one dire snow-lynx appear and attack the party on the Herdways now. It must drop from a ridge or concealed height onto a lone, wounded, young, or rearmost target, or approach a fresh kill while the party is present; do not substitute tracks, a distant cat, nervous herd animals, warnings, or a stampede without a predator. Scale the lynx to a reasonable challenge. Use ridges, concealment, herd movement, and the lynx's attempt to seize prey and escape as active parts of the encounter. A nearby herd may panic or defend its young as a single terrain complication. Complete the event when the lynx is defeated, driven off, escaped, or forced to abandon its prey.

aurora_danger_northport.title: Danger in Northport
aurora_danger_northport.beats: Make one or a few Northport draugr stir in response to the living party's nearby presence, awaken, and attack now. They may rise from a frozen doorway, ship deck, hall, or street where they were laid to guard, but the party need not steal, open, board, or deliberately disturb anything first. Do not substitute an inactive corpse, creaking ship, distant movement, warning, or evidence that draugr may awaken. Scale the guardians to a reasonable challenge and do not awaken the whole city, fleet, several ship-captains, or the crowned dead in the high hall. Draugr do not hunt or parley; they relentlessly defend their appointed ground, allowing escape or withdrawal beyond it. Use frozen streets, ships, halls, and guarded thresholds as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate draugr are defeated, escaped, or bypassed.

aurora_danger_stillwater.title: Danger in Stillwater
aurora_danger_stillwater.beats: Make hostile cold-creatures appear and attack the party in Stillwater now. Choose a few ice mephits or one or two rime-wights appropriate to the party's strength. They must gather in the street, emerge from the frozen buildings, or turn directly on the party and act; do not substitute unnatural cold, an empty shelter, missing bodies, warnings, or wandering shapes that never engage. The wights may be disturbed by the living party's presence rather than requiring a contrived theft. Use lethal cold, fire, shelter, and exposed streets as active terrain. Complete the event when the immediate creatures are defeated, driven off, escaped, or shut away.

aurora_danger_hearth_temple.title: Danger at the Temple of the Hearth
aurora_danger_hearth_temple.beats: Make a limited group of Long Night cultists appear and attack the party at the Temple of the Hearth now. They may rush from a guarded approach, break from an active cold rite, defend a captive or stolen relic, or confront intruders within the frozen shrine, but they must be physically present and hostile. Do not substitute an empty ritual site, distant chanting, warnings, cold alone, or evidence that cultists were here. Scale the group to a reasonable challenge rather than the whole cult. They fight to preserve their holy ground and deepen the Widow's cold. Complete the event when the immediate cultists are defeated, driven off, escaped, or their active rite is broken.

aurora_danger_icefields.title: Danger on the Aurora Icefields
aurora_danger_icefields.beats: Make hostile creatures appear and attack the party on the Aurora Icefields now. Choose a manageable rimewolf pack pacing and closing on the party or one ice drake hunting from the edge of the fields. The creatures must physically engage; do not substitute a blizzard, lost direction, distant shapes, warnings, or a peaceful procession of rime-wights. Scale the enemies to a reasonable challenge. Add at most one weather complication such as hard wind, poor sight, or rapidly drifting snow, and preserve open ice, scarce shelter, and visibility as terrain. Complete the event when the immediate wolves or drake are defeated, driven off, escaped, or diverted.

aurora_danger_firwood.title: Danger in the Firwood
aurora_danger_firwood.beats: Make one snow-troll appear and attack the party in the deep Firwood now. It may rush from a ruined Northrealm hall, trap someone inside a holdfast, follow travelers from a ruin, or defend its den, but it must be physically present and fighting. Do not substitute loggers reporting a troll, tracks, an empty den, warnings, or a request to travel elsewhere. Scale the troll to a reasonable challenge. It regenerates unless wounds are burned or seared, and deep cold makes it sluggish. Use trees, old stone, confined ruins, fire, and colder ground as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the troll is burned down, driven off, escaped, trapped, or otherwise defeated.

aurora_danger_whitefang.title: A Test at Whitefang Hold
aurora_danger_whitefang.beats: While the party remains at Whitefang Hold, bring one contained social danger or opportunity into immediate play: frost giants demand a test of courage, endurance, strength, or storytelling; a boast becomes a contest; a giant offers dangerous work connected to the White Wyrmspire; drake-raided herds create an urgent problem; or outsiders near an egg are mistaken for participants in the old feud. Scale it to a reasonable challenge and do not turn the hold into a hostile horde. The giants are not hostile by default. They respect courage, endurance, deeds, and good stories; they despise cowardice, dullness, empty flattery, and exposed lies. A party that impresses them should receive food, shelter, respect, or opportunity rather than merely avoid violence. Allow contests, storytelling, bold negotiation, service, deception with consequences, endurance, fighting when justified, or withdrawal. Complete the event once the immediate test, misunderstanding, contest, or feud-related problem has been accepted, passed, defused, escaped, or otherwise resolved.

whitemoor_danger_bryngard.title: Danger in Bryngard
whitemoor_danger_bryngard.beats: Create one concrete complication as Bryngard's two dead armies fight across the party's route now. A battle line may sweep through the flooded street they occupy, opposing dead may mistake something the party carries for a fallen standard, a wounded living traveler may be trapped between the forces, or a limited number of revenants or one lesser wraith-captain may break from the battle because the party crosses its line or draws attention. Do not substitute a distant battle, old war-gear, ambient noise, or undead who never affect the party. Scale the complication reasonably and do not mobilize either whole army or several captains. The dead remain absorbed in their war unless the living cross, obstruct, or draw them; preserve slipping around the battle or redirecting the two sides against one another as valid solutions. Complete the event when the immediate crossing, rescue, or pursuing dead are escaped, redirected, bypassed, or defeated.

whitemoor_danger_avelmere.title: Danger in Avelmere
whitemoor_danger_avelmere.beats: Make a manageable group of Avelmere's plague-dead appear and attack the party now. Submerged ghouls or rotted drowned must surge from black water or flooded rooms, swarm the living, drag someone under, or cut off the nearest dry footing; do not substitute ripples, floating corpses, warnings, or signs of undead. Scale the group to a reasonable challenge rather than the whole drowned city. The dead are mindless, do not parley, are clumsy on dry ground, and are most dangerous in open water. Complete the event when the immediate dead are defeated, trapped, escaped, or bypassed.

whitemoor_danger_barrowlands.title: Danger in the Barrowlands
whitemoor_danger_barrowlands.beats: While the party remains in the Barrowlands, bring one contained grave-field danger into immediate play: a single barrow-wight rises because its mound was entered or its grave-goods were touched, armed Syndicate diggers contest a grave, find, or route, or an active excavation threatens to wake the guardian below it. Scale it to a reasonable challenge and do not casually open the Great Barrow or introduce its worst guardian. A wight lies still until its own grave is violated, fights without quarter once awakened, and remains bound near its barrow rather than hunting travelers across the heath. Syndicate diggers may fight, bargain, threaten, withdraw, or make a temporary arrangement as advantage dictates. Allow fighting, negotiation, leaving or returning grave-goods, flight beyond a wight's bounds, stealth, sabotage, magic, and use of mounds or diggings. Complete the event once the immediate guardian or dispute has been defeated, escaped, bargained through, quieted, bypassed, or otherwise resolved.

whitemoor_danger_carrowgate.title: Trouble at Carrowgate
whitemoor_danger_carrowgate.beats: While the party remains at Carrowgate, bring one contained reaver interaction into immediate play after the warband sizes the party up: an offer to trade, fence grave-goods, hire capable outsiders, or exchange information; a demand for payment or tribute; an attempt to rob or ransom someone who appears weak, lost, or rich; a captive seeking help; or suspicion that the party means to cheat the reavers or interfere with their plunder. Scale it to a reasonable challenge and do not turn the whole stronghold against neutral arrivals without cause. The reavers are predatory but practical: they respect strength and coin, hear out useful people, and become collectively hostile when cheated, threatened, or opposed over their camp, captives, or wealth. Allow trade, negotiation, intimidation, deception, rescue, stealth, escape, or fighting when justified. Complete the event once the immediate offer, demand, threat, or captive problem has been accepted, defused, escaped, bargained through, bypassed, or otherwise resolved.

carendon_danger_dauvigne.title: Danger in the Dauvigne Preserve
carendon_danger_dauvigne.beats: Create one concrete incident involving the unknown hunter in the Dauvigne Preserve's wild growth or ravine now. A wounded gamekeeper may stumble into view while something follows; a cry almost like a person calling for help may lure someone toward an immediate ambush; the hunter may seize visible prey, cut off the trail back, or strike suddenly while remaining only partly revealed. Do not substitute disturbed game, a missing person who never appears, vague shadowing, tracks, warnings, or a cry that leads to nothing. Scale the immediate danger reasonably and keep the managed forest near the gate safe. Do not casually name, fully explain, or permanently resolve the hunter unless an established story has earned that revelation. Complete the event when the immediate victim is rescued, the lure is broken, or the attack is survived, escaped, or interrupted.

carendon_danger_wolvesholt_range.title: Danger in the Wolvesholt Range
carendon_danger_wolvesholt_range.beats: Make hostile wolves appear and attack the party in the Wolvesholt Range now. Choose a limited dire-wolf pack or a limited number of cursed werewolves appropriate to the party's strength. They must emerge from the trees, close after dusk, rush from a bad road, or isolate and attack a straggler; do not substitute tracks, howls, missing livestock, warnings, or a distant pack. Dire wolves hunt as a pack. Werewolves are hungry cursed beasts, sometimes former villagers, rather than an organized faction. Use woodland cover, bad roads, hounds, shelter, and silver as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate wolves are defeated, driven off, escaped, or diverted.

carendon_danger_wolvesholt_heights.title: Danger on the Wolvesholt Heights
carendon_danger_wolvesholt_heights.beats: Make a small group of Ferals appear and attack the party on the Wolvesholt Heights now. They must spring an ambush in the ruined estate, drive the party toward a killing ground, isolate someone as prey or a prospective recruit, or block a route into the deep lodge; do not substitute stalking that never becomes an attack, tracks, howls, warnings, or signs of the pack. Scale the group to a reasonable challenge and do not deploy the whole pack, its alpha, or the Grey Mother. The Ferals chose the curse, are cunning and organized, default hostile, and do not parley; they may taunt or tempt a possible recruit only as part of breaking and taking them. Use silver, ruined halls, kennels, overgrowth, and broken approaches as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate Ferals are defeated, escaped, outmaneuvered, or bypassed.

carendon_danger_silver_mine.title: Danger in the Silver Mine
carendon_danger_silver_mine.beats: Make a limited pack of trows appear and attack in the Deep Seams of the Silver Mine now. They emerge from narrow cracks, ambush from a side tunnel, attempt to drag a miner toward a crack, or cut off the party’s route. Do not substitute bad air, a cave-in by itself, failed lamps, warnings, or evidence of trows. Scale the pack to a reasonable challenge rather than an impossible swarm. Trows are cowardly alone, dangerous together, hostile in the deep, and resistant to silver. Their cracks are too tight for people to pursue them into the true warren. Use darkness, lamps, wooden supports, tunnels, and narrow openings as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate pack is defeated, driven back, escaped, trapped, or contained.

carendon_danger_argenval_crags.title: Danger in the Argenval Crags
carendon_danger_argenval_crags.beats: Make hostile warren-creatures appear and attack the party in the Argenval Crags now. Choose a manageable trow ambush along the crag-trails, one lesser troll attacking from broken ground, or a limited group contesting the old tribute shrine or a cave-mouth passage. Do not substitute a difficult climb, empty cave, distant movement, warnings, or signs of the warren. Scale the enemies to a reasonable challenge; danger and strength increase higher and deeper into the Crags. Trolls and trows are hostile ambushers and resistant to silver. The great ancient troll and its generational hoard are major content and must not become this routine encounter. Use cliffs, caves, tribute, narrow paths, and broken ground as active parts of the fight. Complete the event when the immediate creatures are defeated, escaped, diverted, or bypassed.

carendon_danger_drowners_deep.title: Danger in Drowner's Deep
carendon_danger_drowners_deep.beats: Make hostile marsh creatures appear and attack the party in Drowner's Deep now. Choose a limited group of drowners rising from black water, one giant leech or serpent striking from a channel, or a will-o'-wisp actively luring someone into an immediate attack at a bad mere. Do not substitute an impassable ford, lost cargo, a body to recover, strange lights without danger, warnings, or signs of creatures. Scale the threat to a reasonable challenge and do not combine several major threats or introduce the fen-hag by default. Dry margins where fenfolk work remain ordinary; danger begins in the channels and worsens toward the deep meres. Use boats, reeds, black water, and dry islands as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate creatures are defeated, escaped, resisted, diverted, or bypassed.

carendon_danger_harpys_peak.title: Danger at Harpy's Peak Ruins
carendon_danger_harpys_peak.beats: Make a limited number of harpies appear and attack at Harpy's Peak Ruins now. They must stoop from the broken towers, seize a traveler or animal, snatch a bright object, harry the road, defend a nest, or drive the party toward a dangerous drop; do not substitute distant circling, cries, feathers, warnings, an empty nest, or signs of harpies. Scale the group to a reasonable challenge and do not deploy the entire flock. Harpies are hostile, aerial, cunning, and greedy for bright things. Use cover, bait, ruined walls, towers, climbing, and drops as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate harpies are defeated, driven off, escaped, diverted, or bypassed.

carendon_danger_reaver_road.title: Danger on Reaver Road
carendon_danger_reaver_road.beats: Make a manageable reaver band physically appear and confront the party on Reaver Road now. They must spring an ambush from forest cover, block the road and demand payment or ransom, hold a traveler or wagon, or emerge to parley because the party looks valuable but dangerous to attack outright; do not substitute a missing wagon, distant watchers, rumors, warnings, or an abandoned roadblock. Scale the band to a reasonable challenge rather than a reaver army. The outlaws prey on soft marks but may negotiate, withdraw, or make an offer when faced with a strong armed party. Allow fighting, payment, negotiation, intimidation, deception, rescue, stealth, flight, and use of wagons or woodland cover. Complete the event when the immediate reavers are defeated, driven off, escaped, bargained through, or otherwise overcome.

carendon_contact_houndsditch.title: An Interested Face in Houndsditch
carendon_contact_houndsditch.beats: While the party remains in Houndsditch, have one seedy but potentially useful local take an interest in them: a fence, fixer, poacher, failed hunter, renderer with illicit knowledge, or Syndicate-connected regular approaches with a rumor, discreet introduction, questionable purchase, offer of work, request for help, or test of whether the party is useful and trustworthy. Keep the approach conversational and low-pressure. Do not begin with threats, robbery, forced conflict, or automatic hostility, and do not make ordinary workers or the whole quarter criminal. The contact may be self-interested, guarded, or dishonest, but should offer the player a meaningful choice and a possible route into Houndsditch's underworld. Allow engaging, declining, negotiating, investigating, misleading the contact, trading, or following up later. Complete the event once the immediate approach or offer has been accepted, declined, negotiated, investigated, or otherwise answered.

black_fells_danger_fire_mountain.title: Danger at Fire Mountain
black_fells_danger_fire_mountain.beats: Make a contained hostile force physically appear and attack on Fire Mountain's approaches or in its upper binding-works now. Choose an elite Goblinate patrol, a Church of the Pyre escort or guarded supply convoy, or a limited group of fire-creatures leaking upward. Do not substitute a hazardous ward-room, silent mechanism, distant convoy, alarms, warnings, or signs of enemies. Scale the force to a reasonable challenge and do not deploy the mountain's full garrison. Keep the encounter outside the deepest breach: do not introduce the corrupted blue-fire guardian, open or alter the magma gate, bring Atravoraxis through, or advance the Dragon Queen's main quest. Unauthorized approach is treated as an enemy assault. Use old mechanisms, binding works, convoy cargo, and volcanic terrain as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate force is defeated, escaped, disrupted, or bypassed.

black_fells_danger_firewild.title: Danger in the Firewild
black_fells_danger_firewild.beats: Make a characteristic Firewild creature appear and attack the party now. Choose one fire-drake defending a vent, one salamander attacking across the glass, a limited group of giant fire beetles, or one magma ooze emerging from a cooled tube. Do not substitute a sulfur vent, unstable lava-glass, sudden heat, distant creatures, warnings, or tracks. Scale the enemy to a reasonable challenge and do not combine the whole bestiary or create a huge swarm. A basilisk is exceptional and should not appear by default. These creatures are hostile within their ground and do not parley. Use vents, brittle glass, cooled tubes, broken ground, and suitable cold magic as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate creature is defeated, driven off, escaped, diverted, or contained.

black_fells_danger_slag_warrens.title: Danger in the Slag Warrens
black_fells_danger_slag_warrens.beats: Make hostile tunnel creatures appear and attack the party in the Slag Warrens now. Choose a limited group of fire beetles or other warm-tunnel vermin, or—only if the party has entered the deeper galleries—the giant ankheg bursting through a floor or wall to seize prey. Do not substitute an old trap-line, bad air, a failing prop, cooled-slag flooding, warnings, noises, or signs of creatures. Scale the encounter to a reasonable challenge and do not combine several threats or create an impossible swarm. The ankheg never hunts the surface, attacks without parley, and may drag prey toward its burrows. Use narrow galleries, props, slag, abandoned workings, and burrows as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate creatures are defeated, escaped, driven back, trapped, or bypassed.

black_fells_danger_dragonworks.title: Danger at the Dragonworks
black_fells_danger_dragonworks.beats: While the party remains at the Dragonworks, bring one contained industrial or security threat into immediate play: a limited perimeter patrol or group of Pyre wardens, dangerous fumes, a failing vat, an unstable dragonfire vessel, workers caught in an accident, or a guarded reagent convoy approaching the works. Scale it to a reasonable challenge and do not mobilize the entire stronghold. Unauthorized outsiders are treated as saboteurs, but disguise, stealth, diversion, escape, rescue, containment, sabotage, fighting, and magic should remain possible. Dragonfire is catastrophically dangerous: do not accidentally destroy the whole complex or cripple the Goblinate's supply unless the party deliberately creates and carries through that escalation. Complete the event once the immediate guards, accident, vessel, or convoy problem has been defeated, escaped, contained, disrupted, bypassed, or otherwise resolved.

black_fells_danger_firelance_foundry.title: Danger at the Firelance Foundry
black_fells_danger_firelance_foundry.beats: While the party remains at the Firelance Foundry, bring one contained military-industrial threat into immediate play: a limited guard challenge, a proof-firing that fails or crosses the wrong ground, prisoners threatened with a weapon test, a firelance accident, a prototype being moved under guard, or a hazardous route across the proving-slope. Scale it to a reasonable challenge and do not mobilize the entire foundry. Unauthorized outsiders are taken for spies, but stealth, disguise, diversion, rescue, escape, fighting, sabotage, magic, and use of scorched wreckage should remain possible. Prototype theft, acquisition of design-plates, and major destruction are opportunities requiring deliberate action, not automatic event outcomes. Complete the event once the immediate guards, firing, prisoner problem, or weapon hazard has been defeated, escaped, disrupted, bypassed, or otherwise resolved.

black_fells_danger_loot_landing.title: Trouble at Loot Landing
black_fells_danger_loot_landing.beats: While the party remains at Loot Landing, bring one contained guarded-harbor complication into immediate play: marines inspect an outsider's cargo or papers, a prize auction offers questionable goods or captives, a Syndicate intermediary offers forged papers or passage, drunken crew members create a tense dispute, a skimmed prize causes accusations, or someone in the prisoner pens seeks discreet help. Scale it to a reasonable challenge and do not make the whole military harbor attack useful neutral outsiders. Traders, mercenaries, and visitors with coin or cargo are tolerated and watched. Escalate to capture or violence only for spying, freeing captives, cheating the harbor, attacking the fleet, or serious provocation. Allow trade, paperwork, bribery, negotiation, deception, stealth, rescue, withdrawal, or fighting when justified. Complete the event once the immediate inspection, auction, offer, dispute, or captive problem has been accepted, defused, escaped, bargained through, bypassed, or otherwise resolved.

reedmoot_fens_danger_drowned_city.title: Danger in Astarieth's Court
reedmoot_fens_danger_drowned_city.beats: Make one dragon-champion physically appear, openly challenge the intruders, and attack the party in Astarieth's Court's forbidden flooded districts now. The champion may emerge from deep water, guard a route through the Sunken Palaces, or discover the party among flooded buildings; do not substitute signs, a guarded route with no guardian present, warnings, distant movement, or news that champions may arrive later. Use one champion scaled to a reasonable challenge rather than deploying them all. It attacks intruders without parley and fights with a greatsword, poison-spit, and exceptional strength in water. Astarieth remains asleep unless the party deliberately enters the Gilded Cathedral; do not awaken or relocate her. Complete the event when the immediate champion is defeated, escaped, diverted, or bypassed.

reedmoot_fens_danger_fleetwrack.title: Danger on Fleetwrack Isle
reedmoot_fens_danger_fleetwrack.beats: Make hostile wreck-creatures appear and attack the party on Fleetwrack Isle now. Choose one or two merrow emerging from a flooded lower deck, a manageable group of giant crabs ambushing from dark water, or a limited number of mire drakes defending a nest or scorched hulk. Do not substitute splashing, damaged wreckage, an empty nest, warnings, or signs of creatures. Scale the encounter to a reasonable challenge and do not combine the island's whole population or deploy the entire flagship rookery. Merrow are cruel and hostile but greedy enough to distract or bribe with treasure; drakes cannot be reasoned with and break off only when badly wounded or drawn from a nest; hurt crabs flee into the water. Use wreckage, flooded decks, dark water, and unstable footing as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate creatures are defeated, escaped, distracted, driven off, or bypassed.

reedmoot_fens_danger_drowned_road.title: Danger on the Drowned Road
reedmoot_fens_danger_drowned_road.beats: Make hostile enemies physically appear and attack the party on the Drowned Road now. Choose a limited lizardfolk war-party, the guards of a captive column, one giant crocodile at a submerged stretch, a constrictor striking from the reeds, or—farther west—a mire drake. Do not substitute smugglers avoiding notice, mire, quicksand, tracks, warnings, or signs of enemies. Scale the threat to a reasonable challenge and do not deploy a large army or several major beasts. Lizardfolk war-parties attack outsiders without parley, take strong captives, kill the rest, and do not pursue far off the road; captive-column guards will not abandon their prisoners to chase. Use the raised roadbed, flooded stretches, reeds, captives, and surrounding mire as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate enemies are defeated, escaped, diverted, or bypassed and any immediate captive crisis is resolved.

reedmoot_fens_danger_brood_mounds.title: Danger at the Dragon-Brood Mounds
reedmoot_fens_danger_brood_mounds.beats: Make a limited hostile force physically discover and attack the party at the Dragon-Brood Mounds now. Choose a warrior patrol, a drake-handler with one manageable drake, sentries guarding a captive pen or hatchling enclosure, or participants moving through a rite. Do not substitute an empty enclosure, distant ritual, unoccupied route, warnings, or signs of patrols. Scale the force to a reasonable challenge and do not deploy the entire mound field, several priest-kings, or a great drake-pack. Everyone here is hostile to outsiders without parley, and open discovery makes silencing or outrunning the alarm horns urgent because the whole field will answer within minutes. Do not treat this routine encounter as permission to clear the sacred complex or loot the First Mound. Complete the event when the immediate force is defeated, escaped, diverted, or bypassed and any immediate alarm or captive crisis is resolved.

reedmoot_fens_danger_stiltwood.title: A Warning in the Stiltwood
reedmoot_fens_danger_stiltwood.beats: While the party remains in the Stiltwood, bring the heronfolk boundary custom into immediate play. If the party trades fairly at the Root Margin or remains outside the Tangle, keep the interaction peaceful through watched stakes, exchanged goods, signs, or a cautious approach. If they enter the Tangle without invitation, place one deliberate warning arrow close enough to be unmistakable. An intruder who stops, lays down arms, and turns back is allowed to leave; only one who presses onward faces limited volleys from concealed archers above who reposition after firing and leave the wounded room to retreat. Scale any escalation to a reasonable challenge and do not mobilize whole roosts unless they are attacked. Allow trade, withdrawal, surrender of arms, explanation, negotiation if trust permits, stealth, escape, or fighting when the custom is defied. Complete the event once the warning or trade has been respected, answered, escaped, or otherwise resolved.

reedmoot_fens_contact_port_lucre.title: An Opportunity in Port Lucre
reedmoot_fens_contact_port_lucre.beats: While the party remains in Port Lucre, have one self-interested local take an interest in them: a smuggler, fence, fen-guide, salvage recruiter, card-cheat, shipmaster, or Syndicate-connected regular offers work, information, a questionable deal, passage, a crew berth, or a mild attempt to take advantage of an inexperienced visitor. Keep the opening playable and social rather than beginning with a stabbing, mass brawl, kidnapping, or automatic hostility. Port Lucre welcomes useful paying strangers even though scams, theft, and rough behavior are common. Violence should follow the party's choices, obvious vulnerability recklessly displayed, or interference with Syndicate cargo and business. Allow engaging, declining, negotiating, investigating, trading, countering a scam, or following the lead. Complete the event once the immediate offer, approach, or attempted advantage has been accepted, declined, exposed, negotiated, or otherwise answered.

bay_serpents_danger_bronze_wreck.title: Danger at the Bronze Wreck
bay_serpents_danger_bronze_wreck.beats: Make a limited Sea-King raiding band physically appear and attack at the Bronze Wreck now. They must rise from the water or rigging, board a passing vessel, use harpoons or nets to drag someone overboard, or attack while guarding prisoners and plunder in one section of the wreck. Do not substitute an empty occupied wreck, distant swimmers, warnings, evidence of raiders, or unguarded prisoners. Scale the band to a reasonable challenge and do not deploy the whole raider force. Sea-Kings are hostile, taunting, and prone to frenzy around blood in the water, but may slip away underwater when faced by an organized superior force. Use prisoners, reefs, decks, rigging, and water as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate raiders are defeated, escaped, driven off, or bypassed and any immediate prisoner crisis is resolved.

bay_serpents_danger_troll_skerries.title: Danger at the Sea-Troll Skerries
bay_serpents_danger_troll_skerries.beats: Make one or two sea-trolls physically appear and attack at the Sea-Troll Skerries now. They must tip a small boat, pull a swimmer under, attack stranded survivors, drag a captive toward a den, or emerge around a recent wreck whose crew remains in immediate danger. Do not substitute an empty wreck, a missing crew, distant splashing, warnings, or signs of trolls. Scale the trolls to a reasonable challenge and do not deploy every troll on the skerries. Sea-trolls attack without parley, are most dangerous from the water, and become slower on land. Preserve captives and survivors as people who may still be rescued. Use boats, rocks, fire, wreckage, and the transition between water and land as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate trolls are defeated, escaped, driven off, or any immediate captives are rescued.

bay_serpents_danger_serpent_runs.title: Danger in the Serpent Runs
bay_serpents_danger_serpent_runs.beats: Make hostile reef serpents physically appear and attack in the Serpent Runs now. Choose a limited pack striking swimmers or a small boat, one silverback breaching onto a hull, or one serpent attacking amid harpoon-lines and tangling nearby boats. A damaged hunting crew may be present, but an attacking serpent must also be physically engaged; do not substitute a disabled boat, calls for help, distant fins, warnings, or signs of serpents. Scale the encounter to a reasonable challenge and do not create an enormous swarm. Bull serpents are exceptional name-making hunts and should not appear by default. Serpents are cunning and aggressive when hungry or struck, but can be baited, driven, tired, or outsmarted. Use currents, hulls, lines, swimmers, and nearby crews as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate serpents are defeated, escaped, diverted, captured, or driven off.

bay_serpents_danger_tanglewater.title: Danger in the Tanglewater Estuary
bay_serpents_danger_tanglewater.beats: Make one characteristic Tanglewater creature physically appear and attack now. Choose one snapdragon striking from disguise, a great moray lunging from a root hollow, a limited grindylow pack attacking a loaded skiff at dusk, or one bog-kraken tentacle seizing someone or something from a deep pool. Do not substitute shifting channels, a stranded hunt, distant movement, warnings, or signs of creatures. Scale the threat to a reasonable challenge and do not combine the estuary's whole bestiary. A full bog kraken is a major hunt and should not appear by default. Grindylows attack to rob and kill but fear fire on the water and may break off. Use skiffs, deep pools, tangled roots, darkness, and fire on the water as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate creatures are defeated, escaped, driven off, diverted, or bypassed.

bay_serpents_danger_flensers_cove.title: Danger at Flensers' Cove
bay_serpents_danger_flensers_cove.beats: Make a limited group of Flensers physically discover and attack the party at Flensers' Cove now. They may be lookouts closing on intruders, hunters guarding cached bone or oil and a chained prisoner, or an active crew fighting to delay pursuit while launching boats and burning stores. Do not substitute an empty cove, unguarded prisoner, illicit-hunting evidence, warnings, or signs that the Flensers recently left. Scale the group to a reasonable challenge and do not deploy the full outlaw company. They fight with hooks, nets, harpoons, and fire, retreat to sea if outmanned, and destroy caches rather than surrender them. Use prisoners, pillars, beach, boats, caves, stores, and spreading fire as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate Flensers are defeated, escaped, driven off, or any immediate prisoner or fire crisis is resolved.

bay_serpents_danger_shipfall.title: Danger at Shipfall Isle
bay_serpents_danger_shipfall.beats: Make hostile enemies physically appear and attack the party at Shipfall Isle now. Choose a limited group of Stormcallers attacking near their caves, lightning eels striking in the charged shallows, or cultists guarding captives facing an imminent sacrifice. A storm, inward current, wind, or lightning may complicate the fight, but do not substitute weather, difficult salvage, distant drake signs, warnings, or an empty sacrifice site for attacking enemies. Scale the force to a reasonable challenge and do not combine a lethal storm with the whole cult and its drake. Stormcallers use lightning, wind, and thunder. The storm drake is a serious escalation and should not appear routinely. Use wrecks, shallows, caves, captives, wind, and lightning as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate enemies are defeated, escaped, driven off, or any immediate captives are rescued.

bay_serpents_danger_pearl_cave.title: Danger at Pearl Cave Island
bay_serpents_danger_pearl_cave.beats: Make a limited number of reef serpents physically appear and attack from Pearl Cave Island's shallows or cave water now. They must strike a boat or swimmer, surge around someone cut off from safe rock, or attack among the Mother's collected offerings; do not substitute ripples, violent water without a creature, warnings, distant shapes, or signs of serpents. Scale these lesser serpents to a reasonable challenge. Alternatively, the Mother of Serpents may physically surface and block escape, inspect what visitors carry, or silently demand respect for her collection, but she is sovereign and not hostile by default, must never be scaled into a routine fight, and attacks absolutely only if struck or robbed in her presence. Do not force that provocation. Complete the event when the lesser serpents are defeated, escaped, or driven off, or the encounter with the Mother is respectfully resolved.

swordlaw_danger_north_canal.title: Danger on North Canal
swordlaw_danger_north_canal.beats: Make a limited Feathered Fleet corsair crew physically appear and attack on North Canal now. They must strike from rocks or rigging, board the party or another merchant or fishing vessel, or attack an escort while survivors or dumped cargo remain under immediate pressure. Do not substitute pirates merely shadowing a ship, a call for help with no attackers present, floating cargo, rumors, warnings, or signs of a raid. Scale the crew to a reasonable challenge rather than the whole Fleet. Corsairs attack worthwhile shipping quickly, swarm decks from advantageous positions, and break off once resistance makes the prize too costly. Use decks, rigging, shoals, weather, nearby vessels, and survivors as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate corsairs are defeated, escaped, driven off, bargained through from strength, or any immediate survivors are rescued.

swordlaw_danger_falselight.title: Danger at Falselight Reefs
swordlaw_danger_falselight.beats: Make a limited group of Falselight wreckers physically appear and attack now. They must close from huts and black rocks to gaff and rob a vessel, attack survivors struggling ashore, or spring their attack as a false light or sudden fog draws the party toward the reef. Do not substitute the false light, fog, a breaking wreck, survivors, distant watchers, or warnings without wreckers actively closing to attack. Scale the group to a reasonable challenge and use part of the clan rather than all forty. They fight in familiar surf and broken ground, drive targets toward bad footing, and retreat toward the Holt or skiffs when outmatched. The three sea-hags are a site-boss and must not become this routine encounter, though their glamour, voices, fog, or grasping weed may complicate it. Complete the event when the immediate wreckers are defeated, escaped, driven off, or any immediate survivors are rescued.

swordlaw_danger_garrocks_island.title: Danger on Garrock's Island
swordlaw_danger_garrocks_island.beats: Make one characteristic hostile force physically appear and attack on Garrock's Island now. Choose a limited group of drowned dead rising near the shore, gallowsmen dropping from the Greenwall, bonecrews or gravechewers attacking near the diggings, a giant constrictor or monitor lizard striking from overgrowth, or a rival treasure crew whose curse-sharpened greed turns into an immediate robbery or violent confrontation. Do not substitute wary rivals, growing suspicion, tracks, distant movement, warnings, or signs of monsters. Scale the encounter to a reasonable challenge and use one coherent threat rather than every kind at once. Match the dead to where people died and let the curse sharpen greed among living rivals. Garrock's hoard remains a deeper objective. Complete the event when the immediate dead, beast, or rival crew is defeated, escaped, driven off, bargained through, or bypassed.

swordlaw_contact_beggarsbridge.title: An Offer on Beggarsbridge
swordlaw_contact_beggarsbridge.beats: While the party remains on Beggarsbridge, have one locally grounded figure take an interest in them: a fence, fixer, smuggler, forger, ratkin resident, mercenary recruiter, illicit dealer, or person seeking discreet help offers unusual goods, information, an introduction, or criminal work. Give the approach a useful hook and a reason this contact chose the party. Keep it social and opportunistic, with room to engage, decline, negotiate, investigate, trade, mislead the contact, or follow the lead. The contact may test discretion or reliability through a small request, suspicious question, or piece of information that wants action. Complete the event once the immediate offer, introduction, transaction, or test has been accepted, declined, negotiated, exposed, or otherwise answered.

swordlaw_contact_freehaven.title: An Opportunity in Freehaven
swordlaw_contact_freehaven.beats: While the party remains in Freehaven, have one pirate-world figure take an interest in them: a captain recruiting for a raid, an aspiring crewmate looking for a ship, a fence with a recovery problem, a sailor selling a credible treasure rumor, a rival testing the party's reputation, or a known pirate proposing a venture. Give the approach a concrete opportunity, stake, or choice that can launch further play. A boast or dispute may become a formal Swordlaw challenge when the characters knowingly accept it, and its outcome binds those involved. Allow recruitment, negotiation, investigation, alliance, refusal, counterproposal, reputation-building, or an accepted contest. Complete the event once the immediate proposal, rumor, recruitment, or challenge has been accepted, declined, negotiated, settled, or otherwise answered.

elfwood_danger_ashfield.title: Danger in the Ashfield
elfwood_danger_ashfield.beats: Make a characteristic Ashfield threat physically manifest and attack the party now. Choose a limited Church of the Pyre group conducting a rite that turns violently against intruders, or a contained magical echo of the Kindred War that takes visible, dangerous form and reenacts its violence around those crossing the field. Do not substitute spreading blight alone, an abandoned camp, fading memories, distant fire, warnings, or signs of cultists. Scale the threat to a reasonable challenge rather than a whole army. Fire magic runs unusually strong here while other magic falters; make that difference materially affect the encounter. Use scorched ground, temporary cult works, unnatural flame, and the echo's repeated history as active elements. Complete the event when the immediate cultists or manifested echo are defeated, escaped, disrupted, survived, or contained.

elfwood_danger_carrion_spire.title: Danger at Carrion Spire
elfwood_danger_carrion_spire.beats: Make a limited harpy flock appear and attack the party at Carrion Spire now. The harpies mimic the high-elven singing that once filled the tower to draw climbers toward exposed stairs or ledges, then drop from above to rake them and knock them into the long fall. Do not substitute disembodied singing, distant circling, feathers, warnings, or an empty nest. Scale the flock to a reasonable challenge and preserve height, broken stairs, and open sky as the core danger. The harpies do not bargain; after two or three are killed or the flock is badly hurt, the rest break off and circle out of reach. Complete the event when the immediate flock is defeated, driven off, escaped, or bypassed.

elfwood_danger_windreach.title: Danger at Windreach
elfwood_danger_windreach.beats: Make a griffon or hippogriff physically appear and engage the party at Windreach now. It must stoop at climbers, drive someone toward a ledge, defend its nest, attack near a stranded traveler, or contest an attempt to reach, calm, or take a potential mount; do not substitute distant cries, shadows, feathers, warnings, or signs of a nest. Scale the encounter to a reasonable challenge and use one beast, one nest, or a limited pair rather than the whole crag.
