Griffons fight fiercely to hold an eyrie; badly wounded hippogriffs are more likely to withdraw; a parent guarding eggs or young fights without retreat. Use climbing, exposed ledges, rescue, and nesting terrain as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate beast is defeated, escaped, calmed, driven off, or bypassed.

elfwood_danger_stone_warren.title: Danger at the Stone Warren
elfwood_danger_stone_warren.beats: Make one or two cockatrices rush from the Stone Warren's burrows and attack the party now. They must dart at exposed skin, scatter when struck, and return from the holes while defending the warren; do not substitute statues, an already bitten stranger, noises underground, warnings, or signs of cockatrices. Scale the encounter to a reasonable challenge and make a fresh bite's creeping petrification the distinctive pressure rather than treating the cockatrices as ordinary small monsters. A slain or captured cockatrice can provide the restorative gland needed to halt the change. Use cramped tunnels, burrows, and stone victims as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate cockatrices are defeated or escaped and any resulting petrification has been halted, treated, or otherwise resolved.

elfwood_interaction_web.title: The Spinners' Attention
elfwood_interaction_web.beats: While the party remains at Web, bring one alien but purposeful Spinner interaction into immediate play. Boundary-webs halt or capture an uninvited traveler, a Spinner examines something the party carries, the colony projects a request or warning through images and emotions, or a misunderstanding must be resolved before the Weavespeaker. Spinners understand speech but answer through telepathic impressions of sights, sensations, memories, and feelings; the Weavespeaker alone approaches full projected sentences. Build the event around interpretation, intent, curiosity, exchange, or an unusual test. Allow communication, offering something beautiful or interesting, negotiation, patient interpretation, escape from webbing, fulfilling a request, or earning invitation into the colony. Complete the event once the immediate capture, misunderstanding, exchange, warning, or request has been interpreted and answered.

elfwood_contact_ilunethel.title: An Offer in Ilunethel
elfwood_contact_ilunethel.beats: While the party remains in Ilunethel, have one locally grounded figure take an interest in them: a dark-elf house factor, surface agent, Syndicate fixer, disguise-worker, deep-goods trader, or someone with business that must cross the Elfwood approaches with paid work, illicit goods, information, or an introduction. Give the offer a concrete complication, competing interest, or moral edge suited to a rough town where merchant houses settle their own disputes and dark elves need surface agents. The work might involve a message, crate, debt, disguise, person, theft, smuggling route, or rival house. Allow accepting, declining, negotiating, investigating, trading, misleading the contact, choosing sides, or following the lead. Complete the event once the immediate offer, transaction, introduction, or dispute has been accepted, declined, negotiated, exposed, or otherwise answered.

highheath_danger_rocky_gorge.title: Danger in Rocky Gorge
highheath_danger_rocky_gorge.beats: Make one mountain troll physically appear and attack the party in Rocky Gorge now. It must descend from an upper cave, block a narrow section of the route while present, seize a separated traveler, or stalk close enough to spring its attack; do not substitute tracks, evidence of a lair, pressure to cross before nightfall, warnings, or signs of a troll. Scale it to a reasonable challenge and do not use a great group. Preserve steep walls, narrow clearings, caves, changing light, fire, and possible rockfalls as active tactical elements. The troll may attempt to drag prey away rather than fight to the death. Complete the event when the immediate troll is defeated, burned down, escaped, trapped, diverted, or driven off and any captive is rescued.

highheath_danger_rumblehorn_run.title: Danger on the Rumblehorn Run
highheath_danger_rumblehorn_run.beats: Make one coherent Rumblehorn Run threat physically engage the party now. Choose a rumblehorn bull charging, a herd beginning a dangerous stampede, a warg pack closing and attacking during a drive, or an old guardian emerging from a disturbed cairn and attacking. Do not substitute distant herds, nervous cattle, clan arguments, tracks, warnings, or signs of danger. Scale the encounter to a reasonable challenge and use one main threat with at most one natural complication. Rumblehorns are dangerous through mass and temper rather than malice; wargs circle, harry, and isolate prey before striking. Stonewall or Stormhammer crews may be caught in the event or contest the aftermath, but cannot replace the active threat. Use droveways, cairns, herd movement, riders, and crags as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the herd is calmed or escaped, or the immediate wargs or guardian are defeated, driven off, or bypassed.

highheath_danger_crookback.title: Trouble at the Crookback
highheath_danger_crookback.beats: While the party remains at the Crookback, bring one contained Clan Bighorn shakedown into immediate play: goatfolk block the high road and demand tribute, test whether the party can be intimidated, offer to fence stolen goods or move rustled cattle, produce a captive worth ransoming, or charge down the gullies after refusal or an insult to their clanhood. Scale it to a reasonable challenge and use a limited Bighorn crew rather than the whole clan. They prefer profitable robbery to needless killing, fight with headlong horned rushes and salvaged steel, and take their claim to clan dignity with complete seriousness. Allow payment, respectful bluffing, intimidation, trade, negotiation, rescue, escape, fighting, magic, and use of gullies or road terrain. Complete the event once the immediate tribute, deal, captive problem, or attack has been paid through, defused, escaped, bargained through, defeated, or otherwise resolved.

highheath_danger_varrics_span.title: Danger at Varric's Span
highheath_danger_varrics_span.beats: Open on a concrete crisis already underway at Varric's Span, not a traveler merely warning that trolls live below. A laden wagon has broken an axle or lost a wheel on the exposed bridge as night closes in. Give it a small, interesting company appropriate to the road — merchants, pilgrims, clan envoys, craftsmen, a courier, or another useful mix — with a few competent guards who can hold briefly but cannot solve the whole problem alone. One or two trolls climb from beneath the arches, attack the stranded company, try to drag a person or draft animal over the edge, or cut off the safer end of the crossing. Scale the trolls and guards so the current party can plausibly turn the fight, organize an evacuation, repair or shift the wagon, use the cargo, or escape with the travelers. Preserve the sheer drop, narrow bridge, piers, arches, darkness, and river-roar as useful terrain rather than unavoidable instant death. Troll wounds visibly knit, felled trolls rise again, and fire is required to stop their regeneration. Allow fighting, rescue, wagon work, coordinated defense, reaching daylight, fire, retreat, magic, and use of bridge structures. On success, give a concrete proportionate reward from the rescued company: payment, useful cargo or gear, a valuable introduction, reliable road intelligence, clan standing, or a favor owed; troll parts or meaningful fallen war-gear may provide an additional reward when appropriate. Complete the event once the travelers and their wagon or surviving cargo are secured, the trolls are burned down or driven off, or the party achieves another clear resolution.

highheath_danger_storm_crag.title: Danger on Storm Crag
highheath_danger_storm_crag.beats: Make a limited hostile force physically appear and attack climbers on Storm Crag now. Choose a warg pack, hill-troll, or another tribute-beast hunting on the mountain; it may guard or drag along captives held for ransom. Do not substitute violent wind, a lightning-struck route, an exposed climb, distant taunts, warnings, or unguarded captives. Scale the enemies to a reasonable challenge. The permanent storm may complicate the encounter through wind, lightning, exposure, or poor footing. The Laughing Jarl may taunt, observe, or alter the danger for amusement, but remains a major confrontation rather than the routine enemy. Use climbing, shelter, captives, storm, and mountain terrain as active elements. Complete the event when the immediate beasts are defeated, escaped, diverted, or driven off and any immediate captives are rescued.

westmarch_danger_scarps.title: Danger in the Scarps
westmarch_danger_scarps.beats: Make a small orc reaver band physically appear and attack the party in the Scarps now. They must ambush from a ravine, return into view with plunder or captives, collide violently with the party or a rival band, or attack around a camp guarded by one ogre. Do not substitute scouts watching Branton, an abandoned camp, tracks, warnings, or signs of reavers. Scale the force to a reasonable challenge and use a limited band rather than a war-host. Reavers are experienced ambushers who post lookouts, channel targets into kill-zones, and withdraw deeper into the crags rather than fight a losing battle. Use ridges, ravines, scree, caves, lookouts, and immediate captives as active elements. Complete the event when the immediate reavers and any ogre are defeated, escaped, driven off, bargained through from strength, or any immediate captives are rescued.

westmarch_danger_wolfgar_keep.title: Danger at Wolfgar Keep
westmarch_danger_wolfgar_keep.beats: Make a small hostile group physically occupy or arrive at Wolfgar Keep and confront the party now. Choose orc reavers sheltering in the yard and lower tower, Bloodsworn crusaders conducting a secret rite, or one group arriving while the party or its rivals are already present. Do not substitute an apparently empty keep, fresh signs in the undercroft, distant arrivals, warnings, or evidence of a past rite. Scale the group to a reasonable challenge rather than a permanent garrison. Reavers treat intruders as enemies but value survival and plunder; Bloodsworn conceal their activity, defend their rite, and scatter before dawn when able. Use the yard, tower, undercroft, rival occupants, and ritual works as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate occupants are defeated, escaped, driven off, deceived, or their rite is disrupted.

westmarch_danger_deadfall_gulleys.title: Danger in the Deadfall Gulleys
westmarch_danger_deadfall_gulleys.beats: Make hostile enemies physically appear and attack in the Deadfall Gulleys now. Choose a limited elf-renegade band ambushing from the deadfall tops or pinning a woodcutter crew behind cover, or giant spiders attacking from webs in the deeper ravines. Renegades may rig a log bridge or lure targets toward the spiders, but do not substitute preparations for a future raid, an unattended trap, overheard plans, distant scouts, warnings, or signs of enemies. Scale the encounter to a reasonable challenge and use one coherent primary threat. Renegades fight at range, exploit roots, bridges, elevation, and poor footing, then withdraw deeper rather than hold ground; trapped bands fight hard with short blades. Spiders are independent predators, not renegade allies. Complete the event when the immediate renegades or spiders are defeated, escaped, driven off, exposed, or bypassed and any immediate woodcutters are rescued.

orc_wolds_danger_churn.title: Danger in the Churn
orc_wolds_danger_churn.beats: Make one land-shark erupt from beneath the Churn and attack the party now. It senses a rider, herd, horse-line, or other heavy movement through the earth, lunges explosively, then digs away to surface from another direction if wounded. Do not substitute tremors, a distant furrow, animal panic, warnings, or signs of a land-shark. Scale the predator to a reasonable challenge and do not introduce several dens at once. Preserve bare stone shelves as safe tactical ground, movement and vibration as bait, the beast's slow turn after a missed strike, and its softer underside and jaw joints when it rears. Complete the event when the land-shark is defeated, escaped, diverted, or outmaneuvered.

orc_wolds_danger_roc_bluffs.title: Danger at Roc Bluffs
orc_wolds_danger_roc_bluffs.beats: Make a roc appear and attack the party at Roc Bluffs now. It must stoop from the sun at climbers, seize a rider, animal, or wagon, return to a threatened nest, or attack someone on an exposed tor; do not substitute a distant silhouette, shadow, cry, feather, warning, or abandoned eyrie. Scale the encounter to a reasonable challenge and use one bird, or at most a mated pair defending one nest. Preserve climbing, exposure, aerial attacks, rescue from the roc's grip, and the danger of being knocked from the rock. A nesting roc defends its egg or young to the death. Complete the event when the immediate roc is defeated, driven off, escaped, distracted, or its captured target rescued.

orc_wolds_danger_saber_grass.title: Danger in the Saber-Grass
orc_wolds_danger_saber_grass.beats: Make one huge saber-tooth emerge from the tall Saber-Grass and attack the party now. It stalks unseen through grass higher than a mounted rider, briefly reveals itself through moving stems or frightened horses, then leaps onto horse or rider and attempts to bear its prey down by the throat. Do not substitute movement in the grass that never attacks, tracks, animal panic alone, warnings, or a distant predator. Scale it to a reasonable challenge and foreground finding, anticipating, or outmaneuvering the hidden cat. If its first leap fails or resistance becomes strong, it circles back into cover to stalk and strike again. Complete the event when the saber-tooth is defeated, escaped, driven off, exposed, or outmaneuvered.

orc_wolds_danger_northern_foothills.title: Danger in the Northern Foothills
orc_wolds_danger_northern_foothills.beats: Make hostile cold-country creatures appear and attack the party in the Northern Foothills now. Choose a limited yeti pack ambushing from high ground, attacking herders, or dragging captives toward a den; alternatively, use one frost drake striking from among boulders with freezing breath and retreating into the rocks after its first rush. Do not substitute a raided camp, stolen goods without attackers present, tracks, warnings, or distant creatures. Scale the encounter to a reasonable challenge and choose one main enemy type rather than combining both. Preserve snow, slick stone, elevation, pursuit, and rescue of immediate captives as meaningful parts of the fight. Complete the event when the pack or drake is defeated, escaped, driven off, diverted, or any immediate captives are rescued.

orc_wolds_danger_western_border_woods.title: Danger in the Western Border Woods
orc_wolds_danger_western_border_woods.beats: Make hostile enemies physically appear and attack in the Western Border Woods now. Choose a small band of elf renegades ambushing the party or Wold herders from cover, dire wolves attacking travelers, or the local owlbear charging from the undergrowth. Do not substitute scouts who remain distant, preparations for a future raid, a burned steading after the fact, tracks, warnings, or circling that never becomes an attack. Scale the encounter to a reasonable challenge and use one coherent enemy group. Renegades strike first, fight at range, close only with advantage, and withdraw through cover to attack from another direction; cornered renegades fight rather than surrender. Use trees, undergrowth, herders, and border paths as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate renegades or beasts are defeated, escaped, driven off, exposed, or bypassed.

orc_wolds_danger_southern_badlands.title: Danger in the Southern Badlands
orc_wolds_danger_southern_badlands.beats: Make a limited mounted Oathbreaker band and its worg allies appear and attack the party in the Southern Badlands now. They must ambush from gullies, pursue the party or other travelers, return into view with plunder or captives, or attack while scouting a southern target; do not substitute preparations for a future ride, an abandoned camp, tracks, warnings, or news of raiders. Scale the force to a reasonable challenge and do not create a great war-band. Oathbreakers attack without parley, use horseback arrows followed by a rushing close attack, and coordinate with speaking worgs that flank and isolate prey. A badly beaten band scatters into the gullies. Use dust, ridges, gullies, mounts, and immediate captives as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the raiders and worgs are defeated, escaped, driven off, or any immediate captives are rescued.

orc_wolds_danger_blood_altar.title: Danger at Blood-Altar Mountain
orc_wolds_danger_blood_altar.beats: Make one contained hostile ritual group physically appear and attack at Blood-Altar Mountain now. Choose a Wrath-Speaker and limited Oathbreakers guarding captives on the slopes, conducting a sacrifice or battle-blessing on the red plateau, or summoning a manageable group of Wraths or petty demons. Do not substitute an empty altar, traces of a rite, distant chanting, warnings, or captives with no guards present. Scale the group to a reasonable challenge rather than a host. The Wrath-Speaker directs frenzy and summons from behind allies, taking the fury into its own body if cornered; defeating the Speaker ends its summons and breaks its blessing. Use the wooded slope, camps, captives, altar, and ritual as active parts of the encounter. Complete the event when the immediate ritual group is defeated, escaped, disrupted, or any immediate captives are rescued.

orc_wolds_danger_mogra_mines.title: Danger in the Mogra Mines
orc_wolds_danger_mogra_mines.beats: Make a limited kobold group appear and attack the party in the Mogra Mines' lost lower galleries now. They must fire bolts or drop stones from crawlways, rush an isolated target from side-tunnels, or attack while using a rigged collapse, flooded passage, or trap-line to control the fight; do not substitute an unattended trap, darkness, a collapse by itself, noises, warnings, or signs of kobolds. Scale the attackers to a reasonable challenge and emphasize darkness, traps, rescue, and tunnel control rather than a fair open fight. Kobolds see in the dark, attack from passages too small for armored warriors, swarm isolated targets, and retreat from a head-on defense to lure pursuit over prepared hazards. Complete the event when the immediate kobolds are defeated, escaped, driven back, trapped, or bypassed.

silvervale_report_city_ancestors.title: News from the City of Ancestors
silvervale_report_city_ancestors.beats: While the party remains in the City of Ancestors, have a tomb-keeper, independent guide, mourner, squatter, scavenger, private-house caretaker, or adventurer report or reveal news of a recent incident somewhere in the necropolis. The incident might involve restless dead, a breached or robbed crypt, a missing person, a noble house hiding an embarrassment, trouble in the Commons, a guide who led someone down the wrong route, or ominous signs near a descent. Present concrete evidence, witnesses, consequences, and a location or next lead so the report can become an adventure if the party chooses to pursue it. Keep this event as news, aftermath, testimony, or an optional request for help rather than forcing the reported incident to attack the party immediately. Allow questioning witnesses, examining evidence, accepting or declining involvement, negotiating terms with a guide or house, or following the lead. Complete the event once the report has been understood and the party has chosen how, or whether, to respond.

ntar_vanna_danger_greatwild.title: Danger in the Greatwild
ntar_vanna_danger_greatwild.beats: Make one characteristic Greatwild threat physically appear and attack the party now. Choose a dire crocodile exploding from the waterline, a canopy tiger dropping onto the rearmost traveler, a goliath boar herd beginning a dangerous charge, a river drake striking a boat, a provoked thunder-tusk violently forcing through the route, or a limited driftman crew ambushing hunters to seize their haul. Do not substitute distant calls, tracks, damaged vegetation, warnings, or a merely blocked route. Scale it to a reasonable challenge and use one coherent threat rather than combining the region's great beasts. Preserve each creature's characteristic ground and behavior; make boats, canopy, shallows, thick brush, or herd movement matter. Complete the event when the immediate beast or bandits are defeated, escaped, redirected, bargained through, or bypassed.

ntar_vanna_danger_swallowed_cities.title: Danger in the Swallowed Cities
ntar_vanna_danger_swallowed_cities.beats: Make one active hostile threat physically appear and attack the party in the Swallowed Cities now. Choose Children of Ur cultists attacking from ruined cover, a giant constrictor striking from trees or toppled stone, a manageable goliath-scarab swarm bursting from a corpse-filled chamber, dire apes defending the high ruins, stranglevine seizing someone among broken roots, or the giant crocodile attacking in the flooded shrine. Do not substitute digging crews, a newly uncovered relic, distant activity, warnings, or signs of enemies. Scale the threat to a reasonable challenge and use one coherent enemy group or monster rather than the whole ruin's population. Preserve vertical ruins, flooded chambers, roots, overgrowth, and unstable stone as meaningful terrain. Complete the event when the immediate cultists, beast, swarm, or stranglevine is defeated, escaped, driven off, or bypassed.

ntar_vanna_danger_hookmarsh.title: Danger in the Hookmarsh
ntar_vanna_danger_hookmarsh.beats: Make a limited part of Ghessek's lizardfolk warband physically appear and confront the party in the Hookmarsh now. They must force a boat into trapped reed-channels, attack from concealed blinds, spring snares and stakes during an ambush, seize travelers for ransom, present guarded captives for payment, or attack during an attempted rescue from the dry-island fort. Do not substitute empty channels, abandoned traps, distant watchers, warnings, or evidence of captives. Scale the war-party to a reasonable challenge rather than the whole marsh force. Ransom money, surrendered valuables, or arrival to redeem a named captive opens negotiation; otherwise the warband attacks and uses channels, blinds, stakes, and snares to control movement. Complete the event when the immediate war-party is defeated, escaped, paid through, bargained through, or any immediate captive is rescued.

first_blood_common.title: First Blood: The Wrong Suspect
first_blood_common.beats:
Anchor the opening scene on the Workshop Terraces in Fallsmeet at dusk. A woman has been killed, her throat torn; villagers have seized a frightened young man from a rival household and are close to killing him for it. Tarain Rethford has quietly read the blood and knows the accused is alive, terrified, and not the vampire.

For the first beat, keep the pressure social and immediate. The party must decide how to handle the crowd, protect the suspect, preserve the body and scene, or question witnesses without revealing more of the Black Tower's work than they choose. Tarain advises only when asked or when disaster is imminent; this is the initiate's trial mission.

For the second beat, surface the first useful clues naturally from the player's approach: the dead woman's wound is fresh and careless, someone saw movement toward the castle road after sundown, the Tarth and Millner households' rivalry over Games sponsorship is muddying testimony, and the true killer is still nearby enough to feed again. Keep the case local to Fallsmeet and focused on a newly risen vampire or blood-hungry dead thing, not the Seven Named Dead.

This event is complete when the immediate mob scene has been stabilized enough for investigation to continue and the party has a clear next step toward finding the vampire.

onCompleteEffects.text: Investigate the killing on the Workshop Terraces and find the vampire before it feeds again.

long_con_opening.title: Proof on the Table
long_con_opening.beats:
Continue from the opening tableau instead of restating it: the party has returned to its hidden Old Town hideout on a foggy night and found Odisia Santhari already inside. She has apologized for letting herself in and placed a small lead case on the table. Do not make her smug, hostile, or coy. She is courteous, amused, and direct, and she wants to be liked enough to be heard.

First, let Odisia make the intrusion feel like a professional compliment rather than a threat. She says the lock was good, the hidden entrance better, and the party's favorite tavern barmaid very helpful after being told the right lie. She touched nothing that mattered, stole nothing, and left weapons and coin within reach. The purse and bottle she brought are a courtesy. The lead case is not payment. It is proof.

When the case opens, reveal a small soulstone: a gem with a soul trapped inside, old Ur-work, valuable enough to kill for and foul enough that honest folk do not know what to do with it. Keep the moment morally sharp. Odisia closes the case again before the stone can become a toy. She explains that soulstones are moving through Old Town and the Basement, and that the Thieves' Guild and the Syndicate have begun stealing them back and forth because neither side can complain to the Guard.

Odisia's pitch is simple. The Syndicate wants the Basement, the Thieves' Guild holds it, and a low broker in Muckside named Tersavi needs deniable talent that can hurt the Guild without starting open war. Tersavi wants to outdo rival brokers and earn lieutenant rank under the Syndicate boss in Ardan's Watch. Odisia wants the party to approach him as a crew, take his jobs, climb his ladder, and use every door he opens to rob the Syndicate from inside.

She should offer partnership, not charity or command. She names a fair split, offers coin for expenses, and makes clear that she needs people who can steal, lie, fight, and keep their nerve when the mark thinks he owns the room. She does not reveal her private vendetta against the Syndicate or the High Man behind it. If asked why the party, she says capable crews are rare, desperate crews are useful, and Jack's own luck favors people who recognize a fortune hiding inside a bad situation.

This event is complete when Odisia has made the offer, the soulstone proof has been shown, and the party has a clear next step: go to The Still Standing in Muckside, meet Tersavi, and get hired for work against the Thieves' Guild.

onCompleteEffects.text: Go to The Still Standing in Muckside with Odisia and get Tersavi to hire the crew for work against the Thieves' Guild.

dq_briefing_overview.title: Dragon Queen Briefing: The Threat
dq_briefing_overview.beats:
Continue the League briefing in the Watchtower - League Hall.

Rennick explains that Atravoraxis, the Dragon Queen, is an elder dragon whom Suleyvan the Sealer shut out of Larion long ago, and that she is trying to return through Fire Mountain. The goblin army blocks the northern approaches, but the mountain itself is the deeper problem: old magic still guards the breach, and the corrupted guardian of that magic destroys anyone who is not already serving the Dragon Queen.

Alayne explains why the Harbingers matter. The old Seal of Suleyvan once bound Fire Mountain's breach and its guardian, but the seal was broken. Each of the four Harbingers holds one fragment of it, and those fragments are the leverage needed to force a way past the guardian and reach the Dragon Queen's return-rite.

Make the structure of the war clear inside the briefing: four Harbingers, four Seal fragments, then Fire Mountain and Atravoraxis. Questions and interruptions from the room are fine, but keep the scene in the League Hall.

End the beat with a clear handoff that the briefing is continuing, such as Rennick or Alayne saying that the nearest Harbinger is Draelkharion, Prince of the Dead, and that this is where the rookies' work begins.

onCompleteEffects.text: Finish the League briefing.

dq_briefing_drael.title: Dragon Queen Briefing: Draelkharion
dq_briefing_drael.beats:
Continue the briefing with Draelkharion, Prince of the Dead.

Rennick names Draelkharion as the nearest Harbinger and the first practical target: a dracolich in Silvervale, lairing deep in the City of Ancestors with one fragment of the Seal of Suleyvan. The dead are rising around the necropolis because of him.

Alayne explains the local obstacle. A Pyre altar hidden beneath Muckside is feeding a false-fire ward over the deep routes into the City of Ancestors. That ward blinds scouts, fouls portal work, and makes stronger League strike teams vanish from sight or turn back before they can reach Draelkharion.

Make the logic clear in the briefing: Draelkharion is the Harbinger, the City of Ancestors is his lair, and the Pyre altar is the obstacle keeping better adventurers from reaching him. The rookies are not being sent to kill a dragon today. Their first useful job is smaller and local: investigate the fires in Ardan's Watch, find the Pyre cultists, and break the altar that is keeping the way to Draelkharion closed.

End the beat with a clear handoff that the briefing is not over, pivoting to the next Seal fragment and Nuur-Suthra, the Flame Undying.

onCompleteEffects.value: Defeat Draelkharion, Prince of the Dead

onCompleteEffects.text: Finish the League briefing.

dq_briefing_nuur_suthra.title: Dragon Queen Briefing: Nuur-Suthra
dq_briefing_nuur_suthra.beats:
Continue the briefing with Nuur-Suthra, the Flame Undying.

Rennick names Nuur-Suthra as another Harbinger and the holder of another Seal fragment. Nuur-Suthra is a dragon of living fire worshipped along the Alar Coast and laired in the fallen Celestial Citadel of Alar.

Alayne explains why killing it is not enough. Nuur-Suthra returns from death because of the Soul Engine, a tower-tall vessel of brass and black elderstone in the citadel's Engine Vault, where the soul of a djinn is sealed and its rage burns as flame. The dragon lairs coiled around it and heals from its fire. As long as the Soul Engine burns, the Flame Undying can collapse to embers and come back.

Make the path clear in the briefing: reach the Celestial Citadel of Alar, get past the Church's watch at the gate and the old defenses and fire-creatures in its halls, reach the Engine Vault, free the djinn or break the Soul Engine's seal, defeat Nuur-Suthra, and recover its Seal fragment.

End the beat with a clear handoff that the briefing is continuing, pivoting from fire and sky to Astarieth the Risen in the drowned fens.

onCompleteEffects.text: Finish the League briefing.

dq_briefing_astarieth.title: Dragon Queen Briefing: Astarieth
dq_briefing_astarieth.beats:
Continue the briefing with Astarieth the Risen.

Rennick names Astarieth as another Harbinger and the holder of another Seal fragment. She rules the closed Reedmoot Fens and lairs in Astarieth's Court, a half-sunken ruin where old imperial halls stand in black water.

Alayne explains what makes her hard to reach. Astarieth was once a priestess and is now a vast mire dragon, worshipped by a lizardfolk kingdom that has closed the western fens: priest-kings at the brood-mounds, war-parties on the water, and mire drakes raised as war-beasts. The drowned city itself she keeps empty for herself, warded by a handful of dragon-champions.

Make the path clear in the briefing: reach the Reedmoot Fens, find a way into Astarieth's Court, get past the dragon-champions in the deep districts, enter the Gilded Cathedral where she sleeps, confront Astarieth, and recover her Seal fragment.

End the beat with a clear handoff that one Harbinger remains to be named, Ophialtha, Beast of the Deeps.

onCompleteEffects.text: Finish the League briefing.

dq_briefing_ophialtha.title: Dragon Queen Briefing: Ophialtha
dq_briefing_ophialtha.beats:
Continue the briefing with Ophialtha, Beast of the Deeps.

Rennick names Ophialtha as another Harbinger and the holder of another Seal fragment. She is the sea-dragon queen of the Seadeep Kingdoms, and her drowned servants take the living down alive to be changed into drowned themselves.

Alayne explains where she waits. Ophialtha lairs in the Drowned City of Orichala, a sunken ruin whose deepest dome still holds air, jungle, and old magic beneath the sea. She does not stir for fighting in the standing city. Disturb the Dome and she comes up into the Queen's Lake at its heart, with the predators of the deep at her call.

Make the path clear in the briefing: get past the drowned who garrison the standing city, enter the Dome of All Worlds, face Ophialtha at the Queen's Lake, defeat her there, and recover her Seal fragment.

End the beat with a clear handoff back to Ardan's Watch and the first assignment: before anyone can reach Draelkharion, the Pyre altar beneath Muckside has to be found and broken.

onCompleteEffects.value: Defeat Ophialtha, Beast of the Deeps

onCompleteEffects.text: Finish the League briefing.

dq_briefing_close.title: Dragon Queen Briefing: First Assignment
dq_briefing_close.beats:
Conclude the briefing in the Watchtower - League Hall.

Rennick makes the scale of the war plain: the four Harbingers hold the Seal fragments, the fragments are needed for Fire Mountain, and Fire Mountain is where Atravoraxis is trying to return. The party is free to chase any Harbinger when they find a road to one.

Then he brings the room back to Ardan's Watch. The fires in the city are not random. The Church of the Pyre is using those fires to feed the hidden altar beneath Muckside, and that altar is why the League cannot yet reach Draelkharion in the City of Ancestors.

End with the golden path clearly pointed but not forced: investigate the fires in Ardan's Watch, find the Pyre cultists, destroy the altar beneath Muckside, open the way into the City of Ancestors, and then go after Draelkharion's Seal fragment.

Make it clear that the formal briefing is over. End by having the room break into motion as low-rank adventurers start looking for partners, crews, leads, maps, and anyone bold enough to walk into the fires with them.

onCompleteEffects.text: Form up with possible allies and choose your first lead.

dq_briefing_form_up.title: Dragon Queen Briefing: Forming Up
dq_briefing_form_up.beats:
After the briefing, stay in the Watchtower - League Hall as the room breaks into urgent, noisy motion. The briefing is over; this beat is about giving the player social and practical options before the first field step.

Surface a few possible people or small groups the player could work with, speak to, recruit, impress, avoid, or rival. Give the AI permission to make them vivid and capable: dashing, sharp, fearsome, funny, strange, hungry for glory, competent under pressure, or already carrying a useful lead. Favor youth, color, chemistry, and momentum. Do not reduce them to generic labels like human warrior, dwarf fighter, or elf archer. They do not all need names, and none should be forced into the party.

Useful options can include a confident low-rank adventurer looking for a partner, a small crew with a missing role, a local fire-witness who needs help, a mapper or scout with a route toward Muckside, a healer or arcanist with nerve, or a rival who wants the same first lead. Keep the options broad enough that the player can choose direction.

End with the player clearly free to act: talk to someone, form up, investigate the fires in Ardan's Watch, follow a lead toward Muckside, check maps or postings, or leave the hall.

onCompleteEffects.text: Investigate the unnatural fires in Ardan's Watch and follow the trail toward Muckside.

dq_muckside_dull_knives.title: Muckside: The Dull Knives
dq_muckside_dull_knives.beats:
A gang called the Dull Knives holds the Way Down: a cracked stone ramp under a collapsed counting-house, the only dry descent into the Muckwarren anyone local will admit exists.

They are Muckside locals, not Pyre cultists: Hask Drown-Tongue, a half-orc brute with a boat-hook and a voice like wet gravel; two ratkin brothers with crossbows up in the broken rafters; and a handful of hard-faced river trash with knives, cudgels, and lantern-oil bottles. They hate outsiders, hate the clean city across the river, and hate anyone who comes down here acting like Muckside owes them answers.

Hask blocks the ramp and makes it ugly. He jokes that the party will come out softer after the sump-leeches have kissed the marrow, and his people laugh like they have heard men scream down there before. He does not say who paid him, but he keeps glancing toward the dark below when the Pyre is mentioned, and one of his crew is plainly more frightened of the underways than of the party.

Run this as a hard gate, not a polite conversation. The Dull Knives try to keep the high ground and the exit: crossbows from above, knife-fighters pressing close, oil thrown to make fire and smoke on the ramp. They want the party beaten, robbed, and driven off, not honorably killed.

If they start losing, Hask orders the ramp fired and tries to collapse loose masonry across the Way Down, trapping the party above or forcing a dangerous descent through smoke and falling stone. If Hask falls or breaks, the gang's courage goes with him: the ratkin bolt first, the others scatter, and one frightened survivor can be made to point the way into the Muckwarren.

The challenge is over only when the party gets past the Dull Knives and down into the underways: by breaking them, frightening them off, turning one of them, sneaking through, forcing another entrance open, or surviving the attempted collapse.

dq_muckside_sump_leech.title: Muckside: The Chained Sump-Leech
dq_muckside_sump_leech.beats:
Past the Dull Knives' way down, the underways narrow into a drowned brick passage ending at an old plague-door: iron-banded stone, swollen with age, built to seal the crypt road below Muckside.

The door is guarded by the thing the Dull Knives joked about. A gargantuan pale sump-leech fills the flooded trench before it, thick as a wagon and long enough that most of its body vanishes back into the black water. Old iron bands have been sunk around its body, with heavy chains running from the bands to wall-rings on either side of the passage. The chains are long enough for it to reach the whole flooded floor before the door. Bones, boots, and half-dissolved gear show how it has been fed.

It is not loyal to anyone. It is hungry, hurt, and trained by pain. A hooked prod and a bucket of salted offal lie on a high dry ledge where someone has been driving it back from the door when cultists need to pass.

Run this as a physical obstacle with danger, not a simple monster fight. The leech surges from the water with shocking speed, trying to fasten on and drag someone under. The flooded trench makes footing bad. Anyone who falls or gets pulled in is in real trouble. The chains can be used against it, cut, jammed, shortened, or broken. The prod, salt, fire, blood, noise, or food can distract or drive it. A clever party can slip past, calm it, free it, kill it, or turn it loose behind them.

If the party handles it badly, the leech thrashes hard enough to crack the old brickwork and flood the passage deeper, making the door harder to reach and the fight uglier. If it is badly wounded or freed, it panics and tears at anything nearby, including the chains, the ledge, and the door fittings.

The challenge is over only when the party gets past the chained leech and opens or bypasses the plague-door. Beyond it, the air turns dry and dead, and the old plague crypts begin.

dq_muckside_plague_ward.title: Muckside: The Plague-Crypt Ward
dq_muckside_plague_ward.beats:
Beyond the plague-door, the water and rot fall away at once. The party enters the old plague crypts, dry as bone and sealed off from the living city for generations. Niches line the walls, still occupied. The air is dead, powdery, and close, and every sound carries too far.

The route deeper ends at a sealed archway of iron-banded stone. Faded civic ward-signs cover it from floor to lintel, old protection marks raised to keep the plague dead from being carried across the river to the City of Ancestors. A bronze guardian statue stands before the arch, broad and faceless, holding a staff in each hand across the sealed way.

The Pyre cult has not broken this ward. They have learned how to pass it. Fresh heat-marks on the stone, wax drips from red candles, and a line of burned handprints suggest the cultists use a rite or phrase to make the guardian stand aside. The old ward is still doing its original work; the cult is exploiting it.

Run this as a ward-and-guardian challenge. The party can study the signs, reconstruct the old civic warding, search for the cult's bypass rite, trick the guardian, dispel or break the magic, disable the statue, or fight it if it wakes. Rough tampering should animate the guardian: bronze joints grinding, both staffs lowering, the statue moving with slow crushing force to drive intruders back from the arch.

The guardian is not evil and not clever. It is an old protective machine obeying an old command. It blocks, crushes, shoves, and pins; it tries to force intruders away from the arch rather than chase them through the crypts. Radiant or civic authority symbols may confuse it; Pyre fire-marks may briefly command it; brute force can break it, but loudly and dangerously.

The challenge is over only when the party gets through the sealed arch. Beyond it, the crypt walls descend toward the older Hall of Skulls, and heat begins to breathe up from below.

dq_muckside_altar_chamber.title: Muckside: The Pyre Altar
dq_muckside_altar_chamber.beats:
Beyond the sealed arch, the crypt passage descends into older stone. The air grows hotter with every step. The walls change from plague niches to stacked skull-pillars and old sarcophagi worked into the supports. Red light pulses from below.

The party reaches the Hall of Skulls and finds what the Pyre has made of it. A stone altar stands at the center of the vast crypt, carved over with fire-sigils and split by a vertical seam of living flame. An iron ring of braziers surrounds it, each brazier chained to a skull-pillar. Smoke climbs upward through cracks in the ceiling, feeding the false-fire ward above Muckside and over the roads to the City of Ancestors.

Brandrek the Ashen leads the rite. He is calm, gaunt, and intense, with burned hands folded over a fire-blackened blade. Two Pyre cultists tend the braziers and keep the working alive. Brandrek does not rant. He speaks with terrible certainty: Ardan's Watch is corrupt, the dead city is sealed for a reason, and the Dragon Queen's fire will make the old world clean.

Run this as a boss encounter built around the altar. When the party enters, the braziers flare and a ring of fire seals the chamber. Brandrek calls a fire elemental out of the altar seam. The cultists try to keep the braziers burning, relight any that go out, and throw themselves between the party and the altar. Brandrek fights to hold attention and punish anyone who goes for the working.

The altar is the real objective. Defeating Brandrek does not end the threat if the altar still burns. The party can destroy the altar by breaking the braziers, severing the chains, disrupting the fire-sigils, turning the elemental against the seam, using water, stone, or warding magic, or physically cracking the altar while the rite is unstable.

If the fight goes badly for the cult, Brandrek tries to overfeed the altar, making the chamber hotter and more dangerous in order to finish the burn or kill everyone inside. If Brandrek falls, the cultists panic unless the altar is still clearly winning. If the braziers are broken or the altar seam is disrupted, the false-fire working begins to collapse.

The challenge is over only when the Pyre altar is permanently destroyed, extinguished, purified, shattered, disabled, or otherwise made unable to feed the ward. When it falls, the fire in the chamber is sucked inward, the smoke above Muckside dies, and the way toward the City of Ancestors can finally stay open.

sdm_summons.title: Seven Dead: The Summons
sdm_summons.beats:
At the rim of the Pit of Shadow, Iliora the Veiled addresses the gathered Inquisitors: something has broken loose, and the whole order has been called for it.

She turns to the Pit. A faint image appears above the dark shaft: first one distant figure, then another, until seven dim images hang in the air like glimpses seen through deep water. They are only images shown by the Pit; no body, shade, voice, or physical presence enters the chamber. Iliora names each as it appears: Vortigar the Unburied, the warlord who refused the grave, who empties battlefields and graveyards and marshals the risen into armies to refight the wars he lost. Sethelle of the Nine Sorrows, the great lady whose grief outlived her. Karneth Draghmar. The Lady Mavrocine. Ossarine the Pale Crown. Belugar Thoth-Amon. Druathyr the Thrice-Drowned.

Seven of the mighty dead — lords and sorcerers who served the demon-princes of Ur in the age of the Fourth Empire. Long ago they were stopped, put down, and bound to the Shadelands, the land of the restless dead. Now they have crossed over again. Iliora states plainly: 'We do not know where they are - only that they have crossed over, somewhere.'

Let the gathered Inquisitors react — grim recognition, fear mastered, old grudges surfacing — but keep the scene at the Pit and keep Iliora in command of it. The seven faint images remain only as distant signs above the Pit and fade when she is done naming them; they are not tracked characters, arrivals, or people the party can interact with in this chamber.

This event is complete when all seven of the named dead have been named before the gathered order and Iliora has made clear that their locations are unknown.

sdm_charge.title: Seven Dead: The Charge
sdm_charge.beats:
Still at the Pit of Shadow, Iliora the Veiled tells the order what the return of the Seven means and what must be done: the Seven must be hunted down and ended — each by the means its nature demands — and the dead they leave rising in their wake must be put back to rest. This is the work of the whole order now; every full Inquisitor will carry a piece of it. Initiates will support the work through lesser cases until they have proven themselves and undergone the Rite of Bonding.

Questions and reactions from the gathered Inquisitors are welcome; Iliora answers plainly and without comfort. Keep the scene at the Pit.

This event is complete when the order's charge — hunt the Seven, and settle the risen dead they leave behind — has been stated plainly to the gathering.

sdm_dismissal.title: Seven Dead: The Dismissal
sdm_dismissal.beats:
The gathering breaks and the Inquisitors disperse to their tasks. As they do, Vesna Calloway claps the player on the shoulder and tells them the truth without ceremony: hunting the Seven will have to wait, because the player is not ready — that is Inquisitor work, and the player is an initiate. For the time being, Jett has asked for help with smaller related threats in and around Drusavia; the player can find him in the Hall of Shadow for work.

End with the player free to move and act as they choose.

This event is complete when Vesna has redirected the player to Jett in the Hall of Shadow and the gathering has dispersed.

onCompleteEffects.text: See Jett in the Hall of Shadow for work.

academy_great_hall_practica_board.title: Tarnholme: The First Night
academy_great_hall_practica_board.beats:
It's the First-Years' welcome dinner in the Great Hall. Use a few concrete details: glass lanterns of captured sunlight hanging from the rafters, the College tables under their colored runners, the First-Years at the middle tables. Bridie Cahill, the First-Years' master, is going from table to table learning names. Older students at the College tables size up the newcomers and tease each other about College styles. Wes Carrick, the Practica master, is pinning fresh postings to the board on the wall, and students drift over to read them.

Keep it to a short, lively social moment around the newcomers. Make it about people, not a list of jobs or rules. End with the newcomer still in the hall, free to talk to anyone, read the board, or enjoy the dinner.

onCompleteEffects.text: Meet the people in the Great Hall, and look at the Practica board when you're ready.

occasion_open_arrival.title: Occasion: Something Is Happening Today
occasion_open_arrival.beats:
The party has just arrived in this place, and today, something is happening here. Choose a public occasion suited to this location, drawn from what its own character and description would plausibly hold: a festival, a market day, a contest or race, an arena bout, an election or moot, a wedding, a launching, a returning hero, an auction, a seasonal rite. It should be the kind of thing an outsider could attend and would be curious to attend, and it should already be underway or visibly imminent — decorations going up, crowds drifting one way, criers announcing, wagers being laid.

Introduce exactly one named local with a visible want connected to the occasion — a competitor who needs a partner, a vendor short-handed on the biggest day of the year, an official trying to keep order, a proud parent, a bettor in too deep, a performer missing something. A stranger with an agenda, friendly and specific, whose want the party could help with, ignore, or complicate. They should speak to the party or within earshot of them.

Make it plain, diegetically, when the occasion's main moment will happen: the final heat at noon, the vote at sundown, the bout after the drums.

Tone rules for the whole occasion: it invites and never obligates. No quest offers, no forced participation, no danger, no crisis. The party may ignore all of it and do something else entirely; that is a fully supported choice. If the party leaves the location, let the occasion recede without comment and wrap up offscreen.

This event is complete when the occasion has been established in the narration and the named local has spoken to the party or within their earshot.

occasion_open_homecoming.title: Occasion: Home Has Its Own Plans
occasion_open_homecoming.beats:
The party has just come home to this place after time away, and today, something is happening here. Choose an occasion suited to this location, drawn from what its own character and description would plausibly hold: a fair, a harvest, a wedding, a moot, a market day, a launching, a contest, a funeral feast, a seasonal rite. It should be the kind of thing the whole place turns out for — and the kind of thing a returnee is immediately expected to join.

Introduce exactly one named local with a visible want connected to the occasion — family or an old friend of a party member. Their want should be warm and personal: a hand needed with the preparations, a seat saved at the table, an old role the returnee is expected to resume, a piece of news they have been saving, a small worry they've been carrying. Let the region's chronic pressures color their talk if it fits — thin catches, mine trouble, a hard season — as background and conversation, never as an attack or a crisis. They should speak to the party directly; they know them.

Make it plain, diegetically, when the occasion's main moment will happen.

Tone rules for the whole occasion: it invites and never obligates. No quest offers, no forced participation, no danger, no crisis. The party may ignore all of it and do something else entirely; that is a fully supported choice. If the party leaves the location, let the occasion recede without comment and wrap up offscreen.

This event is complete when the homecoming and the occasion have been established in the narration and the named local has spoken with the party.

occasion_main.title: Occasion: The Main Moment
occasion_main.beats:
The local occasion established earlier reaches its main moment, around the party, whether or not they take part: the race is run, the vote is called, the bout is fought, the feast is served, the rite is performed. Stage it as living background if the party is busy elsewhere in the location, or as the scene itself if they have joined in.

The main moment produces exactly one visible upset, decision, or change that bystanders react to: an unexpected winner, a scandal, an announcement nobody saw coming, a reversal of fortune, a public refusal, a surprise arrival. Keep it local in scale — this is the place's story, not the world's.

If the party engaged with the named local and their want, weave that want through the upset — helped, thwarted, or transformed by it. If the party ignored them, show that person acting on their want anyway, and let it succeed or fail on its own terms.

Tone rules for the whole occasion: it invites and never obligates. No quest offers, no forced participation, no danger, no crisis. The party may ignore all of it and do something else entirely; that is a fully supported choice. If the party leaves the location, let the occasion recede without comment and wrap up offscreen.

This event is complete when the occasion's main moment has occurred in the narration and its upset or outcome has been shown.

occasion_aftermath.title: Occasion: The Place Exhales
occasion_aftermath.beats:
The occasion winds down and the place exhales. Show the consequences of the main moment's upset in small, concrete ways: who is celebrating, who is sulking, what is being packed up or repaired, what people are saying about it. The named local's business resolves on-screen — with the party's help acknowledged if they gave it, or without them if they didn't.

End with one soft open door: a single thing the party could look into if they chose, arising naturally from the occasion or the upset — phrased as world texture (a rumor, a departure, a curiosity, an unanswered question), never as a job offer or a request. Do not press it; mention it once and let it lie.

Tone rules for the whole occasion: it invites and never obligates. No quest offers, no forced participation, no danger, no crisis. The party may ignore all of it and do something else entirely; that is a fully supported choice. If the party leaves the location, let the occasion recede without comment and wrap up offscreen.

This event is complete when the occasion has wound down and ordinary life has resumed around the party.

house_work_offer.title: Work for the House
house_work_offer.beats:
At the player's adventuring House, use the authored Gold-ranked veteran who belongs here: Hugh Merrivant at the Wildward House, Tula Vereskar at the House of Many Banners, Calia Delassar at Sky-River House, or Rielle Mazarane at Skygate House. Do not replace the veteran with a generated keeper or another dispatcher.

Have the veteran introduce one named external client or bring forward one concrete request from a named person. Fit it closely to the actual city, region, nearby locations, factions, and the veteran's established knowledge. During the proving stage, the work should be serious, exciting, and reasonably achievable by a new company. After the standard has been raised, it may carry larger regional stakes. If the House is renowned, ordinary offers may be difficult and consequential, but only a separately established defining commission can complete the House's legacy.

State the exact place, the active danger or opportunity, the people threatened or interested, what is known, what decisive success means, and a concrete offered reward. The reward may be an exact amount of coin, a specifically named useful item, access, instruction, transport, materials, or another practical benefit. Make the request field adventure, dangerous investigation, rescue, protection, recovery, monster or outlaw work, supernatural trouble, exploration, or negotiation under pressure. Never make it routine supplies, food, drink, repairs, accounting, licensing, paperwork, or passive management.

Let the client and veteran answer questions. Present only one offer and do not treat it as accepted. End with the player free to negotiate, accept, decline, seek companions, place another existing mission under the House's banner, or ask for time.

house_raise_standard.title: Raise the Standard
house_raise_standard.beats:
At the player's home House, create a proud, interactive homecoming after its third recognized deed. Use the authored Gold-ranked veteran and the House's established community. Let clients, rescued people, witnesses, trophies, recovered proof, companions, or public consequences from the three actual deeds establish what the company has accomplished. Refer only to deeds that truly occurred.

Bring out the House's old League standard and make its return concrete. The veteran explains that the House can field a proven company again and publicly recognizes it as an active League adventuring house. The veteran offers the standard to the captain, with companions and neighbors gathered beside the pole. If the captain declines, the veteran raises it; do not prescribe a speech, attitude, company name, or personal ritual.

If the player does not already hold Bronze or higher League standing, the veteran also publicly names them Bronze standing as the captain who restored the House. Preserve any higher League standing already held. Present one specifically named piece of useful field gear suited to the player's actual class, equipment, and demonstrated style, stating its exact form, material, and practical property clearly enough for the item system to create it.

Keep the ceremony celebratory, stylish, and socially alive. The veteran remains the House's resident anchor and does not automatically join the traveling party. This event is complete when the House has been formally recognized, its League standard has been raised, and any required Bronze recognition has occurred.

house_win_renown.title: A Name Across the Region
house_win_renown.beats:
At the player's home House, create an earned homecoming after three further recognized deeds beyond the raising of the League standard. Use the actual deeds and their visible consequences. Show people from beyond the immediate city seeking the House, capable adventurers discussing its company, and serious clients treating its judgment and promises as meaningful.

The authored Gold-ranked veteran recognizes that the House now carries regional renown. If the player does not already hold Silver or higher League standing, the veteran also publicly names them Silver standing in the same scene. Preserve any higher standing already held. Let one established relationship, companion, regular, patron, rival, or person helped by the company contribute when appropriate. Do not invent a compulsory sponsor, headquarters facility, rival tavern, administrative title, or management problem.

Make clear that ordinary work can continue and Silver-level deeds may now build toward Gold, but the House's next defining step is a major regional commission whose outcome will establish what it is remembered for. Do not choose or begin that commission in this event. This event is complete when the House's regional renown has been clearly established and any required Silver recognition has occurred.

house_legacy_commission.title: The Defining Commission
house_legacy_commission.beats:
At the renowned adventuring House, use the authored Gold-ranked veteran to bring forward one defining regional commission. Connect it strongly to the House's city, region, identity, past deeds, established relationships, and unresolved opportunities. It should matter to the region and be worthy of a renowned company, but it must remain playable rather than becoming an immediate world-ending crisis.

Introduce a named client, faction representative, community, or directly affected person. State the exact location or route, the active threat or opportunity, what is known, the people and interests at stake, what decisive success means, and a concrete reward or lasting access. The commission should admit meaningful choices in method, alliances, priorities, or consequences while retaining a clear field objective.

Do not decide the House's legacy in advance. The legacy must emerge from how the player handles the commission and what visibly changes afterward. Do not begin travel or mark the commission accepted. End with the player free to question, negotiate, accept, decline, seek companions, or postpone it.

house_legacy_homecoming.title: The House's Legacy
house_legacy_homecoming.beats:
At the player's home House, create a major interactive return after the defining regional commission has been decisively completed. Ground the scene in the commission's actual outcome, the people affected, the player's choices, and the visible change produced in the region. Do not replace those consequences with a generic celebration.

Use the authored Gold-ranked veteran, established companions, clients, rivals, regulars, and relationships when appropriate. Let the House's community name what this commission revealed about the company and why people will remember it. The player may embrace, challenge, reinterpret, or ignore those judgments; do not prescribe their speech or values.

Recognize the House as legendary in a way suited to the selected region. Its future remains open to further adventures, relationships, recruits, and great commissions; do not retire the company, turn the player into a passive administrator, or imply that its story is over. This event is complete when the defining commission's consequences and the House's lasting legacy have been clearly established.

tavern_company_founders.title: The Adventuring House
tavern_company_founders.beats:
At the player's home tavern, let the keeper take the commitment seriously and help turn aspiration into a playable choice. Establish the familiar Larion model briefly: the keeper runs the public house and receives petitioners; the player leads the company in the field. No charter, League approval, founder count, accounting, or routine business plan is required.

Ask naturally what the player wants the company to be called, while allowing them to use the tavern's name or defer with a deliberately provisional name. Do not invent the final name. Ask what kinds of work or principles matter only as an open invitation; do not require a mission statement or prescribe morality.

Surface three competent possible field associates already plausibly in the tavern or introduced by the keeper. Vary species, role, experience, and desired work. Each should be capable of becoming a companion, recurring company member, rival, or useful contact, but none is assigned and the company does not require recruiting any of them before it can exist. Existing party members may be treated as potential founders if appropriate.

End with the player able to establish the company under a chosen, tavern-derived, or provisional name; talk further with candidates; invite someone; defer recruitment; or reconsider the project.

tavern_company_first_client.title: The First Client
tavern_company_first_client.beats:
At the newly founded company's home tavern, bring in one named external client with the first request. The keeper has screened them enough to believe the problem is real but does not promise the company's help. Fit the client and job to the actual home region and established local lore.

The request must require going into the field and be reasonable for a new company: a dangerous local rescue, escort, investigation, missing person, monster or outlaw problem, recovery, threatened route, supernatural disturbance, or tense practical negotiation. It must not be repairing the tavern, pouring drinks, collecting routine supplies, bookkeeping, licensing, or paying ordinary bills. State the place, people at risk or interested, what is known, what successful completion means, and a concrete payment or reward opportunity.

Let the client and keeper respond to questions. If possible, let one previously surfaced associate show interest in the work without automatically joining. End with the offer open and the player free to negotiate, accept, decline, seek companions, or ask for time. Do not begin travel or mark the contract accepted.

tavern_doors_open.title: The Old Adventuring House
tavern_doors_open.beats:
During the first one or two exchanges, let the keeper explain the tavern's dormant legacy plainly and conversationally. This used to be an adventuring house: people brought dangerous problems here, its company went into the field to answer them, and the company returned to these tables afterward. The old company is gone or scattered, so that part of the house has fallen quiet. Do not add a detailed history, tragedy, mystery, debt, enemy, or unfinished contract.

Explain the practical division in equally simple terms. The keeper can continue running the tavern, receiving people who need help, and keeping the house functioning. If the player gathers a company, the player leads its important work in the field. Refounding the house does not require a charter, League approval, a fixed number of founders, routine business management, or serving drinks. A company name, companions, clients, facilities, and reputation can emerge later through play; do not present all of them now.

Do not introduce prospective recruits, a first client, a rival house, an inherited obligation, facility choices, or the full progression ladder in this event. End with the keeper asking plainly whether the player wants to gather a company and make this an adventuring house again. Hearing the explanation is not itself a commitment. The event is complete when the premise and the keeper/player roles are clear and the player has a clean opportunity to answer, ask questions, look around, or decline.

tavern_the_incident.title: Reopening Night: The Incident
tavern_the_incident.beats:
One social complication arrives during reopening night, tied to the house's possible future as an adventuring base. Choose what best fits: members of a returning crew dispute credit or payment for a dangerous job; someone claims the previous owner promised help that never came; a rival adventuring house sends a boast, challenge, planted heckler, or attempt to recruit someone in the room; a client publicly accuses a local adventurer of abandoning a contract; or a beloved regular causes a scene about whether the new owner has any right to lead people into danger.

The room watches how the owner handles it. Give the complication a face, name, and reasonable grievance beneath the bad timing. It may be resolved, deflected, investigated, charmed, negotiated, or left standing. Violence occurs only if the player starts it. Do not turn this into licensing, inventory, drink pricing, supplies, or ordinary business administration.

This event is complete when the complication has been handled or consciously left unresolved and the room has registered something about the new owner's judgment.

tavern_last_call.title: Reopening Night: Last Call
tavern_last_call.beats:
The night settles toward last call. Show who stayed late, which adventurers or locals are still talking, and how the room now regards the owner after the social complication. Do not discuss takings, stock, supplies, or routine management.

As the keeper closes the room alongside the owner, lay out the house's central possibility: it could become the seat of the player's own free adventuring company. The keeper can receive petitioners and maintain a request wall while the player leads work in the field. The company needs no charter or fixed founder count; it needs the player's commitment, a name when the player is ready to choose one, people willing to ride under it, and a first deed that makes the name mean something. This is an invitation, not an automatic decision.

Also surface the existing pressures as adventure-facing roads: an old obligation or debt that may be cleared through a dangerous recovery, investigation, escort, or confrontation; a rival adventuring house or company tavern competing for clients, recruits, patrons, and reputation; and the keeper's still-undecided loyalty, which will be earned through leadership, promises kept, people brought home, and what sort of house the player builds.

This event is complete when the company possibility and those three roads are clear, while the player remains free to pursue, combine, defer, or refuse them.

castle_harstone_tava_missing_silverblade.title: A Missing Silverblade
castle_harstone_tava_missing_silverblade.beats: If Tava Rell is here and it is appropriate, have the player overhear a conversation, or be directly involved in one, about a Silverblade who went missing during a Wolvesholt contract. Keep the exchange practical and immediate: someone is asking whether the hunter is late, injured, hiding, or in trouble, and Tava can explain what is known so far or ask whether the player is willing to hear more. Do not force the player to accept the work.

tevantia_two_swords_vianne_opportunity.title: A Name Worth Backing
tevantia_two_swords_vianne_opportunity.beats: If Vianne Damarque is here and it is appropriate, have the player overhear or enter a conversation in which she is matching one dangerous opportunity with someone capable of claiming it. Keep the exchange light and specific, with only one opportunity in view. Let Vianne notice the player and ask what kind of deed they would want their name attached to, without assuming their ambition, offering a menu of work, starting a quest, or forcing their involvement.

arena_bout_call.title: The Sanctioned Bout
arena_bout_call.beats:
Continue from the specific sanctioned arena match the player has accepted. Preserve the already announced opponent or opposing team, exact purse, permitted weapons or magic, victory condition, surrender rules, and any local complication. If any one of those terms was not yet stated, have the arena official state it plainly before the gates open. Do not replace the accepted match with a different hook, chore, delay, investigation, or backstage crisis.

Call the entrants, bring them onto the fighting ground, and let the bout begin. Use the current arena's established character: honorable varied contests at the Field of Valor; formal House sport at Tevantia; sand, heat, and weapon schools at Oasis; cage spectacle and wagering at Gavarra; disciplined judged contests at Caranthoria; rough agreed fights at Gorren Crossing; or wet platforms, nets, teams, and manageable sea creatures at Coriva. Scale all opposition to a fair but meaningful challenge for the fighter's current standing. Never use an impossible enemy or huge swarm.

The player chooses tactics, conduct, persona, and whether to surrender; do not prescribe their actions, attitude, boasts, mercy, or showmanship. Officials enforce the declared rules. The opponent fights competently and wants to win, but does not become a mortal enemy merely for competing. Complete the event when the bout has decisively ended by its announced terms.

arena_bout_aftermath.title: After the Bout
arena_bout_aftermath.beats:
Resolve the immediate public aftermath of the sanctioned bout whose outcome was just established. The official names the winner or result, enforces the announced terms, and pays the exact purse or contracted losing share already established for this match. Do not substitute vague coin, praise alone, or a new unrelated reward, and do not treat the opponent's personal equipment as loot. If the performance changed the player's arena standing, have the official or promoter state the new standing plainly.

Let the crowd, opponent, promoter, possible sponsor, or existing rival react in a way grounded in what actually happened, without choosing the player's arena persona for them. A defeat may produce a rematch or training opportunity, but never erase established renown. End with the player free to celebrate, recover, speak with someone present, inspect future matches, or leave.

arena_title_acclamation.title: A Circuit Champion
arena_title_acclamation.beats:
Stage the immediate, interactive acclamation after the player has just won a formally declared championship match. Name the exact arena and local title. Have the herald announce the victory, pay the exact championship purse established before the bout, and present a distinctive, usable championship prize shaped by this venue. Name the prize precisely—its item type, material, quality, and any magical or damage aspect—so the item system can create it. The prize may be a weapon, armor piece, focus, fighting implement, or other useful item suited to the player's actual build; do not assume a sword or heavy armor.

Make the venue's culture visible in the award: sacred contest at the Field of Valor, House attention at Tevantia, Red Sands weapon schools, Gavarran wagers and sponsorship, Solarian ceremony, Gorren honor, or Corivan hunting Houses. Sponsorship, patronage, challengers, and stable offers are opportunities, never obligations. Do not prescribe the player's speech or public persona. If this is the player's third distinct circuit championship, have the heralds plainly recognize their eligibility for the Grand Champion's Contest in the Champions' Ring at the Field of Valor.

arena_grand_invitation.title: The Grand Champion’s Contest
arena_grand_invitation.beats:
At the Champions' Ring, have the Tournament Masters publicly recognize that the player holds championships from three distinct eligible circuit arenas. Present the Grand Champion's Contest as an immediate, prestigious opportunity, not an automatic fight: name the proposed opponent or qualifying final, state the exact rules, state a great exact purse of at least 1,500 copper florins, and name the non-coin champion's prize or commission that awaits the victor. The challenge must be severe but winnable and suited to the player's established build and history.

Let prior rivals, sponsors, companions, or representatives of the player's three conquered arenas appear when appropriate, but keep the player central. End with the Masters awaiting acceptance. Do not prescribe the player's answer or begin the contest until they accept.

arena_grand_champion_acclamation.title: Grand Champion of the Arenas
arena_grand_champion_acclamation.beats:
Stage an epic but interactive acclamation in the Champions' Ring immediately after the player's victory in the Grand Champion's Contest. The Tournament Masters proclaim the player Grand Champion of the Arenas before the gathered circuit heralds, name the three or more championships that brought them here, pay the exact announced purse, and present the already announced champion's prize. If that prize was not previously specific enough, define it now as one singular named Masterwork weapon, armor piece, focus, fighting implement, or other primary adventuring item fitted to the player's actual build, with exact material, magical aspect where appropriate, and a clear powerful property. It must be usable, not merely ceremonial.

Make the new privileges concrete: the Grand Champion may headline at any circuit arena, choose or accept challengers, command the greatest purses, train or sponsor fighters, and establish a stable if desired. These are options, not assigned duties. Let rivals, companions, sponsors, and crowds respond to the actual career the player built. Do not supply the player's speech, emotions, future plans, or arena persona.

league_champion_council_hearing.title: A Seat at the Council
league_champion_council_hearing.beats: Stage a public League celebration and Council hearing in a League authority space for the Platinum candidates whose contribution to the completed exceptional commission is being presented. Senior guildmasters, chaptermasters, Council delegates, fellow adventurers, and local witnesses honor what they achieved. Name each qualifying recipient as a League Champion, grant that person a Council seat, and charge them with protecting Larion at the highest level. Companions may be celebrated without receiving the title; preserve their individual standing. A later hearing may recognize a contributor who was not invested earlier. Ground the ceremony in the actual commission and the candidates' history, leaving their words, feelings, and future priorities to them. Complete the event when this hearing concludes. Invest only named Platinum characters with Champion Commission Proven in their personal record. Witnesses, companions, and later joiners receive no title. Never invent a completed commission to justify this hearing.

maanvalta_mirelith_request.title: Mirelith's Request
maanvalta_mirelith_request.beats:
Use two narrative turns. Each turn covers one beat and ends with room for the player's response.

Turn 1 — Mirelith's suspicion: Mirelith explains that she suspects House Drelovar arranged or enabled the attack in the Dims and is using the lockdown to search outsiders, isolate rivals, and control movement. Drelovar has money and ties to powerful outsiders, and is using the threat of surface-elf attacks to control the city.

Turn 2 — The favor and protection: Mirelith asks the player to meet Sethira Drelovar, who married into House Drelovar. There are rumors of tension between Sethira and her husband, so her wish to meet someone from Mirelith's inthelin is promising and probably not a trap. Sethira wants to meet at the Stonetome, Maanvalta's dark-elf museum. Meeting her carries risk, but a good-faith effort earns House Orelain's protection during the crisis: a pass granting movement through the city, useful introductions, lodging at the Hang-Over Inn, and Eris's fine cuisine. End with Mirelith giving the player the path to The Stonetome.

onCompleteEffects.text: Go to The Stonetome and meet Sethira Drelovar.

maanvalta_sethira_arrival.title: Sethira at the Stonetome
maanvalta_sethira_arrival.beats:
Use one narrative turn.

At The Stonetome, show Sethira Drelovar arriving with her attendants. She sends them away, then stands before the stone diorama depicting the high-elven Betrayal and the dark elves' descent toward the Sundering. She waits there alone.

onCompleteEffects.text: Approach Sethira Drelovar when you are ready.

maanvalta_sethira_information.title: What Sethira Knows
maanvalta_sethira_information.beats:
Use two narrative turns. Each turn ends with room for the player's response.

Turn 1 — The warning: Sethira explains that House Drelovar has money and ties to powerful outsiders, and is using the threat of surface-elf attacks to control Maanvalta. She says: “I know enough to suspect, but they treat me as an outsider, not their blood. They'll kill anyone sniffing around, but I can tell you who has grudges against them worse than mine…”

Turn 2 — The name: Sethira names a once-promising scion of House Drelovar who caused a scandal when he chose to join the Unseen, the cross-house brotherhood of spies and assassins. The Unseen have secluded themselves in their island monastery, the Needle, during the crisis. Getting in to see him won't be easy. Sethira explains that she has heard rumors the family considers him a thorn in their side, but dares not act against the Unseen. End with the player needing to find a way into the Needle.
