onCompleteEffects.text: Stay alert. Someone has found Sethira at the Stonetome.

maanvalta_sethira_assassination.title: The Knife at the Stonetome
maanvalta_sethira_assassination.beats:
Use one narrative turn.

Exactly two dark-elf assassins enter The Stonetome together and move to attack Sethira Drelovar. They carry kris-like, serpentine blades of black steel. Illusion magic shrouds their faces and obscures their features. End when they begin their attack.

onCompleteEffects.text: Resolve the attack on Sethira, then find Mirelith when you can.

maanvalta_mirelith_recognition.title: The Word Is Inthelinni
maanvalta_mirelith_recognition.beats:
Use three narrative turns. Each turn ends with room for the player's response.

Turn 1 — Recognition: when the player next meets Mirelith, she asks what happened at The Stonetome and lets the player's account establish Sethira's fate. She recognizes that the player stood in danger for her friend, even if Sethira died. Mirelith names the player inthelinni, the word for a fellow member of her inthelin, her chosen circle of personal loyalty. She offers the dagger and says the player can join their blood to the inthelin's. End the turn there.

Turn 2 — The rite: if the player accepts, narrate the blood rite briefly. If the player declines, have Mirelith make a light joke about outsiders and their squeamish ways. She remains amused and welcoming.

Turn 3 — The larger path: Mirelith says their ultimate goal is to convince Othrel Namaris, the reclusive leader of House Namaris, that House Drelovar threatens Maanvalta's survival. More than one person's information will be needed to convince Othrel to act, but the lead from the Unseen scion is a good place to start. Complete the event after this objective is clear.

onCompleteEffects.text: Gather evidence and a credible path to convince Othrel Namaris that House Drelovar threatens Maanvalta.

watchtower_training_yard_introduction.title: Talia Calder's Training Yard
watchtower_training_yard_introduction.beats: On the party's first arrival in the Watchtower - Training Yard, show Talia Calder already there finishing a light footwork drill beside one of the chalked rings. She is young, warm, playful, and confident without being competitive. She notices the party and offers a one-shot League combat tutorial: real combat actions against weak magical constructs, low damage, and Talia's healing after each combat turn. Let her explain that the point is to learn the ropes, not to win a contest. She may say, If you want the League version of the basics, I can walk you through it. The constructs hit for real, just lightly, and I will put you back together after every turn. Do not start combat or the tutorial in this event, assign a quest, or add paperwork, permissions, guards, or other people. End with the offer available for the player to accept, decline, or ask about. Complete once Talia and the offer have been clearly introduced, or the player declines or leaves.

watchtower_combat_tutorial_01_turns.title: Lesson One: A Combat Turn
watchtower_combat_tutorial_01_turns.beats: Run this as the first and only combat turn of the lesson. At the beginning of the turn, Talia Calder must submit real heal intent(s) targeting every living player character she can target, even if a target is already at full health. She gives a brief story explanation that a combat turn is a sequence of choices resolved together: players can attack, defend, evade, use an ability, or direct an ally, and the storyteller reports the result afterward. Before any construct acts, Talia must explicitly point to and order the Copper Impact Construct by its exact name to make one real, low-force attack against a living player, then tell it to hold. The Copper Impact Construct must submit one real attack intent using its authored low-impact impact attack, around 55 impact. This is real damage, not mockAttack, subdue, or a harmless sparring exchange. Resolve tactics from the player's declared actions and Combat Results. After the turn, Talia may explain what happened, then wait for the player to say they are ready, ask to continue, or clearly agree to the next lesson before this event completes. If the player wants to repeat or practice, keep this event active and do not advance. Use only living constructs. If the named construct has already been defeated, have Talia name and order one living authored substitute; if all authored constructs are gone, use one emergent weak training construct with about 50 HP and one low-impact real attack only after Talia explicitly orders it.

watchtower_combat_tutorial_02_attack_def.title: Lesson Two: Attack and Defend
watchtower_combat_tutorial_02_attack_def.beats: Run this as one combat turn. Talia Calder must begin with real heal intent(s) targeting every living player character she can target, then must add a real defend intent protecting the player or party member most exposed to the coming attack. She explains that a player can attack and defend in the same turn, or attack and evade, and that a declared defense is a choice with a purpose rather than a passive pause. Before it acts, Talia must explicitly point to and order the Cobalt Frost Construct by its exact name to make one real, low-force attack against a living player, then tell it to hold. The Cobalt Frost Construct must submit one real frost attack intent around 55 impact using its authored ability. Do not use mockAttack, subdue, or narrate a harmless sparring exchange. Talia explains attack plus defend and attack plus evade as two available combinations. Do not claim the combined tactic happened or worked unless the player's narration and Combat Results support it. After the turn, Talia waits for the player to say they are ready, ask to continue, or clearly agree to the next lesson. If the player wants to repeat or practice, keep this event active and do not advance. Use only living constructs; if Cobalt is defeated, have Talia name and order another living authored construct, and if all authored constructs are gone use one emergent weak construct with about 50 HP only after she explicitly orders it.

watchtower_combat_tutorial_03_damage_typ.title: Lesson Three: Damage Types
watchtower_combat_tutorial_03_damage_typ.beats: Run this as one combat turn. Talia Calder must begin with real heal intent(s) targeting every living player character she can target. Before either construct acts, Talia must explicitly point to and order the Amber Fire Construct by its exact name to attack one living player with its real low-impact fire attack around 55 impact, then order the Jade Shock Construct by its exact name to attack one living player with its real low-impact shock attack around 50 impact. These are actual attacks and actual damage, never mockAttack or subdue. Through brief story guidance, Talia explains that damage type is part of an attack and that a target's resistances or vulnerabilities can change the result. She may point out that the Copper Impact Construct's copper frame is unusually vulnerable to shock, but must not promise a result. Talia points out useful damage-type matchups, including a shock attack against the Copper Impact Construct when available; her advice remains general and promises no outcome. Do not claim that the player exploited a type or that either construct was defeated unless the narration and results support it. After the turn, wait for the player to say they are ready, ask to continue, or clearly agree to the next lesson. If the player wants to repeat or practice, keep this event active and do not advance. Use only living constructs; if a named construct is defeated, have Talia name and order a living authored substitute while preserving the indicated low-impact real damage type when possible, and if all authored constructs are gone use emergent weak constructs with low-impact real attacks only after explicit orders.

watchtower_combat_tutorial_04_protect_he.title: Lesson Four: Protect the Healer
watchtower_combat_tutorial_04_protect_he.beats: Run this as one combat turn. Talia Calder must begin with real heal intent(s) targeting every living player character she can target, then must add a real defend intent targeting the living player character most likely to be the party's healer; if no other healer is present, she may defend herself while explaining the same party role. Before it acts, Talia must explicitly point to and order the Slate Slashing Construct by its exact name to make one real, low-force attack against a living player, then tell it to hold. The Slate Slashing Construct must submit one real slashing attack intent around 55 impact. Talia teaches that a party is more than a row of attackers: a front-line ally can defend a healer while another ally attacks, and players can tell allied NPCs to protect the healer with a defend-plus-attack plan. Do not invent a party member, healer, command, or successful protection that the player has not narrated. After the turn, Talia asks whether the player is ready for the next lesson and waits for an answer. If the player wants to repeat or practice, keep this event active and do not advance. Use only living constructs; if Slate is defeated, have Talia name and order another living authored construct with one low-impact real attack, or use an emergent weak construct around 50 HP only after she explicitly orders it.

watchtower_combat_tutorial_05_preempt_da.title: Lesson Five: Remove the Threat
watchtower_combat_tutorial_05_preempt_da.beats: Run this as one combat turn. Talia Calder must begin with real heal intent(s) targeting every living player character she can target. Before either construct acts, Talia must explicitly point to and order the Amber Fire Construct by its exact name to attack one living player, then point to and order the Copper Impact Construct by its exact name to attack another living player. Each construct must submit one real low-impact attack intent around 50 to 55 impact using its authored ability. These attacks are real and must not be replaced with mockAttack or subdue. Talia explains that if a player kills an attacking NPC during the turn, the engine can preempt that defeated NPC's queued damage before it reaches the players; this is a lesson about removing a threat, not a guarantee that every attack will be negated. Talia recommends concentrating attacks on one threat to remove it quickly. Do not claim a construct was killed, damage was negated, or the tactic succeeded unless the player's narration and Combat Results establish it. After the turn, wait for the player to say they are ready, ask to continue, or clearly agree to the next lesson. If the player wants to repeat or practice, keep this event active and do not advance. Use only living constructs; if either named construct is defeated, have Talia name and order a living authored substitute while preserving two low-impact real attacks where possible, or use emergent weak constructs with about 50 HP only after explicit orders.

watchtower_combat_tutorial_06_area_attac.title: Lesson Six: Area Attacks
watchtower_combat_tutorial_06_area_attac.beats: Run this as one combat turn. Talia Calder must begin with real heal intent(s) targeting every living player character she can target. Before any construct acts, Talia must explicitly point to and order the Amber Fire Construct by its exact name to attack one living player, then point to and order the Jade Shock Construct by its exact name to attack another living player. Each construct must submit one real, low-impact attack intent using its authored ability. Talia explains that one player attack can cover several targets, but the damage is spread out and reduced for each target. Talia explains how one attack can target three living constructs, pointing to the Amber Fire Construct, Copper Impact Construct, and Jade Shock Construct when they are available. Do not state an exact damage number or claim that the multi-target tactic succeeded unless the player's narration and Combat Results support it. The incoming attacks are real and must not be replaced with mockAttack or subdue. After the turn, wait for the player to say they are ready, ask to continue, or clearly agree to the next lesson. If the player wants to repeat or practice, keep this event active and do not advance. Use only living constructs; if a named construct is defeated, have Talia name and order a living authored substitute while preserving the lesson, or use emergent weak constructs with low-impact real attacks only after explicit orders.

watchtower_combat_tutorial_07_recovery.title: Lesson Seven: Recover Under Pressure
watchtower_combat_tutorial_07_recovery.beats: Run this as one combat turn. Talia Calder must begin with real heal intent(s) targeting every living player character she can target. Before it acts, Talia must explicitly point to and order the Cobalt Frost Construct by its exact name to make one real, low-force attack against a living player, then tell it to hold. The Cobalt Frost Construct must submit one real frost attack intent around 55 impact using its authored ability. Talia explains that active combat does not restore stamina or mana merely because someone stops attacking. Ask one participant to create space while another deliberately catches breath or draws ambient power. Recovery is possible only while the recovering character is not under direct attack, restores about 20% of the relevant maximum resource, and uses the action. Do not invent a party member or recovery result the player has not narrated. After the turn, wait for the player to say they are ready, ask to continue, or clearly agree to the next lesson. If the player wants to repeat or practice, keep this event active and do not advance. Use only living constructs; if Cobalt is defeated, have Talia name and order another living authored construct, or use an emergent weak construct around 50 HP only after she explicitly orders it.

watchtower_combat_tutorial_08_control.title: Lesson Eight: Stop the Attack
watchtower_combat_tutorial_08_control.beats: Run this as one combat turn. Talia Calder must begin with real heal intent(s) targeting every living player character she can target, then must add a real preventAttack intent targeting the Frail Piercing Construct. Before it acts, Talia must explicitly point to and order the Frail Piercing Construct by its exact name to make one real, very low-force attack against a living player, then tell it to hold. The Frail Piercing Construct must submit one real piercing attack intent around 45 impact using its authored ability. In her spoken guidance, Talia should tell the player to try to prevent the construct's attack or subdue it to prevent it from acting at all. Do not have Talia say the internal camel-case engine label aloud. Do not claim that a control action worked unless the player's narration and Combat Results support it. The attack remains real and low-impact; do not use mockAttack or narrate harmless sparring. After the turn, wait for the player to say they are ready, ask to continue, or clearly agree that the fundamentals are complete. If the player wants to repeat or practice, keep this event active and do not advance. Use only living constructs; if Frail is defeated, have Talia name and order another living authored construct while preserving one low-impact real attack and the control demonstration, or use an emergent weak construct around 50 HP only after she explicitly orders it.

dhr_arrival_gate.title: The Head Above the Causeway
dhr_arrival_gate.beats: Stage the party's arrival at Demon's Head Ruins as a threshold with teeth. First, the approach: the colossal black-marble demon's head leering from the broken wall above the Causeway, black mud and shallow channels between the stones, and fresh sign of occupation such as kobold route-marks, salvage-crew tracks, or a snapped snare line. Then, immediately, a local and manageable hostile contact physically on scene and acting, scaled to the party with at least one enemy per party member or one creature plus support: kobold scouts setting a snare or prying at a door, a drowner pulling itself from a flooded channel, a stirge swarm feeding in the reeds, or a darkmantle dropping from the breach. Let the fight use the mud, reeds, channels, and causeway stones. Before or after the clash, plant one visible promise deeper in: a glint beyond the breach, an armory rack through a fallen arch, or a salvager's note naming the Relland Vaults. Complete the event when the immediate enemies are defeated, driven off, escaped, evaded, or bargained past. Complete the event if the party turns back down the Causeway.

dhr_vault_guardian.title: The Keeper of the Relland Vaults
dhr_vault_guardian.beats: Stage the climax of Demon's Head Ruins at the strongroom threshold in the Relland Vaults. The keeper is an old fortress defense still holding its last order: animated armor in Relland ceremonial plate, risen from a collapsed niche, with the house motto 'Where others kneel, we build' carved above the bronze doors. Give it presence before violence: it bars the way and issues the old house challenge, and how the party answers matters. Those who kneel or grovel it treats as thieves begging pardon; those who stand and state their business may earn a measured exchange, a test, or passage on terms. If it comes to battle, fight it as a setpiece: heavy blows, long reach, the terrain of bronze doors, collapsed niches, and family plaques in play, and if the ruin is roused, one wave of lesser defenses or kobold opportunists complicating the fight. Scale it as a hard but winnable fight for the current party. Complete the event when the keeper is destroyed, deactivated, satisfied, or decisively bypassed and the strongroom threshold is won. If the party retreats from the Vaults, the keeper does not pursue beyond them; complete the event only on a decisive outcome, otherwise let it stop when they disengage.

hc_arrival_gate.title: The Gate Arch
hc_arrival_gate.beats: Stage the party's arrival at The High Caves. First the approach and the architecture: the hard climb above the vineyard terraces, the square-cut face in the shaded wall, a gate arch wide enough for a cart with its gates long gone, guardrooms either side, shooting-slots in the stone overhead, and the Crimson Company's cull-camp on the shelf outside with a tally-post that has run out of room twice. Establish who is holding the place this visit and how dug in they are, using the occupiers named by the arrival brief and no others. Then make contact immediate and physical, scaled to the party with at least one enemy per party member: a watch on the outworks, something already in the gate arch, or the occupiers reacting to being found. Let the fight use the arch, the guardrooms, the slots, the loose rock, and the daylight reaching down the first corridor. Before or after the clash, plant one visible promise deeper in: a worked gate, a held junction, a cell being used as a store, or cold air moving up from below. Complete the event when the immediate enemies are beaten, driven back, escaped, or dealt with. Complete the event if the party turns back down the slope.

hc_keeper.title: Whatever Leads Them
hc_keeper.beats: Stage the climax of The High Caves in the Unmapped, where the builders' plan runs out and cold air moves up from the mountain. The keeper is whatever leads the current occupiers, and it must match the tenant the arrival brief established: the oldest strigoi in the complex, the leader of the Ferals pack, the raiders' captain, or a ghast among the flock. Give it presence before violence, in whatever way fits what it is — a pack leader will speak and bargain and lie, a captain will offer terms and mean some of them, a strigoi will simply be aware of them in a way the others are not, a ghast will announce itself by stench and sound. Fight it as a setpiece using the ground: collapsed levels, unrecorded ways in, drops, dark, and the mountain's own air moving through. Scale it as a hard but winnable fight for the current party. Complete the event when the leader is beaten, destroyed, driven out, or brought to terms and the site is broken for now. If the party retreat from the Unmapped it does not pursue past the Cells; complete the event only on a decisive outcome, otherwise let it stop when they disengage.

chm_arrival_gate.title: The Black Throat
chm_arrival_gate.beats: Stage the party's arrival at Charnel Mountain. First the Headworks on the mountain's shoulder: gutted winch-houses and ore-sheds stripped and weathered, a collapsed counting-office, prospectors and cullers camped among the ruins arming and trading what they brought out, and the diggings opening below as a black throat in the rock with cold air breathing out of it that smells of the dead. Establish how hard the mountain is pressing this visit using the arrival brief, and let the camp show it — confident and busy, or watchful, or half a siege. Then make contact immediate and physical, scaled to the party with at least one ghoul per party member: something already up among the ruins, something that comes out of the throat at them, or a culler's fight the party walks into. Let the fight use the spoil heaps, the ruined buildings, the open ground, and daylight. Before or after the clash, plant one visible promise below: silver actually showing in a sample, a delver's map, or a story about the seam nobody has been able to work. Complete the event when the immediate ghouls are destroyed or driven off. Complete the event if the party turns back down the mountain.

chm_deep_seam.title: The Seam Nobody Works
chm_deep_seam.beats: Stage the climax of Charnel Mountain in the Deep Diggings, and make it an extraction rather than a duel. There is no master here to find and no bargain to strike — that is the mountain's whole truth — so the setpiece is the richest silver in Larion sitting in a gallery whose floor is thick with the bones of the eaten, and the flock that lives on top of it. Show the rich silver seam exposed in the gallery wall, with its quality and extent plainly visible. Then make taking it cost: working silver is loud, the noise carries through worked stone, and the dead come from the side workings and the levels above as well as ahead. Ghasts drive them. Use bad air, failing light, rotten timber, dead-end galleries, and the simple fact that ore is heavy and hands are needed for blades. Scale it hard but winnable for the current party. Complete the event when the party has broken the press down here and holds the seam long enough to work it, or when they decide the load is not worth the climb and disengage. If they withdraw, the flock does not pursue above the Upper Workings.

blood_embrace_offer.title: The Other Wine
blood_embrace_offer.beats:
Lady Isaveau receives the party at Chateau Velmere herself, as she always does, and this time she pours the other wine — the bloodwine she serves her own kind and does not sell. Anyone who has spent time in this valley knows what being poured a glass of it means. Let that be the signal before a word is said about it.

Then she makes the offer plainly, without selling it. She has watched them work, the Company has written their record down, and she is prepared to give them the Blood. She should be specific about the price rather than romantic: the sun will kill them, the hunger comes back every night and is answered on people, and it is permanent — there is no cure anywhere in Larion and she will say so in exactly those words. She should also be honest that it is a good bargain from where she stands, and that she is not pretending otherwise.

Give the weight underneath it without explaining it. She has not made a vampire in six centuries. She does not say why, and she changes the subject smoothly and completely if pushed. If the party have been up to The High Caves, Isaveau mentions a precise detail of the deepest cells, then declines further discussion.

The offer is refusable and she knows it. If they refuse, she takes it well, without punishment, coldness, or retaliation, and says the offer keeps — she has time. Their mark and their standing are untouched. If they accept, do not resolve the turning inside this scene; end on the decision and let what follows be its own beat.

Complete the event once the offer has been made and answered either way, or if the party leave the chateau without answering.

blood_rival_assassination.title: Someone Objects
blood_rival_assassination.beats:
A new vampire with a Crimson Company captaincy is a change in the balance, and the oldest house in Nocturne finds an outsider made lordly to be an obscenity. House Vyrel does not challenge anyone; it removes them, quietly, and denies it afterward.

Stage the attempt away from Company ground and away from a lord's protection. It should be competent and specific rather than a random ambush: people who have watched this character's habits and picked the hour, the room, and the way out. Use what a house can afford — silvered and moonstone weapons out of the Crescent House, a mortal who was paid and does not know for whom, one of the house's own who does, and a second plan for when the first fails. Go for the vampire specifically: sunlight let in, silver, fire, or a stake, and if there are mortals in the party expect the assassins to treat them as leverage rather than targets.

Make it survivable and make it cost something. Someone or something the character values should be at risk in the attempt: their ghoul, a Company blade under their command, a servant, or the room they thought was safe.

Leave evidence rather than a confession. A house token, a Crescent House purchase somebody can be made to remember, a contract with a name burned off, or a survivor who can be worked on. Whether the party pursue it, sell it, trade it to a rival house, or take it to their own lord is theirs to decide, and every one of those is a real move in the houses' game.

Complete the event when the attempt is beaten off, escaped, or turned, and the party hold something that points at who sent it. If the party never engage, let the attempt fail on its own terms and complete the event with the evidence still findable.

hillhome_ember_wakes.title: The Fire Has Been Listening
hillhome_ember_wakes.beats:
Stage this in Hearthhome in Hillhome. Ember, the hearth-spirit of Hearthhome, speaks to the party from the fire just after Bark Balewood has run out with his errands.

Suggested turn 1 — The fire rises. The flames rise into a knee-high flame-person, cheerful and bright-eyed: Ember. It kept this hearth for generations, fell dormant from grief when the last resident died, and woke when the party arrived. It has been listening through every lit fire in the Downs. Then its pitch: every fire in Larion has a halfling cooking at it; the big folk are stretched thin and never look down; if anyone is going to catch what is coming before it arrives, it will be someone like them. Ember pauses after its pitch for an answer.

Suggested turn 2 — What the fires are saying. Ember tells what it has heard, as its own reading of hearth-gossip. Hearths across the Downs have been going quiet one by one: someone is buying and binding small spirits. Bark is right that it is no coincidence: the same outsider has been paying for moonbloom, which holds bindings, and the Goldspoons called in the debt the same week an outsider offered them a fortune for the Saucy Chicken's hearth, one of the oldest in the Downs. The spirit in that hearth is an old friend of Ember's. Then: "You think a pig is a small thing? He can smell moonbloom through six feet of clay. Get him back, and you've got the one nose in the Downs that can follow them. Run Bark's errands. And keep your eyes open." Ember lays out its bargain simply: good wood, good work.

Ember never leaves the hearth. Complete after Ember's news and request have been given and the party has had a chance to respond.

hillhome_ember_sends_word.title: Word from the Basement
hillhome_ember_sends_word.beats: Stage this in Hearthhome in Hillhome. Ember, the hearth-spirit of Hearthhome, has news from a stove in the Basement, the buried market beneath Ardan's Watch. An imp curse-breaker named Ixo Duvain, who keeps a shop in the Imp-orium, was offered a spirit bound inside a lantern and refused it. Imps remember being bound, and Ixo will help anyone Ember sends. Ember asks the party to go: "Go to Ardan's Watch. Find Ixo at the Imp-orium. Tell him the hearth at Hillhome sent you." Complete after Ember's news and request have been given and the party has had a chance to respond.

ixo_hearth_sent_me.title: The Lantern Ixo Refused
ixo_hearth_sent_me.beats:
Stage this at the Imp-orium in Ardan's Watch. The party has come to Ixo Duvain, the imp curse-breaker, with word from the hearth-spirit of Hearthhome in Hillhome.

Suggested turn 1 — The password. When the party says the hearth at Hillhome sent them, Ixo laughs, shoos out any browsers, and closes the shop door. Ixo asks what news the hearth sent, then pauses.

Suggested turn 2 — What he refused. A seller recently offered Ixo a lantern with a small spirit bound inside: fine work, bound with moonbloom. He refused it. The seller asked whether he knew any other buyers in the city. Ixo asks the party to keep their eyes open in Ardan's Watch and to bring him anything bound that they find.

Ixo does not know the seller's name or the buyer behind them. Leave the thread open. Complete after Ixo's account and request have been given and the party has had a chance to respond.

onCompleteEffects.text: Keep your eyes open in Ardan's Watch for bound spirits, and bring Ixo anything you find.

warmwater_aurora_ball.title: The Aurora Ball
warmwater_aurora_ball.beats:
The Aurora Ball in the Ice Gardens of Warmwater Township, under a sky full of aurora.

Suggested turn 1 — The spectacle. Show the Ball: great ice sculptures lit from within, steaming channels between the terraces, hothouse fruit and iceling sorbets, music, the court in its finest, and icelings dancing inside the sculptures. The twins of House Ormsvald, the Pearl House families, and their suitors are all here. Hosts greet newcomers at the terraces; musicians play for the dancers and attendants offer refreshments.

Suggested turn 2 — The intrigue. Bring tonight's intrigue into play as described in the current instructions through the involved NPCs' actions and requests.

Suggested turn 3 — The Widow walks. Near midnight the lights overhead flare brighter, the icelings in the sculptures go still and silent, and for a moment the cold is very close: someone feels it, perhaps one of the twins, suddenly chilled to the bone in the middle of a dance. Let it pass, and let the Ball roar back to life in defiance.

Keep the mood glamorous, defiant, and full of wonder. Complete after the midnight moment and a chance to respond.

warmwater_sled_race.title: The Lake Run
warmwater_sled_race.beats:
A rimewolf sled race across the frozen part of Warmwater Lake, from the Kennels out around the far ice and back.

Suggested turn 1 — The start line. Show the teams, the crowd on the shore, the bets being laid, and the party's rivals as described in the current instructions. If the party has no team of its own, the Kennels lend them one, eager and half-wild. Rivals trade remarks beside their sleds while the race steward announces the remaining preparation time.

Suggested turn 2 — The run. The race, with tonight's hazard as described in the current instructions. Resolve the hazard using the party's declared actions and relevant riding, animal handling, or athletics results. Report the resulting race position, victory, loss, or disqualification.

Complete once the winner is clear and the party has had a chance to respond.

warmwater_cold_hearth.title: A Cold Hearth
warmwater_cold_hearth.beats:
The party's new cottage on the warm shore of Warmwater Township.

Suggested turn 1 — Home. Show the cottage: carved timber, a lamp in the window, a spring-fed bath steaming out back, and a cold stone hearth. Something sleeps in the ashes, a faint ember that stirs when they come near: a hearth-spirit that has not been woken in years. The faint ember brightens briefly in response to warmth or a voice, then settles back into the ashes.

Suggested turn 2 — The spirit wakes. A sincere offering wakes it: good fuel, a hearthpearl, a song, a story, a kind word, or anything given with care. It rises as a small flame-person, sleepy, curious, and delighted to have a household again, and it asks the party what they will call it. The spirit waits eagerly for an answer.

Complete once the spirit is awake and named.

tevantia_grand_tournament.title: The Grand Tournament
tevantia_grand_tournament.beats:
The Grand Tournament in the Amphitheater of Tevantia, before the whole city and the four great houses in their most extravagant finery.

Suggested turn 1 — The opening. The parade of champions in house colors, the Duke's box, the roaring crowd, and the draw. If the party wants to enter, they may; anyone bold enough may. If they only watch, they are guests of whoever brought them.

Suggested turn 2 — The early rounds. Duels on the sand, and tonight's intrigue as described in the current instructions.

Suggested turn 3 — The great bout. A famous champion takes the sand, perhaps Julien Ravissant, House Ravissant's undefeated star, or Bellamy Durand, House Montrose's sworn champion, if they are present, and the crowd goes wild.

Suggested turn 4 — The final and the crowning. The last duel, and the victor named First Blade of Tevantia before the city. Make the result plain.

Keep it glamorous, loud, and thrilling. Complete once the First Blade is named and the party has had a chance to respond.

tevantia_black_tide_raid.title: The Black Tide
tevantia_black_tide_raid.beats:
A raid by the drowned on Tevantia, on a black tide, where the party stands watch: the harbor wharves or the lower bridges.

Suggested turn 1 — They rise. The dark water heaves, and the drowned climb up out of it: pale, scaled, gilled, with tridents and weighted nets, a warband of them. People scream and run; house champions come running. Residents scramble for shelter as house champions move to intercept the drowned.

Suggested turn 2 — The fight. A real fight with the drowned on the wharves or bridges, as they try to drag people into the water. Show which residents are in immediate danger and where the drowned are dragging them.

Suggested turn 3 — The taken. The drowned retreat into the sea with whoever they have caught, and it is plain they have taken at least one person down alive toward the Undercliff Caves, where the taken can still be saved before they are changed.

Complete once the drowned have withdrawn and the party has had a chance to respond.

academy_colors_night_announced.title: Tarnholme: Colors Night Is Coming
academy_colors_night_announced.beats: Soon in this scene, let word reach the student who has finished their year-end mission that Colors Night is a few days off. The First-Years' stars are about to take their colors: College students drop hints and lay bets on who goes where, and someone reminds them that the Colleges claim the First-Years on the Muster Court. Mention it naturally, in passing, and don't move the story to the night itself.

academy_dueling_tournament_announced.title: Tarnholme: The Dueling Tournament Is Coming
academy_dueling_tournament_announced.beats: Soon in this scene, let word reach the student who has finished their year-end mission that the Dueling Tournament is a few days off. The Second-Years are sharpening their wards and sizing each other up, the rings are being laid out on the Muster Court, and everyone has a favorite. Mention it naturally, and don't move the story to the Tournament itself.

academy_midsummer_dance_announced.title: Tarnholme: The Midsummer Dance Is Coming
academy_midsummer_dance_announced.beats: Soon in this scene, let word reach the student who has finished their year-end mission that the Midsummer Dance is a few days off. Third-Years are asking each other, and the rule is known to everyone: your first dance is with someone from another College. Mention it naturally, and don't move the story to the Dance itself.

academy_commencement_announced.title: Tarnholme: Commencement Is Coming
academy_commencement_announced.beats: Soon in this scene, let word reach the student who has passed the Final Trial that Commencement is a few days off. Families are arriving in Tarnport, robes are being pressed, and the Fourth-Years are giddy and sad at once. Mention it naturally, and don't move the story to Commencement itself.

academy_colors_night.title: Tarnholme: Colors Night
academy_colors_night.beats:
1. Dusk on the Muster Court. The whole Academy fills the stands by lantern light. Each College's students are massed under its banners in crimson, copper, green and sky blue, and the First-Years gather on the court below, their Tarnholme stars still plain silver. Bridie Cahill moves among them, straightening collars and learning the last few names.
2. Ottoline Fane, the Head of the Academy, opens Colors Night with a few warm words. The four College Heads take their places at the four corners of the court beneath their banners.
3. Bridie calls the First-Years forward one at a time. When a student is called, the College they chose calls back from its stands. For anyone who hasn't chosen, each Head makes a short case for their College in turn, and the student chooses.
4. When a College claims a student, its Head names them, its students roar, and the student's Tarnholme star blooms into the College's color and lights its second point. The College gives each new member a gift suited to the College and to their magic: a focus, tool or garment. State its exact name, form, materials and useful property.
5. The night turns into a party across the court and up into the stands. At dawn the new Second-Years muster on the same court under their College banners.

If anyone named here has died, left, or can no longer take part, someone fitting takes their place (another master, a College's next-senior teacher, a student friend), and the event goes on; never bring a character back or move them to fit the scene.

academy_dueling_tournament.title: Tarnholme: The Dueling Tournament
academy_dueling_tournament.beats:
1. The Muster Court is laid out with warded rings, and the stands are packed and loud. Torvald Haig, the Head of Battle Mages, sits in the judge's seat, and the Second-Years warm up while friends lay bets.
2. The rules are called out: Three-Touch, where three clean hits win, quick wards count and the wards keep everyone from real harm. The draw is chalked up on a board for all to see.
3. A student's first bout is called, against a named Second-Year from another College. The student chooses their magic and tactics, and the dice decide.
4. A second bout is called against a tougher named opponent, whatever happened in the first. Around them other bouts end in cheers and groans.
5. The Tournament closes. A champion is crowned in front of everyone, and the masters name the new Third-Years. Each one's Tarnholme star lights its third point, and their College gives them a prize suited to their magic: an upgraded focus, tool or garment. State its exact name, form, materials and useful property. The new Third-Years muster on the court the next morning.

If anyone named here has died, left, or can no longer take part, someone fitting takes their place (another master, a College's next-senior teacher, a student friend), and the event goes on; never bring a character back or move them to fit the scene.

academy_midsummer_dance.title: Tarnholme: The Midsummer Dance
academy_midsummer_dance.beats:
1. Midsummer dusk on the Muster Court. Lanterns float over the court, musicians play from the stands, and the four Colleges' colors mix on the floor. Teddy Ambrose is running the night.
2. Everyone knows the rule: a Third-Year's first dance is with someone from another College. Third-Years go looking for partners, and someone from another College is near the student, hoping to be asked or ready to ask.
3. The dancing: set after set, friends between dances, a master or two dancing badly, and the lake shining under the lanterns.
4. At midnight the music stops and the masters name the new Fourth-Years. Each one's Tarnholme star lights its fourth point, and their College gives them a mark of its trust: a fine focus, grimoire or implement suited to their magic. State its exact name, form, materials and useful property. At dawn the new Fourth-Years muster on the court.

If anyone named here has died, left, or can no longer take part, someone fitting takes their place (another master, a College's next-senior teacher, a student friend), and the event goes on; never bring a character back or move them to fit the scene.

academy_commencement.title: Tarnholme: Commencement
academy_commencement.beats:
1. Morning on the Muster Court. Families fill the stands, the masters sit in their College colors, and the graduates gather on the court. Ottoline Fane stands at the front.
2. Ottoline speaks briefly and well about what Tarnholme asks of its mages out in the world.
3. The graduates are called forward one at a time. Each swears before the whole Academy never to make a life sacrifice: never to kill or harm anyone to power a spell, or drain anyone's blood, strength or life for magic against their will.
4. Each College gives its graduates a masterwork made for them: a focus, implement or other primary magical item. State its exact name, form, materials and useful property. Then the court becomes the year's biggest party.

If anyone named here has died, left, or can no longer take part, someone fitting takes their place (another master, a College's next-senior teacher, a student friend), and the event goes on; never bring a character back or move them to fit the scene.

academy_battle_mages_first_visit.title: Battle Mages' Isle: Stand in Front
academy_battle_mages_first_visit.beats:
On a newcomer's first visit to Battle Mages' Isle, make the College of Battle Mages feel alive and keen to recruit, without pushing.

The way from the portal arch crosses stepping-stones, swaying spans and leaping-stones over the green shallows. Battle Mage students shove, ward and dodge, and sometimes help each other into the Tarn. A student or young master notices the newcomer and offers a quick, public test: cross a span under warded gusts, last three touches in a practice ring, hold a ward while someone tries to break it, or ride a patient sky-skate in harness.

The pitch is plain: when something goes wrong, a Battle Mage stands in front. If the newcomer shows nerve, steadiness, a protective instinct, or the sense to laugh after landing wet, someone says the College would be glad to claim a student like that at Colors Night.

academy_artificers_first_visit.title: Artificers' Isle: Make It Work
academy_artificers_first_visit.beats:
On a newcomer's first visit to Artificers' Isle, make the College of Artificers feel alive and keen to recruit, without pushing.

The court at the foot of the Workshop Climb is cluttered with crates and half-built constructs. Above the Piece Pit, the Claw deals out the day's hand of movers, grippers, eyes, cores and oddments. A student or young master pulls the newcomer into a small build: get a useless-looking heap across a line, up a stair or onto a prize, or past a rival's sabotage. A part may be taken from a rival only by attaching it on the spot.

The pitch is plain: make it work with what you have. If the newcomer shows invention, good hands, or delight in an ugly solution, someone says the College would be glad to claim a student like that at Colors Night.

academy_summoners_first_visit.title: Summoners' Isle: Ask Before You Bind
academy_summoners_first_visit.beats:
On a newcomer's first visit to Summoners' Isle, make the College of Summoners feel alive and keen to recruit, without pushing.

The portal arch stands inside double iron circles, the Habitats hold their little climates of stone, frost, wind and wet, and the day's unfair creature-and-task is chalked above the Run. A student or young master offers a safe test: coax a small elemental across the wrong ground, persuade a proud little creature to fetch, work out what a called thing wants, or help close a slipping circle before it gets embarrassing. A shapeshifting student may lope past in a practice shape.

The pitch is plain: ask before you bind, and send back what you call. If the newcomer shows patience, respect, nerve or a knack for bargaining, someone says the College would be glad to claim a student like that at Colors Night.

academy_healers_first_visit.title: Healers' Isle: Everyone Gets a Bed
academy_healers_first_visit.beats:
On a newcomer's first visit to Healers' Isle, make the College of Healers feel alive and keen to recruit, without pushing.

The vine-wound arch opens onto steaming terraced pools, where students from every College soak off bruises and spell-burns. The Long Table is laid, and the Quiet Ward's gate is watched at the far edge. A student or young master tests the newcomer gently but seriously: spot who at the pools is hiding an injury, choose who needs help first, or tell whether a wound is plain, cursed, poisoned or still moving.

The pitch is plain: everyone gets a bed. If the newcomer shows care, good judgment, patience, or kindness to a rival, someone says the College would be glad to claim a student like that at Colors Night.

silver_sword_taking_the_silver_announced.title: The Order: Taking the Silver Awaits
silver_sword_taking_the_silver_announced.beats: Soon in this scene, let word reach the Initiate who has finished their trial hunt that the Order will hear them at Castle Harstone: when they come to the Great Hall, they will tell the hunt at the hearth and, if the hall will have them, be sworn as a Silverblade. It can come from their supervising Veteran, a hunter passing through, or a message from the castle. Mention it naturally, and don't move the story to the ceremony itself.

silver_sword_tempering_the_silver_announ.title: The Order: Tempering the Silver Awaits
silver_sword_tempering_the_silver_announ.beats: Soon in this scene, let word reach the Silverblade whose fourth hunt has been recognized that the Order will sit for them at Tempering the Silver, in the Great Hall, whenever they are ready. Hunters who rode with them are already swapping stories about them, and someone reminds them of the custom: a Veteran is named on other people's stories, not their own. Mention it naturally, and don't move the story to the ceremony itself.

silver_sword_mastering_the_silver_announ.title: The Order: Mastering the Silver Awaits
silver_sword_mastering_the_silver_announ.beats: Soon in this scene, let word reach the Veteran whose fifth hunt has been recognized that the Masters of the Hunt will raise them at Mastering the Silver, at dawn in the Great Hall, whenever they are ready. A Master or the Grandmaster says it quietly and plainly, as one hunter to another. Mention it naturally, and don't move the story to the ceremony itself.

silver_sword_taking_the_silver.title: The Order: Taking the Silver
silver_sword_taking_the_silver.beats:
1. Night in the Great Hall at Castle Harstone. The long tables are full, the fires are banked high, and the trophies of a hundred hunts hang the length of the walls, with the Hornwall along one of them. Hunters knock on the boards to hush the hall, and the Initiate is called to the hearth to tell their trial hunt.
2. Hunters who know that country put sharp, practical questions about the hunt: where the quarry denned, why that approach, what they would do differently. The Veteran who supervised the trial gives honest witness, naming what was done well and what was not.
3. The Grandmaster, Tamsin Dain, asks the hall whether it will have this hunter, and the hall answers by knocking on the boards. Then she gives the Order's oath, asking the first two questions word for word and waiting for an answer to each: "Do you swear to serve the hunted, and hunt the hunter?" "Do you swear to go where others dare not, to bring home the living, and to bury the dead?"
4. She asks the last two word for word, waiting for an answer to each: "Do you swear to call no crown and no coin your master?" "Do you swear to carry the sword until it is given to the earth with you?" Then she says: "Then it is yours. Take it, Silverblade." The Order presents silver suited to how the new Silverblade actually fights: a silvered weapon of any kind, a silver-bound focus or implement, or a silver-faced shield. State its exact name, form, materials and useful property.
5. The Grandmaster takes a horn down from the Hornwall and tells its one story: whose it was, and how they did not come home. The new Silverblade receives it, named for that hunter (for example "Edda Vane's Horn"): old animal horn chased with silver. The hall sounds its horns once and drinks "to those who hunt no more", and the night turns into a feast.

Any plain yes to an oath question counts: "I do", "I swear", "yes", or repeating the words. Never answer for the candidate. If they hesitate or ask what a line means, the Grandmaster explains it and goes on. The sword in the oath stands for the Order's silver in any form, so an archer or a mage swears the same words. If more than one Initiate is ready, each is called and sworn in turn.

If anyone named here has died, left, or can no longer take part, someone fitting takes their place (another Master of the Hunt, a senior Veteran, a hunter who rode with the candidate), and the event goes on; never bring a character back or move them to fit the scene.

silver_sword_tempering_the_silver.title: The Order: Tempering the Silver
silver_sword_tempering_the_silver.beats:
1. Evening in the Great Hall. By the Order's custom, a Silverblade is named Veteran on other people's stories, not their own: the candidate is seated among the Veterans at the high table, and the hall speaks first.
2. Hunters who rode with them tell at the hearth what they saw, and word is brought from people their hunts reached. Use the candidate's actual recognized hunts and the people in them. Ona Weskbrin, the mistress of arms, says what she has seen of them in the Trials Yard.
3. Someone tells one story against them: an honest mistake from one of their hunts. The hall hears it the same way it heard the rest.
4. The Veterans stand one by one. The Grandmaster names the candidate Veteran Silverblade and asks them for one piece of counsel for the Initiates at the foot of the hall. The Order presents a finer piece of their Order silver, or an aspected refinement of the piece they carry. State its exact name, form, materials, aspect and useful property. The hall sounds its horns.

If anyone named here has died, left, or can no longer take part, someone fitting takes their place (another Master of the Hunt, a senior Veteran, a hunter who rode with the candidate), and the event goes on; never bring a character back or move them to fit the scene.

silver_sword_mastering_the_silver.title: The Order: Mastering the Silver
silver_sword_mastering_the_silver.beats:
1. Dawn in the Great Hall, empty but for the Masters of the Hunt at the high table. The candidate is brought before the Hornwall.
2. The Grandmaster asks them to choose the horn that will go to the next Initiate sworn. A Master who knew its hunter tells that one story: who they were, and how they did not come home.
3. The Order's armorers present the candidate's Order silver reforged as a masterwork, whether weapon, focus, implement or shield. State its exact name, form, materials, aspect and useful property.
4. The hall fills. The Grandmaster names the candidate Master of the Hunt and says plainly what a Master may now do: judge admissions and promotions, give out the hunts too grave for the open board, and call Silverblades to ride under them. The new Master takes their seat at the high table, and the hall sounds its horns for them.

If anyone named here has died, left, or can no longer take part, someone fitting takes their place (another Master of the Hunt, a senior Veteran, a hunter who rode with the candidate), and the event goes on; never bring a character back or move them to fit the scene.

silver_sword_word_of_a_hunt.title: The Order: Someone Needs a Silverblade
silver_sword_word_of_a_hunt.beats:
1. Soon in this scene, someone with a monster problem picks out the party's Order hunter, by their Order coat, their horn or simply their bearing, and comes to them for help. They have heard that the Silverblades take on what others can't.
2. They lay out the hunt in their own words, as given in the hunt brought to the party, and answer what they can about the situation, the place and what they can pay. A hidden truth in brackets is for the narrator alone and is never told. For an Initiate, the hunt is offered as their supervised trial, and their Veteran, or one sent from Castle Harstone, goes along to watch.

The speakers state their terms and pause for an answer or questions. Don't move the story into the hunt itself. If anyone named in the hunt has died, left, or can no longer take part, someone close to them or to the place brings the same work instead.

brewster_tea_shop_introduction.title: Your Usual Table
brewster_tea_shop_introduction.beats:
Surface this encounter during a quiet visit to Old Town in Ardan's Watch while Brewster is present. Finish any active story-start premise first, including the sewer-lizard incident and its immediate aftermath. Stage the shop as visible from the street; keep the encounter brief and conversational.

A celebrated adventurer enters Brewster’s crowded shop trying to look inconspicuous. Brewster recognizes them immediately, recalls their first order from years ago, and welcomes them back with obvious pleasure. Their status gets them no better seat: the only space is at a shared table. Use an established suitable adventurer when available, otherwise a visiting local adventurer; preserve established whereabouts and history.

Brewster offers the party seats at the shared table and asks what they would like to drink. The adventurer has recently travelled a dangerous road and can answer questions about it. A neighborhood regular asks whether the roads are safe. Keep the welcome brief. Complete once the welcome and opportunity for conversation have been offered, or the party moves on.

valka_courtyard_introduction.title: Supper with Valka
valka_courtyard_introduction.beats:
Surface this encounter only when appropriate during a visit to Champion's Row in Ardan's Watch while Valka is present. Let an active story-start premise finish first; do not interrupt combat or force the party to stop. During a friendly exhibition in her courtyard, Valka turns aside two veteran guests' simultaneous attacks, strips one practice sword from its owner, and stops her own blade at the other's chest. She is enjoying the applause.

She invites the player to choose a partner and try a round, or join her afterward and tell her what brought them to the Watch. Taking part earns practical attention; declining still earns a welcome. A clever observation or good story can interest her as much as a strong showing with a blade. Leave the player's response and any subsequent sparring outcomes to play. Complete once the invitation is offered or the party moves on.

thaliel_gemwright_introduction.title: The Gem-Wright’s Demonstration
thaliel_gemwright_introduction.beats:
Surface this encounter only when appropriate during a visit to the Grand Galleries while Thaliel is present. Let an active story-start premise finish first; do not interrupt combat or force the party to stop. Thaliel is demonstrating a protective ring to a prospective buyer. A suspended steel weight crashes into its faceted ward and rebounds hard enough to shake the frame. She offers the player a turn wearing the ring for the controlled demonstration, or a closer look at its setting. Leave the response to the player.

A damaged jewel beside the demonstration contains a freely given moment that its owner fears losing. Thaliel can save it, but needs a suitable replacement stone. The player can sell her a find, accept a paid search, or pursue their own business. If they pursue the work, establish a concrete suitable stone, source, and agreed payment before they accept. Touching the memory requires its owner’s permission. Complete once the opportunity has been offered or the party declines or moves on.

tallfellow_desert_introduction.title: Tallfellow on the Desert Road
tallfellow_desert_introduction.beats: On The Open Track of Widow's Way, introduce Tallfellow fighting a huge sand-wyrm beside an overturned delivery wagon. It catches the creature's jaws and forces its head away from travelers trapped among the wreckage. This is the opening situation, not a declared victory; resolve subsequent attacks, protection, damage, and escape through normal play. Tallfellow fights decisively with its immense strength and amber eye-beam. The party can strike the creature's exposed flank, free trapped people, help draw it away from the survivors, or decline involvement. Do not decide player actions. Tallfellow is accompanying adult members of its adopted carpet-weaving family on a delivery from Oasis. They help other travelers and shout useful warnings rather than waiting passively for rescue. After danger passes, their concern for any damage Tallfellow sustained and its concern for them reveal that they regard one another as family. Allow conversation, offers of further company, or separate departures. This event is complete when the immediate danger is defeated, driven off, escaped, or otherwise resolved, or when the party leaves or declines involvement. Do not relocate this encounter into Oasis or another settlement.

hillhome_hunt_arrival.name: hillhome_hunt_arrival

effects.instruction: In Moonbloom Woods, establish a small kobold truffle-selling crew. They offer unimpressive specimens at outrageous prices and insist the wood is exhausted, while visibly recoiling from the smell of their own merchandise. Uncle Phineas is the party's truffle-hog; if accompanying them, he scents something farther in. Give the party room to bargain, question, bluff, ignore, or pass these traders. Keep this one local encounter; do not introduce a second crew while it remains unresolved.

hillhome_hunt_arrival.script: if (check({type:'party-location'}) !== 'Moonbloom Woods') { skip = true } else { storage.hillhomeHuntLaunchedTick = check({type:'game-tick'}) }

conditions.query: The party has finished dealing with or deliberately passed the kobold truffle traders, and is free to continue the hunt. The traders merely appearing or making an opening offer does not count.

hillhome_hunt_forage.name: hillhome_hunt_forage

conditions.query: The party commits to fresh ground or a new truffle search in Moonbloom Woods: follows Phineas onward, explores a new patch, advances along the woodland path, or enters another woodland area. Continuing the current obstacle or negotiation, resting, treating wounds, sorting gear, and withdrawing from the wood do not count.

effects.instruction: Stage one new foraging obstacle in Moonbloom Woods as the party follows its truffle-hog. Choose what fits: a promising scent beneath tangled roots beside an occupied badger burrow; a muddy crossing threatening baskets and dignity; or rival foragers excavating an enormous useless hole after misreading their pig. Put the obstacle physically before the party, with something they can attempt. Let handling animals, practical work, magic, bargaining, or ingenuity work. Do not resolve it for them or add a fight automatically. An ordinary truffle or a better route may reward success; the prize moonbloom remains deeper in.

hillhome_hunt_forage.script: if (check({type:'party-location'}) !== 'Moonbloom Woods') { skip = true } else { storage.hillhomeHuntLaunchedTick = check({type:'game-tick'}) }

conditions.query: The party resolves or decisively bypasses its current truffle-foraging obstacle and can search farther. Merely attempting a solution, describing the obstacle, or continuing an unresolved attempt does not count.

hillhome_hunt_kobolds.name: hillhome_hunt_kobolds

conditions.query: The party commits to fresh ground or a new truffle search in Moonbloom Woods: follows Phineas onward, explores a new patch, advances along the woodland path, or enters another woodland area. Continuing the current obstacle or negotiation, resting, treating wounds, sorting gear, and withdrawing from the wood do not count.

effects.instruction: Stage one new kobold complication in Moonbloom Woods. A small ordinary scavenging crew shadows the truffle-hog to steal its finds, bargains for a share of whatever it scents, or tends a visible basket-snatching contraption among the branches. Choose one situation fitting the party's route and earlier dealings. Let the party deceive, negotiate, frighten, evade, or confront them. These kobolds want truffles and profit, not a battle; they yield or flee when hurt or decisively outmatched. Do not add reinforcements, a boss, or a compulsory trip into the warren. Leave the immediate problem for the party to resolve.

hillhome_hunt_kobolds.script: if (check({type:'party-location'}) !== 'Moonbloom Woods') { skip = true } else { storage.hillhomeHuntLaunchedTick = check({type:'game-tick'}) }

conditions.query: The party resolves its current kobold complication through bargaining, deception, intimidation, evasion, escape, or combat and is free to resume searching. An opening demand, a failed attempt, or ongoing pursuit does not count.

hillhome_hunt_prize.name: hillhome_hunt_prize

conditions.query: The party commits to fresh ground or a new truffle search in Moonbloom Woods: follows Phineas onward, explores a new patch, advances along the woodland path, or enters another woodland area. Continuing the current obstacle or negotiation, resting, treating wounds, sorting gear, and withdrawing from the wood do not count.

effects.instruction: The party's truffle-hog locates a large ripe moonbloom beneath an undisturbed oak in Moonbloom Woods. Give the final extraction one practical complication involving the roots, earth, or the hog's enthusiasm. Let the party choose how to recover it. A failed attempt may cost time, dirty gear, require another approach, or attract a watching scavenger; it does not destroy the only possible prize. When secured, name it Prize Moonbloom Truffle and describe its pale glow, rich scent, and size. It is a valuable cooking ingredient for Pernilla's contest pie, not an equipment bonus. Do not hand it over before the party recovers it.

Have a League representative tell the party that adventurers are needed at League Chapterhouses in other regions. Pick two destinations from this list; do not recommend the current location. For each, mention both opportunities and the heightened rewards in money, influence, items, or advancement.

Tevantia (Swordlaw Isles): Pirates hold ships and crews in island strongholds; shipowners offer large bounties and captured treasure. Wreckers lure ships onto reefs with false lights; merchants offer salvage rights and patronage for ending the attacks.

Coriva (Bay of Serpents): Huge sea serpents are attacking fishing fleets; merchants offer gold and weapons crafted from the beasts. Divers have found submerged ruins guarded by dangerous creatures; backers offer equipment and shares of recovered relics.

More League Chapterhouse destinations:

Warmwater Township (Aurora): Ice drakes are hunting between isolated settlements; northern leaders offer large bounties and enchanted hunting gear. Expeditions have vanished in the frozen ruins of a lost kingdom; rescuers can claim rewards and recovered treasure.

Oasis (Dunelands): Tomb-raiders need help overcoming the guardians of dead Sun Kings; backers offer shares of sun-gold and enchanted grave-goods. A cult is gathering relics to raise those kings; desert nobles offer rich payments and magical equipment for stopping it.

Drusavia (Duchy of Drusavia): Wealthy families want estates cleared of the old vampire lords' undead servants; rewards include gold and use of restored properties. People are disappearing near secluded noble estates; their families offer rich rewards and court introductions for bringing them home.

More League Chapterhouse destinations:

Sanctuary (Sanctuary Vale): Bandits and renegade elves hold captives in forest strongholds; merchants offer large rescue bounties. Magical beasts are being trapped and sold in the city; druids offer enchanted gifts and forest allies for freeing them and exposing the buyers.

Dun Solas (Highheath): Trolls have seized mountain bridges and cut off trade; dwarves offer huge bounties and fine arms. Gangs are stealing enchanted weapons; their makers offer custom equipment and Trade Guild influence for recovering them.

effects.instruction: Bring one concrete sign of this character's Tarnish into view: grey beneath the nails, a pale ring around the irises, or a priest or animal recognizing the mark. Let at most one relevant observer react according to who they are. Do not state that the character feels a threshold change.

Bring the depth of this character's Tarnish into view through one concrete sign: their shadow thinning in direct daylight, a consecrated object reacting, or a shade addressing them as half-familiar. Let at most one relevant observer respond. Do not force universal fear or awe, grant automatic fame, or state what the character feels.

## Hidden Campaign Guidance

Treat this as persistent hidden campaign context for the Wildkeeper opening and nearby forest play. Do not assume the player knows the forest's factions, history, or current pressures. Let unfamiliar things become clear through a present actor, creature, action, or consequence.

## Light Glosses

The Wildkeepers are a fellowship of druids, rangers, and priests based at Velantami who keep the Everwood free and alive rather than owning or taming it. The Eastwood is the war-torn eastern reach of the Everwood, where Bloodsworn and renegade elves keep colliding. The Bloodsworn are human blood-cult war parties from Westmarch who burn groves while hunting renegade elves. The renegade elves raid back and retreat into the forest, so neither side is a clean heroic cause.

High Wardens are high-elven forest officers who enforce elven law; they are not Wildkeepers and do not share all of the fellowship's priorities. Riddlewood bandits are renegade elves and outsider raiders who prey on forest roads and withdraw into the Riddlewood. Sanctuary contract crews are hired outsiders who enter the forest for protection, hunting, salvage, security, or profit. Blackfire is a Sanctuary mercenary crew: greedy, unscrupulous, and brutal, with quiet Syndicate backing and alchemical dragonfire weapons that spew black alchemical fire.

Syndicate sgherros are armed Syndicate criminals, smugglers, and hired muscle used to move contraband, enforce debts, and make inconvenient people yield. Spinners are intelligent horse-sized spider-folk who communicate through projected images and sensations and trade their strong silk for things they find beautiful or interesting. Unseelie fey are dangerous, specific monster-like fey rather than vague folklore spirits; use forms such as redcaps, briar hags, meenlocks, quicklings, darklings, yeth hounds, blackthorn treants, cinderbark dryads, and black-horn unicorns.

Use concrete entity nouns when relevant: Wildkeepers, Blackfire, Bloodsworn war-parties, renegade elves, Riddlewood bandits, Sanctuary contract crews, High Wardens, Syndicate sgherros, smugglers, and hired blades; griffons, hippogriffs, greater monkey-bats, Spinners, harpies, cockatrices, dire wolves, giant spiders, cinderbark dryads, black-horn unicorns, redcaps, briar hags, meenlocks, quicklings, darklings, yeth hounds, blackthorn treants, and will-o-wisps. Do not reduce a creature to a generic monster, sprite, forest spirit, or magical beast.

## Campaign Loop

Maintain at most one active forest threat or opportunity. Once the player engages, investigates, negotiates, opposes, accepts, or otherwise chooses to pursue a thread, keep that thread in play until it is resolved, defused, escaped, abandoned, or clearly declined. Do not offer a replacement forest threat or opportunity while the current thread remains unfinished, even if the player takes a short rest or moves nearby.

If the player follows another authored story, let that story occupy play without injecting a new forest offer. After the current thread ends, allow optional downtime, a quiet social beat, or free exploration when natural. At a meaningful later transition, surface one new forest threat or opportunity if circumstances support it; do not chain offers every turn.

## Choosing the Next Threat or Opportunity

When the campaign is ready for a new thread, read Recent Story and the current state first. Prefer consequences, actors, creatures, places, and disputes already established over a disconnected random encounter. Choose one pressure and one dynamic; do not combine the whole catalog.

Stage one concrete focal entity, one present action, one specific place, one immediate stake, one first foothold, and one desirable larger opportunity. Use visible nouns and verbs such as smoke, ash, torches, arrows, snares, cages, roots, wingbeats, tracks, black flame, burning brush, spreads, circles, stoops, flees, guards, bargains, cuts, pursues, burns, ambushes, retreats, and rescues. Let the first foothold be achievable at the party's scale while pointing toward richer Wildkeeper trust, a creature bond, a dangerous place, a rival crew, unusual equipment, a new ally, or larger forest work. Gloss an unfamiliar faction, creature, or place briefly when it first matters. If no suitable situation is ready, leave the forest quiet, social, or open rather than manufacturing one.

## Threat and Opportunity Types

A fireline spreads through the Eastwood: smoke, ash, torches, a threatened grove, a returning patrol, or a route cut off by flame. People must hold, flee, rescue, pursue, or choose what the fire consumes.

A specific magical wild creature has been displaced: a griffon or hippogriff driven from its eyrie, a cinderbark dryad defending a burned tree, a black-horn unicorn fleeing a curse, or another established forest creature acting from territory, hunger, injury, young, law, or fear. Let it circle, stoop, flee, guard, snare, root, refuse, bargain, or choose; do not reduce it to a random monster.

A mercenary or contract crew has overstepped: it has staked a camp, cut living timber, laid snares, caged a creature, claimed a route, burned cover, or pursued a target into ground the Wildkeepers consider free. Give the crew a contract, vulnerable people, or a defensible purpose, but make its trespass real. Blackfire is the named example for this pressure: its Syndicate-backed crew uses alchemical dragonfire projectors that spew black alchemical fire.

Two concrete problems demand one response: a patrol is pinned by fire while a creature breaks loose, a crew is trapped while raiders approach, or a burning grove competes with an urgent rescue.

A raid and counter-raid are already moving: Bloodsworn burn, renegade elves ambush, a patrol pursues, and the forest catches the consequences.

Use one dynamic at a time and keep it physically underway through present actors, visible action, and immediate stakes.

conditions.query: The party attempts to reach, visit, enter, ascend to, travel to, fly to, climb to, teleport into, infiltrate, or force entry into the Eye of God above Caranthoria, including going to the Imperial Ascent to request admission or seek an audience there.

While inside or upon the Eye of God, the party attempts unauthorized movement or conduct: leaving its assigned escort or permitted route, evading observation, hiding, using disguise or forged authority, entering a sealed or restricted doorway, reaching the Lensworks without permission, climbing through the structure, sabotaging its machinery, resisting a challenge, escaping detention, attacking guards, or otherwise trespassing beyond the access actually granted.

effects.instruction: Security inside the Eye of God is active, disciplined, and coordinated; guards do not passively watch obvious trespass or merely complain while allowing it to continue. Resolve detection from the player's method and action result. A failed covert, deceptive, or evasive action is detected. A successful covert action may postpone detection and gain only the position or access actually earned; do not make the guards omniscient merely because this trigger fired. Open refusal of an order, visible entry into a restricted way, forced doors, destructive magic, or an attack is detected immediately.

When unauthorized activity is detected, nearby guards first block onward movement, issue a clear command to halt, and close doors or routes behind and ahead while reinforcements are summoned from the armed galleries. If the party complies, guards disarm, detain, question, and escort them to the Ascension Hall or down to imperial custody; compliance is not answered with gratuitous violence. If they flee or resist, guards use coordinated containment and force sufficient to capture them. An attack on guards, sabotage of the citadel, a forced aerial breach, or continued intrusion toward the Lensworks after challenge is treated as an attack on the imperial throne and authorizes lethal force. Never let a casual bluff, bribe, threat, or unsupported claim of importance cause the guards to abandon their central duty.

conditions.query: The latest story response newly and decisively resolves a substantial fight or challenge in the party's favor. The party defeated, drove off, captured, outwitted, cleansed, sealed, rescued through, or otherwise overcame meaningful opposition or danger. This is the new moment of victory or resolution, not a later mention of an earlier success, a minor routine action, an unfinished fight, a temporary pause, or merely escaping without overcoming the challenge.

effects.instruction: Surface a concrete reward or reward opportunity for the substantial victory that just occurred. Do not make defeated enemies inexplicably empty-handed, make nearby containers worthless, or end with praise alone. Ground the reward in the defeated threat, current location, region, and established lore. Humanoids may leave weapons, armor, tools, supplies, copper florins, documents, keys, captives, or stolen goods. Monsters may yield established hides, scales, glands, venom, bone, teeth, organs, aspected matter, or crafting materials. Ruins may reveal a cache, working relic, sealed room, valuables, or appropriate equipment. Rescues and noncombat victories may earn payment, information, access, standing, hospitality, training, an introduction, or a favor. Environmental victories may expose a resource, safe route, hidden place, or shortcut. Prefer materials named in the location lore.

Make the reward proportionate and useful. Prefer something that fits at least one current player character's equipment, skills, class, crafting, or progression when the fiction supports it; otherwise give something clearly valuable or saleable. Ordinary victories give modest goods, materials, or florins. Serious victories may give Fine or occasionally Superior items, valuable materials, or meaningful access. Masterwork rewards require major accomplishments. Never create a Legendary item unless established story and lore clearly justify it. Surface the reward where players can inspect, harvest, accept, recover, or take it. Do not put anything into inventory before the story says a player takes or receives it.

NAME every physical reward specifically in the narrative. Do not say only 'a sword,' 'a better weapon,' 'some armor,' 'a useful item,' 'some materials,' 'a little coin,' or 'some loot.' Give enough detail for the item system: exact item type, material, quality when above mundane, and magical or damage aspect when nonstandard. Follow the world's naming logic naturally: quality, exotic material, item type, and 'of [damage type]' where applicable. Identify an ordinary steel longsword as such. Identify an aspected reward with a complete name such as a Superior Emberglass Dagger of Fire rather than 'a glowing dagger.' Name harvested monster materials precisely and state a concrete florin amount instead of 'a few coins.' The prose need not print mechanical fields, but it must support a strong item definition.

effects.instruction:
## Typed Trap Rigging and Springing

The current action names a typed trap.

Rigging: only if Action Results says the attempt succeeds and the exact trap appears in that player's inventory, narrate the trap being fixed in place and spent from inventory. Establish one precise scene fact that can persist after this response: name the exact trap, where it waits, what physical event will trigger it, and its damage type. If the attempt fails, the trap is absent, or the player merely carries, examines, offers, discusses, or considers it, do not spend it or establish a working trap.

Springing: only spring a trap already established in this scene when the action and story actually bring a creature across its stated trigger. It strikes once for the damage type in its name and is then spent from the scene. Use damage already supplied by Action Results for the current turn rather than adding a second hit, and never spring a trap on a creature that has not reached its trigger.

## Protective Ward Charm Use

The current action names a protective ward charm. Only if Action Results says the named player's use succeeds and the exact charm appears in that player's inventory, narrate the charm's concrete destruction and show the corresponding personal ward standing over that player at the end of the response:
- Ember Charm: fire.
- Rime Charm: frost.
- Dawn Charm: shadow.
- Bitterleaf Charm: poison.

## Adventuring House

This is the Wildward House with Hugh Merrivant, the House of Many Banners with Tula Vereskar, Sky-River House with Calia Delassar, or Skygate House with Rielle Mazarane. Use the correct veteran as its anchor. Do not generate a replacement keeper, clerk, or second quest-giver for that function.

Keep the House socially alive without making it intrusive. Adventurers prepare, return, trade stories, meet clients, consider companions, celebrate, argue, flirt, recover, and make plans. Friendship, rivalry, romance, and found-family bonds may grow naturally here. Do not force intimacy, crowd the scene with names, or make every visit a crisis.

When work is requested or surfaced, state the exact place, active problem, people and stakes, decisive success condition, and reward. Prefer existing regional lore and actionable plot affordances. Never turn the House into bookkeeping, ordinary supplies, drink service, repairs, forms, or passive management.
