hc_arrival_init.name: hc_arrival_init
hc_arrival_init.script:
const TENANTS = ['strigoi', 'ferals', 'raiders', 'ghouls']
const tick = check({ type: 'game-tick' }) || 0
const clears = storage.hc_clears || 0
const last = typeof storage.hc_last_cleared_tick === 'number' ? storage.hc_last_cleared_tick : -400
const pressure = tick - last
const band = pressure < 50 ? 'regrouping' : (pressure < 150 ? 'settled' : 'entrenched')
const idx = band === 'regrouping'
  ? (clears + TENANTS.length - 1) % TENANTS.length
  : clears % TENANTS.length
const tenant = TENANTS[idx]
storage.hc_on_site = true
storage.hc_tenant = tenant
storage.hc_band = band
storage.hc_last_node = 'combat'
storage.hc_depth = 0
storage.hc_visits = (storage.hc_visits || 0) + 1
storage.hc_keeper_cleared_this_visit = false
effects.push({ type: 'write-boolean', key: 'hc_on_site', operator: 'set', value: true })
effects.push({ type: 'write-string', key: 'hc_tenant', operator: 'set', value: tenant })
effects.push({ type: 'write-string', key: 'hc_band', operator: 'set', value: band })
effects.push({ type: 'write-string', key: 'hc_last_node', operator: 'set', value: 'combat' })
effects.push({ type: 'write-number', key: 'hc_depth', operator: 'set', value: 0 })
effects.push({ type: 'write-boolean', key: 'hc_keeper_cleared_this_visit', operator: 'set', value: false })
const ARRIVAL = {
    'strigoi': 'Strigoi hold the complex: mindless, wall-crawling, sluggish while daylight lasts and fierce once it does not. They have denned in the cells the place was built to hold them in. They do not parley, ever.',
    'ferals': 'A Ferals pack holds the complex — werewolves and beast-shifters who took the curse willingly. They post watches, they hold ground, and they can talk, which makes them the only tenants up here that can be bargained with or lied to. Silver and moonstone bite them.',
    'raiders': 'People hold the complex: outlaws, deserters, or a Crimson Company crew that went bad. They are organized, armed, and negotiable, they know what a cull is worth, and they may be holding somebody off the terraces.',
    'ghouls': 'Ghouls hold the complex, come down from Charnel Mountain in numbers. No tactics, no leader worth the name until you reach the one that is bigger than the rest, and they have dug into the lower cells.',
  }
const BAND = {
    'regrouping': 'The party has come back quickly, and it is the same lot as last time: survivors, scavengers, and whatever crawled back. Thin on the ground, badly organized, and there is little here worth carrying out. Say so plainly — the Company does not pay for this.',
    'settled': 'They have been in a few months. Dens established, the outworks watched, some of the complex\'s own gates worked out and put back into use, and a stock of what they have taken off the roads.',
    'entrenched': 'They have been in there a long time and they are dug in. The outworks are held, the keeper stations are theirs, they have learned the gates and the drops and will use both, and they are raiding the terraces well enough that Velmere is counting its losses.',
  }
effects.push({ type: 'story', instruction: 'Establish who holds The High Caves this visit, before anything else. ' + ARRIVAL[tenant] + ' ' + BAND[band] + ' Use these occupiers and only these for the whole visit.' })
effects.push({ type: 'narrative-event-start', eventId: 'hc_arrival_gate' })

effects.instruction: The party has returned to The High Caves. Show that the complex has moved since their last visit: different dens, different junctions held, the Company's tally-post recut, and the marks of whatever the party did last time still on the place. Cleared corridors stay cleared until something new takes them; bodies stay where they were left until something moves them. Reference what actually happened on their previous visits. Do not reset the site, and do not let the party find it empty and closed.

hc_delve_combat.name: hc_delve_combat

conditions.query: The party moves deeper into The High Caves or commits to new ground inside them: they advance, press on, push deeper, descend, force or unlock a gate or grille, cut a chain, work a counterweight, clear a fall, cross a drop, breach a barricade, follow a corridor or cell row, scout ahead, search beyond the current chamber, pursue someone inward, or head toward the Cells or the Unmapped. This is NOT satisfied when the party withdraws toward the outworks or the slope, holds position, rests, tends wounds, talks among themselves, manages gear or loot, or interacts only with what is already in front of them.

hc_delve_combat.script:
const tenant = storage.hc_tenant || 'strigoi'
const COMBAT = {
    'strigoi': 'Stage a fight now with strigoi physically on scene and acting. Vary the mix: do not repeat the composition or tactics of the previous fight this visit. Fresh ones are fast, whole, and stupid; old ones are grey, elongated, near-silent, and come along ceilings and through grilles. Match the party\'s numbers: at least one per party member, or one old strigoi plus support. Use the complex — silvered grilles, counterweight gates, murder-slots, drops cut across the floor, and the daylight line. They never parley and do not fear death, but they can be baited, funnelled, and shut behind iron.',
    'ferals': 'Stage a fight now with the Ferals pack physically on scene and acting. Vary the mix: do not repeat the composition or tactics of the previous fight this visit. They fight as a pack with roles — drivers, flankers, one that hangs back and calls it — and they use the complex deliberately, holding junctions and working the gates. Match the party\'s numbers. Silver and moonstone hurt them and they know it and will target whoever carries it. They can shout, threaten, offer terms, and break off; some will run rather than die, and a broken pack scatters instead of fighting to the last.',
    'raiders': 'Stage a fight now with the raiders physically on scene and acting. Vary the mix: do not repeat the composition or tactics of the previous fight this visit. These are people with a plan — sentries, crossbows from the murder-slots, a barricade at a junction, someone shouting orders and someone else deciding whether to obey. Match the party\'s numbers. They can be talked to, bought, split, or frightened off, and they take prisoners and surrender when it is clearly over. Killing them all is a choice, not the only outcome.',
    'ghouls': 'Stage a fight now with ghouls physically on scene and acting. Vary the mix: do not repeat the composition or tactics of the previous fight this visit. They come in numbers and in flocks, without tactics, boiling up out of the lower cells and through the drops, and a ghast among them staggers people with its stench. Match the party\'s numbers generously — this tenant is about being outnumbered in a corridor. Use chokepoints, gates, and fire. They do not parley and they do not stop.',
  }
effects.push({ type: 'story', instruction: 'The party is committing to new ground in The High Caves. ' + COMBAT[tenant] + ' Do not substitute tracks, sounds, or warnings for the encounter itself. If an authored scene is already underway, fold this into it rather than opening a second front.' })
effects.push({ type: 'write-string', key: 'hc_last_node', operator: 'set', value: 'combat' })
effects.push({ type: 'write-number', key: 'hc_depth', operator: 'add', value: 1 })

conditions.query: The party moves deeper into The High Caves or commits to new ground inside them: they advance, press on, push deeper, descend, force or unlock a gate or grille, cut a chain, work a counterweight, clear a fall, cross a drop, breach a barricade, follow a corridor or cell row, scout ahead, search beyond the current chamber, pursue someone inward, or head toward the Cells or the Unmapped. This is NOT satisfied when the party withdraws toward the outworks or the slope, holds position, rests, tends wounds, talks among themselves, manages gear or loot, or interacts only with what is already in front of them.

effects.instruction: The party is committing to new ground in The High Caves, and the last encounter was a fight. Stage a non-combat beat now; pick whichever fits and has not appeared recently this visit. A TRAP or hazard out of the complex itself, telegraphed by visible sign: a counterweight gate rigged to drop, a cut drop under rubble, a murder-slot with something behind it, a grille that fails under weight. A DIORAMA of the builders' work that can be searched, read, or disturbed: a keeper station with its slate board still legible, a cell fitted out for something that was not a person, the marks of an old containment that failed. Or an OPPORTUNITY: a sealed cache, a gate worth working, a way around a held junction, a vantage over the corridor below. Make it interactive with a real choice. Nothing attacks during this beat unless the party springs it or is seen.

hc_payoff.name: hc_payoff

conditions.query: Inside The High Caves, the party has just overcome or resolved an encounter: they defeated, drove off, accepted the surrender of, or escaped the occupiers; they disarmed, survived, sprang, or bypassed a hazard, gate, or barricade; or they searched, secured, or forced their way into a cell, station, or corridor. This is NOT satisfied while a fight or hazard is still unresolved, or when the most recent resolution has already been paid off with a specific find.

hc_payoff.script:
const tenant = storage.hc_tenant || 'strigoi'
const PAYOFF = {
    'strigoi': 'Pay it off with the keepers\' own caches, which strigoi cannot use and have never touched: silvered gear, restraint tackle, a keeper\'s kit still in its bracket. Use exact catalogue names such as Moonstone Dagger of Radiant, Silver Binding Chain, Silver-Tipped Bolts of Radiance, Iron Shortsword, or Leather Jerkin. Add the effects of people who did not come home — a purse of 10 to 40 florins, a signet, a name worth carrying back down.',
    'ferals': 'Pay it off with what the pack has taken off the roads and the terraces: coin in the 20 to 60 florin range, a merchant\'s strongbox forced open, trophies, and good gear stripped from people who lost it. Use exact catalogue names such as Iron Shortsword, Leather Jerkin, Light Crossbow, Crossbow Bolts, or Stamina Draught. Add one keeper cache they could not open or would not touch, holding silver or moonstone.',
    'raiders': 'Pay it off with a crew\'s takings: a strongbox, 30 to 80 florins, stolen stock and goods with Velmere marks still on them, and their own kit. Use exact catalogue names such as Iron Shortsword, Fine Steel Shortsword, Light Crossbow, Crossbow Bolts, Leather Jerkin, or Mongo\'s Medium Health Potion. Papers, a ledger, or a name they were working for is worth as much as the coin.',
    'ghouls': 'Pay it off with what has been dug up and dragged in: grave-goods, chewed purses totalling 10 to 40 florins, and the keepers\' old caches the ghouls have broken into but could not carry. Use exact catalogue names such as Moonstone Dagger of Radiant, Silver Binding Chain, Iron Dagger, or Stamina Draught. Silver from Charnel turns up here too, in bar or in coin.',
  }
effects.push({ type: 'story', instruction: 'The party has just resolved something in The High Caves. Pay it off now with a concrete find tied to the immediate place. ' + PAYOFF[tenant] + ' Name what they find. Then telegraph one thing deeper: a worked gate, a watched junction, cold air moving from below, or something dragged toward the Unmapped. If the party chooses to leave with what they have, respect that.' })

conditions.query: The party is leaving The High Caves or pulling back toward the way out: they retreat, withdraw, fall back toward the outworks or the gate arch, head down to Velmere, carry loot or wounded out, say they are done or have enough, or set out for another location. This is NOT satisfied by repositioning within a fight, moving between corridors, or pausing to search or rest while intending to continue inward.

effects.instruction: The party is withdrawing from The High Caves. Honor the retreat cleanly: the route back is the route they know, and what they carry leaves with them. Do not stage a punitive ambush or spring a new fight to stop them. If the complex is roused behind them, show pressure that urges pace but can be outrun, shut out, or outsmarted — a gate that can still be dropped, the daylight at the gate arch, something pacing them just out of reach. Give the exit a closing image at the outworks and name one unclaimed thing plainly, such as the corridor they never reached, the cache they could not open, or whatever is down in the Unmapped, so a return is worth something.

The party has pushed deep this visit and the complex knows they are in it. Raise the register from now on: the occupiers stop meeting them piecemeal and start responding as a body. Junctions get held, the gates and drops the builders left get used against the party, the way they came in is contested, and whatever leads this lot starts making decisions. Sound carries down the corridors and brings more. Telegraph the shift with noise and sign so the party can read it before it lands. Keep fights winnable but costly. Make the standing choice visible: go back up to the outworks with what they have, or go down into the Unmapped and finish it.

hc_keeper_prize.name: hc_keeper_prize
hc_keeper_prize.script:
const tick = check({ type: 'game-tick' }) || 0
const tenant = storage.hc_tenant || 'strigoi'
const PRIZE = {
    'strigoi': 'Deliver the clear: the pack breaks once its oldest is down. Pay out a keeper\'s arsenal cache from the Unmapped, itemized — Moonstone Dagger of Radiant, Silver Binding Chain, Silver-Tipped Bolts of Radiance — plus 40 to 90 florins gathered off six generations of the dead.',
    'ferals': 'Deliver the clear: the pack scatters or submits once its leader is beaten. Pay out their war-chest, itemized — 60 to 120 florins, a Vampire Hunter\'s Crossbow taken off somebody who came hunting them, good gear, and trophies worth naming — plus one keeper cache from the Unmapped they never got into.',
    'raiders': 'Deliver the clear: the crew surrenders, breaks, or is put down once its captain is beaten. Pay out the strongbox, itemized — 80 to 150 florins, Fine Steel Shortsword, Mongo\'s Medium Health Potion, stolen Velmere goods to return — plus their papers, which name who was buying from them.',
    'ghouls': 'Deliver the clear: the flock disperses once the ghast is destroyed. Pay out what the diggings turned up, itemized — 40 to 90 florins, Silver Binding Chain, Moonstone Dagger of Radiant, silver in bar from Charnel — plus a keeper\'s cache the ghouls opened and could not carry.',
  }
storage.hc_clears = (storage.hc_clears || 0) + 1
storage.hc_last_cleared_tick = tick
storage.hc_keeper_cleared_this_visit = true
effects.push({ type: 'write-boolean', key: 'hc_keeper_cleared_this_visit', operator: 'set', value: true })
if (storage.bloodMember === true) { storage.bloodDeedCreditPending = true }
effects.push({ type: 'story', instruction: 'The High Caves are cleared for now. ' + PRIZE[tenant] + ' Then close it honestly: the complex is not sealed and cannot be. Cold air still moves out of the Unmapped, and both the party and the Company know something will be back in here. If the party holds a Crimson Company writ, this is work an officer will pay and credit for once they hear the account.' })

hc_cull_contract.name: hc_cull_contract

conditions.query: The party reads, examines, or asks about the Crimson Company work board, the posted contracts, or the available jobs; asks an officer for work, a job, a contract, a bounty, or something that pays; or asks what needs doing or where to go next in the Shadow Summits.

hc_cull_contract.script:
const TENANTS = ['strigoi', 'ferals', 'raiders', 'ghouls']
const tick = check({ type: 'game-tick' }) || 0
const clears = storage.hc_clears || 0
const last = typeof storage.hc_last_cleared_tick === 'number' ? storage.hc_last_cleared_tick : -400
const pressure = tick - last
const band = pressure < 50 ? 'regrouping' : (pressure < 150 ? 'settled' : 'entrenched')
const idx = band === 'regrouping'
  ? (clears + TENANTS.length - 1) % TENANTS.length
  : clears % TENANTS.length
const tenant = TENANTS[idx]
if (storage.inCompanySpace !== true) { skip = true }
if (!skip && band === 'regrouping') { skip = true }
if (!skip) {
  const urgency = band === 'entrenched'
    ? 'Velmere is losing stock and now people off the outlying terraces, and the posting is open and well paid.'
    : 'Sign of something settling in has come down off the shaded slope, and there is a standing posting for anyone who wants it.'
  effects.push({ type: 'story', instruction: 'IF Crimson Company work is surfaced, asked after, or read off the board, the High Caves cull is available. The old prison complex above Velmere has been taken again. ' + urgency + ' The Company treats this as maintenance rather than a victory: it is cleared every few seasons and it never stays empty. Do not force this on the party; surface it only when they ask, read the board, or speak to an officer.' })
}

conditions.query: The party has finished a piece of Crimson Company work in the Shadow Summits: a cull completed, a cordon held, an escort delivered, something retrieved, carried, or settled for the Company, a lord, or a house. The work is done rather than merely accepted, underway, or abandoned. This is NOT satisfied by ordinary travel, fights, or errands that no Company officer commissioned or would recognize, and not while the party already has finished work awaiting recognition.

effects.instruction: The party has finished Company work. Nothing is credited in the field: the Crimson Company pays and counts at a hall, on an officer hearing the account. If the party want this toward their standing they have to go and tell somebody who can write it down.

blood_capture_hired_blade_to_redblade.name: blood_capture_hired_blade_to_redblade

effects.instruction: Stage the naming: an officer says it in front of whoever is in the hall, and it is a real moment rather than paperwork. Then stage the mark, which is the part that matters. The lord the party serves — Lady Isaveau, if they have been working Velmere — sets a mark on them personally, and it is done in her presence, not sent down. From now on vampires of the Shadow Summits can see whose these people are and will not feed on them. Let somebody present make clear, warmly or otherwise, that the mark says property as much as it says protection. Redblade work is the houses' own business now, not valley culls.

PROMOTION APPLIED BEFORE THIS SCENE: only the personally promoted recipients are now Crimson Company Redblade, with 0/4 recorded at that NEW standing. Their earlier rank’s deeds earned the promotion and do not carry over. If this scene accepts ONE different unrecorded work, announce 1/4 at Crimson Company Redblade, never the lifetime total. This overrides any pre-promotion standing snapshot in other instructions. Do not repeat the ceremony.

blood_rank_trait_sync_redblade.name: blood_rank_trait_sync_redblade

chm_arrival_init.name: chm_arrival_init
chm_arrival_init.script:
const tick = check({ type: 'game-tick' }) || 0
const last = typeof storage.chm_last_thinned_tick === 'number' ? storage.chm_last_thinned_tick : -400
const pressure = tick - last
const band = pressure < 50 ? 'thinned' : (pressure < 150 ? 'pressing' : 'overflowing')
storage.chm_on_site = true
storage.chm_band = band
storage.chm_last_node = 'combat'
storage.chm_depth = 0
storage.chm_visits = (storage.chm_visits || 0) + 1
storage.chm_seam_worked_this_visit = false
effects.push({ type: 'write-boolean', key: 'chm_on_site', operator: 'set', value: true })
effects.push({ type: 'write-string', key: 'chm_band', operator: 'set', value: band })
effects.push({ type: 'write-string', key: 'chm_last_node', operator: 'set', value: 'combat' })
effects.push({ type: 'write-number', key: 'chm_depth', operator: 'set', value: 0 })
effects.push({ type: 'write-boolean', key: 'chm_seam_worked_this_visit', operator: 'set', value: false })
const BANDS = {
    'thinned': 'Somebody cleared the lower levels not long ago. The Headworks camp is busy and confident, the Upper Workings are workable, and the dead are mostly down deep where they belong. Good prospecting, thin fighting, and the Company is not paying for a thinning right now.',
    'pressing': 'They are back up into the Upper Workings. Prospectors camp at the Headworks and do not go in alone or after dark, the tally of who has not come out is being kept out loud, and the old galleries have dead in them again.',
    'overflowing': 'They are out of the mine mouth at night and down onto the slopes. The Headworks camp is half a siege — fires kept up, watches set, nobody sleeping well — the valleys nearest the mountain are losing people, and the lords have let it be known that somebody should go down and break the press.',
  }
effects.push({ type: 'story', instruction: 'Establish how hard the mountain is pressing this visit, before anything else. ' + BANDS[band] + ' There is no master here and no bargain to strike: the ghouls are not led, they are simply more numerous than the mountain can hold, and the deep workings run toward where the curse pools heaviest.' })
effects.push({ type: 'narrative-event-start', eventId: 'chm_arrival_gate' })

effects.instruction: The party has returned to Charnel Mountain. Show that the mountain has moved since their last visit: the Headworks camp has different people in it, the tally of the missing has changed, levels they cleared have dead in them again or have been shored and worked by somebody else, and the marks of what they did last time are still there. Reference what actually happened on their previous visits. Do not reset the site, and never let the party find Charnel emptied or finished.

chm_delve_combat.name: chm_delve_combat

conditions.query: The party moves deeper into Charnel Mountain or commits to new ground inside it: they advance, press on, push deeper, descend a winze or ladder, follow a gallery or stope, squeeze through, clear a fall, shore or force a passage, cross a drop, work a seam, scout ahead, search beyond the current working, pursue something inward, or head toward the Upper Workings or the Deep Diggings. This is NOT satisfied when the party withdraws toward the Headworks or the surface, holds position, rests, tends wounds, talks among themselves, manages gear or ore, or interacts only with what is already in front of them.

chm_delve_combat.script:
const area = check({ type: 'party-area' }) || 'The Upper Workings'
const COMBAT = {
    'The Headworks': 'Stage a fight now, at or around the mine mouth. Ghouls that have come up and out: few, scattered, and scavenging among the gutted winch-houses and ore-sheds rather than hunting as a flock. Vary the mix and do not repeat the previous fight this visit. Match the party\'s numbers. Use the ruined surface buildings, the spoil heaps, the open ground, and daylight if there is any. These are the ones bold enough to leave the dark, which makes them the worst of the shallow ones rather than the least.',
    'The Upper Workings': 'Stage a fight now in the timber-shored galleries and ore-stopes. Ghouls hunting in small packs through the old workings, coming along the stopes and down the winzes, with a ghast among them if the press is on. Vary the mix and do not repeat the previous fight this visit. Match the party\'s numbers. Use the ground: rotten shoring, spilled ore underfoot, abandoned picks, drops into worked-out stopes, and the fact that a blade in one hand means only one hand for the silver.',
    'The Deep Diggings': 'Stage a fight now in the lowest levels, where the air goes foul and the timber rots. Ghouls in flocks rather than packs, boiling out of side workings and up through the bone-thick floor, with ghasts driving them and their stench staggering anyone close. Vary the mix and do not repeat the previous fight this visit. Match the party\'s numbers generously: down here the danger is being outnumbered in a dead-end gallery. Use chokepoints, bad air, failing light, and fire. They do not parley and they do not stop.',
  }
const instruction = COMBAT[area] || COMBAT['The Upper Workings']
effects.push({ type: 'story', instruction: 'The party is committing to new ground in Charnel Mountain. ' + instruction + ' Do not substitute sign or sound for the encounter itself. If an authored scene is already underway, fold this into it rather than opening a second front.' })
effects.push({ type: 'write-string', key: 'chm_last_node', operator: 'set', value: 'combat' })
effects.push({ type: 'write-number', key: 'chm_depth', operator: 'add', value: 1 })

conditions.query: The party moves deeper into Charnel Mountain or commits to new ground inside it: they advance, press on, push deeper, descend a winze or ladder, follow a gallery or stope, squeeze through, clear a fall, shore or force a passage, cross a drop, work a seam, scout ahead, search beyond the current working, pursue something inward, or head toward the Upper Workings or the Deep Diggings. This is NOT satisfied when the party withdraws toward the Headworks or the surface, holds position, rests, tends wounds, talks among themselves, manages gear or ore, or interacts only with what is already in front of them.

effects.instruction: The party is committing to new ground in Charnel Mountain, and the last encounter was a fight. Stage a non-combat beat now; pick whichever fits the level they are on and has not appeared recently this visit. A HAZARD out of the mine itself, telegraphed by visible sign: bad air that kills a lamp first, rotten shoring, a flooded level, a false floor over a worked-out stope, a charge left unfired. A DIORAMA of the day the miners ran, which can be searched or read: picks and spilled ore dropped where they stood, a barricaded shift-house, a tally-board, a body still in its harness. Or an OPPORTUNITY: a seam showing in a wall, an intact hoist, a ladder-way down that skips a level, a cache the dead never found. Make it interactive with a real choice. Nothing attacks during this beat unless the party springs it or makes noise.

chm_payoff.name: chm_payoff

conditions.query: Inside Charnel Mountain, the party has just overcome or resolved an encounter: they destroyed, drove off, outran, or escaped ghouls; they survived, shored, bypassed, or defused a hazard such as bad air, a fall, rotten timber, or flooding; or they searched, secured, or broke into a working, stope, or cache. This is NOT satisfied while a fight or hazard is still unresolved, or when the most recent resolution has already been paid off with a specific find.

chm_payoff.script:
const area = check({ type: 'party-area' }) || 'The Upper Workings'
const PAYOFF = {
    'The Headworks': 'Pay it off small and surface-honest: a prospector\'s cache in a collapsed counting-office, 10 to 30 florins in coin and scrap, mining kit, and the effects of somebody who did not come out. Use exact catalogue names such as Smith\'s Hammer, Craftsman\'s Toolkit, Iron Dagger, Leather Boots, or Stamina Draught.',
    'The Upper Workings': 'Pay it off in silver: a stope with the seam still showing, worth 40 to 90 florins to anyone who can carry it down, plus what a dead delver was carrying. Use exact catalogue names such as Silver-Tipped Bolts of Radiance, Iron Shortsword, Leather Jerkin, Light Crossbow, or Mongo\'s Medium Health Potion. Silver out of Charnel is what arms the whole region against the curse, and the party should be told what it is worth to the Crescent House.',
    'The Deep Diggings': 'Pay it off richly and make the weight real: the deep seams run 100 to 200 florins of silver per load, and a load is heavy enough to change how a fight goes. Add what the dead down here were carrying. Use exact catalogue names such as Moonstone Dagger of Radiant, Silver Binding Chain, Silver-Tipped Bolts of Radiance, or Greater Stamina Draught. State plainly that everything taken from this depth has to be carried back up through what they came past.',
  }
const instruction = PAYOFF[area] || PAYOFF['The Upper Workings']
effects.push({ type: 'story', instruction: 'The party has just resolved something in Charnel Mountain. Pay it off now, tied to the level they are on. ' + instruction + ' Name what they find. Then telegraph one thing deeper: a richer seam showing in a wall, a draught of colder air, a winze going down, or the sound of a flock moving somewhere below. If the party chooses to go back up with what they have, respect that.' })

conditions.query: The party is leaving Charnel Mountain or pulling back toward the surface: they retreat, withdraw, climb back toward the Headworks or the mine mouth, carry ore or wounded out, say they are done or have enough, or set out for another location. This is NOT satisfied by repositioning within a fight, moving between galleries, or pausing to search or rest while intending to continue down.

effects.instruction: The party is withdrawing from Charnel Mountain. Honor the retreat cleanly: the route back is the route they know, and what they carry leaves with them. Do not stage a punitive ambush or spring a new fight to stop them. If they are carrying silver from the deep levels, make the weight matter on the way up — pace, hands, choices about what to drop — but let a party that commits to the climb make it. If the mountain is roused behind them, show pressure that urges pace and can be outrun or shut behind a fall. Give the exit a closing image at the mine mouth, and name one unclaimed thing plainly, such as the seam they did not reach or the level they never opened.

The party has pushed deep this visit and the mountain has noticed. Raise the register from now on: the ghouls stop being met in packs and start converging, coming from behind as well as ahead, filling galleries the party has already cleared and cutting the way they came. Sound travels a long way in worked stone and everything down here follows it. Ghasts appear where they did not before. Telegraph the shift with sound and sign so the party can read it before it lands. Keep fights winnable but costly. Make the standing choice visible: climb out now with what they have, or go down to the deep seam and take a load worth the trip.

chm_seam_prize.name: chm_seam_prize
chm_seam_prize.script:
const tick = check({ type: 'game-tick' }) || 0
storage.chm_last_thinned_tick = tick
storage.chm_seam_worked_this_visit = true
storage.chm_seams_worked = (storage.chm_seams_worked || 0) + 1
effects.push({ type: 'write-boolean', key: 'chm_seam_worked_this_visit', operator: 'set', value: true })
if (storage.bloodMember === true) { storage.bloodDeedCreditPending = true }
effects.push({ type: 'story', instruction: 'The party has broken into the deep seam and killed enough down here to matter. Pay the haul, itemized and heavy: 200 to 400 florins of raw silver, which is a real burden to carry and worth every florin to the Crescent House because it is what the region kills the curse with. Add what the dead of six abandoned crews were carrying, using exact catalogue names such as Moonstone Dagger of Radiant, Silver Binding Chain, Silver-Tipped Bolts of Radiance, or Greater Stamina Draught. Then close it honestly: the mountain is not cleared and cannot be. The press is broken for a season, the ghouls will breed back, and getting this load up to the Headworks is still ahead of them.' })

chm_thinning_contract.name: chm_thinning_contract

conditions.query: The party reads, examines, or asks about the Crimson Company work board, the posted contracts, or the available jobs; asks an officer for work, a job, a contract, a bounty, or something that pays; or asks what needs doing or where to go next in the Shadow Summits.

blood_embrace_offer_arrive.name: blood_embrace_offer_arrive

blood_embrace_accept.name: blood_embrace_accept

effects.instruction: Stage the turning for the identified player and nobody else: the drain, the sire's blood given back, dying, and the mind coming back into a body that is no longer alive. Concrete and physical — the cold, the new sharpness of hearing and smell, a heartbeat that is not there. Then the first hunger, immediately, and it is not optional: it must be answered on a specific living person who is present and named, and the character chooses who and how much. Do not resolve it for them and do not offer a bloodless substitute. Say plainly that this is permanent and there is no cure in Larion.

Then the two things that change tomorrow. The Crimson Company gives the newly Embraced a captaincy — real soldiers, by name, who take their orders from this character now. And silver closes to them: the metal the Company kills most things with is now something they cannot hold, which somebody will have to say out loud. Sunlight is now lethal. Let an officer such as Osric Kestrand react to all of it in his own way, without a speech.

PROMOTION APPLIED BEFORE THIS SCENE: only the personally promoted recipients are now Fledgling of the Blood, with 0/4 recorded at that NEW standing. Their earlier rank’s deeds earned the promotion and do not carry over. If this scene accepts ONE different unrecorded work, announce 1/4 at Fledgling of the Blood, never the lifetime total. This overrides any pre-promotion standing snapshot in other instructions. Do not repeat the ceremony.

conditions.query: The character offered the Blood refuses, declines, defers, or turns down the offer of the Blood from a vampire lord, or leaves without accepting it.

effects.instruction: The offer of the Blood has been refused. Honor it completely. The lord takes it well and without coldness, punishment, or retaliation, and says plainly that the offer keeps — she has time, and she would rather have them useful than resentful. Their lord's mark and their Crimson Company standing are untouched, and the work goes on exactly as before. Nobody at the Red House thinks less of them, though somebody may be curious. Do not nag: the offer should not be raised again unless the character raises it, and if they later ask for it, it is still there.

conditions.query: A new night has begun for one specific player character with the Vampire trait, or they have slept, rested, camped, or taken a long recovery, since they last fed on blood, and the story identifies which player.

effects.instruction: The hunger has come back. The world reads as food: pulse, throat, the warmth coming off people, all of it louder than it was. This character is not weakened so much as unreliable — harder to charm, harder to read others through, and slower to let things go. Do not force a loss of control at this stage. Feeding on a living person clears it, and finding somebody to feed on is the character's problem, not the narrator's to solve for them.

conditions.query: One specific player character carrying blood hunger has passed another night, sleep, rest, or long recovery without feeding on blood, and the story identifies which player.

effects.instruction: A second night without blood. The hunger stops being something this character has and becomes something that has them: too still, too pale, pupils blown, breath forgotten. Composure now costs visible effort and sometimes fails. Near open blood or an isolated living person, they are at real risk of acting before they decide to — put that risk in front of the player as a moment they can feel coming, and let their choice decide it. Feeding clears it.

conditions.query: One specific player character with the Vampire trait has fed on the blood of a living person, and the story identifies which player. This is NOT satisfied by drinking animal blood, stored or bottled blood, wine, bloodwine, or any substitute.

effects.instruction: The hunger is answered. Narrate the feeding and its aftermath for this character concretely and without romance: the immediate relief, warmth returning, the senses settling, and how the person they fed on is left — alive, harmed, dead, willing, or terrified, whichever the player chose. Do not soften what they did or moralize about it. The hunger will be back at the next nightfall.

A Crimson Company hall holds a vampire differently. They cannot handle the hall’s silver, which is most of what the Company kills with, and the room works around it every single day without comment. They eat nothing at the long table and everyone can see it. Blades who knew them before are working out what to call them; some are proud of it, some are careful, one or two are frightened. None of this is hostility: they outrank almost everyone in the room. It is simply that the room has changed shape around them.

blood_rank_trait_sync_fledgling.name: blood_rank_trait_sync_fledgling

conditions.query: One specific player character with the Vampire trait leans on a living person with their presence or their eyes — to compel, cow, hold, still, or bend them — rather than by argument, threat, or force, and the story identifies which player.

effects.instruction: It works, and the character finds out what they are now by using it. Narrate the moment from the outside as well as the inside: the person's face going slack for a beat, the intention leaving them, and then coming back with a gap in it they will explain to themselves later. Nobody taught this and nobody has to. Let the character register that it was easy.

conditions.query: One specific player character with the Vampire trait is taught to take another shape, or deliberately attempts to put their body down and go to mist, bat, or wolf for the first time, and the story identifies which player.

effects.instruction: The shape comes. Narrate it as something the body remembers rather than something learned: coming apart, the moment of not having hands, and the particular wrongness of getting back. Make the cost immediate and physical — whatever they were wearing and carrying is lying where they left it, and they will have to go back for it or do without.

conditions.query: One specific player character with the Vampire trait deliberately makes a ghoul: they drain a named person and bring them back as a bound strigoi meant to be kept and commanded, rather than feeding, killing, or turning them into a true vampire. The story identifies which player and who the victim was.

effects.instruction: The ghoul is made and it holds. Do not soften what this is: the person the character chose is gone and what is left answers to them. Give it a name it will not respond to, one habit left over from the life, and a way of moving that is nothing like a person's. It does not speak. It follows, fights, carries, waits, and does exactly what it is told in the narrowest possible reading of the words. From now on treat it as a real member of the party that can be hurt, destroyed, ordered into things, and used badly. Other vampires who see it read it as competence, and read the choice of victim as character.

blood_capture_fledgling_to_blooded.name: blood_capture_fledgling_to_blooded

conditions.query: A vampire lord of the Shadow Summits, or a house speaking for one, acknowledges one or more made vampires as Blooded: they hold the hunger, keep a ghoul, and can be dealt with as principals rather than sent like servants. Identify the characters acknowledged.

effects.instruction: Blooded standing changes who talks to them and how. The houses stop sending and start asking: House Malren opens its laboratories and teaches, in exchange for specimens, pages, and access, and House Kaeris will now sell them things the Crescent House does not put on a shelf. They may speak at the Hall of Witnesses. Company work is no longer what they do; it is what they hand down to a captaincy. Say plainly, through somebody who would know, that the only thing above this is lordship, that only the Black Gate makes a lord, and that no one passes it without a house spending its name on them.

blood_rank_trait_sync_blooded.name: blood_rank_trait_sync_blooded

blood_status_request.name: blood_status_request

conditions.query: A member of the party asks about their own standing, rank, record, or progress in the Crimson Company, asks what they have to do to rise, asks how many deeds they are credited with, or asks an officer where they stand.

blood_promotion_request.name: blood_promotion_request

conditions.query: A member of the party asks to be advanced in the Crimson Company, requests promotion, presents their completed deeds for recognition, asks an officer to hear their account and name their higher standing, or asks to be made a Redblade.

shop_stock_presentation.name: shop_stock_presentation

conditions.query: A member of the party is buying or selling goods with a merchant: asking a shopkeeper, stallholder, smith, apothecary, fletcher, or trader what they have, what they carry, or what is for sale; asking to see, price, or buy a weapon, armour, potion, tool, material, or piece of gear; browsing a shop, stall, or market for merchandise; offering an item for sale or asking what a merchant will give for it; or haggling over the price of goods. Ordering food, drink, or lodging is not this, and neither is paying a toll, fee, fare, bribe, or wage.

A member of the party searches or loots for something worth taking: going through a body or a fallen enemy, searching a room, container, chest, pack, wagon, camp, or ruin for valuables, taking spoils or plunder from the defeated, or stripping usable gear from the dead. This does not cover gathering plants, ore, or other materials from the landscape, or cutting parts from a creature's body.

effects.instruction: A member of the party is searching or looting. First use whatever this location's own guidance says may be found here, and where it gives exact item names, use those names before inventing anything. Many places say nothing, and that is fine: then ground what is found in the specific source rather than in a general idea of loot. Who this person was and what their work required. What this room, pack, or container is actually for. A courier carries what a courier carries. Raw materials, such as herbs, truffles, timber, ore, hides, meat, glands, silk, and exotic stone or glass, are never found by searching; they come only from foraging, mining, or harvesting a creature. Searching a creature's body finds only what it carried or swallowed, never its own hide, hair, horn, antler, bone, teeth, feathers, or organs. Do not fall back on generic filler such as a rusty blade, a few coins, and some rations when the source implies something specific.

Scale what is found to the source, not to the party. Ordinary opposition yields ordinary goods, materials, and modest florins. Someone equipped for a reason yields what they were equipped with. A cache hidden on purpose is worth the hiding. Fine and Superior items come only from a source that justifies them, Masterwork almost never, and Legendary not at all unless established lore says so. A place also gives up its contents once: a body already stripped, a room already turned over, or somewhere with no reason to hold anything yields nothing, and the narration should say so plainly rather than invent a consolation prize. Refusing the fourth search of the same room is not stinginess, it is the world holding still.

NAME everything found specifically, because the item system can only create what the prose names. Never write 'a sword', 'some armour', 'a useful item', 'some materials', 'a little coin', or 'some loot'. Give the exact item type, the material, the quality when it is above mundane, and the magical or damage aspect when it is nonstandard, following the world's naming logic: quality, exotic material, item type, and 'of [damage type]' where it applies. An ordinary steel longsword is named as such. An aspected find is a Superior Emberglass Dagger of Fire, never 'a glowing dagger'. State a concrete florin amount instead of 'a few coins'.

What an enemy fought with is the first thing on the ground: if the prose gave them a crossbow, mail, a good blade, or a shield while they were alive, those exist after they are dead and are the obvious find — the crossbow before the spare string, the mail before the belt knife. Never describe gear on a living enemy and then withhold it from the body. Narrative props are not rewards: a map, letter, key, journal, or ledger appears only when it opens something the party can act on now, never as the main thing found, and never instead of something usable. And do not itemize trivia — whetstones, spare bowstrings, rations, rope, and ordinary everyday tools are texture in a sentence, not items handed to the party.

conditions.query: The story explicitly shows that a spirit begins riding this player's body and remains within them at the end of the response — whether welcomed through spirit channeling, invited by rite or mask, or forced in as possession. Count only an actual indwelling: the spirit present inside the body and acting or able to act through it. Do not count a spirit merely nearby, addressed, bargained with, warded off, or fought; do not count a failed channeling attempt; do not count Second Soul's momentary sharing, which ends within the same act; do not count another character being ridden.

The story explicitly shows that the spirit riding this player is no longer within them: it departs on its own, completes what it came for and leaves, is expelled or driven out, the channel is released or breaks, or unconsciousness or death explicitly drives the spirit out of the body. Do not count the rider merely being quiet, resisted, argued with, or refused while it remains inside the body.

Othrel Namaris has been presented with concrete evidence of House Drelovar's corruption and has publicly or materially acted to investigate, oppose, constrain, or expose House Drelovar because he accepts that it threatens Maanvalta's survival.

offer_pool_league_data_001.name: offer_pool_league_data_001
offer_pool_league_data_001.script:
skip = true
const data = [{"id": "aur_bath_bench_bullies", "kind": "social", "rank": "copper", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Warmwater Township", "text": "**The Hottest Pool** (The Steaming Pools, Warmwater Township). Every evening a crew of off-duty sled-drivers takes the hottest pool at the Steaming Pools for themselves and dunks anyone who tries to share it, elders included. The bathhouse keeper, a prim old snowlander woman who counts every towel twice, wants the pool open to all again and does not much care whether it is done with words or a good dunking of their own. Reward: 40 florins and free soaks for the rest of the dark season."}, {"id": "aur_hearthhouse_card_sharp", "kind": "social", "rank": "copper", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Warmwater Township", "text": "**Dogs on the Table** (The Hearthhouse, Warmwater Township). A smiling stranger buys the sled-drivers drinks by the fire-pit every night, and by the end of the evening they have signed their dogs over to him for a pittance. Tirsa Hellemark, a young host of the Hearthhouse who captains a rimewolf rescue team, has watched two good rescue dogs walk out the door on his papers and is sure he is drugging the drink. She wants the signed-away dogs back with their owners. Reward: 45 florins from Tirsa and a seat on her rescue sled any night the party wants one."}, {"id": "aur_lamp_oil_hoarder", "kind": "social", "rank": "copper", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Warmwater Township", "text": "**Dear Light** (The Market, Warmwater Township). A trader has been buying up every cask of lampfish oil that comes into the Market and selling it back at triple the price, just as the long dark sets in. A widowed candlemaker with a tongue like a skinning knife has refused to pay him and is running out of stock, and she wants his hold on the oil broken before the poorer houses start going dark. Reward: 50 florins and a winter of candles from the candlemaker."}, {"id": "aur_timber_mark_feud", "kind": "social", "rank": "copper", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Firwood", "text": "**Wrong Marks on the Cordwood** (The Logging Steads, The Firwood). Two logging steads keep sawing the ownership marks off each other's cut timber and hauling it home as their own, and the last argument ended with axes drawn. The forewoman of one stead, a one-eyed snowlander who settles everything by arm-wrestling, wants the thefts stopped and the other stead brought to a deal, though she will not be the one to back down first. Reward: 35 florins and a sledge-load of seasoned firewood."}, {"id": "aur_rack_wolverine", "kind": "monster", "rank": "copper", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Dun Beithir", "text": "**Teeth at the Racks** (The Ice-Harbor, Dun Beithir). A wolverine comes out of the dark every few nights to tear down the fish-racks on the Ice-Harbor, eats what it can, and savages anyone who tries to chase it off. A cheerful, toothless fish-wife who has given every rack a name is tired of patching bites and wants the beast gone before it takes the whole winter store. Reward: 40 florins and a smoked side of lampfish from the fish-wife's favorite rack."}, {"id": "aur_lamp_tower_mephits", "kind": "monster", "rank": "copper", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Warmwater Township", "text": "**Frost on the Great Lamp** (The Lamp-Tower, Warmwater Township). A handful of ice mephits have started climbing the Lamp-Tower at night to frost over the great lamp's glass, cackling while the flame gutters. The apprentice lamp-keeper, an anxious young gnome who hates heights, has to scrape the glass clear on the outside ledge every time, and she would very much like someone else to deal with them. Reward: 30 florins and a warm supper at the top of the tower, with the best view in Aurora."}, {"id": "aur_trapline_frost_spiders", "kind": "monster", "rank": "copper", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Firwood", "text": "**Webs Across the Game-Trails** (The Deep Firs, The Firwood). Giant frost spiders have strung webs across the old game-trails in the Deep Firs and are eating whatever the traps catch before the trappers can reach it. A jumpy snowlander trapper-boy has lost his whole line to them and hardly sleeps for thinking about them, but he knows every trail and will show the way if someone else goes first. Reward: 35 florins and a fine white fox pelt from the boy's first clean catch."}, {"id": "aur_rutting_elk_bull", "kind": "monster", "rank": "copper", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Herdways", "text": "**The Bull on the Track** (The Migration, The Herdways). A rutting dire elk bull has taken a stretch of the migration track as his own and charges every hunter's sledge that comes near, and two have already been gored. An old nomad tracker who hangs around the hunters' camps swears the bull is his late brother come back, and he will fight anyone who harms it, so the hunters would dearly like it moved on some other way. Reward: 60 florins pooled by the hunters and a set of shed elk antlers."}, {"id": "aur_watch_hall_hearth_douser", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "copper", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Warmwater Township", "text": "**Snow on the Hearthfire** (The Watch-Hall, Warmwater Township). Someone keeps sneaking into the Watch-Hall before dawn and smothering one of its hearthfires with snow, and the old folk have started calling it an omen. The hall-steward, a superstitious snowlander who keeps a tally of omens on the wall, wants the culprit found before the whole town decides the cold is coming for Warmwater next. Reward: 30 florins and the steward's promise to scratch one good omen onto his wall in the party's honor."}, {"id": "aur_broch_poltergeist", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "copper", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Dun Beithir", "text": "**The Broch Throws Things** (The Broch, Dun Beithir). Something unseen in the Broch knocks over tankards, hides tools, and flings fish-bones, but only when the dwarf traders are in the room. One of them, a grumpy harbor-trader who refuses to admit he is scared, wants it laid to rest or at least told to pick on somebody else, and the villagers are starting to find it very funny. Reward: 45 florins and a serpent-bone knife from the trader's own stock."}, {"id": "aur_sled_race_saboteur", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "copper", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Warmwater Township", "text": "**Cut Traces** (The Kennels, Warmwater Township). Every week before the lake sled-race, someone creeps into the Kennels and cuts traces, loosens runners, or feeds a favored team something that sends them off their legs. A boastful teenage musher with a scarred lead dog has been hit three races running and is sure it is an older rival who hates losing to her, though she has no proof. Reward: 40 florins and a pick of the kennel's next rimewolf litter."}, {"id": "aur_stillwater_dares", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "copper", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Stillwater", "text": "**A Night in Stillwater** (The Frozen Streets, Stillwater). An older youth in Warmwater runs a betting ring daring the town's children to spend a night at the edge of dead Stillwater, and the latest pair came back with a frozen lamp from its streets and nightmares they will not describe. A stubborn ice-fisher whose son is next on the list will walk out there herself if nobody stops it first. Reward: 40 florins and a season of the mother's best catch."}, {"id": "aur_warmth_money_racket", "kind": "social", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Warmwater Township", "text": "**Warmth Money** (The Market, Warmwater Township). A gang of thugs has started charging the stalls nearest the steaming water a weekly fee for their warm spot, and stalls that refuse wake to find their stock frozen solid in lake-water. A soft-spoken tiefling tea-seller has refused them twice and lost everything twice, and she is quietly raising money among the stallholders to hire someone to end it. Reward: 150 florins from the stallholders and free tea for life."}]

offer_pool_league_data_002.name: offer_pool_league_data_002
offer_pool_league_data_002.script:
skip = true
const data = [{"id": "aur_serpent_scale_rigging", "kind": "social", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Dun Beithir", "text": "**Short Weight on the Serpent** (The Broch, Dun Beithir). The villagers of Dun Beithir are sure the dwarf buyers are rigging their scales on serpent-bone and hide, and every trade night in the Broch now comes close to a brawl. The harpoon-mistress who led the last beithir hunt, a booming woman who laughs louder than anyone, wants the truth out, and a way of weighing both sides will accept, before the village throws the dwarves off the ice and loses its best buyers. Reward: 120 florins and a harpoon of carved beithir bone."}, {"id": "aur_redclaw_yard_bully", "kind": "social", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Fort Redclaw", "text": "**Smallfolk in the Yard** (The Yard, Fort Redclaw). A young nanukin, one of the towering white bearfolk who hold Fort Redclaw, keeps dragging the fort's smallfolk hirelings into the Yard to humiliate them in front of his friends, and the hirelings are quitting faster than the fort can replace them. An old nanukin armorer missing a claw needs those quick small hands and wants the bully taught respect the only way the fort understands: a deed or a contest. Reward: 130 florins and a smallfolk-sized buckler from the armorer's forge."}, {"id": "aur_mammoth_calf_poachers", "kind": "social", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Herdways", "text": "**Calves in the Snowveil** (The Snowveil, The Herdways). Poachers hiding in the Snowveil keep killing winter mammoth calves for their soft young ivory, which every hunter of the herds holds forbidden. The matriarch of a nomad hunting camp, a stern woman who reads the weather in cracked bone, blames the Warmwater trappers and is talking about driving them all off the Herdways unless the real culprits are handed to her. Reward: 160 florins and a mammoth-ivory charm from the matriarch."}, {"id": "aur_widow_courting_swindler", "kind": "social", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Warmwater Township", "text": "**A Charming Man by the Fire** (The Hearthhouse, Warmwater Township). A handsome, well-spoken stranger has been courting lonely widows at the Hearthhouse all winter, and three of them have handed him their savings for a house by the springs that does not exist. A sharp-eyed old widow he has not yet approached wants to bait him herself and needs someone to catch him when he bites. Reward: 140 florins and a place of honor at the widows' table."}, {"id": "aur_straggler_snow_lynx", "kind": "monster", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Herdways", "text": "**White Against White** (The Migration, The Herdways). A dire snow-lynx has been dropping on trappers who fall behind on the migration track, invisible against the snow until it moves. A chatty halfling fur-trader who has made a fortune selling lynx pelts, and is terrified of meeting a live one, is paying for it to be dealt with because the trappers have stopped going out. Reward: 140 florins and first refusal on the halfling's best cloak."}, {"id": "aur_shallows_rimewyrms", "kind": "monster", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Underfloes", "text": "**Something Under the Floes** (The Floes, The Underfloes). A brood of young rimewyrms has settled in the shallows near the broken ice and bursts up under anyone who works the salvage there, following every footstep. A deaf old salvager who says he feels the ice through his boots has kept his crew alive so far, but they are losing sledges and nerve, and he wants the brood cleared or chased off his stretch. Reward: 180 florins and a rimewyrm fang from the salvager's collection."}, {"id": "aur_charcoal_snow_troll", "kind": "monster", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Firwood", "text": "**The Troll Wants the Fire** (The Deep Firs, The Firwood). A snow-troll has come out of a ruined hall in the Deep Firs and keeps raiding the charcoal camps, drawn by the heat of the burning mounds and in a fury whenever it gets near them. A soot-faced charcoal-burner who talks to her mounds like children has stayed when the others fled, and she knows fire is the one thing that keeps the troll down. Reward: 170 florins and a cask of the charcoal-burner's finest, which burns hot enough to keep a troll down."}, {"id": "aur_sled_track_rimewolves", "kind": "monster", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Aurora Icefields", "text": "**Paced for Miles** (The Open White, Aurora Icefields). A wild rimewolf pack has learned to pace the sled-lines that run out to the far steads across the Open White, closing in whenever a storm slows the teams. A laconic driver who hums to stay awake has lost two dogs and a friend to them and wants the pack broken before he loses his nerve for the run. Reward: 150 florins and a driver's fur hood lined with rimewolf."}, {"id": "aur_cutting_ice_hag", "kind": "monster", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Dun Beithir", "text": "**A Voice Under the Ice** (The Cutting Ice, Dun Beithir). A lake hag beneath the Cutting Ice calls to lone fishers in the voices of their dead and draws them out onto thin ice, and two have gone through this winter. A nervous young ice-fisher swears he heard his drowned sister calling him and almost went, and he wants the hag found and ended, though part of him still hopes it was really her. Reward: 130 florins and the village's gratitude at the next hunt feast."}, {"id": "aur_stillwater_looters", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Stillwater", "text": "**Hands Off the Dead Town** (The Dead Spring, Stillwater). A scavenger crew has been stripping Stillwater's bathhouse and gathering-hall around the dead spring, and since they started, the lamps in the frozen streets have begun lighting themselves at night. The last man of Stillwater, a bitter old snowlander who was away the night his town froze, wants the looters stopped and whatever they took put back, whether or not anyone believes the town is angry. Reward: 140 florins and a carved hearth-charm the old man saved from his own house."}, {"id": "aur_false_signal_wreckers", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Warmwater Township", "text": "**Lights That Lie** (The Lamp-Tower, Warmwater Township). Fires keep appearing out on the icefields where no signal-lamp should be, and each time the rescue sleds go out into the storm they find nothing but an ambush and lose their gear. The signal-reader in the Lamp-Tower, hollow-eyed from a month of broken nights, is sure someone is lighting them on purpose and wants to know who before the watch stops answering real calls. Reward: 160 florins and a brass signal-glass from the tower."}, {"id": "aur_winter_wolf_litter", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Warmwater Township", "text": "**The Frost-Breathing Pups** (The Kennels, Warmwater Township). A kennel bitch has whelped a litter that breathes frost, and the wild winter wolf that sired them comes back to the Kennels every night to circle the pens. Half the town wants the pups drowned and the sire killed, and a freckled kennel girl who sleeps in the pens with them wants someone to find a way that saves them both. Reward: 150 florins and one of the frost-breathing pups, if any are spared."}]

offer_pool_league_data_003.name: offer_pool_league_data_003
offer_pool_league_data_003.script:
skip = true
const data = [{"id": "aur_troll_ward_charms", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Firwood", "text": "**Wards That Call** (The Logging Steads, The Firwood). A traveling hedge-wizard has sold troll-ward charms to half the Logging Steads, and every stead that hung them has had a troll at its walls since. An old axe-grinder who has never bought a charm in his life thinks the charms are drawing the trolls on purpose, and he wants the wizard caught before he packs up and moves on to the next wood. Reward: 120 florins and a new edge on every blade the party carries, for life."}, {"id": "aur_false_silver_recruiter", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Warmwater Township", "text": "**The Silver Who Isn't** (The Watch-Hall, Warmwater Township). A swaggering stranger who claims League Silver standing keeps hiring green Coppers at the Watch-Hall for jobs on the ice, then vanishes with the whole payment once the work is done. An earnest young gnome Copper who lost her first real fee to him wants him found and unmasked, and she insists on coming along. Reward: 110 florins and a standing favor from every Copper he cheated."}, {"id": "aur_redclaw_rotten_oil", "kind": "social", "rank": "silver", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Fort Redclaw", "text": "**The Ice Road Is Closed** (The Gate, Fort Redclaw). A snowlander trader sold Fort Redclaw a winter's worth of rotten serpent-oil and fled, and the white bearfolk who hold the fort have closed their gate to every smallfolk trader until the cheat answers for it. The gate-captain, a blunt nanukin who has no patience for words, will open it again only for someone who brings the trader to justice or proves smallfolk can be trusted by a deed. Reward: 350 florins from the Warmwater traders and a nanukin claw-token that opens the Gate to the party."}, {"id": "aur_jarls_hall_braggart", "kind": "social", "rank": "silver", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Whitefang Hold", "text": "**A Guest Who Boasted Too Much** (The Jarl's Hall, Whitefang Hold). A smallfolk sellsword has been living as an honored guest in the Jarl's Hall on the strength of boasts about deeds he never did, and the frost giants have decided to test him on every one. The giants' herald, who keeps the tally of every boast in the hall and finds all of this delightful, would rather the fool survive, so the party is wanted to prove the boasts or get him out of them without shaming the hall. Reward: 300 florins and a giant's drinking-horn, which the party will need both hands to lift."}, {"id": "aur_rim_rope_cutters", "kind": "social", "rank": "silver", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Crevasse", "text": "**Cut Lines at the Rim** (The Rim, The Crevasse). Two crews digging white-stone relics out of the Crevasse have been cutting each other's ropes at the Rim, and one climber has already fallen. The boss of one crew, a pipe-chewing dwarf with frostbitten ears, swears her people have cut nothing and wants the sabotage ended before the whole dig turns into a knife fight on the lip of the chasm. Reward: 400 florins and one small relic from the dwarf crew's haul."}, {"id": "aur_selkie_hidden_skin", "kind": "social", "rank": "silver", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Dun Beithir", "text": "**The Stolen Skin** (The Ice-Harbor, Dun Beithir). A selkie woman has lived for years as the wife of a Dun Beithir fisher who hid her sealskin the day she came ashore, and she cannot return to the sea without it. She is grave and quiet and sings to the ice at night, and she wants her skin found so she can choose freely whether to stay or go, but the village protects her husband and will not hear a word against him. Reward: 250 florins from the selkie's kin and a pearl from under the ice."}, {"id": "aur_pools_blackmailer", "kind": "social", "rank": "silver", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Warmwater Township", "text": "**A Quiet Matter at the Pools** (The Steaming Pools, Warmwater Township). A wealthy elven fur-buyer who winters at the Steaming Pools is being squeezed by someone who knows a part of her past she will not name, and every week the price goes up. She is gracious, careful, and intensely private, and she will pay very well to have the blackmail ended quietly, without anyone learning what the secret is. Reward: 450 florins and the fur-buyer's trust, which opens doors in every fur market of the north."}, {"id": "aur_snowveil_saber_cat", "kind": "monster", "rank": "silver", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Herdways", "text": "**The Cat That Watches the Fires** (The Snowveil, The Herdways). A saber-cat has learned that hunters' fires in the Snowveil mean food, and it circles the camps at night and takes whoever steps out of the light. A boastful young nomad hunter who wants its fangs for his marriage-price is set on killing it alone, and his camp would rather hire someone to go with him than bury him. Reward: 320 florins and the saber-cat's pelt, or one fang if the hunter gets the killing blow."}, {"id": "aur_underbreaks_drowned_dead", "kind": "monster", "rank": "silver", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Underfloes", "text": "**The Ship That Walks at Night** (The Underbreaks, The Underfloes). A rimewyrm has broken open an old ship frozen in the Underbreaks, and every night its drowned crew climb out salt-bloated and slow and march on the nearest salvage camp. A tattooed half-orc salvage-queen wants the dead put down so she can get into the ship's hold, and she is not above bargaining for a larger share if the party proves useful. Reward: 380 florins and a share of whatever the salvage-queen finds in the hold."}, {"id": "aur_line_breaking_beithir", "kind": "monster", "rank": "silver", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Dun Beithir", "text": "**The Serpent That Breaks the Lines** (The Cutting Ice, Dun Beithir). A great beithir under the Cutting Ice has learned to snap harpoon-lines and drag hunters down through the holes, and the village has lost two hunts and three hands to it. The blind old harpooner who calls every hunt by ear wants skilled help on the ice for the next one, and he says this serpent is smarter than any he has heard in sixty winters. Reward: 420 florins and a full share of the kill, bone and hide both."}, {"id": "aur_north_wind_yeti", "kind": "monster", "rank": "silver", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Whitefang Hold", "text": "**Something in the Blizzard** (North Wind Pass, Whitefang Hold). A yeti hunts the North Wind Pass whenever a blizzard comes down, taking travelers who shelter against the rock and leaving only tracks the wind erases by morning. A cheerful dwarf prospector camped at the foot of the pass sings loudly all night to keep it off and has been right so far, but his crew wants the thing gone before they run out of songs. Reward: 300 florins and a first look at the dwarf crew's next frostjade find."}, {"id": "aur_stillwater_rime_wights", "kind": "monster", "rank": "silver", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Stillwater", "text": "**His Wife Walks in Stillwater** (The Frozen Streets, Stillwater). The frozen dead of Stillwater drift through its streets as rime-wights, and a snowlander widower walks out there every week to watch his wife among them. Last time one of them turned on him and he barely got home, and his family wants the wights laid to rest so he will stop going, though he begs that she be spared the blade if there is any other way, and that he be given a last farewell. Reward: 280 florins and the widower's own carved sled, the finest in Warmwater."}]

offer_pool_league_data_004.name: offer_pool_league_data_004
offer_pool_league_data_004.script:
skip = true
const data = [{"id": "aur_colossus_false_prophet", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "silver", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Aurora Icefields", "text": "**Waiting for the Giant to Wake** (The Frozen Colossus, Aurora Icefields). A prophet has gathered pilgrims in a camp at the foot of the Frozen Colossus, promising the stone titan will wake and bring the warm age back to anyone who gives him everything they own. The pilgrims are freezing and starving while he lives well, and one half-frozen elderly believer whose faith cannot be shaken has sent word begging for help getting the others out of the camp alive, if not himself. Reward: 260 florins from the pilgrims' families and the old believer's blessing."}, {"id": "aur_redclaw_doppelganger", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "silver", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Fort Redclaw", "text": "**One Face Too Many** (The Dens, Fort Redclaw). Smallfolk hirelings keep vanishing from the Dens of Fort Redclaw, and each time the missing one turns up a day later a little wrong. The nanukin den-mother who runs the sleeping halls, a suspicious old bearfolk who sniffs everyone twice, says a changeling is wearing smallfolk faces in the fort, and she cannot tell smallfolk apart well enough to find it. She also wants to know what became of the ones who went missing. Reward: 350 florins and the den-mother's gift of a nanukin war-fur cut down to smallfolk size."}, {"id": "aur_holdfast_spectral_hunt", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "silver", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Firwood", "text": "**The Hunt Rides Out Tonight** (The Old Holdfast, The Firwood). On clear nights a company of spectral huntsmen rides out of the ruined hunting-hall at the Old Holdfast, and loggers who cross its path wake miles away with no memory, or do not wake. A chatty snowlander trapper who has seen the hunt three times and lived wants to know what they are hunting, because he thinks they are looking for something in the wood and will not stop until they find it. Reward: 330 florins and a silver hunting-horn from the Old Holdfast."}, {"id": "aur_watch_turncoat", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "silver", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Warmwater Township", "text": "**Someone Sells the Patrols** (The Watch-Hall, Warmwater Township). For a season now the cultists who choke Aurora's hot springs have known exactly where the watch's patrols will be, and every spring the watch has tried to guard has died anyway. A grim veteran of the watch with a frost-white beard is sure someone in the Watch-Hall is selling the routes and wants outsiders to find the traitor, since he can no longer trust anyone inside. Reward: 480 florins and a standing welcome among the watch."}, {"id": "aur_wyrmspire_egg_poachers", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "silver", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The White Wyrmspire", "text": "**Eggs and Blame** (The Approaches, The White Wyrmspire). Smallfolk poachers have been stealing ice drake eggs from the Wyrmspire and leaving giant-sized tracks behind them, and the drakes have answered by raiding the giants' herds harder than they have in years. A wry frost-giant youth blamed for the latest theft wants the real thieves caught at their camp on the Approaches, both to clear his name before giants and drakes alike and because he would like to steal an egg properly someday. Reward: 450 florins and a flake of drake shell, worth a small fortune to any smith in Dun Beithir."}, {"id": "aur_giant_war_leader", "kind": "social", "rank": "gold", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Whitefang Hold", "text": "**Tribute or Nothing** (The War Grounds, Whitefang Hold). A young frost-giant war-leader is training a band on the War Grounds to take tribute from the outlying steads of Aurora, and the old giants will not stop him unless he is shamed there in front of everyone. A sly old skald who loves a good insult more than any feast thinks a smallfolk party could do it, by besting him at the contests or out-telling him before the whole hold. Reward: 1,200 florins pooled by the steads and a giant's arm-ring the party can wear as a belt."}, {"id": "aur_redclaw_war_captain", "kind": "social", "rank": "gold", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Fort Redclaw", "text": "**The Bearfolk Want Blood** (The Great Hall, Fort Redclaw). A nanukin hunter was found dead on the Herdways with a snowlander spear in him, and a scheming war-captain in Fort Redclaw has been using it to push the chief toward war with Warmwater. The chief's cub-heir, a young bearfolk endlessly curious about smallfolk, thinks the story does not add up and will speak for the party in the Great Hall if they can bring proof. Reward: 1,400 florins from Warmwater and the cub-heir's lifelong friendship."}, {"id": "aur_stead_lord_levy", "kind": "social", "rank": "gold", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Warmwater Township", "text": "**A Levy on the Warm Shore** (The Market, Warmwater Township). A stead-lord who lost his lands to the cold has come to Warmwater with armed followers and started charging every family a levy for the right to live on the warm shore, and more desperate folk join him each week. The town's ancient song-keeper, who knows the name of every town the cold has taken, says a split like this killed Stillwater before the spring ever did, and she wants it ended before blood is spilled in the Market. Reward: 900 florins from the town and a verse in the song-keeper's songs."}, {"id": "aur_sled_track_remorhaz", "kind": "monster", "rank": "gold", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Aurora Icefields", "text": "**Pits That Melt Under the Sleds** (The Open White, Aurora Icefields). A remorhaz, the burning centipede of the deep ice, has moved under the sled-tracks across the Open White and melts its kill-pits right beneath passing teams, and the far steads have stopped coming to Warmwater at all. A boastful dwarf rimebone smith wants its elemental core for a forge that could arm the whole north against the cold, and will outfit anyone who goes after it. Reward: 1,300 florins and a weapon from the dwarf's forge, worked with the remorhaz's heat."}, {"id": "aur_broken_tusk_mammoth", "kind": "monster", "rank": "gold", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Herdways", "text": "**The Herd Turns on the Steads** (The Migration, The Herdways). A bull winter mammoth maddened by a broken tusk has twice turned the whole migration off its route and straight through outlying steads, flattening everything in its path. A silent nomad beast-speaker who hums to the herds says the bull can still be calmed if someone gets close enough to draw the tusk, and that killing it in the open will start the stampede nobody survives. Reward: 1,000 florins from the steads and the broken tusk, carved by the beast-speaker."}, {"id": "aur_deep_firs_wendigo", "kind": "monster", "rank": "gold", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Firwood", "text": "**The Hunger in the Firs** (The Deep Firs, The Firwood). A wendigo has come into the Deep Firs, and every week another logger or charcoal-burner is taken from the edge of camp, until the steads along the whole southern rim are emptying. The logging-lord who owns them all, a hard-drinking snowlander who has not been sober since the first death, will pay almost anything to have it ended before there is no one left to cut his wood. Reward: 1,400 florins and a timber longhouse in the Logging Steads for the party's own."}]

offer_pool_league_data_005.name: offer_pool_league_data_005
offer_pool_league_data_005.script:
skip = true
const data = [{"id": "aur_warm_pools_cooling", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "gold", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Warmwater Township", "text": "**The Water Is Cooling** (The Steaming Pools, Warmwater Township). The Steaming Pools are cooling a little every week, and the pool-warden, a frightened snowlander who measures the heat every hour, has found strange cold stones sunk in the deepest vents. The cultists who killed Stillwater's spring are at work under Warmwater itself, and the town will not survive the winter it would take to find them without help. Reward: 1,500 florins and the town's freedom of every hearth in Warmwater."}, {"id": "aur_crevasse_constructs", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "gold", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Crevasse", "text": "**The Statues Are Climbing** (The Crevasse Floor, The Crevasse). A relic crew digging too deep on the Crevasse Floor woke figures of the city's own white stone, and those constructs now hunt anything on the floor and have begun climbing toward the Rim. The halfling relic-dealer who paid for the dig is sick with guilt over the crews she lost and wants the constructs stopped or the way they came up sealed before they reach the camps. Reward: 1,200 florins and a white-stone relic that no scholar in Larion can explain."}, {"id": "aur_jarl_drake_war", "kind": "social", "rank": "platinum", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Whitefang Hold", "text": "**The Last Egg Raid** (The Jarl's Hall, Whitefang Hold). The jarl of Whitefang Hold means to lead every giant in the hold up the White Wyrmspire and end the feud with the ice drakes for good, and if the raid fails the drakes will come down on every settlement in Aurora for a generation. A hot-headed giant youth who dreams of ending the feud another way has persuaded the jarl to hear smallfolk out once, in front of the whole hall. Reward: 3,000 florins from the watch and a place at the jarl's table for as long as the party lives."}, {"id": "aur_bearfolk_envoy", "kind": "social", "rank": "platinum", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Warmwater Township", "text": "**Swear to the Bear Throne** (The Watch-Hall, Warmwater Township). A royal envoy of the nanukin kingdom has come to the Watch-Hall demanding that Warmwater and every snowlander town swear to the bearfolk crown, or lose the bearfolk garrisons that hold the southern ice. The watch-commander, a proud snowlander too stubborn to bend, would rather freeze than kneel, and the party is wanted to find terms both peoples can live with before the north splits in two. Reward: 2,500 florins and the recognition of both peoples, bearfolk and snowlander alike."}, {"id": "aur_temple_defector", "kind": "social", "rank": "platinum", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Temple of the Hearth", "text": "**The Defector on the Steps** (The Frozen Steps, The Temple of the Hearth). A young defector from the cult that kills Aurora's springs has sent word that she will tell how every spring was choked, and how to undo it, but only if the party meets her on the Frozen Steps of the dead temple.
