He suspects a visitor has trained it to steal and is selling the gear below the clouds, and wants the thief found out without hurting the monkey. Reward: 100 florins and a pair of the workshop's sandals, fitted to the party."}, {"id": "red_caravan_yard_guides", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Saffra", "text": "**Guides Who Lose Their Caravans** (The Caravan Yards, Saffra). Caravans leaving Saffra with a certain smiling guide keep getting ambushed by gnoll raiders in exactly the same stretch of canyon, and the guide keeps walking home without a scratch. A widowed caravan-master with one wagon left is sure he is selling them out and wants proof before she hires anyone again. Reward: 120 florins and a place in the caravan-master's next profitable run."}, {"id": "red_ascension_false_master", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Redrock", "location": "The Sky Temple of the Ascension", "text": "**The Master Who Isn't** (The Ascension Court, The Sky Temple of the Ascension). A robed stranger in the Ascension Court claims to be a wandering master of the Temple's art and sells private lessons to pilgrims, promising that they can run on air after three days. Several have jumped, and one starry-eyed dwarf pilgrim with a sprained ankle still believes in him. The monks want the fraud shown up gently so the believers are not broken along with him. Reward: 90 florins and a true lesson from a monk of the Temple."}, {"id": "red_huzad_captive_bargain", "kind": "social", "rank": "silver", "region": "Redrock", "location": "The Ruins of Naran-Kadish", "text": "**An Audience with the Sultan** (The Palace Quarters, The Ruins of Naran-Kadish). A band of gnoll captive-traders has brought a dozen people taken off the canyon road to the Palace Quarters of Naran-Kadish to be sold. Huzad, the vain and dangerous gnoll sultan who rules the ruin's princes from the Palace Quarters, will hear an offer for them, but his price may be coin, flattery, or a service against a rival prince. Their families want them home. Reward: 400 florins from the families, and whatever goodwill the sultan chooses to remember."}, {"id": "red_peacocks_blackmail", "kind": "social", "rank": "silver", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Cloudtop", "text": "**Letters at the Prince of Peacocks** (The Prince of Peacocks, Cloudtop). A charming fortune-hunter at the Prince of Peacocks is courting the heir of a proud Cloudtop house, and holds love letters she wrote him that he threatens to read aloud at the revels unless the house agrees to the match. A weary old poet who has sat in the same shaded gallery for thirty years and knows every secret in the hall has seen through him, and will talk to someone discreet; the house wants the letters recovered or destroyed and the match given up, without a scandal. Reward: 450 florins from the house and a standing welcome at its revels."}, {"id": "red_edict_stolen_glory", "kind": "social", "rank": "silver", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Cloudtop", "text": "**Whose Trophy Is It?** (The Court of Edicts, Cloudtop). A noble heir of Cloudtop has presented the Court of Edicts with the trophy of a great beast and claimed the princes' reward and favor, but a bitter dwarf crew-leader swears his crew made that kill and lost two friends doing it, and that the heir's retainers took the trophy from their camp. The court will only listen to proof. Reward: 350 florins and the dwarf crew's lasting loyalty."}, {"id": "red_wadi_trophy_poachers", "kind": "social", "rank": "silver", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Wadi of the Beasts", "text": "**The Keepers' Last Warning** (The Canyon Floor, Wadi of the Beasts). A company of trophy poachers has been killing in the wadi for spikes and pelts alone, leaving carcasses in the water and ignoring the keepers. An ancient desert druid who never speaks above a whisper has told the hunters who come in good faith that the keepers will close the wadi to everyone unless the poachers are stopped. Reward: 300 florins and the keepers' permission to hunt anything in the wadi, once."}, {"id": "red_waystation_ore_buyer", "kind": "social", "rank": "silver", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Copperstone", "text": "**Copperstone Is Not for Sale** (The Waystation, Copperstone). A smooth ore-buyer from the brass-cities has set up at the Copperstone Waystation, lending generously to miners against their shops and mine-shares, and the loans come due when the thin veins fail. A young pygmy smith just back from the heights with fancy airs was first to spot the trick, and he needs help to break the scheme before half the village belongs to one outsider. Reward: 250 florins and a masterwork piece from the village's finest smith."}, {"id": "red_cliff_path_manticore", "kind": "monster", "rank": "silver", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Wadi of the Beasts", "text": "**The Manticore Over the Cliff Path** (The Cliff Caves, Wadi of the Beasts). A manticore has made the cliff path to the keepers' caves its hunting perch, flinging spikes at anyone who climbs it and chatting pleasantly with them while they bleed. A one-armed old lion-hunter who lost his arm to this very beast wants it dead and its tail on his wall, and will fight beside anyone who asks. Reward: 480 florins and the manticore's spikes and tail-stinger."}, {"id": "red_dune_court_ifrit", "kind": "monster", "rank": "silver", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Suleyvan's Folly", "text": "**The Fire in the Dune Courts** (The Dune Courts, Suleyvan's Folly). A sunburnt half-elf digger opened the wrong lamp in the Dune Courts of Suleyvan's Folly, and the ifrit inside has been burning its way from court to court ever since, driving every treasure-seeker out. She kept the lamp and very badly wants it back inside, or failing that, dead. Reward: 420 florins and the emberglass it leaves, or its sworn favor."}]

offer_pool_league_data_042.name: offer_pool_league_data_042
offer_pool_league_data_042.script:
skip = true
const data = [{"id": "red_glassways_live_demon", "kind": "monster", "rank": "silver", "region": "Redrock", "location": "The Flamebleed", "text": "**Bottle One Alive** (The Glassways, The Flamebleed). A burn-scarred demon-hunter from the Citadel of the Pact, who has bottled forty demons and lost count, wants it caught alive in a warded vessel rather than cut down to gather itself again, and needs a crew to hold it in place. Reward: 500 florins from the demon-hunters, or its burning heart if it has to be killed."}, {"id": "red_crypts_ghasts", "kind": "monster", "rank": "silver", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Ghoultown", "text": "**Down into the Crypts** (The Crypts, Ghoultown). Reward: 380 florins and the brother's axe, if the dwarf can bear to part with it."}, {"id": "red_redgate_raider_band", "kind": "monster", "rank": "silver", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Redgate Caravanserai", "text": "**Redgate Is Taken Again** (The Cellars, Redgate Caravanserai). Reward: 450 florins and the pick of the raiders' plunder."}, {"id": "red_thousand_seals_marid", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "silver", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Suleyvan's Folly", "text": "**The One True Answer** (The Hall of a Thousand Seals, Suleyvan's Folly). Reward: 300 florins and the loremistress's help with any other seal in the Folly."}, {"id": "red_market_robed_buyers", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "silver", "region": "Redrock", "location": "The Ruins of Naran-Kadish", "text": "**Who Buys the Marked Shards?** (The Market Ruins, The Ruins of Naran-Kadish). Reward: 350 florins and first refusal on the fence's next strange find."}, {"id": "red_hall_of_breath_thief", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "silver", "region": "Redrock", "location": "The Sky Temple of the Ascension", "text": "**Pages Missing from the Hall of Breath** (The Hall of Breath, The Sky Temple of the Ascension). Reward: 280 florins and a lesson from the Temple's instructors."}, {"id": "red_workshop_stolen_vessel", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "silver", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Citadel of the Pact", "text": "**One Bottle Short** (The Workshops, Citadel of the Pact). Reward: 400 florins and a sealing-ring made to the party's measure."}, {"id": "red_forge_spirit_cruelty", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "silver", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Saffra", "text": "**The Forges Are Dimming** (The Forges, Saffra). Reward: 900 florins from the town's elders and the swordmaster's own sword."}, {"id": "red_palace_poisoner_prince", "kind": "social", "rank": "gold", "region": "Redrock", "location": "The Ruins of Naran-Kadish", "text": "**If the Sultan Dies** (The Palace Quarters, The Ruins of Naran-Kadish). offer_pool_league_data_043.name: offer_pool_league_data_043
offer_pool_league_data_043.script:
skip = true
const data = [{"id": "red_vaults_soul_eater", "kind": "monster", "rank": "gold", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Ghoultown", "text": "**What Waits Under Ghoultown** (The Lower Vaults, Ghoultown). Something in the Lower Vaults beneath Ghoultown drinks the souls of the living and turns the empty bodies into more ghouls, and it has been feeding well on plunderers this year. A gaunt priestess who lost her whole pilgrim band in the ruin, and saw them rise again, will lead a crew back down to kill it, and will not rest until it is done. Reward: 1,400 florins and the soulstone it leaves, a dark gem worth a fortune."}, {"id": "red_high_nests_blue_dragon", "kind": "monster", "rank": "gold", "region": "Redrock", "location": "The Bonecrags", "text": "**Lightning over the Bonecrags** (The High Nests, The Bonecrags). A lightning drake has driven the vultures off the High Nests of the Bonecrags and taken the cliff-tops and their glittering hoard for its own, and it has begun striking cloudwing condors, riders and all, out of the sky with lightning. An eccentric gnome treasure-hunter who has watched it for weeks through a spyglass thinks it can be killed, driven off, or bargained with, and mostly wants the hoard in its nest. Reward: 1,100 florins from the condor-keepers and a share of the nest."}, {"id": "red_sanctum_great_djinn", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "gold", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Suleyvan's Folly", "text": "**The Wind in Suleyvan's Sanctum** (Suleyvan's Sanctum, Suleyvan's Folly). The master's own seals in Suleyvan's Sanctum are failing, and the great djinn bound there is waking, its winds already tearing through the Folly and scouring the canyon outside. An exacting dwarf binder who failed her demon-hunter training by a hair thinks she knows how to bind it into service instead of fighting it, if a crew can hold it while she works. Reward: 1,500 florins, a vessel of thunderglass, and perhaps a djinn's service."}, {"id": "red_terrace_false_prophet", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "gold", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Cloudtop", "text": "**The Sun-Dragon Is Not Coming** (The Cloud Terrace, Cloudtop). A silver-tongued prophet on the Cloud Terrace preaches that the old sun-dragon of the peaks will return if Cloudtop proves worthy, and the proof he demands grows wilder: fasting, burned wealth, and now a leap from the terrace edge. A skeptical old stargazer who knows exactly how the prophet fakes his signs wants help stopping him before his followers start jumping. Reward: 800 florins from the city's houses and a night at the stargazer's telescope."}, {"id": "red_chapter_hall_schism", "kind": "social", "rank": "platinum", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Citadel of the Pact", "text": "**Keep the Pact** (The Chapter Hall, Citadel of the Pact). A faction of hunters within the Citadel of the Pact has begun keeping the demons they catch instead of casting them out, arguing that bound demons could be turned against the others, and many of the young hunters agree. A stooped half-elf master of the citadel, leaning on a rose-stone staff, knows a kept demon always gets loose, and wants outsiders to help turn the chapter and see the kept demons cast out through the Gate of Gaol before the split becomes war. Reward: 2,500 florins and the right to carry the Citadel's writ anywhere in the land."}, {"id": "red_spire_close_the_ladders", "kind": "social", "rank": "platinum", "region": "Redrock", "location": "The Sky Temple of the Ascension", "text": "**Do Not Haul Up the Ladders** (The Ascendants' Spire, The Sky Temple of the Ascension). The elder masters of the Ascendants' Spire are close to a vote to haul up the Temple's long ladders forever and close the Temple to a land they say is past saving, taking its teaching out of the world. The youngest of them, a laughing goblin who disagrees with everyone on principle, thinks outsiders who have seen what the land still is might sway the vote. Reward: 2,000 florins and training in the Temple's deeper art."}, {"id": "red_peacocks_demon_envoy", "kind": "social", "rank": "platinum", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Cloudtop", "text": "**The Charming Guest** (The Prince of Peacocks, Cloudtop). A charming guest at the Prince of Peacocks has been courting the great houses of Cloudtop with gifts, favors, and a proposal of peace with the demons below, in exchange for small concessions. A jaded revel-mistress in a coat of peacock feathers has noticed that the peacocks will not go near him, and fears the houses are about to sell the region to whatever sent him. Reward: 3,000 florins from the princes and a place of honor at every revel in Cloudtop."}, {"id": "red_beast_pens_brass_dragon", "kind": "monster", "rank": "platinum", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Wadi of the Beasts", "text": "**What Stirs the Wadi** (The Beast-Pens, Wadi of the Beasts). The beasts of the wadi have been breeding and raging past all measure, and the penned ones in the keepers' Beast-Pens now scream toward the deep desert every night. A scarred lizardfolk beast-master who trusts no hunter has finally admitted why: an elder sand drake, grown huge in an age under the deep sand, has come up out of the badlands, and its hunger is driving every creature in the region toward the only water. Reward: 2,800 florins and a plate of the drake's hide, forged into a shield in Cloudtop."}, {"id": "red_quick_balor", "kind": "monster", "rank": "platinum", "region": "Redrock", "location": "The Flamebleed", "text": "**The Balor in the Quick** (The Quick, The Flamebleed). A balor is forcing its way up through the burning pools of the Quick, the deepest reach of the Flamebleed, and every night more of it is in the world. An old djinnborn fire-smith who swore long ago to forge the blade that would end such a thing has finished it, and needs a crew to carry it down and use it before the demon is fully free. Reward: 4,000 florins and the blade itself, still burning."}, {"id": "red_aerie_cloud_giant", "kind": "monster", "rank": "platinum", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Cloudtop", "text": "**The Giant Who Wants the Peaks** (The Condor Aerie, Cloudtop). A cloud giant has come down out of the high sky claiming Cloudtop's peaks as his ancestors' hall, and each day he tears down another condor spire to make his point. The old eaglekin aerie-master with white-tipped wings has lost a dozen nests and wants him stopped, by battle, bargain, or proof that the peaks were never his. Reward: 3,500 florins and a cloudwing condor of the party's own."}, {"id": "red_gaol_traitor_warden", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "platinum", "region": "Redrock", "location": "Citadel of the Pact", "text": "**Someone Means to Open the Gate** (The Vault of Gaol, Citadel of the Pact). Someone among the wardens of the Vault of Gaol has been quietly weakening the locks on the Gate, one night at a time, and when the Gate is opened wrongly what it holds can come back. A blind old gate-keeper who says she can hear the abyss breathing has heard it change, and trusts no one inside the Citadel enough to say so. Reward: 3,000 florins and the Citadel's gratitude, which is rarely given."}, {"id": "red_diggings_demon_cult", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "platinum", "region": "Redrock", "location": "The Ruins of Naran-Kadish", "text": "**What Lies Under Naran-Kadish** (The Diggings, The Ruins of Naran-Kadish). Robed cultists have bribed their way into the deepest pits of the Diggings under Naran-Kadish, and are directing the captive diggers toward the old seal that burned the city and drove the demons back. The gnoll princes neither know nor care. An old gnoll dig-mistress who hears voices from the pit has decided she does care, and will help anyone who means to stop them. Reward: 3,500 florins and whatever relics of the burned city the cult has hoarded."}]

Giant spiders have webbed the empty upper floors above the Dead Ring's barrow market and have started dropping on stall-keepers at dusk. A demonborn fence who has sold from the same doorway for years and flatly refuses to move wants them burned out, and he is not particular about how, so long as his goods survive. Reward: 60 florins and a pick from the fence's table, where nothing has a history anyone will admit to."}, {"id": "san_cave_bear_camp", "kind": "monster", "rank": "copper", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "The Cold Iron Caverns", "text": "**The Bear at the Cave Mouth** (The Entrance Cave, The Cold Iron Caverns). A cave bear comes up out of the dark into the Entrance Cave every night, scatters the diggers' fires, and eats the camp's food down to the last sack, and the diggers are going in hungry. The gruff dwarven digger-boss who guards the stores has lost two nights' sleep and one good cook to it, and wants it gone before his crew gives up the caverns. Reward: 70 florins and a small share of the next haul of cold iron ore."}, {"id": "san_shrine_boggart", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "copper", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "Sanctuary", "text": "**The Wandering Crook** (The Shrine of Mother Mayreth, Sanctuary). Every morning the crook of the great statue at the Shrine of Mother Mayreth has moved to a new hand, the candles have been relit in odd patterns, and a crowd of pilgrims now camps outside waiting for the next sign. The half-elf shrine-keeper wants very much to believe it is a miracle, but someone should find out whether a boggart has moved in first. Reward: 35 florins and the shrine-keeper's blessing, which is sincerely meant."}, {"id": "san_ember_sprites", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "copper", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "Velantami", "text": "**The Fire That Never Dies** (The Hollow Hall, Velantami). Each night a flurry of sprites slips into the Hollow Hall and tries to carry off embers from the great fire pit, and twice now the fire has nearly gone out. The grumbling old dwarf druid who has tended that fire for longer than most initiates have been alive blames the initiates, the initiates blame him, and the sprites seem to be enjoying all of it. Reward: 40 florins and a Velantami remedy for burns, cuts, and bad tempers."}, {"id": "san_pact_stone_prophet", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "copper", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "Sanctuary", "text": "**The Weeping Stone** (Pact Square, Sanctuary). A street preacher has drawn bigger crowds every market day by pointing to red streaks on the Pact stone and crying that it weeps blood because the Pact is ending. The market is jammed, fights keep breaking out, and the harried gnome market warden who rings the opening bell would dearly like to know who is really painting the stone at night. Reward: 45 florins and a prime stall in Pact Square for a week, if the party has anything to sell."}, {"id": "san_piping_satyr", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "copper", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "The Eastwood", "text": "**Dancing Till Dawn** (The Wildkeeper Camp, The Eastwood). A satyr has taken to piping outside the Wildkeeper Camp every night, and whoever hears the tune gets up and dances until sunrise whether they wish to or not. The camp's wood elf cook has not slept in a week, is burning the porridge, and would take anyone's help who can stop the piping, trade for it, or outplay the thing. Reward: 40 florins and a hot meal from a cook who has finally slept."}]

offer_pool_league_data_045.name: offer_pool_league_data_045
offer_pool_league_data_045.script:
skip = true
const data = [{"id": "san_wake_body_snatchers", "kind": "social", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "Sanctuary", "text": "**Empty Coffins** (Grave Street, Sanctuary). Twice this month a coffin laid out at a Grave Street wake has been found empty by morning, and the neighborhood is ready to hang the first stranger it sees. The bellowing minotaur barkeep whose back room hosts most of the street's wakes wants the body-snatchers found and whoever is buying from them named, before his tavern gets a reputation it will never shake. Reward: 120 florins from the barkeep and a round on the house at every wake thereafter."}, {"id": "san_underhalls_makers_mark", "kind": "social", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "Sanctuary", "text": "**Two Clans, One Mark** (The Underhalls, Sanctuary). A hot-headed young clan heir has started striking his family's forge-mark on work another clan swears is theirs, and their brawls now spill across the Underhalls' ale-halls every week. The clans settle their own quarrels down here, but the weary dwarven alewife who pours for both of them wants someone from outside to sort it before it goes from fists to axes. Reward: 150 florins and a keg of dwarven ale brewed for the occasion."}, {"id": "san_cabin_blackmailer", "kind": "social", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "Sanctuary", "text": "**Sweet Wine Below Deck** (The Floating World, Sanctuary). Guests invited below deck on the Floating World by friendly strangers keep waking in an empty cabin with a thick head and nothing in their pockets. A nervous gnome fiddler in the barge's band has seen who pours the wine and where the robbers go ashore, and is too frightened to say it to anyone but hired blades who can keep him out of it. Reward: 140 florins, raised quietly among several embarrassed passengers."}, {"id": "san_child_thief_ring", "kind": "social", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "The Outer Ring", "text": "**Light Fingers** (The Unfinished House, The Outer Ring). A thief-master who deals from a back table at the Unfinished House has been luring city children over the broken wall with sweets and easy coin, and sending them back through the gates to pick pockets for him. A sharp-eyed halfling mother whose son has joined his crew has tracked him this far and wants her boy back and the ringleader finished in the city. Reward: 100 florins, all the mother has saved, and her fierce gratitude."}, {"id": "san_false_mire_guide", "kind": "social", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "The Sundwen Mire", "text": "**The Guide Who Always Comes Back** (The Black Water, The Sundwen Mire). A friendly mire guide keeps hiring out to travelers crossing the Black Water, and keeps coming back alone with a sad story about raiders in the reeds. A lanky foxkin eel-trapper who has lost two partners that way is sure the guide is leading people into an ambush on purpose, and wants proof, and an end to it. Reward: 130 florins and the eel-trapper's safe paths across the Black Water."}, {"id": "san_char_shadows", "kind": "monster", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "Sanctuary", "text": "**What Lives in the Char** (The Char, Sanctuary). Shadows have gathered in the gutted cellars of the Char, the dark shapes of the fire's dead, and at night they reach over the barricades to drain the strength from anyone sleeping too close. A hard-bitten ratkin rag-picker who has lived against the barricade since the fire knows the ruins better than the watch and will show the way in, for a cut of whatever turns up. Reward: 180 florins and the rag-picker's pick of salvage from the block, split fairly, she says."}, {"id": "san_gallery_gricks", "kind": "monster", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "The Cold Iron Caverns", "text": "**The Ceiling Has Teeth** (The Workings, The Cold Iron Caverns). Gricks have moved into the richest gallery of the Workings, clinging to the roof among the roots and dropping on anyone who stops to swing a pick. A young dwarf digger who found that seam and badly wants her name on it will go in with anyone willing to clear the gallery, and is likely to go in without them if no one comes. Reward: 160 florins and a cold iron dagger hammered from her first ore."}, {"id": "san_sinkhole_wolves", "kind": "monster", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "The Riddlewood", "text": "**Wolves in the Sinkholes** (The Broken Slopes, The Riddlewood). A pack of dire wolves has denned in a sinkhole on the Broken Slopes, and it has started running down the herb-gatherers who work the limestone for rare moss. A gap-toothed gnome herbalist who has foraged these slopes for decades will not stop, not for wolves and certainly not for the bandits, and wants company that can deal with the pack. Reward: 110 florins and a pouch of her rarest remedies."}, {"id": "san_canal_eel", "kind": "monster", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "Sanctuary", "text": "**Something Under the Gondolas** (Canal Square, Sanctuary). A giant eel has come up the canals and now lurks under Canal Square, rolling small boats and snatching whatever falls in, including one poleman last week. A loud-mouthed human gondolier who swears it is a sea serpent and has been telling everyone so wants to be there when it comes out of the water, mostly to be proved right. Reward: 140 florins and free passage on the canals for the rest of the season."}, {"id": "san_trail_drider", "kind": "monster", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "The Eastwood", "text": "**Silk Across the Trails** (The Deep Wood, The Eastwood). A drider has been stringing webs across the game trails of the Deep Wood and hauling off scouts who blunder into them. A sullen half-orc tracker whose brother went out on those trails ten days ago is still looking, has found silk and nothing else, and wants help reaching its lair while there might still be someone alive in it. Reward: 150 florins and a bolt of the drider's silk, worth a good deal in the city."}, {"id": "san_keep_grave_robbers", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "Terlothis", "text": "**The Dead Walk Further** (The Broken Keep, Terlothis). A crew of grave-robbers keeps slipping into the Broken Keep to pry old elven blades off the fallen, and each time they do, the dead come a little further past the walls after them. A shaken woodcutter whose hut sits nearest the ruin has found footprints of bare bone in his yard, and wants the robbing stopped before the dead reach his door. Reward: 90 florins from the woodcutter and a nearby village, and a cord of good firewood."}, {"id": "san_twice_seen_merchant", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "Sanctuary", "text": "**The Man Who Was in Two Places** (The Greenwarren, Sanctuary). Customers across the Greenwarren swear a foxkin spice merchant has sold them sawdust at twice the price, on days he was nowhere near their terrace. The bewildered merchant has lost half his trade and been punched twice, and he is beginning to suspect that some fey changeling is walking around in his face, because he has seen himself across the market, and he wants it stopped and his name cleared in the Greenwarren. Reward: 120 florins and a lifetime of spices at the honest price."}]

Reward: 90 florins from the woodcutter's family and a hand-carved charm for the road."}, {"id": "san_goldmount_poisoner", "kind": "social", "rank": "silver", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "Sanctuary", "text": "**A Slow Illness on Goldmount** (Goldmount, Sanctuary). Someone needs to get him out by bargain, trick, or steel. Reward: 300 florins, raised by the washerwomen of the canals, and their loyalty for life."}, {"id": "san_council_leak", "kind": "social", "rank": "silver", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "Sanctuary", "text": "**Someone Is Selling the Watch** (Pact Square, Sanctuary). Reward: 450 florins and a cold iron blade from the smith's own hand."}, {"id": "san_open_wood_displacer", "kind": "monster", "rank": "silver", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "The Eastwood", "text": "**Where It Seems to Be** (The Open Wood, The Eastwood). A quiet elven healer at the Wildkeeper Camp who tends the survivors keeps a careful count of the missing and has drawn a map of every attack, and wants it stopped by people who can hit something that is not there. A gnome engineer who maps its path by listening to the stone says it will break into the dwarven halls within the season, and after that the whole city stands on shaking ground. Reward: 3,500 florins from the clans and council together, and a cold iron weapon of the party's choosing."}, {"id": "san_terlothis_lich", "kind": "monster", "rank": "platinum", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "Terlothis", "text": "**The Door Beneath Terlothis** (The Underkeep, Terlothis). A master necromancer has made a lair in the Underkeep of Terlothis and works night after night at the great sealed door there, while the dead gather ever thicker around it as if to stop him. An ancient high-elf warden who was a child when the keep fell will not say what lies behind that door, only that it must stay shut, and that he cannot go down alone. Reward: 5,000 florins from the Council and a high-elven blade that has not left the Wardens' keeping in an age."}, {"id": "san_pact_revocation", "kind": "social", "rank": "platinum", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "Sanctuary", "text": "**The Pact in the Balance** (Pact Square, Sanctuary). A high-elf lord has come to Sanctuary with a long list of the city's broken promises, and is pressing the high elves to revoke the Pact that lets the city exist at all. The council has put a young half-elf envoy, far out of her depth and aware of it, in charge of changing his mind, and she needs people who can dig out his real reasons and win his peers over. Reward: 3,000 florins from the council and Sanctuary's thanks written into its own records."}, {"id": "san_renegade_war_leader", "kind": "social", "rank": "platinum", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "The Riddlewood", "text": "**Before the Wood Goes to War** (The Warrens, The Riddlewood). The renegade elves' war-leader is planning a massacre across the border, bloody enough to drag the high elves and the humans into open war. A weary deserter from his own band, with a price on her head from both sides, will get a party into the Warrens to face him, whether to talk him down, split his followers, or end him. Reward: 3,500 florins from the Council and a hold on the high elves' gratitude."}, {"id": "san_oak_firebrand", "kind": "social", "rank": "platinum", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "Velantami", "text": "**The Hollow Hall Divides** (The Hollow Hall, Velantami). An old druid of Velantami has been preaching in the Hollow Hall that the wood will only heal when every outsider is driven from it, Sanctuary included, and more of the fellowship listen each night. Vaska Oradine, the First Keeper of Velantami, wants outsiders to answer him in open council, and hunt down the burnings he has been blaming on the city. Reward: 2,500 florins, the fellowship's oath of friendship, and a guide through any part of the wood."}, {"id": "san_wild_hunt", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "platinum", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "Yslaine's Demesne", "text": "**When the Horns Blow** (The Edgewood, Yslaine's Demesne). At every new moon, a wild hunt of horned riders comes out of the Edgewood and takes whoever is on the roads, and each moon it rides further toward Sanctuary. A jittery ratkin tinker is the only one ever to come back, and has not slept since, but he remembers the rules of their chase, and says they can be beaten, if the right people ride. Reward: 4,500 florins from the Council and a horn the hunt left behind."}, {"id": "san_envoy_assassin", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "platinum", "region": "Sanctuary Vale", "location": "Sanctuary", "text": "**The Envoy at the Window** (The Last Stand Tavern, Sanctuary). A high-elf envoy has taken to drinking at the Last Stand Tavern every night, at the table by the window, and a master assassin has already failed twice to kill him there. If he dies inside the walls, the Pact dies with him. The envoy, who loves low company and will not be moved, laughs off both attempts, and someone must catch the assassin, and learn who hired them, before the third. Reward: 3,000 florins from the Council and a signet of high-elven favor."}, {"id": "crew_claims_feud", "kind": "social", "rank": "copper", "region": "Silvervale", "location": "Ardan's Watch", "text": "**The Claims Feud** (The Fist & Flagon, Ardan's Watch). Two rival Copper crews keep filing claims on the same salvage bounties and brawl about it every night they end up drinking at the Fist & Flagon. Odran Strath, the orc veteran who runs the tavern's fighting pit, wants the feud ended for good before one of them sets his bar on fire. Reward: 35 florins from Odran and a month of free drinks at the rail."}, {"id": "runaway_daughter", "kind": "social", "rank": "copper", "region": "Silvervale", "location": "Ardan's Watch", "text": "**A Guest Who Keeps Slipping Away** (The High City, Ardan's Watch). A visiting dignitary's daughter, a sharp-tongued young woman who hates being guarded, keeps slipping out of her family's High City residence to see how the rest of the city lives, and she is out there again. Her fretful halfling chamberlain wants her brought home quietly, and she will not come without a good reason. Reward: 60 florins and the household's goodwill."}]

A giant sewer lizard as long as a rowboat has learned that the Basement's cookhouses throw out fish at closing time, and now it comes up through the drains to take the fish early, and the cooks too if they are slow; a ladle-wielding gnome cook has already fought it off twice. The Overburden's salvage buyers would pay extra to have it alive for one of their cages. Reward: 50 florins from the river traders, plus whatever the war-chief has hoarded."}, {"id": "crypt_banshee", "kind": "monster", "rank": "copper", "region": "Silvervale", "location": "The City of Ancestors", "text": "**The Banshee in the High Tombs** (The High Tombs, The City of Ancestors). Reward: 30 florins and a standing corner table on the dry floor."}, {"id": "swi_wall_sword_claim", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "copper", "region": "Swordlaw Isles", "location": "Tevantia", "text": "**Whose Sword Is on the Wall?** (The Two Swords, Tevantia). A braggart swordsman keeps turning up at the Two Swords swearing one of the crossed blades on its walls was stolen from his grandfather, and he challenges anyone who laughs. Vianne Damarque, the tavern's proprietress and a celebrated former house champion, finds him amusing but bad for trade, and wants the truth of that sword settled. Reward: 50 florins and an introduction from Vianne to someone worth knowing."}, {"id": "swi_siren_offerings", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "copper", "region": "Swordlaw Isles", "location": "Freehaven", "text": "**The Siren's Missing Coins** (Ligeia's Landing, Freehaven). Someone keeps stealing the coins sailors leave at the siren statue's feet in the grotto at Ligeia's Landing, and crews putting out swear their luck has turned. A superstitious retired pirate who sweeps the grotto every morning has seen wet little footprints leading back into the grotto pool and is sure a nixie has moved in, and he wants it caught, bargained with, or chased off before the haven turns on itself. Reward: 45 florins and a lucky coin he swears the siren blessed."}, {"id": "swi_fraud_fencing_master", "kind": "social", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Swordlaw Isles", "location": "Tevantia", "text": "**Lessons That Get You Killed** (Tevantia Harbor, Tevantia). A swaggering fencing master runs a dueling school on the harbor-plaza, takes huge fees from hopeful young commoners, and teaches them flashy tricks that look grand and get them cut to ribbons in their first real duel. A limping young commoner cut in her first duel wants him beaten in an open bout in front of his pupils, and his school shut or made honest, before his next class steps onto the bridges. Reward: 150 florins and free lessons from a real master."}, {"id": "swi_marked_deck_ship_paper", "kind": "social", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Swordlaw Isles", "location": "Gavarra", "text": "**The Ship Paper at the Tables** (The Tower of Fortune, Gavarra). A shipwright's son gambled away his family's ship paper at the Tower of Fortune to a card sharp who plays marked decks and wins most nights. The shipwright's iron-willed widow wants the paper back, by beating the sharp at his own table or by exposing him in a House that punishes cheats. Reward: 180 florins and a berth on the family's ship when it next sails."}]

offer_pool_league_data_056.name: offer_pool_league_data_056
offer_pool_league_data_056.script:
skip = true

A moneylender's leg-breakers have started breaking the hands of Midmarket stallholders who fall a day behind on interest that doubles every week. A frogkin rope-seller with a dozen children and no patience left has had enough, and she wants the leg-breakers stopped, by fear, by bargain, or by a trip into the canal. Reward: 120 florins and the best rope on the bridge, as much as you can carry."}, {"id": "swi_redfin_salvage_feud", "kind": "social", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Swordlaw Isles", "location": "North Canal", "text": "**Two Crews, One Wreck** (Redfin Waystation, North Canal). The bored orc harbormaster, who plays solitaire through every crisis, wants the claim settled before blood spills on neutral ground and the waystation loses its peace. Now the rake waits on the bridge below the lord's tower every dawn, mocking him for not yet coming out. The flustered dwarf steward of the house, who polishes her spectacles whenever she is nervous, wants the old man saved without shaming him: a champion to stand for him, or an apology from the rake. Reward: 140 florins and the sailmaker's salvaged sea-chest."}, {"id": "swi_landing_harpies", "kind": "monster", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Swordlaw Isles", "location": "Freehaven", "text": "**Screaming Over the Landing** (Ligeia's Landing, Freehaven). A clutch of pseudodragons, cat-sized drakes with a magpie's love of anything that shines, has nested in the cliffs above Ligeia's Landing and dives on the square at dusk, snatching rings, coin, and buttons and biting whoever holds on. Reward: 190 florins and a genuine-looking, entirely forged League commendation."}, {"id": "swi_caged_merrow_show", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "bronze", "region": "Swordlaw Isles", "location": "Tevantia", "text": "**The Sea-Beast in the Barrel** (Tevantia Harbor, Tevantia). effects.text: Go to Ardan's Watch and find Ixo Duvain at the Imp-orium. Tell him the hearth at Hillhome sent you.

conditions.query: A member of the party asks to join the Long Watch, accepts an invitation to join it, or swears its oath.

effects.instruction: A member of the party is joining the Long Watch. Stage it simply and warmly, with no forms or tests: a knight of the Watch, Hakon Falk if he is present, has them lay a hand on the great lamp and say the oath, "while one fire burns," and pins a plain iron lamp-badge to their coat. The Watch is glad to have them. Then point them to the great map, where the dark fires are marked.

effects.text: Study the Lamp-Tower map and choose a dark watchfire to relight.

longwatch_fire_relit.name: longwatch_fire_relit

conditions.query: In this narration the party actually rekindles a dark Long Watch watchfire or signal-fire so that it is burning again. The moment of relighting counts; a fire that was already burning, a plan to relight one, or an ordinary campfire does not.

effects.instruction: A dark watchfire has just been relit. Let it catch and roar, and show the answer: the next fire in the chain visible far across the ice, or the relief of the people who depend on it.

longwatch_fire_relit.script:
const now = storage.auroraTurns || 0
if (now - (storage.longWatchLastRelitTurn ?? -99) < 3) { skip = true } else { storage.longWatchLastRelitTurn = now }

effects.instruction: The Long Watch makes the character who relit them a lamp-bearer for the fires they have relit. Keep it brief and proud: the iron lamp-badge is exchanged for a silver one in front of whoever is in the tower. If the party does not already have a Shore Cottage, the Watch also gives them the key to one it keeps for its own, a home on the warm shore of the lake, free for as long as they serve.

The Long Watch knights the lamp-bearer. Make it a real moment: before the great lamp, a knight of the Watch, Hakon Falk if he is present, calls a hearth-spirit out of the lamp, and the spirit freely gives a spark of itself, which is set into their own weapon. The weapon now holds a living watchfire spark that can wake into flame. They are a knight of the Long Watch, and the Watch is a little less alone.

When it fits the scene, show this: far out on the frozen sea, beneath the ice, a long glow of green and violet light moves slowly and then fades, like something vast turning over in its sleep. Anyone who sees it knows the old stories of the aurora serpents. If the party is indoors, someone rushes in with the news.

When it fits the scene, show this: far out on the frozen sea, the ice cracks with a sound like thunder, and for a moment a great crest glowing with aurora light breaks the surface before sinking again. The whole north will be talking about it. If the party is indoors, someone rushes in with the news.

When it fits the scene, show this: an aurora serpent rises. Far out where the sea-ice meets the open white, a great white serpent lifts its glowing crest into the night, looks toward the chain of burning watchfires, and calls, a long, deep sound that rolls across the north, before sinking back beneath the ice. The serpents are waking. If the party is indoors, someone rushes in with the news.

warmwater_aurora_ball_start.name: warmwater_aurora_ball_start
warmwater_aurora_ball_start.script:
const o = storage.warmwaterAurora
if (!o || o.open < 0) { skip = true } else {
  o.open = -1
  storage.warmwaterAuroraNights = (storage.warmwaterAuroraNights || 0) + 1
  effects.push({ type: 'narrative-event-start', eventId: 'warmwater_aurora_ball' })
  effects.push({ type: 'story', instruction: "The aurora is burning over Warmwater tonight, and the Aurora Ball is beginning in the Ice Gardens." })
}

conditions.query: The party asks to race, enters a rimewolf sled race, or accepts a challenge to race on the lake.

warmwater_sled_race_details.name: warmwater_sled_race_details
warmwater_sled_race_details.script:
const rivals = ["a Pearl House heir's hotshot team in gold-plated harness, driven by a showoff who has never lost", "a Hearthhouse rescue team, fast, proud, and furious at anyone who calls rescue sledding slow", "a young frost giantess pulling her own sled, who treats the whole race as a joke she is winning", "a southern gambler with a team he bought yesterday and money riding on every leg", "a grizzled old mail-sled driver who knows every crack in the lake", "a pair of brothers who race as a team and are known to cheat", "a nanukin cub of the white bearfolk, racing on foot and keeping up", "a Long Watch recruit on a borrowed team, desperate to prove themselves"]
const hazards = ["thin ice cracking open behind the leaders", "a rimewyrm stirring under the course", "a sudden whiteout halfway around the far ice", "a rival cutting across and tangling the lines", "a snow-lynx bursting from a snowbank and spooking the teams", "a pressure ridge the teams must jump", "the lead wolf picking a fight with a rival team mid-race", "the crowd surging onto the ice at the finish"]
const n = storage.warmwaterRaceCount || 0
const race = storage.warmwaterRace = storage.warmwaterRace || { n: -1 }
if (race.n !== n) {
  const a = rivals[Math.floor(Math.random() * rivals.length)]
  let b = rivals[Math.floor(Math.random() * rivals.length)]
  while (b === a) b = rivals[Math.floor(Math.random() * rivals.length)]
  race.n = n; race.rivals = [a, b]; race.hazard = hazards[Math.floor(Math.random() * hazards.length)]
}
effects.push({ type: 'story', instruction: 'This race\'s main rivals: ' + race.rivals.join('; and ') + '. The hazard on the run: ' + race.hazard + '. Give the rivals fresh names of your own.' })

warmwater_sled_race_won.name: warmwater_sled_race_won

conditions.query: The party wins the rimewolf sled race on Warmwater Lake in this narration.

warmwater_sled_race_won.script:
const race = storage.warmwaterRaceCount || 0
if (storage.warmwaterRaceWonFor === race) { skip = true } else { storage.warmwaterRaceWonFor = race }

effects.instruction: The Kennels have noticed the party's wins. The kennel-masters, with Tirsa Hellemark of the Hearthhouse rescue teams if she is present, offer them a rimewolf team of their own: a sled and a half-wild pack of white rimewolves that has chosen them. Make it a proud moment, and let the lead wolf make its own first impression.

conditions.query: The party asks about renting, buying, or staying in one of the Shore Cottages, or says they want a home in Warmwater.

effects.instruction: A Shore Cottage is free. The shore-warden who keeps them, or a neighbor, shows the party a snug carved-timber cottage with a spring-fed bath behind it and a cold stone hearth. It is theirs for a single payment of 150 florins, for as long as they want it, with no papers. They may bargain or earn it another way if the story offers one.

conditions.query: The party pays for, is given, or otherwise takes one of the Shore Cottages as their own home in this narration.

effects.text: Wake the sleeping hearth-spirit in your cottage.
Wake the sleeping hearth-spirit in your cottage.

effects.instruction: This Shore Cottage is the party's home, and its hearth-spirit, the one they named, lives in the hearth. It greets them when they come in and keeps house in exchange for good fuel: hot meals, dried gear, a hot bath, lamps lit. If asked, it passes on what it has heard through the other hearths in town: a watchfire gone dark, whether the lights are coming, or what the court is whispering.

conditions.query: In this narration a member of the party wins the final of the Grand Tournament and is named First Blade of Tevantia. Identify the champion.

effects.instruction: The party's champion has just been named First Blade of Tevantia. Let the city explode with celebration: the crowd on its feet, the houses bowing, a garland and the First Blade's crimson-and-gold sash, and every eye in the city on them.

tevantia_cast_pool.name: tevantia_cast_pool
tevantia_cast_pool.script:
const pool = ["House Montrose courtier in crimson and gold", "House Marenne swimmer with pearls in her hair", "House Ravissant dandy in violet and silver", "House Levantine wind-wright apprentice", "famous beauty holding a salon", "fencing-school student", "retired champion with a famous record", "harbor regatta sailor", "sail-lift operator", "wind-harp tuner", "gossiping lady's companion", "house herald", "tailor to the great houses", "jeweler who makes sword-hilts", "young noble looking for a second", "duelist's second with a black book of challenges", "Amphitheater master of arms", "visiting envoy from Gavarra", "merfolk trader at the harbor", "demonborn harbor pilot", "parrotfolk crier", "halfling pastry chef to the houses", "dwarven banker's heir who fences badly", "wind-glider racer", "court portrait painter", "matchmaker's go-between", "house tower steward", "Tournament bookmaker", "poet's rival", "young sworn champion of a minor house"]
const picks = []
while (picks.length < 4) { const c = pool[Math.floor(Math.random() * pool.length)]; if (!picks.includes(c)) picks.push(c) }
const guidance = "In Tevantia, anyone new whom you name or give dialogue should make a clear first impression: flamboyant clothing in house colors or bright sea-city style, something they are doing with flair, and a line in their own voice that shows what they want. Tevantia's people care about honor, love, pride, and precedence. Ordinary passers-by can stay unnamed. Established characters keep their own descriptions."
effects.push({ type: 'story', instruction: `${guidance} If this scene needs a new character, you may draw on these: ${picks.join(' · ')}. Use at most one, only when a new person fits naturally; otherwise ignore this list.` })

A fisher-girl climbs the broch every night to check the dark lamp and wants the fire lit again and someone to make him return the oil or keep the lamp fed. Reward: A hearthpearl from the Watch and a feast of smoked fish from the village."}, {"id": "lw_herdways_owl", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "recruit", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Herdways", "text": "**Something Nests on the Fire** (The Snowveil, The Herdways). Reward: A hearthpearl from the Watch and a fine white owl-feather cloak from the herders."}, {"id": "lw_icefield_snow_goblins", "kind": "monster", "rank": "recruit", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Aurora Icefields", "text": "**They Took the Fire Itself** (The Open White, Aurora Icefields). The old spirit-keeper who tended that fire for thirty years walked all the way to Warmwater to beg the Watch to bring it home. Reward: Two hearthpearls from the Watch and the old keeper's own lamp-badge, kept since his youth."}, {"id": "lw_harbor_family_feud", "kind": "social", "rank": "recruit", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Dun Beithir", "text": "**Whose Turn Is the Fire** (The Ice-Harbor, Dun Beithir). The youngest son of one family is sweet on a daughter of the other and wants the whole stupid feud over before someone drowns. Reward: A hearthpearl from the Watch and a place at both families' tables for life."}, {"id": "lw_holdfast_ogre", "kind": "monster", "rank": "recruit", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Firwood", "text": "**The Ogre in the Watch-Hut** (The Old Holdfast, The Firwood). The nervous carpenter who built the hut wants his work back and the roof fire lit, and would rather nobody got sat on. Reward: A hearthpearl from the Watch and a snug new hut door carved with a serpent, from the carpenter."}, {"id": "lw_floes_polar_bear", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "recruit", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Underfloes", "text": "**The Bear on the Floes** (The Floes, The Underfloes). A dire polar bear has claimed the ice around the floe watchfire as her hunting ground and smashed the fire-post to get at the seal-oil stored beneath it. A seal-hunter whose family depends on those floes is going hungry, wants the fire-post rebuilt and burning, and thinks the bear is starving too. Reward: A hearthpearl from the Watch and a share of the next season's seal-oil."}, {"id": "lw_migration_herd_chief", "kind": "social", "rank": "recruit", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Herdways", "text": "**The Fire on the Migration** (The Migration, The Herdways). A stubborn herder-chief put out the watchfire on the migration track because he says its light spooks the mammoth herds, and he will not let the Watch relight it. His youngest grandson, who wants to join the Watch more than anything, is caught in the middle, and thinks the fire might be moved or shielded. Reward: A hearthpearl from the Watch and the herders' promise of a mammoth-ride across the Herdways."}, {"id": "lw_rim_frost_wraiths", "kind": "monster", "rank": "lampbearer", "region": "Aurora", "location": "The Crevasse", "text": "**Cold Hands at the Rim** (The Rim, The Crevasse). A young historian camped at the rim to study the city has been sleeping with her back against the dead fire-post and is running out of courage; she wants the fire to burn through a night. Reward: Two hearthpearls from the Watch and the historian's sketches of the white city."}, {"id": "lw_pass_wyvern", "kind": "monster", "rank": "lampbearer", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Whitefang Hold", "text": "**The Wyvern on North Wind Pass** (North Wind Pass, Whitefang Hold). A wyvern has nested in the stone beacon tower on North Wind Pass and throws down anyone who climbs to the fire. A cheerful frost-giant herald who uses the pass says the giants would help, but only for someone who has earned the Watch's lamp. Reward: Two hearthpearls from the Watch and a giant-forged cloak-pin from the herald."}, {"id": "lw_stillwater_preacher", "kind": "social", "rank": "lampbearer", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Stillwater", "text": "**Let the Fire Die** (The Frozen Streets, Stillwater). A widow who kept the nearby watchfire has let it go out and is half-persuaded to walk into the white; the Watch wants her to choose her fire again and the preacher exposed or driven off. Reward: Two hearthpearls from the Watch and the widow's late husband's carved serpent housewarden."}, {"id": "lw_colossus_wisps", "kind": "wildcard", "rank": "lampbearer", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Aurora Icefields", "text": "**The Lights Around the Colossus** (The Frozen Colossus, Aurora Icefields). A sledder who followed the wrong lights and barely crawled out wants the true fire back so no one else does. Reward: Two hearthpearls from the Watch and the sledder's best rimewolf pup."}, {"id": "lw_cutting_ice_merrow", "kind": "monster", "rank": "lampbearer", "region": "Aurora", "location": "Dun Beithir", "text": "**Hands Through the Ice** (The Cutting Ice, Dun Beithir). The ice-cutter crew boss has stopped work and wants the fire lit and the raiders taught to stay below. Reward: Two hearthpearls from the Watch and a merrow-pearl the crew boss has been saving."}]

conditions.query: The party chooses to stand watch for the drowned or to wait for the black tide on the wharves or the lower bridges of Tevantia.

gather_forage.name: gather_forage

conditions.query: A member of the party forages or gathers from the land: picking herbs, digging roots or truffles, gathering wild plants, fungi, fruit, or wood, or looking over the ground for anything useful that grows. Searching a body, room, or container is not foraging, and neither is mining, cutting parts from a creature, tracking, or looking for clues, people, or hidden things.

gather_mine.name: gather_mine

conditions.query: A member of the party mines or prospects: digging, chipping, or cutting ore, stone, crystal, or glass from rock, a seam, a vein, a spoil heap, or a cave wall. Searching a body, room, or container is not mining, and neither is digging a hole or grave, clearing rubble, or breaking through a wall or door.

gather_harvest_creature.name: gather_harvest_creature

conditions.query: A member of the party cuts parts from a creature's body: skinning, butchering, or taking hide, scale, meat, glands, venom, blood, silk, bone, or a core from a slain or subdued creature. Searching a body for belongings or gear is looting, not harvesting.
A member of the party hunts, stalks, chases, or shoots at a game animal or bird: deer, boar, hares, rabbits, goats, wildfowl, or other wild beasts that are not attacking the party.

effects.instruction: Game animals behave like prey. A careless approach, a missed shot, or a wounded animal sends the herd or flock bolting, and a hit animal runs rather than stands. Fleeing game stays in sight or on a clear trail for a turn or two, so a quick second shot, a good chase, or tracking can still bring it down; only after that is it gone. A predator or a cornered, wounded animal may turn and fight instead.

conditions.query: A member of the party asks to join the Shadow Inquisition, asks Jett or another Inquisitor to take them on as an Initiate, or asks how one becomes an Inquisitor.

effects.instruction: Have Jett, or another Inquisitor of the Hall of Shadow, hear out the character who asked. The Inquisition takes people who can keep a secret and look at the dead without flinching. Let them ask a few hard, plain questions about why the character wants this work, and let the character answer in their own way. If satisfied, they invite the character to swear the Inquisition's oath at the edge of the Pit of Shadow below and take the Mark of Rhadan, and tell the warders to let them pass. Swearing is the character's choice; nothing is decided until they swear.

conditions.query: A member of the party asks to enroll at Tarnholme Academy, to sit its entrance examination, or to be admitted as a student.

effects.instruction: A master hears the request and tests them on the spot: a short, practical test of the magic they already have, judged fairly and kindly. Tarnholme takes most people who show real talent and want to learn. Admit them as a First-Year. In a sentence or two, explain that First-Years take three Practica from the board in the Great Hall and one year-end mission, and that the Colleges claim the First-Years at Colors Night, at the end of the year.

conditions.query: A sponsored Blooded vampire presents themselves to the priest-wardens of the Black Gate, asks to pass the Gate, or asks to begin the trial of lordship.

effects.instruction: The priest-wardens of the Black Gate hear the sponsored aspirant who asked. Their house sponsor has spent its name on them in the Hall of Witnesses, the Company has written down their record, and the wardens rarely refuse a sponsor strong enough. If the wardens approve and the aspirant chooses to go on, prepare them in the Preparation Chambers and open the Gate in the Gate Chamber. The aspirant passes through alone; companions wait in the Supplicants' Quarters. Beyond the Gate is the realm of the Lady of Blood, where a Fiend of the Blood waits: the Hunger with a mind. Make the trial a real fight the aspirant must win in their own way and finish by drinking the Fiend's blood. Do not resolve it for them, and say plainly that those who fail do not return. Wardens stand ready in case something tries to come back through.

blood_capture_lord_of_the_blood.name: blood_capture_lord_of_the_blood

effects.instruction: The new lord comes back through the Gate changed, and every warden and envoy in the fortress knows it at once. Under the truce, the houses must now treat them as a Lord of the Blood: a rival, a neighbor, and a permanent fact. A lord holds a valley. The Vale Sable has had no lord since House Sable fed without limit and fell; whoever holds the claim to it, and what happens to Nerisse Setharis somewhere inside Keep Sable, will decide who can take it. Let the sponsor, Lady Isaveau if it was her, say what she expects in return, and let the new lord answer in their own way.

effects.text: Decide what kind of lord to be, and which valley to hold.

conditions.query: A member of the party asks to sign the Crimson Company's writ, join the Company, or take its pay as a Hired Blade.

effects.instruction: An officer of the Crimson Company, Osric Kestrand if he is present, puts the writ in front of the character who asked. The terms are plain: armed passage in the lit valleys, a bed in the Red House, the work board, good pay counted in florins, and work that is hard and dangerous. Nothing counts until an officer hears the account at a Company hall. If they sign, they are a Hired Blade from this moment, and the hall treats them as one of its own, useful and watched.

tavern_company_work_request.script:
storage.companyOfferOpen = true
const stage = storage.companyStage || 'new_house'
const scope = stage === 'new_house' ? 'small, local, and reasonable for a new field company' : stage === 'known' ? 'substantial local work with clear stakes and a useful reward' : stage === 'established' ? 'difficult work from serious clients, potentially crossing the region or involving factions' : 'a consequential regional commission worthy of a renowned company'
effects.push({ type: 'story', instruction: 'At the company’s home tavern, have the keeper introduce one named external client or present one request left by a named petitioner. The job must be ' + scope + '. Give a specific place, active problem, threatened or interested people, what is known, what successful completion means, and concrete offered payment or access. Make it field adventure, investigation, rescue, escort, recovery, diplomacy under pressure, or dangerous opportunity, not pouring drinks, repairs, supplies, accounting, or routine tavern management. The company may question, negotiate, accept, or refuse. Present only one offer and do not treat it as accepted.' })

const pool = [["Ardan's Watch", "The Fist & Flagon"], ["Beggarsbridge", "The Waterline Inn"], ["Canopy", "The Silver Bough"], ["Coriva", "The Harpoon House"], ["Dun Solas", "The Wetted Whistle"], ["Freehaven", "The Above Board"], ["Gavarra", "Brightlights"], ["Gorren Crossing", "The Hearthstone"], ["Greenmeadow", "The Golden Grain"], ["Maanvalta", "The Hang-Over Inn"], ["Fallsmeet", "The White Wheel"], ["Tevantia", "The Two Swords"], ["The Crossroads Inn", "Taproom"]]

  storage.tavernReopeningInitDone = true
