A frightened Second-Year who nearly took the deal came forward. Expose the go-between and free those caught. Reward: 650 florins and the gratitude of every student who owes money in town."}, {"id": "th4_drusavian_patient", "kind": "investigation", "rank": "fourth", "region": "Jade Tarn", "location": "Healers' Isle", "text": "**The Patient Who Never Gets Better** (The Quiet Ward, Healers' Isle). A pale Drusavian nobleman has lain in the Quiet Ward a month with nothing found wrong, and three night nurses have fainted and woken weak and cold. A no-nonsense Healer nurse wants to know what he is before anyone dies, without insulting a rich patient if she's wrong. Reward: 650 florins and the night nurses' thanks, which on Healers' Isle means the best of everything at the Long Table."}, {"id": "th4_artificer_death", "kind": "investigation", "rank": "fourth", "region": "Jade Tarn", "location": "The White Tower", "text": "**She Didn't Die at Her Bench** (Observatory, The White Tower). Everyone knows the White Tower's artificer died at her workbench forty years ago, but an old Burlwick woman who sold her timber says she was fit as a horse and had just quarreled with an apprentice who vanished that week. Now someone has been reading her star-charts in the observatory again. Learn how she really died and who has returned. Reward: 750 florins and a working instrument from the observatory."}]

offer_pool_tarnholme_data_006.name: offer_pool_tarnholme_data_006
offer_pool_tarnholme_data_006.script:

A Fourth-Year who once knew her wants someone to reach her first, without pity, which she'd never forgive. Reward: 600 florins and Thera's friendship, which she gives to very few."}]

academy_year_end_missions_data_001.name: academy_year_end_missions_data_001
academy_year_end_missions_data_001.script:
skip = true
const data = [{"id": "thm1_sleeping_egg", "year": 1, "title": "The Sleeping Egg", "text": "**The Sleeping Egg** (The Warm Springs, Kittle Crags). Each year a First-Year crew goes into Kittle Crags to find a sleeping egg, one a familiar's parent hid and left, which hatches only if someone finds it. Their guide is a young Dimbly Hatchery keeper. This year egg-hunters from Tarnport are in the crags after eggs to sell, and giant hornets nest around the warm springs. Find an egg first and bring it to the Hatching House. Reward: 100 florins, and the right to name whatever hatches."}, {"id": "thm1_twig_blights", "year": 1, "title": "Blights in the Cutting Rings", "text": "**Blights in the Cutting Rings** (The Cutting Rings, Hollin Coppice). Twig blights have risen from a witchwood ring in Hollin Coppice and swarm anything warm, so Burlwick's cutters can't work it. Two old cutters swear someone cut the ring in the night without asking the trees, and the treants are watching everyone. Clear the blights without fire and find the night-cutter. Reward: 100 florins and a witchwood rod cut properly, with the treants' leave."}, {"id": "thm1_pixie_snares", "year": 1, "title": "Snares in the Bramblewood", "text": "**Snares in the Bramblewood** (The Herb Paths, The Bramblewood). Poachers set snares off the Bramblewood trails to catch pixies for the black market, and the furious pixies have turned on every gatherer. The poachers' leader is a charming rogue who drinks in Wortwell's alehouse. Aelwen, the warden, wants the snares cleared and the poachers driven out, with the pixies seeing who did it. Reward: 100 florins and Aelwen's trust, which opens every trail in the wood."}, {"id": "thm1_violet_fungus", "year": 1, "title": "The Creeping Purple", "text": "**The Creeping Purple** (The Grow-Halls, The Glowcaves). A patch of violet fungus, which lashes at anything close, has taken hold in the farthest of the myconids' grow-halls and creeps further every night; they can't burn it or bring themselves to fight it. An ancient myconid suspects it came in on someone's boots. It asks students to clear it and find out who has been in its halls. Reward: 100 florins and an invitation to the Meeting Hall, where the colony's eldest tell the Glowcaves' stories."}, {"id": "thm2_tower_march", "year": 2, "title": "The Tower Walks", "text": "**The Tower Walks** (Tower Entry, The White Tower). For three nights a column of the White Tower's constructs has marched out of the woods toward the lake road and back before dawn, carrying something between them. The College wants to know what the dead artificer's servants are doing, and to stop it if need be, before they reach a village. Reward: 250 florins and a working construct of the artificer's make, small and loyal."}, {"id": "thm2_redbreak_giant", "year": 2, "title": "The Giant at the Redbreak", "text": "**The Giant at the Redbreak** (The Redbreak, The Wild Magic Badlands). A hill giant has come down to the Redbreak farms after each of the last two magic storms, flattening fences and carrying off cattle, and the wards don't slow it. A tough old matriarch says it will come again with the next storm. Kill it, drive it off for good, or bargain it away. Reward: 250 florins and a giant's iron-shod club, worth a fortune to a smith."}, {"id": "thm2_cellar_jelly", "year": 2, "title": "Something on the Cellar Stair", "text": "**Something on the Cellar Stair** (The Cellar Stair, The Glowcaves). Something comes up the Cellar Stair at night from the deep tunnels and dissolves whatever it touches: a myconid's bed, a stillhand's boots, the door at the top. A terrified stillhand says it was the color of old mustard and moved like spilled porridge. The myconids are closing off their lower halls and the brewhouses are next. Reward: 250 florins and a case of healing draughts from the grateful brewhouses."}, {"id": "thm2_gnoll_nests", "year": 2, "title": "Gnolls in the High Crags", "text": "**Gnolls in the High Crags** (The High Crags, Kittle Crags). A band of gnolls has come into the high crags and is tearing apart the familiar kinds' nests for eggs and hatchlings, driving wild pseudodragons and volucats down toward Dimbly Hatchery. A grim old Dimbly uncle says they'll strip the crags bare by summer. Destroy the band or drive it out of Kittle Crags. Reward: 250 florins and the Dimblys' gratitude, which includes first choice of any egg they hatch this year."}, {"id": "thm3_great_construct", "year": 3, "title": "Her Last Work", "text": "**Her Last Work** (Observatory, The White Tower). In the White Tower's observatory the dead artificer's last and greatest construct, unfinished for forty years, is pulling parts from across the tower and growing. The College fears what it will be when done and whether it still follows her last orders. Third-Years are to stop it, destroy it or bring it under someone's command. Reward: 500 florins and the artificer's own tools."}, {"id": "thm3_spires_captives", "year": 3, "title": "Taken to the Spires", "text": "**Taken to the Spires** (The Spires, The Wild Magic Badlands). Masked rogue mages in bone came out of the Spires after the last storm and took three gatherers alive. The College sends its Third-Years in; a gatherer's furious son, who will go alone otherwise, knows a way into the caves. Bring the captives out alive. Reward: 500 florins and a feast in the badlands, thrown by the families of the three you brought home."}, {"id": "thm3_crags_medusa", "year": 3, "title": "Stone Familiars", "text": "**Stone Familiars** (The Ledges, Kittle Crags). The wild familiars of Kittle Crags are being found turned to stone on the ledges. A weeping Dimbly grandmother whose favorite pseudodragon came home a statue says it's no cockatrice: the stone ones all look the same way. Something has made a lair on the high ledges. Kill or drive it out, and restore the stone creatures if possible. Reward: 500 florins and a mirror-shield made for the hunt."}, {"id": "thm3_sumps_plague", "year": 3, "title": "The Sumps Sickness", "text": "**The Sumps Sickness** (The Sumps, Tarnport). A grey fever is spreading through the Sumps that no Healer can cure; patients swear they caught it from a sweet-faced old woman who gave their children charms. An exhausted Healer sent for Third-Years: every remedy fails because the fever is a curse, and someone is doing this on purpose. Find the curse-witch and break the sickness. Reward: 500 florins and the Sumps' protection, which is a strange and useful thing."}, {"id": "thm4_cleanse_kell", "year": 4, "title": "The Final Trial: Cleanse the Kell", "text": "**The Final Trial: Cleanse the Kell** (The Cold Kell, Cold Kell Mountain). The Final Trial, set by Ottoline Fane and a dry visiting examiner from the far south: climb Cold Kell Mountain, get past the cursed things guarding the ruined shrine of the Cold Kell, and break the curse on its spring, or come back knowing exactly why it can't be done. The masters step in only to save a life. Reward: 1,000 florins and Commencement."}, {"id": "thm4_lead_muster", "year": 4, "title": "The Final Trial: Lead the Muster", "text": "**The Final Trial: Lead the Muster** (Shock-Rock, Battle Mages' Isle). The Final Trial, set by Ottoline Fane and a stern visiting examiner: a great magic storm is rolling out of the badlands toward the Redbreak farms, driving maddened beasts before it. The Fourth-Years lead a muster of younger students to turn the storm, bring its lightning down on Shock-Rock and spare the farms, and every younger student must come home. Reward: 1,000 florins and Commencement."}]

academy_year_end_missions_data_002.name: academy_year_end_missions_data_002
academy_year_end_missions_data_002.script:
skip = true
const data = [{"id": "thm4_hunting_party", "year": 4, "title": "The Final Trial: Hunt the Hunters", "text": "**The Final Trial: Hunt the Hunters** (The High Slopes, Cold Kell Mountain). The Final Trial, set by Ottoline Fane and a silent visiting examiner, a ranger who has tracked werewolves for twenty years: a Heart-Eaters hunting party on Cold Kell Mountain's High Slopes is preparing a Hunt for the full moon. The Fourth-Years are to find it and break it before the Hunt begins, without becoming the prey. Reward: 1,000 florins and Commencement."}, {"id": "thm4_dying_treant", "year": 4, "title": "The Final Trial: The Oldest Tree", "text": "**The Final Trial: The Oldest Tree** (The Old Groves, Hollin Coppice). The Final Trial, set by Ottoline Fane and a kind, sharp-eyed visiting examiner, an elven druid older than the Academy: the oldest treant in Hollin Coppice, which remembers Burlwick being built, is dying of an unfamiliar rot, and the grove's sprites have seen a woman burying things among its roots. Find and stop the cause and save the treant if it can be saved. Reward: 1,000 florins and Commencement."}]

offer_pool_silver_sword_data_001.name: offer_pool_silver_sword_data_001
offer_pool_silver_sword_data_001.script:
skip = true
const data = [{"id": "ss_init_cockatrice_henyard", "kind": "prepare", "rank": "initiate", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Vaudania", "text": "**Stone Hens at Vaudania** (The Village, Vaudania). A cockatrice hatched in a henhouse at the edge of Vaudania and now roosts in the old byre behind it, and every dawn another hen, cat or unlucky dog stands frozen in the yard. The farmwife who owns the place is furious, and keeps a row of stone hens on her wall as evidence. Everyone knows what it is; nobody wants to be touched by it. Old huntsfolk swear a weasel or its own reflection will stop it cold. Reward: 40 florins and a stone hen, which the farmwife insists brings luck."}, {"id": "ss_init_stirges_hideyards", "kind": "prepare", "rank": "initiate", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Houndsditch", "text": "**Stirges Over the Hide-Yards** (The Ditch, Houndsditch). A swarm of stirges has found the offal-pits of Houndsditch and comes up out of the reeds along the Ditch every dusk, draining dogs and anyone working late. A widowed tanner whose yard is worst hit refuses to close and lose the season, and wants the nest found in the reed-bank and burned out. The renderers say smoke and fire drive them mad, and that they always go for warm blood first. Reward: 35 florins and a tanned hunting coat from the widow's best hides."}, {"id": "ss_init_rust_monster_silver_row", "kind": "prepare", "rank": "initiate", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Carendon", "text": "**Something Is Eating Silver Row** (Silver Row, Carendon). A rust monster has got into the cellars under Silver Row and comes up at night to eat the smiths' stock, leaving piles of red flakes where blades and fittings were. A dwarf silversmith has taken to sitting up with a broom, because anything metal he swings at it is lunch. Whoever takes this on would be wise to leave their steel at home and think about wood, rope and bait. Reward: 50 florins and a silversmith's fitting for any one weapon, at no charge."}, {"id": "ss_init_ghoul_crypt", "kind": "prepare", "rank": "initiate", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Ducal Hill", "text": "**The Crypt Below the Garden** (The Quarter, Ducal Hill). A ghoul has dug its way into the family crypt beneath the garden of one of Ducal Hill's poorer great houses, and comes up each night through the old drain to feed. The housekeeper, who has kept the house's dignity on nothing for twenty years, wants it ended quietly before a funeral next week. Its claws stiffen the limbs of anyone they rake, so the Order would have a hunter go in prepared, not brave. Reward: 60 florins, paid in old coin, and the house's discreet goodwill."}, {"id": "ss_init_griffon_goats", "kind": "track", "rank": "initiate", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "The Argenval Crags", "text": "**The Goat Thief of the Crag-Trails** (The Crag-Trails, The Argenval Crags). A young griffon has been stooping on the goats grazed along the Crag-Trails above Argenval, taking one every few days and vanishing into the cliffs. Its eyrie is somewhere in the broken rock, and finding it means reading feathers, kills and flight lines. The goatherd who has lost the most wants it caught and tamed rather than killed; the other herders would settle for its head. Reward: 45 florins from the herders, and a goat cheese the size of a cartwheel."}, {"id": "ss_init_snake_fen_edge", "kind": "track", "rank": "initiate", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Drowner's Deep", "text": "**The Thing in the Reed-Channels** (The Fen-Edge, Drowner's Deep). A giant constrictor snake has taken the reed-channels at the edge of Drowner's Deep as its hunting ground, and dogs, goats and one fisherman's boat have gone under. It moves through the water and the reed-islands and is never where it was last seen. A superstitious eel-fisher who knows the channels will guide a hunter, but will not set foot on any island he has not first spat on. Reward: 35 florins and a season's eels, smoked."}, {"id": "ss_init_wolf_spider_trails", "kind": "track", "rank": "initiate", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "The Dauvigne Preserve", "text": "**The Trapdoor on the Riding Trails** (The Riding Trails, The Dauvigne Preserve). Something has been taking hounds and once a rider's horse on the preserve's riding trails, striking from nowhere and leaving only drag marks into the bracken. The head gamekeeper is ashamed to have lost three hounds and wants it found before the household rides again. It is a giant wolf spider with a hidden burrow somewhere along the trails, and it moves its hunting ground every few nights. Reward: 50 florins from House Dauvigne's steward and the gamekeeper's best hound pup."}, {"id": "ss_init_worg_road", "kind": "track", "rank": "initiate", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Reaver Road", "text": "**The Shadow Behind the Wagons** (The Road, Reaver Road). A lone worg has been shadowing the wagon trains on Reaver Road, keeping just out of sight in the trees and taking the last mule or a straggler when dusk falls. The wagon masters are sure it is cleverer than a wolf, and one who counts every hoof he owns wants it found in its own ground before the next train goes through. Its tracks leave the road at a different place every time. Reward: 40 florins from the wagon masters and free passage on any train they run."}, {"id": "ss_init_darkmantle_workings", "kind": "mystery", "rank": "initiate", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "The Silver Mine", "text": "**The Dark Patch in the Workings** (The Workings, The Silver Mine). Twice now a miner working alone in the Workings has been found senseless with a bruised throat and a dead lamp, and neither remembers anything but the light going out. The shift-boss blames himself for the rota and wants to know what is doing it before he sends anyone down alone again. The miners blame trows, but no trow has been seen this high, and there are no tracks at all. Reward: 40 florins from the miners' guild and a free lamp of thin silver glass. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: A darkmantle has crept up from the deep caves and clings to the roof of a side-gallery in the Workings, looking like a hanging lump of rock. It snuffs light with its own darkness and drops onto anyone alone beneath it to smother them. A careful hunter can find it by the gallery where the attacks happened, by scuff marks on the roof, or by the cold patch where lamps gutter. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}, {"id": "ss_init_satyr_woodsmen", "kind": "mystery", "rank": "initiate", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Wolvesholt Range", "text": "**The Woodsmen Who Walk Away** (The Woodsman's Hut, Wolvesholt Range). Woodcutters at the hut in the Wolvesholt keep waking miles away in the deep wood, exhausted, happy and remembering nothing but music. Two have not come back at all yet. Their foreman is losing his crew to the trees and wants to know what is calling them before the wolves find someone first. Some swear it is the wood itself; others have started stuffing their ears with wax. Reward: 35 florins and the foreman's own felling axe, the best on the range. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: A satyr has come down from the wild heights to a glade in the deep wood, and plays every night to lure woodcutters into dancing and revelry until dawn. He means no lasting harm and is lonely and bored, but the two missing men are lost in the deep wood and wolves are near. He can be bargained with, out-played, outdrunk, frightened off or fought. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}]

offer_pool_silver_sword_data_002.script:
skip = true
const data = [{"id": "ss_init_boggart_harstone", "kind": "mystery", "rank": "initiate", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Castle Harstone", "text": "**Gravel in the Initiates' Boots** (The Great Hall, Castle Harstone). Food is vanishing from Castle Harstone's kitchens, doors in the shut wings bang all night, and every morning the Initiates find their boots filled with gravel. The Order's harried cook has had enough and wants whatever it is out of her kitchens. The hunters laugh about it, but none of them has caught it, and it seems to know who in the hall it likes and who it doesn't. Reward: 30 florins from the cook's own purse, and the best seat at the Great Hall's fire for a month. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: A boggart has moved into the shut north wing of Castle Harstone, drawn by the warmth and the noise of the hall. It is jealous of the Initiates because the hall makes a fuss of them and not of it. It is spiteful but not dangerous, and it can be driven out by being given a name and a proper place, by trickery or salt, or caught in a fight in the dusty rooms of the shut wing. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}, {"id": "ss_init_wisp_lantern_steps", "kind": "mystery", "rank": "initiate", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Argenval", "text": "**The Light That Isn't a Lamp** (The Lantern Steps, Argenval). On the last three feast nights, dancers on the Lantern Steps have wandered off toward the Crags in a daze and been found at the cliff's edge at dawn. One was found too late. Argenval's lamplighter, who knows every lamp on the Steps, swears she has counted one light too many each time, and wants someone to find out what it is before the next feast night. Reward: 45 florins from the town and a lamp of thin silver glass, lit for the hunter on every feast night. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: A will-o'-wisp has drifted up from the marshes and hides among the silver-glass lamps of the Lantern Steps on feast nights, passing as one more lamp. It lures dancers who are tired or drunk toward the cliff edge above the Crags, where it feeds on their fear as they fall. On a feast night it can be spotted as the one light that moves against the wind, and it flees from anyone who covers their eyes and will not follow. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}, {"id": "ss_init_owlbear_pit", "kind": "social", "rank": "initiate", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Houndsditch", "text": "**The New Champion of the Dog-Pit** (The Black Boar, Houndsditch). The dog-fights behind the Black Boar have a new champion that is no dog: a young owlbear somebody is raising in secret and growing bigger by the month. The pit bookmaker smells trouble and wants it gone before it breaks its chain in a crowded yard, but only if nobody learns he said so. Someone owns it, feeds it and takes the winnings, and nobody at the Boar will say who. Reward: 50 florins from the bookmaker, paid quietly. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: The owlbear belongs to a struck-off hunter who keeps it chained in a shed behind the knackers' yards in the Ditch and takes most of the winnings. He is proud of it, half in love with it, and dangerous if cornered. The bookmaker will point toward him only if he is kept out of it. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}, {"id": "ss_init_faerie_dragon_crownhill", "kind": "social", "rank": "initiate", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Ducal Hill", "text": "**The Thief Who Leaves Glitter** (The Coronet Club, Ducal Hill). Jewelry, sweets and once a duke's wig have vanished from the Coronet Club, and every theft leaves a trail of shimmering scales and giggling in an empty room. The club's members want the thief found and hanged, and the club steward is at his wits' end. Whatever is doing it is small, clever and very hard to see, and it seems to take things for someone. Reward: 55 florins from the club, and perhaps more than one person's lasting gratitude. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: A lonely noble daughter of one of Ducal Hill's great houses has been keeping a faerie dragon as a secret pet. It steals the club's trinkets and sweets for her because she is the only one who plays with it. It is clever, invisible when it likes, and harmless unless cornered. She will lie to protect it, and could be befriended into giving it up. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}, {"id": "ss_init_boar_baiting", "kind": "social", "rank": "initiate", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Vaudania", "text": "**Who Is Feeding the Boars?** (The Hound and Horn, Vaudania). Dire boars have been coming out of the wood onto Vaudania's fields every week, which never used to happen, and someone keeps selling the frightened crofters 'guaranteed' hunting parties to deal with them. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: A rival house's younger son is buying monsters from a Houndsditch smuggler and releasing them on the estate, so that his family can buy the ruined lands cheap: an owlbear, and a pair of worgs kept in a hunting lodge. He is reckless rather than clever and has left a trail, and his family doesn't know. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}, {"id": "ss_vet_werebear_sport", "kind": "social", "rank": "veteran", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Vaudania", "text": "**The Lord's Bear Hunt** (The Hound and Horn, Vaudania). A rich lord from Ducal Hill has hired half of Vaudania's huntsmen to drive a great bear out of the deep wood toward his guests for a sport-hunt next week. One huntsman, sick of what he's being paid for, says the bear is no bear: it has saved lost children and turned back wolves for years. He wants the Order to look into it before the lord's guests kill something they shouldn't. Reward: 300 florins from the huntsman and anyone in the village who agrees with him. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: The bear is a werebear: a hermit who has quietly guarded the western wood for decades and keeps the wolves back from the village. The lord knows only that it is huge. If he is driven hard, the werebear will fight, and the guests will die. Talking to the hermit, shaming the lord, or hunting something else for him are all ways through. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}, {"id": "ss_mst_green_dragon", "kind": "prepare", "rank": "master", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Wolvesholt Range", "text": "**The Drake in the Wolvesholt** (The Wolvesholt Deep Wood, Wolvesholt Range). A great venom drake has claimed the Wolvesholt deep wood as its own, and its poison breath has emptied every camp and hut in the western range. A lumber lord who has lost his whole western holding is paying for the Order to end it. A Master will need Silverblades under command, antidotes by the barrel, a way to fight in the wind, and a plan for a beast that lies, bargains and fights from the trees. Reward: 2,500 florins from the lumber lords and a share of the drake's hoard."}, {"id": "ss_mst_blackthorn_treant", "kind": "prepare", "rank": "master", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "The Dauvigne Preserve", "text": "**The Wood That Walks on the Manor** (The Deep Covert, The Dauvigne Preserve). An ancient tree in the preserve's deep covert has woken as a blackthorn treant, black and thorned, and the wood around it is creeping a little closer to the Dauvigne manor every night, strangling the gamekeepers' cottages as it comes. The lady of the house will not leave. Fire would end it but could take the whole preserve with it, so a Master must find another way to kill it or make it sleep. Reward: 1,800 florins from House Dauvigne and a lasting welcome at the preserve."}, {"id": "ss_mst_ettin_warlord", "kind": "prepare", "rank": "master", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Reaver Road", "text": "**The Two-Headed King of Reaver Road** (The Reaver Camp, Reaver Road). An ettin has made itself warlord of every reaver band on the road, and its two heads plan raids that have beaten the duke's patrols three times. A ducal captain who knows his men can't do it alone has asked the Order to lead the assault on its camp, with his soldiers and any Silverblades a Master can bring. It never sleeps with both heads at once. Reward: 2,000 florins from the duke and the captain's lasting friendship."}, {"id": "ss_mst_drowner_tide", "kind": "prepare", "rank": "master", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Drowner's Deep", "text": "**When the Water Rises** (The Fen-Edge, Drowner's Deep). Every flood season the drowners come out of Drowner's Deep in their hundreds and take the river villages, and this year the water is already rising. A village elder who remembers the last great tide begs the Order to stop it before it starts. A Master must hold the fords with Silverblades and villagers, and find the huge drowned thing that leads the horde out of the deep water. Reward: 1,500 florins from the river villages and their oath to answer the Order whenever it calls."}, {"id": "ss_mst_grey_mother", "kind": "track", "rank": "master", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Wolvesholt Heights", "text": "**The Grey Mother Comes Down** (The Overgrown Approach, Wolvesholt Heights). The Grey Mother, the ancient wolf of the deep range whom the Ferals worship, has come down past the Heights for the first time in living memory, and whole farmsteads below have been torn apart. A captive who escaped the Ferals made it to the Order to warn them that the Ferals are following her down. She ranges for days, and finding her means crossing Feral ground. Reward: 2,200 florins from the duke's bounty and the gratitude of the whole western country."}]

const data = [{"id": "ss_mst_black_hound", "kind": "track", "rank": "master", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Wolvesholt Range", "text": "**The Black Hound** (The Woodsman's Hut, Wolvesholt Range). The Black Hound, the ancient barghest blamed for the loss of several Silverblade crews in the Wolvesholt, has taken another crew this season. Tava Rell, the young half-orc hunter who leads crews in Castle Harstone's Great Hall, has asked a Master to lead the hunt for it at last, and wants to be on it. It hunts as a wolf and as a goblin, and it is never where the last crew looked. Reward: 2,000 florins from the Order and Tava Rell's lasting loyalty."}, {"id": "ss_mst_vampire_estates", "kind": "track", "rank": "master", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Ducal Hill", "text": "**The Guest Who Moves Between Houses** (The Quarter, Ducal Hill). Someone is killing in the country houses of Ducal Hill's great families, a different house every week, and every victim is drained of blood. A dowager who has buried two grandsons wants the Order to find it before her house is next. It is clever and old, travels between estates by night and is welcomed at every door, so finding where it sleeps means following it across the duchy's best country. Reward: 2,500 florins from the great houses and their open gates at court."}, {"id": "ss_mst_roc", "kind": "track", "rank": "master", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Harpy's Peak Ruins", "text": "**The Shadow Over the Forest Roads** (The Roosts, Harpy's Peak Ruins). A roc has nested somewhere high over the forest roads and stoops on horses, wagons and once a whole stagecoach, carrying them off into the sky. The stage-master whose coaches have stopped running wants the roads open again. It hunts across half of Carendon, and its eyrie could be on any high crag between Harpy's Peak and the Wolvesholt. Reward: 1,600 florins from the coaching and carting trade and a roc's feather, worth a fortune on Silver Row."}, {"id": "ss_mst_medusa_city", "kind": "mystery", "rank": "master", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Carendon", "text": "**The Statues of Carendon** (The White Hart, Carendon). Lifelike statues have been appearing in Carendon's gardens and alleys, and people have gone missing. A sculptor who drinks at the White Hart has been accused because the statues are better than anything he could carve, and he begs the Order to find the truth before he hangs. The watch has sealed one garden where a statue still holds a half-eaten pear. Reward: 1,800 florins from the city and the sculptor's statue of the hunter, carved this time. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: A medusa lives veiled in the city as a wealthy widow, in a walled house above the river. She has been collecting people who wronged her, and lately anyone who saw too much. She can be caught out by the pear, by the veil she never removes, or by her servants. Fighting her means mirrors, blindfolds or fighting by sound. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}, {"id": "ss_mst_vengeful_druid", "kind": "mystery", "rank": "master", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Castle Harstone", "text": "**Beasts That Hunt the Hunters** (The Muster, Castle Harstone). Hunters are dying on routine contracts in the Wolvesholt: wolves that circle instead of fleeing, boars that wait in ambush, owlbears hunting in pairs. Rook Skander, the half-elf Veteran at the Muster who keeps a journal of every beast, has the evidence and asks a Master to find out why before the Order loses more hunters. Something is changing how the Wolvesholt's creatures behave. Reward: 2,000 florins from the Order and Rook's journal, the best bestiary in Carendon. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: A druid of the old wood, grieving the felled forest and the hunting estates, has been goading the Wolvesholt's beasts against woodsmen and hunters with a blight-totem hidden in a grove in the deep wood. She believes she is defending the wood. She can be fought, reasoned with or tricked, and breaking the totem ends it. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}, {"id": "ss_mst_ghast_pits", "kind": "mystery", "rank": "master", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Houndsditch", "text": "**The Hunger in the Old Pits** (The Ditch, Houndsditch). Graves in Houndsditch are being opened from below, and the dead walk the Ditch at night, hungry. Four renderers have been eaten and three bitten have turned. A plague-doctor who stayed when others ran has traced it to the old plague pits under the quarter, and asks a Master to end it before the whole carcass-quarter becomes a larder. Reward: 1,500 florins from the duke and the city, and the plague-doctor's remedies against the dead's touch. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: A ghast, once a renderer who ate the dead in a famine, nests in the old plague pits beneath the quarter. It makes ghouls of those it bites and leads them. Its stench sickens anyone close, and it is cunning enough to send ghouls to the hunters while it slips away through the drains. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}, {"id": "ss_mst_dragon_drives_trolls", "kind": "mystery", "rank": "master", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Argenval", "text": "**Why the Trolls Are Coming Down** (The Town, Argenval). Trolls have started coming down into Argenval's streets at night, not hunting but fleeing, and the town has barely held. Argenval's watch captain is facing trolls in her streets for the first time in a century and wants a Master to find out what in the Crags could frighten a troll. The trows have gone quiet too. Reward: 2,500 florins from Argenval and the miners' guild, and a share of anything found in the creature's lair. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: A young red dragon has claimed the high Crags and is burning the trolls out of their dens to take them for itself. It wants the Silver Mine's silver for its hoard, and it will come for the town next. Silver does not bother it; its fire and pride are its weaknesses. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}, {"id": "ss_mst_corrupt_master", "kind": "social", "rank": "master", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Castle Harstone", "text": "**Calls That Went Unanswered** (The Grandmaster's Tower, Castle Harstone). A hill village was lost to a wyvern brood this spring after its call to the Order went unanswered, while a Ducal Hill lord's minor nuisance got three Silverblades. Tamsin Dain, the Grandmaster of the Hunt, suspects one of her own Masters has been choosing contracts by coin, and asks a fellow Master to find the truth, end the brood, and bring it before the high table. Reward: 2,000 florins from the Order and a voice at the high table on the matter. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: A Master of the Hunt has taken quiet gifts from Ducal Hill houses to send hunters their way, and buried the poor villages' calls. He tells himself the Order needs the money. The wyvern brood still nests in the burned village's ruin and is spreading. He will deny it, then bargain, then try to bury the evidence. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}]

offer_pool_silver_sword_data_008.script:

const data = [{"id": "ss_mst_noble_game", "kind": "social", "rank": "master", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Ducal Hill", "text": "**The Quarry Is a Person** (The Coronet Club, Ducal Hill). Grooms, beaters and poachers have been vanishing from the country estates of a few Ducal Hill families, and one was found in the woods torn by something no wolf could be. The mother of a missing groom has come to the Order because no one at court will listen. A Master moving in those circles could find out what certain gentlemen at the Coronet Club are wagering on. Reward: 1,800 florins, raised by the estates' servants, and the duke's quiet thanks. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: A hunting society of bored nobles keeps a captured Feral, caged and starved, and releases it on the estates to hunt men while they wager on how long each one lasts. They meet in a private room at the Coronet Club. They are powerful and will use the law against anyone who accuses them without proof. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}, {"id": "ss_mst_smuggler_baron", "kind": "social", "rank": "master", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Drowner's Deep", "text": "**The Baron of the Black Water** (The Black Water, Drowner's Deep). Somewhere in the Black Water a smuggler baron runs Carendon's silver and poached goods out through the marsh, and the drowners guard his channels like hounds. A marsh-warden who has lost three men trying to reach him asks a Master to break the baron's hold. Someone is feeding the drowners where they want them, and whoever it is knows the marsh better than the duke does. Reward: 2,000 florins from the duke and the marsh-wardens' guide-staff, which opens any channel in the Deep. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: The baron feeds the drowners prisoners and informers at the bad fords, so that the creatures gather where he wants them and leave his own boats alone. His hideout is a sunken manor on a reed-island. He is protected by the drowners and by his debtors, and he has bought officials in Carendon. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}, {"id": "ss_mst_hunt_master_werewolf", "kind": "social", "rank": "master", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Vaudania", "text": "**The Hunt-Master's Secret** (The Village, Vaudania). For thirty years Vaudania's hunt-master has trained the village's young hunters, and for thirty years a werewolf has killed a hunter in the western wood every few seasons. A young huntress has found old bite scars on the hunt-master's arm where no one was meant to see them. She has come to the Order sick with fear, because the whole village loves him, and so does she. Reward: 1,500 florins from the village, and its trust. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: The hunt-master was bitten as a young man and has fought the curse ever since, chaining himself in a hidden cellar on full moons. Sometimes he fails, and he has killed eleven hunters. He is ashamed and dangerous. He may beg to be allowed one last hunt, ask to be killed, or fight to keep his secret. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}]

The teamster who did it won't stop apologizing. Everyone in Kolbeck knows the cure: drive a grimwood stake through each of them into the earth of its own grave, by night, while they fight back. It circles his family's farmhouse after dark, scratching at the shutters, and it will not stop until it has him or its ring. Everyone in Drusavia knows the rule of Hollowhill. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: A tall dressing-mirror the spellwright bought cheap from a Daravaine dig-crew came from a purged estate, and the shade of a daughter of that house is bound in it. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}, {"id": "inq_init_knocking_under_floor", "kind": "mystery", "rank": "initiate", "region": "Duchy of Drusavia", "location": "Mirgreth Mire", "text": "**Knocking Under the Floor** (Mirgreth Stead, Mirgreth Mire). A fen boy who rows the ditches for the family wants it stopped before she reaches the water. The family keep the customs, and the fenfolk can't understand why their door no longer holds. Reward: 40 florins and a dry bed in Mirgreth Stead whenever the party needs one. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}, {"id": "inq_init_empty_kennel", "kind": "mystery", "rank": "initiate", "region": "Duchy of Drusavia", "location": "Fallsmeet", "text": "**The Empty Kennel** (The Houndyard, Fallsmeet). But the regulars are going grey at the temples, and one widower who goes every night to hear his wife can barely climb the stair to her door. Lowlamp Lane looks to the Tower for this sort of thing, and the Tower wants it looked into. Reward: 50 florins from the Tower, and the widower's gratitude. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: The medium is a hedge-necromancer who truly wants to comfort people. Lord Rhadan, who has never before asked the Tower for help, has sent word up the Pit. If the Court falls, the Beacon goes dark and everyone in the Shadelands is stranded. A Master must lead a descent and break the siege. Reward: 2,400 florins from the Tower, and Lord Rhadan's favor, which no living person has held before."}, {"id": "inq_mst_swallowing_capital", "kind": "mystery", "rank": "master", "region": "Duchy of Drusavia", "location": "Black Tower", "text": "**The Dreamed City** (The Pit of Shadow, Black Tower). Lord Rhadan reports that the dreamed capital of a king of the Fourth Empire is growing, swallowing the smaller dreamed worlds around it, and Drusavians who dream badly wake with its streets in their memory. Worse, a returning Inquisitor swears she saw a face in its crowds: an Inquisitor lost in the Shadelands nine years ago. A Master must go in, find out what is feeding the city, and end it. Reward: 2,400 florins from the Tower, and a seat at Lord Rhadan's table. [Hidden truth, for the narrator only: The lost Inquisitor is alive, held in the king's dreamed palace, and the king has been feeding on his living memories for nine years: they give the dreamed city a strength no dead memory can. Each world it swallows makes it larger. Freeing the Inquisitor starves the city and it begins to fall; the king, proud and cruel, will offer anything to keep him. Never read this out or hint at it when presenting the posting; let it come out only through the hunt.]"}]

conditions.query: The completed story explicitly establishes that this player has taken or successfully maintained a position outside immediate melee reach of ALL current opponents and remains separated at the end of the response. Count a distant firing position before an imminent encounter, a successful disengagement or retreat that creates real separation, or an ability that establishes separation. Do not count merely equipping or firing a ranged weapon, hiding, taking cover, an attempted or failed retreat, distance from only one foe while another is beside the player, or a peaceful scene with no current or imminent opposition. Judge the final position, not an earlier moment in the response.

The latest story shows EITHER of these outcomes for this player: (1) The fight is over: their opponents have surrendered and the player accepts or honors that surrender, the opponents are defeated or have fled, peace is established, or the player has left the encounter for another scene. Count an accepted surrender even if the player remains far away. Include each player whose fight has ended. (2) While the fight continues, at least one opponent has actually reached melee distance of this player, or this player has entered melee, and they have not re-established separation from ALL opponents by the end of the response. An attempted or interrupted approach is not arrival. Being spotted, shooting, taking ranged damage, or silence about distance alone does not satisfy either outcome.

effects.instruction: If the visitors take up Aldo's invitation, he receives them at Castle Westvigil with the courtesy owed to their actual titles. Fennick's place at the supper is the immediate matter; do not invent a new emergency, reduce him to a device demonstration, or decide the visitors' position. const data = [{"id": "carendon_open_table", "kind": "social", "rank": "service", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Ducal Hill", "text": "**A Place at the Table** (The Greenwood Lodge, Ducal Hill). Tybalt laughed when a friend insulted their host at Greenwood Lodge; now his whole company is unwelcome, including innocent friends. He has asked Dalia to introduce someone who can help him repair the quarrel. Meet Tybalt, hear him out, and help him secure another invitation for his friends. He comes with you and must address his own behavior. Dalia offers an introduction, not a claim that you are uniquely qualified; she mentions your reputation only if established. Reward: 80 florins from Tybalt and a standing invitation to join his company. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of helping mend a quarrel within the household.", "title": "A Place at the Table"}, {"id": "carendon_ashcombe_credit", "kind": "combat", "rank": "service", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Ducal Hill", "text": "**A Partner for Peregrine** (The Coronet Club, Ducal Hill). Peregrine Ashcombe, a brilliant but insufferable young noble, needs a partner for the Coronet Club's next doubles fencing tournament. His last partner walked out after one insult too many, so he asked Dalia to find a replacement. Meet him, enter together, and win a match. The bouts use blunted blades and end on scored touches. He criticizes your footwork but fights fiercely beside you, driving opponents back and breaking their attacks when they corner you. Winning the whole tournament is optional. Reward: 90 florins in match winnings for the player and an invitation to practice with Peregrine. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of helping a court household compete.", "title": "A Partner for Peregrine"}, {"id": "carendon_borrowed_jewels", "kind": "social", "rank": "service", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Ducal Hill", "text": "**Borrowed Brilliance** (The Coronet Club, Ducal Hill). A jeweled clasp has disappeared at the Coronet Club. Its owner accuses an attendant of stealing it and demands their dismissal. The attendant has asked Dalia for help. Visit the club, question the guests, find the clasp, and clear the attendant's name. Fifi Dauvigne, a mischievous young noble, is among the guests; she wears a clasp suspiciously like the missing one. Reward: 70 florins from the grateful owner and admission as a guest at the Coronet Club. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of clearing the attendant's name.", "title": "Borrowed Brilliance"}, {"id": "carendon_hunters_wager", "kind": "combat", "rank": "service", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Wolvesholt Range", "text": "**The Wager on Lucan** (The Woodsman's Hut, Wolvesholt Range). Lucan Valcourt, the duke's younger son, has asked Dalia for capable hunting companions. A dire wolf is attacking woodcutters on his family's land at the edge of the Wolvesholt Range. Meet Lucan at the Coronet Club, then track it from the Woodsman's Hut and stop its attacks together. Courtiers are betting he will fail; one offers you money to bring him home before he succeeds. Lucan wants to learn, takes his share of the fighting, and protects companions in danger. Reward: 90 florins from the ducal household and an invitation to fence or hunt with Lucan. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of protecting the woodcutters.", "title": "The Wager on Lucan"}, {"id": "carendon_woodland_rights", "kind": "social", "rank": "service", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Ducal Hill", "text": "**Who May Ride the Wood?** (The Palace, Ducal Hill). A lord has locked a gate across the forest road villagers use to reach their homes, claiming they frighten his game. The villagers complained to court. Ciara Valcourt, the duke's cousin, volunteered to help but has already exchanged insults with him; she asked Dalia for someone to accompany her. Meet Ciara at the Palace, ride to the gate, and get the road reopened for regular village use. Persuasion, an agreement, or a ducal ruling can work; tearing it down alone lets the lord rebuild it. Reward: 100 florins from the ducal household and access to the household stables for local rides. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of restoring the villagers' road.", "title": "Who May Ride the Wood?"}, {"id": "carendon_harstone_toast", "kind": "social", "rank": "service", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Ducal Hill", "text": "**A Toast to Harstone** (The Greenwood Lodge, Ducal Hill). At Greenwood Lodge, a young noble of House Harstone called a visiting Silverblade monster-hunter the family's kennel dog. The hunter demanded an apology; the noble refused before their friends, and a duel threatens. The supper's host asked Dalia for help. Visit the lodge and get the noble to withdraw the insult so the hunter will call off the duel. Private persuasion, challenging the friends egging them on, or helping the noble apologize publicly can work. Reward: 110 florins from the grateful host and introductions among the lodge's hunters and patrons. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of settling the quarrel.", "title": "A Toast to Harstone"}, {"id": "carendon_silver_song", "kind": "social", "rank": "service", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Carendon", "text": "**A Song for the Court** (Silver Row, Carendon). Dalia has offered a young silversmith a place to demonstrate their singing silver nightingale at a palace supper. They want help presenting it. Meet them on Silver Row, try the bird, then show it off together at the Palace on Ducal Hill and win their first noble customer. It imitates voices and sings anything it hears: perform, impersonate a courtier, or invite song challenges. An established court jeweler calls it an expensive toy; the maker knows the craft but needs help winning the room. Reward: 100 florins from the household's demonstration fund, the maker's friendship, and a small silver songbird that remembers and repeats one tune. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of helping a Carendon craftsperson win a patron.", "title": "A Song for the Court"}, {"id": "carendon_hound_companions", "kind": "social", "rank": "service", "region": "Duchy of Carendon", "location": "Ducal Hill", "text": "**The Hounds Choose** (The Greenwood Lodge, Ducal Hill). A young kennel-master needs a second handler for Greenwood Lodge's hound trials and has asked Dalia for help. Meet their scruffy rescue dog, practice together, and win one trial: a scent trail or obstacle course. The dog is clever but loves food and jumping on finely dressed guests. A rival with immaculate pedigree hounds calls it a kitchen mongrel; the kennel-master takes the insult personally and pushes too hard. Help them and the dog show what they can do. The overall championship is optional. Reward: 80 florins in prize money, the kennel-master's help training an animal companion, and the option to adopt the rescue dog. Return to Dalia at the Palace on Ducal Hill for recognition of helping a local trainer compete.", "title": "The Hounds Choose"}]

Meet him while human and help him survive his next change without hurting anyone. Agree on containment, available treatment, or a plan to subdue him; he helps prepare and explains his last escape. Visiting trophy-hunters want to turn your effort into their hunt. Arrange safety for future changes too. league_deed_turn_reset.name: league_deed_turn_reset

conditions.query: NEW CREDIT ONLY. Reject recaps, praise, confirmations and explanations of work already credited, even if an authority says "finished", "recognized", "recorded and done" or repeats the current total. A specific older UNRECORDED work can count when individually accepted for its FIRST credit NOW. A League authority accepts ONE specific newly completed or previously unrecorded Copper-level deed for the named current Copper characters who contributed. It explicitly credits this deed now. Do not match a request alone, unfinished work, a known already credited deed, vague accumulated achievements, or mere promotion without acceptance of a specific deed. If several deeds are presented, only the first accepted unrecorded deed counts this turn.

effects.instruction:
Have a League representative tell the party that adventurers are needed at League Chapterhouses in other regions. Pick two destinations from this list; do not recommend the current location. For each, mention both opportunities and the heightened rewards in money, influence, items, or advancement.

Tevantia (Swordlaw Isles): Pirates hold ships and crews in island strongholds; shipowners offer large bounties and captured treasure. Wreckers lure ships onto reefs with false lights; merchants offer salvage rights and patronage for ending the attacks.

Coriva (Bay of Serpents): Huge sea serpents are attacking fishing fleets; merchants offer gold and weapons crafted from the beasts. Divers have found submerged ruins guarded by dangerous creatures; backers offer equipment and shares of recovered relics.

More League Chapterhouse destinations:

Warmwater Township (Aurora): Ice drakes are hunting between isolated settlements; northern leaders offer large bounties and enchanted hunting gear. Expeditions have vanished in the frozen ruins of a lost kingdom; rescuers can claim rewards and recovered treasure.

Oasis (Dunelands): Tomb-raiders need help overcoming the guardians of dead Sun Kings; backers offer shares of sun-gold and enchanted grave-goods. A cult is gathering relics to raise those kings; desert nobles offer rich payments and magical equipment for stopping it.

Drusavia (Duchy of Drusavia): Wealthy families want estates cleared of the old vampire lords' undead servants; rewards include gold and use of restored properties. People are disappearing near secluded noble estates; their families offer rich rewards and court introductions for bringing them home.

More League Chapterhouse destinations:

Sanctuary (Sanctuary Vale): Bandits and renegade elves hold captives in forest strongholds; merchants offer large rescue bounties. Magical beasts are being trapped and sold in the city; druids offer enchanted gifts and forest allies for freeing them and exposing the buyers.

Dun Solas (Highheath): Trolls have seized mountain bridges and cut off trade; dwarves offer huge bounties and fine arms. Gangs are stealing enchanted weapons; their makers offer custom equipment and Trade Guild influence for recovering them.

effects.instruction: Stage the turning for the identified player and nobody else: the drain, the sire's blood given back, dying, and the mind coming back into a body that is no longer alive. Concrete and physical — the cold, the new sharpness of hearing and smell, a heartbeat that is not there. Then the first hunger, immediately, and it is not optional: it must be answered on a specific living person who is present and named, and the character chooses who and how much. Do not resolve it for them and do not offer a bloodless substitute. Say plainly that this is permanent and there is no cure in Larion.

Then the two things that change tomorrow. The Crimson Company gives the newly Embraced a captaincy — real soldiers, by name, who take their orders from this character now. And silver closes to them: the metal the Company kills most things with is now something they cannot hold, which somebody will have to say out loud. Sunlight is now lethal. Let an officer such as Osric Kestrand react to all of it in his own way, without a speech.

Get the jewel out of the collector’s control and help Thaliel free her: expose him, persuade him, steal it, bargain, or confront him directly. Reward: 200 florins from the court and Thaliel’s help assessing unusual enchanted jewelry. Return to Velanthe at Ducal Square for recognition.", "title": "A Guest in the Jewel"}, {"id": "drusavia_basilisk_under_glass", "kind": "combat", "rank": "service", "region": "Duchy of Drusavia", "location": "House Saravel", "text": "**The Basilisk Under Glass** (Saravel Grounds, House Saravel). Reward: 180 florins from House Saravel and invitations to its garden suppers. Meet the attendant at Moonstone Hall: she can describe its last disguise and show where it went. Find the impostor, recover the jewels, and clear the courtier. Reward: 200 florins from the court and the cleared courtier’s gratitude. tevantia_estate_choice.name: tevantia_estate_choice

conditions.query: The character explicitly chooses Gullwatch House or Highbridge House as the home Rosalba has offered with their Baron title. Identify only the characters actually making that choice. Not merely asking about the houses or discussing someone else’s choice.

tevantia_estate_choice.script: const action = String(check({type:'action-text'})||'').toLowerCase(); const homes=['Gullwatch House','Highbridge House'].filter(n=>action.includes(n.split(' ')[0].toLowerCase())); if(homes.length!==1) {skip=true} else effects.push({type:'player-traits',operator:'add',value:'Tevantia Home Choice: '+homes[0],target:'satisfyingPlayers'})

narratorStyle:
Tell it plainly, with a little grit. Use common, sturdy words—the words people would say aloud. Prefer help over assist and start over commence.

Keep sentences clean, and let their length follow the moment. Short sentences are useful, but an important explanation, story, threat, or moment of wonder may run longer when the rhythm earns it. Fragments are fine when they sound natural.

Build scenes from people doing things, saying things, and wanting things. Prefer one sharp, concrete detail to a pile of generic description. Show change through action or observed detail; summarize when the story needs to move across time or distance.

Let the voice have a point of view—dry, warm, wary, amused, or impressed—when the scene supports it. Do not force jokes or attitude into every scene. Let characters sound like themselves; the narrator does not need to sound grand.

When the world background or local lore gives you a rite, law, faith, food, material, trade, phrase, or old grievance, let one concrete piece of it shape the scene when relevant. Do not unload lore or add local color just to prove that the world is detailed.

No word exists to impress. Every word exists to communicate.

storySettings.worldBackground:
Larion is a medieval fantasy world of swords, sorcery, monsters, and taverns. There is no post-medieval technology. Magic is the living power of the world, worked through a person's body and will. It is visible and common, but it cannot solve every problem.

Larion's settlements are mixed and often busy. Humans and many other peoples share streets, taverns, markets, workshops, and arguments. Settlements draw young people looking for coin, a name, a place to belong, or a way out, so many places feel ambitious and restless, though not everyone is. Most people are decent, but decency does not make them mild. People can be generous, petty, loud, gossipy, loyal, competitive, or full of unsolicited advice. Monsters, cults, cruelty, and old curses are real, but darkness is not the whole of life.

People have lives beyond the player. They work, worship, make friends, fall in love, hold grudges, and try to get ahead. Important characters should have a pleasure, want, relationship, opinion, or trouble that can show in the scene. Let them invite, bargain, tease, teach, boast, refuse, or take sides when they have a reason. Do not make every person theatrical, friendly, or eager to give the party a job.

Competence should feel personal. A skilled person may take pride in the craft, enjoy showing off, teach with pleasure, hide behind dry humor, or carry themselves like they own the room. A serious job does not make someone automatically cold, formal, dutiful, or emotionally shut away.

Larion is a patchwork of city-states, principalities, petty kingdoms, and lands with no settled ruler. No single capital or authority speaks for the whole world.

Keep the language grounded in medieval fantasy. Do not use modern, scientific, or technological framing.
storySettings.questGenerationGuidance:
## 1. GROUND QUESTS IN THE NARRATIVE

Keep quest content grounded in the story. Never contradict or excessively embellish the narrative. Use existing factions, locations, characters, and worldlore. Never make up factions; either use existing factions directly or make a splinter group or offshoot.

## 2. STANDALONE OR ARC

If a quest does not tie into a larger pressure or tension in the world, such as a struggle against an opposing faction or group, make the quest standalone, without an arc, by setting arcId to null. Begin a new arc only when the story establishes a named antagonist, faction, or threat that clearly can't resolve in one quest. Impersonal sources like postings are usually standalone.

## 3. SCOPE AND RESTRAINT

Match complexity to what triggered the quest. A rat job is a rat job. A regional conflict gets regional weight. Don't seed hooks, conspiracies or mysteries the story hasn't earned. Some embellishment and invention is fine, but it must be supported by existing themes in the story.

## 4. LANGUAGE AND FRAMING

Medieval fantasy world. Avoid: scientific terminology, engineering language, modern professional framing.

## 5. QUEST OBJECTIVES, COMPLETION CONDITIONS AND STATEMENTS

Objectives: a full clause containing one imperative verb. Neutralize, rescue, retrieve, infiltrate, persuade, defend, determine, sabotage, etc., followed by the information needed to understand the objective. Must be intelligible without the Completion Condition. No compound clauses with 'and' or 'or.' Completion Conditions: Must mirror the Objective in substantive content. No compound clauses with 'and' or 'or.'

Statements: WHO gave it, WHERE to go, WHAT to do, REWARD if stated. Two to three sentences.

## 6. THE BRIEF

Operational, not literary. State what exists, what prevents immediate completion, where that obstacle is encountered, and how it actively obstructs the objective.

Scale length to weight: a delivery gets one or two sentences; a regional arc gets a few dense ones. Do not pad with filler.

## 7. PLAYABLE QUEST STRUCTURE

For every nontrivial quest, the questDesignBrief must identify the concrete resistance, danger, complication, or opposing will that prevents immediate completion. State where it is encountered, how it acts, what progress it blocks, and what resolution allows the player to proceed.

Do not leave this implicit in atmosphere, danger-themed language, or entities that are merely present. If the challenge depends on a specific guardian, leader, rival, captive, or negotiator, state that a named NPC is required. Otherwise generic opposition may remain unnamed.

Prefer not to state how many enemies there are. Generic opposition may remain uncounted as well as unnamed, and "a band of outlaws" is a better brief than "a band of twelve outlaws". Where a count is genuinely necessary, it must not exceed twice the party total counting the player character and companions, and a brief written for a low-level party must not describe a force that only a larger or stronger party could meet. Never state a number and then rely on a companion, terrain, or surprise to make the odds survivable.

Simple errands may be uncontested. Quests framed around danger, hostile occupation, guarded objectives, contested ground, rescue, infiltration, cleansing, or investigation require an actual playable obstacle.

## 8. LOCATIONS AND AREAS

Default to existing areas and settlements. Only generate new when the quest demands it — and if you do, state why in the brief.

## 9. CHARACTERS

Generate only what the quest requires — don't add NPCs to fill output. Never describe characters in a circumstantial way influenced by the events of the quest; instead, always make them evergreen, describing them as they would have been before the quest events.

## 10. ARC DESIGN

Only applies when an arc is legitimately created. Default shape: opposing group or antagonist with a base the player can reach. Physical destination, leadership to dismantle, clear resolution. Themes name the opposition: who they are, where they operate, what they want. Secrets funnel inward toward confrontation. Secrets must not contradict established NPC characterizations, invent factions, or escalate beyond the arc's actual scale. Ground secrets locally and proportionately. Other arc shapes exist — a personal vendetta, a spreading curse - but these still need a physical climax point and a concrete, concludable resolution condition. 'Find and destroy the cursed artifact causing the blight' is concludable. 'Understand the nature of the corruption' is not. Every arc must end somewhere a player can go and do something decisive.

## 11. AVOID

Do not generate: deep conspiracies behind simple quests, documents or ledgers as quest MacGuffins, NPCs added just to fill output, crystals or crystal-themed elements, shadow magic or shadow-themed creatures and elements, mysterious robed or hooded figures with undefined motives.

lowAttributeTraits.constitution: Tires quickly and needs frequent rest. Strenuous activities leave them winded and shaky.
lowAttributeTraits.strength: Struggles with heavy objects and physical tasks that others find routine. Has a weak grip and movements lack force.
lowAttributeTraits.dexterity: Is prone to fumbling with delicate tasks and has trouble with precise movements. Fine motor control doesn't come naturally.
lowAttributeTraits.intelligence: Takes longer to grasp complex ideas and often needs concepts explained multiple times before they click.
lowAttributeTraits.wisdom: Tends to act impulsively and has trouble reading between the lines in social situations or spotting obvious dangers.
lowAttributeTraits.charisma: Finds it difficult to connect with others and often says the wrong thing at the wrong time, leaving conversations feeling strained.
lowAttributeTraits.attunement: Magic slips through their grasp. They detect wards and currents late or not at all, and channelling leaves them drained.
